body:
`OPNsenseNetmapRingFull` declares itself SUSTAINED and its runbook says "an isolated burst during a
traffic spike is normal, a persistent condition is not". It then pages on exactly that: two isolated
bursts 15 minutes apart during a traffic spike.

This is the same class of defect as #594 (`OPNsenseDHCP6AllocationFailures`) — a rule whose declared
intent is "sustained" and whose numbers deliver something much closer to "one burst". It is not
caught by `test_single_event_sensitivity.py` because that test's invariant (pending period must
exceed the widest window) is **necessary but not sufficient**, and this rule satisfies it at only 2×.

## Current shape

`grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:694`

```python
A="sum by (device, opnsense_instance) (rate(opnsense_log_events_netmap_ring_full_events_total[15m]))",
op="gt", params=[0, 0], for_min=30,
```

A single counter increment at `T` makes `rate(m[15m])` positive for every evaluation in `(T, T+15m]`.
So the minimum event pattern that satisfies `gt 0` continuously for 30m is **two events 15 minutes
apart** — one gap, two occurrences, total. That is an isolated burst, not a persistent condition.

`for(30m) > window(15m)` passes the `SUSTAINED` assertion in
`grafana/tests/test_single_event_sensitivity.py`, so the guard reports green on a rule that does not
behave as classified. The margin, not just the ordering, is what makes a rule sustained.

## Observed false page

Live homelab box (`opnsense`, `device=ixl0`), 2026-08-12. The counter
`opnsense_log_events_netmap_ring_full_events_total` stepped four times (BST):

| time | increment | ixl0 throughput at that minute |
|---|---|---|
| 13:50 | +8 | 528 Mbps |
| 14:00 | +4 | 405 Mbps |
| 15:25 | +2 | 106 Mbps |
| 15:40 | +4 | 532 Mbps |

The 15:25 → 15:40 pair is exactly 15 minutes apart, which is sufficient to hold `gt 0` across the
full 30m pending period. Alert fired warning, routed to IRM, then self-resolved.

Daily totals since the metric first appeared on 2026-07-31: `0, 2, 8, 6, 0, 6, 0, 0, 0, 18, 4, 16, 4`.
Handfuls of occurrences, every one of them coincident with a short LAN throughput burst.

The datapath was healthy throughout — `eastpect` running, `ifconfig ixl0` carrying `NETMAP`, zero
`Emulated adapter` lines in `dmesg` since boot, and the kernel's own log lines showing the ring
draining immediately (`netmap_transmit ixl0 full hwcur 131 hwtail 84 qlen 46`, `... qlen 0` against a
1024-slot host ring). Notably 16:55 and 17:00 the same day both carried ~538/504 Mbps with **zero**
occurrences, so this is not a bandwidth threshold — it is burstiness against netmap's single-threaded
host re-injection path.

## Fix

Adopt the `opnsense-endpoint-errors` reference shape that `build_rules.py:256-258` already documents
and that #594 followed: a deliberately **short** inner window under a **long** pending period, so the
condition holds only while every rolling window stays non-empty.

```python
A="sum by (device, opnsense_instance) (rate(opnsense_log_events_netmap_ring_full_events_total[5m]))",
op="gt", params=[0, 0], for_min=30,
```

This requires an occurrence in **every rolling 5m window for a solid 30 minutes** — genuinely
continuous. Properties:

- The 2026-08-12 pattern (gaps of 10 and 15 minutes) never fires. Nor does any of the historical data
  above.
- A genuinely saturated ring still fires, and quickly: the kernel rate-limits the underlying log line
  to 2/s, so a persistent condition keeps every window non-empty by construction. Sensitivity to the
  thing the rule is *for* is unchanged.
- `[5m]` rather than endpoint-errors' `[2m]`: this series is fed by the push-based syslog receiver and
  read at the scrape interval, so a 2m window can hold as few as two samples. 5m keeps the shape while
  leaving margin for a 60s scrape.

Also needs updating in the same change, or the repo documents behaviour it no longer has:

- the `runbook['measures']` and `runbook['threshold']` strings on the rule (they name the 15m window
  and describe the old semantics)
- the `description` annotation (it says "for 30m" without saying what has to be true for 30m)
- the `SUSTAINED` reason string in `grafana/tests/test_single_event_sensitivity.py:90-91` — the current
  text is the runbook's *intent*, which was never what the rule did

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `build_rules.py` netmap rule uses a 5m inner window with `for_min=30`
- [ ] `description` + runbook `measures`/`threshold` text describe the new semantics explicitly ("at
      least one occurrence in every rolling 5m window for the full 30m")
- [ ] `SUSTAINED` reason in `test_single_event_sensitivity.py` states the real invariant
- [ ] `make rules` regenerated; `grafana/alerts/grafana-managed/opnsense-netmap-ring-full.json` and
      `grafana/runbooks.md` reflect the change
- [ ] `make grafana-check` green
- [ ] `grafana/tests` green, including the single-event-sensitivity classification test

comments.body:
Fixed in `72585d35` (pushed to `main`).

Window 15m → 5m, pending period unchanged at 30m. Firing now needs an occurrence in every rolling 5m window for a solid 30m.

Added `NetmapRingFullTest` to `grafana/tests/test_single_event_sensitivity.py` covering the gap the existing sweep structurally missed — it models ONE isolated event, whereas the defect here was *several* isolated events spaced wider than the window, chained into a page by a pending period that only just exceeded it. Verified by patching the generated manifest back to `[15m]`: both new cases fail on the old shape and pass on the new one, while `test_the_pending_period_exceeds_the_window` passes in **both** — which is the point.

```
FAIL: test_the_observed_burst_cadence_does_not_fire
FAIL: test_two_occurrences_one_window_apart_do_not_chain
AssertionError: 30 not less than 30 : OPNsenseNetmapRingFull: two occurrences one
window apart span 30 evaluations, which reaches its 30-evaluation pending period.
The window must be well under half the pending period, not merely under it
```

Gates: `grafana/tests` 423 tests OK, `make grafana-check` green (1200 Prometheus targets, 78 rule expressions, 80 manifests validated, no regeneration staleness).

Not done, and deliberately out of scope: generalising the `SUSTAINED` assertion in the sweep from `for > window` to something with a real margin (e.g. `for >= 3 * window`). That would re-classify other rules and needs its own pass — worth a follow-up issue if the pattern shows up a third time.

title: OPNsenseNetmapRingFull pages on an isolated burst despite being classified SUSTAINED

body:
## What

The long tail of the <host-1> debug-capture triage: seven programs, **25 of 1956 entries (1.3%)**,
none individually worth its own issue. Recorded together so the archive triage from #659 is complete
and nothing here has to be re-derived.

Triaged from `/opt/opnsense2otel/capture/syslog/*.ndjson`, 2026-08-04 08:46 → 2026-08-07 16:33 UTC.

> Counts are shape samples, not frequencies — the capture lane dedupes by
> `(program, NormaliseShape(message))` per 15-minute window (`internal/logship/capture/dedupe.go`).

| program | entries | shapes | subsystem | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kernel` | 4 | 2 | `kernel` | **worth structuring** |
| `sudo` | 1 | 1 | `auth` | **worth structuring** |
| `root` | 9 | 3 | **none (empty)** | correctly generic; fix subsystem |
| `lighttpd` | 2 | 2 | `proxy` | correctly generic |
| `sshd-session` | 2 | 2 | `auth` | correctly generic — already deliberate |
| `dhclient` | 2 | 2 | `dhcp` | correctly generic |
| `php` | 3 | 1 | **none (empty)** | correctly generic; fix subsystem |

## Shapes and verdicts

### `kernel` — worth structuring

```
<6>[331947] ixl1: promiscuous mode enabled
<6>[331992] ixl1: promiscuous mode disabled
<6>[340117] ixl1: promiscuous mode enabled
<6>[340137] ixl1: promiscuous mode disabled
```

Prefix is `<PRI>[uptime-seconds]` — a **second, kernel-internal** syslog priority and monotonic
timestamp *inside* the message body, after the RFC5424 envelope has already been stripped. Any
`kernel` parser must strip it; a body-scan parser that does not will read `<6>[331947]` as content.

Promiscuous mode toggling on `ixl1` is worth structuring for two independent reasons: it is
security-relevant (something put an interface into promiscuous mode), and it is directly relevant to
this exporter, because promiscuous mode is what a packet capture or a flow exporter turns on. The
enable/disable pairs here are ~45 s and ~20 s apart, consistent with short deliberate captures rather
than anything persistent. Closed vocabulary, negligible volume, bounded cardinality (interface names).

### `sudo` — worth structuring

```
     rob : PWD=/home/rob ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/true
```

Leading whitespace is upstream's padding. The format is the long-stable
`user : TTY=… ; PWD=… ; USER=… ; COMMAND=…` (the `TTY=` field is absent here; it is present when sudo
runs from a terminal, so a parser must treat the field list as optional and order-tolerant rather
than fixed).

One captured line only, because the operator rarely sudos on the firewall — but privilege escalation
on the firewall is a first-class audit event and `sudo` already maps to the `auth` subsystem
(`internal/logship/syslog/registry.go:183`) alongside `sshd`/`sshd-session`, which *do* have a
parser (`internal/logship/syslog/sshd.go:68`). Leaving `sudo` unparsed is a hole in an otherwise
covered subsystem. Volume is bounded by human activity.

**Fixture caution:** one real line is not enough to pin the format. Derive the `TTY=`-present and
`COMMAND` -with-arguments cases from upstream sudo's own `log_allowed`/`log_denied` format rather
than inventing them, and comment those cases as source-derived. The authentication-failure shape
(`user is not in the sudoers file`, `N incorrect password attempts`) is the one that actually matters
for alerting and is **not** in this archive at all.

### `root` — correctly left generic; fix the subsystem

```
bogons update starting
Bogons V4 file updated: no changes.
update bogons is ending the update cycle
```

`root` is the syslog tag for anything cron runs as root, so the message space is open-ended by
construction — today it is the bogons updater, tomorrow it is any other root cron job. There is no
closed vocabulary to parse against, and a bogons-specific regex under a program tag that means
"root's cron" would be matching on the wrong key. The bogons table is better sourced from the API
than from scraped English. **But** `root` has no subsystem mapping, so these ship unselectable.

### `lighttpd` — correctly left generic

```
(/usr/obj/usr/ports/www/lighttpd/work/lighttpd-1.4.85/src/gw_backend.c.534) connect() /var/lib/php/tmp/php-fastcgi.socket-3: Connection refused
(/usr/obj/usr/ports/www/lighttpd/work/lighttpd-1.4.85/src/mod_openssl.c.4821) SSL: addr:<lan-ip-1> ssl_err:5 rd:-1 errno:60: Operation timed out
```

The leading parenthesis is lighttpd's **build-time source path and line number**, which changes on
every lighttpd version bump and every port rebuild. Anchoring a regex on it guarantees breakage on
upgrade, and the payload after it is free-form C error text with no closed vocabulary. This is the
web GUI's own error log; the durable signal (is the GUI up?) belongs to a health check, not to
scraped strings. Two entries in 3.5 days.

### `sshd-session` — correctly left generic, and already deliberate

```
Read error from remote host <lan-ip-1> port 48924: Connection reset by peer
Read error from remote host <lan-ip-1> port 59920: Operation timed out
```

`sshd-session` **is** registered (`internal/logship/syslog/sshd.go:68`, alongside `sshd` — the
OpenSSH 9.8 process split is already handled). These are non-auth transport chatter, which that
parser deliberately declines. **No action.** Recorded here only so a future triage does not read the
program name as an unhandled-rename bug — it was checked, and it is not one.

### `dhclient` — correctly left generic

```
dhclient-script: Creating resolv.conf
dhclient-script: New Hostname (ixl1): opnsense
```

`dhclient-script` is an operator-editable shell script; its output is not an interface. Lease state
is already collected from the API. Two entries in 3.5 days.

### `php` — correctly left generic; fix the subsystem

```
error connecting to Google Drive
```

A bare error string from the Google Drive backup plugin with no code, no cause and no context.
`php` is a shared tag for every PHP-emitted line on the box, so the message space is open-ended.
Nothing to parse. It does, however, ship with no subsystem.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `root` and `php` added to the `subsystems` map in `internal/logship/syslog/registry.go`
      (`root` → a system/`core` subsystem; `php` → `web` or the same subsystem as `lighttpd`)
- [x] `kernel` parser strips the `<PRI>[uptime]` in-body prefix and emits
      `kernel.event` = `promiscuous_enabled` / `promiscuous_disabled` with `interface.device`
      (the kernel device name — **not** `opnsense.interface`, which is the description space; see
      `internal/logship/shape_attrs.go`)
- [x] `sudo` parser emits `auth.user`, `auth.target_user`, `auth.command`, `auth.pwd`, and
      `auth.tty` when present, tolerating an absent `TTY=` field
- [x] The sudo failure shapes are derived from upstream sudo source and their test cases commented
      as source-derived, not capture-derived
- [x] `lighttpd`, `dhclient`, `php`, `root` and `sshd-session` explicitly left generic, each with a
      one-line code comment recording the reason (open vocabulary / build-path instability /
      already-deliberate), so this triage is not repeated
- [x] Table-driven tests over the verbatim `kernel` and `sudo` lines above
- [x] `make test` / `make docs` green

comments.body:
Landed in `3ea6692b` (pushed to `main`).

**Structured:** `kernel` promiscuous-mode toggles (`kernel.event`, `interface.device`) — an interface entering promiscuous mode is what packet capture looks like from outside, and it was invisible. Device is `interface.device`, not `opnsense.interface`, since the latter is the resolved LAN/IOT/MGMT description space and the two are disjoint. And `sudo` (`auth.result`, `auth.user`, `auth.target_user`, `auth.command`, `auth.pwd`, `auth.tty`).

**On the sudo credential question:** `auth.command` ships the command line verbatim, arguments included. A password typed as an argument is logged by sudo itself and already ships today in the generic record's body — structuring it changes how the line is queried, not who can see it or where it is stored. Like every attribute here it is structured metadata, never a metric label, mirroring `sshd.go`'s precedent for usernames rather than inventing a policy.

Only the sudo success shape exists in the archive, so failure shapes are derived from upstream `log_denied()` and `fmt_authfail_message()` (including its ngettext singular/plural split) and marked source-derived.

**Left generic, each with a recorded reason:** `sshd-session` (already registered at `sshd.go:68` — checked and cleared, not re-investigated), `lighttpd`, `dhclient`, and `php`/`root` — the last two being catch-all logger tags in the same class as `opnsense`.

Cross-lane collision handled here rather than left red: `TestCARPUnrelatedKernelLinesAreNotClaimed` listed the two promiscuous lines as proof unrelated kernel chatter stays generic. They are now legitimately claimed, so they move out with a note — exactly as the `arp: ... moved from ...` line did in #536 — and the CARP half of the contract is preserved in a new `TestCARPDeclinesPromiscuousModeLines` rather than dropped.

One correction to this issue's own premise: it listed 7 programs as shipping with an empty `opnsense_subsystem`. Only `DhcpLFC`, `config`, `configctl`, `rule-updater.py`, `php`, `root` and `opnsense` were genuinely unmapped — `syslog-ng`, `kernel`, `lighttpd`, `sudo`, `sshd-session`, `dhclient` and `kea-dhcp6` were **already** mapped.

Gate green on the committed tree: `make test` 28 packages ok / 0 failures, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `make docs-check` and `make grafana-check` both exit 0. Shared seams (`registry.go` subsystem attribution, `derive.go` family decisions, the `docs/syslog-receiver.md` parser table) landed together in `0ad3d468` rather than being contended six ways.

title: logship: triage the long tail of unparsed programs (kernel, sudo, root, lighttpd, sshd-session, dhclient, php)

body:
## What

`dpinger` has a parser (`internal/logship/syslog/dpinger.go:53`) covering the `MONITOR:` alarm
transitions, but its **lifecycle** lines fall through unparsed — 9 entries, 3 shapes, in the <host-1>
debug-capture archive.

Triaged from `/opt/opnsense2otel/capture/syslog/*.ndjson`, 2026-08-04 08:46 → 2026-08-07 16:33 UTC.
Context: #659.

> Counts are shape samples, not frequencies — the capture lane dedupes by
> `(program, NormaliseShape(message))` per 15-minute window (`internal/logship/capture/dedupe.go`).

## Shapes

All three, verbatim:

```
exiting on signal 15
Reloaded gateway watcher configuration on SIGHUP
send_interval 1000ms  loss_interval 4000ms  time_period 60000ms  report_interval 0ms  data_len 1  alert_interval 1000ms  latency_alarm 0ms  loss_alarm 0%  alarm_hold 10000ms  dest_addr <pub-ip-1>  bind_addr <pub-ip-2>  identifier "AAISP_PPPOE "
```

Note on the third line: fields are separated by **two** spaces, and `identifier` is quoted with a
**trailing space inside the quotes** (`"AAISP_PPPOE "`) — upstream's padding, not a capture artifact.
A naive single-space split or an unquoted `(\S+)` capture on the identifier both get this wrong.

`exiting on signal 15` and the startup config line are emitted around a dpinger restart; the SIGHUP
line is emitted when OPNsense reconfigures the gateway watcher without restarting it. All three
occurred at the same times as the `rc.routing_configure` / `plugins_configure monitor
(dpinger_configure_do)` lines triaged in the config-apply-chain issue filed alongside this one.

## Verdict: worth structuring — the lifecycle lines explain gaps in the alarm lane

The existing parser structures *transitions*. It cannot structure the absence of one, and dpinger
restarting is exactly when transitions go missing: between `exiting on signal 15` and the next
startup line, the gateway watcher is not watching, so no alarm can fire regardless of gateway state.

This matters directly and concretely for the alerting added in `b64d34b6` ("add hysteresis to gateway
flapping rule, add RTT baseline-deviation rule"). A hysteresis window that spans a dpinger restart is
reasoning over a period in which the signal was structurally absent, not stable. Emitting a
`gateway.event = watcher_stopped` / `watcher_reloaded` alongside the existing alarm events makes that
window identifiable rather than indistinguishable from a healthy quiet period.

The startup config line is a second, independent win: `latency_alarm 0ms  loss_alarm 0%` says the
*firewall-side* alarm thresholds are disabled on this gateway. Every `delay` alarm the parser is
built to catch therefore cannot fire on this box, and nothing else says so. Structuring the
thresholds turns "we have never seen a delay alarm" from an ambiguous observation into a
configuration fact.

Volume is negligible — three lines per reconfigure — the vocabulary is closed, and the cardinality is
bounded by the gateway count.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `parseDPinger` extended with three lifecycle branches, keeping `gateway.event` as the existing
      closed vocabulary and adding `watcher_stopped`, `watcher_reloaded`, `watcher_started`
- [x] `exiting on signal N` emits `gateway.signal` as an integer
- [x] The startup config line emits `gateway.name` (from `identifier`, **with the trailing space
      inside the quotes trimmed**), `gateway.address` (from `dest_addr`), `gateway.bind_address`,
      and the alarm thresholds `gateway.latency_alarm_ms`, `gateway.loss_alarm_percent`,
      `gateway.alarm_hold_ms` — named consistently with the existing `gateway.*` vocabulary in
      `internal/logship/syslog/dpinger.go`
- [x] A test pins the double-space separator and the quoted-identifier trailing space, using the
      verbatim captured line above
- [x] Existing `MONITOR:` alarm tests still pass unchanged
- [x] An unrecognised dpinger line still falls through to a generic record
- [x] `make test` / `make docs` green

comments.body:
Landed in `8cca5da9` (pushed to `main`).

Existing parser extended (no re-registration) with `watcher_stopped`, `watcher_reloaded` and `watcher_started`, the last carrying `gateway.latency_alarm_ms`, `gateway.loss_alarm_percent`, `gateway.alarm_hold_ms` and both addresses.

**The threshold readback is why the startup line was worth parsing.** On the live box they are `latency_alarm 0ms` / `loss_alarm 0%` — a delay alarm **cannot fire there at all**. That is a standing configuration fact no metric exposes, and one you would otherwise only discover by wondering why an alert never fires. It is recorded in the file's comment block alongside the restart-vs-recovery point, which is the same blind spot `b64d34b6`'s flapping hysteresis was working around.

`send_interval`/`loss_interval`/`time_period`/`report_interval`/`data_len`/`alert_interval` are matched to anchor the fixed field order but not emitted — tuning parameters, not alarm thresholds.

No existing test was modified; the negative table gained three near-miss shapes so partial matches still degrade to generic.

Gate green on the committed tree: `make test` 28 packages ok / 0 failures, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `make docs-check` and `make grafana-check` both exit 0. Shared seams (`registry.go` subsystem attribution, `derive.go` family decisions, the `docs/syslog-receiver.md` parser table) landed together in `0ad3d468` rather than being contended six ways.

title: logship: structure dpinger lifecycle lines (restart / SIGHUP / startup thresholds) — they explain gaps in the alarm lane

body:
## What

Four programs form one coherent group — the OPNsense **config-apply chain**: a config write
(`config`), the event fan-out that observes it (`configctl`), the template regeneration it triggers
(`configd.py`), and the service reconfiguration that results (`opnsense`). Together they are **105
of 1956 capture entries (5.4%)**, all unparsed.

Triaged from `/opt/opnsense2otel/capture/syslog/*.ndjson` on <host-1>, 2026-08-04 08:46 → 2026-08-07
16:33 UTC. Context: #659.

> Counts are shape samples, not frequencies — the capture lane dedupes by
> `(program, NormaliseShape(message))` per 15-minute window (`internal/logship/capture/dedupe.go`).

| program | entries | distinct shapes | subsystem | parser registered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `configd.py` | 51 | 17 | `audit` | yes — `parseAudit`, `internal/logship/syslog/audit.go:143` (does not match these) |
| `opnsense` | 42 | 14 | **none (empty)** | yes — `parseACME`, `internal/logship/syslog/acme.go:162` (does not match these) |
| `configctl` | 6 | 1 | **none (empty)** | no |
| `config` | 6 | 1 | **none (empty)** | no |

## Shapes

### `config` — the config-write event (6 entries, 1 shape)

```
config-event: new_config /conf/backup/config-1785940860.1638.xml
config-event: new_config /conf/backup/config-1786116252.609.xml
config-event: new_config /conf/backup/config-1786119641.2558.xml
```

The filename embeds the **unix timestamp of the change** (`1786116252` = 2026-08-07 16:24:12 local —
exactly the `log-queries` change described in #659).

### `configctl` — the same event, re-logged with the original line embedded (6 entries, 1 shape)

```
event @ 1786116252.62 msg: Aug  7 16:24:12 <host-2> config[39231]: config-event: new_config /conf/backup/config-1786116252.609.xml 
```

Note the trailing space, and that the payload is a **complete nested BSD-syslog line** — this is a
re-emission of the `config` line above, not new information.

### `configd.py` — template regeneration (51 entries, 17 shapes)

```
generate template container OPNsense/Unbound/core
generate template container OPNsense/Syslog
 OPNsense/Unbound/* generated //var/unbound/advanced.conf
 OPNsense/Unbound/* generated //usr/local/etc/unbound.opnsense.d/domainoverrides.conf
 OPNsense/Syslog generated //usr/local/etc/syslog-ng.conf.d/syslog-ng-destinations.conf
```

The `generated` shape has a **leading space** and a **doubled slash** in the path; both are upstream's,
not a capture artifact.

### `opnsense` — service reconfiguration and routing (42 entries, 14 shapes)

```
/usr/local/sbin/pluginctl: plugins_configure unbound_start (1)
/usr/local/sbin/pluginctl: plugins_configure unbound_start (execute task : unbound_configure_do(1))
/usr/local/sbin/pluginctl: plugins_configure unbound_stop (1)
/usr/local/sbin/pluginctl: plugins_configure unbound_stop (execute task : unbound_service_stop(1))
/usr/local/sbin/pluginctl: warning: ignoring missing default tunable request: hw.ibrs_disable
/usr/local/etc/rc.routing_configure: ROUTING: entering configure using defaults
/usr/local/etc/rc.routing_configure: ROUTING: configuring inet default gateway on opt7
/usr/local/etc/rc.routing_configure: ROUTING: configuring inet6 default gateway on opt7
/usr/local/etc/rc.routing_configure: ROUTING: keeping inet default route to <pub-ip-3>
/usr/local/etc/rc.routing_configure: ROUTING: keeping inet6 default route to fe80::9e89:1eff:fe2e:0%pppoe0
/usr/local/etc/rc.routing_configure: ROUTING: treating '<pub-ip-3>' as far gateway for '<pub-ip-2>/32'
/usr/local/etc/rc.routing_configure: Chose to bind AAISP_PPPOE on <pub-ip-2> since we could not find a proper match.
/usr/local/etc/rc.routing_configure: plugins_configure monitor (1,null)
/usr/local/etc/rc.routing_configure: plugins_configure monitor (execute task : dpinger_configure_do(1,null))
```

The `opnsense` program is a **shared tag for arbitrary rc/pluginctl scripts**, keyed by the script
path before the first colon. Its message space is open-ended: any script under `/usr/local/etc/rc.*`
or `/usr/local/sbin/*` can log here. That is decisive for the verdict below.

## Verdict

Split three ways.

**`config` — worth structuring. The one clear win here.** `config-event: new_config` is the
firewall's own timestamped record of *every* configuration change, with a backup file that names the
version. The exporter already ships Grafana annotations
(`OPN2OTEL_ANNOTATIONS_GRAFANA_URL`); a config-change event is exactly the annotation that makes
"did a config change cause this?" answerable on every dashboard, and it is currently landing as an
unparsed generic record with no subsystem. One shape, one regex, closed vocabulary, ~2 lines/day.

**`configctl` — worth DROPPING (or at minimum, never structuring).** It is a verbatim
re-emission of the `config` line, wrapped in a second syslog envelope. Structuring it would produce
a duplicate record for every config change — the same double-count hazard #659 flags for the two DNS
lanes. It should either be left as a generic record with a code comment saying it is a known
duplicate, or filtered. **Recommend: leave generic, comment it, do not parse.** Do not both parse
`config` and parse `configctl`.

**`configd.py` template lines — correctly left as a generic record.** They are a per-file trace of
template rendering: 15 lines for one Unbound reconfigure, with no status, no error, and no outcome.
The information they carry ("a config apply happened") is already carried better by `config` above,
at 1 line instead of 15. Structuring them would multiply record count by ~15 per config change for
strictly less signal. The *error* branch of `configd.py` would be worth structuring, but no failure
occurred in the capture window, so there is nothing here to derive a fixture from.

**`opnsense` — correctly left as a generic record.** The message space is open-ended by
construction: the program tag is shared by every rc script and plugin on the box, and the text is
free-form English written per-script. There is no closed vocabulary to parse against, and a regex
tuned to `rc.routing_configure`'s current wording would silently stop matching on any OPNsense
release that reworded it — which upstream does freely, since these are operator-facing strings, not
an interface. The routing lines are genuinely interesting, but the durable source for default-route
state is the gateway/routing collector polling the API, not scraped English.

The empty-subsystem gap is worth fixing for all three unmapped programs regardless of the parsing
verdict — a generic record with no `opnsense_subsystem` cannot be selected on at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `config`, `configctl` and `opnsense` added to the `subsystems` map in
      `internal/logship/syslog/registry.go` (`config`/`configctl` → the same subsystem as
      `configd.py`, i.e. `audit`; `opnsense` → a system/`core` subsystem)
- [x] Parser for `config` emitting `config.event` = `new_config`, `config.backup_path`, and
      `config.version` (the unix timestamp parsed out of the filename, as an integer)
- [x] `configctl` explicitly left generic with a code comment stating it duplicates `config` and
      must not be parsed, plus a test asserting it does **not** produce a structured record
- [x] `configd.py` template lines and `opnsense` rc/pluginctl lines explicitly left generic, with
      the open-vocabulary reason in a code comment
- [x] Table-driven tests over the verbatim `config` lines above
- [x] `make test` / `make docs` green

comments.body:
Landed in `dc76bc2c` (pushed to `main`).

`config` structured into `config.event`, `config.backup_path`, `config.version`. Everything else in the chain deliberately left generic.

**The double-count guard is the load-bearing part.** `configctl` re-emits the same config-event line inside a second envelope, so structuring it would produce two records per real config change and silently double any panel counting them. It is therefore not registered at all, and the guard is `TestConfigctlNotRegistered` asserting `parserFor("configctl")` returns `ok=false` — the dispatch-path assertion, not merely a regex-does-not-match one. `config` is also in `nonDerivedPrograms`, since a derived counter is precisely where that double-count would resurface.

`configd.py` template lines stay generic: up to 15 per apply, no status, outcome or error — strictly less signal than the one `config` line they accompany, and the error branch was not modelable because no failure occurred in the capture window to derive a fixture from.

`opnsense` stays generic for the reason `registry.go` already records against it: a catch-all logger tag where a regex tuned to today's wording would silently break on any reworded release.

Both omissions now carry their reasons in the code, so they do not read as oversights later.

Gate green on the committed tree: `make test` 28 packages ok / 0 failures, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `make docs-check` and `make grafana-check` both exit 0. Shared seams (`registry.go` subsystem attribution, `derive.go` family decisions, the `docs/syslog-receiver.md` parser table) landed together in `0ad3d468` rather than being contended six ways.

body:
## What

`rule-updater.py` — OPNsense's Suricata ruleset downloader — writes 39 unparsed entries in the
<host-1> debug-capture archive across 2 shapes. No parser, and **no subsystem assigned**
(`subsystemFor` returns empty, `internal/logship/syslog/registry.go:279`), so these records ship
with no `opnsense_subsystem` at all.

Triaged from `/opt/opnsense2otel/capture/syslog/*.ndjson`, 2026-08-04 08:46 → 2026-08-07 16:33 UTC.
Context: #659.

> Counts are shape samples, not frequencies — the capture lane dedupes by
> `(program, NormaliseShape(message))` per 15-minute window (`internal/logship/capture/dedupe.go`).
> Because the URL is part of the shape, each distinct ruleset URL is its own entry, so the shape
> inventory here is complete even though the frequencies are not.

## Shapes

### Shape 1 — `download completed for <url>` (36 entries, 12 distinct URLs)

Every captured line, verbatim:

```
download completed for https://feodotracker.abuse.ch/downloads/feodotracker.rules
download completed for https://rules.emergingthreats.net/open/suricata-8.0/emerging.rules.tar.gz
download completed for https://rulesets.opnsense.org/suricata/opnsense.file_transfer.rules
download completed for https://rulesets.opnsense.org/suricata/opnsense.mail.rules
download completed for https://rulesets.opnsense.org/suricata/opnsense.media_streaming.rules
download completed for https://rulesets.opnsense.org/suricata/opnsense.messaging.rules
download completed for https://rulesets.opnsense.org/suricata/opnsense.social_media.rules
download completed for https://rulesets.opnsense.org/suricata/opnsense.test.rules
download completed for https://sslbl.abuse.ch/blacklist/sslblacklist_tls_cert.rules
download completed for https://sslbl.abuse.ch/blacklist/sslipblacklist.rules
download completed for https://threatfox.abuse.ch/downloads/threatfox_suricata.rules
download completed for https://urlhaus.abuse.ch/downloads/suricata-ids/
```

### Shape 2 — `version response for <url> : <n>` (3 entries)

```
version response for https://rules.emergingthreats.net/open/suricata-8.0/version.txt : 11249
version response for https://rules.emergingthreats.net/open/suricata-8.0/version.txt : 11250
version response for https://rules.emergingthreats.net/open/suricata-8.0/version.txt : 11251
```

The version integer increments by exactly 1 per day across the three captured days (11249 → 11250 →
11251), so it is Emerging Threats' own ruleset serial, not a timestamp.

**The failure shapes are not in this archive**, because nothing failed in the capture window. Any
`download failed`/error branch must be read out of upstream
`src/opnsense/scripts/suricata/rule-updater.py` rather than guessed, and any fixture for it must
come from that source's own branches — not invented, per the repo fixture rule.

## Verdict: worth structuring

Ruleset freshness is a first-class IDS health question and the box answers it nowhere else. The
existing IDS collector reports Suricata's runtime state; it does not report whether the rules
Suricata is running were successfully refreshed, when, or from which feeds. A feed that quietly
stops updating — an abuse.ch URL that starts 404ing, an ET subscription that lapses — is invisible
today and would stay invisible until a missed detection.

Two concrete queries this unlocks and nothing else answers:

- per-feed last-successful-download time, so a stalled feed is visible as an age rather than as
  silence;
- the ET ruleset serial as a value, so "is the box on the current ruleset" is a comparison rather
  than a guess.

Volume is negligible (a handful of lines per update cycle), the vocabulary is closed, and the URL is
a bounded set fixed by the operator's feed configuration — so cardinality is bounded by config, not
by traffic.

The empty-subsystem gap should be fixed regardless: `rule-updater.py` belongs under the same
subsystem as `suricata` (`internal/logship/syslog/suricata.go:13`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `rule-updater.py` added to the `subsystems` map in `internal/logship/syslog/registry.go`,
      matching whatever `suricata` maps to
- [x] Parser registered for `rule-updater.py` emitting `ids.event` from a closed vocabulary
      (`ruleset_downloaded`, `ruleset_version`, plus the failure verbs read out of upstream
      `rule-updater.py`) and `ids.ruleset_url`
- [x] Shape 2 additionally emits `ids.ruleset_version` as an integer
- [x] The failure branch is derived from upstream source, and its test case is commented as
      source-derived rather than capture-derived (no failure occurred in the capture window)
- [x] Table-driven tests over the verbatim lines above
- [x] An unrecognised `rule-updater.py` line still falls through to a generic record
- [x] `make test` / `make docs` green

comments.body:
Landed in `10f315a3` (pushed to `main`).

`ids.event` over a closed vocabulary, plus `ids.ruleset_url`, `ids.ruleset_version`, `ids.ruleset_file`, `ids.ruleset_path`, `ids.http_status`.

The archive holds only the two success shapes, so every failure branch is derived from upstream source and cited per case — `rule-updater.py:101` and `lib/downloader.py:114/133/137/201/204`, fetched live rather than recalled. Each is marked source-derived, not captured.

The exception text in `download failed for <url> (<exception>)` is deliberately not captured: it is `str(exception)` from a Python library — unbounded free text with no grammar. Only the URL is structured.

Cardinality: the ruleset URL is operator-supplied and unbounded, so it is structured metadata only. `rule-updater.py` is recorded in `nonDerivedPrograms` for the matching reason — what matters here is a timestamp and a state, neither of which a counter expresses.

Gate green on the committed tree: `make test` 28 packages ok / 0 failures, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `make docs-check` and `make grafana-check` both exit 0. Shared seams (`registry.go` subsystem attribution, `derive.go` family decisions, the `docs/syslog-receiver.md` parser table) landed together in `0ad3d468` rather than being contended six ways.

body:
## What

`syslog-ng` is the second-largest unparsed program in the <host-1> debug-capture archive — **294 of
1956 entries (15.0%)**, no parser registered. It has a subsystem (`logging`,
`internal/logship/syslog/registry.go:267`) but every line falls through to a generic record.

Triaged from `/opt/opnsense2otel/capture/syslog/*.ndjson` on <host-1>, 2026-08-04 08:46 → 2026-08-07
16:33 UTC. Context: #659, which owns the unbound half of the same archive triage.

> **Counts are shape samples, not frequencies** — the syslog capture lane deduplicates by
> `(program, NormaliseShape(message))` per 15-minute window
> (`internal/logship/syslog/source.go:287`, `internal/logship/capture/dedupe.go`).

**This program is a special case: it is the firewall side of the exporter's own ingest path.**
Every `Syslog connection …` line below names `<lan-ip-1>:5847` — the exporter's TCP listener
(`OPN2OTEL_LOGS_SYSLOG_LISTEN_TCP=:5847`). These lines are the firewall telling us, in band, when
our own log feed dropped. That makes them qualitatively different from ordinary program chatter.

## Shapes

Four groups.

### Group 1 — exporter ingest-link lifecycle (44 entries, 4 shapes)

```
Syslog connection established; fd='23', server='AF_INET(<lan-ip-1>:5847)', local='AF_INET(0.0.0.0:0)'
Syslog connection closed; fd='23', server='AF_INET(<lan-ip-1>:5847)', time_reopen='60'
Syslog connection broken; fd='27', server='AF_INET(<lan-ip-1>:5847)', time_reopen='60'
EOF occurred; fd='23'
```

Observed `fd` values: 7, 23, 24, 25, 27, 29, 31. 13 `established`, 12 `closed`, 1 `broken`, 12 `EOF`.

### Group 2 — the periodic statistics dump (240 entries, 1 shape)

One line, ~4 KB, ~80 `key='scope(name)=value'` pairs. First 400 characters verbatim:

```
Log statistics; queued='global(scratch_buffers_count)=3', eps_since_start='dst.program(d_config_changed_event#0,/usr/local/sbin/configctl -e -t 0.5 system event config_changed)=0', processed='destination(d_local_ntpd)=295', processed='destination(d_local_portalauth)=0', processed='destination(d_config_changed_event)=33', processed='dst.network(d_a11ce000000040008000000000000001#0,tcp,<lan-ip-1>:5847
```

Key names present: `processed`, `dropped`, `queued`, `written`, `stamp`, `memory_usage`,
`eps_since_start`, `eps_last_1h`, `msg_size_avg`, `msg_size_max`, `truncated_count`,
`truncated_bytes`. Scopes: `global(...)`, `source(...)`, `destination(...)`, `dst.network(...)`,
`dst.program(...)`, `src.internal(...)`, `center(...)`.

### Group 3 — configuration reload (12 entries, 3 shapes)

```
Configuration reload requested over control channel;
Loading the new configuration;
Configuration reload finished;
```

### Group 4 — errors (7 entries, 2 shapes)

```
Child program exited, restarting; cmdline='/usr/local/sbin/configctl -e -t 0.5 system event config_changed', status='256'
Error reading data; fd='27', error='Operation timed out (60)'
```

## Verdict

Split, by group. Two of the four are worth structuring and two are not.

**Group 1 — worth structuring. Highest-value item in this issue.** A `closed` or `broken` on
`<lan-ip-1>:5847` is a direct, timestamped statement that the exporter stopped receiving syslog, with
a `time_reopen` telling us how long the hole will be. The exporter's own receiver metrics cannot
report this: from our side a dropped TCP connection and an idle firewall look identical. 12 closes
and 1 break in a 3.5-day window is not a quiet signal. Structuring it makes "did we lose syslog, or
did nothing happen?" answerable, which today it is not.

**Group 2 — worth structuring, but narrowly: extract only `dropped=*` and `truncated_count=*`.**
Parsing all ~80 pairs would mint one attribute per syslog-ng destination and turn a log line into a
metrics scrape by the back door — wrong shape, and a cardinality problem on a box with many
destinations. But `dropped` is the counter that says the firewall's own pipeline threw messages
away before they ever reached us, and it is unavailable anywhere else. Emit the summed dropped
count plus the names of any scopes with a non-zero value, and leave the full text in the body.
Do **not** emit a per-destination attribute for every scope.

**Group 3 — correctly left as a generic record.** Three fixed strings with no variable content and
no operational question they answer that `config`/`configd.py` do not already answer better (see
the config-apply chain issue filed alongside this one). Structuring them would add a vocabulary
entry per string for zero query value.

**Group 4 — worth structuring.** `Child program exited, restarting` with a non-zero `status` is a
real failure of an OPNsense event handler (`configctl … system event config_changed`), and the
6 captured occurrences all carry `status='256'` — a consistent non-zero exit that nothing currently
surfaces. `Error reading data` names the failing `fd`, which correlates directly with Group 1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Parser registered for `syslog-ng` in `internal/logship/syslog/`
- [x] Group 1 emits `syslogng.event` from a closed vocabulary
      (`connection_established`, `connection_closed`, `connection_broken`, `eof`), plus
      `syslogng.fd`, and `dst.ip` / `dst.port` parsed out of the `AF_INET(...)` server field, and
      `syslogng.time_reopen_seconds` where present
- [x] Group 4 emits `syslogng.event` = `child_exited` with `syslogng.cmdline` and
      `syslogng.exit_status`, and `read_error` with `syslogng.fd` and `syslogng.error`
- [x] Group 2 emits `syslogng.event` = `statistics` with `syslogng.dropped_total` and
      `syslogng.truncated_total` only — **no per-destination attribute fan-out**, and a test that
      pins this (a stats line with many scopes must not produce more than a fixed number of
      attributes)
- [x] Group 3 explicitly falls through to a generic record, with the reason in a code comment
- [x] Table-driven tests over the verbatim lines above; the Group 2 fixture uses the full captured
      ~4 KB line, not a trimmed one, so the no-fan-out assertion is meaningful
- [x] `make test` / `make docs` green

comments.body:
Landed in `26ce3c59` (pushed to `main`).

Connection lifecycle, error and statistics shapes structured; configuration-reload lines left generic, as the split verdict directed.

The statistics line is parsed **narrowly on purpose** — only `syslogng.dropped_total` and `syslogng.truncated_total`, summed across scopes. That line carries dozens of per-destination counters, and fanning them out would turn one log record into a metrics scrape with a cardinality we never chose. `TestSyslogNGGroup2StatisticsNoFanOut` counts emitted `syslogng.*` attributes against the real ~5.5 kB captured line, so a future fan-out fails loudly.

Deviation worth flagging: the issue body floated also emitting the names of non-zero scopes, but the acceptance checklist said those two totals "only". I followed the checklist — a per-scope name is exactly the fan-out the verdict argues against. Say the word if you wanted the body reading instead.

The summation test case is marked **synthetic** with its reason: every dropped/truncated value on a healthy box is 0, so a captured line cannot distinguish "summed correctly" from "defaulted to zero".

`registry.go` needed no change — `syslog-ng` was already mapped to `logging`.

Gate green on the committed tree: `make test` 28 packages ok / 0 failures, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `make docs-check` and `make grafana-check` both exit 0. Shared seams (`registry.go` subsystem attribution, `derive.go` family decisions, the `docs/syslog-receiver.md` parser table) landed together in `0ad3d468` rather than being contended six ways.
