body:
## What

The 2026-07-31T14:10Z live-canary run (#607 release-vm, #608 nightly) surfaced ~36 paths needing an exemption-ledger verdict. All of them are consequences of **#589's second-stage descent** reaching subtrees that were structurally invisible, not upstream movement. The one genuine bug in that run (`nginxVts` `overCounts`) is already fixed as #609; this issue owns the ledger remainder.

Triaged with preliminary verdicts on #607 / #608. Each still needs its own upstream-source read before it lands, per the repo's canary-triage rules — that is why this is an issue rather than a same-session edit.

## The four batches

| batch | paths | verdict | target |
|---|---|---|---|
| `smartInfo` `output.endurance_used`, `output.spare_available` | 2 | box-state → `missingOK` | both |
| `quaggaOspfOverview` `response.areas.*` | 17 | opportunity → `knownExtraPaths` | both |
| `unboundBlocklistPolicies` `*` | 10 | opportunity → `knownExtraPaths` | both |
| `healthCheck` `subsystems.*` | 7 | opportunity → `knownExtraPaths` | nightly only |

## The one decision that is not mechanical

`smartInfo`'s two wear fields must be **profile-scoped to `nightly` + `release-vm`**, not base-scoped. They are smartctl's own vendor-regex-derived wear percentages, so a virtual disk cannot emit them — but **prod has real hardware and may well report them**, and a base-scoped `missingOK` would blind the only profile that can verify a field backing an exported metric (#577). Needs a live read of prod's `smartInfo` before the scope is written.

Same two-list nuance as `SchemaExemption.Profiles` elsewhere; see #611 for the parallel gap on the coverage ledger, which has no profile scoping at all.

## Two stale ledger claims to correct in the same pass

1. **`smartInfo`'s note is false.** It asserts "the nightly virtio testbed cannot produce ANY smartInfo data at all (`api/smart/service/list` 404s on virtio disks)". `smartInfo` is not among the absent 404s on either target in this run — it returned data on both. Documentation rot of the class #588 was filed for.
2. **`quaggaOspfOverview`'s note predates the descent** and should record that `areas` was invisible until #589 rather than reading as though the subtree were new upstream data.

## Non-goals

Not a bulk reclassification. `#591` finding 6 already established that the four `opnsense_frr_ospf_area_*` counters are modelled; the 17 `areas.*` keys are the remainder and each needs checking against `ospfd/ospf_vty.c` individually — the `lsa*{Number,Checksum}` pairs in particular are per-LSA-type counts that may be genuine metric candidates rather than identity fields.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every one of the ~36 paths carries a verdict verified against the producing source, not bucketed by name
- [ ] `smartInfo`'s two entries profile-scoped, after a live prod read decides whether prod can clear them
- [ ] `smartInfo`'s false virtio claim corrected
- [ ] `quaggaOspfOverview`'s note records the #589 visibility change
- [ ] Any `areas.*` key that is a genuine metric candidate called out as an opportunity rather than silently exempted
- [ ] `make schemas` clean; goldens stay structure-only
- [x] A clean run on both testbed targets, closing #607 and #608

comments.body:
## Batch 1's verdict is REFUTED by a live prod read. It is not box state — it is a P0 decode bug, filed as #615.

Read prod's `smartInfo` before writing the profile scope, as this issue's "one decision that is not mechanical" required. The answer inverts the verdict.

Prod **has** a real disk and **does** serve both fields — as **objects**:

```
smartList (POST) -> {"devices":["ada0"]}
smartInfo output.endurance_used   -> {"current_percent": 84}
smartInfo output.spare_available  -> {"current_percent": 100, "threshold_percent": 10}
output.rotation_rate              -> 0
```

The struct models them as `*float64` (`opnsense/smart.go:48-49`). So this was never "absent because a virtual disk cannot report SSD endurance" — on the profile that matters it is a **type mismodelling**, the same class as #609. A `missingOK` scoped to `nightly` + `release-vm` would have been technically true and completely beside the point: it would have left a live decode failure on the only profile that exercises the endpoint, and this issue would have closed reporting the ledger tidy.

Blast radius, because it is much worse than the two fields: `unmarshalBody` turns the decode failure into an `APICallError`, and `FetchSMART` handles a failed per-device info call by appending the device with **nothing but its name** (`smart.go:226-233`). Every per-device SMART metric on prod is gone — health, temperature, power-on hours, the whole ATA attribute table, rotation rate, wear. `opnsense_smart_devices_total` is the only `opnsense_smart_*` series on the live stack, and `collector_success{collector="smart"}` is **1**.

Filed as **#615** (P0). **Batch 1 is removed from this issue's scope** — nothing to exempt, there is a bug to fix.

### Also confirmed for the note correction in this issue's scope

`smartInfo`'s claim that "the nightly virtio testbed cannot produce ANY smartInfo data at all (`api/smart/service/list` 404s on virtio disks)" is false in a **second** way beyond the one this issue already identified. The live behaviour is neither a 404 nor data: `smartList` requires **POST** (a GET returns `{"message":"Unable to run list action"}` — `smart.go:199-203` documents this), and on a virtio box it POSTs 200 with no devices, so `resolveParam` returns `""` and the canary **skips `smartInfo` entirely** on both CI targets (`cmd/apidrift/probe.go:264-280`). That is why no gate has ever seen this payload.

### A new ledger item this issue should absorb

The live prod run surfaced 6 paths needing a verdict that were not in this issue's four batches:

**`ipsecSad` `rows[].allocated`, `allocated_hard`, `allocated_soft`, `bytes_current`, `bytes_hard`, `bytes_soft`** — reported as **Missing** (not Unverified), because prod's `sad/search` returns **one** row and those six keys are absent from it. Prod configures no phase 1 and no policy (`ipsecPhase1` and `ipsecSpd` both return zero rows), so the row is an orphan SA with `ikeid`/`phase1desc`/`phase2desc`/`satype`/`spi` all null. **Needs an upstream-source read**: are those six counters emitted only for a fully-resolved SA? This is the last thing standing between prod and a clean run, alongside #615 — see #531.

Note this also refutes #611's premise that "prod has no IPsec SA".

### Remaining scope, unchanged

Batches 2–4 (`quaggaOspfOverview` `response.areas.*` ×17, `unboundBlocklistPolicies` ×10, `healthCheck` `subsystems.*` ×7, nightly only) still need their per-path upstream-source reads. Untouched so far.

- [x] ~~`smartInfo`'s two entries profile-scoped after a live prod read~~ → **refuted; #615**
- [x] `smartInfo`'s false virtio claim characterised (POST-only + canary-skips, not a 404)
- [ ] The note text itself corrected in the ledger
- [ ] `quaggaOspfOverview`'s note records the #589 visibility change
- [ ] Batches 2–4: ~34 paths, each against its producing source
- [ ] NEW: `ipsecSad`'s six absent counters

## The `ipsecSad` six: verdict is **box-state**, but the exemption must NOT be written — the finding is a canary defect

Source-read plus a live prod read. The premise carried into this issue (and into #531 and my own brief) is wrong in a way that changes the answer.

### Prod does not have an orphan SA. Prod has no SA at all

The single row prod's `sad/search` returns is a **parse artifact of the empty case**, not an unresolved SA:

```json
{"src":"No","dst":"SAD","nat":"ntries","satype":null,"spi":null,
 "ikeid":null,"phase1desc":null,"phase2desc":null,
 "id":"<hash-3>"}
```

`setkey -D` on a box with no SAs prints the literal line `No SAD entries.`, and `list_sad.py` parses it as a record: `keyparts[0]` → `src="No"`, `keyparts[1]` → `dst="SAD"`. The `nat="ntries"` is upstream's own bug showing — the guard is `if len(keyparts) > 2 and keyparts[2].find("[")`, and `str.find` returns **-1** when the substring is absent, which is truthy in Python, so `nat = keyparts[2][1:-1]` slices `entries.` into `ntries` unconditionally.

**We already know this.** `opnsense/ipsec.go:327-330` documents the placeholder verbatim, `nat="ntries"` and all, and `FetchIPsecSAD` discards the row. So the exporter has been correct about this the whole time.

That corrects three things at once:

1. **"prod has no IPsec SA" (#611's premise) was RIGHT, and the refutation of it was wrong.** Prod really has none. My brief carried the refutation as settled fact — it is not.
2. **There is no "orphan SA with everything null".** The nulls are `SadController.php`'s own `else` branch stamping `ikeid`/`phase1desc`/`phase2desc` to null when the reqid does not resolve (searchAction), applied to a row that was never an SA.
3. **The six counters are absent because there is no SA to count**, not because they are "emitted only for a fully-resolved SA". Source confirms they are unconditional on resolution: `list_sad.py` derives `bytes_current/hard/soft` from the `\tcurrent:` line of `setkey -D` and `allocated/allocated_hard/allocated_soft` from the `\tallocated:` line, and `SadController.php` merges **only** `ikeid`/`phase1desc`/`phase2desc` on top. Phase 1 and policy state cannot suppress them.

### Why the exemption must not be written

These six are **modelled and consumed**: #578 exports them as `opnsense_ipsec_sa_bytes_*` and `_allocated_*`, and the `ipsecSad` ledger note already records that. This repo's own triage rule says an exemption on a field backing an exported metric blinds the canary to real drift and that fixing the testbed is preferred. A `missingOK` here would permanently blind six consumed fields on the strength of a row we discard.

**The defect is canary-side.** `cmd/apidrift` is validating key presence against a synthetic row that `FetchIPsecSAD` throws away, so it is reporting "Missing" for fields on a record that never reaches a struct. The fix is for the probe to recognise the same placeholder the client already recognises (`src=="No" && dst=="SAD"`, or more robustly a row with a null `spi`) and treat `ipsecSad` as **no rows** rather than one row with 6 missing keys. Then the finding disappears on prod *and* on both testbeds, none of which run IPsec either — and the day a real SA appears, the six are checked properly instead of being exempted forever.

Recommended, in preference order:

1. Teach the probe to skip the placeholder row (small, fixes every profile at once, keeps the six fields covered).
2. Failing that, configure one IPsec SA on a testbed so the path is genuinely exercised — the triage rule's preferred remedy.
3. Do **not** write `missingOK` for these six.

Filing (1) separately rather than folding it into this ledger issue, since it is a code fix to `cmd/apidrift` and not a ledger verdict.

### Also worth recording: `list_sad.py` crashes when it cannot read the SAD

Running it as a non-root user on prod:

```
File "/usr/local/opnsense/scripts/ipsec/list_sad.py", line 57, in <module>
    sad_entry["src"] = keyparts[0]
IndexError: list index out of range
```

`setkey -D` fails with `pfkey_open: Operation not permitted`, the payload is empty, and the section loop still manufactures one empty section. Harmless in production (configd runs it as root) and **not our bug** — recorded only so the next person who runs it by hand does not read the traceback as a box fault.

### Scope of this issue after this comment

- [x] ~~NEW: `ipsecSad`'s six absent counters~~ → **box-state, no exemption; canary-side fix instead** (see above)
- [ ] The `smartInfo` note text corrected in the ledger
- [ ] `quaggaOspfOverview`'s note records the #589 visibility change
- [ ] Batches 2–4: ~34 paths, each against its producing source — **still untouched**

## All four batches landed. 34 of 34 paths cleared on both targets; one endpoint left, and it is not this issue's

Commits: `540f3ac2` (smartInfo note), `36b0c79f` (batch 3), `957cc1e8` (batch 4), `d0297126` (batch 2), `16fbfd17` (profile scoping + two corrections).

Live-canary run at 18:48Z, both targets: **173 of 175 endpoints clean, 0 breaking type drift, 0 unexpected top-level keys, 0 unexpected nested keys, 1 endpoint with missing paths.** The 18:41Z run before the last commit had 2. Every one of batches 2, 3 and 4 is gone.

| batch | paths | verdict as landed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quaggaOspfOverview` `response.areas.*` | 17 | 8 opportunity + 9 not-a-metric — **the name-bucketing trap was real** |
| `unboundBlocklistPolicies` `*` | 10 | config; 2 called out as genuine candidates |
| `healthCheck` `subsystems.*` | 7 | identity/presentation; `timestamp` called out as the one opportunity |
| `smartInfo` wear fields | 2 | box-state, **profile-scoped away from prod** |
| `ipsecSad` counters (new) | 6 | box-state, folded into the existing prod-only placeholder exemption |

### What the per-path reads actually changed

The instruction not to bucket by name earned its keep twice.

**`lsa*Number` vs `lsa*Checksum` are different classes.** They read as one family. `ospf_vty.c:3167-3251` shows the Number keys are `ospf_lsdb_count()` per LSA type — the decomposition of the `lsaNumber` total we already export, a closed set of seven, all moving quantities, and the strongest metric candidates in the whole issue. The matching Checksum keys are `ospf_lsdb_checksum()`, a Fletcher sum used to detect LSDB divergence between routers — it moves arbitrarily on any LSA change, so it is churn as a gauge and unbounded as a label. Bucketing by prefix would have written off eight good candidates or adopted nine bad ones.

**`areaIfTotalCounter`** is `listcount(area->oiflist)`, the partner of the `areaIfActiveCounter` we model. The pair gives an area's active/total ratio; neither half gives it alone.

**`unboundBlocklistPolicies`** turned out to need no source archaeology at all: `getPoliciesAction()` is a bare `$this->mdl->dnsbl->blocklist->getNodeContent()`, so the response **is** the model node and `Unbound.xml` is authoritative for all ten. Eight are unbounded config (feed selections, CSV URL lists, networks, free-text description). `nxdomain` (BooleanField) and `cache_ttl` (IntegerField, default 72000) are bounded and are the same shape as the `enabled` field we already model — recorded with a prune trigger rather than written off.

**`healthCheck subsystems.*`** — `SystemStatus::collectStatus()` does `if ($obj->getStatus() == SystemStatusCode::OK) { continue; }`. A subsystem is emitted **only while it is not OK**, so an all-healthy box serves an empty map by construction. That is a far crisper statement of the nightly-only asymmetry than the ledger's previous "it reappears the moment any subsystem reports", and it also explains why `scope` never appears in a finding despite being in the record — `statusAction()` unsets it. `age` is a *localised human string* ("5 minutes ago") built from `timestamp` via gettext; `timestamp` is the real opportunity. One caveat worth knowing: `statusAction()` ACL-filters this map, so a missing subsystem can be a **credential** property, not just a healthy box.

### Two corrections to this issue's own record

1. **The `ipsecSad` six are not "the last thing standing between prod and a clean run" in the way the earlier comment framed them, and my own reading of them was also wrong.** There is no orphan SA. Prod has **no IPsec SA at all** — the single row is `setkey -D`'s literal `No SAD entries.` line parsed as a record, which `opnsense/ipsec.go:327-330` already documents and `FetchIPsecSAD` already discards. #611's "prod has no IPsec SA" premise was **right**; the refutation of it was wrong. The six join the five paths already exempted prod-only for that exact row.
2. **The `smartInfo` "skipped entirely on both CI targets" claim — which I wrote into the ledger in `540f3ac2` — is wrong**, and the canary refuted it within the hour: `0 skipped (no live parameter)`, with findings returned for `smartInfo` on both. The testbeds do probe it. What they cannot produce is a *value*, because a virtio disk has none of the vendor attributes smartctl regex-matches. Corrected in `16fbfd17`, with the exemption scoped to `nightly` + `release-vm` so prod keeps enforcing both — which is what #613's batch 1 argued for originally, and it was right for a reason nobody had yet found.

### Remaining, and it is not this issue's scope

`nginxVts` `overCounts` ×9 (`serverZones.*.overCounts.responseMsecCounter`, `upstreamZones.*[].overCounts.{bypass,expired,hit,miss,revalidated,scarce,stale,updating}`) is the only endpoint still reporting. This issue's body explicitly scoped `nginxVts` out ("already fixed as #609; this issue owns the ledger remainder"), and these are a **new** remainder created by #609's fix rather than part of the original ~36. Worth flagging for whoever picks it up: the split looks structural — the cache-state counters appear under `upstreamZones` where upstreams have no cache — so this may be one `overCounts` struct being shared across two zone types that do not carry the same keys. **That is a hypothesis from the finding's shape, not a source read**, and #609's history (a fixture that agreed with the wrong code, shipping a total nginx metric outage) is the reason it must be read against nginx-module-vts before anything is exempted.

- [x] Every one of the ~36 paths carries a verdict verified against the producing source
- [x] `smartInfo` entries profile-scoped after a live prod read
- [x] `smartInfo`'s false virtio claim corrected (twice — the correction was itself wrong once)
- [x] `quaggaOspfOverview`'s note records the #589 visibility change
- [x] `areas.*` metric candidates called out as opportunities rather than silently exempted
- [x] `make schemas` clean; goldens structure-only
- [ ] A clean run on both testbed targets — **blocked only on the `nginxVts` remainder above**, which needs its own source read

## The `nginxVts` remainder is resolved, and your hypothesis was half right

> the split looks structural — the cache-state counters appear under `upstreamZones` where upstreams have no cache — so this may be one `overCounts` struct being shared across two zone types that do not carry the same keys. **That is a hypothesis from the finding's shape, not a source read**

**The structural half is right. The "possible bug in #609's shipped fix" half is refuted.**

Read against `ngx_http_vhost_traffic_status_display_json.h` on `vozlt/nginx-module-vts` master before touching anything, as this issue's rules require:

| zone kind | macro | overCounts keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| server | `FMT_SERVER_END` | common + `requestMsecCounter` + the eight cache keys (NGX_HTTP_CACHE builds only). **Never** `responseMsecCounter` |
| upstream | `FMT_UPSTREAM` | common + `requestMsecCounter` + `responseMsecCounter`. **Never** a cache key |
| cache | `FMT_CACHE` | `inBytes`/`outBytes` + the eight cache keys only |

So the nine paths are exactly what one union struct standing in for two different shapes produces — not upstream drift, not box state.

**#609 is not buggy.** Absent keys decode to 0 and contribute 0 to `total()`, which is the correct reading: a counter that cannot exist has not wrapped. And the fixtures already carried each kind's real key set, so nothing was agreeing with wrong code this time.

**Fixed by splitting the model, not by exempting** (`db05cf5d`): `nginxVtsOverCountsServer` and `nginxVtsOverCountsUpstream` are now distinct types, so each golden schema states its zone kind's real key set and the canary keeps **enforcing** all of them. Nine consumed paths stay checked instead of being permanently blinded — which is what this repo's own triage rule asks for and what a `missingOK` here would have cost.

### The run

Live-canary at 21:0xZ, both targets: **0 breaking type drift, 0 missing paths, 0 unexpected nested keys.** #607 and #608 both closed on it.

One new finding appeared and was ledgered in the same pass (`731ddf86`): #603's new `firewallStates` endpoint models only the pre-NAT 5-tuple, the direction and `route-to`, so its other sixteen row keys went to `knownExtraPaths` with a per-key reason rather than a bucket note.

### Same defect class, found next door

`smartInfo` had the identical shape: one `smartWearPercent` type standing in for two smartctl wrappers, which put a `threshold_percent` into `endurance_used`'s golden schema that no emitter can produce. Verified against smartmontools master — `threshold_percent` is written for `spare_available` only (`nvmeprint.cpp:505` unconditionally, `ataprint.cpp:1208` when `0 < threshold < 50`); all three `endurance_used` sites write `current_percent` and nothing else. Split the same way in `25838278`. That was the last finding standing between prod and a clean run, and **#531 closed itself on the next prod canary**.

### Acceptance

- [x] A clean run on both testbed targets, closing #607 and #608

All four batches landed, the nginxVts remainder resolved by splitting the model, and the live-canary run at 21:0xZ came back clean on both targets — #607 and #608 closed on it. Every acceptance box is ticked.

title: canary: exemption-ledger verdicts for the ~36 paths #589's descent newly exposed

body:
## What

<host-1>'s prod canary (`/usr/local/bin/opnsense-prod-canary.sh`, driven by `opnsense-prod-canary.timer`, `OnCalendar=*-*-* 07:20:00 UTC`) **files and comments but never closes.** Verified on the box 2026-07-31: the script's only `gh` calls are `issue list`, `issue create` and `issue comment`. There is no `issue close`.

The GitHub workflow has the missing half — `Close drift issue when clean` (`.github/workflows/live-canary.yml:248-266`) — but that step exists only in the CI job and only ever touches its own target's title, so the `prod` issue is outside its reach.

## Why it matters

A prod drift that is later fixed leaves its issue open forever. Worse, the asymmetry actively misleads triage: #531's triage comment concluded *"closing it by hand achieves nothing… it closes itself on the next clean run"*, reasoning by analogy from the CI job. Both halves are wrong for prod — hand-closing is the **only** mechanism that ever closes it, and a clean prod run leaves it open. That wrong belief is why #531 sat open being described as self-closing.

Note hand-closing only buys one day: dedupe is on open-issue title, so the next 07:20 UTC run files a fresh duplicate.

## Fix

Port the workflow's close-on-clean logic into the script: when the report has no `### 🟡` section, comment "clean" on the matching open `api-drift` issue titled `OPNsense live-box canary drift - prod` and close it. Same title-scoped dedupe the create path already uses, so it can never touch another target's issue.

Note this is gated in practice by #611: until the coverage ledger has per-profile scoping, a prod run always emits a `🟡` section, so a close step would never fire. Both are needed; this one is the smaller half.

## Acceptance

- [ ] <host-1>'s script closes its own issue on a clean run, title-scoped to `- prod`
- [ ] It can never close another target's issue (assert the title match, mirroring `live-canary.yml:259-263`)
- [ ] The script's clean-run early-exit path is exercised at least once against a real clean report
- [ ] Wherever this script is version-controlled, the change lands there rather than only on the box
title: canary: <host-1>'s prod canary never closes its issue — no close-on-clean step exists

## What

The live-box canary's **coverage ledger has no per-profile scoping**, so a path that is legitimately absent on one probe target is reported as coverage debt on all three. `SchemaExemption` already has `Profiles` (`cmd/apidrift/main.go:79`); `CoveragePath` has no equivalent.

The consequence is #531: the prod canary has reported 15 required-coverage paths since 2026-07-31 that **can never clear**, because the production firewall legitimately has no CARP VIP, no Kea DHCPv4, no DHCPv6 PD pool and no WireGuard instance. Those same paths verify correctly on both testbeds (#607 and #608 have no required-coverage section at all).

## Why an exemption is not the workaround

Checked in code, not inferred. `missingOK` is consulted only in the `absentFinal > 0 && !unverifiable` branch and suppresses `ValidationResult.Missing` (`opnsense/schema_validate.go:544`). An **empty parent array** — which is what prod returns for all four endpoints — files its children under `ValidationResult.Unverified` (`:547-549`) with no `missingOK` check, and the coverage ledger reads that. So the standing "prefer fixing the testbed over exempting a metric-backing field" rule is not a live choice here: there is no exemption to reach for.

The only existing knobs are `stateOptional` and `opaque`, and both are base-scoped — using either would blind **all three** profiles on paths the two testbeds currently verify correctly. That is strictly worse than the warning.

## Proposal

Mirror `SchemaExemption.Profiles` on `CoveragePath`: an optional per-profile override letting a path be `required` under `nightly`/`release-vm` and `stateOptional` under `prod`, each override carrying a reason and a prune trigger the same way the exemption ledger does.

With it, the prod report has no `🟡` section, <host-1>'s script exits before touching GitHub, and #531 can close and stay closed — without weakening what the testbed runs assert.

## Why this is getting worse, not better

#599 moved 67 paths from informational into `required` on 2026-07-31, **after** #531's current report was generated. Prod additionally has no OpenVPN instance, no IPsec SA, no shaper pipe, no Suricata and no HA peer (all probed live 2026-07-31), so the next prod run's required-coverage list **grows**. Every added path is prod box state, not drift.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `CoveragePath` gains per-profile scoping mirroring `SchemaExemption.Profiles`
- [ ] A per-profile override requires a reason and a prune trigger, enforced the way the exemption ledger's are
- [ ] The four prod-absent endpoint groups (`carpStatus`, `keaLeases4`, `keaPdPools6`, `wireguardClients`) scoped `stateOptional` under `prod` only
- [ ] A guard that a per-profile override cannot silently widen to another profile
- [ ] Prod run produces no `🟡` section; testbed runs still assert every one of these paths
- [ ] #531 closed by the resulting clean prod run
title: canary: coverage ledger needs per-profile scoping — prod reports 15 permanently-unclearable required paths

## Summary

`opnsense_log_events_netmap_ring_full_events_total` has **no series at all** on the m7kni prod stack, while the firewall kernel emitted **98** `netmap_transmit ... full` lines over a 2d19h uptime and **those raw lines are reaching Loki**. The syslog lane ships them; the log-events parser does not match them. The one metric whose entire purpose is to make Zenarmor's datapath drops visible is silent exactly when the condition is live.

Found while investigating why the prod box was running Zenarmor in netmap **emulated** mode (`dev.netmap.admode=2`), which pins `dev.netmap.generic_rings=1` — a single 1024-slot ring in front of a 6-queue X710. The ring-full drops were the cost of that, and this metric would have surfaced it years ago.

## Evidence

Kernel side, `ssh opnsense`, read-only:

```
# dmesg | grep -c netmap_transmit
98

[232659] 743.279886 [4335] netmap_transmit           ixl0 full hwcur 839 hwtail 842 qlen 1020
```

The lines are in Loki, under the syslog lane with `opnsense_subsystem="kernel"`:

```
{service_name="opnsense-exporter"} |= "netmap_transmit"
-> stream: {opnsense_source="syslog", opnsense_subsystem="kernel",
            service_instance_id="opnsense", service_name="opnsense-exporter"}
   line:   "[232659] 743.279886 [4335] netmap_transmit           ixl0 full hwcur 839 hwtail 842 qlen 1020"
```

The metric is absent:

```
opnsense_log_events_netmap_ring_full_events_total   -> []
count(group by (__name__) ({__name__=~"opnsense_log_events_.*"}))  -> 15
```

So the collector is running and publishing 15 other families in the same subsystem; this one has never been incremented for any `device`.

## Why this is worse than a normal missing metric

The metric's own help text (`internal/collector/logevents.go:1079`) already warns that it under-reports, because `netmap_transmit()` logs through `nm_prlim(2, ...)` and flat-tops at 2 lines/sec:

> "Absence of growth means no report, NOT no drops."

Right now it is a step beyond that: the series does not exist, so a dashboard or alert reading it sees neither growth nor a zero — it sees nothing, which renders as "no data" and is indistinguishable from a healthy box. The help text also records that this was once **live-corroborated** ("14 kernel reports since boot against an API-reported dropped-packets of 0"), so either the parser regressed or the corroboration was done by reading the box rather than by observing the metric.

## Likely cause (needs confirming, not yet diagnosed)

The line's shape is unusual for this parser registry: no program token in the message body, a bracketed kernel sequence counter, a bracketed source-line number, then the text. The syslog envelope resolves `opnsense_subsystem="kernel"` but the parser may be keyed on a program name that a kernel message never carries. Start at the `netmap` matcher in `internal/logship/syslog/` and check it against the verbatim line above, including the **multiple runs of spaces** between `netmap_transmit` and `ixl0` — a single-space or `\s` pattern that does not allow a run will fail on every real line.

Note the line arrives **duplicated** (identical content, consecutive `sequenceId="1"` and `"2"`), which is the kernel's own double-log, not a shipping bug. Whatever counts these should decide deliberately whether that is one event or two — the help text says the counter measures "intervals in which the kernel reported", which argues for de-duplicating within a scrape interval.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirm the cause by feeding the verbatim prod line through the parser in a test — it must fail before the fix and pass after
- [ ] `opnsense_log_events_netmap_ring_full_events_total{device="ixl0"}` accumulates on the prod box within one scrape of a kernel report
- [ ] A table-driven test case pins the exact prod line, whitespace runs included, derived from the capture above rather than hand-written
- [ ] Decide and document whether the kernel's duplicate emission counts once or twice, and test that decision
- [ ] Re-verify on prod after deploy: `dmesg | grep -c netmap_transmit` and the counter move together
- [ ] Full gate green (`make test lint docs-check grafana-check`)

## Context worth keeping

The prod box has since been switched to native netmap (`dev.netmap.admode=0`), and `iflib_netmap_config txr 6 rxr 6 txd 1024 rxd 1024` confirms native attach with 6 ring pairs instead of the single generic ring. If the ring-full condition stops occurring there, this metric becomes hard to verify against live data — so build the test from the captured line above rather than waiting to observe it again.

## Related

- #602 — the flow-divergence alert whose investigation surfaced this

## Premise refuted: the parser matches, the metric increments, and it has 952 samples on the live stack

Checked every link in the chain against the live stack and the code rather than reasoning from the instant query. The parser is not broken and never was. The `[]` in this issue's evidence is an artefact of **when** the query ran, not of what the parser does.

### 1. The parser matches — proved twice, independently

**Loki already carries the structured output.** The very line this issue quotes arrives with the netmap attributes fully populated as structured metadata:

```
line: "[232659] 743.279886 [4335] netmap_transmit           ixl0 full hwcur 839 hwtail 842 qlen 1020"
structuredMetadata:
  netmap_event:   "ring_full"
  netmap_device:  "ixl0"
  netmap_hwcur:   "839"
  netmap_hwtail:  "842"
  netmap_qlen:    "1020"
  program:        "kernel"
```

`netmap_event="ring_full"` is set **only** by `parseNetmap` after `reNetmapRingFull` matched (`internal/logship/syslog/kernel.go:127-138`). Its presence on the shipped record is proof of the match.

**The run of spaces was already handled.** The suspected cause — "a single-space or `\s` pattern that does not allow a run will fail on every real line" — was fixed when the grammar was written. The regex is `netmap_transmit +(...)`, and `kernel.go:51-57` says so in capitals: *"THE RUN OF SPACES AFTER THE FUNCTION NAME IS REAL and is ` +`, not ` `"*. Four verbatim captured lines with the same padding have been in `TestNetmapCapturedRingFullLines` since #536, including one with a space-padded source-line field (`[ 902]`).

### 2. The metric increments, and always has

```
count_over_time(opnsense_log_events_netmap_ring_full_events_total[7d])  -> 952   {device="ixl0"}
max_over_time(opnsense_log_events_netmap_ring_full_events_total[30d])   -> 2     {device="ixl0"}
```

952 samples over 7 days. The series exists, is labelled `device="ixl0"` as designed, and reaches 2 within a process lifetime.

### 3. Why the instant query returned `[]`

Two facts multiply:

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| <host-1> redeploys the exporter hourly (watchtower, at :00) | `process_start_time_seconds` was **233 seconds** old when I queried |
| netmap reports on this box | last one **~3.8h** before that |

A counter family with zero keys emits **no series at all** — `snap.netmap` is empty, so `Collect` never calls `MustNewConstMetric` (`internal/collector/logevents.go:1457`). So for most of any given hour there is legitimately no series, and an instant query lands in that gap far more often than not. `count(group by (__name__) ({__name__=~"opnsense_log_events_.*"})) -> 15` in the issue was measured the same way: the 15 families present were the ones that had seen an event since the last restart, not the ones that work.

Range queries see it fine. `increase(...[24h])` on a dashboard returns data.

So the "renders as no-data, indistinguishable from a healthy box" concern is real for an **instant** read of a rare event, but it is the correct semantics of a sparse counter under hourly restarts, not a parser bug — and the help text's own *"Absence of growth means no report, NOT no drops"* already says what an operator must not conclude.

### 4. The duplicate-emission question — decided: counts TWICE

The issue's framing ("identical content, consecutive `sequenceId`... the kernel's own double-log") does not survive the capture. **The two lines differ:**

```
[232659] 743.279886 [4335] netmap_transmit           ixl0 full hwcur 839 hwtail 842 qlen 1020
[232659] 743.279956 [4335] netmap_transmit           ixl0 full hwcur 839 hwtail 842 qlen 1020
                ^^^^^^ 70us apart
```

Different uptimes means two distinct `netmap_transmit()` calls, each of which found the host ring full and each of which passed `nm_prlim`'s limiter. They are not one event logged twice. `hwcur`/`hwtail`/`qlen` agree because the ring state had not moved in 70us — which is exactly what a full ring looks like.

Counting per line is also the only reading consistent with the documented ceiling. `nm_prlim(2, ...)` permits **two** lines per second, and the help text documents the counter as flat-topping at 2/s; de-duplicating per second would make the real ceiling 1/s and the documentation wrong. The value carries no severity information either way — 1 and 2 both mean "the ring was full during that second" — so halving it buys nothing and costs per-`(device, second)` state in the store.

Pinned as `TestNetmapRateLimitedPairCountsTwice`, written as the decision rather than as an observation of current behaviour.

### 5. The one real defect found

The help text contradicted itself in its first word. It opened *"**Intervals** in which the FreeBSD kernel reported..."* and then said *"THIS COUNTS OCCURRENCES"* and *"FLAT-TOPS at 2/s"* — the body is right, the opening implied the per-interval dedupe this issue then asked for. That is very likely where the dedupe idea came from. Reworded to state the unit plainly and to record why the pair is two events.

### Acceptance, as resolved

- [x] ~~Confirm the cause by feeding the verbatim prod line through the parser in a test — it must fail before the fix and pass after~~ — **it passes before**, so there is no fix. Both halves of the pair added to `TestNetmapCapturedRingFullLines` as a guard, with a comment recording that #610 asserted otherwise.
- [x] `...{device="ixl0"}` accumulates on the prod box — it does, 952 samples/7d, max 2 per process lifetime
- [x] A table-driven test case pins the exact prod line, whitespace runs included, derived from the capture
- [x] Decide and document whether the duplicate emission counts once or twice — **twice**, per emitted line; documented in the help text and pinned by a test
- [x] Re-verify on prod — the raw lines and the counter agree; the parse is visible in Loki's structured metadata on the same records
- [ ] ~~Full gate green~~ — green (below)

Nothing to fix in the parser. Closing on the guard test + the help-text correction, per the standing triage rule that a wrong premise gets said out loud on the issue and closed with a guard rather than forced into a change.

**Worth carrying forward:** an instant query against `opnsense_log_events_*` on this stack tells you what has happened *since the last hourly restart*, not what the exporter can produce. Three of this issue's four evidence lines were instant queries.

title: netmap_ring_full_events_total never increments: kernel emits the lines, Loki has them, the parser does not match

## What

`#584` modelled nginx-module-vts's `overCounts` as a **single number** (`opnsense/nginx.go:73` and `:89`, `OverCounts float64`). It is a **JSON object**. The decode therefore fails, and because `unmarshalBody` (`opnsense/client.go:816`) turns any `json.Unmarshal` error into an `APICallError`, `FetchNginxVTS` returns that error instead of data — so **every nginx VTS metric is lost on any box whose nginx serves vts output**, not merely the wrap counter.

Regression introduced today in `b0728fc` (#584). Unreleased: it is after v3.0.0 and would have shipped in the open 4.0.0 release PR #358.

## Evidence

The 2026-07-31T14:10Z live-canary run (`workflow_dispatch`, run 30637517316) failed on **both** testbed targets, reporting the same breaking type drift on each — #607 (release-vm) and #608 (nightly):

```
nginxVts serverZones.*.overCounts: expected number, live box serves object
nginxVts upstreamZones.*[].overCounts: expected number, live box serves object
```

Both targets agreeing rules out box-state. Reproduced locally against the real shape:

```
json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field
  nginxVtsServerZone.serverZones.overCounts of type float64
```

Upstream confirms the object form twice over:

- `vozlt/nginx-module-vts` README: "The `overCounts` **objects** in JSON document are mostly for 32bit system and will be increment by 1 if its value is overflowed."
- `src/ngx_http_vhost_traffic_status_display_json.h` emits it as an object with one wrap counter **per underlying counter**, plus a `maxIntegerSize` capability constant:
  - server zones: `maxIntegerSize`, `requestCounter`, `inBytes`, `outBytes`, `1xx`–`5xx`, `miss`, `bypass`, `expired`, `stale`, `updating`, `revalidated`, `hit`, `scarce`, `requestMsecCounter` (the eight cache keys only on an `NGX_HTTP_CACHE` build)
  - upstream zones: `maxIntegerSize`, `requestCounter`, `inBytes`, `outBytes`, `1xx`–`5xx`, `requestMsecCounter`, `responseMsecCounter`
  - cache zones: `maxIntegerSize`, `inBytes`, `outBytes`, `miss`, `bypass`, `expired`, `stale`, `updating`, `revalidated`, `hit`, `scarce`

So #584's premise that there is one scalar wrap counter per zone was wrong. What it read (`add_oc` incrementing `stat_X_counter_oc`) is real, but the emitter **groups those `_oc` fields into an object** rather than emitting a single total.

## Why this survived its own gate

#584 added `TestFetchNginxVTS_OverCounts` (`opnsense/nginx_test.go:138`) — but the fixture it asserts against encodes `"overCounts": 3` and `"overCounts": 7`, a shape upstream cannot produce. That is the failure mode CLAUDE.md's canary-triage rules already name: *"A fixture must never encode a shape upstream cannot produce."* A hand-written fixture derived from the issue's own wrong premise passed, and only a live payload caught it.

## Fix

The exported metrics do not change. `server_zone_counter_wraps_total` / `upstream_server_counter_wraps_total` are already described as *"count of times **one of** this server zone's own vts counters (requests/bytes/response-code/request-time) has been detected to wrap"* (`internal/collector/nginx.go:139`), which is exactly the sum across the object's wrap sub-counters. So:

1. Model `overCounts` as a struct carrying every sub-key, so the canary sees no unexpected nested keys and the golden schema records the real shape. `maxIntegerSize` is `2^64-1` — it overflows `int64`, so it takes `flexString`, not `flexInt`.
2. Define `CounterWraps` as the sum of the wrap sub-counters, excluding `maxIntegerSize` (a capability constant, not a wrap count).
3. Replace the impossible fixture with the real emitter shape.

Rejected: adding a `counter` label naming the wrapped field. It is more faithful but multiplies series ~17× per zone for values that are permanently 0 on any 64-bit box (`maxIntegerSize` = 2^64-1), and the operational question — did anything wrap in this zone — is answered exactly by the sum. Recorded here so the next reader does not re-derive it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `overCounts` modelled as an object for server zones and upstream zones, with every sub-key present
- [ ] Failing test written first against the real emitter shape, watched fail for the unmarshal error
- [ ] `TestFetchNginxVTS_OverCounts`'s impossible `"overCounts": 3` fixture replaced with the upstream shape
- [ ] A guard that a vts payload carrying the object form decodes without error and still yields the zone's other counters
- [ ] `make schemas` regenerated; goldens stay structure-only
- [ ] No metric name, label or dashboard change; catalogue count unchanged
title: fix(nginx): overCounts is an object, not a number — #584's model breaks the whole nginxVts decode

## Triage — one real bug (ours, fixed), four ledger batches. Zero upstream drift.

Run [30637517316](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/actions/runs/30637517316), dispatched by hand as the acceptance test for **#589** (second-stage descent through 19 `json.RawMessage` envelope endpoints) and **#599** (67 paths moved into `required`). Both targets failed. That was the expected outcome and it earned its keep on the first run.

The five verdicts, in the order the report lists them.

---

### 1. `nginxVts` `*.overCounts` — **not drift. Our bug, shipped today.** → #609, fixed.

`serverZones.*.overCounts` and `upstreamZones.*[].overCounts` are **objects**; #584 modelled them as `float64` (`opnsense/nginx.go:73`, `:89`). Both targets report it identically, which rules out box-state.

The blast radius is larger than the field. `unmarshalBody` turns any `json.Unmarshal` failure into an `APICallError` (`opnsense/client.go:816`), so `FetchNginxVTS` returned **nothing** — every nginx VTS metric lost, not just the wrap counter. Reproduced locally:

```
json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field
  nginxVtsServerZone.serverZones.overCounts of type float64
```

Upstream confirms the shape twice. The vts README: *"The `overCounts` **objects** in JSON document are mostly for 32bit system"*. And `src/ngx_http_vhost_traffic_status_display_json.h` emits one wrap counter **per underlying counter** plus a `maxIntegerSize` constant — server zones get `requestCounter`, `inBytes`, `outBytes`, `1xx`–`5xx`, the eight cache keys on an `NGX_HTTP_CACHE` build, and `requestMsecCounter`; upstream zones get `responseMsecCounter` instead of the cache keys.

So #584 read the `add_oc` macro correctly and missed that the emitter **groups** those `_oc` fields into an object rather than totalling them.

**Why it passed CI.** `TestFetchNginxVTS_OverCounts` asserted against `"overCounts": 3` — a shape upstream cannot produce. A second copy of the same impossible fixture sat in `internal/collector/nginx_test.go`. This is exactly the rule already written down in CLAUDE.md: *a fixture must never encode a shape upstream cannot produce*. A hand-written fixture derived from the issue's own wrong premise agreed with the wrong code, and only a live payload disagreed.

Fixed with no metric, label, dashboard or catalogue change — the shipped description already reads "count of times **one of** this server zone's own vts counters … has been detected to wrap", which is precisely the sum across the object's sub-counters. A per-sub-counter `counter` label was considered and rejected: ~17× the series per zone for values permanently 0 on any 64-bit box. Reasoning is in the code so it is not re-derived.

### 2. `smartInfo` `output.endurance_used` / `output.spare_available` — verdict **box-state**.

Both are smartctl's own *derived* wear percentages, computed by regex-matching **vendor-specific** attribute names (the `SSD_Life_Left`/`Wear_Leveling` and `Reallocated_Sector_Count`/`Spare_Blocks` families). The exemptions ledger already describes them that way. A drive whose vendor attributes smartctl cannot match emits neither key — absent, not renamed or removed.

Both back exported metrics from #577, so the standing rule prefers fixing the testbed. That is not possible here: you cannot make a virtual disk report SSD endurance. A `missingOK` is the only option, and it should be **profile-scoped to `nightly` + `release-vm`** rather than base-scoped, because prod has real hardware and may well report these — base-scoping would blind the one profile that can actually verify them. Needs a live prod read before the scope is fixed.

**A stale ledger claim found while triaging this.** The `smartInfo` note asserts *"the nightly virtio testbed cannot produce ANY smartInfo data at all (`api/smart/service/list` 404s on virtio disks)"*. That is now false: `smartInfo` is **not** among the absent 404s on either target in this run (release-vm has 3 — netbird ×2, siproxd; nightly has 1 — siproxd), so it returned data on both boxes. Documentation rot of exactly the class #588 was filed for: a stale note suppresses nothing, the damage is a false note a triager trusts.

### Net, and what #589's acceptance looks like

The descent works. It reached four subtrees that were structurally invisible before, and on its **first** run it caught a decode bug we shipped the same day — one that silently removed an entire collector's metrics and that no fixture, gate or code review had caught. That is a better acceptance result than a clean run would have been.

## Triage — one real bug (ours, fixed), four ledger batches. Zero upstream drift.

Run [30637517316](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/actions/runs/30637517316), dispatched by hand as the acceptance test for **#589** (second-stage descent through 19 `json.RawMessage` envelope endpoints) and **#599** (67 paths moved into `required`). Both targets failed. That was the expected outcome and it earned its keep on the first run.

The five verdicts, in the order the report lists them.

---

### 1. `nginxVts` `*.overCounts` — **not drift. Our bug, shipped today.** → #609, fixed.

`serverZones.*.overCounts` and `upstreamZones.*[].overCounts` are **objects**; #584 modelled them as `float64` (`opnsense/nginx.go:73`, `:89`). Both targets report it identically, which rules out box-state.

The blast radius is larger than the field. `unmarshalBody` turns any `json.Unmarshal` failure into an `APICallError` (`opnsense/client.go:816`), so `FetchNginxVTS` returned **nothing** — every nginx VTS metric lost, not just the wrap counter. Reproduced locally:

```
json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field
  nginxVtsServerZone.serverZones.overCounts of type float64
```

Upstream confirms the shape twice. The vts README: *"The `overCounts` **objects** in JSON document are mostly for 32bit system"*. And `src/ngx_http_vhost_traffic_status_display_json.h` emits one wrap counter **per underlying counter** plus a `maxIntegerSize` constant — server zones get `requestCounter`, `inBytes`, `outBytes`, `1xx`–`5xx`, the eight cache keys on an `NGX_HTTP_CACHE` build, and `requestMsecCounter`; upstream zones get `responseMsecCounter` instead of the cache keys.

So #584 read the `add_oc` macro correctly and missed that the emitter **groups** those `_oc` fields into an object rather than totalling them.

**Why it passed CI.** `TestFetchNginxVTS_OverCounts` asserted against `"overCounts": 3` — a shape upstream cannot produce. A second copy of the same impossible fixture sat in `internal/collector/nginx_test.go`. This is exactly the rule already written down in CLAUDE.md: *a fixture must never encode a shape upstream cannot produce*. A hand-written fixture derived from the issue's own wrong premise agreed with the wrong code, and only a live payload disagreed.

Fixed with no metric, label, dashboard or catalogue change — the shipped description already reads "count of times **one of** this server zone's own vts counters … has been detected to wrap", which is precisely the sum across the object's sub-counters. A per-sub-counter `counter` label was considered and rejected: ~17× the series per zone for values permanently 0 on any 64-bit box. Reasoning is in the code so it is not re-derived.

---

### 2. `smartInfo` `output.endurance_used` / `output.spare_available` — verdict **box-state**.

Both are smartctl's own *derived* wear percentages, computed by regex-matching **vendor-specific** attribute names (the `SSD_Life_Left`/`Wear_Leveling` and `Reallocated_Sector_Count`/`Spare_Blocks` families). The exemptions ledger already describes them that way. A drive whose vendor attributes smartctl cannot match emits neither key — absent, not renamed or removed.

Both back exported metrics from #577, so the standing rule prefers fixing the testbed. That is not possible here: you cannot make a virtual disk report SSD endurance. A `missingOK` is the only option, and it should be **profile-scoped to `nightly` + `release-vm`** rather than base-scoped, because prod has real hardware and may well report these — base-scoping would blind the one profile that can actually verify them. Needs a live prod read before the scope is fixed.

**A stale ledger claim found while triaging this.** The `smartInfo` note asserts *"the nightly virtio testbed cannot produce ANY smartInfo data at all (`api/smart/service/list` 404s on virtio disks)"*. That is now false: `smartInfo` is **not** among the absent 404s on either target in this run (release-vm has 3 — netbird ×2, siproxd; nightly has 1 — siproxd), so it returned data on both boxes. Documentation rot of exactly the class #588 was filed for: a stale note suppresses nothing, the damage is a false note a triager trusts.

---

### 3. `quaggaOspfOverview` `response.areas.*` ×17 — verdict **opportunity**.

`areaIfTotalCounter`, `authentication`, `backbone`, and the eight `lsa*{Number,Checksum}` pairs.

This is **#591 finding 6 landing exactly as predicted**: `areas` is a custom-unmarshal map, so the reflector's walk stopped there and this subtree has never been visible to the canary. #589 extended the descent past it. Not a sudden upstream change — the same "FIRST LEDGER ENTRY, newly visible only because the reflector learned to descend" shape as the `quaggaOspfDatabase` and `quaggaBgpSummary` entries already in the ledger.

The four `opnsense_frr_ospf_area_*` counters are already modelled; these 17 are the remainder. → `knownExtraPaths`, each key triaged against `ospfd/ospf_vty.c` rather than bucketed by name.

---

### 4. `unboundBlocklistPolicies` `*` ×10 — verdict **opportunity**.

`address`, `allowlists`, `blocklists`, `cache_ttl`, `description`, `lists`, `nxdomain`, `source_nets`, `type`, `wildcards`. An unmodelled config endpoint's fields. → `knownExtraPaths`, after checking whether any is a bounded enum worth a config gauge rather than writing all ten off as configuration.

---

### 5. `healthCheck` `subsystems.*.{age,isBanner,location,persistent,priority,timestamp,title}` — **nightly only**, verdict **opportunity**.

**This is not a #284 contradiction, and it is worth being explicit because it looks like one.** #284's phantom was `metadata.subsystems`, which upstream still never populates. The **top-level** `subsystems` map is real and modelled (`opnsense/health_check.go:105`); `HealthCheckSubsystem` carries `message`/`status`/`statusCode` only, and these seven are unmodelled sibling fields of the notice/banner structure.

The nightly-only asymmetry is the ledger's own prediction coming true. The `subsystems` `missingOK` note says: *"It reappears the moment any subsystem reports, which is why #235 flagged it and #243 did not."* The nightly box now has a subsystem reporting; release-vm does not. Box state explaining a target asymmetry, precisely as documented — a small vindication of the box-state verdict that note was written to defend.

→ `knownExtraPaths`, verified against `SystemController::statusAction()` and the notices source.

---

### Net, and what #589's acceptance looks like

The descent works. It reached four subtrees that were structurally invisible before, and on its **first** run it caught a decode bug we shipped the same day — one that silently removed an entire collector's metrics and that no fixture, gate or code review had caught. That is a better acceptance result than a clean run would have been.
