**Tests** (all pass, no sleeps — the injected clock is used throughout): `TestWatcherBacksOffAfterARateLimit` is the regression bar (exactly `MaxPerCycle` attempts on tick 1, **zero** on tick 2, `seen` still empty so the backlog was not consumed) · `TestWatcherHonoursRetryAfterInDeltaSeconds` · `TestWatcherHonoursRetryAfterAsAnHTTPDate` · `TestWatcherFallsBackToExponentialOnAnUnparseableRetryAfter` · `TestWatcherBackoffGrowsWithConsecutiveRateLimits` · `TestWatcherResetsBackoffAfterASuccess` · `TestWatcherDoesNotRetryANonRetryable4xx` · `TestWatcherStillRetriesATransientRejection` (408) · `TestParseRetryAfter` (9 cases). Negative controls were run: disabling the backoff gate fails with `a backed-off tick made 3 further attempts`, disabling the permanent classification fails with `a permanently rejected event was retried: 2 attempts`.

**<host-1>.** Still `ANNOTATIONS_ENABLED=false`. Re-enable once watchtower has pulled a `:main` image built from `4fde7ba4` or later — re-enabling on the current binary would restart the storm. Service account, custom role and token remain provisioned and proven.

title: annotations: MaxPerCycle counts successes, so a 429 causes an unbounded self-sustaining retry storm

body:
## Finding

`--config.check` validates the effective configuration and prints a summary. On <host-1> today, with the syslog receiver, the Zenarmor receiver, the NetFlow receiver, flow rollups and Grafana annotations all enabled, the summary prints only:

```
[Connection]
[Exporter / Server]
[Collectors]
[Telemetry (OTLP)]
[Pyroscope]
```

Missing: annotations, log shipping (`logs.*`, including both receivers), and flow (`flow.*`, including the NetFlow receiver).

Exit code was 0 and the configuration is genuinely fine, so this is a reporting gap rather than a validation gap - but it is the gap that matters most for these particular settings.

## Why it matters more than a cosmetic omission

The omitted sections are exactly the ones an operator most needs to eyeball before starting:

- **Annotations is the exporter's only outbound write.** A preflight that does not mention it cannot be used to confirm whether this start will write to Grafana, or which Grafana.
- **All three receivers open listening sockets, and all three are UNAUTHENTICATED by default.** Whether an allowlist is actually in effect is a security-relevant fact the preflight silently withholds. An operator who typo'd `--logs.syslog.allowed-peers` gets exit 0 and a wide-open socket, with nothing in the summary to contradict them.
- The docs sell `--config.check` as the way to preflight a deployment (`docs/deployment/docker.md`). Sections that silently do not appear read as "not configured", which is the opposite of the truth here.

## Work

- [ ] Add `[Annotations]` - enabled, target URL, whether a token is present (presence only, never the value), lookback and max-per-cycle
- [ ] Add `[Log shipping]` - enabled, sink, and per receiver: enabled, listen addresses, **whether a peer allowlist is set and how many prefixes**, TLS on/off, debug capture on/off and its directory
- [ ] Add `[Flow]` - enabled, correlate, log mode, and for the NetFlow receiver the same listen/allowlist/capture treatment
- [ ] Secrets stay presence-only, matching how Pyroscope auth already renders as `••••`
- [ ] A test that fails when a new configuration family is added without a summary section, so this cannot silently recur

## Related

Found while aligning <host-1>'s deployment onto the shipped defaults (#515). The same "a setting that is configured but invisible" failure is what #517's autodiscovery report addresses from the other direction.

comments.body:
Closed by `4fde7ba4`. Verified end to end — real `--config.check` output on the new sections:

```
[Annotations]
  Enabled                      on
  Grafana URL                  https://x.grafana.net
  Token                        ••••
  Lookback                     24h0m0s
  Interval                     1m0s
  Max Per Cycle                20

[Log shipping]
  Enabled                      off
  Sink                         otlp
  Syslog Enabled               on
  Syslog Listen                udp :5514, tcp :5514
  Syslog Allowed Peers         set (2 prefixes)
  Syslog TLS                   off
  Syslog Debug Capture         off
  Zenarmor Enabled             off
  Zenarmor Listen              :9200
  Zenarmor Allowed Peers       open (no allowlist)
  Zenarmor TLS                 off
  Zenarmor Debug Capture       off
  Debug Capture Dir            —

[Flow]
  Enabled                      on
  Correlate                    on
  Log Mode                     per_flow
  NetFlow Enabled              on
  NetFlow Listen               :2055
  NetFlow Allowed Peers        open (no allowlist)
  NetFlow Debug Capture        off
```

Notes on the judgement calls:

- **Allowlists render as a COUNT, not a bool and not the prefixes** — `open (no allowlist)` vs `set (2 prefixes)`. `open (no allowlist)` is the wording precisely because an unauthenticated socket should read as a fact, not as an absent row. The prefixes themselves are omitted so a long list cannot make the row unbounded.
- **Secrets stay presence-only.** The annotations token is reduced to a boolean in `configInputs` before it reaches any renderer, same as the Pyroscope fields, so `TestBuildEffectiveConfig_SecretsRedacted`'s structural guarantee covers it automatically.
- **`--logs.debug-capture.dir` is shown once** at the Log shipping level rather than per receiver, since both receivers write into the one shared directory.
- **`gatherConfigInputs` reads the raw flag vars** rather than the `Annotations()`/`Logs()`/`Flow()` constructors — those validate and can error, and this is a status view.

Anti-recurrence: `TestConfigSummaryCoversEveryFlagFamily` (new file `internal/options/config_summary_coverage_test.go`) walks the real kingpin model, maps every flag family to a required summary section, and fails on any unmapped family. Families that legitimately have no section (`web.*`, `collector.*` scheduler tuning, `log.*`, kingpin built-ins, `config.check` itself) are exempted with a written reason, and a blank reason fails the test too.

title: config.check omits annotations, log receivers and flow from its summary

body:
## The asymmetry

Default-on collectors self-activate. Verified live today: the `os-acme-client` plugin was installed on the production firewall and <host-1> started exporting 6 `opnsense_acme_*` series with **no config change at all**, because `--exporter.disable-acme` is default-on and the collector is simply silent while the plugin is absent.

Opt-in features do not. The 24 `--exporter.enable-*` collectors, plus the syslog / Zenarmor / NetFlow receivers, stay silent forever until someone reads the docs and finds the flag. An operator who installs `os-smart` or `os-tor` gets nothing and no indication anything is available.

## Requested

**1. Startup availability report.** On first poll, determine which plugin-gated endpoints answer successfully, and for each feature that is available but not enabled, emit one friendly log line naming the flag and env var that would turn it on.

**2. `enable everything available`.** One opt-in setting that enables every feature autodiscovery finds, using the same detection.

## Reuse, do not reinvent

The detection primitive already exists. `PluginGatedEndpoints()` in `opnsense/cache.go` answers "does this 404 mean a plugin is absent?" (#495), and it is already what the canary and `acl.go` read. Availability discovery is that set, inverted. Do not build a second mechanism.

## Design constraints that must be respected

- **Opt-in collectors are opt-in for stated reasons, and "enable everything" silently accepts all of them at once.** `--exporter.enable-smart` runs `smartctl -a` per disk and wakes spun-down disks. `--exporter.enable-hasync` makes a live XML-RPC call to the CARP peer every poll. `--exporter.enable-unbound-qstats` is backed by a configd+python+pandas+DuckDB query at ~1s per poll. `--exporter.enable-openvpn-details` exposes usernames and per-client tunnel addresses. Several detail collectors are unbounded cardinality by construction. A blanket enable must be loud about what it just turned on - log every feature enabled and why it was gated - rather than presenting itself as a convenience toggle.
- **The receivers are not discoverable the same way.** Syslog, Zenarmor and NetFlow are push-based: nothing on the firewall API says "a syslog sender is configured to point at you", and each opens an UNAUTHENTICATED listening socket. A blanket enable must NOT open sockets. Scope the toggle to collectors, or gate the receivers separately and say so.
- **The negative cache delays discovery.** A plugin-gated 404 is cached for `--exporter.cache-ttl` (default 1h), so a plugin installed after startup is not noticed until that expires. Either the availability probe bypasses the negative cache, or the docs state the delay. Silently taking up to an hour to notice would look like the feature not working.
- **The probe must not be a startup scrape storm.** It runs against a firewall that may be small hardware. One pass, bounded concurrency, and it must not block serving `/metrics`.
- **Watch the series budget.** `--exporter.series-budget` defaults to 100000 and blanket-enabling every detail collector on a large network could cross it. The budget only warns (#494), but the availability report is the right place to say so up front.
- **Log once, not every poll.** A message repeated every 60s is noise that gets filtered, which defeats the purpose.

## Open questions

- Should the report be log-only, or also a metric (e.g. `opnsense_feature_available{feature,enabled}`) so a dashboard panel can show "available but off"? A metric is more useful than a log line nobody reads, and the web UI at `/` already has a natural home for it.
- Should the blanket toggle be all-or-nothing, or exclude the cardinality-unbounded detail collectors by default (`enable-all-available` vs `enable-all-available=safe`)?

## Acceptance

- [ ] Availability determined from the existing `PluginGatedEndpoints()` set, not a new mechanism
- [ ] One-shot friendly log naming the flag and env var per available-but-disabled feature
- [ ] Opt-in blanket enable, which logs every feature it turned on and never opens a receiver socket
- [ ] Cache-TTL discovery delay either bypassed or documented
- [ ] Docs regenerated via `make docs`; dashboard panel added if a metric is introduced (the coverage gate requires it)

comments.body:
Implemented in `eef61c76`, with a follow-up fix in `c5fb5037`. Both on main.

**What shipped**

- `opnsense_feature_available{feature,enabled}` — emitted only for a feature whose plugin endpoint answers, so absence means unavailable rather than a zero to filter out. Panel added to the Health dashboard's Exporter Runtime tab.
- One-shot log naming the flag and env var per available-but-disabled feature, re-emitted only when the availability **set changes**, not every probe.
- `--exporter.enable-all-available` — flips every opt-in collector switch the operator has not set themselves, logs each one with the reason it defaults to off, and reminds about `--exporter.series-budget` past 5. It never opens a receiver socket.
- Probes bypass the negative-404 cache via a new `Client.WithoutCache()`, so a plugin installed after startup is noticed on the next 15m cold-tier probe rather than up to `--exporter.cache-ttl` later.
- `FetchSMARTAvailable()` / `FetchVnstatAvailable()` hit only the plugin's list endpoint — the probe must never trigger the collector's own fan-out, or discovering SMART would itself spin up the disks the flag exists to avoid waking.

**Two scoping calls worth recording**

The **probe set is SMART, Tor and Vnstat only**, while the **blanket switch still flips all 24** opt-in collectors. That is not an inconsistency: availability discovery is only meaningful where a plugin is either installed or not, and that is the intersection of `PluginGatedEndpoints()` with the `enable-*` set. The other 21 flags are gated on cost, cardinality or exposing usernames — there is no plugin to detect and nothing for a probe to discover, so they are absent from the table deliberately.

An explicitly-set flag always beats the blanket switch, **including one set via its env var**. Kingpin's `IsSetByUser` only fires on a CLI token and never for an `Envar`-sourced value, so env precedence needed a direct `os.LookupEnv` check — a container operator setting `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_ENABLE_SMART=false` would otherwise have been silently overridden. Tested in both forms.

**Corrections made on merge**

- The env var was `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_EXPORTER_ENABLE_ALL_AVAILABLE`. Every other switch drops the `exporter.` segment; renamed to `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_ENABLE_ALL_AVAILABLE` before release, so nothing to deprecate.
- Each probe duplicated its flag's `Reason` string from `CollectorFlags`. Nothing failed when the two drifted, and the visible symptom would be an operator reading a stale justification for a collector we had just recommended. Now asserted equal by a test.

**No web UI page.** The metric plus the panel cover it, and the console reads a passive snapshot rather than probing — bolting availability onto it would have meant new plumbing for a second rendering of the same fact.

Gate: all Go packages ok, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `make docs-check` and `make grafana-check` passed, dashboard coverage 884/884.

title: Autodiscovery: tell operators which available features they have not enabled, and offer to enable them all

body:
## Finding

Live on <host-1> (`/opt/opnsense-exporter`, `:main`), read from `/metrics` on 2026-07-29:

```
opnsense_flow_ifindex_conflicts 3
opnsense_flow_ifindex_entries 18
opnsense_flow_ifindex_source_disagreements{reason="stated_index"} 0
opnsense_flow_ifindex_source_disagreements{reason="unlisted_device"} 0
opnsense_flow_ifindex_unmapped_total 0
```

<host-1> pins 10 indices via `--flow.netflow.ifindex-map`:

```
1=ixl0,2=ixl1,5=igb0,7=lo0,11=ixl0_vlan100,12=ixl0_vlan25,13=ixl0_vlan50,14=zen0,15=pppoe0,16=tailscale0
```

3 of those 10 disagree with the derived map. Per the metric's own help text: non-zero means "the derived enumeration does not reproduce the box's own ifinfo ordering - the override is winning, so labels are right, but **every index the operator did not pin is suspect**."

So the pin is still load-bearing and must stay. It was added for #361, where the derived map was off by one from index 10 up because the API enumeration omits `pfsync0`, mislabelling ~93% of volume as "tailscale".

## The metric conflates two different things

`internal/flow/ifmap.go:365-368`:

```go
prev, existed := m.byIndex[idx]
if !existed || prev.Device != resolved.Device || prev.Name != resolved.Name {
    m.conflicts++
}
```

`conflicts` increments both when an override **disagrees** with a derived entry and when the derivation **never produced that index at all**. Those are different failures with different fixes:

- a genuine disagreement means the enumeration ordering is wrong (the #361 off-by-one)
- an absent index means the API does not enumerate that interface at all, which is plausible for `lo0`, `pppoe0` and `zen0`

`conflicts = 3` on a box pinning exactly those three interfaces is suggestive but **not proof** of either. The metric as it stands cannot distinguish them, so it cannot answer the question the pin's comment says it answers.

## Work

- [ ] Determine which 3 of <host-1>'s 10 pins are counted, and whether each is a disagreement or an absence. Compare the derived map against `ifinfo | awk '$1 == "Interface" { n++; print n, $2 }'` on the firewall - that enumeration is the ground truth ng_netflow indexes against
- [ ] Split the metric so the two cases are distinguishable (a `reason` label matching the existing `ifindex_source_disagreements` shape, or a separate series). Today a non-zero value cannot be triaged without shell access to the box
- [ ] If the enumeration ordering is genuinely wrong, fix the derivation and confirm the pinned indices then agree
- [ ] If the interfaces are simply absent from the API enumeration, say so in the flag help and the metric help, so a permanently non-zero reading is not mistaken for unfixed drift
- [ ] Only once conflicts reads 0 against the pins, consider removing them from <host-1>. **Do not remove the pin before then** - wrong interface labels are worse than missing ones

## Do not re-chase

Selecting a PPPoE interface for NetFlow captures nothing on any OPNsense box (ng_netflow attaches to mpd's framing node, not the ng_iface node). That is a closed negative result and is not the cause here; `pppoe0` still occupies a position in the `ifinfo` enumeration regardless of whether it exports flows.

Split out from #515.

comments.body:
Closed by `4fde7ba4`. The answer is the opposite of what the issue assumed: **the derivation is correct and the pin is stale.**

## Which 3, and which kind

All 3 are genuine **disagreements**, not absences. From the running exporter on <host-1> (`/api/ifindex.json`, 2026-07-29):

| index | pin says | derivation says | API-stated |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14 | `zen0` | `ixl0_vlan90` | — |
| 15 | `pppoe0` | `zen0` | 15 |
| 16 | `tailscale0` | `pppoe0` | 16 |

`Disagreements` (stated vs derived) reads **0** — the derivation agrees with the API on every device it enumerates.

## Ground truth, from the firewall

`ifinfo` order:

```
1 ixl0   2 ixl1   3 ixl2   4 ixl3   5 igb0   6 igb1   7 lo0   8 enc0
9 pfsync0   10 pflog0   11 ixl0_vlan100   12 ixl0_vlan25   13 ixl0_vlan50
14 ixl0_vlan90   15 zen0   16 pppoe0   17 tailscale0
```

Decisive, because it is the number `rc.d/netflow` actually passed to `ngctl mkpeer` and therefore the number stamped on every record — the live netgraph hook names:

```
netflow_ixl0          iface1
netflow_ixl1          iface2
netflow_ixl0_vlan100  iface11
netflow_ixl0_vlan25   iface12
netflow_ixl0_vlan50   iface13
netflow_ixl0_vlan90   iface14
netflow_pppoe0        iface16
```

`iface16 = pppoe0`. The derivation says 16=pppoe0. **The pin says 16=tailscale0.**

## Root cause

Adding VLAN 90 for #497 inserted `ixl0_vlan90` at position 14 and shifted everything above it up one. The pin predates that, so it was correct when written and went stale on its own — and because an override wins outright, it was **actively mislabelling the PPPoE WAN (~91% of the box's volume) as `tailscale`**. That is #361's exact failure, reintroduced by the mitigation for #361.

## Shipped

- `opnsense_flow_ifindex_conflicts` now carries `reason="derived_differs"` / `reason="derived_absent"`, so absence and disagreement are distinguishable without shell access. `IfMapStats` gained `ConflictsDiffering`/`ConflictsAbsent`; `Conflicts` stays the sum for the console. Test: `TestBuildIfMap_ConflictReasonsAreCountedSeparately`.
- The metric help no longer asserts the derivation is the suspect. It now says non-zero does **not** say which side is right, explains that a pin is a static assertion against a positional index that goes stale when any interface is added or removed, and names `ngctl show netflow_<device>:` as the tiebreak. Same correction in the `--flow.netflow.ifindex-map` flag help and `docs/flow.md`.
- Dashboard legend now renders `{{reason}}`.
- No change to the derivation itself — it is right.

## <host-1>

`docker-compose.yml` edited: the pin is **removed entirely** (backup `docker-compose.yml.bak.PRE-IFINDEX-UNPIN.20260729`), with a comment recording why re-pinning is now the wrong reflex — an unpinned index cannot go stale. **The container recreate has NOT been run** (blocked by a local permission gate), so <host-1> is still running with the stale pin until:

```
cd /opt/opnsense-exporter && docker compose up -d
```

After that, `opnsense_flow_ifindex_conflicts` should read 0 on both reasons and NetFlow volume should move from `tailscale` onto the PPPoE WAN.

title: flow: ifIndex derivation still disagrees with 3 operator pins on <host-1>

body:
## Why

`docs/configuration.md` already documents all 200 flags with defaults (docgen `flags-full-reference`, gated by `make docs-check`). What does **not** exist is an example *config artifact* an operator can copy that shows every setting at its default. Today's examples are all deliberately minimal:

| Artifact | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `docs/deployment/docker.md` | 5 flags + credentials |
| `charts/opnsense-exporter/values.yaml` | 51 lines, `extraArgs` escape hatch |
| `deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml`, `docs/deployment/systemd.md` | same minimal shape |

Hand-writing a 200-entry example is a rot machine, so all three new artifacts are **generated by docgen from the kingpin model** and gated by `make docs-check`.

## Frozen seam (already landed, do not re-derive)

`scripts/docgen/flaggroups.go` partitions the kingpin model into 16 ordered sections shared by all three generated artifacts, so they cannot drift into three different layouts. `TestGroupFlagsCoversEveryFlag` proves every flag lands in exactly one group — a new flag whose prefix matches no rule fails the build.

Current partition (200 flags): connection 8, collectors-opt-in 24, collectors-default-on 56, webui 4, server 7, exporter 11, otlp 14, pyroscope 6, annotations 8, logs-syslog 16, logs-zenarmor 14, logs-lanes 3, logs-debug-capture 2, logs 11, flow-netflow 5, flow 11.

Lane contract: each lane adds its **own** new file under `scripts/docgen/`, emits via `out.write(absPath, []byte(content))` (which already handles write-vs-check mode), and consumes `[]FlagDoc{Name, Help, Envar, Default, Required}`. Wiring into `main.go` / `mkdocs.yml` is a single pass by one owner, never in parallel.

## Scope

- [ ] **A** — generated `.env.example` at repo root: every flag as a commented-out `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_*` line at its default, grouped and blurbed
- [ ] **B** — generated Compose reference page under `docs/deployment/`, every flag present and commented at its default
- [ ] **C** — Helm: generated `settings:` block in `values.yaml` covering every flag, `templates/deployment.yaml` renders `range .Values.settings` so new flags need no template change, `values.schema.json` updated. Curated keys (`opnsense.address`, `ports.*`) keep winning; a duplicate between a curated key and `settings` must `fail` the render rather than silently pick one
- [ ] **D** — extend doclint's `lintTargets` to `charts/`. It already covers `docs/`, `deploy/`, README, CLAUDE.md, Makefile, `grafana/tabs/` — `charts/` is the gap, so a renamed flag can currently rot the chart undetected
- [ ] **E** — wiring pass: register A/B/C in `main.go`, add B to `mkdocs.yml` nav, run `make docs && make test && make lint`

## <host-1> alignment (`/opt/opnsense-exporter/docker-compose.yml`)

Deliberate and staying: opt-in functionality (OTLP, Pyroscope, all 24 opt-in collectors, syslog/Zenarmor/NetFlow receivers, the three `allowed-peers` allowlists), debug capture to disk, `opnsense.insecure`, ports `:9098`/`:5847`.

- [ ] Drop 7 lines that restate the default: `otlp.protocol`, `otlp.export-interval`, `otlp.service-name`, `logs.sink`, `logs.zenarmor.listen-http`, `flow.netflow.listen`, `logs.debug-capture.max-bytes`
- [ ] Fix two stale comments that contradict their values: the `max-bytes` block still says "RAISED … PUT THIS BACK to 256MiB" when the value **is** `256MiB` (the #360 window closed and the value was restored; only the comment lagged), and `FLOW_NETFLOW_DEBUG_CAPTURE` carries two contradictory paragraphs, of which the first (arguing for `all`) is leftover
- [ ] Remove `FLOW_LOG_MODE: "off"` so <host-1> matches the shipped `per_flow` default. **Cost note:** this starts shipping one OTLP log per correlated flow on top of the Zenarmor conn stream (~4-6 GB/day)
- [ ] Enable `--annotations.enabled` with a Grafana URL + service-account token (annotation-write scope only). This is the exporter's only outbound write and needs a new token
- [ ] Keep `FLOW_NETFLOW_DEBUG_CAPTURE: unidentified` (diverges from the `off` default on purpose)
- [ ] Keep the pinned `FLOW_NETFLOW_IFINDEX_MAP` — see below

## Decisions made, do not re-litigate

- `--flow.log-mode` keeps its `per_flow` default; <host-1> changes to match rather than the default changing to match <host-1>.
- `--flow.netflow.debug-capture` keeps its `off` default; <host-1> stays on `unidentified` as a deliberate local divergence.

## Live finding: the ifIndex derivation is still wrong (split out)

`opnsense_flow_ifindex_conflicts = 3` on <host-1> right now — 3 of the 10 operator pins disagree with the map derived from the API. Per the metric's own help text, non-zero means "the derived enumeration does not reproduce the box's own ifinfo ordering — the override is winning, so labels are right, but **every index the operator did not pin is suspect**." The compose comment blames the API enumeration omitting `pfsync0`.

So the pin is still load-bearing and must stay. Needs its own issue: identify which 3 indices disagree and fix the derivation.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `make docs && make docs-check` clean; every one of the 200 flags appears in each of the three generated artifacts
- [ ] `make test`, `make lint`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make deployment-test` green
- [ ] Adding a flag with no group rule fails the build
- [ ] <host-1>'s compose diff contains only the changes ticked above; exporter healthy after restart

comments.body:
Done and pushed as `b0f4338`.

**Repo side.** Three generated artifacts now cover all 200 flags, each with its own coverage gate:

| Artifact | Size |
|---|---|
| `.env.example` | 59 KB |
| `docs/deployment/reference.md` | 59 KB |
| `charts/opnsense-exporter/values.yaml` `settings:` block | +958 lines |

`scripts/docgen/flaggroups.go` is the shared 16-section seam; a flag matching no rule fails the build. The chart renders `settings` through `range` in `_helpers.tpl`, so new flags need no template change. Repeatable flags detected via kingpin's `IsCumulative`, not name-guessed — 4 real ones. doclint now walks `charts/`.

Two traps found on the way:
- `.env.*` in `.gitignore` would have kept the generated file out of git entirely, failing `docs-check` on a fresh clone. Negation added.
- `injectRegion` structurally cannot target a YAML host (its splice drops the `#` prefix off the end marker and breaks parsing), so the chart uses a line-based `injectYAMLRegion` instead.

Gate: `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `gofmt`, `docgen -check`, `make deployment-test` including the chart contract tests — all green.

**<host-1>.** Applied: 7 redundant lines dropped, both stale comments corrected, `FLOW_LOG_MODE` removed so it matches the `per_flow` default. Kept on purpose: `FLOW_NETFLOW_DEBUG_CAPTURE=unidentified` and the pinned ifIndex map. Healthy, `/-/ready` 200, zero errors.

Measured flow-log cost of restoring `per_flow`: ~7,100 records shipped in 7 minutes, about 1.5M/day, against Zenarmor's ~3.4M/day. Roughly a 43% increase in log volume.

**Annotations are provisioned but disabled.** A tightly-scoped service account and token are working, but enabling them exposed #519 — a self-sustaining retry storm on Grafana Cloud's 429. Core fix pushed as `eec1461`; <host-1> stays off until that image lands.

Split out: #516 (ifIndex derivation still disagrees with 3 pins), #517 (autodiscovery), #518 (`config.check` omits annotations/receivers/flow), #519 (annotation retry storm).

title: Ship generated example configs covering every flag, and align <host-1> onto them

body:
## What

Three families of inconsistency found by the #491 rendering sweep. None of them renders a wrong *number* — each makes the dashboard read as if two neighbouring panels mean different things when they don't. Filed together because they are one mechanical pass, not three investigations.

## 1. ~50 rate panels label a per-second axis `short` while their neighbours use a rate unit

Every panel below applies `rate()`/`irate()` and says "per second" in its title or description, but sets `unit: "short"` — so the axis and legend print a bare number.

- **Protocol Stats:** `panel-315`, `318`, `320`, `321`, `322`
- **Log-derived Events:** `panel-641`-`648`, `649`-`652`, `654`, `655`
- **Nginx / syslog:** `panel-71`, `44`, `466`, `468`, `473`, `475`, `477`, `480`, `483`, `487`, `386`, `388`, `389`, `391`, `395`
- **Zenarmor / flow:** `panel-529`, `530`, `501`, `502`, `504`, `511`, `678`, `679`, `682`, `686`, `688`, `689`, `695`, `700`
- **Interfaces:** `panel-93` "Interface Errors", `panel-94` "Collisions", `panel-96` "Queue Drops"

The interfaces three are the clearest case: they sit on the same row as `panel-90`/`91`/`92`, which are built from identically-shaped queries and correctly use `pps`. An interface dropping 2 packets a minute reads `0.0333` with no unit, directly beside "Packets RX: 1.2 Kpps". Read as a count, 0.0333 errors is nonsense and gets dismissed; read as a rate it is 2/min and real.

Same pattern on the Zenarmor Overview row, where `panel-678` (`short`) and `panel-680` (`reqps`) disagree about the same class of value.

**Fix:** `pps` for packet-valued counters, `reqps` for request counters, `ops` for mixed event rates. `ops` is what `panel-159` already uses for `opnsense_log_events_gateway_total`.

Two related but weaker cases — `panel-103` "LAGG Port Flapping" and `panel-590` "APC Mains Transfer Rate" — rate non-packet events, so `short` is defensible; `ops` would be the consistent choice. Judgement call, not a defect.

## 2. 54 tables render a raw `opnsense_instance` column header, 58 rename it to `Instance`

Confirmed by render on `panel-98` and `panel-161`: the column header reads the literal Prometheus label name `opnsense_instance`, sitting between properly-titled columns like `Device` and `MTU (bytes)`.

It is an even split — 54 tables leave it, 58 rename it — so neither is "the convention"; it is just drift. Affected panels span Certificates, Chrony, CrowdSec, DHCP, FRR, Gateways, HAProxy, Interfaces, Monit, NetBird, Q-Feeds, Relayd, System, Tailscale, Tor, UPS and VPN.

**Fix:** the table helper in `grafana/builder.py` should add the `opnsense_instance -> Instance` rename by default rather than leaving it to each call site.

## 3. Dead threshold blocks on colour-complete mapped panels

`panel-29`, `panel-268`, `panel-270`, `panel-291`, `panel-385`, `panel-581`, `panel-591`, `panel-621` all carry a thresholds block alongside value mappings that specify their own colours. A value mapping with a colour wins over the threshold, so the threshold steps are inert.

Nothing renders wrong today. Three reasons to clean it up anyway:

- It reads as intent. Someone adjusting a threshold on `panel-291` will see no change and conclude the panel is broken.
- Several are also *backwards* — `panel-621` "Leap Status" has `[red@base, green@0]`, which would colour `3 = Not synchronised` green. It only renders correctly because the mappings shadow it, and it becomes a live bug the moment the box reports a value outside the mapped 0-3 range.
- `panel-385` "Syslog Service" is the mirror case: it is the only one of ~10 service-state stats with no `green@1` step, so it loses its colour entirely if the mapping is ever dropped.

**Fix:** either drop the thresholds where mappings own the colour, or drop the colours from the mappings and let thresholds drive — one rule, applied to all eight.

## Also worth a line

`panel-282` / `panel-283` (NetBird) reuse the shared `RUNSTOP` mapping, so "Management Connected" renders as "Running". The encoding and colour are right; the noun describes a daemon rather than a connection, which are different faults on a NetBird node. A `CONNDISC` mapping would fix it.

`panel-27` "Collector Poll Interval" (health dashboard, Diagnostics) has no unit on the value column, so the cold tier prints `900` while the panel's own description spells the tiers out as "fast 15s / medium 60s / slow 5m / cold 15m". A `byName` override with `unit: "s"` — the pattern `panel-38` and `panel-383` already use — makes it read `15 min`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Rate panels carry a per-second unit
- [ ] `opnsense_instance` renamed by default in the table helper
- [ ] Threshold-vs-mapping colour ownership settled with one rule
- [ ] `make dashboard` + `make grafana-check` green

Found by the #491 rendering sweep.
title: Dashboard consistency: unitless rate axes, raw opnsense_instance headers, dead threshold blocks

body:
## What

Seven panels apply a unit that contradicts the quantity, or apply none where the magnitude is unreadable without one. Several were confirmed by rendering the live dashboard; the rest are unambiguous from the metric catalogue.

### `panel-607` "Pipe Packets" / `panel-610` "Queue Packets" (Traffic Shaper) — a count labelled as a rate

Both queries read raw gauges with **no `rate()`**: `opnsense_trafficshaper_pipe_packets` and the queue equivalent, documented "Total packets processed by this pipe (gauge)" (catalogue lines 1084, 1089). Both panels set `unit="pps"` (`grafana/tabs/trafficshaper.py:76`, `:105`).

A pipe that has processed 4.2 million packets displays **"4.2 Mpps"** — a wire rate no OPNsense box can produce, so the panel reads as an absurd throughput figure rather than a total. The sibling byte panels 606/609 correctly use `bytes` rather than `Bps` for the identical gauge shape, so the two are wrong side by side on the same tab.

**Fix:** `unit="short"`.

### `panel-691` "Top Talkers by Bytes" (Zenarmor) — bytes as a bare integer

Confirmed by render: the `Total` column reads `10451890958`. The panel's own description says "Value column is raw bytes". `unit` is null and there is no field override, so it renders as an 11-digit number that reads as a connection count.

**Fix:** a `byName: "Total"` override with `unit: bytes` — it becomes `10.5 GB`.

### `panel-98` "Interface Info (MTU / Line Rate / Device / Type)" (Interfaces) — MTU in KiB

Confirmed by render: under a column header that literally says **"MTU (bytes)"**, a standard 1500-byte MTU displays as **"1.46 KiB"** and the tailscale interface as "1.25 KiB". MTU is a figure operators compare against an exact configured value (1500 / 9000 / 1492); the IEC-scaled form cannot be pattern-matched and has to be converted back by hand.

**Fix:** drop the `bytes` override on `Value #A`. The `Value #B -> bps` line rate override is correct and should stay.

### `panel-145` "GeoIP Database Age" (Firewall & PF) — hours with no unit

Confirmed by render: the stat reads a bare **"21.2"**. The thresholds (orange at 24, red at 168) are calibrated in hours, but the display gives the reader no scale — read as seconds it is meaningless, read as days it is alarming. Every other hours-derived panel in the repo sets `unit="h"` (`tabs/clamav.py:67`, `tabs/captiveportal.py:164`).

**Fix:** `unit="h"` — renders "21.2 hour".

### `panel-412` "Capture Coverage: Expected vs Last Record" (NetFlow) — two incompatible quantities on one axis

Confirmed by render. The panel plots `netflow_capture_expected` (0/1 boolean) and `netflow_capture_last_record_seconds` on a single `unit: "short"` axis. The age series spikes to 140+, so the y-axis runs 0-160 and **the 0/1 boolean is flattened onto the baseline and invisible** — the legend is the only place it appears. The age is also unitless, while the two adjacent stat panels the description tells you to compare against (`panel-413`, `panel-414`) both correctly use `unit: "s"`.

**Fix:** `unit="s"` on the panel plus a `byName` override forcing the `expected` series to `short`/`max: 1`, or split into two panels.

### `panel-453` "Server Health Transitions" (HAProxy) — a rate formatted as a duration

Panel-level `unit: "s"` with no overrides, but query A is `rate(opnsense_haproxy_server_check_downs_total[...])`, legended "down transitions/s". A server flapping once a minute gives `rate ~ 0.0167`, which the axis and tooltip print as **"16.7 ms"** — a transition rate rendered as a duration, sharing an axis with a genuine 3600 s "time since last change" series.

**Fix:** keep `s` for `last_state_change_seconds`, add a `byName` override setting the `chkdown` series to `short`.

### `panel-671` "NetFlow ifIndex Map" (Flow Volume) — the staleness signal is the unreadable one

`opnsense_flow_ifindex_map_age_seconds` is plotted with the panel's `unit: "short"`. Today the map age is ~2 s so it renders innocuously, but a map that has not refreshed for two hours reads **"7.20 K"** and a day-old one "86.4 K". The one series on the panel where absolute magnitude is the alarm is the one rendered in the least readable form.

**Fix:** override that series to `unit: s`, or split it to its own stat.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All seven render in the correct unit
- [ ] `panel-412` shows the `expected` boolean legibly
- [ ] `make dashboard` + `make grafana-check` green

Found by the #491 rendering sweep.
title: Dashboard: seven panels display a value in the wrong unit or no unit at all

body:
## What

`Builder.ts()` sets `defaults["min"] = 0` whenever `min0` is truthy, and `min0` defaults to True (`grafana/builder.py:329-330`). Four panels plot metrics that are **signed by definition** and never override it, so the y-axis floor is pinned at 0 and every negative reading is drawn below the visible area.

In each case the panel flatlines on the axis, which is visually identical to "the value is zero and everything is fine" — the failure state and the healthy state render the same.

### `panel-624` "System Time Offset" (Chrony)

Its own series legend reads `offset (fast=+, slow=-)` and the description says "Negative = slow". `opnsense_chrony_system_time_offset_seconds` is documented fast=positive / slow=negative, and the repo's own parser test asserts `-0.000123456` (`opnsense/chrony_test.go:118`). The panel deletes exactly the half of the signal its description tells you to look at. Half of all clock-drift incidents are invisible here.

Call site: `grafana/tabs/chrony.py:97-107`.

### `panel-629` "Source Offset" (Chrony)

`opnsense_chrony_source_offset_seconds` is ± relative to local time. Every source whose offset is negative flatlines, so comparing sources — the whole point of the panel — only works for the ones that happen to be positive. `grafana/tabs/chrony.py:162-170`.

### `panel-625` "Frequency Error (ppm)" (Chrony)

`frequency` and `residual_frequency` are signed (the parser test asserts `ResidualFrequencyPPM == -0.001`, `opnsense/chrony_test.go:124`). On a box whose oscillator drifts negative, both lines sit flat at 0 and only `skew` — which is genuinely non-negative — is ever visible. The panel reads "no frequency error", the opposite of the truth. `grafana/tabs/chrony.py:108-115`.

### `panel-109` "SFP Lane RX Power (dBm)" (Interfaces)

Optical RX power in dBm is essentially always negative (-3 to -20 dBm typical), and the panel's own description warns the values are "often negative". A healthy 10G optic at -6.0 dBm is not drawn at all — the operator sees an empty plot area with a legend table reading "-6.02 dBm". A dying optic at -22 dBm looks identical to a healthy one: both invisible. The panel exists to show a falling trend and can never show one. `grafana/tabs/interfaces.py:297-307`.

## Fix

Pass `min0=False` at all four call sites.

`panel-352` "Peer Timing" (NTP) already does exactly this for clock offset, which is what establishes these four as oversights rather than house convention.

## Related, lower priority

`panel-107` "SFP Temperature" carries the same `min: 0` via the same default. Correct for commercial-temp optics (0-70 C); an industrial-temp module in an unheated cabinet reporting -5 C would be clipped the same way. Same one-word fix, much narrower blast radius.

## Worth considering

A builder-level guard: if a panel's metric is known-signed, `min0=True` should be an error rather than a silent default. Otherwise the next signed metric added gets clipped the same way.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All four panels render negative values
- [ ] `panel-107` decided either way and the reasoning recorded
- [ ] `make dashboard` + `make grafana-check` green

Found by the #491 rendering sweep.
title: Dashboard: min0 default clips every negative value on four signed-metric panels

body:
## What

Six panels colour a state the opposite way round from what the metric means, or leave a documented state unmapped so it falls through to a threshold that colours it green. All verified against `docs/metrics/metrics.md` and the builder source; none of them fails a test or a gate.

### 1. `panel-476` "Upstream Server Down" (Nginx) — fully inverted

`opnsense_nginx_upstream_server_down` is documented `1 = down, 0 = up` (`docs/metrics/metrics.md:839`), and the panel description repeats it. `grafana/tabs/nginx.py:145-151` applies the shared `UPDOWN` mapping, which is `{0: Down/red, 1: Up/green}` (`grafana/builder.py:171`) — the opposite polarity.

A healthy nginx renders as a solid red timeline labelled "Down". A genuinely down upstream renders green, labelled "Up".

**Fix:** add a `DOWNUP` constant next to `UPDOWN` and use it here, thresholds `green@base / red@1`.

### 2. `panel-421` "CARP VIP Status" (CARP / HA) — missing the state #503 added

`#503` gave `opnsense_carp_vip_status` a fifth value, `3 = DISABLED` (catalogue line 110, `opnsense/carp.go:48-72` — emitted for any configured VIP the ifconfig pass did not find, i.e. admin-disabled or interface down, both routine). `_VIP_STATUS` at `grafana/tabs/carp.py:30-35` was never extended, so `3` has no mapping and falls through to the thresholds `[red@base, green@1]` — **3 >= 1, so a disabled VIP paints green, labelled with the bare number `3`, indistinguishable from a healthy MASTER.**

The panel description is stale the same way: it lists "MASTER, BACKUP, INIT, or Unknown".

**Fix:** add `"3": ("DISABLED", "text")` and update the `desc=` at `tabs/carp.py:115`.

### 3. `panel-371` "Total Signatures Loaded" (ClamAV) — permanently red

`grafana/tabs/clamav.py:41`: `thresholds=[{"color":"blue","value":None},{"color":"red","value":0}]`. The red step covers `>= 0` and the metric is a count that is never negative, so **red always wins** — a healthy box showing 8.7M signatures renders the number in red, and blue is unreachable. The one condition the panel exists to flag (0) looks identical to every healthy state.

**Fix:** `[{"color":"red","value":None},{"color":"blue","value":1}]`.

### 4. `panel-591` / `panel-581` / `panel-270` — polarity inverted on the good-when-1 series

One field-wide mapping is applied to series with opposite polarity:

- `panel-591` APC Status Flags and `panel-581` NUT Status Flags use `{0: No/green, 1: Yes/orange}` (`grafana/tabs/ups.py:113`, `:212`) across `*_status_online`, `*_on_battery`, `*_low_battery`, `*_charging`, `*_replace_battery`. `online` and `charging` are **good** at 1, so a UPS sitting healthily on mains paints its `online` row solid orange for the whole window, and flips to green when mains actually fails.
- `panel-270` IPsec Config State does the same with `{0: No/green, 1: Yes/yellow}` over `ipsec_legacy_enabled` (1 = enabled = normal) and `ipsec_config_dirty`.

On a state timeline the colour is the whole signal, so the top row reads as a persistent warning during normal operation and as all-clear during an outage.

**Fix:** per-series mappings or a `byName` override, so good-when-1 series map `1 -> green`.

### 5. `panel-58` "ZFS Boot Environments Supported" (System & Resources) — contradicts itself

`opnsense_snapshots_supported` is `1 = capable`. `grafana/tabs/system.py:557-567` passes `YESNO` (`{0: No/green, 1: Yes/orange}`), which is the "is this a problem?" polarity shared with Needs Reboot. With `color_mode="background"`, a ZFS box — the recommended install — renders **"Yes" on a full orange background**, and a UFS box renders green. The explicit `green@1` threshold on the same panel shows green was intended; the mapping colour overrides it.

**Fix:** a local `{0: No/red, 1: Yes/green}` mapping instead of `YESNO`.

### 6. `panel-540` "Check Monitored State" (Monit) — wrong words

`opnsense_monit_check_monitored` is `1 = monitored, 0 = not monitored` — a configuration state, not health. `UPDOWN` renders a deliberately-unmonitored check as red "Down", identical in colour and wording to a failing check on the "Check Status Over Time" panel stacked directly above it.

**Fix:** `{0: Unmonitored/grey, 1: Monitored/green}`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All six panels render the healthy state in a non-alarm colour
- [ ] `panel-421` maps `3 = DISABLED` and its description lists it
- [ ] `panel-371` is blue when signatures are loaded, red at 0
- [ ] `make dashboard` + `make grafana-check` green

Found by the #491 rendering sweep.
title: Dashboard: six state panels have inverted, incomplete or self-contradicting colour encoding

body:
## What

`panel-323` "TCP Connections by State (over time)" (Protocol Stats tab) colours a **state count** with an up/down threshold ladder, so every TCP state that currently has zero connections paints a solid red band.

Rendered against the live dashboard, a completely healthy firewall shows:

- `CLOSING`, `FIN_WAIT_1`, `FIN_WAIT_2`, `LAST_ACK` — **solid red for the entire window**
- `CLOSE_WAIT`, `SYN_RCVD`, `SYN_SENT` — red with occasional green flecks
- `ESTABLISHED`, `LISTEN`, `TIME_WAIT`, `CLOSED` — green

The legend reads, literally, `< 1` (red) and `1+` (green). Roughly two thirds of the panel is alarm-coloured in the normal steady state.

## Cause

`grafana/tabs/protocols.py:202` calls `statetimeline(...)` with `mappings={}`, so the helper's default thresholds `[{red, base}, {green, 1}]` are used unmodified. That ladder encodes "0 is an error", which is right for an up/down flag and wrong for a connection-state census — `FIN_WAIT_2 == 0` is the *normal* state of a quiet firewall, not a fault.

Two secondary problems on the same panel:

- Magnitude is invisible. 5,000 ESTABLISHED and 1 ESTABLISHED are the same shade of green, so the panel carries one bit per state.
- `mappings: [{"type": "value", "options": {}}]` — an empty mapping object ships in the generated JSON because the empty dict is still emitted.

## Why it matters

This is worse than a cosmetic issue: a panel that is loudly red during normal operation trains the reader to ignore it, which is exactly when a genuine anomaly stops being noticed. It is the most visually misleading panel on the dashboard.

## Fix

Either:

- drop the thresholds to a single neutral base step and let the state labels carry the meaning, or
- switch `color.mode` to a continuous palette so the band shade tracks the count, which is what a census panel wants.

Also suppress the `mappings` array entirely when the dict is empty.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A healthy box renders `panel-323` without alarm colouring on zero-count states
- [ ] No empty `{"type":"value","options":{}}` mapping in the generated JSON
- [ ] `make dashboard` + `make grafana-check` green

Found by the #491 rendering sweep.
title: Dashboard: TCP Connections by State renders a healthy firewall as a wall of red

body:
## What

`panel-146` "GeoIP Database Last Update" (Firewall & PF tab) renders as a **one-column table containing only `Instance`**. The timestamp it exists to show is never drawn.

Verified by rendering the published dashboard (`gcx dashboards snapshot opnsense-exporter --panel 146`): the panel draws a header row `Instance` and a single body row `opnsense`. Nothing else.

## Cause

`grafana/tabs/firewall.py:375-383` builds the organize transform as:

```
excludeByName: {..., "Value": true}
renameByName:  {"opnsense_instance": "Instance", "Value #A": "Last Update"}
override:      byName "Last Update" -> unit dateTimeAsIso
```

A **single-query Prometheus** table names its value field `Value`. That is the convention every other Prometheus table on this dashboard uses (panels 131, 132, 134, 137-141, 148, 357, 358, 362, 365-368, 613 and ~55 more all key `renameByName` on `Value`). `Value #A` is the **Loki** table convention — `grafana/builder.py:606`, `LOKI_TABLE_VALUE_FIELD`.

So here the real field `Value` is excluded, the `Value #A` rename matches nothing, the `Last Update` column never exists, and the `dateTimeAsIso` override is dead.

The `#112` exclude-vs-rename guard at `grafana/builder.py:460-466` misses it precisely because the rename key is spelled `Value #A` rather than `Value` — it has no reason to think the two are the same field.

This is the **exact class of bug #491 was opened to find**: valid manifest, passing tests, passing coverage gate, renders without error, and shows nothing.

## Fix

Drop `"Value"` from `excludes` and key the rename on `"Value"`, i.e. match sibling `panel-365` "ACME Last Renewal" exactly.

Worth also extending the `#112` guard to flag a `Value #X` rename key on a single-expr **Prometheus** table, since that spelling can only ever be a mistake there.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `panel-146` renders a `Last Update` column with an ISO timestamp
- [ ] Builder guard rejects a `Value #X` matcher on a single-query Prometheus table
- [ ] `make dashboard` + `make grafana-check` green

Found by the #491 rendering sweep.
