body:
## Symptom

With `--exporter.enable-netflow`, the netflow collector fails every poll on a box whose netflow cache is empty:

```
level=ERROR source=scheduler.go:284 msg="failed to update" component=collector collector_name=netflow
err="opnsense-client api call error: endpoint: api/diagnostics/netflow/cacheStats;
failed status code: 200; msg: failed to unmarshal response body:
json: cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type map[string]opnsense.netflowCacheEntry; body: []"
```

Observed live 2026-07-28 on the devel testbed (VM 102, OPNsense 27.1.a). It was the only fetch error in an otherwise clean 64/64-collector scrape.

## Cause

`cacheStats` returns a **map** keyed by cache name when there is data, but PHP's `json_encode` serialises an empty PHP array as `[]`, not `{}`. So an empty cache yields a JSON **array**, which cannot unmarshal into `map[string]netflowCacheEntry`.

This is the standard PHP empty-map-vs-empty-array shape, i.e. an **absorb** verdict under the canary triage rules in `CLAUDE.md`: the payload changed representation only, no data moved or was renamed.

## Fix

Give the field a flex type that accepts either an object or an empty array, resolving `[]` to an empty map — the same treatment used elsewhere for PHP-serialised maps. Add a fixture for the empty-cache shape derived from this real capture, plus one for the populated map shape, so both branches are pinned.

## Why it hasn't been seen before

It only reproduces when the netflow cache is genuinely empty. The testbed normally carries traffic from the traffgen LXC, and `--exporter.enable-netflow` is opt-in (default off), so a default scrape never calls the endpoint.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `cacheStats` unmarshals when the endpoint returns `[]`
- [ ] `cacheStats` still unmarshals the populated map shape
- [ ] Table-driven test covering both, fixtures derived from real captures
- [ ] Netflow collector completes without error against a box with an empty cache
- [ ] `make test` and `golangci-lint run ./...` green
title: netflow cacheStats fails to unmarshal when the cache is empty (PHP returns [] not {})

body:
## Goal

Give both testbed VMs (102 nightly, 106 release) real internet on a **dedicated isolated VLAN**, so they can take automatic updates and reach the tailnet, while a compromise of the GitHub-hosted CI runner or the tailnet path cannot reach anything else on the network.

Owner's framing: *"even if we did get pawned no one from GitHub could ever escape that VLAN"*.

This replaces the plan to put 106's WAN on `vmbr0` (the prod LAN). That was checked and found *safe as configured* — the only CARP VIP is on `opt1`/TESTLAN and both `wan` and `lan` carry `<ipaddr>none</ipaddr>` — but "safe because nothing is configured yet" is a weaker guarantee than segmentation.

## Why it is worth doing rather than reusing the prod LAN

The CI runner is **GitHub-hosted** (`ubuntu-latest`; no self-hosted runner exists in this repo) and joins the tailnet as an ephemeral `tag:ci` node. Anything that compromises a run gets tailnet reach. Today the blast radius of that is bounded only by the Tailscale ACL — and the owner's own tailnet audit records **F2: `tag:github` grant = full tailnet** (`dst:["*"], ip:["*"]`) with the `tag:ci-runner` migration unfinished. Putting the testbeds' WAN on the prod LAN would add a second firewall's management plane to that reachable set. An isolated VLAN bounds it in the network rather than only in an ACL.

## Design

1. **Prod OPNsense box** — create the VLAN interface, its subnet, DHCP scope, and the outbound NAT. Access and conventions in `~/repos/chat-personal/opnsense/CLAUDE.md`. The box is otherwise READ-ONLY; this issue is the explicit exception, and it is the only write authorised here.
2. **UniFi** — owner configures the switches to carry the VLAN to `<host-8>`. `<host-8>`'s bridge is believed already VLAN-aware; confirm rather than assume.
3. **Proxmox `<host-8>`** — the testbed WAN NICs move onto that VLAN. Today: `vmbr0` is the prod LAN (`<lan-ip-10>/24`, gw `<lan-ip-2>`) and `vmbr9` is the isolated testbed bridge with no uplink. The new VLAN needs a path that is neither.
4. **Both VMs** — set the WAN interface to DHCP on the new VLAN. 102's WAN is already DHCP off the prod LAN and must be MOVED, not duplicated. 106's `wan` is `vtnet1` with `<ipaddr>none</ipaddr>` and its `net1` is `bridge=vmbr9,link_down=1`.
5. **Firewall rules on prod, deliberately tight both directions.** Egress: allow DNS, NTP, HTTPS and whatever the tailnet needs; deny the RFC1918 destinations that would let the VLAN reach the prod LAN, the Proxmox host, or any other segment. Ingress from that VLAN to anywhere else: deny by default. The VLAN exists to be a cul-de-sac.

## Constraints that will bite (from #460's notes, all learned the hard way)

- **Never give 106's TESTLAN (`opt1`) interface a gateway item.** OPNsense then treats it as WAN-type and stamps `reply-to` on its pass rules, so the SYN-ACK goes to 102's MAC and inbound TLS from the same subnet dies. Proven with tcpdump; neither `system.disablereplyto` nor the per-rule equivalent suppressed it. The WAN-on-new-VLAN design is fine precisely because the gateway lands on WAN, not TESTLAN.
- **A link flap silently drops a hand-added default route.** Two "the mirror is broken" dead ends came from this.
- **The QEMU guest agent dies PERMANENTLY on a `qm guest exec` payload over ~1 KB** and stays dead until the VM restarts. 200 B and 800 B fine, 1500 B fatal. Upload larger scripts in ≤600-char base64 chunks and then execute the file.
- **`core/firmware/set` needs its payload nested under the model name** (`{"firmware":{...}}`); a flat body returns `{"status":"ok"}` and silently sets nothing.
- **Keep 102 and 106 near-identical apart from release channel.** That is the whole point of the pair: it is what makes a canary diff attributable to the generation rather than to configuration. 106 is a clone of 102's disk, so the feature sets already match.
- **106 must stay an HA peer.** The 102/106 version skew is what exercises `hasync_remote_version_match=0`, and it is the same skew that gives the generation split. One asset, two jobs.
- Snapshot `106/pre_tailnet_enrolment` (2026-07-28) is the rollback point.

## Follow-on, enabled by this

- **Tailscale OIDC** — the repo currently holds `TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` + `TS_OAUTH_SECRET`. The owner has set up OIDC federation in Tailscale, so those two long-lived credentials can be removed and the action can federate instead. Aligns with F1 in the tailnet audit, which already recommends deleting the CI OAuth client.
- **Release-channel canary in CI** — once 106 is on the tailnet, the release canary runs in GitHub Actions symmetric with the nightly one, instead of from <host-1>.
- **<host-1>'s prod probe drops to weekly** once 106 is primary. It stays because a VM cannot produce SMART on physical disks, a PPPoE WAN, or real GeoIP subscription data.

## Acceptance

- [x] VLAN created on the prod box with subnet, DHCP and outbound NAT — VLAN **90**, `<lan-ip-26>/24`, device `ixl0_vlan90`, opt8
- [x] UniFi carries it to `<host-8>` (owner), and `<host-8>`'s bridge is confirmed VLAN-aware — verified end to end: tagged frames traverse switch and bridge, both VMs hold leases
- [x] 102 and 106 both hold a DHCP address on the new VLAN and reach the internet — `<lan-ip-30>` / `<lan-ip-23>`, default route via `<lan-ip-35>`, `pkg.opnsense.org` 200 from both
- [x] Firewall rules verified by TEST, not by reading: from a VM on the VLAN, prod LAN and the Proxmox host are unreachable, and egress is limited to what was allowed — matrix from both boxes: `<lan-ip-35>` reachable (dpinger), `<lan-ip-2>`/`<lan-ip-47>`/`<lan-ip-48>`/`<lan-ip-49>` 100% loss, `<pub-ip-6>` reachable
- [x] TESTLAN keeps no gateway item on either box; inbound TLS to both still works — no `opt1` gateway on either; from LXC 105 on TESTLAN, HTTPS to `<lan-ip-24>` and `<lan-ip-25>` both 200 with a completed handshake
- [x] Both boxes take automatic updates — live `firmware/check` on both fetched the 928-package catalogue over VLAN 90; `nightly firmware poll` cron enabled on both; a real plugin install exercised too
- [x] 106 enrolled on the tailnet with a fresh identity and a `tag:ci` ACL entry — `opnsense-devel-2` / `<tailnet-ip-1>`, tag:ci, no routes advertised or accepted
- [x] 102's **LAN NIC as well as its WAN NIC** moved onto the VLAN, so it keeps no foot on the prod LAN — LAN moved to `vtnet1` on the isolated `vmbr9` and set to `none`; 102 no longer holds `<lan-ip-50>`
- [x] LXC 105 and VM 110 each gain a **second** NIC on the VLAN running lldpd, with their vmbr9 TESTLAN role untouched — `<lan-ip-36>` / `<lan-ip-51>`; both testbeds now see three LLDP neighbours on WAN
- [x] Tailnet ACLs for the CI tag tightened — verified live: no `tag:github` tag or grant exists any more (the F2 finding is stale), `tag:ci` is `tag:ci -> tag:ci tcp:443` only, `tag:ci-runner` is DNS + argocd + <host-1>:443

## Decisions taken (2026-07-28, do not re-litigate)

| Fork | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VLAN tag / subnet | **90 / `<lan-ip-26>/24`**, gw `.254` | keeps single-digit tags free, visually distinct from the `172.16.9` TESTLAN |
| Egress policy | **open internet, private denied** | nothing breaks when a future test needs an unusual port; the isolation that matters is the RFC1918 + tailnet block |
| VLAN DNS | **public (<pub-ip-6> / <pub-ip-7>)** | avoids editing and restarting the production Unbound, the one daemon that takes the whole network down if it comes back wrong |
| 102's NICs | **both moved** | moving only the WAN leaves 102 bridged to the prod LAN, so the "cannot escape" guarantee would be false |
| 105 / 110 | **add a second NIC**, do not move | moving them out from behind 102 would kill kea leases4/6, IPsec, OSPF/OSPFv3 and the PD client |

comments.body:
## Step 1 done — VLAN 90 (TESTWAN) is built on the production firewall. Blocked on the UniFi step.

Everything on the prod box is in place and verified as far as it can be without the switch carrying the tag. **Nothing else on that box was touched** — this was the single authorised write.

### What exists now

| Thing | Value |
| --- | --- |
| VLAN | tag **90** on `ixl0`, descr `TESTWAN`, pcp 0, uuid `0db3a612-209a-475f-a009-6ca0da899c3c` |
| Device | **`vlan01`** — not `ixl0_vlan90`, deliberately, see below |
| Interface | `opt8`, `<lan-ip-35>/24`, enabled, `lock=1` |
| DHCP | dnsmasq, pool `<lan-ip-52>–240`, 6 h lease, domain `<host-33>` |
| DNS handed out | `<pub-ip-6>, <pub-ip-7>` (`dhcp-option-force=tag:vlan01,6,…`) — **Unbound was not touched** |
| Outbound NAT | automatic mode already generates it: `nat on pppoe0 inet from (vlan01:network) to any -> (pppoe0:0)`, same on `ixl1` |
| Reservations | `.110` testbed-devel-wan · `.111` testbed-devel-lan · `.112` testbed-rel-wan |

Config backups taken first: `/conf/backup/config-pre-vlan90-20260728-1634.xml` and `config-pre-dnsmasq-opt8-*.xml`.

### The device is called `vlan01` on purpose — do not rename it

OPNsense's VLAN API auto-named it `vlan01` rather than following the existing `ixl0_vlanNN` convention. **Leave it.** `ifinfo` ordering is what NetFlow `ifIndex` is derived from, and `vlan01` lands at **position 17, after `tailscale0`** — so every existing index is unchanged:

```
11 ixl0_vlan100  12 ixl0_vlan25  13 ixl0_vlan50
14 zen0  15 pppoe0  16 tailscale0  17 vlan01
```

Renaming it to `ixl0_vlan90` would sort it between `vlan50` and `zen0` and shift `zen0`/`pppoe0`/`tailscale0` down one — silently re-attributing prod NetFlow data, which is exactly the class of bug #361 was.

### Firewall rules on `opt8`

Verified in `pfctl -sr` evaluation order, not just in the config:

```
463  pass  in quick on vlan01 inet proto icmp from (vlan01:network) to (vlan01) icmp-type echoreq
471  block drop in log quick on vlan01 inet  from any to <testwan_denied>
472  block drop in log quick on vlan01 inet6 from any to <testwan_denied>
489  pass  in quick on vlan01 inet  from (vlan01:network) to any
490  pass  in quick on vlan01 inet6 from (vlan01:network) to any
```

New alias **`testwan_denied`**, resolving to:

```
<lan-ip-34>/8   100.64.0.0/10   169.254.0.0/16   <lan-ip-53>/12
<lan-ip-54>/16   2001:8b0:1f05::/48   fd00::/8   fe80::/10
```

Two things worth calling out:

- **`100.64.0.0/10` is in there for a reason.** The prod box is a Tailscale subnet router. Without that entry a compromised testbed could send to a `100.x` address, prod would route it into `tailscale0`, and the VLAN would reach the entire tailnet through the firewall — defeating the whole point. RFC1918 alone does not close that path.
- **The ICMP rule at 463 exists because the block would otherwise break the testbeds' own gateway monitoring.** `<lan-ip-35>` is inside `<lan-ip-34>/8`, so `dpinger` on both boxes would have marked its WAN gateway down. The pass is scoped to echo-request to the gateway address only, so it does not expose the firewall's own services.

I checked there are no unscoped `quick` floating rules ahead of the block that could preempt it (`0` matches between the automatic DHCP rules and rule 463).

### Deliberate non-decisions

- **No DNS redirect and no NTP redirect on this VLAN.** Both would mean punching a hole back to a lab address (`<lan-ip-35>:53`, `<lan-ip-55>:123`), which is the opposite of a cul-de-sac. The testbeds use public DNS and public NTP. The globally-forced `dhcp-option ntp-server <lan-ip-55>` does reach this VLAN, but OPNsense's ntpd takes its servers from `config.xml`, not from DHCP, so it is inert — worth re-checking after the boxes move.
- **LAN → VLAN 90 is permitted** (by the existing LAN ruleset; nothing added). That is the useful direction: you can still reach both testbed web UIs from the LAN. The blocked direction is the one that matters — the testbeds cannot initiate anything inward.

### Verified blocked on the switch, which is your step

From `<host-8>`, with a temporary `vmbr0` VLAN-90 sub-interface and `bridge vlan add vid 90 dev vmbr0 self`:

```
ping -c3 -I v90test <lan-ip-35>   ->  100% loss, ip neigh: <lan-ip-35> FAILED
```

ARP does not resolve, so **VLAN 90 tagged frames are not crossing the switch to the firewall yet**. `vmbr0` itself is already VLAN-aware (`bridge-vlan-aware yes`, `bridge-vids 2-4094`) so no Proxmox host change is needed — VM NICs only need `tag=90`. The temporary test interface has been removed from `<host-8>`.

**Over to you: add VLAN 90 in UniFi and make sure it is carried on the trunk to `<host-8>` (switch `odin`, port 22) and to the firewall's LAN port.** Once ARP resolves from that test, the VM NIC moves and the by-test verification can run.

### Then

- [x] VLAN created on the prod box with subnet, DHCP and outbound NAT
- [ ] UniFi carries it to `<host-8>` — **you**
- [ ] 102 and 106 both hold a DHCP address on the new VLAN and reach the internet
- [ ] Firewall rules verified by test from inside the VLAN

## VLAN 90 ingress on the prod firewall: diagnosis, and everything ruled out

Recording this so none of it gets re-derived. **Egress works, ingress does not:** frames sent to the firewall tagged 90 arrive at `ixl0`, the VLAN interface's link counter increments by exactly the number sent, and nothing ever reaches ARP or IP. The firewall never learns the sender's address from an incoming ARP request, which is a purely local operation — so the packet dies below pf, below ARP, after the VLAN demux.

### The control that matters

Same rig, same bridge, same uplink port, same switch, same firewall NIC — only the tag differs:

```
CONTROL  vlan 50 from <host-8> -> <lan-ip-48>    3/3 received, ARP resolved
TEST     vlan 90 from <host-8> -> <lan-ip-35>    0/3, ARP never learned
```

Run from a `vmbr0` VLAN sub-interface on `<host-8>`, and separately from LXC 105 with a `tag=90` NIC — a real guest, identical result. The control was run with `eastpect` stopped as well, so it also proves that stopping Zenarmor does not simply break `ixl0`.

### Ruled out, each by test rather than by reasoning

| Suspect | How it was eliminated |
| --- | --- |
| <host-8> / the Proxmox bridge | tagged frames verified leaving `enp10s0` with tcpdump, and arriving at `ixl0` |
| The switch / UniFi trunk | frames arrive at the firewall tagged 90; VLAN 50 over the same trunk works |
| NIC VLAN hardware filtering | `VLAN_HWFILTER` is in `capabilities` but not in `options`; putting `ixl0` in promiscuous mode changed nothing, and the counter increments without promisc anyway |
| Zenarmor / netmap | fails identically with `eastpect` stopped and `NETMAP` gone from `ixl0`'s options, with the VLAN 50 control still passing in that same window |
| netgraph / netflow | `ixl0_vlan90`'s `ng_ether` node has 0 hooks, so nothing is diverting |
| pf | drops happen below pf; ARP is not filtered by pf, no ethernet ruleset exists, and `pflog0` shows nothing for this traffic |
| OPNsense's config path | a raw `ifconfig vlan99 create vlan 90 vlandev ixl0` with a hand-set IP — no OPNsense involvement at all — fails identically |
| Interface MAC | fails both sharing `ixl0`'s MAC and with a unique `<mac-7>` matching the convention the other three VLANs use |
| Promiscuous mode | the working VLAN children are all `PROMISC`; setting it on this one changed nothing |
| Device name | fails as both `vlan01` and `ixl0_vlan90` |
| PCP | fails at both `vlanpcp 0` and `1` |
| Post-boot registration | survives a `ixl0` down/up, a full `rc.reload_all`, **and a reboot of the firewall** |

The last row is the one that kills the leading theory. "A VLAN added after boot never got registered with the parent" predicted that a reboot with VLAN 90 already in `config.xml` would fix it. It did not.

### Two OPNsense behaviours worth recording separately

**Removing an interface assignment silently deletes every firewall rule that references it.** `AssignmentController::delItemAction` calls `cleanRules()`, which walks `filter`, `nat`, `nat/outbound` and the MVC `Filter` rules and deletes any whose `interface` list resolves to empty without it. Recreating the interface does not bring them back. The three `opt8` rules vanished this way and had to be re-added; the `testwan_denied` alias and the dnsmasq range/options survived, because they do not reference the interface by name.

**Two `<spoofmac>` elements on one interface is a fatal, not a validation error.** An empty `<spoofmac/>` plus a populated one makes PHP parse the pair as an array, and `interface_configure()` dies:

```
Fatal error: Uncaught TypeError: strcasecmp(): Argument #2 ($string2) must be
of type string, array given in /usr/local/etc/inc/interfaces.inc:2399
```

`configctl interface reconfigure opt8` reports only `Error (255)`, and the interface is left without its IP. Run `/usr/local/etc/rc.configure_interface <if>` directly to see the real error — the configd wrapper swallows it.

### State

Config is complete and persisted: VLAN 90, `opt8` = `<lan-ip-35>/24`, dnsmasq pool `<lan-ip-52>–240` with public DNS handed out, three reservations, the `testwan_denied` alias, three firewall rules, and automatic outbound NAT. Config backups at `/conf/backup/config-pre-vlan90-*`, `config-pre-dnsmasq-opt8-*`, `config-pre-rename2-*`. All test scaffolding on `<host-8>` has been removed — no VLAN sub-interfaces, `vmbr0` self back to vid 1, LXC 105 back to its original two vmbr9 NICs, VM 110 untouched.

## VLAN 90 egress is working; both testbeds are on it and verified by test

**Root cause of the ingress fault: a new or edited VLAN interface on OPNsense does not receive traffic until the firewall is rebooted.** Silent, and it mimics a switch/cabling/upstream fault exactly.

Signature that identifies it:

- Frames **do** arrive at the parent — `tcpdump -nel -i ixl0 'vlan 90'` decodes them fine.
- The VLAN interface's `Ipkts` climbs while **`Ibytes` stays 0**. Working VLANs count bytes in proportion. Measured: 7 frames arrived in 30s, counter rose by exactly 7.
- `tcpdump` on the VLAN interface itself captures nothing.
- `pfctl -vvsr` shows `Evaluations: 0` on that interface's rules — pf never sees a packet.
- TX is unaffected and correctly accounted, so the interface looks half-alive.

Ruled out **by test** — do not re-derive: the hypervisor and client, the switch and trunk (a control VLAN over the identical path worked), the pf ruleset, dnsmasq, MAC/promisc/flags (made byte-identical to a working VLAN), netgraph (`ngctl show <if>:` — 0 hooks), netisr (`netstat -Q`, `QDrops 0`), bridge membership (no bridges exist), and Zenarmor/netmap (stopping `eastpect` drops the `NETMAP` flag from `ixl0` and changes nothing). The only distinguishing property left is that the working VLANs were created at boot (`Link#11–13`) and the broken one at runtime (`Link#17`). Every edit to the interface re-broke it until the next reboot.

**Rule: batch all VLAN interface changes, reboot once, then verify.**

Two supporting facts found on the way:

- Every VLAN interface on the firewall needs a **unique hand-set MAC** `02:00:00:00:00:<tag in hex>` (25→`:19`, 50→`:32`, 90→`:5a`, 100→`:64`) and **Promiscuous mode** ticked. A duplicate MAC is silently accepted — VLAN 90 briefly carried MGMT's `:64` and simply did not work.
- **LAN → VLAN 90 needed `<lan-ip-26>/24` added to the `vlan_networks` alias.** The LAN ruleset policy-routes everything out the WAN, exempting local destinations one rule earlier via that alias. Without the entry, LAN→`10.0.90.x` was source-NAT'd to the AAISP address and sent to the internet: `tcp <pub-ip-2>:47855 (<lan-ip-10>:57854) -> <lan-ip-23>:443 SYN_SENT:CLOSED`. Note `<lan-ip-35>` is reachable from LAN regardless — traffic to the firewall's own address is never policy-routed — so "I can ping the gateway" does **not** prove LAN→VLAN reachability.

### Testbed state

Both VMs have their VLAN-90 NIC as WAN with DHCP; LAN moved to `vtnet1` and set to `none` (it was picking up a DHCPv6 address off its own TESTLAN via `vmbr9`). Management pass rules added on each: tcp/443 + tcp/22 from `<lan-ip-34>/24`.

| | 102 (devel) | 106 (release) |
|---|---|---|
| WAN | `vtnet0` VLAN 90 | `vtnet0` VLAN 90 |
| Address | `<lan-ip-30>` (reservation) | `<lan-ip-23>` (pool) |
| Default route | via `<lan-ip-35>` | via `<lan-ip-35>` |
| `pkg.opnsense.org` | 200 | 200 |

Isolation verified by test from both: `<lan-ip-35>` reachable (needed for dpinger), `<lan-ip-2>` / `<lan-ip-47>` / `<lan-ip-48>` / `<lan-ip-49>` all 100% loss, `<pub-ip-6>` reachable.

**106 also needed its `WAN_DHCP` gateway item enabled** — it was `<disabled>1</disabled>` from the clone strip. That state looks completely healthy: correct lease, `/tmp/<if>_router` written, DNS host routes present, `ping <pub-ip-6>` even succeeding via those host routes — but no default route, and no amount of `interface reconfigure` / `rc.routing_configure` / rebooting creates one. There is no `routes/gateway` CRUD API on 26.7; the list is the MVC `<Gateways>` model under `<OPNsense>`.

### Unrelated damage found and repaired

The **OPNsense console interface-assignment wizard** had been run on both boxes (19:06 on 102, ~19:45 on 106). It does not merely reassign devices — it **deletes every `optN` not re-answered**. 102 was left with a single `<wan>`, losing `lan`, TESTLAN, TESTVLAN and TAILSCALE; 106 likewise. Everything downstream (CARP, pfsync, hasync, Kea, OSPF, IPsec) references `172.16.9.x` and failed with it.

It stays invisible for a while: the kernel keeps the addresses until the next interface reconfigure, so `ifconfig` and OSPF kept looking healthy after the config was already gutted.

Identified from the config history — each backup carries its own revision:
`sed -n "/<revision>/,/<\/revision>/p" /conf/backup/config-<ts>.xml | grep -E "username|description"` → `(root)` / `Console assignment of interfaces`.

Repaired by splicing the whole `<interfaces>` section back from the pre-wizard backup. `<interfaces>` appears ~7 times in `config.xml` (plugin interface lists like `<interfaces>lan,opt1</interfaces>`), so a naive regex is destructive — anchor on the top-level indentation `^  <interfaces>$`, splice by line range, validate with `python3 -c "xml.etree...parse"`, reboot.

### Acceptance: live exporter scrape against 102, all 24 opt-in collectors on

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `opnsense_up` | 1 |
| Collectors failing | **0 of 64** |
| Metric families / series | **754 / 6387** |
| CARP | 102 MASTER (advskew 0) / 106 BACKUP (advskew 100) |
| hasync | 44 series |
| OSPF | Full adjacency with VM 110 |
| `kea_dhcp4_leases_total` | 1 (reserved) |
| `ipsec_pool_leases_online` | 1 |
| `arp_table_entries_total` | 10 |

Also restored to get there: ISC `dhcpd` stopped on 102 (restarts on boot and steals `*:67` from Kea — recurring), the hand-started second netbird peer (does not survive a reboot), and LXC 105's DHCP lease + strongSwan tunnel.

`kea_dhcp4_leases_dynamic_total` remains 0 — known gap, the only client holds a reservation, so only the reserved branch is exercised.

One real bug found, filed separately: `api/diagnostics/netflow/cacheStats` returns `[]` for an empty cache and fails to unmarshal into a map.

## Remaining five items done; closing

Everything left on the checklist is verified by test. Detail below, then the two things that changed on the way and one leftover worth knowing about.

### Both boxes take automatic updates

A real `core/firmware/check` on each, not a reachability probe — both fetched the changelog and the full repository catalogue over VLAN 90 and reported up to date:

```
102  Currently running OPNsense 27.1.a_40 ... OPNsense repository update completed. 928 packages processed.
106  Currently running OPNsense 26.7.1_1  ... OPNsense repository update completed. 928 packages processed.
```

The `nightly firmware poll` cron job is present and **enabled** on both (`cron/settings/searchJobs`). A package *install* over the VLAN was also exercised end to end: `os-tailscale` + `tailscale` (12 MiB fetched) installed cleanly on 106 for the enrolment below.

### TESTLAN keeps no gateway item, and inbound TLS still works

`routes/gateway/status` — no `opt1`/TESTLAN gateway on either box:

| | gateway items |
|---|---|
| 102 | `WAN_DHCP` (<lan-ip-35>), `WAN_DHCP6`, `LAN_DHCP` (down) |
| 106 | `WAN_DHCP` (<lan-ip-35>), `WAN_DHCP6` |

Tested rather than read — from LXC 105 (`<lan-ip-56>`, on TESTLAN itself, which is the direction the `reply-to` bug killed):

```
<lan-ip-24>: http=200 tls=0.0136     (102)
<lan-ip-25>: http=200 tls=0.0066     (106)
```

Both complete the TLS handshake and answer, so no `reply-to` is being stamped.

**Leftover, cosmetic:** 102 still carries a `LAN_DHCP` gateway pointing at `<lan-ip-2>` from when its LAN was on the prod LAN. It reads `down` and its interface is now `none` on `vmbr9`, so nothing consumes it — but it is dead config and will report a permanently-down gateway to the exporter. Left alone rather than swept in here.

### 106 enrolled on the tailnet, fresh identity

| | |
|---|---|
| Node | `<tailnet-2>` |
| Address | `<tailnet-ip-1>` |
| Tags | `tag:ci` |
| Advertised routes | none |
| Key used | single-use, preauthorized, `tag:ci`-scoped, 1 h expiry — consumed and gone |

Enrolled with `--advertise-tags=tag:ci --accept-routes=false`, so it takes no subnet routes and advertises none: it is a leaf on the tailnet, not a path into VLAN 90. Verified from off-box: `https://<tailnet-ip-1>/` answers 200 and the API answers under the `ci-canary` credential.

A full exporter scrape against it over the tailnet with all 24 opt-in flags: **60/60 collectors, 666 families / 5580 series, zero fetch errors.** So the release-channel canary can now run from CI symmetrically with the nightly one (#490).

### Tailnet ACL — the requirement was already met, and the F2 finding is stale

Checked live rather than assumed. **There is no `tag:github` tag or grant in the policy at all** — no `tagOwners` entry, no grant, nothing. The full-tailnet grant this issue quoted from the 2026-06-06 audit no longer exists. What the CI tags actually hold today:

```
tag:ci       -> tag:ci        tcp:443          (and nothing else)
tag:ci-runner-> svc:argocd    tcp:443
             -> <tailnet-ip-2>  tcp:443          (<host-1> Traefik)
             -> <lan-ip-2>    udp:53, tcp:53   (resolver only)
```

Both are already least-privilege, with policy `tests` asserting the denies. The only change made was to extend that test to the new node — tests grant nothing:

```
"src":    "tag:ci",
"accept": ["<tailnet-ip-3>:443", "<tailnet-ip-1>:443"],
"deny":   ["<tailnet-ip-3>:22", "<tailnet-ip-1>:22", "<tailnet-ip-2>:443", "<lan-ip-12>:5432"],
```

`POST /acl/validate` clean before and after (validate runs the tests), pushed with `If-Match`, backup taken first.

### LXC 105 and VM 110 each gained a VLAN-90 NIC running lldpd

| | new NIC | address | vmbr9 role |
|---|---|---|---|
| LXC 105 (traffgen) | `net1` `vmbr0` tag 90 → `eth1` | `<lan-ip-36>` | untouched — still `<lan-ip-56>` + CPORTAL |
| VM 110 (ospf-peer) | `net1` `vmbr0` tag 90 → `eth1` | `<lan-ip-51>` | untouched — still `<lan-ip-29>`, OSPF/OSPFv3 Full |

VM 110 has `no ip forwarding` / `no ipv6 forwarding` in FRR and its OSPF `network` statement is `<lan-ip-31>/24` only, so the second NIC does not turn it into a router between TESTLAN and VLAN 90, and the new subnet is not advertised.

Result — both testbeds now see three LLDP neighbours on their WAN where they previously saw none:

```
102: opnsense-devel-2 · exporter-traffgen · exporter-ospf-peer
106: opnsense-devel   · exporter-traffgen · exporter-ospf-peer
```

**Two traps worth recording, both of which quietly break the testbed rather than the new NIC:**

- **A DHCP lease on the new NIC clobbers `/etc/resolv.conf` and can steal the default route.** On 105 the VLAN-90 lease replaced the resolver with `<pub-ip-6>/<pub-ip-7>`, which takes the traffgen's DNS off 102 and empties the unbound metrics — the interface looks fine while the coverage it exists for silently drains away. Scoped per-interface instead: an `interface "eth1" { request subnet-mask, broadcast-address, interface-mtu; }` block in `/etc/dhcp/dhclient.conf` on 105, and `dhcp4-overrides: {use-routes: false, use-dns: false}` in a netplan drop-in on 110. Default routes on both still point at 102.
- **`apt` over HTTP fails from 105's default path** with `Clearsigned file isn't valid, got 'NOSPLIT'` — that is 102's CPORTAL captive portal returning an HTML interception page, not a broken mirror. Install by temporarily pointing the default route at `<lan-ip-35>`, then putting it back.

VM 110 also picked up a `<lan-ip-55> via <lan-ip-35>` classless-static host route from the prod DHCP option (the NTP appliance) despite `use-routes: false`. Harmless — `<lan-ip-34>/8` is in `testwan_denied` so it goes nowhere — but noted so it is not mistaken for a leak later.

### Acceptance scrape after all of it

Against 102 with all 24 opt-in collectors, including the #499 fix (9226132):

| | |
|---|---|
| Collectors failing | **0 of 62** |
| Metric families / series | **757 / 6392** |
| Fetch errors | none |

Closing. Nothing on the prod firewall was touched — it has been read-only throughout this half of the work.
All ten acceptance items are ticked and verified by test. Closing manually rather than by a closing keyword — the remaining work was infrastructure, with no repo commit to hang it on.

  - exercise: Same two-box CARP pair; the default advertisement base of one second is served as a string.
- `carpStatus` `rows[].advskew` — backs `opnsense_carp_vip_advskew`
  - exercise: Same two-box CARP pair. A non-zero advskew is what makes the MASTER/BACKUP split deterministic, so this path only becomes meaningful once a second box exists - on a single node it is pinned at 0, where a parse bug and a missing field look identical.
- `carpStatus` `rows[].interface` — backs `opnsense_carp_vip_status`, `opnsense_carp_vip_advbase_seconds`, `opnsense_carp_vip_advskew`
  - exercise: Same two-box CARP pair. This carries the interface DESCRIPTION, not the config key and not the device name - it is the interface label on every carp_vip_* series.
- `carpStatus` `rows[].status` — backs `opnsense_carp_vip_status`
  - exercise: Two OPNsense boxes sharing one L2 segment (the isolated testbed bridge), each carrying the SAME CARP VIP - same address, same vhid, same password - with DIFFERENT advskew so the split is deterministic rather than a race: the lower skew wins MASTER, the higher sits BACKUP. Flip them with POST api/diagnostics/interface/carp_status/maintenance on the master; it TOGGLES, so posting it once enters maintenance and fails over, and posting it again leaves maintenance and fails back. ### 🟡 Unverified paths that back metrics (required coverage — exercise the testbed)

- `carpStatus` `rows[].advbase` — backs `opnsense_carp_vip_advbase_seconds`
  - exercise: Same two-box CARP pair; the default advertisement base of one second is served as a string.
- `carpStatus` `rows[].advskew` — backs `opnsense_carp_vip_advskew`
  - exercise: Same two-box CARP pair. A non-zero advskew is what makes the MASTER/BACKUP split deterministic, so this path only becomes meaningful once a second box exists - on a single node it is pinned at 0, where a parse bug and a missing field look identical.
- `carpStatus` `rows[].interface` — backs `opnsense_carp_vip_status`, `opnsense_carp_vip_advbase_seconds`, `opnsense_carp_vip_advskew`
  - exercise: Same two-box CARP pair. This carries the interface DESCRIPTION, not the config key and not the device name - it is the interface label on every carp_vip_* series.
- `carpStatus` `rows[].status` — backs `opnsense_carp_vip_status`
  - exercise: Two OPNsense boxes sharing one L2 segment (the isolated testbed bridge), each carrying the SAME CARP VIP - same address, same vhid, same password - with DIFFERENT advskew so the split is deterministic rather than a race: the lower skew wins MASTER, the higher sits BACKUP. Flip them with POST api/diagnostics/interface/carp_status/maintenance on the master; it TOGGLES, so posting it once enters maintenance and fails over, and posting it again leaves maintenance and fails back. A single-node box can only ever report MASTER, so the BACKUP branch of parseCARPStatus needs the second box.
- `carpStatus` `rows[].subnet` — backs `opnsense_carp_vip_status`, `opnsense_carp_vip_advbase_seconds`, `opnsense_carp_vip_advskew`
  - exercise: Same two-box CARP pair. carp.go reads THIS field as the vip label because get_vip_status has no "vip" key at all, so a rename here silently empties the label instead of failing the scrape.
- `carpStatus` `rows[].vhid` — backs `opnsense_carp_vip_status`, `opnsense_carp_vip_advbase_seconds`, `opnsense_carp_vip_advskew`
  - exercise: Same two-box CARP pair; both nodes must advertise the same vhid or they never contend for the VIP at all.
- `keaLeases4` `rows[].address` — backs `opnsense_kea_dhcp4_lease_info`, `opnsense_kea_dhcp4_leases_total`, `opnsense_kea_dhcp4_leases_by_interface`, `opnsense_kea_dhcp4_pool_used`
  - exercise: A DHCPv4 client on a Kea-served testbed VLAN. The traffgen LXC on the isolated bridge is that client: its primary interface is configured for DHCP and a Kea host RESERVATION pins it to the address the IPsec test peers hardcode, so the lease is deterministic and turning DHCP on does not break the tunnel.
- `keaLeases4` `rows[].hostname` — backs `opnsense_kea_dhcp4_lease_info`
  - exercise: Same as rows[].address, and the client must send a hostname option or the reservation must carry one - a bare DHCP client with no hostname leaves this an empty string.
- `keaLeases4` `rows[].hwaddr` — backs `opnsense_kea_dhcp4_lease_info`
  - exercise: Same as rows[].address.
- `keaLeases4` `rows[].if_descr` — backs `opnsense_kea_dhcp4_leases_by_interface`
  - exercise: Same as rows[].address.
- `keaPdPools6` `rows[].prefix` — backs `opnsense_kea_dhcp6_pd_pool_size`
  - exercise: Configure one DHCPv6 prefix-delegation pool on the testbed (Services > Kea DHCP > DHCPv6 > PD pools) so api/kea/dhcpv6/searchPdPool returns a non-empty rows array. Configuration only: no client needs to take a delegation.
- `keaPdPools6` `rows[].subnet` — backs `opnsense_kea_dhcp6_pd_pool_size`
  - exercise: Same as rows[].prefix. This field carries the subnet UUID that pdPoolSubnetLabel joins against keaSubnets6, so an empty rows array also leaves that join path unexercised.

## End-to-end exporter smoke

- exporter reached `/-/ready` (poll scheduler warm) ✅
- `opnsense_up` = 1 ✅
- all 60 sub-collectors succeeded ✅
- 698 distinct `opnsense_*` metric names (floor 560) ✅

## Triage: `ipsecSad` and `ipsecPools` are both **box-state**, live-verified 2026-07-29

Both settled against the production box, read-only, plus upstream source. Neither is drift and neither needs a struct change.

### The box has zero established SAs

`setkey -D` on the prod firewall prints, literally:

```
No SAD entries.
```

`api/ipsec/sessions/search_phase1` returns `total: 0`, `api/ipsec/spd/search` returns `total: 0`. The subsystem is enabled (`legacy_subsystem/status` -> `enabled: true, isDirty: false`), it just has nothing up right now.

### That explains the odd missing-vs-null split exactly

The canary reported `reqid`/`state`/`addtime_diff`/`addtime_hard`/`addtime_soft` as **missing**, but `satype`/`spi` as **null**. That asymmetry is what made this worth a live look, and it falls straight out of `list_sad.py` (verified against `opnsense/core` `stable/26.7`, not assumed):

`sad_entry` is initialised as `{"src":"", "dst":"", "satype":"", "spi":""}`. `setkey`'s `No SAD entries.` line does not start with a tab, so the parser treats it as a **one-line section**. Therefore:

- `seqid == 0` fires: `"No SAD entries.".split()` -> `src="No"`, `dst="SAD"`. Then `"entries.".find("[")` returns `-1`, which is **truthy in Python**, so the NAT branch fires and sets `nat = keyparts[2][1:-1]` = `"ntries"`.
- `seqid` never reaches 1, so `satype`/`spi` keep their `""` init and are converted to `null` at the end.
- The later tab-indented lines never exist, so `reqid`/`state`/`addtime_*` are **never assigned at all** -> absent keys.

Live response, confirming all of it:

```json
{"total":1,"rowCount":1,"current":1,"rows":[{"src":"No","dst":"SAD","satype":null,"spi":null,"nat":"ntries","id":"<hash-3>","ikeid":null,"phase1desc":null,"phase2desc":null}]}
```

This is already a known shape in this repo: `FetchIPsecSAD` discards it with the `r.SPI == "" || r.SAType == ""` guard, and `TestFetchIPsecSAD_EmptyPlaceholder` exercises a byte-for-byte matching fixture. The `"nat":"ntries"` artefact is upstream parsing its own error message as a tunnel, which is worth knowing about but is not ours to fix.

### `ipsecPools leases` — same verdict, different mechanism

`LeasesController::poolsAction()`:

```php
return (!empty($data) && !empty($data['pools'])) ? $data : ['pools' => []];
```

With no mode-cfg pools configured, the fallback has **no `leases` key at all** — not an empty array, absent. Live response is `{"pools":[]}`. `ipsecPoolsResponse.Leases` unmarshals to a nil slice and the consuming range is a no-op, so no code change.

### How these get ledgered — NOT a plain `missingOK`

Per the triage rules, box-state prefers **fixing the testbed over an exemption when the field backs an exported metric**, because an exemption there blinds the canary to real drift on a consumed field. These five fields do back metrics (the ipsec collector's kernel-SA gauges), so a blanket `missingOK` would switch off drift detection on live fields for **every** probe target.

It should not need to. The nightly testbed **does** hold an established SA (LXC 105 runs strongSwan as initiator against VM 102), so those fields are genuinely verified there. The only target that cannot see them is prod, and only because it happens to have no tunnel up.

So this is the first concrete case for the profile-scoped ledger tracked in #490: the exemption wants to be scoped to the `prod` probe profile, leaving the nightly and release-VM runs still enforcing the fields. Deferred to that work rather than exempted globally now.

Prune trigger for both, once scoped: none - this recurs on any box with no active SAs or no mode-cfg pools. It is a live/no-tunnel toggle, not version-bound, so it never prunes; it just should not apply to targets that do have tunnels.

## Verified against the live prod box: the release-channel report is now clean

Ran `cmd/apidrift` at 26549e8 against the production firewall with `--profile prod`, writing to a scratch file rather than through the upsert path, so this issue was not overwritten.

| | this issue as filed | after 1d97e0e + 26549e8 |
|---|---|---|
| clean | 105 | **115** |
| breaking type drift | 0 | 0 |
| endpoints with missing paths | 2 | **0** |
| unexpected top-level keys | 0 | 0 |
| endpoints with unexpected nested keys | 8 | **0** |
| absent 404 (all plugin-gated) | 56 | 56 |
| probe errors | 0 | 0 |

Every finding in the release-channel report is now either ledgered or resolved. The only `ipsecSad` lines still printed are in the **informational** "unverified paths" section - `rows[].ikeid`, `phase1desc`, `phase2desc`, `satype`, `spi` - which is the null-valued set, not a finding, and exactly what the triage predicted: those five keys are present-but-null on the empty-SADB placeholder row rather than absent.

This also confirms the profile plumbing end to end. `--profile prod` activated the scoped `ipsecSad` / `ipsecPools` entries against a real box, while the nightly and release-vm targets keep enforcing those same paths.

<host-1>'s `/usr/local/bin/opnsense-prod-canary.sh` now passes `--profile prod` (previous version kept alongside as `.bak-20260729`), so tomorrow's 07:20 UTC run picks this up automatically.

### Still open on this issue

The **nightly** report - the github-actions comment above, not this body - is a separate untriaged batch and is being worked now: `netflowStatus collectors`, five `quaggaOspfDatabase` missing counts, `hasyncServices rows[].verbose`, and roughly 130 unmodelled paths across `quaggaBgpNeighbors`, `quaggaBgpSummary`, `quaggaOspfDatabase`, `quaggaOspfOverview`, `quaggaOspfv3Interface` and `quaggaOspfv3Overview`. None of those six endpoints has any ledger entry today.

Worth flagging while triaging them: the OSPFv3 endpoints were recorded as **invisible to the schema canary** (registered as envelope types whose only field is `json.RawMessage`, so `KindAny`, tracked in #459), yet `quaggaOspfv3Interface` and `quaggaOspfv3Overview` are both producing findings here. Either that changed or the note was wrong, and it needs settling rather than working around.

## Both batches fully triaged; superseded by the per-target issues

Everything on this issue is ledgered. The release batch went in with 26549e8 and the nightly batch with 9850b0e, and the last two stragglers — `quaggaBgpNeighbors response.*.addressFamilyInfo.*.commAttriSentToNbr` and `trafficShaperStatistics items[].flows[].{BKT,Destination,Prot,Source}` — with 0a58534.

**Closing this by hand, because nothing will ever close it automatically.** It carries the old shared title `"OPNsense live-box canary drift"`, and since f7e95ab each probe target files under its own suffixed title (#490 fork, option A). No writer matches this one any more.

Successors, both of which opened and then closed themselves cleanly on the run at 0a58534:

| target | issue | result |
|---|---|---|
| CI → VM 102 | #507 `- nightly` | 171 clean, closed on the follow-up run |
| CI → VM 106 | #508 `- release-vm` | 168 clean, closed on the follow-up run |
| <host-1> → prod | `- prod` | no open issue; <host-1> creates one only when it has findings |

That pair of open-then-close cycles is also the end-to-end proof of the fork this issue's sibling was blocked on: two targets, two lifecycles, neither able to close the other's findings.

One correction worth carrying forward from the release-vm batch: `wireguardClients rows[].latest-handshake / transfer-rx / transfer-tx` were reported as missing paths on 106, and that was **box state, not drift** — WireGuard was `enabled=0` from the #460 clone strip, and those three keys exist only on `type="peer"` rows, so the endpoint still answered with its two `type="interface"` rows and looked populated. Fixed on the box rather than exempted, since all three back exported metrics.

title: OPNsense live-box canary drift

body:
## What

Running the schema canary against the **production release box** (OPNsense 26.7.1_1, no os-vnstat installed) reports:

> `vnstatGetJsonData` (`api/vnstat/service/get_json_data`) — a non-plugin endpoint 404'd; investigate

That classification is wrong. `vnstatGetJsonData` is plugin-gated in every meaningful sense — it is an os-vnstat route and 404s exactly when the plugin is absent.

**The exporter itself behaves correctly.** `FetchVnstat` (`opnsense/vnstat.go:158-170`) probes `vnstatInterfaceList` first and returns "feature absent" on its 404, never reaching `get_json_data`. Nothing is broken at runtime. This is purely a canary false positive — but a loud one, in the section reserved for "a core route vanished upstream", which is the report's highest-signal category.

## Root cause: one list answering two different questions

`cmd/apidrift/report.go:16` uses `opnsense.PluginGatedEndpoints()` as its oracle for "is a 404 expected here". But that list's actual contract is narrower, and `opnsense/cache.go:255-262` says so explicitly:

> `vnstatGetJsonData` is deliberately NOT listed here: its actual request path always carries a per-interface `?iface=` query string, but this negative cache is keyed on the fixed, registered path (no query) — so a TTL set on it would never match a real request and would be a no-op.

So the exclusion is a **caching-mechanics** decision, and the canary reads it as a **semantic** statement. Two questions:

| Question | Correct answer for `vnstatGetJsonData` |
| --- | --- |
| May a 404 here be negative-cached? | **No** — the cache key omits the query string, so a TTL would never match |
| Does a 404 here mean a plugin is absent? | **Yes** |

Consumers split cleanly along that line: `main.go:446` wants the cacheable set; `cmd/apidrift/report.go` and `opnsense/acl.go:221` want the semantic set.

## Why only the release box found this

The nightly testbed has os-vnstat installed, so `vnstatGetJsonData` answers 200 there and the misclassification never fires. It is only visible on a box **without** the plugin. This is the asymmetry #490 is about, found on the first probe of the release box.

## Proposal

Split the concepts rather than special-casing the canary:

- `PluginGatedEndpoints()` — the semantic set: a 404 here means the plugin is absent. Gains `vnstatGetJsonData`. Consumed by the canary and by `acl.go`.
- a separate negative-cacheable set — the subset whose 404 may be cached, excluding `vnstatGetJsonData` for the query-string reason above. Consumed by `main.go`.
- An invariant test that cacheable is a **subset** of gated, so the two can never drift into contradiction.

`CLAUDE.md` step 2b instructs collector authors to add plugin-gated endpoints to `PluginGatedEndpoints()` for caching purposes, and needs updating to say which list gets the new entry and why they differ.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The two sets exist separately with their contracts documented
- [ ] `vnstatGetJsonData` is in the semantic set and absent from the cacheable one
- [ ] Test enforcing cacheable ⊆ gated
- [ ] Existing `TestPluginGatedEndpoints` core-endpoint guard still applies to the semantic set
- [ ] Canary run against a box without os-vnstat no longer reports it as a vanished core route
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` step 2b updated

comments.body: Closed by 66eb588. Verified against the live release box: unexpected-absent count 1 → 0 and the "core endpoints absent" section no longer renders. Full gate green.

title: Canary misreports vnstatGetJsonData as a vanished core route: plugin-gating and 404-cacheability are one list answering two questions

body:
## What

Track total series against a configurable budget, report it on `/cardinality`, and log a warning when it is exceeded. **Soft only — nothing is ever dropped, capped or refused.**

Decided by the owner 2026-07-28, replacing #489's trim-to-save-series framing. We design against roughly **100k total active series** as available headroom; at ~7,530 today the exporter is at about 7.5% of that. The point is to notice if that ever stops being true, not to stay small.

## What exists today, and why it is not this

| Mechanism | Scope | Limits or reports? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--exporter.enable-*` (53 in `collectors.go`) | Per collector | Limits, as a manual on/off gate — this is the existing opt-in half |
| `topN` + `maxKeys` (`internal/flow/rollup.go:98-107`) | Flow rollup only | Real numeric caps, deliberately two separate bounds |
| `maxLogResources` (`internal/logship/sink_otlp.go:37`) | OTLP log resources | Explicitly **not** a cardinality control — its own comment says so |
| `warnCardinality` / `critCardinality` (`internal/webui/cardinality.go:15-17`) | **Per metric** (500 / 2000) | Reports only |

The last row is the closest thing and it is **per metric**, not total. A total budget is a new dimension alongside it, not a change to those two numbers. Do not repurpose them — a 2100-series metric is already over the per-metric critical threshold and that is fine and expected.

## Scope

1. **Config.** A flag for the total-series budget, default `100000`, following the `internal/options` kingpin pattern (see `cache.go` for the shape). Env var auto-derives as `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_*`. Setting it to `0` should mean "no budget, never warn" — that needs to be a supported value, not an accident.
2. **Report.** `/cardinality` shows total series against the budget: the number, the percentage, and an over/under state. `CardinalityReport` already carries `TotalSeries` (`cardinality.go:26`) and threshold fields, so this is an addition to an existing model, not a new one. The JSON endpoints (`/api/cardinality.json`, `/cardinality/export.json`) encode the report verbatim, so they pick it up for free — confirm that rather than assuming.
3. **Log.** Warn when the budget is exceeded. **Rate-limit it.** The obvious naive implementation logs on every scrape, which turns one warning into a permanent log flood and costs more than the cardinality did. Log on the transition into the over-budget state, and periodically thereafter at most.

## Design questions to settle before implementing

- **Where does the check fire?** The webui page is passive — it renders from `internal/metricsnap`, and `webui` handlers must never `Gather()` the live registry. The warning must not introduce a gather either. The natural home is wherever the recorder is already teed (`main.go`, both scrape sites), reading the count that already exists. State the choice and why.
- **Does this need a self-metric?** An `opnsense_exporter_series_total` style gauge would make the budget alertable rather than only greppable, which is arguably the whole value. If added it must be counted in its own total — and note it is one series, so it cannot meaningfully move the number it reports.

## Explicitly not in scope

Any enforcement: no dropping series, no refusing to register a collector, no auto-disabling. Soft reporting only.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Budget flag, default 100000, `0` meaning disabled, documented via `make docs`
- [ ] `/cardinality` shows total vs budget with an over/under state
- [ ] JSON endpoints carry it (verified, not assumed)
- [ ] Warning logged on transition into over-budget, rate-limited — with a test proving it does **not** log once per scrape
- [ ] Existing per-metric warn/crit thresholds unchanged
- [ ] No new `Gather()` call anywhere in the path

Ledger entries pruned and prune-triggers updated in the same commit.

body:
## What

`parseCARPStatus("INIT") == 2` is unit-tested at `opnsense/carp_test.go:150-152`, but the **end-to-end collector path has never seen it**. `TestCarpCollector_Update_WithVIPs` feeds only `MASTER` and `BACKUP` rows through to Prometheus, no fixture in `opnsense/testdata/` contains `INIT`, and no live capture has produced it.

`INIT` is the state a CARP VIP occupies between BACKUP and MASTER during failover and at startup — exactly the window an operator most wants their monitoring to be correct in.

## Honest severity

Reading the code, nothing looks wrong: the collector passes the int through as a label value with no special handling. This is "verified at the unit level, never verified end to end or against a real box", not a suspected bug.

It is worth closing anyway because it is now **cheap**. #460 built a two-node HA pair (VM 102 + VM 106), so `INIT` is reproducible on demand rather than hypothetical — and a captured fixture is strictly better evidence than a hand-written one, per the standing rule that a fixture must never encode a shape upstream cannot produce.

## Method

Trigger the transition on the testbed pair (disable CARP on the master interface, or bounce the peer) and capture `get_vip_status` while the VIP is in `INIT`. Timing is the only difficulty — the window is short, so poll the endpoint in a tight loop during the transition rather than trying to catch it by hand.

## Also worth capturing while there

`carpStatus rows[].mode` was confirmed constant `"carp"` in #460. Any transition-time payload is a chance to confirm that holds mid-failover too, and to check whether `INIT` rows carry the same field set as steady-state rows.

## Not in scope

`kea_dhcp4_leases_dynamic_total` reading zero was checked as part of the same sweep and is **not** a code gap: the reserved/dynamic split is table-driven and unit-tested with `is_reserved: "0"` fixtures at both the parse layer (`opnsense/kea.go:141-166`) and the metric layer (`internal/collector/kea_test.go:57,75`). The permanent zero is a testbed data gap — the box only ever provisions reserved leases. Recorded here so the next audit does not re-derive it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `INIT` captured from the live HA pair, not hand-written
- [ ] Fixture added and the collector test extended to assert the metric value for `INIT`
- [ ] Confirmed whether `INIT` rows carry the same fields as steady-state rows
- [ ] `make schemas` if the capture reveals any new path

comments.body:
## Closing as a documented negative result — INIT is real upstream, but not observable through this endpoint

Dedicated capture attempt run against the live 102/106 HA pair. **INIT was never observed**, across ~14,700 samples.

### What was tried

| trigger | what the poll loop saw |
|---|---|
| `configctl interface reconfigure opt1` on the backup (106) | no status change, no gap, no INIT |
| `carp_status/maintenance` toggle on the master (102) | a real bidirectional failover - 102 demoted to BACKUP, 106 promoted to MASTER, then reversed - zero INIT rows on either box |
| `ifconfig vtnet2 down` on the backup's CARP interface | a genuine interface flap (it triggered a full pf filter reload), sampling continued with no gap, zero INIT rows |

Sustained poll rate: 102 ~11.2/s over 651s (7,284 samples), 106 ~11.6/s over 637s (7,417 samples), with bursts to ~100/s. Every single sample was `MASTER` or `BACKUP`.

### INIT is not a phantom shape, which is worth stating explicitly

The prior note in #497 called INIT a sub-second bring-up transient. Confirmed against upstream source rather than left as an inference: `InterfaceController::getVipStatusAction()` (`opnsense/core` `stable/26.7`) passes `status` straight through from the kernel's `ifconfig` carp block, and its translation switch carries an explicit `case 'INIT'`. So the endpoint genuinely can serve it - this is a **sampling** limit, not a modelling error, and `parseCARPStatus("INIT") == 2` is correctly implemented against a state upstream really emits.

That distinction matters because #284's lesson was the opposite case: a shape modelled from a guess that upstream never produced. This is not that.

### Secondary questions from this issue, answered

- **`rows[].mode` constant `"carp"`**: confirmed across all ~14,700 samples, including through the real failover in trigger 2.
- **Does an INIT row carry the same field set?** Unanswerable, no INIT row was captured. For the record, every MASTER/BACKUP row on both boxes carried the identical set: `advbase, advskew, interface, mode, status, status_txt, subnet, vhid, vhid_txt`.

### No fixture was written

Deliberately. The standing rule is that a fixture must never encode a shape upstream cannot produce, and hand-writing an INIT payload to close a checkbox would have been exactly the fabrication that rule exists to prevent. `opnsense/testdata/`, `opnsense/carp_test.go` and `internal/collector/carp_test.go` are untouched.

### Reading the source turned up a real bug next door

`getVipStatusAction()` has a second loop that emits `'status' => 'DISABLED'` for any configured VIP not currently instantiated - a disabled VIP, or one on a down interface. `parseCARPStatus` has no `DISABLED` case, so it falls to `default` and returns `-1`, "unknown". Filed separately as #503, because it produces a false page today.

### Side effect found and fixed on 106

Trigger 3's interface-down event made OPNsense reload 106's packet filter, which locked SSH out from the test subnet: five WAN pass rules in `/conf/config.xml` still referenced the stale pre-#497 prod-LAN `<lan-ip-34>/24` instead of `<lan-ip-26>/24`. Corrected, original backed up to `/root/config.xml.pre-carp-fix.bak` on 106. Worth noting against #497 as leftover state from that migration.

Final state verified: 102 CARP MASTER (advskew 0), 106 CARP BACKUP (advskew 100), neither in maintenance, TESTLAN up on both.

### Recommendation

Close. Reopening only makes sense if a mechanism appears that holds a VIP in INIT long enough to sample - a slow-booting node, or a `carp` devd hook capturing state at the transition rather than polling for it.

body:
## What

`--otlp.export-interval` defaults to `60s` and applies uniformly (`internal/options/otlp.go:36-43`). There is an optional fast lane (`--otlp.fast-export-interval`, default `0s`/disabled) for fast-tier collectors, but **no slow or cold lane**.

So every metric from a `slow` (5m) or `cold` (15m) tier collector (`internal/collector/interval_tiers.go:53-84`) is exported every 60 seconds, re-sending a value that by the code's own declaration only changes every 5-15 minutes.

Measured live:

```
count({__name__=~"opnsense_(firewall_rule|alias|ntp_peer|dyndns|qfeeds|lldp|tor_|siproxd|chrony)_?.*"})  → 1251   (slow tier)
count({__name__=~"opnsense_(firmware|certificate|acme|smart|cron_job|snapshots|auth|backup)_.*"})        → 133    (cold tier)
```

Slow tier at true cadence: 1251×1440 → 1251×288 samples/day. Cold: 133×1440 → 133×96. Combined **≈1.62M fewer samples/day**, about 15% of this instance's ~10.8M/day.

## Why this is an owner's call, not a clear win

Grafana Cloud Metrics bills primarily on **active series**, and these series stay active regardless of how often they are exported. Sending them less often does not remove them from the bill under that model. I could not confirm per-job sample attribution live — `grafanacloud_instance_attributed_samples_per_second{service=~"opnsense.*"}` returned no data under the `service` label.

So the saving is real for **network egress and backend query/storage load**, and unproven for **dollar cost on this plan**.

What it is not: risky. The code already tiers these collectors by declared volatility; this only makes the export cadence match a decision the operator has already expressed. The fast lane is an existing template.

## What is lost

Nothing functional. A slow-tier metric exported every 5 minutes instead of every minute is exported at the rate its data changes. The one behavioural consequence worth stating: a Grafana panel with a short `$__rate_interval` over a slow-tier metric would see fewer points, so any panel or alert already tuned to the 60s cadence needs checking.

## Decide before building

Is sample rate worth reducing on this plan, or is active series the only number that matters? If the latter, close this — the egress saving alone probably does not justify a third export lane and its config surface.

## Acceptance (if built)

- [ ] Slow and cold export lanes mirroring the existing fast lane, defaulting to the tier interval
- [ ] Any alert or panel tuned to the 60s cadence identified and re-checked
- [ ] Sample volume re-measured live after deploy and the actual reduction recorded here
- [ ] `make docs` for the new flags

comments.body:
Closing as **not worth it**, owner's decision 2026-07-28.

The measurement stands: slow-tier collectors carry 1,251 series and cold-tier 133, all exported every 60s against underlying data that changes every 5-15 minutes, so a tier-matched export lane would cut roughly 1.62M samples/day — about 15% of this instance's sample volume.

The reason not to build it: **Grafana Cloud Metrics bills primarily on active series, and those series stay active regardless of export cadence.** Exporting them less often does not remove them from the bill. The saving is real for network egress and for backend query/storage load, and unproven for cost on this plan — per-job sample attribution returned no data under the labels available (`grafanacloud_instance_attributed_samples_per_second{service=~"opnsense.*"}`), so it could not be confirmed live either way.

Against an unproven saving, a third export lane adds config surface and one more thing that can be misconfigured, and any alert or panel currently tuned to the 60s cadence would need re-checking.

Recorded so this is not re-derived: the code already tiers these collectors correctly (`internal/collector/interval_tiers.go`), and `--otlp.fast-export-interval` already exists as the template if this is ever revisited. Reopen if the billing model changes or if backend load rather than cost becomes the motivation.
