## Fixed in `7ed2631` — and the diagnosis in this issue's body was right; my first fix was not

### Correcting the record first

I posted a fix (`df1a448`) claiming the limit is tripped by a **range** query returning the union of series across its steps, and that an instant query therefore fixes it. **That was wrong.** It rested on a `gcx datasources loki metrics` call that returns `resultType: "matrix"` — it was running a range query the whole time, so the A/B that "proved" instant beat range was comparing a range query against another range query. The three panels stayed broken after it shipped, which is what exposed it.

Re-measured through **Grafana's own query path** (`POST /api/ds/query`, `instant: true`, the exact panel expression), on the DNS-name table:

| | 1h | 3h | 6h |
|---|---|---|---|
| `topk(25)` | 25 frames | **500-limit** | **500-limit** |
| `topk(200)` | 200 frames | **500-limit** | **500-limit** |

**The rank depth is irrelevant** — 25 and 200 behave identically — and the limit tracks the **time range**. `topk` prunes the result while the limit is enforced on an intermediate, which is exactly what this issue's body said and what my first fix talked itself out of.

### The fix

The four tables ranking an **unbounded** label — DNS name, SNI, JA3 hash, URI — pin a 1h window with `timeFrom` and are decoupled from the dashboard picker. The eight ranking a **bounded** vocabulary (country, app, category, user agent, device) stay on the picker: the pin is a real cost and is only worth paying where the query would otherwise fail outright.

1h is a measured fit for this box's traffic, not a constant — the cliff moves with log volume. The code comment says so and names `timeFrom` as the number to lower if a table starts returning "No data".

### Rendered from the published dashboard

`Top DNS Queries`, previously "No data" with a query error:

```text
Query                                Instance    Total
profiles-prod-023.grafana.net        opnsense     1388
_ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.cam.…           opnsense      880
_ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.iot.…           opnsense      880
<host-34>             opnsense      540
api.meraki.com                       opnsense      516
```

`Top JA3 Fingerprints`:

```text
JA3 Fingerprint                      Instance    Total
<hash-4>     opnsense     3695
<hash-5>     opnsense     3552
<hash-6>     opnsense     3271
```

`Top TLS Server Names (SNI)`:

```text
Server Name                          Instance    Total
adsb.feed.sdrmap.org                 opnsense     2453
logs-prod-035.grafana.net            opnsense     2158
profiles-prod-023.grafana.net        opnsense     1699
```

All three ranked descending, with Grafana showing the "Last 1 hour" override badge in the panel header so the decoupled range is visible rather than silent.

### Two things kept from the first attempt, on their own merits

- **The instant query.** It is the right shape for a top-N table — one aggregate over the window rather than a time series a reduce then flattens. Not a fix for the limit.
- **`topk` at 200**, up from 15/20/25. Since N has no bearing on the limit, ranking deeper is free. 500 is not available: `topk(500)` fails and `topk(450)` returned 465 series, so N is not an exact bound on the result and anything near 500 has no headroom.

### A regression the first attempt introduced, also fixed

Removing the range query left a `groupBy` with nothing to aggregate. `groupBy` resolves its target field by **display name**, and the Loki datasource stamps `displayNameFromDS` with the serialised label set — so it found no field called `Value` and **silently dropped the value column**. Every one of the twelve tables rendered its key and instance columns with no number and no ranking, sorted alphabetically. It was caught by rendering the published dashboard, not by any test.

Then `merge` names the value field `Value #A`, suffixed with the refId. Renaming only `Value` left the column titled `Value #A` **and** broke the sort, which resolves `Total` by display name and falls back to alphabetical when it does not match — a table that looks correct while no longer being ranked at all. Both spellings are now renamed.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] All twelve `loki_table()` panels return data at the dashboard's default range, verified by rendering the published dashboard rather than by regenerating JSON
- [x] A guard that fails when a shipped Loki panel would exceed the series limit — `UnboundedLabelTablesPinTheirOwnWindowTest` fails if an unbounded-label table follows the picker, and equally if a bounded one is needlessly pinned. Mutation-checked: dropping `timeFrom` from the DNS table turns it red. It also fails if a pinned table is renamed, rather than silently checking nothing.
- [x] The chosen approach documented on the panels it affects — each of the four says "over this panel's own 1h window" in its description, so a decoupled range does not read as a bug
- [x] Full gate green

### On the recording-rule idea

Worth recording why it is not needed. A Loki recording rule would have worked — evaluated at `[5m]` the inner aggregation is 154–228 series, well under the limit — but it would have cost the `$zenarmor_client` filter (a pre-aggregated metric cannot carry a dimension it did not record), made the top-N approximate (a name outside the top-N in some windows undercounts over a longer one), and added three rules plus permanent Prometheus churn of ~80 new series/hour for the DNS names alone. Pinning the window costs none of that and keeps the top-N exact.

### Gate

`go test ./...` clean · `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` OK · `golangci-lint run ./...` 0 issues · `make docs-check` passed · `make grafana-test` 333 tests OK · `make grafana-check` 58 manifests valid.

Deployed via gitsync (`gc-gitsync-m7kni` `90ad21f`); every render above is from the published dashboard.

body:
Portable finding from `tailscale2otel`'s `deploy/grafana/gen/test_empty_state_contract.py`, spotted while looking for prior art for #429's behaviour harness. Different problem, but it applies here and we have no equivalent gate.

## The defect class

A stat-like panel inside a conditionally-rendered row may zero-fill with `or vector(0)`. That is only honest if the row's gating sentinel is fed by the **same collector** as the panel's own query.

If they come from different collectors, the row renders because collector A is present while the panel's metric comes from collector B — which may be absent — and the panel shows a green **0**. An operator reads that as "checked, nothing found". The truth is "never checked". A silently wrong zero on a security or failure-count panel is worse than a blank one, because a blank panel prompts a question and a green zero ends the conversation.

Crucially, **metric-name identity is not the test — collector identity is.** Two metrics from one collector always co-exist; two metrics from different collectors do not.

## Applies to us

`rg "or vector\(0\)" grafana/` finds **7** sites across the tab builders today, none of them checked against their row's sentinel. We already have the two ingredients needed to derive ownership rather than hand-list it:

- `sentinel-contract.json` (#417) is a machine-readable manifest of every sentinel, its scope, and its metric.
- `docs/metrics/metrics.md` is generated per collector subsystem, so a metric name maps back to its owning collector; `docs/metrics/self-metrics.md` (#428) does the same for self-metrics, where the answer is "shared" rather than one collector.

So the gate can be derived end to end, with no per-panel list to rot — the same property that makes the #428 self-metric gate trustworthy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A generator-level test resolves, for every `or vector(0)` panel, the owning collector of its query metric and of its row's gating sentinel
- [ ] Fails when they differ, naming the panel, the two collectors, and why the zero would be a lie
- [ ] Cross-cutting/self-observability metrics that genuinely co-exist with every collector are bucketed as shared and permitted, derived rather than listed
- [ ] Ownership is derived from the generated metric docs and the sentinel contract, never hand-maintained
- [ ] Existing violations are either fixed or carry a rationale-bearing exemption, in the style of `NOT_ANNOTATED` in `grafana/annotations.py`
- [ ] A regression test proves the gate fails on a deliberately mismatched panel

## Not a duplicate

#417 built the sentinel contract but gates its documentation, not panel/sentinel provenance. #428 gates whether a metric is charted at all, not whether its empty state is honest. #114 fixed one instance of the adjacent "present but zero vs absent" confusion in DHCP by hand; this generalises it into a gate.

Prior art to read first: `~/repos/tailscale2otel/deploy/grafana/gen/test_empty_state_contract.py`. Its ownership-derivation approach transfers; its collector layout does not, so this is a port rather than a copy.

comments.body:
## Landed in `a62b25a` — no violations found, gate is live

All six acceptance criteria met. `grafana/tests/test_empty_state_contract.py`, 10 tests, wired into `make grafana-test`.

### Result

**All 7 `or vector(0)` sites are clean.** Six (2 CrowdSec, 4 Tor) are gated by their own collector's sentinel; the seventh, "Unhealthy Subsystems", charts `opnsense_system_subsystem_status_code`, a `## General` metric emitted regardless of which collectors are enabled. So `ZERO_FILL_EXEMPT` ships **empty**, which is the outcome worth having — the gate is now the thing that keeps it that way rather than a snapshot of today.

### Ownership derivation

As specified: `docs/metrics/metrics.md` (one `##` section per collector subsystem) plus `docs/metrics/self-metrics.md` plus `sentinel-contract.json`. Nothing hand-listed. A metric in `## General`, in the self-metric inventory, or under two sections is bucketed shared. A metric in **neither** inventory resolves to `<unknown:...>` rather than to shared, so a typo cannot pass by looking harmless.

### Two soundness details that needed a second pass

**Only `and` gates count as a guarantee.** The VPN domain tab is gated on `has_wireguard OR has_openvpn OR has_ipsec OR has_tailscale OR has_netbird OR has_tor`. Reading `has_tor` out of that OR group as proof the Tor collector is running would be precisely the unproven zero this issue is about — the domain renders when WireGuard alone is present. The Tor panels still pass, on their leaf tab's own `has_tor` gate, but they now pass for a reason that is actually true. `notMatches` items are absence assertions and prove nothing about presence either, so they are excluded too.

**The metric-name regex has to reject two things in every selector that look like metric names**: the LABEL in `{opnsense_instance=~"..."}` and the interpolated VARIABLE `$opnsense_instance`. Without both exclusions every panel appeared to chart a metric named `opnsense_instance` and the whole gate resolved to `<unknown>` — which is exactly what happened on the first run, and would have been a gate that reported violations everywhere rather than one that silently passed, so it announced itself.

### Proving it can go red

The gate and the red tests call the **same** `violations()` function rather than two similar copies, so a gate that stopped comparing anything fails the red tests too. Verified by making the comparison always pass: 2 tests fail. Covered cases: a Tor panel gated by a CrowdSec sentinel (violation), the same panel gated by `has_tor` (control, not a violation), a zero-fill gated by nothing at all (violation), and an exemption suppressing the failure.

Full gate green at `a62b25a`.
