body:
## Problem

Three pollers write to one Loki tenant — `opnsense-exporter`, `tailscale2otel`, `graph2otel` — and Loki's OTLP label-promotion slots are **tenant-wide, keyed by attribute name, and capped at 15**. Today only this repo promotes anything, under an `opnsense.*` namespace. If each poller namespaces its own shape dimensions, the budget runs out.

## Measured current state (2026-07-27, live)

Index labels on the tenant from OTLP promotion:

```
service_name, service_instance_id, opnsense_source, opnsense_subsystem, opnsense_action
```

Plus `opnsense.device_category` and `opnsense.interface`, which #473 put on the resource and which are pending tenant-side promotion (confirmed arriving as structured metadata on a live Zenarmor record, so they are promotable the moment the config lands). That takes this repo to **7 of 15**.

**The other two pollers promote nothing, and cannot.** Verified by reading their resource construction:

- `tailscale2otel/internal/telemetry/provider.go` `buildResource()` — `service.name`, optional `service.version`, `service.instance.id`, plus `WithTelemetrySDK/WithOS/WithProcess*` detectors. No custom attributes.
- `graph2otel/internal/telemetry/provider.go` — the same shape.

Their domain attributes (e.g. `tailscale.webhook.type`, `tailscale.webhook.node.device.name`) are **log** attributes, on the record. Loki's `index_label` action exists only under `otlp_config.resource_attributes`; `log_attributes` accepts `structured_metadata` or `drop` and nothing else. So they are unpromotable by construction, not by configuration.

## Slot arithmetic — the forcing function

| Approach | Slots consumed |
|---|---|
| Today | 7 / 15 |
| Each poller namespaces its own ~4-5 dimensions | ~15 / 15 — at the cap, no headroom |
| One shared namespace across all pollers | ~7 / 15, regardless of poller count |

The per-poller path does not scale past the third poller. This is the substantive reason to settle a contract, not tidiness.

## Why now, and why the cost is asymmetric

**t2o and g2o would adopt a shared contract for free** — they have no promoted labels, so no queries, dashboards or alerts depend on a name they do not yet emit.

**Only this repo pays a migration cost.** Renaming `opnsense_source` and friends touches 13 Loki stream selectors in `grafana/tabs/*.py` (21 occurrences in generated `dashboard.json`), and every historical log line keeps the old label — so a rename means a dual-label transition window on a live tenant, with queries matching both until retention rolls over.

**These two decisions should therefore be decoupled.** Define the contract, have the siblings adopt it from birth, and treat migrating this repo as a separate, explicitly-scoped decision that can be declined.

## OTel semantics — what is and is not safe

A shared private namespace is exactly what OTel prescribes for custom attributes. Two things would genuinely be wrong:

- **Bare, unnamespaced names** (`source`, `action`, `interface`). OTel warns against these precisely because they collide with future semconv. They are also what a first draft of the pending tenant config reached for.
- **Squatting a semconv namespace with a different meaning.** semconv `device.*` means *the device the telemetry originates from* (`device.id`, `device.manufacturer`, `device.model.name`). Using it for an observed network **client** would be a reserved name carrying a foreign meaning — worse than a private namespace.

Worth considering per-attribute rather than blanket: **`network.interface.name` is real semconv** and is a defensible fit for the interface dimension. Using a genuine standard name where one exists beats inventing one; the trade is that Loki's default promotion list may cover it independently, which is either a convenience or a surprise depending on `ignore_defaults`.

## Which concepts are actually shared

Needs deciding per dimension, not in bulk:

| Dimension | Genuinely poller-agnostic? |
|---|---|
| `source` | Yes — "which sub-collector produced this" applies to all three |
| `subsystem` | Yes — coarse functional grouping |
| `action` | Probably — a binary allow/deny disposition; needs checking whether t2o audit events and g2o have one |
| `device_category` | Unclear — t2o has devices too, but the category vocabularies are unrelated |
| `interface` | Firewall-specific in practice; semconv `network.interface.name` may be the better answer |

A dimension that is not genuinely the same concept should stay emitter-namespaced. Unifying a label whose values mean different things per poller makes `{shared_subsystem="dns"}` ambiguous, and `service_name` is the only thing disambiguating it.

## Decisions needed

1. Namespace: a private org namespace (e.g. `m7kni.*`), or semconv names where they exist, or a mix?
2. Which dimensions are shared vs emitter-specific (table above)?
3. Does this repo migrate at all, or keep `opnsense.*` and let the siblings use the shared set? Given 8 free slots, keeping both is viable and costs nothing today.

## Scope

- [ ] Agree the namespace and the per-dimension shared/specific split
- [ ] Document the contract somewhere all three repos can reference
- [ ] Sibling issues in `tailscale2otel` and `graph2otel` to hoist their agreed dimensions onto the log resource (they currently hoist nothing)
- [ ] Decide explicitly whether this repo migrates; if yes, a separate issue covering the dual-label transition, the 13 stream selectors, and the tenant config sequencing
- [ ] Whatever lands, the tenant `otlp_config` must list **dotted OTLP attribute names** — Loki matches the attribute name and does the dot-to-underscore conversion itself

## Note on the config format, recorded here because it has already caused one wrong draft

The promotion list takes the attribute name **as sent**, dotted: `opnsense.source`, not `opnsense_source`, and `service.instance.id`, not `service_instance_id`. Loki's docs: *"Attributes with dots in their names are converted to underscores"* — that conversion is Loki's, on the way to the label, and every documented example lists dotted names. With `ignore_defaults: true`, an underscored list matches nothing and silently drops `service_name`/`service_instance_id` as labels too.

Related: #473 (put the two shape dimensions on the resource), #474 (why `device_name` is enumerated from Prometheus rather than promoted).

comments.body:
## Attribute tiers, verified against the Loki docs

Checked properly rather than from memory, because the three tiers are configured differently as well as behaving differently.

### What each tier can become

| Tier | Config shape | Allowed actions | Default when unconfigured |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resource_attributes` | **object**: `ignore_defaults` + `attributes_config` list | `index_label`, `structured_metadata`, `drop` | on the default list → **index label**; otherwise → structured metadata |
| `scope_attributes` | **bare list** of attributes_configs | `structured_metadata`, `drop` | structured metadata |
| `log_attributes` | **bare list** of attributes_configs | `structured_metadata`, `drop` | structured metadata |

**Only `resource_attributes` can produce a label.** Sourced, not inferred — from Loki's own operator guide:

> "the field in the distributor configuration is limited to resource-level attributes and **can only produce stream-labels as an output**, the `otlp_config` needs to be used to map resource, scope or log level attributes to **either be dropped or saved as structured metadata**"

So scope and log attributes have exactly two possible fates. No tenant configuration can index them. Both already default to structured metadata, which is why every `device_name` / `app_name` / `flow_interface` field is queryable with `|` today without anyone configuring anything.

### Config-shape gotcha

The shapes are **not interchangeable** — a common way to get this wrong:

```yaml
limits_config:
  otlp_config:
    resource_attributes:            # an OBJECT
      ignore_defaults: <bool>
      attributes_config:
        - action: index_label
          attributes: [...]
    scope_attributes:               # a bare LIST — no attributes_config wrapper
      - action: drop
        attributes: [...]
    log_attributes:                 # a bare LIST
      - action: structured_metadata
        attributes: [...]
```

`attributes_config` entries take `action`, plus **either** `attributes: [<names>]` **or** `regex: <re>`.

### Two config locations, not one

Index-label defaults live in the **distributor** config (`default_resource_attributes_as_index_labels`), separately from `limits_config.otlp_config`. The default candidate list is:

```
service.name, service.namespace, service.instance.id, deployment.environment,
deployment.environment.name, cloud.region, cloud.availability_zone,
k8s.cluster.name, k8s.namespace.name, k8s.pod.name, k8s.container.name,
container.name, k8s.replicaset.name, k8s.deployment.name, k8s.statefulset.name,
k8s.daemonset.name, k8s.cronjob.name, k8s.job.name
```

**`service.name` and `service.instance.id` are both on it**, which is exactly why they are labels today without anyone configuring them — and exactly why `ignore_defaults: true` is dangerous unless they are re-listed explicitly. The 15-label cap is a limit on what is *stored*, not on the length of this candidate list.

Also noted in the config reference: indexing `severity_text` is possible but discouraged for performance.

## The finding that changes this issue's cost model

My framing above — "t2o and g2o would adopt a shared contract **for free**" — is **wrong, and I am correcting it.**

Adopting the *naming* is free. **Hoisting is not.** Since only resource attributes can be indexed, and an OTLP resource is bound to a `LoggerProvider` rather than to a record, a poller that wants `N` distinct values of a shape dimension needs **one LoggerProvider per distinct resource combination**. That is precisely the machinery in this repo's `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go`: a provider map keyed on `resourceKey`, a shared exporter so partitioning costs no extra connections, deterministic per-partition flush ordering, a `maxLogResources` cap, and a safe degrade path when the cap is hit — which #473 had to raise from 64 to 256, and where overshooting silently destroys the labels that already work.

So each sibling adopting the contract needs that pattern, not just a rename. That is materially more than a config change, and it should be weighed per repo against how much either actually gains from a promoted label.

It also strengthens the recommendation to decouple: the naming contract can be agreed cheaply and now; the hoisting work is a separate, per-repo decision that may reasonably come out as "not worth it" for one or both siblings.

## Corrected tenant config for the pending ticket

Recording it here so it does not live only in a chat log. This is correct regardless of how the naming question in this issue resolves:

```yaml
- action: index_label
  attributes:
    - service.name
    - service.instance.id
    - opnsense.source
    - opnsense.subsystem
    - opnsense.action
    - opnsense.device_category
    - opnsense.interface
  regex: null
```

Seven of fifteen slots. Dotted names — Loki matches the attribute name as sent and does the dot-to-underscore conversion itself on the way to the label.

**Do not apply the earlier draft**, which used bare underscored names (`source`, `subsystem`, `service_name`) with `ignore_defaults: true`. Nothing in it would have matched, and dropping the defaults at the same time would have removed `service_name` and `service_instance_id` as labels — breaking every existing query against this tenant, not merely failing to add the new labels. It also listed `device_category`, `interface_name`, `flow_interface` and `device_name`, all of which are **log** attributes and therefore unindexable by construction; `device_name` was additionally rejected in #473 on cardinality grounds.

## Decision request — and a correction that changes what is being decided

Three decisions are pending below with a recommendation and a default-if-unanswered for each. Before them: **the slot arithmetic in the issue body is wrong, and it was the entire forcing function.**

## The correction: 15 is a per-stream limit, not a tenant-wide slot budget

The body reasons that three pollers each namespacing ~5 dimensions consumes ~15/15 and exhausts a shared budget. That treats the 15 as a tenant-wide pool of distinct promotable attribute *names*. It is not. It is `max_label_names_per_series` — **the maximum number of label names on any one stream**, enforced by the distributor at ingest, returning `400 Bad Request` on breach.

From Loki's own troubleshooting page: *"The `max_label_names_per_series` error occurs when a log stream exceeds the default limit of 15 label names"*, and the operator API defines it as *"the maximum number of label names per series in each log stream."*

Pollers do not share that budget, because **a `tailscale2otel` stream never carries an `opnsense_*` label**. Promoting `opnsense.*` costs t2o and g2o exactly nothing. Each poller independently gets 15 label names on its own streams.

Measured against the live tenant just now, the widest stream this repo produces carries **7** label names:

```
gcx datasources loki series -d grafanacloud-logs --match '{opnsense_source=~".+"}'

{opnsense_action="pass", opnsense_device_category="server", opnsense_interface="LAN",
 opnsense_source="zenarmor", opnsense_subsystem="dns",
 service_instance_id="opnsense", service_name="opnsense-exporter"}
```

7 of 15 **on this repo's own streams**, with 8 free that no sibling can consume. Syslog streams are narrower still (3–4), because `device_category`/`interface`/`action` are set only where meaningful.

### This also resolves the 15-vs-30 discrepancy

The two numbers were never in conflict; they measure different things.

| Number | What it actually limits | Shared across pollers? |
|---|---|---|
| **15** | `max_label_names_per_series` — label names on a single stream | **No** — per stream |
| **30** | Grafana Cloud self-serve cap on the length of the promoted-attributes list | **Yes** — one tenant list |

The genuinely shared resource is the **tenant `attributes_config` list**, not per-stream slots. Three pollers at ~5 custom attributes each plus the two `service.*` entries is ~17 of 30 — comfortable, and additive: adding `tailscale.*` entries to that list cannot affect an `opnsense_*` stream.

The applied tenant config, fetched live, confirms the current list is well-formed (dotted names, `ignore_defaults: true` with both `service.*` keys correctly re-listed):

```yaml
otlp_config:
    resource_attributes:
        ignore_defaults: true
        attributes_config:
            - action: index_label
              attributes: [service.name, service.instance.id, opnsense.source,
                           opnsense.subsystem, opnsense.action,
                           opnsense.device_category, opnsense.interface]
              regex: null
```

All 7 are **applied and live**, not pending — the body's "5 promoted, 2 pending" is stale.

### What survives the correction

Not much of the original case. The scale argument is gone: the per-poller path scales past the third poller fine, and past the tenth. What is left as an argument for a shared contract is query ergonomics — being able to write one selector across pollers — which is a real but much weaker driver, and is bought at the price of ambiguity (see decision 2).

The other finding in my earlier comment stands unchanged and still matters: **hoisting is not free.** Only resource attributes can be indexed, and an OTLP resource binds to a `LoggerProvider`, so N distinct values of a dimension means N providers — the `sink_otlp.go` machinery, its `maxLogResources` cap, and its silent-degrade path. That cost is per-repo and independent of naming.

---

## Decision 1 — namespace

**Recommendation: keep per-emitter namespaces. `opnsense.*` here, `tailscale.*` and `graph2otel.*` for the siblings. No shared `m7kni.*` namespace.**

With the slot pressure gone, a shared namespace buys cross-poller selector ergonomics and costs a live-tenant migration on the only repo that has promoted labels. On the semconv question specifically: `network.interface.name` is a genuine standard name and would be defensible for the interface dimension, but `opnsense.interface` is already promoted, live, and referenced by 13 stream selectors — renaming it to a standard name is the same dual-label transition as any other rename, for an aesthetic gain. Not worth it on its own; worth reconsidering only if the interface dimension is ever rebuilt for another reason.

Both genuine errors the body identifies stay prohibited either way: **no bare unnamespaced names** (`source`, `action`, `interface`), and **no squatting a semconv namespace with a foreign meaning** (semconv `device.*` means the device the telemetry originates from, not an observed network client).

**Default if unanswered:** keep per-emitter namespaces; change nothing.

## Decision 2 — shared vs emitter-specific per dimension

**Recommendation: all dimensions stay emitter-specific.**

Unifying a label whose values mean different things per poller makes the unified label actively misleading. `{shared_subsystem="dns"}` matching both an OPNsense Zenarmor DNS record and whatever t2o calls DNS leaves `service_name` as the only thing disambiguating them — at which point the shared label has bought nothing that `service_name` did not already provide. The body's own table already concedes `device_category` vocabularies are unrelated and `interface` is firewall-specific in practice; `source` and `subsystem` are shared only at the level of "both are strings naming a producer", which is not the same concept.

**Default if unanswered:** emitter-specific throughout.

## Decision 3 — does this repo migrate?

**Recommendation: no.** Under decisions 1 and 2 there is nothing to migrate to. Even under a different answer to those, the asymmetry in the body holds and is now stronger: this repo pays a dual-label transition window across 13 stream selectors and 21 occurrences in generated `dashboard.json`, plus every historical line keeping the old label until 31d retention rolls over — and the reason to pay it (slot exhaustion) does not exist.

**Default if unanswered:** no migration; `opnsense.*` stays.

---

## What I recommend actually landing, whatever is decided

The naming *rules* are worth writing down even though the shared *namespace* is not, because two of them have already caused a wrong config in production:

1. A short contract doc all three repos can reference: namespace every custom resource attribute under an emitter prefix; never bare names; never squat a semconv namespace with a foreign meaning; **the tenant `otlp_config` lists dotted names as sent** (`opnsense.source`, not `opnsense_source` — Loki does the dot-to-underscore conversion itself); the tenant `attributes_config` list is shared, so edits to it are coordinated and must be GET-merge-PUT, never blind partial.
2. Sibling issues in `tailscale2otel` and `graph2otel` recording that they hoist nothing today, that their domain attributes are **log** attributes and therefore unindexable by construction, and what the hoisting pattern and its cost would be **if** either ever wants a promoted label. Filed as "here is the cost if you want this", not as work to do — for both, the honest current answer is probably that it is not worth it.

## Awaiting

- [ ] **Decision 1** — namespace: per-emitter (recommended) vs shared `m7kni.*` vs semconv-where-available
- [ ] **Decision 2** — per-dimension shared/specific split: all emitter-specific (recommended) vs unify `source`/`subsystem`
- [ ] **Decision 3** — does this repo migrate: no (recommended) vs yes with a dual-label transition issue

Nothing else in this issue is blocked on these. The correction above is independent of all three and stands regardless.

## Decided and closed in `a4340cc`

Decisions taken, all three as recommended above:

1. **Namespace** — per-emitter. `opnsense.*` here, `tailscale.*` / `graph2otel.*` for the siblings. No shared namespace.
2. **Per-dimension split** — all emitter-specific. Nothing unified.
3. **Migration** — none. `opnsense.*` stays exactly as it is.

`opnsense.interface` specifically stays rather than becoming semconv `network.interface.name`. The standard name is defensible, but it is already promoted, live, and behind 13 stream selectors — a rename is the same dual-label transition as any other, for an aesthetic gain.

### What landed

**`docs/otlp-attribute-contract.md`**, referenced from both sibling repos. It carries the structural rule (only resource attributes can be indexed), the two limits and why they are not the same limit, the naming rules, the tenant-config rules, the hoisting cost, the current registry, and this decision record with its reasoning.

**The corrected paragraph in `docs/log-shipping.md`.** It said:

> On Grafana Cloud the promotion slots are shared across the **whole tenant** and keyed by attribute name, so count them against everything else writing to the same Loki.

That is true of the tenant's promoted-attribute *list* and false of the per-stream budget it reads as — the same conflation this issue's body was built on, sitting in the shipped docs. Replaced with the distinction and a link to the contract.

**Sibling issues** — rknightion/tailscale2otel#511 and rknightion/graph2otel#404. Each records that its domain attributes are log attributes and therefore unindexable by construction, that promotion needs the `LoggerProvider`-per-resource pattern rather than a rename, and the naming to use if it ever happens. Filed as reference, explicitly not as queued work.

### Not done, deliberately

No dual-label transition issue, because there is no migration. No change to the tenant `otlp_config` — it is already correct and applied, verified against both the applied config and the live stream labels rather than assumed.

### Scope checklist

- [x] Agree the namespace and the per-dimension shared/specific split
- [x] Document the contract somewhere all three repos can reference
- [x] Sibling issues in `tailscale2otel` and `graph2otel`
- [x] Decide explicitly whether this repo migrates — no
- [x] Whatever lands, the tenant `otlp_config` must list dotted OTLP attribute names — it does, and the contract doc states why

Full gate green on `a4340cc`.

title: design: a shared cross-poller OTLP resource-attribute contract for Loki label promotion

body:
## Problem

`opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_device_info` (#474) can carry two rows for one device — one keyed on the kernel interface device, one on the description-space name. Live on <host-1>, minutes after the #474 deploy:

| device_name | device_category | interface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <host-35> | camera | `ixl0` |
| <host-35> | camera | `LAN` |

## Cause

`internal/logship/zenarmor/derive.go` resolves the interface once for both the counter and the inventory:

```go
iface := firstNonEmpty(attrs[attrInterfaceName], attrs[attrInterfaceDev])
```

`interface.name` is only set when the enrichment snapshot resolved the device (`parse.go`, inside `if snap != nil { if name, ok := snap.InterfaceName(...)`). Records parsed before the snapshot has loaded — i.e. the window right after start-up — therefore fall back to the raw device. The inventory then keeps that row for the full 24h TTL, alongside the enriched row that appears once the snapshot lands.

## Why it matters, and why it is not urgent

- The **picker is unaffected**: `label_values(opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_device_info, device_name)` dedupes, so the dropdown shows one `<host-35>`.
- The **inventory table** shows duplicate rows, and the series count is inflated by however many devices were seen during the pre-enrichment window. On the observed sample that is a minority of devices, and it decays after 24h — but it recurs on every restart.
- It also mixes two disjoint label spaces in one column (#98), so the `interface` value cannot be joined against `$interface` for the affected rows.

This is not a regression: `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total` already labels `interface` with the same fallback, deliberately. The difference is that a counter's rows are aggregate, whereas an inventory's rows are one-per-entity, so the duplicate is visible as a wrong row rather than a split total.

## Also fix while here

The header comment on `TestObserveDerived_DeviceInventoryFallsBackToTheRawDevice` (`internal/logship/zenarmor/derive_test.go`) claims the inventory "takes the DESCRIPTION-space interface ... the kernel device (ixl0) ... would make the picker's rows disagree with every other interface selector", and then the test asserts the exact opposite. The assertion matches the code; the comment does not. Whichever way this issue resolves, the comment and the test must agree.

## Options

1. **Inventory takes the resolved name only**, leaving `interface=""` when unenriched. Honest and joinable, at the cost of an empty column for early records. The device still appears, so the picker is unharmed.
2. **Re-key the inventory on (name, category)** and treat interface as a most-recently-seen attribute rather than part of the key. Removes the duplicate by construction, but means an entry mutates rather than being immutable.
3. **Accept it** and document the column as best-effort. Cheapest; leaves the disjoint-space mixing in place.

Option 1 is the smallest change consistent with how every other promotable interface value in this codebase is resolved (see #473, where the OTLP resource attribute is set only inside the enrichment-resolved branch for exactly this reason).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One device produces one inventory row regardless of when in the process lifetime it was first seen
- [ ] The `interface` label is unambiguously one label space, or documented as best-effort with the reason
- [ ] The test and its explanatory comment agree
- [ ] A regression test covers the pre-enrichment-then-enriched sequence for the same device
- [ ] Full gate green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check`

Found by live verification of #474 (see https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/474#issuecomment-5096952118).

comments.body:
## Verdict after working it through: option 2, and option 1 does not actually work

Recording this before implementing, because option 1 reads as the obvious minimal fix and it is wrong.

**Option 1 (resolved name only, empty when unenriched) does not remove the duplicate.** It only changes what the stale row says. A device first seen pre-enrichment gets `interface=""`; when the snapshot loads, `(<host-35>, camera, "LAN")` is inserted as a *new* key while `(<host-35>, camera, "")` sits out its 24h TTL. Two rows, same as today, just with an emptier first column.

**Skipping unenriched records entirely** — the other tempting minimal fix — is worse than the bug. If the enrichment snapshot never loads, or a device sits on an interface absent from the box's config, the inventory stays empty and the picker silently shows nothing. Trading intermittent duplicate rows for a picker that can break completely is a bad trade.

**Option 2 is the only one that fixes it by construction.** The duplicate exists because a mutable attribute is part of an immutable key. Interface and category are properties *of* a device, observed over time; the device is the entity. So key on the device name and carry category and interface as last-seen values, last-write-wins. One row per device, no dependence on enrichment being up, and a device that genuinely moves segments updates its row instead of forking one.

This is also just what an info metric means: one series per entity, labels describing its current state.

Requires generalising `boundedInventory` to carry a value alongside the key. Small change, and the type is two commits old with one caller.

Fixed in `96a35b7`, pushed to `main` — auto-closed by the commit.

Implemented option 2 as decided above. `boundedInventory` is now `[K comparable, V any]`: identity is the key, everything observed about the entity is the value, last write wins. The Zenarmor inventory keys on `device_name` with `{category, interface}` as the value.

The derive-time fallback to the raw kernel device **stays**, and is now safe — the row corrects itself the moment enrichment resolves, instead of forking. That keeps the picker working even if the enrichment snapshot never loads.

## Verification

Three regression tests, and I mutation-checked all three rather than trusting that they were meaningful — temporarily inverting `seen()` to first-write-wins made every one of them fail, and restoring it made them pass:

- `TestBoundedInventory_ValueIsLastWriteWinsNotASecondEntry` — the primitive
- `TestLogEventsCollector_ZenarmorDeviceIsOneRowAcrossEnrichment` — the exact live scenario, `<host-35>/ixl0` then `<host-35>/LAN`, asserting one row carrying `LAN`
- `TestLogEventStore_ZenarmorDeviceCategoryIsLastWriteWins` — the same for a reclassified category

Plus `TestBoundedInventory_ValueUpdateRefreshesTheClock`, since an attribute update has to refresh the expiry too or a device whose interface keeps changing would expire on its first sighting.

Full gate green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] One device produces one inventory row regardless of when it was first seen
- [x] The `interface` label is unambiguously one label space — it converges on the description space once enrichment resolves, and the fallback is documented as the deliberate fail-open behaviour
- [x] The test and its explanatory comment agree
- [x] Regression test covers the pre-enrichment-then-enriched sequence for the same device
- [x] Full gate green

Existing duplicate rows on the live stack will age out within 24h of the next deploy; no manual cleanup needed.

title: fix(logship): Zenarmor device inventory records a device twice when enrichment has not loaded

body:
## Problem

Zenarmor log shipping is **~6.2 GB/day** and 98.7% of the entire Grafana Cloud Loki tenant's volume. Each line carries the same payload roughly **twice**: the full upstream JSON as the log body, *and* ~50 of that same JSON's fields re-extracted into structured metadata.

Structured metadata is billed as ingested volume, so this is close to a 2× multiplier on the largest log source in the estate.

## Measured evidence

Live `grafanacloud-logs`, 2026-07-27, 6h window:

| scope | lines | bytes | mean body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service_name="opnsense-exporter"` total | 2,100,164 | 1.63 GB | 775 B |
| └ `opnsense_source="zenarmor"` | — | **1.54 GB** (95%) | — |
| └ `opnsense_source="syslog"` | — | 85.7 MB | — |

By subsystem: flow 995 MB, dns 257 MB, tls 200 MB, web 96.9 MB, firewall 60.4 MB, audit 16.2 MB.

Structured-metadata key counts and mean body size, per subsystem sample:

| subsystem | metadata keys | mean body |
|---|---|---|
| flow | **55** | 2,033 B |
| web | 51 | 2,111 B |
| dns | 49 | 1,924 B |
| tls | 45 | 1,811 B |

A single `dns` line's body is the complete upstream record — including nested `src_geoip`/`dst_geoip` objects with latitude, longitude and a duplicated `location{lat,lon}` — while structured metadata separately carries `dst_geoip_latitude`, `dst_geoip_longitude`, `dst_geoip_city_name`, `dst_geoip_country_name`, `dst_geoip_country_code2` and so on for both directions.

## Candidate reductions, cheapest first

None of these are decided; this issue is to pick among them with measurement.

1. **Drop the redundant body.** If structured metadata already carries every field a query needs, the body is dead weight at ~2 KB/line. Emitting a compact summary line (or an empty body) instead would roughly halve Zenarmor volume on its own. Needs an audit of what actually reads the body — the merged Zenarmor panels from #435 all filter and aggregate on structured metadata, not body text.
2. **Prune duplicated geo precision.** `*_latitude`/`*_longitude` for both src and dst are 4 keys of ~18 significant figures each per line, and the dashboard uses country/city, not coordinates. `src_geoip_*` measured 1–2 distinct values across a 300-line sample, because the source is always the local network.
3. **Prune single-valued metadata.** `organization`, `policyid`, `interface`, `scope_name`, `severity_number`, `severity_text`, `detected_level` measured **1 distinct value each** over a 300-line sample. `scope_name` alone is a 48-byte constant (`github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/logship`) repeated on every one of ~2.1M lines per 6h.
4. **Reconsider `observed_timestamp` as metadata** — measured distinct-per-line by construction, so it never aggregates and is already available as the entry timestamp.

## Non-goals

- **Not** a label-promotion change. #473 covers promotion; promotion does not reduce ingest billing at all, it only changes query scan. The two are independent.
- Not a sampling or drop-rules change. Adaptive Logs drop rules are a tenant-side lever; this issue is about not shipping redundant bytes in the first place.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Measured baseline recorded: bytes/line split between body and structured metadata (per subsystem)
- [ ] An explicit decision on the body, with the reason, and an audit showing nothing queries what is removed
- [ ] Single-valued and duplicated-precision metadata keys either removed or justified in a code comment
- [ ] Re-measured after the change against the same 6h window shape, with the before/after in a closing comment
- [ ] No loss of any field consumed by the Zenarmor tab, its merged panels (#435), or the exported Zenarmor metrics

## Context

Filed from the cross-project Loki assessment (2026-07-27) that produced #473 and #474. Flagged there as the real cost lever, deliberately kept out of that scope: #473 is query ergonomics, this is volume.

comments.body:
## Closed by `e3a957c` — 0.58 GB/day removed; body deliberately kept

### Correction to the issue's baseline, worth carrying forward

`bytes_over_time` counts the **log line only**. The "6.2 GB/day / 1.54 GB per 6h" in the body is therefore **body-only**; real ingested volume is body **plus** structured metadata, and structured metadata is billed the same way. Also, Zenarmor has **four** live families, not six — `gcx datasources loki series --match '{opnsense_source="zenarmor"}'` returns 41 streams over flow/web/dns/tls only. The body's `firewall 60.4 MB` and `audit 16.2 MB` are **syslog**-source subsystems, not Zenarmor.

### Measured baseline (live `grafanacloud-logs`, 6h window, 2026-07-28)

| family | lines/6h | body B/line | metadata B/line | total B/line | metadata share | ingest/6h |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flow | 405,448 | 2,020 | 1,259 | 3,279 | 38.4% | 1,329 MB |
| dns | 96,312 | 1,916 | 1,156 | 3,071 | 37.7% | 296 MB |
| tls | 87,833 | 1,792 | 1,137 | 2,930 | 38.9% | 257 MB |
| web | 38,343 | 2,129 | 1,199 | 3,328 | 35.7% | 128 MB |
| **total** | **627,936** | **1,979** | **1,223** | **3,201** | **38.2%** | **2,010 MB** |

**8.04 GB/day — 4.97 GB body + 3.07 GB structured metadata.** So the issue's "roughly twice" framing is close: metadata is 38% of ingest, not 50%, because the body is bigger than the re-extraction.

### Consumer audit — nothing filters or aggregates on the body

Every shipped Loki query was extracted programmatically from `grafana/**/*.py`. The complete set of structured-metadata keys any panel touches: `app_name`, `device_name`, `domain_category`, `dst_geoip_country_name`, `dst_nbytes`, `host`, `http_status_code`, `ja3`, `opnsense_subsystem`, `query`, `rcode`, `server_name`, `uri`, `user_agent`, plus the annotation `*_event` keys (syslog only).

- **Exactly one line filter exists in the entire dashboard build**, and it is on structured metadata, not body text — `grafana/tabs/zenarmor.py:72` `'| uri!~"/zenarmor_.*/_bulk"'`. No `|=`, `|~`, `| json`, `| logfmt` or `line_format` anywhere else.
- The only body consumer is a **display** panel, `zenarmor.py:216` `b.logs("Raw Zenarmor Records", ...)`. It renders lines for a human; it does not query them.
- **No alert rule issues a Loki query at all.** `build_rules.py` mentions Loki only in alert prose.
- Exported Zenarmor metrics read the attribute map, never the body — `internal/logship/zenarmor/derive.go:21-59`. No geo, no `organization`, no `policyid`.

### Removed — 231 B/line

| key | distinct in sample | B/line | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src`/`dst_geoip.latitude`/`.longitude` | 2 / 55 | 148 | ~17 significant figures for a precision nothing consumes; every geo consumer ranks country or city, and Zenarmor sends each pair **twice** (flat + nested `location{lat,lon}`) |
| `scope_name` | **1** | 57 | Loki appends the OTLP instrumentation scope name as metadata on every record, gated only on non-empty; ours was this module's import path |
| `organization` | **1** | 17 | no panel, alert or derived metric reads it |
| `policyid` | **1** | 9 | same |

**≈ 0.58 GB/day, 8.04 → 7.46 GB/day (-7.2%).** All four remain in the log body verbatim.

### Kept, each justified in a comment next to it

"Measured single-valued" is a property of this box, not always of the field, so the ones that survived say why in the code:

- **`interface`** (kernel `ixl0`) — `derive.go:25` reads it as the fallback for the metric's interface label when enrichment cannot resolve the friendly name. Single-valued here because this box has one Zenarmor-facing NIC.
- **`severity_number`/`severity_text`** (33 B/line) — single-valued in a sample drawn from `action="pass"` streams. `SeverityWarn` is what a blocked record and every syslog error carry, and it is what Loki's level detection reads. 0.4% of volume for the estate's only severity signal.
- **`interface_name`, `device_category`** (~95 MB/day) — byte-identical duplicates of the promoted index labels, kept deliberately so the `| interface_name=` filters #473 preserved keep working.

### Two that cannot be removed from this side

Verified against Loki source (`pkg/loghttp/push/otlplabels/labels.go`), not inferred:

- **`observed_timestamp`** (37 B/line ≈ 93 MB/day) — Loki emits it whenever both timestamps are set, and the Go SDK stamps `ObservedTimestamp` itself at `Emit`. The only way to suppress it is to stop setting the **event** time, which would replace every flow's close time with our receive time. Tenant-side lever only.
- **`detected_level`** (18 B/line ≈ 45 MB/day) — not in our OTLP output at all; Loki's distributor adds it via log-level discovery.

### The body: measured, put to the owner, deliberately kept

| option | body/day | total/day | saved vs 7.46 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **V0 keep as-is (chosen)** | 4.97 | 7.46 | — |
| V1 drop `src_geoip`/`dst_geoip`/`device` objects | 2.77 | 5.25 | -30% |
| V2 V1 + drop empty/zero-valued keys | 2.17 | 4.65 | -38% |
| V3 compact to only fields not already in metadata | 0.65 | 3.13 | -58% |
| V4 empty body | 0.00 | 2.48 | -67% |

Only about **0.65 GB/day of the body is data that exists nowhere else** — `start_time`/`end_time`, `tcp_flags`, `session_id`, `tags`, `handshake_result`, `dst_dir`/`src_dir`, `overlay_transport_type`, `cloud_policyid` and similar. The remaining 4.3 GB/day is the geo/device sub-objects (2.4 GB) and flat keys byte-identical to a metadata value (1.8 GB).

**Owner chose V0.** The body is the lossless safety net that lets the rest of the parser clamp, bucket and drop things without losing data, and `parse.go`'s "the raw line, not a re-encoding" contract fails in the dangerous direction if broken: a field Zenarmor adds in a future release would be silently dropped rather than shipped. If 7.46 GB/day needs to come down further, the next lever is `--logs.zenarmor.families`/`--logs.zenarmor.exclude` (flow alone is 66% of everything) or tenant-side Adaptive Logs — both explicitly out of scope here.

### Breaking

`--logs.zenarmor.exclude` rules naming `organization` or `policyid` now **fail at startup** as unknown fields. Such a rule was always either a no-op or a total drop, since both carry exactly one value per deployment. `docs/upgrading.md` entry added; commit is `!`-marked with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Measured baseline recorded: bytes/line split between body and structured metadata, per subsystem
- [x] An explicit decision on the body, with the reason, and an audit showing nothing queries what is removed
- [x] Single-valued and duplicated-precision keys either removed or justified in a code comment
- [ ] **Re-measured after the change against the same 6h window** — blocked on deployment, see below
- [x] No loss of any field consumed by the Zenarmor tab, its merged panels (#435), or the exported Zenarmor metrics

### Why one box is unticked

The re-measure needs the new build shipping. Live `opnsense_exporter_build_info` still reports `46e90f5`; the `:main` edge image carrying `e3a957c` is still building, and watchtower pulls hourly. **Re-run the per-family `bytes_over_time` and the metadata key-set on a Zenarmor record once the deployed version reports `e3a957c` or later**; the four removed keys being absent from a live record, and the per-line total dropping ~231 B, is the criterion.

### Gate

`go test ./...` clean, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` OK, `golangci-lint run ./...` 0 issues, `make docs-check` passed. Red-then-green evidence for all three new tests is in the commit's history; a mutation check on `TestKnownAttributeKeysCoverEveryKeyTheParserSets` (re-adding `organization` to the list while the parser no longer sets it) confirmed it bites.

## Re-measured live — the last acceptance box is now ticked

`a4340cc` (which carries `e3a957c`) deployed to <host-1> and has been running since 09:01Z. Live `opnsense_exporter_build_info` reports `a4340cc`, so this is the changed build, not the old one.

### The seven keys are gone from a live record

A live `flow` record now carries **48** structured-metadata keys, down from 55. Absent, exactly as intended:

```
scope_name  organization  policyid
src_geoip_latitude  src_geoip_longitude  dst_geoip_latitude  dst_geoip_longitude
```

Every key that was deliberately kept is still present and still queryable — `interface`, `interface_name`, `device_category`, `severity_number`, `severity_text`, `observed_timestamp`, `detected_level`. So nothing was over-pruned, which was the risk worth checking rather than assuming.

The drop is exactly **7 keys on every family**: flow 55→48, dns 49→42, tls 45→38, web 51→44.

### Bytes, same 6h window shape

Note the method, because the obvious approach does not work here: **`bytes_over_time` counts the log line only**, and this change removed *metadata*, not body. A `bytes_over_time` comparison would have shown no improvement at all and looked like a failed change. The figures below are computed from 300-line samples per family, the same way the baseline was.

| family | lines/6h | metadata B/line before | after | delta | keys | MB/6h before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flow | 405,448 | 1,259 | 1,029.5 | **-229.5** | 55→48 | 1,329 | 1,240 |
| dns | 96,312 | 1,156 | 940.7 | **-215.3** | 49→42 | 296 | 276 |
| tls | 87,833 | 1,137 | 910.8 | **-226.2** | 45→38 | 257 | 238 |
| web | 38,343 | 1,199 | 966.4 | **-232.6** | 51→44 | 128 | 120 |
| **total** | **627,936** | | | | | **2,010 MB** | **1,873 MB** |

**8.04 → 7.49 GB/day, saving 0.55 GB/day (-6.8%).** The estimate in the closing comment was 0.58 GB/day, so the prediction held within about 5% — the small shortfall is `dns` losing 215 B/line rather than the predicted 230, since its geo values are shorter on the records sampled.

**The body is unchanged, confirming V0 was applied as decided**: 2,020→2,027.7 (flow), 1,916→1,921.4 (dns), 1,792→1,794.6 (tls), 2,129→2,156.3 (web). Those deltas are sample noise, not drift — no code touched the body.

### Acceptance criteria — all met

- [x] Measured baseline recorded: bytes/line split between body and structured metadata, per subsystem
- [x] An explicit decision on the body, with the reason, and an audit showing nothing queries what is removed
- [x] Single-valued and duplicated-precision metadata keys either removed or justified in a code comment
- [x] **Re-measured after the change against the same 6h window shape, with the before/after above**
- [x] No loss of any field consumed by the Zenarmor tab, its merged panels (#435), or the exported Zenarmor metrics

### One methodological note worth keeping

A false alarm on the way to this: `opnsense_*` briefly appeared to have vanished from Prometheus entirely, which read like a catastrophic regression from this change. It was not — `gcx`'s current context had flipped to an unrelated stack, so the queries were hitting the wrong tenant. **Check `gcx config current-context` before concluding that live data has disappeared**; `-d grafanacloud-prom` resolves per-context and will happily answer from the wrong stack. Passing `--context cloud` explicitly is the safe form.

title: perf(logship): Zenarmor lines ship the same payload twice — body plus ~50 re-extracted metadata keys

body:
## Problem

The Zenarmor tab's `$zenarmor_client` variable is a **TextVariable** — a free-text regex box — because the field it filters on, `device_name`, is Loki **structured metadata** and cannot be enumerated. `label_values()` returns nothing for it: it is not among the datasource's 44 label names. (This is also why the retired companion dashboard's `Device` query variable could never have populated; see #435.)

So an operator has to already know a device's name to filter by it.

## Why not fix it by promoting `device_name`

That was assessed and rejected in #473. It measures 273 resource combinations at 1h (~400–600 realistic), would need `maxLogResources` raised to ≥1024 with 400+ LoggerProviders, and `device_name` is not a closed set — live values include `10-0-0-5.<hash-7>.plex.direct`, i.e. Plex DNS names. Promoting it also risks the cap-overflow failure mode in #473 where the three existing `opnsense.*` labels are silently dropped.

## Proposed change

Solve it from **Prometheus** instead, with no Loki label and no stream growth: add a bounded info metric

```
opnsense_zenarmor_device_info{device_name, device_category, interface} 1
```

`device_name` measured **154 distinct over 24h** and is saturating (119 → 145 → 154), so this is ~154 series — negligible. The picker then becomes a normal query variable over `label_values(opnsense_zenarmor_device_info, device_name)`, and the dashboard keeps filtering Loki by structured metadata exactly as it does now (`| device_name=~"$zenarmor_client"`), which already works.

This follows the pattern already proven by `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total`, which carries `interface`, `category`, `action`, `rcode` and `status_class` but has no device dimension today.

## Scope

- Emit the info metric from the Zenarmor log-shipping path's device inventory, gauge-style, value `1`.
- Bound it explicitly: cap the tracked device set and expire entries, so a churning DNS-derived name cannot grow it without limit. State the cap and the expiry in the code comment.
- Convert `$zenarmor_client` from `TextVariable` to a query variable in `grafana/tabs/zenarmor.py`, keeping the existing structured-metadata filter unchanged.
- `test_cold_load_budget.py` counts query variables and subtracts `TextVariable` as free; converting one adds a round trip to cold load, so re-check the census and the `MAX_LOAD_VARIABLES` budget in the same change.
- `test_zenarmor_tab.py` pins the textbox rationale — update it with the new reason rather than deleting the assertion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `opnsense_zenarmor_device_info` exists, is bounded with a stated cap and expiry, and is in the generated metric catalogue
- [ ] `$zenarmor_client` is a query variable and populates against the live stack
- [ ] The Loki filter still matches on structured metadata; no promotion required
- [ ] Cold-load census and budget re-checked and updated with the measured figure
- [ ] Full gate green including `make docs-check` and `make grafana-check`

## Context

Filed from the cross-project Loki label-promotion assessment (2026-07-27) that produced #473. The two are independent: #473 promotes bounded shape dimensions, this one fixes enumeration without a label. Neither depends on the other.

comments.body:
Shipped in `e543af8`, pushed to `main` — issue auto-closed by the commit.

## One deviation from the body, deliberate

The metric is **`opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_device_info`**, not `opnsense_zenarmor_device_info`. `zenarmor` is not a collector subsystem in this repo; Zenarmor's derived Prometheus metrics live in the `log_events` collector, next to `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total`. Reusing that subsystem needs no new subsystem const, no new disable flag, no new collector file and no `main.go` wiring — a whole collector for one info metric would have been disproportionate. Everything else follows the body.

## What landed

**`internal/collector/boundedinventory.go` (new)** — the bound needed a new primitive, and the reason is worth recording. `cappedCounter` is cumulative: a key that stops being observed must keep its total, so the map never shrinks and a budget alone is a one-way ratchet. An inventory answers "what is here now", so entries have to leave *and give their slot back* — otherwise one burst of churn wedges it for the life of the process and a genuinely new device never appears again. `boundedInventory` adds last-seen expiry to the same insert-time budget. `TestBoundedInventory_ExpiryFreesBudget` pins exactly that.

**`internal/collector/logevents.go`** — `zenDeviceKey`, the inventory, the descriptor and the emit path. Bounds:
- **512 devices** (~3x the measured 154, which was saturating 119 → 145 → 154 over 24h)
- **24h TTL** from last sighting — long on purpose; the picker's job is to list devices worth investigating, and a laptop seen this morning is still worth offering this evening
- refusals counted as `opnsense_log_events_cardinality_capped_total{family="zenarmor_device"}`, reusing the existing per-family saturation pair so a truncated inventory needs no metric of its own

**`internal/logship/logmetrics.go` + `zenarmor/derive.go`** — fed through a **new `ObserveZenarmorDevice` sink method**, not a third field on `ZenarmorObservation`. That struct is the counter's label tuple and carries an explicit "device_name must never join it" rule; on the counter the name would multiply through all seven dimensions, whereas here it costs one series per device. A record with no device is skipped — an empty name would be a permanent empty-named series reading as a real entry on the picker.

**`grafana/tabs/zenarmor.py`** — `$zenarmor_client` is now a QueryVariable over `label_values(opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_device_info{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}, device_name)`, instance-scoped like `$interface`. `allValue=".+"` so an untouched dashboard still filters nothing, matching the old textbox default. **`CLIENT_FILTER` is untouched** — the Loki panels still match `| device_name=~"$zenarmor_client"` on structured metadata, which already worked. Plus a `Zenarmor Devices` table panel (required by the coverage gate; also a useful inventory view).

**Docs** — a "device inventory" section in `docs/zenarmor-receiver.md` stating both bounds, why each one matters on its own, and why `device_name` is deliberately absent from the counter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The metric exists, is bounded with a stated cap and expiry, and is in the generated catalogue (837 → 838 metrics)
- [x] `$zenarmor_client` is a query variable — **populates against the live stack pending deploy**, see below
- [x] The Loki filter still matches on structured metadata; no promotion required
- [x] Cold-load census re-checked and updated with the **measured** figure — load variables 104 → 105, total cold-load queries 136 → 137. Both still fit the existing ceilings (112 / 145), so only the measured numbers moved: a budget quietly raised stops being a guard.
- [x] Full gate green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check`

`test_zenarmor_tab.py`'s textbox-rationale assertion was updated rather than deleted, as the body asked — it now asserts the QueryVariable and its exact query, and still asserts the Loki panels filter on structured metadata. The #435 finding it recorded is preserved in the rewritten rationale: `label_values()` against **Loki** still returns nothing for `device_name`, which is precisely why the picker is populated from Prometheus instead.

## Pending

The picker cannot populate until <host-1> runs a build containing this commit (watchtower pulls `:main` hourly). Once it does, `label_values(opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_device_info, device_name)` should return on the order of 154 devices. The dashboard also does not self-update — it needs pushing to `gc-gitsync-m7kni` by hand.

## Verified live

<host-1> picked up `e543af8`, so the metric is now on the stack:

```
count(opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_device_info)                              =>  85
opnsense_log_events_cardinality_capped_total{family="zenarmor_device"}     =>  0
```

85 devices and nothing refused, so the 512 cap has ample headroom against the measured 154 — as expected, the inventory is still filling after the restart and the 24h TTL means it accrues rather than appearing all at once.

Dashboard deployed to GitSync in rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni@`2db8a03`; the picker is a real dropdown now.

## One defect this surfaced, filed as a follow-up

Sample rows:

| device_name | device_category | interface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <host-35> | camera | **ixl0** |
| <host-35> | camera | **LAN** |
| C4E7AE021595 | iot | LAN |

`<host-35>` is present twice — once under the kernel device `ixl0`, once under the description-space `LAN`. `observeDerived` resolves the interface as `firstNonEmpty(interface.name, interface)`, so a record parsed before the enrichment snapshot had loaded records the raw device, and that row then persists for the full 24h TTL alongside the enriched one.

The picker itself is unaffected — `label_values(..., device_name)` dedupes to one `<host-35>` — but the inventory table shows duplicate rows and the series count is inflated. The fallback is consistent with how `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total` already labels `interface`, so this is not a regression, but it is wrong for a per-device inventory.

Tracked separately rather than widened into this issue.

title: feat(grafana): make the Zenarmor client picker enumerable via a bounded device info metric

body:
## Problem

The exporter ships ~6.5 GB/day of logs (98.7% of the whole Loki tenant), and the only dimensions an operator can select a **stream** on are `opnsense_source`, `opnsense_subsystem` and `opnsense_action` — 19 live streams. Every dimension an investigation actually starts from (which device, which interface) is a record attribute in structured metadata, so a query for one device still scans the whole subsystem.

## The constraint (verified)

Loki's `index_label` action exists **only** under `otlp_config.resource_attributes`; `log_attributes` accepts `structured_metadata` or `drop` and nothing else. So a field must be on the **OTLP resource** to be promotable, and this exporter's log resource carries exactly six attributes: `service.name`, `service.version`, `service.instance.id`, `opnsense.source`, `opnsense.subsystem`, `opnsense.action`.

## Chosen scope (owner decision, 2026-07-27)

Hoist **two bounded dimensions** onto the log resource and promote them tenant-side:

- `opnsense.device_category` — from the Zenarmor record's `device_category`
- `opnsense.interface` — from the Zenarmor record's `interface_name` (the description space: `LAN`, `IOT`, `MGMT`, matching the dashboard's `$interface`, **not** the kernel device space per #98)

Both are empty on syslog records; omit-when-empty, exactly as `opnsense.action` already does.

## Measured cardinality — the reason these two and not the tempting ones

Live `grafanacloud-logs`, three windows so churn is visible:

| attribute | 1h | 12h | 24h | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `device_category` | 10 | – | 10 | flat — **promote** |
| `interface_name` | 7 | – | 8 | flat — **promote** |
| `app_category` | 27 | – | 32 | saturating — maybe later |
| `device_name` | 119 | 145 | 154 | saturating but large; see below |
| `domain_category` | 30 | – | 47 | still climbing — reject |
| `dst_geoip_country_code2` | 40 | 51 | 72 | climbing toward ~200 — reject |
| `app_name` | 138 | 245 | **345** | not converging — **reject** |

## The trap: `maxLogResources = 64` must be raised in the same change

`sink_otlp.go` builds one `LoggerProvider` per distinct resource and caps it at `maxLogResources = 64`. **Past the cap it degrades to the base resource, dropping `opnsense.source`/`subsystem`/`action` entirely** (`sink_otlp.go:411`). So overshooting does not merely add streams — it silently destroys the three labels that already work.

Measured observed combinations over 1h:

| resource key | combos |
|---|---|
| current (source, subsystem, action) | 16 |
| + `interface_name` | 37 |
| + `device_category` | 44 |
| + **both (this issue)** | **79 — over the cap** |
| + `device_category` + `flow_interface` | 65 — over the cap |
| + `device_name` | 273 |

**79 > 64**, so this change is incorrect without raising the cap. Raise `maxLogResources` to **256**: ~3× the measured steady state, still a hard bound against a future source putting something wire-derived behind one of these keys.

## Explicitly rejected: promoting `device_name`

It measures 273 combinations at 1h (~400–600 realistic), needs the cap at ≥1024 and 400+ LoggerProviders each with its own batch processor, and it is **not a closed set** — live values include `10-0-0-5.<hash-7>.plex.direct`, i.e. Plex-generated DNS names rather than device names. That violates the closed-set rule in `record.go`.

The Zenarmor client picker that motivated looking at `device_name` should instead be solved without a Loki label, by a bounded info metric — tracked separately in #474.

## Scope

- Extend `resourceKey` with the two fields and hoist them off the record in the OTLP sink, mirroring how `action` is handled (omit when empty).
- Raise `maxLogResources` to 256 and update the comment's arithmetic — it currently reasons from "~4 sources and ~22 subsystems", which stops being the whole story.
- Keep both keys namespaced (`opnsense.*`) for the collision-safety reason already documented in `record.go`.
- Keep the values available as structured metadata as they are today, so nothing breaks before the tenant opts in. An unpromoted resource attribute lands in structured metadata, so this change is query-neutral until promotion.
- Assert the closed-set rule: a test must fail if either key can carry a wire-derived value.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `opnsense.device_category` and `opnsense.interface` are on the log resource, omitted when empty
- [ ] `maxLogResources` is 256 and a test still proves the cap holds and degrades safely
- [ ] A test pins the observed resource-key count for a representative batch, so a future high-cardinality key trips CI rather than the live cap
- [ ] Existing queries filtering these values as structured metadata keep working
- [ ] Docs state that promotion is a tenant-side opt-in costing the exporter nothing
- [ ] Full gate green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check`
- [ ] Verified live after the tenant promotion: stream count for `{service_name="opnsense-exporter"}` lands near the measured 79 and the three existing labels are still present on every stream

## Maintainer-only step (tenant, not repo)

Promotion is configured in Grafana Cloud (Logs → OTLP label promotion). The 15 slots are shared across the whole Loki tenant and keyed by attribute name; currently populated: `service_name`, `service_instance_id`, `opnsense_source`, `opnsense_subsystem`, `opnsense_action`. This change takes it to 7 of 15.

## Note on cost

This is a query-ergonomics change, **not** a cost reduction. Ingest is billed on volume; labels only change query scan. The cost lever on the 6.2 GB/day of Zenarmor traffic is that each line ships a ~2 KB JSON body *and* re-extracts ~50 of that body's own fields into structured metadata — carrying the payload roughly twice. That is #475 and is not in scope here.

comments.body:
Shipped in `ea161c7`, pushed to `main` — issue auto-closed by the commit.

## What landed

**`internal/logship/shape_attrs.go` (new)** — `AttrDeviceCategory` = `opnsense.device_category`, `AttrInterface` = `opnsense.interface`, with the doctrine for why each is a closed set (they are closed for *different* reasons; the two guards are not interchangeable).

**`internal/logship/sink_otlp.go`** — `resourceKey` extended to five fields; both hoisted onto the OTLP resource and stripped from the record, omit-when-empty exactly as `opnsense.action` already does; `sortResourceKeys` extended so flush order stays deterministic. **`maxLogResources` 64 → 256** in the same commit, per the trap in the body — at 64 the sink would have degraded to the base resource and silently dropped the three labels that already work.

**`internal/logship/zenarmor/devicecategory.go` (new)** — `clampDeviceCategory`, same explicit-map shape as `zenAlertSeverities`. The vocabulary is the 9 values observed live across five 1h probes spanning 24h (2026-07-27): `camera`, `iot`, `laptop`, `mobile`, `multimedia`, `network`, `other`, `printer`, `server`. Deliberately **not** padded with plausible-sounding extras — unknowns fold into Zenarmor's own `other` bucket, which is what that bucket means, and inventing taxonomy members would encode a shape upstream may not produce.

**`internal/logship/zenarmor/parse.go`** — sets the clamped category, and sets the interface **only inside the enrichment-resolved branch**. That placement is the closed-set guard: an interface the box does not have never resolves, so the wire cannot introduce a value at all, and no clamp is needed.

**Docs** — `docs/log-shipping.md` label-model table + promotion section (renamed to cover all five attributes), `docs/zenarmor-receiver.md` label model. Both state that promotion is a tenant-side opt-in costing the exporter nothing, that it is **not** a cost reduction (Loki bills on volume), and that Grafana Cloud's slots are shared across the whole tenant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `opnsense.device_category` and `opnsense.interface` on the log resource, omitted when empty
- [x] `maxLogResources` is 256; `TestOTLPSink_ResourceCountIsCapped` still proves the cap holds and degrades without dropping records
- [x] Resource-key count pinned — `observedResourceCombos = 79` + `TestOTLPSink_ResourceKeyBudgetHasHeadroomOverObserved`, which asserts both that the cap keeps 3x headroom over the measured figure and that the measured shape builds 79 undegraded providers. A future wide-vocabulary key trips CI, not the live cap.
- [x] Existing structured-metadata queries keep working — the lane's verbatim `device.category` / `interface.name` are a different key space and are untouched; asserted directly in `TestOTLPSink_HoistsDeviceCategoryAndInterfaceOntoResource`
- [x] Docs state promotion is a tenant-side opt-in costing the exporter nothing
- [x] Closed-set rule asserted — `TestParseDoc_DeviceCategoryPromotedAndClamped` (free text and injection-shaped input fold to `other`), `TestParseDoc_InterfacePromotedFromEnrichmentOnly` (an interface the box does not have is not promotable)
- [x] Full gate green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check`
- [ ] **Verified live after the tenant promotion** — see below

Two side effects worth recording: the existing `TestKnownAttributeKeysCoverEveryKeyTheParserSets` guard caught the new `set()` calls before I added them to `KnownAttributeKeys`, which is exactly what it exists for; and both keys are now valid `--logs.zenarmor.exclude` fields, consistent with `opnsense.action`.

## Still pending, and not blocked on this repo

The last box needs the **tenant-side promotion step** (Grafana Cloud → Logs → OTLP label promotion), which is submitted but not applied. Nothing is broken until it lands: an unpromoted resource attribute goes to structured metadata, so the change is query-neutral at deploy time. The label genuinely cannot be observed live before then — this is not something to keep re-checking against the current stack.

Once promotion applies, confirm: stream count for `{service_name="opnsense-exporter"}` lands near 79, and `opnsense_source` / `opnsense_subsystem` / `opnsense_action` are still present on **every** stream (their absence is the cap-degrade signature, and `opnsense_exporter_logs_resource_capped_total` is the metric that would show it).

## Live verification — promotion is PARTIALLY applied

Checked against the tenant just now. Deployed exporter is `4c529e3` (`opnsense_exporter_build_info`), which is well past `ea161c7`, so all three new resource attributes are being emitted.

**Promoted today** (confirmed by `loki series`, which returns stream labels only — structured metadata cannot appear there):

```
{opnsense_action="pass", opnsense_source="zenarmor", opnsense_subsystem="flow",
 service_instance_id="opnsense", service_name="opnsense-exporter"}
```

- `opnsense_action` — **new, and working.** It was not in the 2026-07-15 config, so this proves the updated tenant config has been applied at least in part.
- `opnsense_source`, `opnsense_subsystem` — as before.
- `service_name`, `service_instance_id` — **still present.** This is the important negative result: `ignore_defaults: true` did NOT strip them, so the breakage I flagged on #477 did not happen.

**NOT promoted:** `opnsense_device_category` and `opnsense_interface` appear nowhere in the tenant's label-name list. Since the emitting build is deployed, they are landing as structured metadata rather than labels.

Stream count is **16** for `{opnsense_source=~".+"}`, not the ~79 expected once all seven keys are promoted — consistent with exactly one new dimension having been added.

### Most likely cause, and it is the one already flagged

The draft config reviewed on #477 named these two as **`interface_name`** and bare **`device_category`**. Neither matches: the attributes are sent as `opnsense.interface` and `opnsense.device_category`, and **Loki matches the OTLP attribute name as sent** and does the dot-to-underscore conversion itself. `interface_name` and `device_category` match nothing, while `opnsense.action` — which the draft happened to spell in a form that resolved — went through. That is exactly the split we are seeing.

The alternative reading is that the change is simply still propagating (self-serve changes return `pending` and can take up to ~2 business days). Both are consistent with the evidence; the naming split is the better explanation because a partial application landing exactly on the correctly-named key is a coincidence otherwise.

### Correct block

Note the self-serve `PUT` **fully replaces** the tenant `otlp_config` — it is GET-merge-PUT, never a partial — so this list must be complete, not just the two missing keys:

```yaml
otlp_config:
  resource_attributes:
    ignore_defaults: true
    attributes_config:
      - action: index_label
        attributes:
          - service.name
          - service.instance.id
          - opnsense.source
          - opnsense.subsystem
          - opnsense.action
          - opnsense.device_category
          - opnsense.interface
```

Re-verify after it applies: stream count near 79, **and** `opnsense_source`/`opnsense_subsystem`/`opnsense_action` still present on every stream. Their disappearance would mean the 256-resource cap is degrading, which silently drops ALL `opnsense.*` attributes rather than failing loudly.

## Promotion verified live — all five keys, no cap degradation

The corrected config is applied. Confirmed against the tenant just now.

**All five `opnsense_*` keys are index labels:**

```
opnsense_action, opnsense_device_category, opnsense_interface,
opnsense_source, opnsense_subsystem
```

**55 streams** on `{opnsense_source=~".+"}`, with the presence breakdown:

| label | streams |
|---|---|
| `opnsense_source` | **55/55** |
| `opnsense_subsystem` | **55/55** |
| `service_name` | **55/55** |
| `service_instance_id` | **55/55** |
| `opnsense_action` | 48/55 |
| `opnsense_device_category` | 42/55 |
| `opnsense_interface` | 31/55 |

**The cap-degrade check passes.** `opnsense_source` and `opnsense_subsystem` are on every single stream — zero missing. That was the failure mode worth watching for: past `maxLogResources` the sink silently drops **all** `opnsense.*` attributes rather than failing loudly, so partial presence of those two would have been the tell that 256 was still too low. It is not. The 64→256 raise in `ea161c7` was sufficient.

`service_name`/`service_instance_id` also survive at 55/55, so `ignore_defaults: true` did not strip the distributor defaults.

**The partial coverage of the other three is correct, not degradation.** Each is set only where it is meaningful, which is the closed-set guarantee that made them promotable in the first place:

- `opnsense_action` — firewall and Zenarmor records only; a cron or DNS line has no pass/block verdict.
- `opnsense_device_category` — Zenarmor only, clamped to the nine live-measured values.
- `opnsense_interface` — set **only inside the enrichment-resolved branch**, so a record whose interface could not be resolved to a description carries no attribute rather than a kernel name. That placement is deliberately the guard that keeps the label space closed (`LAN`/`IOT`, never `ixl0`).

55 rather than the ~79 estimated: 79 was the cartesian upper bound, and not every source × subsystem × action × category × interface combination actually occurs.

Nothing outstanding on this issue. The cross-poller naming contract remains open as #477.

title: feat(logship): promote device_category and interface to Loki index labels (raise the resource cap first)

body:
## Problem

`service_version` is a label on **552 metric names** pushed by this exporter, including every `go_*` runtime metric and `target_info`. Every redeploy therefore mints a fresh series set: for the query-lookback window after a restart, old-version and new-version series coexist, so any `sum`-style panel transiently double-counts, and active-series cardinality grows by the number of versions ever seen.

Measured live on `grafanacloud-prom`, 2026-07-27:

```
count(group by (__name__) ({job="opnsense-exporter", service_version!=""}))  =>  552
```

The two sibling exporters do **not** have this. Same tenant, same Grafana Cloud OTLP gateway:

| repo | metric names carrying `service_version` | which |
|---|---|---|
| opnsense-exporter | **552** | everything, incl. `go_*` and `target_info` |
| tailscale2otel | 4 | `traces_spanmetrics_*`, `traces_target_info` — Tempo-generated from the **traces** resource, not its metrics |
| graph2otel | **0** | — |

## This supersedes #270, which closed on a false premise

#270 raised exactly this and was closed as **accept + document** (`eee3006`), on the reasoning that the promotion is a Grafana Cloud gateway default "which no exporter-side change can prevent". That reasoning is recorded in `internal/telemetry/resource.go:25` today.

**The gateway behaviour is real; the conclusion drawn from it is wrong.** Grafana Cloud promotes `service.version` *if the resource carries it*. It cannot promote an attribute that is absent. `graph2otel` proves it empirically with 0 affected metric names, and it got there by the split-resource approach in rknightion/graph2otel#104 and rknightion/tailscale2otel#187: **`service.version` on the logs/traces resource, omitted from the metrics resource.**

#270 was internally contradictory rather than blocked — its change list said "keep `service.version` on the OTel resource" while its AC1 said the label must disappear from ordinary series. Given the gateway's behaviour those two cannot both hold, which is what made AC1 look unachievable. Dropping the first for **metrics only** satisfies AC1 and keeps semconv correctness where it matters. #270 also declined a Support request to alter the tenant promote list; that stays declined and is not needed — this is a code fix.

## Change

In `internal/telemetry/resource.go`, stop putting `service.version` on the resource built for the **MeterProvider**. `buildResource` feeds only `sdkmetric.WithResource` (`provider.go:144`); there is no tracer provider in this repo, and the **logs** resource is built independently in `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go:557`, so it is untouched and keeps `service.version` (correct — log records are never summed, and it lands in structured metadata).

Mirror the sibling repos' shape: an explicit `includeServiceVersion bool` parameter, so the omission is a stated decision at the call site rather than a deletion someone re-adds.

## Consequence to accept deliberately

`target_info` loses `service_version` too, since the gateway derives `target_info` from the same resource. Version stays queryable from **`opnsense_exporter_build_info{version, goversion, opnsense_instance}`**, which already exists and is already exported through the OTLP path (verified present live) — join with `group_left` where a panel needs it. This is the Prometheus-native answer the const-block comment already recommends.

## Query safety

No dashboard change is required. The generated dashboard strips deployment identity with `max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (...)`, and `without` on an absent label is a no-op. Keep `service_version` in `grafana/builder.py`'s strip list as belt-and-braces — it also protects against other senders on the tenant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `service.version` is absent from the metrics resource; present on the logs resource
- [ ] A test asserts both halves, so re-adding it to the metrics resource fails CI
- [ ] `opnsense_exporter_build_info` still carries the version and is still exported over OTLP
- [ ] The `resource.go` const-block comment and `docs/configuration.md`'s "Resource attributes and `service_version`" section are corrected — they currently assert the unfixable framing from #270
- [ ] Full gate green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check`
- [ ] Verified live after deploy: `count(group by (__name__) ({job="opnsense-exporter", service_version!=""}))` drops to 0

## Context

Found during a cross-project Loki/Prometheus label assessment of the `m7kni` tenant. Unrelated to the log-label promotion work, but the same promotion mechanic.

body:
## Problem

Every `loki_table()` panel renders its key column as the **whole series label set** rather
than the field the table is about. Rendered from the live dashboard (2026-07-27, generation
7), `Top Applications` reads:

```text
Field                                                        Total
{app_name="Domain Name Resolution", service_instance_id="…    65925
{app_name="STUN", service_instance_id="opnsense"}             57495
{app_name="Secure Web Browsing", service_instance_id="opns…   36459
```

The value is right and the ordering is right, but the column is a serialised label set,
truncated mid-string at any sensible column width, and the instance label is repeated on
every row. `Top DNS Queries` is worse, because a DNS name is long to begin with.

## Why it happens

`Builder.loki_table()` builds `topk(...) → reduce{reducers:[sum], mode:seriesToRows}`. The
reduce transform names each row after the frame it came from, and for a LogQL metric query
that name is the label set. There is no per-label column because nothing splits it into
fields.

## Scope

Affects **all 14** `loki_table()` panels, not just the six merged from the retired Zenarmor
companion in #435 — `Top Blocked Servers`, `Top Talkers by Bytes`, `Blocked by Country`,
`Top JA3 Fingerprints` and the syslog top-N tables render the same way today.

The fix belongs in the shared helper, once: give the reduce output a label-to-field split
(or reshape the query so the ranked label arrives as its own field), pass the field name
through from the call site so the column can be titled (`Application`, `Query`, `Host`), and
keep the instance column as a distinct column rather than smuggling it into the key string —
`test_instance_identity.py` requires the identity to be visible, and it currently is, just
unreadably.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `loki_table()` renders one column for the ranked label and one for the value, each
      titled, with instance identity in its own column.
- [ ] All 14 existing call sites keep working with no per-call-site special cases, and the
      instance-identity and Loki-scoping guards still pass unchanged.
- [ ] Rendered before/after from the published dashboard for at least one long-value table
      (`Top DNS Queries`) and one short-value table (`Destination Countries`).
- [ ] Full gate green.

## Notes

Found by rendering the published dashboard while closing #435, not by reading the manifest —
the same way #470 was found. The generated JSON is valid and the queries are correct, so no
test could have caught this: it is only visible as pixels.

This is presentation-only. Do not change what any query ranks or aggregates while fixing it.
