title: OPNsense live-box canary drift

body:
Follow-up from epic #447. That epic built a second VM for OSPF/OSPFv3 peering, but deliberately made it **Debian 13 + FRR 10.3** rather than OPNsense, because the OSPFv3 payload is generated entirely by the dev box's own `ospf6d` — the peer's vendor is invisible in the response, so a second OPNsense bought zero extra coverage there.

CARP and HA-sync are different: those payloads describe the **peer relationship itself**, so they genuinely require a second OPNsense. Rob has confirmed he wants one.

## What is uncovered today

The `hasync` and `carp` collectors are wired and green, but their interesting states have never been observed live — the dev box has no HA peer, so the code only ever exercises the unconfigured/unreachable branches.

`hasync` (5 metrics), from `api/core/hasync_status/version` and `/services`:

- `opnsense_hasync_remote_reachable`
- `opnsense_hasync_remote_version_match`
- `opnsense_hasync_remote_version_info`
- `opnsense_hasync_remote_services_total`
- `opnsense_hasync_remote_service_running`

Every one of these is meaningless without a peer. `opnsense/hasync_test.go` today pins four *negative* paths — `Unconfigured`, `ResponseFalse` (single-node), `UnconfiguredServices`, and an unreachable case — against exactly one synthetic `hasyncVersionConfiguredFixture`. The committed ledger says so plainly: `hasyncVersion` carries `missingOK` for `message`/`status` with the note *"present only for some HA peer states; box has no HA peer"*. That exemption is currently unfalsifiable.

`carp` (7 metrics) partially works single-node, but the states that matter do not:

- `opnsense_carp_vip_status` — a real MASTER/BACKUP split, and a transition between them
- `opnsense_carp_demotion`, `opnsense_carp_allow`, `opnsense_carp_maintenance_mode` — maintenance mode is only meaningful with somewhere to fail over to
- `opnsense_carp_vips_total`, `..._vip_advbase_seconds`, `..._vip_advskew`

The older testbed audit put the HA peer at ~5 otherwise-unreachable catalogue metrics; with the CARP peer states it is realistically more.

## Scope

- Build a second OPNsense VM on `<host-8>` (VMID 111+ is free; the DVD ISO `OPNsense-26.1.6-dvd-amd64.iso` is already staged on the NFS ISO store).
- Attach it to **`vmbr9` only** — the isolated host-internal bridge with no physical uplink. It must never touch the bridge carrying production. Same rule the #447 peer followed.
- Configure `hasync` between it and VM 102, plus at least one CARP VIP with a deliberate MASTER/BACKUP split.
- Exercise a **failover and a failback**, and maintenance mode, so `vip_status` and `demotion` are observed in more than one state.
- Add the now-reachable paths to `opnsense/testdata/schemas/coverage.json` as `required`, each with its metric families and an exercise recipe. Prune the `hasyncVersion` `missingOK` entry if a real peer proves `message`/`status` are actually present — or keep it with a corrected note naming the specific peer state that omits them.
- Replace the synthetic `hasyncVersionConfiguredFixture` with one derived from a real capture, or state explicitly in the case comment that it stays synthetic and why.

## Worth doing at the same time

- **Cross-version testing.** If the second box tracks a *different* release channel from VM 102 (which is on 26.7 devel), it becomes the only way to test the "current + previous stable" support window by payload shape rather than by reasoning about source. That is directly useful to the drift canary.
- **`opnsense_hasync_remote_version_match`** specifically cannot be exercised as `0` without two boxes on deliberately different versions.
- **`keaLeases4` is currently empty** (no DHCPv4 client on the test VLAN, noted in the coverage ledger). A second box or a v4 host reservation for VM 110 would close that too — cheap to fold in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A second OPNsense VM exists on `vmbr9` only, with `onboot` set and a documented access path (the #447 peer is reached via `pct exec 105 -- ssh ...` because `<host-8>` deliberately has no IP on that bridge — follow the same pattern).
- [ ] `api/core/hasync_status/version` and `/services` return configured, reachable payloads, captured (runner-local, never committed).
- [ ] All 5 `hasync` metrics emit non-trivial values; `remote_version_match` observed as both 1 and 0.
- [ ] `carp_vip_status` observed as MASTER on one box and BACKUP on the other, and observed changing across a failover; maintenance mode observed.
- [ ] `coverage.json` records the newly reachable paths as `required` with recipes; the `hasyncVersion` exemption is either pruned or its note corrected with evidence.
- [ ] A snapshot of VM 102 is taken before the HA config is applied, and the undo steps are documented on this issue.
- [ ] `cmd/apidrift` run after provisioning shows no new breaking drift; any new nested extras are classified (or folded into #457's baseline).
- [ ] Full gate green.

## Traps carried forward from #447

- **`configctl <service> restart` is often required and easy to miss.** The quagga plugin's `reconfigure` rewrote the config correctly but left `watchfrr` on its old daemon list, so endpoints returned `{"response":[]}` for minutes against a valid on-disk config. Expect the same class of thing from hasync/CARP — verify through the API, not by reading config.
- **Root's unix password is blanked on every config write** by design on OPNsense. Use SSH keys; the QEMU guest agent (`qm guest exec`) is the out-of-band path.
- **Snapshots on VM 102 are crash-consistent only** — the guest-fs freeze fails on that VM, and a rollback has never actually been tested.
- **Do not give `<host-8>` an IP on `vmbr9`.** It has IP forwarding and would become a router between the testbed and production.
- Leave netflow **targets** empty. Separately, VM 102 currently has `127.0.0.1:2056` selected, which predates #447 and is worth clearing.
- Production firewall stays strictly read-only and out of scope.

## Not blocking anything

No shipped metric is wrong because of this — the collectors correctly report an unconfigured/unreachable peer. This converts permanently-unexercised code paths and one unfalsifiable exemption into real coverage.

comments.body:
## Done in `4f0da1d` — second OPNsense live, all 12 metrics observed in multiple states

### Topology

```
vmbr9  (isolated host-internal bridge, NO physical uplink, <host-8> has NO IP on it)
  ├── VM 102  opnsense-devel     TESTLAN   OPNsense 27.1.a_40  (devel channel)
  ├── VM 106  opnsense-devel-2   TESTLAN   OPNsense 26.7.1_1   (community/production)
  ├── VM 110  exporter-ospf-peer           (from #447, untouched)
  └── LXC 105 exporter-traffgen            (now a DHCP client — see keaLeases4)

  shared CARP VIP, vhid 9  →  102 = MASTER (advskew 0), 106 = BACKUP (advskew 100)
```

VM 106 has four NICs, all on `vmbr9`, **three with `link_down=1`**. That is deliberate. It is a
byte-for-byte clone of 102's disk, so it boots holding 102's `config.xml` — same addresses, same
tailscale and netbird enrolments, same API keys. Matching the NIC *count* stops OPNsense dropping
into the interactive interface-assignment prompt at boot (which would take the guest agent with
it), and links-down meant it could be stripped of every cloned identity before a single frame left
the guest. Only the TESTLAN NIC is live.

Stripped from the clone before anything was brought up: tailscale and netbird packages and state,
the tailscale interface assignment, LAN/WAN disabled, the TESTVLAN/CPORTAL VLANs disabled so they
cannot collide with 102's on the same bridge, the IPsec ipalias VIP, IPsec/OpenVPN/WireGuard, Kea
and dnsmasq and dhcpd (102 owns DHCP there), and the whole Netflow section. Hostname changed, and
**all three cloned API keys deleted from every user and replaced with box-specific ones** — the
cloned key now returns `401 Authentication Failed` against 106, verified rather than assumed.

### hasync — and 102's existing config had never worked

Both boxes: `pfsyncinterface=opt1`, `pfsyncversion=1400`, `verifypeer=0`, peer pointed at the other
box, `syncitems=''` — nothing is actually synchronised, only the status endpoints are wanted. A
dedicated `hasync` user with `page-all` exists on **both** nodes, because the XML-RPC account is
authenticated on the box being *called*.

102's pre-existing hasync block dated from the original 2026-07-12 build and was **broken**:
`synchronizetoip` pointed at 102's own address, and the endpoint answered
`{"response":"Authentication failed"}`. So the "unconfigured" coverage this issue described was in
fact "misconfigured", which is a different thing and would have kept returning the wrong envelope
forever.

### Observed values

Steady state, cross-version:

```
opnsense_carp_vip_status{...}   1   (102, MASTER)      0   (106, BACKUP)
opnsense_carp_vip_advskew{...}  0   (102)            100   (106)
opnsense_carp_demotion 0 · maintenance_mode 0 · allow 1 · vips_total 1 · advbase_seconds 1
opnsense_hasync_remote_reachable 1
opnsense_hasync_remote_services_total   38 (102)   48 (106)
opnsense_hasync_remote_version_info{local_version="27.1.a_40",remote_version="26.7.1_1"} 1
opnsense_hasync_remote_version_match 0
```

Failover — maintenance mode entered on 102:

```
opnsense_carp_demotion{102} 240 · maintenance_mode{102} 1 · allow{102} 1
opnsense_carp_vip_status{102} 0   ← MASTER → BACKUP
opnsense_carp_vip_status{106} 1   ← BACKUP → MASTER
opnsense_carp_demotion{106} 0     ← demotion is local, not synchronised
```

Two behaviours worth having on the record: **demotion does not clear `allow`**, and **demotion is
not synchronised to the peer**. Failback (toggling again) returned every value to its steady state.

`version_match = 1` was captured before the release skew, while 106 was still an identical clone.
Peer-unreachable was exercised by dropping 106's link, which produced the exception envelope that
had never been captured from a *configured* box:
`{"status":"error","message":"fetch error. remote host down? (Connection timed out after 60009 ms)"}`.

Full smoke, no regression: VM 102 → 685 distinct metric names, zero failed collectors, zero API
errors.

### How `version_match = 0` was reached

There was no newer *devel* snapshot for 102, so upgrading it was not an option. Instead 106's
release family was switched from devel to production and updated 27.1.a_40 → 26.7.1_1, cleanly,
with CARP and hasync surviving the switch. That also gives the drift canary its first
**current-stable** box, which is the harder half of the support window.

Trap: `core/firmware/set` needs its payload **nested under the model name** (`{"firmware":{...}}`).
A flat body returns `{"status":"ok"}` and silently sets nothing.

### The exemption is kept, and its note was backwards

`hasyncVersion`'s `missingOK` on `message`/`status` said *"present only for some HA peer states; box
has no HA peer"* — which implies a real peer would produce them. **A real peer proves the opposite.**
They are the exception envelope, emitted only when the XML-RPC call throws, and absent from the
configured-and-reachable response too. Source: the `version` action echoes `['response' => $payload]`
with neither key on every success path; the only emitters are the `catch` handler and an
unknown-action default the controller can never reach.

A third live shape no fixture had: **a reachable peer with rejected credentials does not throw** —
the endpoint answers `{"response":"Authentication failed"}`, a JSON *string* where success serves an
object. A refactor decoding `response` into `any` would report a live, answering peer as a scrape
failure; `TestFetchHasyncStatus_ResponseString` now pins it.

### Two ledger gaps closed

- **`hasyncServices` `rows[].running`** — a `missingOK` entry. It is a defensive alias upstream has
  never populated on any release, so it can never be present: not box-state, not drift, and without
  an entry the canary reports it every run forever. The live 38-row response from a configured,
  reachable peer is the strongest available evidence because it excludes every other reason a path
  can be missing. `TestFetchHasyncStatus_RunningAliasNeverOnTheWire` pins the alias inert — if the
  effective-running expression is ever "simplified" to prefer it, every stopped service on every real
  box silently flips to 1.
- **`carpStatus` `rows[].mode`** — moved from the not-triaged prose into `knownExtraPaths`. It was
  parked on the theory that `get_vip_status` might return non-CARP VIP types, making `mode` a
  VIP-type label candidate. It does not: `mode` is the constant string `"carp"`, and the box's own
  `ipalias` VIP on `lo0` does not appear in `rows[]` at all.

### Fixtures are now real captures

The header comment records the two things the synthetic ones got wrong. Service rows carry far more
than the consumed keys — `uid`, `pidfile`, nested `configd`/`php` objects, `dns_ports`, `locked` —
so a fixture with only the consumed keys cannot catch a decoder that chokes on a nested object where
it expected a scalar. And **`id` is not a small integer**: real values are config UUIDs, gateway
names and short instance names, so the old `"id": "1"` made the label look numeric when it never is.

### `keaLeases4` closed

The traffgen container's interface was **static**, which is why nothing on the Kea-served segment
ever asked for a lease. Switching it to DHCP was not enough on its own — the legacy ISC `dhcpd` had
restarted and was wildcard-binding UDP/67, starving `kea-dhcp4` of its socket, so `DHCPDISCOVER` drew
no offers at all. Same collision recorded on 2026-07-13; it recurs because dhcpd is only ever
*stopped*, never disabled. Stopping it and restarting Kea produced an offer immediately, and the host
reservation handed back the pinned address, so the IPsec peers that hardcode it are unaffected.

### `cmd/apidrift` after provisioning

```
Probed 174 endpoints: 158 clean, 0 with breaking type drift, 5 with missing paths,
0 with unexpected top-level keys, 14 with unexpected nested keys,
1 absent 404 (0 unexpected, 1 plugin-gated/expected), 0 probe errors, 0 skipped.
```

**No new breaking drift.** New findings are the two ledgered above, plus 16 nested extras on
`hasyncServices` and `keaLeases4` that are **opportunity** and fold into #457's baseline (nested
detection is report-only). Everything else is pre-existing and already ledgered.

### A real defect the second box exposed — filed as #481

The full smoke against 106 fails the `firewall_rule` collector outright:

```
json: cannot unmarshal array into Go struct field firewallRuleStatsResponse.stats
of type map[string]opnsense.firewallRuleStat; body: {"status":"ok","stats":[]}
```

PHP encodes an empty array as `[]` and a populated one as an object, so `stats` changes shape. Verdict
**absorb**. Crucially this is **not** a 26.7 behaviour and not drift — it breaks the whole collector on
**any** release whenever a box has no rule statistics, which a single-box testbed could never reach
because a firewall in service always has stats. Out of scope here; filed as #481.

### Undo for VM 102

Snapshot `pre_460_hasync_carp` predates every change, but it is crash-consistent only (the guest-fs
freeze fails on that VM, as expected) and rollback is still untested — prefer the manual steps:

1. **Fastest full undo, no config change:** stop VM 106. 102 reports `Reachable=false` and the hasync
   collector goes silent again. Everything else keeps working.
2. Delete the `hasync` user.
3. Clear `$config['hasync']` — it was never doing anything on 102 anyway.
4. **CARP:** nothing to undo; 102's VIP is unchanged and its advskew was already 0.
5. **Netflow:** `capture.targets` was cleared (was `127.0.0.1:2056`) per the standing rule.
   Deliberate — do not restore.
6. **`dhcpd`** is only *stopped*, not disabled, so a reboot of 102 brings it back and re-breaks Kea
   DHCPv4. Restarting it restores the old arrangement but re-empties `keaLeases4`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Second OPNsense VM on `vmbr9` only, `onboot` set, documented access path (guest agent, plus
      LXC 105 as an SSH jump — its key is in 106's `config.xml` so it survives config writes)
- [x] `hasync_status/version` and `/services` return configured, reachable payloads, captured
      runner-local and never committed
- [x] All 5 hasync metrics emit non-trivial values; `remote_version_match` observed as both 1 and 0
- [x] `carp_vip_status` MASTER on one box and BACKUP on the other, observed changing across a
      failover; maintenance mode observed
- [x] `coverage.json` records the newly reachable paths as `required` with recipes; the
      `hasyncVersion` exemption note corrected with evidence
- [x] Snapshot of VM 102 taken before the HA config, undo steps documented above
- [x] `cmd/apidrift` shows no new breaking drift; new nested extras classified
- [x] Full gate green — `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`
      (0 issues), `make docs-check`

### Not achieved, with reasons

- **CARP `INIT` (`vip_status = 2`) not observed.** A sub-second transient during interface bring-up;
  a poll-interval scrape is unlikely ever to catch it. Deliberately not ledgered rather than faked.
- **`opnsense_kea_dhcp4_leases_dynamic_total` still 0.** The only DHCPv4 client on the segment holds
  a *reservation*, so only the reserved branch of the reserved/dynamic split is exercised. A second,
  unreserved client would close it — noted in the ledger.

### Traps for the next session

- **The QEMU guest agent dies permanently on a `qm guest exec` payload over roughly 1 KB.** The call
  returns `got timeout`, the command never runs, and the agent stays dead until the VM is restarted.
  200 B and 800 B are fine; 1500 B kills it. Upload larger scripts in ≤600-char base64 chunks, then
  execute the file.
- **A gateway item on the TESTLAN interface breaks inbound TLS to 106 from its own subnet.** OPNsense
  treats a gateway-bearing interface as WAN-type and stamps `reply-to` on its pass rules, so the
  SYN-ACK goes to 102's MAC instead of the client's — proven with tcpdump. Neither
  `system.disablereplyto` nor the per-rule equivalent suppressed it. If 106 needs internet, add a
  default route by hand, do the work, then delete it.
- **`carp_status/maintenance` toggles, it does not set.** A script that posts it to "ensure"
  maintenance does the opposite on its second run.
- **A link flap drops any hand-added route** — the cause of two "the mirror is broken" dead ends.

body:
Found while closing #377 in epic #447. This is the reason the OSPFv3 coverage entries are permanently `opaque`, and it is a **code** gap, not a testbed gap — a distinction worth recording, because it was independently rediscovered twice during that work.

## Problem

`opnsense/schema_registry.go` registers `quaggaOspfv3Overview` and `quaggaOspfv3Interface` as their **envelope** types (`frrOSPFv3OverviewEnvelope`, `frrOSPFv3InterfaceEnvelope`). Each envelope has exactly one field:

```go
Response json.RawMessage `json:"response"`
```

`json.RawMessage` implements `json.Unmarshaler`, so `walkType` maps it to `KindAny` and stops. Both goldens therefore contain a single path — `response`, `kind: any` — and `ValidateResponseSchema` accepts literally any payload there.

## Consequence

The canary can never verify the inner structure of these endpoints **no matter what the box reports**. Fields like `areas.*.numberOfAreaScopedLsa`, `ospf6InterfaceState`, `cost` and `priority` back real exported metrics and are structurally invisible to drift detection:

- `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_area_lsa_count`
- `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_interface_up`
- `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_interface_cost`
- `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_interface_state`
- `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_interface_pending_lsa`

#377 handles this honestly rather than pretending otherwise: those paths are marked `opaque` in `opnsense/testdata/schemas/coverage.json`, which makes them render as a permanent **standing blind spot** in the report instead of an unresolved-required warning a live run could never clear. `TestCommittedCoverageLedgerIntegrity` enforces `opaque` iff the schema field really is `KindAny`, so the flag cannot be misapplied. But a named blind spot is still a blind spot.

Proof it is not a testbed problem: OSPFv3 was brought up on the dev box during #447 with a `Full` adjacency, and all 13 source-derived field names in `frr.go` were confirmed present in the live payload. The canary still cannot verify a single one of them.

## Proposed scope

Two candidate approaches; the second is more general and probably correct.

1. **Register the inner body types.** Point `schemaRegistry` at `frrOSPFv3OverviewBody` and `map[string]frrOSPFv3InterfaceEntry`. Cheap and local, but wrong-ish: the schema `Path`/`Method` then describe the endpoint while the reflected shape describes a sub-object, and the validator would need to know to descend into `response` before matching.
2. **Teach the reflector to descend through a single-field `json.RawMessage` envelope.** Introduce an explicit registry annotation — an envelope wrapper naming the field to unwrap and the type beneath it — so the derived schema carries `response.areas.*.numberOfAreaScopedLsa` and the validator resolves it normally. This generalises: grep shows the same `Response json.RawMessage` envelope pattern across the FRR family and elsewhere, so any of them could be unwrapped by declaration rather than one-off surgery.

Whichever is chosen, the two-stage decode in the client stays as it is — this is about what the schema *describes*, not how the client parses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The derived schema for both OSPFv3 endpoints carries the inner field paths with real kinds, not a single `any`.
- [ ] `ValidateResponseSchema` reports a type conflict when an inner OSPFv3 field changes JSON type, proven by a test.
- [ ] The `opaque` entries for `quaggaOspfv3Overview` / `quaggaOspfv3Interface` are removed from `coverage.json` and become ordinary `required` paths, resolvable by a live run against a box with an OSPFv3 adjacency.
- [ ] `TestCommittedCoverageLedgerIntegrity` still passes (it asserts `opaque` iff the field is `KindAny`, so removing the flag requires the schema change to be real).
- [ ] Every other endpoint using the same envelope pattern is audited: either unwrapped too, or explicitly ledgered as an accepted blind spot with a reason.
- [ ] `make schemas` regenerated; goldens remain structure-only; full gate green.

## Risk

Unwrapping widens the canary's surface, so the first run afterwards may surface a wave of previously-invisible nested extras for these endpoints — the same effect #457 is triaging globally. Land this after #457 has established the baseline, or classify the new paths as part of this change.

body:
Found by the #376/#377 live canary work in epic #447, immediately after OSPFv3 was enabled on the testbed. This is a genuine modelling bug, not box state — the exporter emits a meaningless empty label today.

## Problem

`frrOSPFRouteRow` (`opnsense/frr.go:970`) is shared by BOTH route endpoints:

```go
type frrOSPFRouteRow struct {
    Type flexString `json:"type"`
}
```

`countOSPFRoutes` uses it for `quaggaOspfRoute` (v2) and `quaggaOspfv3Route` (v3). That is correct for v2 and wrong for v3.

## Live evidence (dev box, OPNsense 26.7.r_35, OSPFv2 + OSPFv3 both up with Full adjacencies)

`api/quagga/diagnostics/search_ospfroute` (v2) — `rows[]` keys:
`area, cost, network, type, via, viainterface, viainterfaceDescr`
`type` values across 4 rows: `"N E2"` ×2, `"N"`, `"R "`.

`api/quagga/diagnostics/search_ospfv3route` (v3) — `rows[]` keys:
`destinationType, duration, interfaceDescr, interfaceName, isBestRoute, network, nextHop, nextHops, pathType`
**There is no `type` key at all.** Across 2 rows: `destinationType` = `"N"`, `pathType` = `"IA"`.

The canary reported it as `quaggaOspfv3Route` `rows[].type` missing — and it only became visible once OSPFv3 was actually brought up, because an empty `rows[]` puts the path in `Unverified` rather than `Missing`. Exactly the class of defect #377 exists to surface.

## Impact

For every OSPFv3 row, `row.Type.String()` is `""`, so `countOSPFRoutes` buckets all v3 routes under the empty string and the collector emits:

```
opnsense_frr_ospfv3_routes{type=""} 2
```

The route-type breakdown — the whole point of the metric — is silently lost for OSPFv3, and the series carries an empty label value. `opnsense_frr_ospf_routes` (v2) is unaffected and correct.

## Verdict: chase

The data has not been removed, it is under a different name on a different endpoint. Per the repo's triage rules this needs a **tolerant reader**, resolved by shape rather than by version-sniffing — both spellings are current, they just belong to different endpoints.

v2's `type` is FRR's composed route code: `"N E2"` = destination `N` + path `E2`. v3 splits the same information into two fields. So composing `destinationType` + `pathType` reproduces v2's notation exactly: the v3 rows above become `"N IA"`.

## Proposed scope

- Keep `Type` (v2 wins when present).
- Add `DestinationType` and `PathType`.
- Resolve in an accessor: `type` if non-empty, else `strings.TrimSpace(destinationType + " " + pathType)`, else `""`. Template to follow: the new-wins-else-legacy accessor pattern in `opnsense/health_check.go`.
- Emit no series, or an explicitly-labelled unknown bucket, if all three are empty — do not keep emitting `type=""` silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failing test proves the v3 fixture currently yields `type=""` for every row.
- [ ] After the fix, a v3 payload with `destinationType`/`pathType` produces a composed type label; the live pair (`N` + `IA`) yields `N IA`.
- [ ] A v2 payload with `type` is unchanged, including the trailing-space case `"R "` (currently `TrimSpace`d — preserve that).
- [ ] A row with none of the three fields does not silently produce an empty-string label.
- [ ] Fixtures derive from the live captures above or from FRR source branches — no invented shapes.
- [ ] `quaggaOspfv3Route` `rows[].type` stops being reported Missing by the canary, WITHOUT an exemption (this is a real bug; exempting it would be misusing the compat ledger to hide a defect).
- [ ] Schema goldens regenerated; full gate green.

## Note

This was deliberately NOT exempted in `exemptions.json` while it stands open, so the daily canary keeps reporting it. One honest warning is not noise; silencing a live defect would be.

body:
Follow-up from #376, which shipped nested-key detection in epic #447. The detector works; the baseline it exposed is too large to classify in the same change.

## Baseline result (live, 2026-07-25, dev box on OPNsense 26.7.r_35)

`cmd/apidrift` against the dev box: **174 endpoints probed, 0 breaking type drift, 0 unexpected top-level keys, and 1003 unmodelled nested paths across 62 endpoints.**

## Why nested extras ship report-only

#376's acceptance criteria said "a baseline live run is reviewed before enabling issue warnings; after justified exemptions, the current canary is clean". The frozen seam contract for the epic had specified warning-level from the start; the baseline proved that wrong at this scale, so it was corrected on the evidence before landing.

1003 warning-level paths would keep the drift issue permanently open and train everyone to ignore it — the exact permanent-noise risk #376's own risk section names. So `aggregate()` deliberately excludes `UnknownPaths` from the warning signal (`cmd/apidrift/report.go`), and the report section is labelled `REPORT-ONLY baseline`. Discovery is unaffected: all 1003 still render in full, with endpoint + normalized path only.

## The work

- [ ] Triage all 1003 paths. They are highly systematic, so this is far less work than the count suggests — see the categories below.
- [ ] Add `knownExtraPaths` entries for the deliberate ones, each with a reason and a prune trigger.
- [ ] Anything that turns out to back a metric, or is genuinely worth modelling, becomes an `opportunity` roadmap candidate rather than an exemption.
- [ ] Re-enable warnings: drop the `UnknownPaths` exclusion in `aggregate()`, restore the section to `🟡`, and flip the `unknown nested path is report-only, not a warning` case in `cmd/apidrift/report_test.go` back to expecting a warning.
- [ ] Confirm the canary is clean after the exemptions land.

## Categories seen in the baseline

- **Bootgrid `%`-prefixed twins.** Many `rows[]` surfaces carry both `field` and `%field` (e.g. `acmeCertificates` `rows[].account` + `rows[].%account`, `authUsers` `rows[].%priv`). OPNsense's bootgrid emits a `%`-prefixed formatted variant alongside the raw value. These are protocol noise, almost certainly a blanket exemption per endpoint, and possibly worth handling structurally in the validator instead of one entry at a time.
- **Whole unmodelled sub-objects** on endpoints where the exporter deliberately decodes a narrow slice (config/GUI metadata).
- **Genuine opportunities** — fields backing no metric today that arguably should. `keaLeases6` `rows[]` is the clearest: 16 keys served, `keaLeaseRow` models 8.

## Care needed

- Do NOT reach for a blanket `rows[].*` subtree exemption just to shrink the count. That masks every future addition under `rows[]`, which is the drift this detector exists to catch. Prefer exact paths, or fix the `%`-twin class structurally.
- Report output must stay structure-only. `TestRenderReportNeverEchoesResponseValues` guards this; keep it passing.
- Paths are spelled in the **schema's** casing, not the live payload's. #376 fixed a bug where live casing was used, which would have made an exemption match only one spelling of a key OPNsense serves in a different case (`metadata.System` vs live `system`). Write exemptions in struct casing.

## Not blocking anything

The canary is green on every breaking signal today, so this is hygiene and opportunity-discovery, not a defect. It should be done before the next endpoint-expansion push, so new nested drift is not lost in the baseline noise.

## Problem

`opnsense_interfaces_sfp_lane_rx_power_dbm` is semantically wrong for the current OPNsense API representation. The API returns a combined string such as `0.48 mW (-3.16 dBm)`, but the parser extracts the leading number and publishes `0.48` under a `_dbm` metric name.

Live evidence on `opnsense` (2026-07-25):

- API: `sfp.lane_1_rx_power = "0.48 mW (-3.16 dBm)"` for `ixl0`.
- Prometheus: `opnsense_interfaces_sfp_lane_rx_power_dbm{device="ixl0",lane="1"} = 0.48`.

## Scope

Extend the existing `interfaces_info` SFP/DOM extraction introduced by #214:

- Preserve and emit `opnsense_interfaces_sfp_lane_rx_power_dbm{device,lane}` using the parenthesized dBm value.
- Add `opnsense_interfaces_sfp_lane_rx_power_milliwatts{device,lane}` using the leading mW value.
- Keep absent DOM readings absent; never substitute zero.
- Update the generated metric documentation and canonical exporter dashboard to show the two values with correct units.

## Approach

Parse the labelled values rather than using the generic leading-float helper: recognise `NN mW (NN dBm)` regardless of whitespace and signed dBm values. Retain tolerant behaviour for malformed/partial values: emit the independently parseable unit and leave the other series absent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixture containing `0.48 mW (-3.16 dBm)` emits mW=`0.48` and dBm=`-3.16`.
- [ ] Negative dBm values, whitespace variation, and an independently malformed component are covered by unit tests.
- [ ] Copper/non-DOM SFPs still emit no optical-power series.
- [ ] Generated metrics documentation and dashboard panels use the correct names and units.
- [ ] `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check` pass.

## Duplicate check

#214 added the API-backed SFP/DOM extraction and is closed. It does not cover this unit/value mismatch or the missing mW family.

comments.body:
Delivered in [`8098023`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/8098023), pushed to `main`.

- `opnsense_interfaces_sfp_lane_rx_power_dbm{device,lane}` — now the **parenthesised dBm** value
- `opnsense_interfaces_sfp_lane_rx_power_milliwatts{device,lane}` — new, the **leading mW** value

Red receipt:
```
opnsense/interfaces_test.go:86:28: undefined: parseSFPRXPower
FAIL	github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/opnsense [build failed]
```
Green: `go test ./...` exit 0, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` clean, `golangci-lint run ./...` 0 issues, `make docs-check` "all generated docs current", dashboard coverage **827/827**.

### Root cause

FreeBSD `ifconfig(8)` (`sbin/ifconfig/sfp.c`) formats the DOM line as `"RX power: %.2f mW (%.2f dBm) TX bias: %.2f mA"`, and OPNsense's `interfaces.lib.inc` captures that combined string verbatim into `lane_<n>_rx_power`. The old parser used the generic leading-float helper, which takes the first number regardless of unit — so it published mW under the `_dbm` name.

Parsing now locates each unit by **its own label rather than by position**, so it is order-independent, and the two components are gated independently through separate presence booleans on `SFPLane`. A value where only one half parses emits exactly that one series; the other stays absent, never a substituted zero. Proven at both layers by `TestFetchInterfacesOverview_SFPRXPowerPartial` and `TestInterfacesCollector_Update_SFPRXPowerPartial` (three lanes: mW-only, dBm-only, fully malformed). Copper/non-DOM still emits no optical-power series (`TestFetchInterfacesOverview_SFPCopperNoDOM`).

`tx_bias` is untouched — upstream formats it as a single plain `TX bias: %.2f mA` with no combined form, so it still uses the leading-float helper.

### A pre-existing fixture was also wrong

`TestFetchInterfacesOverview_SFPOpticalWithDOM` encoded `"-2.32 dBm (0.59 mW)"` — **dBm-leading**, which is backwards from what upstream emits and was never captured from a live box. It only ever "passed" because that reversed order happened to put dBm first for the old leading-float parser, so the test was quietly asserting the bug was correct. Per this repo's rule that a fixture must never encode a shape upstream cannot produce, it now carries the real ordering — and the reversed string is kept deliberately as an explicit **order-independence** case, since the new parser genuinely does not care.

### Behaviour change — worth telling anyone with a panel on this

For the same physical optic the `_dbm` series steps from ~`0.48` to ~`-3.16`: typically negative and far smaller in magnitude. Anything dashboarding or alerting on the old values will show what looks like a step drop. The old number was never dBm, so this is a correction rather than drift, and both the metric help text and the Grafana panel description carry a `NOTE (#456)` explaining it.

### Dashboard

An "SFP Lane RX Power (mW)" timeseries (`unit="mwatt"`) added beside the renamed "SFP Lane RX Power (dBm)" (`unit="dBm"`) in the existing SFP/Optics row; the descriptions cross-reference each other and the dBm one flags the step change. Schema-validated via `gcx resources validate`; **not** visually render-checked.

### Unverified

The dev box is virtio-only and has no SFP cage, so every fixture here derives from the live production capture quoted in this issue plus the upstream format string — not from a canary run. `interfacesOverview` `rows[].sfp.*` remains classed `stateOptional` in the coverage ledger for exactly that reason.

body:
Split out of #379, which was closed won't-do because `sessionExpiresAt` is structurally unavailable through the os-netbird plugin (setup-key peers can never carry a login-expiry deadline). The *state* half of that signal is available today and is not exported.

## Problem

`opnsense/netbird.go` decodes `daemonStatus` into `NetbirdStatus.DaemonStatus` (`netbird.go:87` wire field, `netbird.go:186` assignment), but **the netbird collector never reads that field** — it has no descriptor for it, so the value reaches no metric. Verified on `main`: `grep -rn "DaemonStatus" internal/collector/` returns nothing.

So an operator cannot alert on the overlay daemon needing re-authentication, sitting idle, or having had its session expire.

## Operator value

`daemonStatus` distinguishes states that today are invisible or conflated with "management disconnected":

- `NeedsLogin` — the peer requires re-authentication. Actionable, and the single most useful value: it is the state a box lands in when its enrollment goes stale, and it is meaningful for setup-key **and** SSO peers.
- `SessionExpired` — `DaemonStatusSessionExpired` exists at the currently packaged 0.74.4 (`client/status/status.go:38`, set via `internal.StatusSessionExpired` at `server.go:1237`). This is the recoverable part of #379's intent.
- `Idle` — lazy-connection idling. Observed live on the dev box; NOT a fault, and must not be alerted on. Today it is indistinguishable from a real problem.
- `Connected` — healthy.

The existing `netbird_management_connected` / `netbird_signal_connected` gauges do not cover these: a peer can be `NeedsLogin` while transport-level state looks unremarkable.

## Proposed scope

- Add `opnsense_netbird_daemon_state{state} 1`, emitting exactly one series for the current state, in the same shape as the firmware update-check state metric added in #373.
- Canonicalize the closed upstream vocabulary and collapse anything unrecognised to `unknown`. Take the vocabulary from the **installed** package's `client/status/status.go` constants rather than from master, and record which version it was read from.
- Do NOT alert on `Idle` (normal under lazy connections) or on `unknown`. A `NeedsLogin`/`SessionExpired` warning alert is the useful one, and it should state that recovery requires operator action, not a restart.
- No new API call: `api/netbird/status/status` is already fetched and the field is already decoded.
- No identity-bearing labels. `state` only — never fqdn, profile name, node key or peer address.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `daemonStatus` reaches a metric; a test proves the field no longer dead-ends in the client struct.
- [ ] Exactly one series per scrape, value 1, with the current state.
- [ ] Every documented state maps to its canonical label; an unrecognised/future string collapses to `unknown`.
- [ ] An absent or empty `daemonStatus` emits no series rather than a fabricated state.
- [ ] Tests cover each canonical state, absent, empty, and an unknown future string.
- [ ] `Idle` is asserted NOT to be treated as a fault by any shipped alert.
- [ ] Generated docs, dashboard panel coverage and the full gate pass.

## Dependencies and risks

- One bounded series per instance; no cardinality risk.
- Cheap and low-risk: the data is already fetched, decoded and live-verified.
- The only real trap is treating `Idle` as unhealthy. It was observed live on the dev box under `lazyConnectionEnabled: true` and is normal.

## Live evidence

The dev box is enrolled and reports `daemonStatus: "Connected"` (and `"Idle"` when the lazy connection idles). Both shapes were validated against the committed `netbirdStatus` golden schema during the #377 coverage work — 22/22 paths verified, no mismatches, in both states.

## Mission

Give each live companion dashboard an explicit generated owner, portable instance/schema contract, and reason to exist—or retire it in favor of the canonical operational/self-observability dashboards.

## Audit baseline

- The live standalone Firewall Logs dashboard is entirely No data because it targets a stale service/syslog schema.
- Network Activity hard-codes one firewall, WAN/interface names, IP address, and external ktranslate metrics; it is partly blank and overlaps the canonical dashboard.
- SFP/Port Monitor mostly works but duplicates canonical content and treats normal no-DOM/copper hardware as warning-like.
- Zenarmor exact DNS/SNI/JA3 queries return data, but the dashboard lacks generated ownership, exporter-instance scoping, consistent legends, and measured performance.

The audit baseline was clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4). Read every child issue in full, including later comments, before changing code: the child acceptance criteria and comments are binding and may supersede this summary.

## Binding decisions

- Retirement is a valid result when a companion has no unique portable value. Do not preserve duplication for its own sake.
- No source-controlled dashboard may hard-code Rob's instance, IP, interfaces, WAN names, datasource UID, or stack-local ktranslate schema.
- Use current structured log fields and stable exporter identity; do not reparse raw CSV when normalized attributes exist.
- Do not claim the audited Zenarmor DNS/SNI/JA3 queries are broken. Measure their performance and preserve their data-bearing behavior.
- No-DOM/unsupported hardware is neutral; only proven DOM alarm states are warnings.
- Freeze UIDs and variable names with the drilldown/self-observability work before parallel migration.

## Child worklist

- [x] #432 — fix(grafana): replace stale standalone firewall-log queries with the current structured schema (`P1`)
- [x] #433 — refactor(grafana): reconcile the personalized Network Activity dashboard with the canonical dashboard (`P2`)
- [x] #434 — refactor(grafana): consolidate SFP and port monitoring and treat no-DOM hardware as neutral (`P3`)
- [x] #435 — refactor(grafana): bring the Zenarmor companion dashboard under generated, instance-scoped ownership (`P2`, delivered in `59c4dfe`: nine unique panels merged into the generated Zenarmor tab, companion UID retired and 404ing)

## Implementation waves

1. Restore or replace the broken firewall-log view in #432 after stable logship instance identity #395.
2. Inventory unique/duplicate content and decide rebuild-versus-retire for #433 and #434.
3. Bring Zenarmor under generated ownership in #435 while retaining live-proven query families and recording measured costs.
4. Wire context-preserving links through #419 and verify every retained dashboard visually and by query against live Grafana.

## Cross-epic dependencies

- #395 provides stable instance identity; #419 owns shared link helpers and variable propagation.
- The dedicated self-observability dashboard #431 determines the final dashboard navigation hierarchy.

## Coding-agent launch prompt

Deliver the retained scope in this epic. Start by reading this epic and every open child issue in full, including all comments. Reconfirm each premise against current `main`; if a premise is already fixed or disproven, record the evidence on that issue and close or rescope it instead of forcing a change.

Before parallel work, freeze every shared seam named above: exact metric names and types, labels and closed vocabularies, config keys/defaults, generated artifact ownership, and compatibility behavior. Use one file owner per lane. Keep integration/composition files in one lane or one wiring pass.

For each implementation issue, use strict TDD: add the smallest failing regression test, observe the correct failure, implement the minimum fix, then refactor. Keep the issue body/checklist current and post meaningful progress comments with commit SHAs. Completing commits must include `Closes #N` and land by direct push to `main` under the repository workflow.

At every wiring checkpoint and before claiming completion, run the full gate: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`. Run targeted race, parser, integration, live-canary, release, or Grafana checks required by each child. Generated files must be regenerated from source; do not hand-edit generated JSON or docs.

For live Grafana or OPNsense validation, keep production read-only unless a child explicitly defines a controlled testbed write. A successful local test, API response, or GitHub create call is not delivery proof: use scoped read-back, exact CI/release receipts, and live query/visual evidence where required.

## Epic completion bar

Every retained live dashboard is reproducibly generated, instance-safe, schema-current, linked, visually validated, and non-duplicative; retired dashboards are removed from GitSync with the replacement/rationale recorded.

- Every retained child is closed by its completing commit or explicitly descoped with a durable rationale.
- The epic checklist and phase comments reconstruct what landed, which SHAs delivered it, what was rejected, and what remains.
- The full gate is green on the final integrated `main`, with exact remote CI/release/live receipts for affected surfaces.

```text
after              1: opnsense-exporter, generated, GitSync-owned at generation 7

```

### #435 in one paragraph

The companion was not regenerated, it was **absorbed**: nine of its seventeen panels said
something the generated tab could not (DNS query names, response codes, domain categories;
HTTP hosts, URIs, user agents, status codes; application names; and all-verdict counterparts

scoping and per-instance `topk` — neither of which the companion had. The other eight
duplicated content the tab already derives from `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total`, which is

- **"Freeze UIDs with the drilldown work"** — done under #419; this epic consumed that

- **The companion's `Device` picker could never have worked.** Its query was a bare stream

  decoded `spec.query` as an object, so a single `TextVariable` (whose `query` is a string)

  regression test.

  published dashboard rather than by reading the manifest. Same discovery route as #470.
- **The stale-clone trap this epic recorded twice is real and was avoided:** both publications
  this run were made from a fresh clone of `origin/main`, never from `~/repos/gc-gitsync-m7kni`.

### Boundaries

No release published or announced; PR #358 untouched; production OPNsense read-only
throughout. The only writes were the GitSync dashboard commits, and the only deletion was the
Zenarmor companion, authorized by this epic's retirement decision and the owner's tab
decision on #435.

Closing.

## Mission

Make every shipped release artifact, install path, container example, public fact, secret path, permission guide, parser boundary, and contribution template executable and owned; then add operator conveniences from the same frozen configuration sources.

## Audit baseline

- The live v3.0.0 publish run failed its notices job because the go-licenses v2 module path is wrong, leaving the release without `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- The documented systemd binary URL is 404, root-owned 0600 file secrets are unreadable by the service user, and the Compose healthcheck calls `wget` in a distroless image.
- Public counts/defaults/manifests drift, CODEOWNERS/templates still target an inherited upstream owner, and no parser fuzzing, Helm chart, secret reload, or preflight mode exists.

The audit baseline was clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4). Read every child issue in full, including later comments, before changing code: the child acceptance criteria and comments are binding and may supersede this summary.

## Binding decisions

- Repair and test existing install/container/release surfaces before adding Helm or reload/preflight convenience layers.
- Keep the distroless runtime; fix probes rather than adding shell/curl/wget.
- Generate defaults, metric/collector counts, flags, manifests, and ACL guidance from executable sources instead of duplicating prose.
- Secrets must be readable only by the service, never printed, and rotation/reload must be atomic with rollback.
- Release Please remains the publishing owner; Docker publishing stays in release workflows, not ordinary CI.
- Parser fuzz corpora must contain no raw production secrets, addresses, or tenant payloads.

## Child worklist

- [x] #436 — fix(release): restore third-party notices and gate release tooling (`P0`)
- [x] #437 — fix(systemd): make install, secrets, and verification executable (`P1`)
- [x] #438 — fix(docker): make Compose health and secrets examples executable (`P1`)
- [x] #439 — deprecate(config): retire obsolete scrape-deadline and skip surfaces (`P1`)
- [x] #440 — test(docs): make public facts and deployment examples executable (`P1`)
- [x] #441 — chore(repo): replace inherited ownership and intake templates (`P1`)
- [x] #442 — feat(security): generate collector-to-ACL guidance and actionable 403s (`P1`)
- [x] #443 — test(parsers): continuously fuzz NetFlow, syslog, and Zenarmor inputs (`P2`)
- [x] #444 — feat(deploy): publish a supported Helm chart (`P3`)
- [x] #445 — feat(config): support atomic secret reload without exporter restart (`P3`)
- [x] #446 — feat(config): add a no-side-effect configuration check mode (`P3`)

## Implementation waves

1. Stop the release/integrity defects first: #436, then systemd/container correctness #437 and #438.
2. Remove dead config semantics and executable-doc drift in #439 and #440; fix repository ownership/intake in #441.
3. Generate least-privilege/API permission guidance in #442 and continuously exercise parser boundaries in #443.
4. After those sources are stable, add #446 and #445.
5. Publish Helm support in #444 only when it renders from the same tested defaults and probes rather than becoming another drifting surface.

## Coding-agent launch prompt

Deliver the retained scope in this epic. Start by reading this epic and every open child issue in full, including all comments. Reconfirm each premise against current `main`; if a premise is already fixed or disproven, record the evidence on that issue and close or rescope it instead of forcing a change.

Before parallel work, freeze every shared seam named above: exact metric names and types, labels and closed vocabularies, config keys/defaults, generated artifact ownership, and compatibility behavior. Use one file owner per lane. Keep integration/composition files in one lane or one wiring pass.

For each implementation issue, use strict TDD: add the smallest failing regression test, observe the correct failure, implement the minimum fix, then refactor. Keep the issue body/checklist current and post meaningful progress comments with commit SHAs. Completing commits must include `Closes #N` and land by direct push to `main` under the repository workflow.

At every wiring checkpoint and before claiming completion, run the full gate: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`. Run targeted race, parser, integration, live-canary, release, or Grafana checks required by each child. Generated files must be regenerated from source; do not hand-edit generated JSON or docs.

For live Grafana or OPNsense validation, keep production read-only unless a child explicitly defines a controlled testbed write. ## Epic completion bar

A clean machine can verify, install, configure, rotate, health-check, upgrade, and contribute using copied commands that are exercised in CI; releases contain the mandatory artifact set; generated security/deployment facts cannot drift silently.

- Every retained child is closed by its completing commit or explicitly descoped with a durable rationale.

ncoming execution run — binding decisions (2026-07-25)

Owner decisions taken before implementation. These are binding and supersede any softer wording in the child bodies.

## 1. `#439` compatibility policy: remove, do not deprecate

The child asks for an explicit deprecate-vs-remove call. **Decision: remove now.**

- `--exporter.scrape-timeout-offset` is deleted, not accepted-and-warned.
- `opnsense_exporter_scrape_skips_total` is unregistered, not left at zero.
- The `X-Prometheus-Scrape-Timeout-Seconds` header plumbing in `internal/server/metrics.go` goes with them.

Rationale: both surfaces are provably inert after `#336` — the flag influences nothing and the counter has no increment site — so removing them cannot break a working deployment; it only stops the exporter lying about what it does. The run already carries breaking commits, so release-please cuts a major regardless and a deprecation window would only preserve the misleading signal across that boundary.

Requirement: `docs/upgrading.md` entry plus a `!`-marked conventional commit. The Grafana panel is replaced with a signal that actually moves, not deleted silently.

## 2. `#438` health probe: in-binary subcommand

**Decision: add a native probe to the binary** rather than removing the healthcheck from the docs. The runtime image stays distroless — no shell, no `curl`, no `wget` is added. The probe performs a local HTTP GET of `/-/healthy` and exits 0/1, so the published Compose example becomes executable and CI-testable.

This is a new public CLI surface and is treated as one: it gets CLI tests, docs, and an upgrading note. The docs must also stop claiming an unhealthy container "gets restarted" — Docker restart policies react to process exit, not health status.

## 3. P3 tail scope

**In:** `#446` (config-check preflight), `#443` (continuous parser fuzzing), `#444` (Helm chart).

**Descoped:** `#445` (atomic secret reload). Not rejected on merit — it is the most invasive of the four, it touches the API/TLS/OTLP client rebuild paths, and its stated dependency (correct file-secret permissions and install guidance, `#437`) has not landed yet. It will be closed with this rationale rather than left open as an implied commitment; refile when `#437` is settled and rotation is an actual operational need.

`#444` ships only if it renders from the same tested defaults and probes as the raw manifests, per the epic binding decision. If it cannot, it stays unbuilt and that becomes the recorded outcome rather than a second drifting source of flags.

## 4. Lane discipline

`main.go` is contended by `#438` (probe subcommand), `#439` (flag removal), and `#446` (preflight), and `docs/security.md` by `#437` and `#442`. Those are serialized behind one owner each, not run as parallel lanes. `#436`, `#441`, and `#443` are file-disjoint and run concurrently.

remise revalidation complete — all 11 children still valid on `main` @ `58a51e5`

Every child was re-audited against current `main` rather than the `52ef4b2` baseline, including live GitHub, GHCR and HTTP checks. Ten commits landed in between; none touched the Makefile, Dockerfile, deployment docs, `.github/` metadata, or the scrape-skip machinery. No child was already fixed and no premise was disproven. #445 is closed as descoped (rationale on that issue).

## Live receipts taken during revalidation

- **#436 reproduced locally.** `go install github.com/google/go-licenses@v2.0.1` fails on this machine with exactly the error from the failed release run: `invalid version: go.mod has post-v2 module path "github.com/google/go-licenses/v2" at revision v2.0.1`.
- **v3.0.0 is still missing its notices file.** `gh release view v3.0.0 --json assets` returns 23 assets — checksums, Sigstore/in-toto bundles, per-arch `.tar.gz` and `.sbom.json`, CycloneDX and SPDX SBOMs — and no `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- **The 404 in the systemd guide is real.** `opnsense-exporter_linux_amd64` → 404; so is the `.tar.gz` of that lowercase name. The actual GoReleaser output `opnsense-exporter_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz` → 302 to the real asset.
- **The image tag convention in the release docs is wrong.** Anonymous GHCR manifest lookup: tag `3.0.0` → 200, tag `v3.0.0` → 404. `docs/development/release-process.md:55-57` still shows the leading-`v` form.
- **CODEOWNERS cannot work as written.** `gh api repos/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/collaborators/ihatemodels/permission` → `{"permission":"read","role_name":"read"}`. GitHub requires write access for a code owner, so the single `* @ihatemodels` rule assigns nobody.

## Findings that change scope

**#436 — the divergence is wider than the issue states.** `Dockerfile:31` independently hardcodes `ARG GO_LICENSES_VERSION=v1.6.0` against the Makefile's `v2.0.1`, which is precisely why the container build never caught the break. Worse, `renovate.json`'s customManager scans only `/^Makefile$/`, so it cannot see the Dockerfile ARG default at all — Renovate can bump one and leave the other, unnoticed, forever. The single-source-of-truth acceptance item is therefore load-bearing, not tidying. Also note the last `publish.yml` run was 2026-06-29, predating the v3.0.0 publish on 2026-07-23 — the notices job has not executed since, so nothing has re-tested it.

**#439 — both surfaces are provably dead, which makes removal safe.** `opnsense_exporter_scrape_skips_total` has exactly one write in the entire codebase: `.Add(0)` at `collector.go:1291`. There is no increment site. And the scrape-timeout context terminates at `collector.go:1431-1432`, `func (c *Collector) collect(_ context.Context, ...)` — the parameter is discarded, with an adjacent comment saying so explicitly. Removing the flag and the counter cannot break a working deployment.

**#440 — the metric-count contradiction has got worse since the audit.** It is no longer 818-vs-808. `README.md:30` and `:124` now say **829** while `README.md:173` still says **808**. Two of three mentions were updated and the third was not, which is exactly the failure mode the issue wants a generated contract to prevent.

**#440 — the Kubernetes divergence is confirmed by direct diff.** The canonical `deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml` probes `/-/healthy` and declares `syslog-udp`/`syslog-tcp` ports on both the container and the Service. The copy embedded in `docs/deployment/kubernetes.md:41-141` probes `/` and has no syslog ports at all. `release-please-config.json:7-13` rewrites the version marker in both files, which is exactly why the drift is invisible — the one field that is synced looks correct.

**#438 — no in-image probe exists to build on.** Grepped for kingpin subcommands: there are none anywhere in the codebase, only flags. The only liveness surface is the network-served `/-/healthy` in `internal/server/health.go`. The probe subcommand the owner chose has to be built from scratch, and it is a new public CLI surface.

**#441 — the documented contributor gate is materially short.** Root `CONTRIBUTING.md` lists `make sync-vendor`, `make test`, `make lint`. The real `ci-success` gate is `needs: [tests, race, docs, grafana, docker-build-verify]`. The race detector, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check` and the container build-verify job are all missing from the guide, so a contributor following it lands a red PR.

**#442 — an existing idiom to extend, rather than a new pattern.** `defaultEndpoints()` currently registers **175** endpoints. `opnsense/cache.go`'s `PluginGatedEndpoints()` and `opnsense/contract.go`'s `postEndpoints` are already `EndpointName`-keyed classification maps, each with its own completeness test. The ACL map should mirror that shape exactly rather than inventing a new mechanism.

## Phase 1 recovery checkpoint

Inherited work has been reconstructed into issue-linked commits and pushed to `main`:

- `1753ddf` — #441 ownership/intake repair (manually closed because the published commit body contained a literal escaped newline before the closer)
- `d8a7824` — #442 generated ACL guidance and completeness contract
- `0168186` — #439 breaking removal of obsolete scrape deadline surfaces
- `3ad3966` — #436 release-notice pipeline repair (`Refs`; v3.0.0 backfill remains approval-gated)
- `ed8fa84` — #438 native distroless health probe + #446 side-effect-free config check

Verification on the final Phase 1 tree:
- full test/build/lint/docs/Grafana gate — pass
- exact staged-tree tests/build for #438/#446 — pass
- documented Compose secrets + native health path — container reached `healthy`; UID 65532 read both secrets
- old `wget` healthcheck reproduction — exit 127, executable absent as expected
- clean go-licenses v2 install + `make notices` — 64 modules

The tag-correct v3.0.0 notices artifact is prepared from tag commit `28f5234`, SHA-256 `91c47a8b...`, but no release write has been performed. Exact upload/read-back proposal is recorded on #436 and awaits explicit approval.

Shared worktree is clean; local `main` and `origin/main` are both `6caece73e36efb84e92e88938b0852cc1d6821cd`.

## Phase 2/hosted verification checkpoint

Remaining executable children are complete and pushed:

- `80e3e468208f436aeacdd581fa0d4875516e4e48` closes #437, #440, and #444: verified systemd install/permissions, generated executable public deployment contracts, and supported release-only Helm publication with real kind install/test/upgrade.
- `d47b09a540446ef255e315d5f36cef9ec67bae37` closes #443: four bounded parser fuzz targets, blocking smoke CI, and scheduled retained-corpus runs.
- `af16b8502b705c9a2a55ca2d1d90a18d1112cccd` and `428df7e538d53ad32b77772975bce8075b7e49bd` fix Linux-hosted contract defects exposed after the first push: undeclared ripgrep use and non-root Compose secret ownership/mode ordering.

Final hosted CI receipt for `428df7e`:
- run 30202100025: success
- tests/linters, race, four fuzz smoke jobs, generated docs, executable deployment contracts, Grafana, real Compose config-check/health, and disposable-kind Helm install/test/upgrade all passed
- actionlint, zizmor, CodeQL, Docker Security, Scorecard, and docs dispatch also passed

Release Please run 30202100253 succeeded and opened #358, `chore(main): release 4.0.0`, under the trusted PAT identity. Every release-PR check is green, including `ci-success`, deployment contracts, all fuzz jobs, dependency review, actionlint, and zizmor.

Only #436 remains open. Its core repair is in `3ad3966`; the tag-correct v3.0.0 notices artifact is prepared and reviewed, but attaching it to the already published release remains an explicit-approval GitHub write. No release asset has been uploaded or replaced.

## Epic completion receipt

The final open child, #436, is complete. The approved tag-correct v3.0.0 `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` asset was uploaded without replacement and downloaded again with matching SHA-256 `91c47a8b6d5825cd5282c58ffab32381082f6cfe68e71fa994e1d625af15c62c`.

All 11 children now have a durable disposition: ten delivered, with #445 explicitly descoped. Final `main` CI and Release Please receipts are green, and release PR #358 (`chore(main): release 4.0.0`) has a fully green check set for maintainer merge.

## Mission

Separate exporter/poller health from firewall operational telemetry with a generated self-observability dashboard, complete metric inventory, fleet-safe alerts, executable alert behavior, and per-rule runbooks.

## Audit baseline

- The live main dashboard mixes Diagnostics, Log Shipping, and Recording Rules into the operational view; no separate OPNsense exporter self-observability dashboard exists.
- The live stack exposed 34 self-metric names and 45 healthy rules, but current coverage gates exclude self metrics.
- One exporter can disappear from a multi-instance rule as MissingSeries, `/metrics` overload is log-only, and current runbook links point to incomplete inventories.

The audit baseline was clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4). Read every child issue in full, including later comments, before changing code: the child acceptance criteria and comments are binding and may supersede this summary.

## Binding decisions

- Self-observability covers exporter process, HTTP admission, scheduler/collectors, snapshots, OPNsense reachability, OTLP metrics delivery, log delivery/queues, rules, and build identity—not firewall domain health.
- Keep the main operational dashboard to a compact exporter-health summary and context-preserving link.
- Generate dashboard/rules/runbooks from source and inventory every self metric or document an explicit exemption.
- Alert tests must cover MissingSeries, total NoData, multi-instance isolation, pending windows, stale retained data, and recovery.
- Stable `opnsense_instance`/resource identity is mandatory; one firewall must never mask another.
- Do not duplicate notification routing policy or stack-specific contact points in this repository.

## Child worklist

- [x] #426 — feat(server): instrument metrics-handler admission, latency, and partial-gather failures (`P3`)
- [x] #427 — feat(grafana): make exporter disappearance fleet-safe (`P1`)
- [x] #428 — test(grafana): generate and gate the exporter self-metric inventory (`P1`)
- [x] #429 — test(grafana): add deterministic query and alert-behavior validation (`P1`)
- [x] #430 — docs(grafana): generate complete per-rule runbooks (`P2`)
- [x] #431 — feat(grafana): create a dedicated exporter self-observability dashboard and rule namespace (`P1`)

- [x] #466 — fix(grafana): OTLP delivery panels filter on a label the `otlp_*` metrics never carry (`P1`, filed from #414's inventory)

## Implementation waves

1. Freeze self-metric identity and inventory seams using #428 plus cross-epic dependencies #395, #382, and #388.
2. Add missing server telemetry in #426 and fleet-safe disappearance in #427.
3. Build deterministic alert/query behavior in #429 before expanding or reorganizing rule manifests.
4. Generate the dedicated dashboard/rule namespace in #431; keep artifacts single-owner during wiring.
5. Finish complete per-rule runbooks in #430 and live-validate navigation, queries, alerts, and empty states.

## Cross-epic dependencies

- #382 supplies retained-content/full-success clocks; #388 supplies optional metric-push health.
- #394, #395, and #400 supply honest log freshness, identity, pressure, and loss semantics.
- #419 owns cross-dashboard navigation helpers.

## Coding-agent launch prompt

Deliver the retained scope in this epic. Start by reading this epic and every open child issue in full, including all comments. Reconfirm each premise against current `main`; if a premise is already fixed or disproven, record the evidence on that issue and close or rescope it instead of forcing a change.

Before parallel work, freeze every shared seam named above: exact metric names and types, labels and closed vocabularies, config keys/defaults, generated artifact ownership, and compatibility behavior. Use one file owner per lane. Keep integration/composition files in one lane or one wiring pass.

For each implementation issue, use strict TDD: add the smallest failing regression test, observe the correct failure, implement the minimum fix, then refactor. Keep the issue body/checklist current and post meaningful progress comments with commit SHAs. Completing commits must include `Closes #N` and land by direct push to `main` under the repository workflow.

At every wiring checkpoint and before claiming completion, run the full gate: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`. Run targeted race, parser, integration, live-canary, release, or Grafana checks required by each child. Generated files must be regenerated from source; do not hand-edit generated JSON or docs.

For live Grafana or OPNsense validation, keep production read-only unless a child explicitly defines a controlled testbed write. A successful local test, API response, or GitHub create call is not delivery proof: use scoped read-back, exact CI/release receipts, and live query/visual evidence where required.

## Epic completion bar

A responder can open one generated dashboard and determine whether collection, scheduling, retained data, HTTP serving, metric export, log delivery, or rule evaluation is unhealthy for a specific exporter; every self metric and rule has tested coverage and a usable runbook.

- Every retained child is closed by its completing commit or explicitly descoped with a durable rationale.
- The epic checklist and phase comments reconstruct what landed, which SHAs delivered it, what was rejected, and what remains.
- The full gate is green on the final integrated `main`, with exact remote CI/release/live receipts for affected surfaces.
