## Clean programme pause — queued, not started

This epic has not entered implementation. #426–#431 are all open, have no comments, and the parent checklist matches live child state. No child body has been adopted as an implementation plan, no interface or metric contract has been frozen, and no source, generated dashboard/rule, Grafana, or external state has changed under #451.

Resume only after #450 reaches its own clean disposition. Start with the complete self-observation catalogue, then reconcile the parent/child priority mismatch for #428/#429 before coding. #450 must freeze #419’s UID/navigation contract first; #429 must not be pulled into #450 for convenience.

## Final safe-pause reconciliation

All six children #426–#431 remain open, queued, and untouched; each now has an issue-local pause receipt. The parent checklist matches live state. No metric/interface contract, test, source edit, generated dashboard/rule/runbook, or live Grafana change exists under #451.

Repository baseline: `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`, clean and identical locally/remotely, with all eight exact-SHA workflows terminal-success. Resume only after #450 has a clean disposition; reconcile the #428/#429 priority mismatch and consume the frozen #419 navigation contract before implementation.

## Clean safe-pause confirmation — 2026-07-26

No #451 implementation has started. Its child issues remain open with their queued status receipts; no dashboard UID, navigation, generated catalogue, rule, or runbook seam was changed. The #428/#429 parent-versus-child priority inconsistency remains to reconcile before implementation.

Repository main is clean, fully pushed at `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`, and all eight workflows for that exact SHA are successful. This epic is paused before inventory and design work, with no partial changes.

## Updated clean-pause baseline — 2026-07-26

No #451 implementation has started. The repository's fully pushed green baseline is now `9470bf6568382e8636e30184a53d0ec28d90f317`; all eight exact-SHA workflows succeeded. No self-observability dashboard, UID, navigation, rule, catalogue, or runbook work is partially present.

## Tracker inconsistency reconciled — #428 and #429 are P1

Recorded before implementation, as this epic's pause receipts required.

**#428 and #429 each had three priority sources disagreeing:** the `P1` label, this epic's worklist entry (`P1`), and their own body text (`**Priority:** P2`). Two of three said P1.

**Resolved as P1; the body text was the stale one.** The decisive argument is this epic's own wave plan rather than a majority count: wave 1 is "freeze self-metric identity and inventory seams using #428" and wave 3 is "build deterministic alert/query behavior in #429 **before** expanding or reorganizing rule manifests". Both are foundations that gate #430 (runbooks) and #431 (the dedicated dashboard), and a prerequisite cannot sensibly rank below the work that depends on it. Labels and parent were already correct; only the body lines were edited, each annotated with the correction and its date so a future reader does not silently flip them back.

No other #428–#431 priority disagreement exists: #426 is P3, #427 P1, #430 P2 in every source; #431 carries no body priority line and is P1 by label and worklist.

## A defect routed into this epic from #414

While inventorying dashboard instance scoping for #414, four panels were found **structurally guaranteed to render empty**, and they are self-observability panels, so they belong here rather than in #450.

`Builder.sel_pipeline()` (`grafana/builder.py:517-520`) is a pure alias of `sel()`, so it injects `opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"`. The four OTLP delivery panels built with it (`grafana/build_dashboard.py:375-407`) query the `opnsense_exporter_otlp_*` family, which is registered on the **raw** self-metrics registry (`internal/telemetry/provider.go:61`) with **no** `opnsense_instance` label — unlike `opnsense_exporter_logs_*`, which goes through `SelfMetricsRegisterer` (`internal/logship/pipeline.go:88-89`) and does carry it. A `=~` matcher never matches an absent label, so those four panels cannot return data for any selection.

Compounding it, the comment at `build_dashboard.py:371-373` asserts the opposite — that `sel_pipeline()` is a "bare selector" and that using `sel()` "would render every panel here permanently empty". The premise about the missing label is right; the conclusion is inverted, because `sel_pipeline` is not bare. **A successor must not trust that comment.**

This is the same class of problem #427 and #428 exist to prevent: a self-metric whose identity story is undocumented and untested, and an inventory gate that does not cover self metrics. #414 deliberately left it untouched. Either fix the identity (wrap the OTLP registry the way logship does, so the family carries `opnsense_instance`) or fix the scoping to a target join, but do it here with a test, not as a drive-by.

No #451 implementation has started. No source, generated dashboard/rule/runbook, or live Grafana state has changed under this epic.

## Pause state — still not started, and two things now waiting for it

No #451 implementation has begun. No self-observability dashboard, UID, navigation contract, generated catalogue, rule namespace or runbook exists in partial form. Nothing under this epic was changed beyond issue bookkeeping.

Two items were resolved or routed here today:

- **The #428/#429 priority contradiction is settled at P1** and their bodies corrected with the reasoning attached (see the comment above). Labels and this epic's worklist were already right; only the body text was stale.
- **#466 was filed and added to the worklist** — the four OTLP delivery panels filter on `opnsense_instance`, a label the `otlp_*` family never carries, so they are structurally always empty. It was found while inventorying scoping for #414 and deliberately left unfixed there, because self-metric identity is this epic's mission rather than #450's. The issue carries both candidate fixes and the evidence for each.

### What #451 can now build on that did not exist this morning

- **`d55384c` (#413/#414)** froze the instance-identity contract in code: `SCOPE_COLLECTOR` / `SCOPE_SELF_LABELED` / `SCOPE_TARGET_JOIN` / `SCOPE_GLOBAL`, with `target_join` being the tested pattern for a metric that carries no appliance label (join to `opnsense_up` on `(job, instance)`). That is directly reusable for #427's fleet-safe disappearance work and for whatever #428 decides about self-metric identity. Both scoping guards ship with **empty** allowlists.
- **`4002fb1` (#424)** extended `tools/promqlcheck` to parse all **100** dashboard variable queries in addition to 970 panel targets. Any variable a self-observability dashboard adds is now syntax-checked in CI.
- **`3514a9e` (#418)** and **`ae0f13d` (#464)** established that a counter must end in `_total` or the OTLP-fed backend and the repo disagree about its name, and left an **unconditional** cross-surface guard enforcing it. #426's new server metrics must satisfy it.
- The exporter's self-metric identity split is now documented rather than folklore: `opnsense_exporter_logs_*` carries `opnsense_instance` via `logship.SelfMetricsRegisterer`; `opnsense_exporter_otlp_*` does not, because `telemetry.Start` receives the raw registry; `go_*` and `process_*` never will. That asymmetry is the thing #428's inventory has to reckon with, and #466 is the first bug it produced.

### Standing guidance for whoever resumes

Start with the complete self-observation catalogue, per this epic's own wave plan, and reconcile it against the identity split above before designing anything. Do not pull #429 into #450 for convenience. #419 owns cross-dashboard navigation and is itself waiting on #431's destination existing, so the UID/navigation contract has to be frozen here before #419 or #453's #435 can consume it.

One caution carried from #414's inventory: the comment at `grafana/build_dashboard.py:371-373` used to invert its own conclusion about `sel_pipeline()`. It has been corrected and now names #466, but the episode is the reason #428 exists — a self-metric whose identity story is undocumented and untested will grow a confident wrong comment.

## Premise revalidation complete — run resumed 2026-07-27, baseline `96a35b7`

Per this epic's own binding rule, every child's premises were reconfirmed against current `main` before any code. The children were audited at `52ef4b2`; ~87 commits have landed since. Findings below are the durable record — **three acceptance criteria are already satisfied and should not be re-implemented**, and two children are materially larger than their bodies suggest.

### #428 — three criteria already met, the core gap is unchanged

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| `scrape_skips_total` removed/deprecated + tested | **ALREADY DONE** — `0168186` (Closes #439) retired it; `TestScrapeSkipsCounterIsRetired` guards reintroduction; `docs/upgrading.md` carries the v4.0 migration note |
| `process_*`/`go_*` treatment explicit and transport-aware | **ALREADY DONE** — `build_dashboard.py` scopes them via the `has_go_runtime` target-join sentinel with a Go-runtime row |
| Queue byte occupancy has panels | **ALREADY DONE** — `logs_queue_bytes`/`logs_queue_max_bytes` are on `grafana/tabs/logs.py` and in `build_rules.py` |

Still live, and the substance of the issue: the coverage catalogue is built by regexing `docs/metrics/metrics.md`, which docgen fills **from the collector registry only**. The gate's 838/838 therefore says nothing about self-metrics. Confirmed uncovered today:

- `opnsense_exporter_logs_debug_captured_total`, `opnsense_exporter_logs_debug_capture_dropped_total`
- **all four `opnsense_exporter_annotations_*` metrics** — a family the issue never named, in the same state. Folding it into scope.

`grafana/README.md:41` still claims coverage of "**every** metric the exporter emits", which is false as worded.

### #427 — fully live, nothing pre-empted

All 41 alert rules enumerated. `opnsense-exporter-down` is still bare `opnsense_up` / `lt 1` / `for 15m` / `noDataState: Alerting`, and **no rule implements per-instance disappearance**. The two rules using `unless` (`collector-never-stored`, `carp-vip-fault`) suppress a sub-condition on an instance that still reports — they do not detect one vanishing.

Correction to this epic's own figure: the live rule count is **41 alerts + 14 recording**, not the "45 healthy rules" recorded in the audit baseline. `build_rules.py` has not changed since `52ef4b2`, so the 45 was already wrong when written.

### #429 — live; the reusable half is bigger than the issue implies

`tools/promqlcheck` already embeds the real `prometheus/promql/parser` plus a Grafana-token substitution table — but it runs **only against `grafana/dashboard.json`**. No alert or recording expression is syntax-checked by anything in CI. Extending it to the rule manifests is a small change against working code and should be split out and landed early.

The timeline/MissingSeries half is genuinely net-new: `rg promtool` returns nothing repo-wide, and there is no rule-evaluation harness of any kind.

Stale figure: the suite is **191 tests**, not 16. The double-run in CI (`grafana-test` as both its own step and a prerequisite of `grafana-check`) is still real.

### #430 — live, citations stale

`RUNBOOK_URL` moved to `grafana/uids.py:127` as part of #419's registry work, but behaviour is unchanged: **all 41 rules share one generic anchor**. README parity is now 23 of 41 alert rows and 8 of 14 recording rules — worse in absolute terms than the 19/31 and 8/14 the issue recorded. Nothing validates that a runbook link resolves.

### #431 — significantly larger than the body suggests; two blockers confirmed

- **The builder cannot emit more than one dashboard.** `OUT` is a hardcoded literal path and `main()` writes exactly one manifest; `DASH_NAME` overrides only `metadata.name`, so a second invocation overwrites the same file. `organize_tabs` additionally raises on any leaf-tab set that is not exactly its fixed expected set.
- **Splitting content breaks `make grafana-check` today.** `coverage()` is scoped to a single `Builder` instance with no cross-dashboard aggregation, so moving Diagnostics/Log Shipping panels out would make their metrics report MISSING on the main dashboard.

#419 is CLOSED and deliberately left the link to this issue: `HEALTH_UID` is reserved with `exists=False`, and `test_links.py::test_reserved_destinations_emit_no_link` enforces that no link is emitted until #431 flips it in the same commit that generates the dashboard.

**Open scoping question for the owner:** the Recording Rules tab is precomputed *operational* signals (firewall, gateway, DNS), not exporter self-health. It does not match this epic's own scope line ("not firewall domain health"), so I plan to leave it on the main dashboard and move only Diagnostics + Log Shipping. Say if that is wrong.

### Execution order

Unchanged from the epic's wave plan, which the findings support:

1. **#427** — self-contained, alerts-only, highest operator value (a firewall can vanish unpaged). Starting here.
2. **#429a** — point `promqlcheck` at the rule manifests. Small, independent, runs in parallel with #427.
3. **#428** — the inventory/gate foundation, minus the three criteria already met.
4. **#426** — depends on #428's gate existing, per its own dependency note.
5. **#429b** — the timeline harness.
6. **#431**, then **#430**.

**Not in scope this run:** #466, #471 and #475 were explicitly excluded by the owner at the start of the session and that exclusion has not been lifted. #466 is a child of this epic, so it will need picking up separately.

## Wave 1 + 2 delivered — `bf581a7`

Four issues closed and one advanced since the revalidation comment. Baseline was `4c529e3`; main is now `bf581a7`, full gate green (`go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-test`, `make grafana-check`).

| Issue | SHA | State |
|---|---|---|
| #428 self-metric inventory + gate | `bf581a7` | **closed** |
| #455 netbird `daemonStatus` | `bf581a7` | **closed** |
| #458 FRR OSPFv3 route type | `f199ef4` | **closed** |
| #429 manifest contract + CI double-run | `55d3ce9` | open — behaviour harness outstanding |

### #428, the part that matters for the rest of this epic

`docs/metrics/self-metrics.md` is now generated by **scanning the source** for Prometheus metric declarations (`scripts/docgen/selfmetrics.go`) and feeds `load_catalogue()` alongside the collector catalogue. A source scan rather than a registry gather, deliberately: gathering means reproducing `main.go`, and a metric registered through a path the reproduction happens not to build is silently absent from the inventory — which is the failure #428 exists to end.

The gate has teeth: **an unresolvable metric name is a hard docgen failure, not a skip.** Skipping would leave the bypass open — build a name from a variable and the gate stops seeing you. `internal/collector/utils.go` is the single allowlisted dynamic site and a test fails if that list grows.

Coverage went 838/838 → **869/869**, and the 31 newly-visible metrics were previously ungated in their entirety.

Two scanner bugs worth recording, both now regression-tested:

- Constants resolved **per file** missed `namespace`, which `internal/collector` declares in `collector.go` and uses from `utils.go`. Scope is per *package*.
- Ruling a declaration out by comparing its `Namespace` field alone to `opnsense_exporter` **silently lost seven metrics** declared as `Namespace: "opnsense", Subsystem: "exporter"` — `scrapes_total`, `endpoint_errors_total` and the whole `api_*` family. Rule out on the **composed prefix**, never on one field.

Turning it on surfaced exactly the six predicted misses and nothing else. Both `logs_debug_*` counters are now on a presence-gated Debug Capture row; all four `annotations_*` on a presence-gated Diagnostics row. Both families go through `logship.SelfMetricsRegisterer` so they carry `opnsense_instance` — verified before writing the selectors, precisely to avoid re-creating #466.

It also surfaced **five instant-valued self-metrics the annotation ledger had never been asked about**. All five are freshness heartbeats rather than events and are now in `NOT_ANNOTATED` with reasons. That guard firing on its own is the clearest evidence the inventory is doing something the old catalogue could not.

`grafana/README.md`'s "every metric the exporter emits" claim is now true as worded, with the one deliberate exclusion (`go_*`/`process_*`, client-library owned) stated.

### Remaining children

Order unchanged: **#426 → #429b → #431 → #430**. #426's dependency is now satisfied — the gate it wanted to enter exists, so its new server metrics will be forced onto a panel automatically.

Standing note: **#466 remains excluded by the owner** and is still a child of this epic. It needs picking up separately, and #428 did not touch it.

## Wave 3 delivered — main at `0a24a5a`

Everything below is pushed, with the full gate green at each commit (`go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-test`, `make grafana-check`).

| Issue | SHA | State |
|---|---|---|
| #426 metrics-handler instrumentation | `a73f84c` | **closed** |
| #430 per-rule runbooks | `2d303c1` | **closed** |
| #457 nested-key baseline triaged + flipped to warnings | `206026a` | **closed** |
| #459 reflect through RawMessage envelopes | `0a24a5a` | **closed** |
| #462 canary drift | — | **closed**, both halves resolved by #458 and #457 |
| #431 step 1, coverage union | `076971a` | open — steps 2 and 3 remain |

### #431 is now the only substantive child left, and step 1 is done

`coverage()` is variadic and takes the union across builders. `grafana/dashboard.json` came out **byte-identical**, which `make grafana-check` proves through its own `git diff --exit-code` rather than by assertion. Step 2 (the `DashboardSpec` refactor, also byte-identical) is in flight; step 3 is the actual split.

**Scoping call confirmed by the owner, and it is finer than the question I asked.** Recording Rules do not move as a tab. A recording rule that relates to **self-observability** may move to the health dashboard; everything else stays on the main dashboard, because those rules generate data used for monitoring OPNsense and that is where they belong. So step 3 sorts `RECORDING` per rule rather than relocating the tab wholesale.

### #429 — the remaining half needs redesigning, per owner input

The manifest-contract half landed in `55d3ce9`. The behaviour-harness half was specified around `promtool`, and that is now the wrong tool for this repo: **promtool validates queries, not whole files**, and this project ships Grafana **v2 dashboards and Grafana-managed** alert/recording rules. `tools/promqlcheck` already parses all 56 rule expressions with Prometheus' own parser (`7db33f3`), so a promtool step would largely duplicate it while still being unable to model the thing #429 actually cares about.

What is left is exactly the part promtool could never do: **MissingSeries eviction, `noDataState`/`execErrState` behaviour, and multi-instance semantics.** That points at a Python harness over the generated manifests rather than a new binary in CI. The sister pollers (`tailscale2otel`, `graph2otel`) have prior art in this area and should be checked before anything is written twice.

### Not in scope, unchanged

**#466, #471 and #475 remain excluded by the owner.** The exclusion was re-raised and not lifted. #466 is still a child of this epic and is still a live defect — four OTLP delivery panels filter on `opnsense_instance`, which `opnsense_exporter_otlp_*` never carries. #430 hit the same gap independently: `opnsense-otlp-delivery-failing` is the ONE alert that could not be given instance identity in its summary, and it is exempted with that reason recorded.

### Deployed

The dashboard is live at `gc-gitsync-m7kni@c4858ba` — ten new panels and two new sentinels, UID unchanged. **The alert manifests are NOT deployed.** All 57 changed (per-rule `runbook_url`, 20 summaries gained instance identity) and pushing them is an alerting change rather than a dashboard one, so it is left for the owner. Note the trap: `build_rules.py` currently emits `stack-labels: False`, so a `gcx resources push` without regenerating under `--stack` would strip the IRM routing labels off the live rules.

## Wave 4 delivered — every child except #466 is closed

Main is at `a62b25a`, pushed, full gate green at each commit.

| Issue | SHA | State |
|---|---|---|
| #431 self-observability split | `a486d0c` + `4a33aa5` | **closed** |
| #429 behaviour harness | `b5afdac` | **closed** |
| #478 zero-fill provenance gate | `a62b25a` | **closed** |

### #431 — the dashboard family is real

`grafana/dashboard-health.json` (uid `opnsense-exporter-health`) carries Diagnostics + Log Shipping, 49 panels. The main dashboard keeps a three-tile **Exporter Health** row on Overview linking through — the tripwire the split would otherwise remove, since a reader looking at a flat graph has no reason to suspect the collector stopped rather than the firewall going quiet. **#419's last criterion is discharged**: `HEALTH_UID` flipped `exists=True` in the same commit that generated the dashboard.

**Recording rules did not move.** Sorted per rule per the owner's call: all 14 derive from firewall metrics, none from `opnsense_exporter_*`, so the self-observability set is empty. A test with a control assertion now enforces that going forward rather than leaving it as a comment.

Step 4 routed 12 of 42 alerts into `opnsense-exporter-health-alerts`. Membership is declared per rule, not inferred, because `OPNsenseExporterDown` and `OPNsenseExporterInstanceMissing` fire on `opnsense_up` — not an `opnsense_exporter_*` metric but entirely a statement about the exporter.

### #429 — and the finding that justifies #427 retroactively

`grafana/alerts/ruleeval.py` models Grafana's state machine against the generated manifests. Not promtool: promtool evaluates Prometheus rules, this ships Grafana-managed ones, and every remaining criterion was about behaviour promtool has no concept of. Semantics fetched from the Grafana 13.1 docs, not recalled.

The finding: **`OPNsenseExporterDown` has `noDataState: Alerting`, which reads like "page when a firewall goes away", and does not do that.** With any other firewall still reporting, the vanished one is a stale *series* — held two evaluation intervals, then resolved. Nothing pages. There is now a test saying so beside one showing `OPNsenseExporterInstanceMissing` does catch it.

### #478 — clean, and now gated

All 7 `or vector(0)` sites pass, so the exemption list ships empty. Two soundness details needed a second pass: only `and` gates count as a guarantee (the VPN domain's OR group proves nothing about `has_tor` individually), and the metric-name regex has to reject both the `opnsense_instance` label and the interpolated `$opnsense_instance` variable, which on the first run made every panel look like it charted a metric of that name.

### Standing epic-wide notes

**Deployment is owner-gated and has grown.** Now 58 alert manifests across **two** folders, plus a **new** dashboard file. Importing only `dashboard.json` leaves the summary row's link 404ing. The `--stack` trap is unchanged and is now written into `grafana/README.md` at the push instructions: regenerating without `--stack` and pushing would strip IRM routing labels off live rules.

**#466 is the only child left open and remains excluded by the owner.** It is a live defect — four OTLP delivery panels filter on `opnsense_instance`, which `opnsense_exporter_otlp_*` never carries — and those panels now sit on the health dashboard, where an operator is *more* likely to open them. Asking rather than assuming: this epic cannot close until it is either fixed or explicitly deferred.

## Epic complete — closing

All seven children are closed. The last one, #466, closed today once the fix reached the live stack and the four OTLP delivery panels could be verified by live query rather than by regenerating JSON.

### The completion bar, verified rather than asserted

> A responder can open one generated dashboard and determine whether collection, scheduling, retained data, HTTP serving, metric export, log delivery, or rule evaluation is unhealthy for a specific exporter.

Rendered the published `opnsense-exporter-health` dashboard against the live stack over a 6h window. Every row returns data for a real instance selection:

| row | state on the live render |
| --- | --- |
| Scrape Health | `opnsense_up` green throughout; scrape rate vs OPNsense API rate both plotted; endpoint errors 0 across every endpoint |
| Per-Collector Scrapes | poll duration per collector (8.02 ms – 184 µs range visible), poll success green for all |
| Per-Collector Poll Schedule | interval, scheduler liveness (last attempt age) and next-poll countdown, per collector |
| Per-Collector Data Freshness | retained data age and time-since-last-full-success, per collector |
| OTLP Delivery Health | Enabled, 0 consecutive failures, 1.19 min since last success, export rate split by `result` |
| API Requests | per-endpoint request rate and p95 latency |
| API Response Cache | 98.1% hit rate, hits by kind and by endpoint |
| Metrics Handler Serving Path | in-flight, requests by status, admission rejections, gather errors, request p95 |
| Exporter Build & Collectors | build info (Go version, instance, version) and per-collector enabled state |
| Exporter Runtime | goroutines, memory, CPU |

That is collection, scheduling, retained data, HTTP serving, metric export and rule evaluation all answerable for a named exporter from one page, with log delivery on the dashboard's second tab.

The OTLP Delivery Health row is the one worth calling out: it was structurally guaranteed to be empty for the entire life of this epic, and only started returning data today. Its export-rate panel shows data appearing part-way through the window, which is exactly the deployment of #466's fix.

### What landed

| child | completing commit |
| --- | --- |
| #426 metrics-handler admission/latency/partial-gather | closed in-epic |
| #427 fleet-safe exporter disappearance | closed in-epic |
| #428 self-metric inventory gate | closed in-epic |
| #429 deterministic query and alert-behavior validation | `b5afdac`, `a62b25a` |
| #430 per-rule runbooks | closed in-epic |
| #431 dedicated self-observability dashboard and rule namespace | `a486d0c`, `4a33aa5` |
| #466 `otlp_*` instance identity | `46e90f5` |

Current inventory: **50 self metrics**, **42 alerts of which 12 are exporter-health**, **14 recording rules**, 58 generated Grafana-managed manifests, and a 49-panel health dashboard across 2 tabs.

### Binding decisions, all held

Self-observability stayed scoped to the exporter rather than firewall domain health. The main operational dashboard kept a compact three-tile exporter-health summary with a link through to the detail, so an operator reading a flat graph has a tripwire telling them the exporter stopped collecting rather than the firewall going quiet. Dashboard, rules and runbooks are all generated from source. Notification routing policy is not duplicated in this repo.

**Stable identity is mandatory, and #466 was the last place that was not true.** `SUMMARY_INSTANCE_EXEMPT` is now empty as a direct consequence — its single entry existed only because the OTLP family had no instance to name. The mechanism stays for a family that genuinely cannot carry one.

### Not in scope, filed separately

#479 — three `loki_table()` panels on the *main* dashboard exceed Loki's 500-series limit and render "No data". Found while gathering render evidence for #471. It is firewall telemetry presentation, not exporter self-observability, so it is not a child of this epic.

### Gate

Green on the final integrated `main` (`a4340cc`): `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `make docs-check`, `make grafana-test` (326 tests), `make grafana-check` (991 Prometheus targets, 108 variable queries, 20 annotation queries, 56 rule expressions; 58 manifests valid).

Both dashboards are deployed to the live stack via gitsync (`gc-gitsync-m7kni` `a28a384`).

### Correction to the SHA table above

Two rows in the previous comment were wrong, and the table is the part a future reader will trust, so here it is derived from the closing keywords rather than from recent-commit context:

| child | completing commit |
| --- | --- |
| #426 metrics-handler admission/latency/partial-gather | `a73f84c` feat(server): instrument the /metrics serving path |
| #427 fleet-safe exporter disappearance | `4c529e3` feat(grafana): alert when one exporter vanishes and the others do not |
| #428 self-metric inventory gate | `bf581a7` test(grafana): inventory the exporter's self-metrics and gate them |
| #429 deterministic query and alert-behavior validation | `b5afdac` test(alerts): model Grafana's rule state machine against the shipped manifests |
| #430 per-rule runbooks | `2d303c1` docs(grafana): generate a runbook per alert instead of one shared anchor |
| #431 dedicated dashboard and rule namespace | `4a33aa5` feat(grafana): route exporter self-health alerts to their own folder (dashboard split landed in `a486d0c`) |
| #466 `otlp_*` instance identity | `46e90f5` fix(telemetry)!: give the otlp_* self-metrics an opnsense_instance label — closed by hand, no keyword in the commit |

Specifically: **`a62b25a` closes #478, not #429**, and `a486d0c` carries no closing keyword — it is the dashboard-split half of #431, which `4a33aa5` closed. Everything else in the previous comment stands.

body:
## Mission

Turn the generated operational dashboard, recording rules, and alert rules into syntax-, semantics-, unit-, instance-, compatibility-, and performance-checked contracts rather than JSON that merely imports.

## Audit baseline

- Current main generates 731 panels/elements across 41 tabs; repository gates report 831/831 catalogue coverage, 39 alerts, and 14 recordings. The deployed GitSync dashboard remains at 711 elements and 100 variables pending an ownership-safe publication.
- Live inspection found one invalid generated Zenarmor query, eight PF counter consumers using impossible names, 94 of 95 Prometheus sentinels unscoped, nine unscoped Loki panels, misleading thresholds/units, and no drilldowns.
- Grafana 13.2 live rendering is polished overall; the work is targeted correctness and operability, not a wholesale redesign.

The audit baseline was clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4). Read every child issue in full, including later comments, before changing code: the child acceptance criteria and comments are binding and may supersede this summary.

## Binding decisions

- Generated Python/source files own dashboards and rules. Never hand-edit generated JSON/manifests.
- Grafana 13 schema v2 remains canonical. Older compatibility must be generated/tested and may degrade explicitly.
- Selected instance must constrain optional-feature sentinels and diagnostic panels. Intentional fleet totals must be labelled, not silently merged.
- Parse PromQL with a real parser; use deterministic time-series fixtures for behavior. Regex/schema checks alone are insufficient.
- Metric type, exported Prometheus name, unit, threshold, dashboard query, recording rule, alert, and docs must agree.
- Measure performance before collapsing sentinels or changing query windows. Preserve honest optional-feature gating.

## Child worklist

- [x] #412 — fix(grafana): validate and repair malformed generated PromQL (`P1`)
- [x] #413 — fix(grafana): scope Loki panels and sentinels to the selected instance (`P1`)
- [x] #414 — fix(grafana): scope Prometheus feature sentinels to the selected instance (`P1`)
- [x] #415 — fix(grafana): remove synthetic thresholds from non-percentage bar gauges (`P2`)
- [x] #416 — fix(grafana): separate mixed units in ingest panels (`P2`)
- [x] #417 — docs(grafana): generate the feature-sentinel contract (`P2`)
- [x] #418 — fix(metrics): align PF packet counter names and types across export, docs, dashboards, and rules (`P0`)
- [x] #464 — fix(metrics): suffix the nine remaining counters that lack `_total` (`P1`, filed from #418)
- [x] #467 — fix(grafana): `gauge()` still injects the synthetic 70/90 thresholds #415 removed from `bargauge()` (`P3`, filed from #415)
- [x] #468 — fix(grafana): preserve exporter-instance identity through panel aggregations and tables (`P1`, filed from #425's audit)
- [x] #419 — feat(grafana): add context-preserving dashboard and panel drilldowns (`P2`, delivered in `6100ad6`; criterion 2's self-observability link carried by #431 as a one-flag change, criterion 5 won't-do per owner)
- [x] ~~#420 — feat(grafana): provide a Grafana 11 and 12 compatibility dashboard~~ (`P2`, **DESCOPED** by owner decision 2026-07-27: Grafana 13 only, given the dynamic dashboard. Implemented, then reverted in `c89248a`; the version-failure matrix is kept in the docs.)
- [x] #421 — feat(grafana): add event annotations for reboots, interface resets, HA, and gateway transitions (`P2`, delivered in `9f20ac9` + `7b943b6`; rendered criteria closed against the published dashboard)
- [x] #422 — perf(grafana): profile dashboard load and collapse redundant sentinel and log queries (`P2`, measured live + regression guard in `421bf96`; dashboard published via GitSync and read back at generation 6; criterion 1 won't-do per owner)
- [x] #470 — fix(grafana): move rarely-toggled annotation layers and links into the v2 controls menu (`P3`, filed from this epic's own rendered validation, delivered in `db30892`)
- [x] #423 — docs(grafana): describe ambiguous operator-facing panels (`P3`)
- [x] #424 — fix(grafana): keep the device variable populated when firewall metrics are disabled (`P2`)
- [x] #425 — research(grafana): audit fleet-mode panels for cross-instance row merging (`P2`)

## Implementation waves

1. Land executable correctness guards first: #412, #418, and the semantic fixture foundation needed by #429.
2. Fix instance scoping and fleet behavior: #413, #414, #424, and #425. Freeze variable/label names before parallel edits.
3. Correct presentation contracts: #415, #416, #417, and #423.
4. Add navigation/compatibility/event context: #419, #420, and #421.
5. Profile and optimize only after correctness: #422.

## Cross-epic dependencies

- #421 depends on interface-reset/CARP event inputs from #375 and #405.
- #419 must freeze UIDs/variables with the self-observability and companion-dashboard epics.

## Coding-agent launch prompt

Deliver the retained scope in this epic. Start by reading this epic and every open child issue in full, including all comments. Reconfirm each premise against current `main`; if a premise is already fixed or disproven, record the evidence on that issue and close or rescope it instead of forcing a change.

Before parallel work, freeze every shared seam named above: exact metric names and types, labels and closed vocabularies, config keys/defaults, generated artifact ownership, and compatibility behavior. Use one file owner per lane. Keep integration/composition files in one lane or one wiring pass.

For each implementation issue, use strict TDD: add the smallest failing regression test, observe the correct failure, implement the minimum fix, then refactor. Keep the issue body/checklist current and post meaningful progress comments with commit SHAs. Completing commits must include `Closes #N` and land by direct push to `main` under the repository workflow.

At every wiring checkpoint and before claiming completion, run the full gate: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`. Run targeted race, parser, integration, live-canary, release, or Grafana checks required by each child. Generated files must be regenerated from source; do not hand-edit generated JSON or docs.

For live Grafana or OPNsense validation, keep production read-only unless a child explicitly defines a controlled testbed write. A successful local test, API response, or GitHub create call is not delivery proof: use scoped read-back, exact CI/release receipts, and live query/visual evidence where required.

## Epic completion bar

Every generated Prometheus query parses; representative queries/rules have deterministic behavioral tests; live panels/recordings return correctly typed and scoped data; navigation, compatibility, units, and performance have explicit tested contracts.

- Every retained child is closed by its completing commit or explicitly descoped with a durable rationale.
- The epic checklist and phase comments reconstruct what landed, which SHAs delivered it, what was rejected, and what remains.
- The full gate is green on the final integrated `main`, with exact remote CI/release/live receipts for affected surfaces.

## Final safe-pause reconciliation

All fourteen children #412–#425 remain open, queued, and untouched; each now has an issue-local pause receipt. The parent checklist matches live state. No seam was frozen and no RED test, source edit, generated artifact, live Grafana write, or local half-change exists under #450.

Repository baseline: `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`, clean and identical locally/remotely, with all eight exact-SHA workflows terminal-success. Resume with a full parent/child reread and current ownership validation, then #412 and #418 first. Do not pull #451/#429 forward.

## #412 completion and clean pause receipt

#412 is complete at [`9470bf6568382e8636e30184a53d0ec28d90f317`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/9470bf6568382e8636e30184a53d0ec28d90f317). Its parent checkbox is now checked. The delivered gate parses all 968 generated Prometheus targets with the pinned upstream parser and fixes the only rejected query.

The full local gate and all eight exact-SHA workflows are green. Local `main`, `origin/main`, and remote `main` match; the worktree is clean. No dashboard/rule deployment, release publication, testbed mutation, or release-please PR merge occurred.

This is the next logical safe pause: #412 is fully delivered and #418 has not begun. Resume with P0 #418's atomic PF counter contract migration after rereading its current body/comments and revalidating live ownership.

## Phase 1 — P0 #418 delivered; scoping pair in flight

### #418 closed by [`3514a9e`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/3514a9eecd30646e659558fcbc1752b472c6906b)

The eight PF packet descriptors now end in `_total`, so the direct `/metrics` and OTLP-canonicalized names agree, with no alias. All eight workflows for the exact SHA are terminal-success. Full receipt with RED evidence and gate output is on the child.

**A premise correction worth carrying:** the audit's phrasing that the eight consumer names were *impossible* was not accurate — they were real exported descriptors, just unsuffixed. The child's own 2026-07-26 reconciliation had already restated it correctly as an OTLP-canonicalization mismatch, and that is what was implemented. A successor should not go looking for a nonexistent metric.

Two independent defects were fixed alongside it, neither of which any existing gate could have caught:

- **`docgen` mis-typed the eight packet metrics as Gauge.** The sixteen pf pass/block metrics were emitted through a `map[*prometheus.Desc]int64` loop keyed by one desc variable, defeating static per-field type attribution and falling back to the `_total`-suffix heuristic. Fixed at the root — each metric now emits via its own `c.<field>` selector — so the catalogue types all sixteen as Counter *because resolution succeeds*, not because the suffix is now present.
- **Four invented metric names in hand-written docs** (`docs/metrics/overview.md`, `docs/integration-dashboards.md`) that never existed in any form, plus `opnsense_firewall_states_{current,limit}` which are really `opnsense_firewall_pf_states_{current,limit}`. Neither file is generated and `doclint` only validates flag/env tokens, so nothing covered them.

`tools/promqlcheck` from #412 is syntax-only — `rate(<nonexistent_metric>[5m])` parses fine — so #412 could not have caught this either. The new guards close that: a Go test asserting every counter-typed firewall family ends in `_total`, and a Python test asserting no Counter-typed metric referenced by the generated dashboard or Grafana-managed rules lacks the suffix.

### Deviation: nine more metrics share the defect — filed as #464

`opnsense_ipsec_phase{1,2}_{bytes,packets}_{in,out}` and `opnsense_vnstat_total_bytes` are Counters without `_total`, consumed with `rate()` today, so they are in the same live-blank state. They are out of #418's enumerated scope, so they are carried in an explicitly commented `KNOWN_PRE_EXISTING_VIOLATIONS` set in the new guard and filed as **#464**, whose acceptance requires emptying and deleting that set. `opnsense_vnstat_total_bytes` needs a naming decision there rather than a mechanical suffix. **#464 is a new child of this epic and is not yet on the worklist checklist above.**

### Scope grew, on owner instruction, and it was the right call

The issue as filed defined derived annotation *queries*. Mid-implementation the owner
restated the intent: the exporter should **push** annotations into Grafana when the
operator opts in, and the event set should cover everything derivable, explicitly including
configuration changes so a new firewall rule can be traced to the graph that stepped. Both
halves shipped. The push half is a new package (`internal/annotations`) and a new
`--annotations.*` family, off by default because it is the exporter's only outbound write.

The two halves are not redundant. Derived layers need no configuration and work for anyone
importing the dashboard; pushed annotations exist once in Grafana and therefore show on
every other dashboard, in Explore, and beside alerts. They are held in agreement by a test
that reads the Go catalogue out of the Go source, because that divergence has no symptom —
the exporter would write annotations nobody queries while the dashboard queries a tag nobody
writes, each half looking healthy alone.

### A finding this epic should keep

**The v2 `AnnotationQuery` envelope is not what the docs describe, and the live stack was
the only reliable source for it.** The real query lives under `legacyOptions`
(`expr`, `titleFormat`, `tagKeys`, `useValueForTime`) while `query.spec` stays empty — with
one exception, the built-in annotation store, whose tag query *is* `query.spec`. Both shapes
were read off Grafana's own converted node_exporter dashboard as deployed on the m7kni
stack. `useValueForTime` is what makes an event marker land at the metric's *value* rather
than at the sample that carried it, which is the difference between a reboot marker at the
real boot instant and one up to a poll interval late.

This is the same lesson as the epic's Loki-identity mapping and the LogQL prefix-`topk`
form: for Grafana schema and query semantics, the deployed stack has been right and the
documentation has not.

validation is won't-do** — applied to #422's criterion 1 *and* to #419's criterion 5, since
they are the same ask.

### Four new executable contracts

1. **A dashboard UID is unwritable at a call site.** `grafana/uids.py` is the registry;
   `dash_url()` refuses an unregistered UID, a retired UID, and — the load-bearing one — a
   **reserved** UID. `opnsense-exporter-health` is frozen with `exists=False`, so the
   main-to-self link cannot be shipped before #431 generates the dashboard. That is #419's
   criterion 2, and it is now carried on #431 as a one-flag change rather than as prose here.
2. **Every internal link carries time, instance and datasource, and nothing hidden.** A
   `var-` param must name a declared non-hidden variable, so no presence sentinel can leak
   into navigation. Grafana's `includeVars` was rejected precisely because it would.
3. **A field link may only template a label its own panel returns**, and `panel_links()`
   raises on a `${__field.…}` URL — a panel-header link has no series context, so that
   mistake is otherwise completely silent.
4. **Cold-load fan-out has a measured ceiling**, including that `preload` stays false and
   the cold tab stays a small fraction of all panel queries. 984 of 1004 panel queries are
   deferred; flattening the tab layout would multiply cold load by fifty and every count
   would still have passed.

### Findings worth carrying

- **#422's premise inverted by measurement.** The issue assumed a large fan-out implied a
  bottleneck. Live: 134 queries, none erroring, 604–1066 ms, mean 794 ms — and a control
  pair (trivial query ~0.8 s vs a 44,525-series match ~1.5 s) shows the band is per-request
  overhead, not backend work. So there is no expensive query to fix; cost is a **count of
  round trips**. Sentinel collapsing is therefore *not* justified by the numbers and was not
  done — the epic's own rule to preserve honest optional-feature gating stands.
- **Three genuinely duplicated cold-load queries exist and are kept knowingly.** Overview's
  three health tiles duplicate the Health History panel's queries verbatim; Grafana cannot
  share a query set across panels, so collapsing means deleting a visualisation. Recorded
  with that reason; a new duplicate now fails the build.
- **Flow's `interface` label is description space, checked live.** Values are `AAISP, CAM,
  IOT, LAN, MGMT, VIRGIN` plus unresolved device names — so flow drilldowns set `$interface`.
  The #98 trap is real and silent: the wrong label space navigates to a selection matching
  nothing while looking like it worked.
- **Tab deep-linking is `dtab` / `<domain>-dtab`,** slug = title with space runs hyphenated,
  case preserved, so `Firewall & PF` MUST be percent-encoded or the query string truncates.
  Source-verified against Grafana's `TabsLayoutManager`; **not** verified against the running
  13.2 build, which has no matching OSS tag. It degrades safely — an unsupported key or a
  sentinel-hidden tab lands on the default tab with time and instance intact.
- **Annotation text is not interpolated against dashboard variables**, so #419's
  `${__url_time_range}` form cannot be reused in #421's annotation links. Concrete epoch
  milliseconds instead, with the UID and instance parameter pinned across Go and Python by
  test — the same cross-language technique #421 already used for its tag constant.

### The one blocked step, and what it gates

Publication is **prepared and validated but not pushed**: a clean shallow clone of the
GitSync repo's `origin/main`, the generated manifest staged (711 elements / 100 variables /
1 annotation layer → **739 / 106 / 16 plus the first 2 dashboard links**),
`gcx resources validate` clean. The commit+push into `rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni` was
**blocked by my own tool permissions** — a git write in a repository outside the working
directory — so the live dashboard is unchanged and the change exists only in a throwaway
clone. Nothing is half-applied.

That single step gates three criteria across two children: #422's read-back, and #421's two
rendered criteria (reset-marker alignment against rate panels, and live visual validation).
Everything else on all three children is done.

Also confirmed while staging, since it was an open risk on #421: publishing does **not**
delete the retained `n8n changes` layer. It is generator-owned as `External change events`
with byte-identical tags; only the display name changes.

### Remaining under this epic

- **#419** — closed. Criterion 2's other half is recorded on **#431**; criterion 5 is
  won't-do by owner decision.
- **#421** — link criterion ticked; two rendered criteria open, both waiting on publication.
- **#422** — four of five criteria ticked, criterion 1 won't-do; read-back waiting on
  publication.

## Epic complete — all 18 children closed, dashboard published, live-verified

### This run's commits, all pushed to `main`, all workflows terminal-success on their exact SHA

| child | SHA | what |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #419 | [`6100ad6`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/6100ad6) | frozen UID registry, URL builder, 2 dashboard links + 40 panel/field drilldowns |
| #421 | [`7b943b6`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/7b943b6) | pushed annotations link back to the dashboard at the event's instance and window |
| #422 | [`421bf96`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/421bf96) | cold-load fan-out measured live; budget + no-new-duplicates + deferred-panel guard |
| #470 | [`db30892`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/db30892) | filed from this run's own rendered validation: 16 toggles + 2 links were 3 rows of chrome |

`db30892`: 7/7 workflows green (the eighth, Trigger Documentation Sync, is path-filtered and
correctly did not fire — these commits touch no `docs/` file). CI's own job set fully green
including `ci-success`, `Grafana artifacts up-to-date`, `Generated docs up-to-date` and all
four fuzz-smoke jobs.

### The publication this epic had been blocked on, done

Two GitSync commits in `rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni`
([`4689a44`](https://github.com/rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni/commit/4689a44),
[`df87455`](https://github.com/rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni/commit/df87455)), published from a
clean shallow clone of `origin/main` — never the stale local checkout this epic warned about
twice. Read back with `gcx dashboards get`:

```text
generation        4 -> 5 -> 6
sourceChecksum    f31142912de66fa1 -> 108a8479628a9be8 -> 6b8028e57acf8fd9
elements 711 -> 739 · variables 100 -> 106 · annotations 1 -> 16 · links 0 -> 2
40 drilldown URLs · 0 retired UIDs · 0 reserved UIDs
```

**Every "live panel returns data" criterion in this epic is now met at the RENDERED level,
not just the query level.** The unlock was `gcx dashboards snapshot`, which renders through
Grafana's image renderer and needs no authenticated browser session — so the "no headless
browser on this machine" blocker recorded on #422 never applied to rendered verification, only
to client-side timing, which stays won't-do by the owner's decision.

### What the epic's mission produced, counted

Five executable contracts this run, on top of the fourteen from earlier runs: a UID cannot be
typed at a call site; a reserved UID is unwritable until its dashboard exists; every internal
link carries time + instance + datasource and no hidden sentinel; a field link may only
template a label its own panel returns; cold-load fan-out has a measured ceiling including the
deferred-panel property. `make grafana-check` now runs **185 tests**.

### Findings a successor should keep

- **#422's premise was inverted by measurement.** A large fan-out was assumed to be a
  bottleneck. Live: 134 queries, none erroring, 604–1066 ms, mean 794 ms — and a control pair
  (trivial query ~0.8 s vs a 44,525-series match ~1.5 s) shows that band is per-request
  overhead, not backend work. There is no slow query to fix; cost is round-trip COUNT.
  Sentinel collapsing is therefore not justified and was not done.
- **Rendering found a defect that reading the manifest could not.** #470 existed only because
  the published dashboard was looked at. `placement: "inControlsMenu"` IS honoured by the
  deployed 13.2 build — verified, since there is no OSS tag to pin that build against.
- **A value-as-time annotation needs a SAMPLE in the window, not just a value pointing into
  it.** A window containing the interface-reset instant rendered no marker, because the metric
  supplying the boot epoch is new in `9f20ac9` and had no series at that time. Widen the window
  to reach live samples and it renders. Self-resolves as history accumulates; applies to every
  value-as-time layer.
- **Tab deep-linking is `dtab` / `<domain>-dtab`;** slug = title with space runs hyphenated,
  case preserved, so `Firewall & PF` must be percent-encoded or the query string truncates.
  Source-verified against Grafana's `TabsLayoutManager`, and it degrades safely.
- **Annotation text is not interpolated against dashboard variables**, so #419's
  `${__url_time_range}` form cannot be reused in annotation links — concrete epoch
  milliseconds, with the UID pinned across Go and Python by test.
- **`opnsense_zenarmor` is not ours and is not retired** — it exists on the deployed stack.
  #435 folds Zenarmor into a tab here; the UID is deliberately absent from the registry rather
  than listed as never-reuse.

### Carried out of this epic, deliberately

- **#419's criterion 2** (instance + time surviving navigation to self-observability) is
  recorded on **#431** as a one-flag change: set `exists=True` on `HEALTH_UID` in
  `grafana/uids.py` in the same commit that generates that dashboard, and add the link. A test
  fails today if anyone links it early, and stops applying the moment the flag flips.
- **#419's criterion 5 and #422's criterion 1** are **won't-do** by the owner's 2026-07-27
  decision on browser-based validation, substituted with generated-URL tests, live UID
  resolution and image-renderer snapshots.
- **#420** stays descoped (Grafana 13 only), with the version-failure matrix kept in the docs.
  Confirmed this run that the repo carries no schema-v1 dashboard artifact and no legacy
  Prometheus-ruler rule file: the 41 alert + 14 recording rules are all Grafana-managed
  `rules.alerting.grafana.app/v0alpha1`.

### Boundaries

No release was published and none announced; latest release remains v3.0.0 and **PR #358 was
not merged or modified**. Production OPNsense was never mutated — every OPNsense-side check
was a read. The only writes were the two GitSync dashboard commits, both authorized on #422.
The local worktree is clean at `db30892`.

Closing this epic.

title: epic: make Grafana operational dashboards and rules executable contracts

body:
## Mission

Make event time, receiver pressure, queueing, OTLP acknowledgement, retries, drops, and source identity honest end to end; then extend the normalized syslog/flow event surface from captured evidence without reopening privacy or cardinality hazards.

## Audit baseline

- The exporter already receives NetFlow, RFC3164/RFC5424 syslog, Zenarmor documents, derives bounded metrics, enriches/correlates flows, and ships OTLP/stdout logs through a byte/count-bounded queue.
- The audit found six P1 data/delivery correctness gaps, three narrower parser/admission gaps, four operational follow-ups left by closed issues, six evidence-backed event-family opportunities, and two design spikes.
- No IPFIX receiver, exporter-managed syslog target, embedded SSH, or arbitrary structured-data promotion is justified.

The audit baseline was clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4). Read every child issue in full, including later comments, before changing code: the child acceptance criteria and comments are binding and may supersede this summary.

## Binding decisions

- Keep OPNsense target configuration manual. The exporter must not mutate firewall logging configuration or infer its externally reachable address.
- Keep the queue bounded by records and bytes and all pressure/loss counted. Any disk spool remains opt-in, bounded, permission-hardened, and honest about at-least-once behavior.
- Event time, first-observed time, queue admission, successful export time, and retry time are different clocks.
- Never add addresses, ports, SIDs, MACs, hostnames, usernames, arbitrary programs, sequence values, or arbitrary RFC5424 SDATA as Prometheus/resource labels.
- Preserve expiry-only flow correlation and Zenarmor-as-enrichment. Do not use NetFlow `source_id=0` as a sequence-loss signal.
- Sequence-gap, CARP/gateway, VPN, FreeRADIUS, and miniupnpd parsing are capture/research-gated where their child says so. Redaction happens before raw fallback and debug capture.
- One file owner for the generic record, queue, OTLP sink, metrics registry, and pipeline wiring seams.

## Child worklist

- [x] #391 — fix(flow): preserve flow-close event time on per-flow log records (`P1`)
- [x] #392 — fix(logship): make OTLP delivery outcomes resource- and protocol-aware (`P1`)
- [x] #393 — fix(logship): keep derived-metric observation off receiver read goroutines (`P1`)
- [x] #394 — fix(logship): make log freshness timestamps stage-correct (`P1`)
- [x] #395 — fix(logship): give every self-metric stable instance identity (`P1`)
- [x] #396 — fix(syslog): derive DHCP metrics for dnsmasq-dhcp (`P1`)
- [x] #397 — fix(syslog): preserve malformed RFC5424 structured data through raw fallback (`P2`)
- [x] #398 — fix(syslog): make TCP oversize handling framing-independent (`P2`)
- [x] #399 — fix(syslog): count connection-limit and TLS-handshake rejections (`P2`)
- [x] #400 — fix(grafana): reconcile log-shipping alerts, panels, and docs with delivery semantics (`P2`)
- [x] #401 — refactor(syslog): make the ProgramProcessor registry rebuild-safe (`P3`)
- [x] #402 — feat(flow): alert when a configured NetFlow hook is conclusively dead (`P1`)
- [x] #403 — research(flow): measure VLAN hold sizing and subnet-evidence relabel value (`P2`)
- [x] #404 — research(syslog): validate RFC5424 sequence semantics and bounded gap telemetry (`P2`)
- [x] #405 — feat(syslog): derive CARP demotion and gateway transition events (`P1`)
- [x] #406 — feat(syslog): normalize IPsec and OpenVPN lifecycle events (`P2`)
- [x] #407 — feat(syslog): parse FreeRADIUS events with mandatory credential redaction (`P2`)
- [x] #408 — spike(telemetry): link derived metrics to retained log events with exemplars (`P2`)
- [x] #409 — feat(syslog): parse miniupnpd mapping and error events (`P3`)
- [x] #410 — spike(logship): evaluate a bounded disk spool for sink outages and restarts (`P3`)
- [x] #411 — feat(flow): add start, end, and duration fields to per-flow logs (`P3`)

- [x] #465 — fix(flow): attribute VLAN child flows by subnet evidence instead of arrival order (`P2`, filed from #403's measurement)

## Implementation waves

1. Freeze delivery and time semantics, then land #391, #392, #393, #394, and #395.
2. Fix bounded parser/admission defects: #396, #397, #398, #399, and registry lifecycle #401.
3. Wire honest operational coverage in #400 and #402; finish the VLAN evidence pass in #403.
4. Run capture-gated event-family lanes in parallel only after the record/identity seams are stable: #404, #405, #406, #407, and #409.
5. Evaluate additive value/durability work last: #408, #410, and #411. No-go conclusions are acceptable with evidence.

## Cross-epic dependencies

- #395 provides instance identity for the self-observability and companion-dashboard epics.
- #405 provides CARP/gateway event inputs for annotation work in #421.

## Coding-agent launch prompt

Deliver the retained scope in this epic. Start by reading this epic and every open child issue in full, including all comments. Reconfirm each premise against current `main`; if a premise is already fixed or disproven, record the evidence on that issue and close or rescope it instead of forcing a change.

Before parallel work, freeze every shared seam named above: exact metric names and types, labels and closed vocabularies, config keys/defaults, generated artifact ownership, and compatibility behavior. Use one file owner per lane. Keep integration/composition files in one lane or one wiring pass.

For each implementation issue, use strict TDD: add the smallest failing regression test, observe the correct failure, implement the minimum fix, then refactor. Keep the issue body/checklist current and post meaningful progress comments with commit SHAs. Completing commits must include `Closes #N` and land by direct push to `main` under the repository workflow.

At every wiring checkpoint and before claiming completion, run the full gate: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`. Run targeted race, parser, integration, live-canary, release, or Grafana checks required by each child. Generated files must be regenerated from source; do not hand-edit generated JSON or docs.

For live Grafana or OPNsense validation, keep production read-only unless a child explicitly defines a controlled testbed write. A successful local test, API response, or GitHub create call is not delivery proof: use scoped read-back, exact CI/release receipts, and live query/visual evidence where required.

## Epic completion bar

A record can be traced from receiver observation through bounded queue and classified OTLP outcome with honest counters/timestamps; proven parser/event additions are redacted and low-cardinality; dashboards/alerts distinguish pressure, retry, loss, and staleness.

- Every retained child is closed by its completing commit or explicitly descoped with a durable rationale.
- The epic checklist and phase comments reconstruct what landed, which SHAs delivered it, what was rejected, and what remains.
- The full gate is green on the final integrated `main`, with exact remote CI/release/live receipts for affected surfaces.

ncoming execution run — binding decisions (2026-07-25)

Owner decisions taken before implementation. These are binding and supersede any softer wording in the child bodies.

## 1. Compatibility policy: remove, do not deprecate

`#394` asks for an explicit compatibility decision on `opnsense_exporter_logs_last_event_timestamp_seconds`. **Decision: remove it outright** and replace with the two stage-correct gauges (`..._logs_last_received_timestamp_seconds`, `..._logs_last_exported_timestamp_seconds`). No alias, no deprecation window.

Rationale: the run already contains `feat`/breaking commits, so release-please will cut a major regardless. Carrying a deprecated ambiguous gauge through that boundary buys nothing and leaves the dashboards ambiguous for another cycle. Same policy applies to the `#439` surfaces in the sibling epic.

Requirement: every removal gets a `docs/upgrading.md` entry and a `!`-marked conventional commit.

## 2. Capture-gated lanes: captures will be taken, not inferred

`#404`, `#405`, `#406`, `#407`, `#409` stay capture-gated as written. Captures will be taken from the live OPNsense box, the devel testbed VM, the Debian dev VM, and an LXC container on `<host-8>` as each format requires. Plugins may be installed on the **devel testbed only** to generate real lines (this is the controlled-testbed write the epic permits); production stays read-only.

**Explicitly parked:** standing up a second OPNsense devel box to produce a real CARP HA pair. Consequence for `#405`: the dpinger gateway alarm/recovery half is in scope and will ship from real captures; any event class that can only be produced by a genuine MASTER/BACKUP transition between two nodes is deferred with that reason recorded on the issue rather than modelled from documentation. Per the repo canary-triage rule, a fixture must never encode a shape upstream cannot produce — and a shape we have not observed is not a shape we may invent.

## 3. Spikes

`#408` (exemplars) and `#410` (disk spool) run as spikes with evidence. A documented no-go closes them; neither will be implemented speculatively.

## 4. Lane discipline

`#392`, `#394`, `#395` all touch `internal/logship/pipeline.go`, and `#392`/`#394` both touch `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go`. They are therefore a **single serialized lane**, not three parallel ones — order `#395` → `#394` → `#392`. `#391`/`#411` (flowlog bridge) and the syslog receiver/registry work run in parallel lanes with disjoint file ownership.

Correction for implementers: the `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:182-188` citation in `#394` and `#395` has drifted; the `opnsense-logship-cursor-stalled` rule now lives near line 315. Locate by rule name, not line number.

remise revalidation complete — all 21 children still valid on `main` @ `58a51e5`

Every child was re-audited against current `main` rather than the `52ef4b2` baseline. Ten commits landed in between; **none of them touched the flow, logship, syslog, or grafana-alerts code these issues describe.** No child was already fixed, no premise was disproven, nothing needed rescoping. Line numbers drifted where files grew; corrections below.

## Line-reference corrections implementers must use

- **#394 and #395 both cite `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:182-188`. That has drifted to ~line 315.** Locate the `opnsense-logship-cursor-stalled` rule by name, not by line. Content is unchanged — still `max by (source)`, still built on the ambiguous gauge.
- #392: `Emit` is now 188-235, the `touched` map at 190, `errors.Join` at 234. `shipBatch` is 331-369.
- #393: `observeDerived` is called synchronously at `syslog/source.go:265`; `serveUDP` calls the handler inline at `listener.go:305`; `logevents.go:305-320` copies all seven family maps under the single mutex.
- #396: `derive.go:42-60` has five DHCP entries (`dhcpd`, `dnsmasq`, `kea-dhcp4`, `kea-dhcp6`, `dhcrelay`). `dnsmasq-dhcp` is confirmed absent while being registered as a parser alias at `dhcp.go:35` and mapped to subsystem `dhcp` at `registry.go:68`.
- #399: the four uncounted sites are `listener.go:333-341` (TCP cap), `:381-389` (TLS cap), `:433-436` (handshake), `:419`/`:439` (deadline setup/clear).
- #400: the sink-error alert is at `build_rules.py:293-299`, queue-near-capacity at `:300-305`. Panels: queue depth `tabs/logs.py:42-50`, sink errors `:52-58`, parse stages `:92-102`.
- #402: the four-clause detector is published verbatim at `docs/flow.md:361-373` and baked into `grafana/dashboard.json:46319`. Copy it from there.
- #442: `internal/webui/status.go` grew 318 lines in the telemetry work — `parseAPIStats` is now at `:482-491`, not `:248-258`. It still reduces every 401/403 to one `AuthOK bool`.
- #411: the attribute list to extend is `internal/flow/logemit.go:21-118` (`Record.LogAttributes()`), not `flowlog.go` — the bridge just forwards it.

## Three findings that change implementation approach

**#392 — the vendored OTLP exporter cannot be introspected.** Both `otlploghttp/internal/partialsuccess.go` and `otlploggrpc/internal/partialsuccess.go` sit under `internal/`, so they are unimportable from `internal/logship`. `otlploghttp/client.go:353`'s `retryableError` is unexported. Both `Exporter.Export()` return a bare `error`. Since the issue forbids matching vendor error text, the fix needs a transport-level seam — a `RoundTripper`/gRPC interceptor that reads the raw response before the SDK swallows it. That is a design decision, not a mechanical fix, and it is being resolved before code is written rather than guessed at.

**#398 is two bugs, not one.** (a) `framing.go:109-119` `scanNewline` has no length check at all, so an over-64KiB newline frame produces `bufio.ErrTooLong`, which `listener.go:507-511` merely debug-logs before closing the connection — no `oversized` rejection is counted and the next valid frame is lost. (b) Separately, `listener.go:470` sizes the scanner buffer at exactly `maxMessageBytes` with **zero headroom** for the delimiter or octet-count prefix, so a nominally legal 64 KiB frame can also fail. Both need the `cap-1`/`cap`/`cap+1` boundary tests across LF, CRLF and octet-counted framing.

**#400 is worse than written.** `logs_queue_bytes`, `logs_queue_max_bytes` and `logs_resource_capped_total` are not merely under-documented in `docs/log-shipping.md` — they are absent from it entirely. And the parse-stage panel copy at `tabs/logs.py:92-102` describes a `filterlog` stage that no source has ever emitted: syslog's actual `ParseStages` is `["envelope"]` and Zenarmor's is `["bulk","document"]`. There is no `ParseError("filterlog")` call site anywhere in the codebase.

## Sequencing consequence

#400 explicitly asks to be sequenced last so the same prose and queries are not rewritten twice. It is therefore not a parallel lane — it runs after the metric renames, instance labelling, and new reject reasons have all landed, and consumes their outputs.

un interrupted by a rate limit — recovery state (2026-07-25)

Seven implementation lanes were killed mid-edit by a weekly API limit. **No work was lost.** The tree was left with uncommitted changes from every lane; nothing was reverted, and `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` passes. Recording the exact resume state here so it survives a context loss.

## Landed and verified green

- **#396** — `dnsmasq-dhcp` added to the derived-family map, plus a new contract test (`TestEveryParserProgramHasAFamilyDecision`) enumerating every registered parser alias against `programFamily` and an explicit `nonDerivedPrograms` allowlist (`cron`, `/usr/sbin/cron`, `radvd`, `unbound`). End-to-end coverage proves a real `DHCPACK`/`DHCPREQUEST` now increments the counter with the right labels. The guard was itself verified by removing the new entry and watching it fail.
- **#401** — the panicking package-global `programProcessor` is now an `RWMutex`-guarded slot; `RegisterProgramProcessor` replaces instead of panicking, and a new `ResetProgramProcessor()` gives tests a real lifecycle instead of poking an unexported var. **The exported signatures did not change**, so `source.go` and `zenarmor/source.go` needed no edits — the cross-lane risk here did not materialise. Concurrency covered by a 16-goroutine × 200-iteration race test.
- **#441** — CODEOWNERS repointed to `@rknightion` (verified `admin` via the API; `ihatemodels` re-confirmed `read`, which is why the old rule assigned nobody). Markdown issue templates converted to forms with secret-pasting warnings; the PR template now names the real generated path and forbids hand-edits between docgen markers; the contributor gate now lists all five `ci-success` jobs. New `repo-meta.yml` validates template schema and CODEOWNERS syntax, with a regression guard that fails if `ihatemodels` ever reappears.
- **#439** — flag, inert counter and header plumbing removed; `internal/options`, `internal/server` and `internal/collector` all pass.
- **#436 — P0 verified fixed by direct execution.** With `.tools/go-licenses` deleted to defeat the cache, `make notices` now installs the correct `github.com/google/go-licenses/v2` path and writes notices for **64 modules**. The Dockerfile now has **no** `GO_LICENSES_VERSION` default and hard-fails without the build-arg, so the two paths can no longer diverge silently; CI resolves both values from the Makefile via `make -s print-go-licenses-version` / `print-go-licenses-module` and exercises the install from a clean Docker layer.

## Resumed, in flight

- **#395 / #394 complete.** `logs_last_event_timestamp_seconds` is gone, replaced by `logs_last_received_timestamp_seconds{source}` (admission, exporter clock) and `logs_last_exported_timestamp_seconds{source}` (acknowledged delivery). Every `opnsense_exporter_logs_*` series now carries `opnsense_instance` through a single wrapped registerer (`instanceLabelName`, `selfMetricsRegisterer`). `enqueue` now returns `(time.Time, bool)`.
- **#392 not started** — `Sink.Emit` still returns a bare `error`. Resumed with an explicit instruction to settle the transport seam before writing code, and to escalate rather than guess if no injection point exists.
- **#391 / #411 substantively done.** A stdout record confirms both: the log timestamp equals the flow close time, and `flow.start_time` / `flow.end_time` / `flow.duration_ms` are present. One test still asserts the deleted gauge name — expected cross-lane churn, being repointed at the correct new stage gauge.

No capture was synthesized and production OPNsense remained read-only. The epic stays open on #403–#407 and #409, all now blocked on explicit controlled-lab/capture authority rather than local implementation.

## Capture phase started

All locally executable and spike children are closed. The remaining open children are #403–#407 and #409.

- #403: seven-day real NetFlow window started with a 50 GiB application cap, 200 GiB free-space floor, and automatic baseline restoration.

## Clean-pause checkpoint — capture phase

Work paused at a verified baseline after all active lanes completed.

Delivered since the prior checkpoint:

- [`8ef49ed`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/8ef49ed847aa20bfecf47c1b0c1f838b61bc3b42) implements the captured #405 dpinger alarm/clear half: bounded transition counters, dashboard state/event correlation, and repeated-flap alerting. #405 stays open for genuine CARP transitions.
- #406 captured real development IPsec behavior: establish/terminate, wrong-PSK authentication failure, DPD/retransmit-driven SA disappearance, and recovery without disturbing the existing tunnel. Exact sanitized IPsec message templates were not retained before private teardown, so parser implementation remains gated on a short repeat capture. A dedicated OpenVPN setup never reached a valid session; it was stopped and completely removed. No OpenVPN grammar was inferred.

Long #403 capture remains intentionally active on <host-1>:

Verification/delivery for `8ef49ed`:

Testbed cleanup was independently read back: CT406 absent; no #406/#407 config markers, temporary listeners/processes/generated configs/PF rules/syslog targets, or scratch objects; syslog syntax valid with two processes. VM110 remained healthy. Repository `main` is clean and local/remote both equal `8ef49ed847aa20bfecf47c1b0c1f838b61bc3b42`.

Remaining epic children: #403, #405, #406, #407, and #409. No capture was fabricated and production OPNsense remained read-only.

## Capture-family checkpoint: #407 delivered

#407 is complete in [`18b4b90`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f): capture-backed FreeRADIUS access outcomes, a pre-generic fail-closed confidentiality boundary, bounded derived metrics, docs, and dashboard coverage.
