## Capture-family resumption checkpoint

Current `main` and `origin/main` remain `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`; the worktree is clean and the exact-SHA workflow set remains green.

Remaining children:

- #403: bounded read-only guard check is healthy. The systemd timer is active, capture uses 159,196,531 bytes, and available space is 1,311,667,458,048 bytes. The child has the exact receipt; no agent monitor was started.
- #405: dpinger is complete. CARP remains blocked on the conflict between #449’s binding “second OPNsense devel box” parking decision and later #460. Rob owns the explicit supersession decision; no second VM was created.
- #406: remains evidence-backed blocked on stable-release OpenVPN lifecycle formats or an explicit scope decision. Development-only grammar will not be silently promoted into supported behavior.
- #409: the approved isolated IGD topology is live and discovery works, but the first real mapping request proved the approved RFC1918 external address cannot create mappings under os-upnp 1.9’s supported configuration surface. miniupnpd returned `501 Action Failed`; client and PF read-backs remained empty. Source review proves the plugin does not expose miniupnpd’s required `ext_allow_private_ipv4=yes` option and that a private external-IP override would also be rejected. Rob owns the decision whether to authorize one temporary generated-config injection for the isolated capture. No unsupported setting has been applied.

No parser, metric, dashboard, rule, release, production OPNsense, or second-VM state was changed at this checkpoint. #449 remains open while those explicit evidence/authority blockers are resolved.

## Epic #449 parked on explicit evidence/authority blockers

Every currently executable child is complete. The remaining open set and exact unblock owners are:

- #403 — autonomous seven-day capture guard; owner: the systemd guard until 2026-08-02, then the primary agent for pair-gap/hold/subnet analysis. Elapsed time alone is not acceptance.
- #405 — genuine CARP HA transitions; owner: Rob for the explicit #449/#460 supersession decision. No second OPNsense VM was provisioned.
- #406 — stable-release OpenVPN lifecycle grammar; owner: Rob for an explicit development-only scope decision, or future stable capture evidence. No development format is being silently promoted.
- #409 — successful miniupnpd lifecycle grammar; owner: Rob for authority to use the unsupported private-WAN daemon option, or an approved replacement topology/plugin version. The failed private-WAN capture is sanitized and durable; the entire testbed is now absent with exact read-backs.

#404 remains a permanent capture-backed no-go and will not be reopened. #407 remains delivered at `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f` with green exact-SHA workflows.

No temporary #406/#407/#409 object remains. The only intentionally active external state is #403 under its existing autonomous guard. In accordance with the epic sequencing rule, #449 stays open with only evidence-backed blocked children while work moves to #450. Blocked #449 children will be revisited after the remaining epic sequence or when Rob supplies the required decision.

## Final safe-pause reconciliation

The pause remains clean at `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`: local `main`, `origin/main`, and remote main are identical (`0/0` ahead/behind); `git status`, untracked-file status, and `git diff --check` are clean; all eight workflows for the exact SHA are terminal-success; and no child agent remains active.

The parent checklist matches live child state. The only open children have durable current dispositions:

- #403 — guarded long capture continues autonomously; analysis requires pair-gap percentiles/max, hold peak, and parent-subnet evidence.
- #405 — dpinger is delivered; CARP is owned by Rob pending explicit resolution of the #449/#460 second-VM authority conflict.
- #406 — development IPsec/OpenVPN evidence is complete and cleaned; blocked on stable sanitized grammar or Rob explicitly narrowing scope to captured development grammar.
- #409 — approved topology was fully removed; owned by Rob pending authority for the unsupported private-WAN guard injection or an approved supported replacement.

No independent #449 lane remains running and no temporary #406/#407/#409 state remains. #403 is the only intentional external process and stays under its systemd guard.

## Updated clean-pause baseline — 2026-07-26

No #449 state changed during #412. The repository's fully pushed green baseline is now `9470bf6568382e8636e30184a53d0ec28d90f317`; all eight exact-SHA workflows succeeded. #403 remains the sole intentional guarded background capture, and the existing #405/#406/#409 blockers and cleanup receipts remain authoritative. No testbed mutation occurred.

## Capture-family resumption — three of four blockers cleared without the escalations

Baseline reconciled at resumption: `main` = `origin/main` = `9470bf6568382e8636e30184a53d0ec28d90f317`, worktree clean, all eight exact-SHA workflows terminal-success. That is **two commits ahead of the pause receipt's stated `8ef49ed`** — `18b4b90` (#407) and `9470bf6` (#412) had landed. Corrected here so a successor does not resume from the stale SHA.

The owner was shown the three genuine decisions and answered all three. Two of the resulting blockers then dissolved under read-only investigation, and no second VM, no unsupported config injection, and no repeat capture were needed.

### #405 — CARP unblocked by retained-log evidence; the authorized VM build is NOT needed

The owner authorized building the second OPNsense VM per #460. Investigation before provisioning found the evidence already existed: **44 real kernel CARP records in the development box's retained logs, covering all three states** — `INIT -> BACKUP` (10), `BACKUP -> MASTER` (10), `MASTER -> INIT` (2) — plus 22 demotion records carrying a signed delta and cause. `net.inet.carp.log=1` is the FreeBSD default, so this needs no configuration at all. Newest record 2026-07-26T20:45:31+01:00 on the current release, so it is current-generation evidence.

**No VM was created.** #460 remains open on its own terms: it covers *API payload* coverage (the five `hasync` metrics, a real `BACKUP` peer, `remote_version_match=0`, the unfalsifiable `hasyncVersion` exemption) which is unreachable from syslog and out of scope for this epic. Full grammar, the frozen metric contract, and one load-bearing parser detail (the kernel prefix `<6>[754]` precedes `carp:`, so a regex anchored on `carp:` will not match) are recorded on #405.

### #406 — narrowed to captured development grammar by owner decision

**The pause receipt was stale on this child.** It said the IPsec templates were destroyed before preservation and a repeat capture was required. The newest child comments (2026-07-26 18:33Z and 18:54Z) record that the repeat IPsec capture *and* a full OpenVPN capture both completed with verified sanitized templates retained. Both bundles were retrieved and verified against their recorded digests: IPsec `ff3de8f23876f67c4f182f7aec933d1608dcc8a1997dbd3591a0e378e3324c6d`, OpenVPN `ea915378429a23aafc036f35df794ef10a0454da229c1f08ec976c54eaaf460e`.

The owner narrowed scope to exactly the captured development grammar with unmatched and version-new lines shipping generically — matching the precedent `8ef49ed` already set for dpinger. **Provenance correction applied:** the OpenVPN bundle labels itself "OpenVPN 2.6.14"; that was the Debian *client*. `pkg info openvpn` on the box returns **2.7.5**, and every retained template is a server-side line. Fixtures state 2.7.5.

### #409 — unblocked by production evidence; both escalations withdrawn

The owner confirmed production runs miniupnpd and authorized inspecting it. Read-only scan found **1,598 real records over five days**, including **61 genuine mapping-expiry events** — materially better than the errors-only outcome this epic had settled for. Production runs `enable_pcp_pmp=yes` with `enable_upnp=no`, i.e. NAT-PMP/PCP with IGD disabled, which inverts the earlier plan's assumption that IGD was the thing to capture.

The two escalations — authority for the unsupported `ext_allow_private_ipv4=yes` injection, and reversing the approved design's external-IP-override restriction — are **both unnecessary and withdrawn**. Neither was ever applied. Full grammar census and frozen contract are on #409.

### #403 — analysis underway

The guarded capture is healthy and untouched: timer active, capture 594,513,615 bytes against the 50 GiB cap, `/opt` free 1,310,291,177,472 bytes against the 200 GiB floor, exact Compose backup present, container running, deadline 2026-08-02T15:20:15Z intact. No agent monitor was started; the systemd guard remains the sole continuous monitor.

The capture and its private topology snapshot (SHA-256 `98a1ec5f…`, unchanged from the recorded value) were copied to temporary local storage for offline analysis, which is running now against the real `Repairer` rather than a model. Acceptance remains pair-gap p50/p95/p99/max, observed hold peak, and the subnet-evidence-without-child-copy count. Elapsed time alone is still not acceptance.

### Implementation sequencing

#405, #406 and #409 all add a derived syslog family, so they all touch `registry.go`, `derive.go`, `logmetrics.go` and `logevents.go`. They are **one serialized lane, not three** — order #406, then #405, then #409. #406 is in flight.

### An incident, disclosed

A long `guest-exec` payload wedged the development box's QEMU guest agent (several `php -r` calls with `config.inc` exceeded the agent timeout). VM102 itself never stopped — `qm status` running, 4d20h uptime, and its API answered HTTP 200 throughout over the tailnet. Recovered by restarting the `qemu-ga` service through the supported API; `qm agent 102 ping` returns PING-OK. No configuration, service, or CARP state was altered. Keep guest-exec payloads short; `php -r` with `config.inc` is slow enough to blow the timeout on its own.

## Phase receipt — capture family complete except #409, which is unblocked and specified

Baseline correction first, because the pause receipt this run resumed from was stale: `main` was **`9470bf6`**, not `8ef49ed`. `18b4b90` (#407) and `9470bf6` (#412) had already landed.

### Closed this run

| child | how |
| --- | --- |
| **#403** | Measured, closed. Capture stopped early, baseline restored byte-identical, apparatus torn down by exact identity, private capture destroyed on <host-1> and locally. Follow-on **#465** filed with measured thresholds. |
| **#405** | `f0f1a26`. CARP state and demotion events, from retained-log evidence. **No second VM built.** |
| **#406** | `3c51776`. IPsec and OpenVPN lifecycle from the captured development grammar. |

### Three blockers dissolved rather than being escalated

The owner answered three decisions. Two of the resulting authorizations then turned out to be unnecessary:

- **#405 did not need the #460 VM.** 44 real kernel CARP records already existed in the development box's retained logs, covering all three states, because `net.inet.carp.log` defaults to `1`. The authorization was granted and deliberately not used. **#460 remains valid for API-payload coverage**, which is unreachable from syslog.
- **#409 needed no configuration change.** Production runs miniupnpd, and read-only inspection yielded **1,598 records over five days including 61 genuine mapping-expiry events** — better than the isolated IGD capture would have produced. Both escalations (unsupported `ext_allow_private_ipv4=yes` injection; reversing the external-IP-override restriction) are **withdrawn as unnecessary** and neither was ever applied.
- **#406's recorded state was stale.** The pause receipt said its IPsec templates were destroyed before preservation. The child's own newest comments record that the repeat IPsec capture *and* a full OpenVPN capture both completed with templates retained. Both bundles were retrieved and verified against their recorded digests before code was written, and a provenance error was corrected: the OpenVPN bundle self-labels "2.6.14", which was the Debian *client* — the server is verified 2.7.5 and every template is server-side.

### #409 — the only open implementation child

Unblocked, evidence complete, needs no further capture or authority. Queued only because it contends with #405/#406 on the same four files. Its comment above carries the frozen metric contract, all five grammars, the deliberate exclusions, the missing `subsystems` entry, and the step-by-step path through the seams #406 and #405 established. **A successor can implement it with no live access.**

Note the sentinel API changed under it: `b.sentinel()` is structured and keyword-only since `d55384c`, and the old positional form raises rather than degrading.

### #465 — new child from #403's measurement

#403 found a correctness defect, not just a measurement: `Repairer.admit()`'s mechanism C never consults `moreSpecific()`, so the first-admitted copy wins permanently. **29.2% of pairs exceed the 2-second hold window and all 108,678 of them were trunk-first**, so the misattribution is systematic rather than a coin flip. Subnet evidence agreed with the correct winner on **362,678 pairs with zero disagreements**, and 247,105 records have subnet evidence with no child copy at all — cases no hold window of any size can fix. Enlarging the window is ruled out quantitatively: peak hold occupancy was 2,115 of 10,000, and a p99-covering window projects past the cap, where the overflow path degrades straight back to first-seen-wins.

### External state

`/opt` on <host-1> recovered to ~1.28 TB. Exporter running, `/metrics` HTTP 200, debug-capture env back to `unidentified` / 256MiB / `/capture`. A filesystem sweep for `*issue403*` returns only unrelated Go compiler test files inside Docker layers. Production OPNsense was read-only throughout; reads were confined to `/var/log/miniupnpd/`, `/var/etc/miniupnpd.conf` and the plugin config node.

**One incident, disclosed.** A long `guest-exec` payload wedged the development box's QEMU guest agent — several `php -r` calls loading `config.inc` exceeded the agent timeout. VM102 never stopped and its API answered HTTP 200 throughout; recovered by restarting `qemu-ga` through the supported API, `qm agent 102 ping` now returns PING-OK. No configuration, service or CARP state was altered. Keep guest-exec payloads small.

### Epic status

Retained children are complete except **#409** (implementable now) and **#465** (new, from #403). This epic cannot close until both land, and neither is blocked on anything external.

## Programme pause pointer

The full clean-pause receipt for this run is recorded once on #450 rather than duplicated across four epics: https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/450#issuecomment-5091166487

It carries the verified repository state, the nine landed SHAs, the full green gate on `fd94cbd`, the exact-SHA Actions evidence (including the one commit whose two runs were cancelled by concurrency rather than passing), external-state cleanup receipts, and the open-work disposition across all four epics.

For this epic specifically, see the phase receipt immediately above: retained children are complete except **#409** — unblocked, evidence complete, and fully specified in its own comment so it can be implemented with no live access — and **#465**, newly filed from #403's measurement. Neither is blocked on anything external.

## #409 delivered — every original child of this epic is now closed

`6d812f8` closed #409, the last of the 21 children this epic was filed with (#391–#411). All eight workflows green on the exact SHA.

It was the one child recorded as blocked. It turned out not to need what its block was about: the two escalations parked on the owner — authority for an unsupported `ext_allow_private_ipv4=yes` generated-config injection, and reversing the approved design's external-IP-override restriction — were both withdrawn as unnecessary and neither was ever applied. Read-only inspection of production instead produced 1,598 real records over five days, including 61 genuine mapping-expiry events. Scope landed at **errors plus expiry**, which is better than the errors-only outcome the issue had settled for; a successful add and delete remain unknown and were not inferred. Full receipt on #409.

### What remains under this epic

**#465** — `fix(flow): attribute VLAN child flows by subnet evidence instead of arrival order` (`P2`), filed from #403's measurement rather than planned. Not started. It is the one substantive finding this epic produced that is still open: mechanism C of the VLAN repair stage never calls `moreSpecific`, so all 108,678 above-window pairs in the 18h35m capture — 29.2% of pairs — are systematically misattributed to the trunk. The measurement backing it is complete and on #403, so #465 needs no further capture.

Nothing else is outstanding, and no external state is left behind: the isolated testbed topology was torn down with absence read back by exact identity, the #403 private capture was destroyed on both hosts, and production was read-only throughout.

## Epic complete — closing

Every child of this epic is closed: all 21 it was filed with (#391–#411) plus #465, which was filed from #403's measurement rather than planned. Nothing is parked, blocked or awaiting a decision.

### The last two

**#409** (`6d812f8`) was the one child recorded as blocked, on authority for an unsupported generated-config injection. It turned out not to need it: read-only inspection of production produced 1,598 real records over five days, including 61 genuine mapping-expiry events, so both escalations were withdrawn as unnecessary and neither was ever applied. Scope landed at errors *plus* expiry, better than the errors-only outcome the issue had settled for.

**#465** (`1b203ee`) implemented #403's finding: mechanism C of the VLAN repair stage never called `moreSpecific()`, so all 108,678 above-window pairs — 29.2% of the 372,109 measured — were systematically misattributed to the trunk, every one of them trunk-first. Subnet evidence now resolves attribution on first sight, which removes the arrival-order dependency rather than improving the odds of beating it, and also reaches 247,105 records that had no second copy at all and could never have been attributed by timing. The 2-second hold stays for the 9,431 ambiguous cases, and what the stage still cannot correct is now counted rather than silent.

### What this epic changed, in one place

Loss and misattribution that were previously invisible are now either fixed or counted. The pattern repeated across children: a repair that looked correct because docs, catalogue and dashboard all agreed with each other, while nothing was checked against what the live backend actually held — the OTLP `_total` canonicalization (#418, #464), the Loki `service_instance_id` label (#413), and the VLAN attribution above. Each of those now has a guard that fails the build rather than a comment saying it should be fine.

### Deliberate residuals, so nobody re-litigates them

- **`opnsense_flow_vlan_late_child_copies_total`** is a residual by design. A record already emitted is through the rollup and shipped; re-emitting a better copy would double-count real bytes, which is worse than a misattribution because it is invisible in the totals. It is counted so it can be seen, not fixed.
- **No successful UPnP add or delete grammar** exists, on either the production box or the isolated testbed, and none was inferred. No attempt line is treated as proof of success.
- **No active-mapping gauge** for UPnP, and **no CARP stable-release evidence** — production has neither IGD enabled nor any CARP VIP.
- **No alert rule** for either the UPnP family or the VLAN residual: in one case the failure mode is the routine state on the only deployment with real clients, in the other no post-fix measurement exists to pick a threshold from. Both are recorded on their issues with the condition that would justify revisiting.

### External state

Nothing outstanding. The isolated testbed topology was torn down with absence read back by exact identity, the #403 private capture was destroyed on both hosts, and production was read-only throughout every child that touched it. No release was published and PR #358 was never merged or modified.

title: epic: make flow, syslog, and log shipping loss-aware

body:
## Mission

Make scheduler state, retained-data age, upstream reachability, optional OTLP delivery, and UI health truthful under concurrency and partial failure while preserving the one-firewall-per-process failure boundary.

## Audit baseline

- The poller uses volatility tiers, concurrency admission, error-aware last-good snapshots, pull metrics, optional OTLP push, and a web console.
- The audit found one profiling redirect regression, three scheduler/health correctness gaps, two configuration gaps, two optional-push visibility/latency opportunities, and one partial-gather UI gap.
- Current baseline tests, race-sensitive packages, build, lint, docs, and Grafana gates were green before issue creation.

The audit baseline was clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4). Read every child issue in full, including later comments, before changing code: the child acceptance criteria and comments are binding and may supersede this summary.

## Binding decisions

- Retain #336 last-good data on empty failure; expose its age honestly instead of dropping it.
- Keep attempt time, snapshot-content time, full-success time, and next scheduled deadline semantically distinct.
- Keep one exporter process per firewall. Do not broaden this epic into multi-firewall multiplexing.
- Optional OTLP failure must remain visible without taking down the pull exporter. Do not pretend construction/export failure is success.
- Do not add unauthenticated pprof or request-level distributed tracing without a separate demonstrated need and redaction policy.
- Health-check cadence and collector tiers need explicit defaults and fixed names; unknown override names must fail closed.

## Child worklist

- [x] #381 — security(profiling): restore Pyroscope redirect prohibition (`P1`)
- [x] #382 — feat(poller): expose retained snapshot age and tier-aware stale-data alerts (`P1`)
- [x] #383 — fix(scheduler): re-check reachability after poll-slot admission (`P1`)
- [x] #384 — fix(webui): include upstream reachability in top-level health (`P2`)
- [x] #385 — fix(scheduler): publish the actual next-poll deadline (`P2`)
- [x] #386 — feat(scheduler): separate health-check cadence from collector defaults (`P2`)
- [x] #387 — fix(config): reject unknown poll-interval override names (`P2`)
- [x] #388 — feat(telemetry): expose OTLP metric delivery health (`P2`)
- [x] #389 — fix(webui): record and mark non-empty partial gathers (`P2`)
- [x] #390 — feat(telemetry): add an optional fast-collector OTLP lane (`P2`)

## Implementation waves

1. Land the security/correctness regressions first: #381, #383, #384, #385, #387, and #389.
2. Freeze scheduler and freshness clocks across #382, #385, and #386; update console, metrics, dashboard, and alert semantics in one wiring pass.
3. Add optional-push observability in #388 before the fast lane in #390, so the new path cannot fail invisibly.

## Cross-epic dependencies

- #382 supplies snapshot-age semantics to the dedicated self-observability epic.
- #388 and #390 must coordinate with log-delivery outcome work in #392 without conflating metrics OTLP and logs OTLP.

Deliver the retained scope in this epic. Start by reading this epic and every open child issue in full, including all comments. Reconfirm each premise against current `main`; if a premise is already fixed or disproven, record the evidence on that issue and close or rescope it instead of forcing a change.

Before parallel work, freeze every shared seam named above: exact metric names and types, labels and closed vocabularies, config keys/defaults, generated artifact ownership, and compatibility behavior. Use one file owner per lane. Keep integration/composition files in one lane or one wiring pass.

## Wave 0: premises revalidated + seams frozen

Baseline for this run: `main` at `8098023` (the audit baseline `52ef4b2` is an ancestor; nothing since touched the audited code paths).

### Premise revalidation — all 10 children still stand

| Issue | Premise re-checked against current `main` | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| #381 | `internal/profiling/profiling.go:126-128` still builds `&http.Client{Timeout: timeout}` with no `CheckRedirect` | CONFIRMED |
| #382 | `snapshot.go:65-71` retains the buffer on `!ok && empty` but unconditionally sets `e.lastPoll = time.Now()`; `collector.go:1327-1330` exports that as last-poll | CONFIRMED |
| #383 | `scheduler.go:164-166` checks `unreachable` **before** the `pollSem` acquire at 167-171; no re-check after | CONFIRMED |
| #384 | `webui/status.go:104-132` `deriveHealth` takes only `[]CollectorStat`; nothing folds in reachability | CONFIRMED |
| #385 | `scheduler.go:126` fixed `time.NewTicker`, but `collector.go:1333` publishes `e.lastPoll.Add(interval)` | CONFIRMED |
| #386 | `scheduler.go:65` passes `c.pollGlobalInterval()` straight into `runHealthPoller` | CONFIRMED |
| #387 | `main.go:719-728` parses only the duration half; keys are never validated | CONFIRMED |
| #388 | `telemetry/provider.go` has no delivery accounting; `main.go:781` logs "enabled" before any network I/O | CONFIRMED |
| #389 | `metricsnap/recorder.go:42` records only on `err == nil`; `recorder_test.go:38-70` pins that as intended | CONFIRMED |
| #390 | `telemetry/provider.go:65-69` is a single `PeriodicReader` over all gatherers at one interval | CONFIRMED |

No child is stale or already-fixed; none is being descoped on premise grounds.

### Decisions taken (repo owner, this session)

1. **#382 clock model — TWO new clocks, not one.**

   | metric | meaning | success | partial+err | empty+err |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `opnsense_exporter_collector_last_poll_timestamp_seconds` (existing, unchanged) | last **attempt** completion | advances | advances | advances |
   | `opnsense_exporter_collector_snapshot_timestamp_seconds` (NEW) | stored buffer last **replaced** | advances | advances | retained |
   | `opnsense_exporter_collector_last_success_timestamp_seconds` (NEW) | last **fully clean** poll | advances | retained | retained |

   Rationale: one clock alone leaves a persistently-partial collector reading "fresh" forever and gives alerting no "has not fully succeeded since T" signal. Cost is ~124 extra series against a ~4.6k baseline (~2.7%), which is worth it. Both new gauges are absent until first set, rather than emitting a misleading 0.

2. **#385 schedule contract — FIXED CADENCE, publish the real deadline.** The `time.Ticker` stays; the scheduler records the actual next tick in shared state and both `collector_next_poll_timestamp_seconds` and the console read that single value. Completion-anchored timers were rejected: they would cut effective sample rate by the poll duration on every tier (a 20s poll on the 15s fast tier would silently become a 35s cadence).

3. **#388 OTLP construction failure — FATAL at startup.** Requesting `--otlp.enabled` and failing to construct the exporter now `os.Exit(1)`s, matching the existing fail-fast on malformed OTLP config. This does not weaken the epic's "optional OTLP failure must remain visible without taking down the pull exporter" decision: that governs *export* failure, which stays non-fatal and is now counted. There is therefore no configured-but-inactive state to model.

4. **#390 — BUILD IT, opt-in, default off**, landing after #388 per the epic's wave 3. Existing deployments stay byte-identical. It will be enabled and verified live on the <host-1> deployment before the epic closes.

### Frozen seams — binding on every lane

**Metrics** (`opnsense_exporter_*`, labels `{collector, instance}` for the per-collector ones, matching the existing poll series):
- `collector_snapshot_timestamp_seconds`, `collector_last_success_timestamp_seconds` — new gauges per the table above.
- `collector_next_poll_timestamp_seconds` — name unchanged, source changes to the real scheduler deadline.
- `otlp_exports_total{result="success"|"error"}` — counter, CLOSED two-value label set. Error text, endpoint, tenant and credentials never become labels.
- `otlp_last_success_timestamp_seconds`, `otlp_consecutive_failures`, `otlp_enabled` — unlabelled gauges.

**Go APIs:**
- `collector.HealthSnapshot() HealthSnapshot` — `{Polled, CheckOK, Unreachable, CheckedAt, LastError}`. Passive: no API call, no registry `Gather`. This is the seam #384 consumes and #386 keeps current.
- `metricsnap.Recorder.Capture() Capture` — `{Families, At, Partial, LastErrorAt, ErrorCount}`. `Snapshot()` retained verbatim. Records whenever `len(mfs) > 0` regardless of error; retains the previous capture only on a zero-family gather. No error strings stored.
- `telemetry.Start(...)` gains a `prometheus.Registerer` before `log`; nil disables delivery accounting.
- `collector.ValidatePollOverrideNames(...)` — #387's fail-closed check, run in `main.go` before duration parsing, accepting known-but-disabled collectors.

**File ownership:** `main.go`, `internal/options/`, docs and all cross-package wiring are done in a single wiring pass, never in parallel. One package = one owner for the rest.

## Epic complete — all 10 children landed

Two commits, both direct-pushed to `main`:

| SHA | Closes | What |
|---|---|---|
| [`f159ad3`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/f159ad3) | #381, #383, #385, #386, #387 | Profiling redirect prohibition; post-admission reachability re-check; real next-poll deadline; independent health cadence; fail-closed override names |
| [`58a51e5`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/58a51e5) | #382, #384, #388, #389, #390 | Retained-data age + tier-aware alerts; upstream reachability in the health badge; OTLP delivery health; partial-gather capture; optional fast OTLP lane |

Nothing was descoped. Every premise was revalidated against current `main` before implementation and all ten still stood — the table is in the [wave-0 comment](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/448#issuecomment-5080215661).

### Completion bar

> The console, self metrics, scheduler, and alerts agree on attempt, success, content age, reachability, partial results, and next-run state.

- **attempt / content / success** — three distinct clocks written in exactly one place (`snapshotStore.put`, which already owns the retain/replace decision). Exported as `collector_last_poll_`, `collector_snapshot_` and `collector_last_success_timestamp_seconds`; the console reads the same values via the `StatusTracker`, not by re-deriving them; Grafana panels and the three new staleness rules read the same gauges.
- **next-run** — one value, the scheduler's actual fixed-cadence deadline, published to both the metric and the console. Cleared when a poller stops, so nothing ages into a permanent false "due".
- **reachability** — one passive `HealthSnapshot`, precedence over collector history, transport-unreachable distinguished from reachable-but-erroring.
- **partial results** — the recorder now mirrors what the real serving paths receive, and the console says "partial" instead of quietly showing old data.
- **optional OTLP paths have bounded, testable failure semantics** — construction failure is fatal; export failure is counted, logged and non-fatal; both lanes shut down under the existing bounded contract; and the "an exporter cannot ship its own failure through the failing path" limitation is documented rather than papered over.

### Decisions taken (all recorded on the child issues)

1. **Two data clocks, not one** — a single clock leaves a persistently-partial collector reading fresh forever.
2. **Fixed cadence, publish the real deadline** — completion-anchored timers would have cut effective sample rate by the poll duration on every tier.
3. **OTLP construction failure is fatal** — export failure stays non-fatal, so the pull exporter is never taken down by a flaky backend.
4. **`OPNsenseEndpointErrors` supplemented, not replaced** — it is the only rule carrying the `endpoint` label, and widening its window would reintroduce the #94 fire-after-recovery defect.

### Notable finding beyond the audit

Splitting the OTLP export gather also splits the gather feeding the operator console, which would have silently under-reported its family/series and cardinality figures by the whole fast tier (~7%). Rather than ship that, `metricsnap` captures are now lane-keyed and merged, reporting the **oldest** contributing lane's time. Caught while wiring #390; recorded on #389 and #390.

### Gate on the final integrated `main` (58a51e5)

```
go test ./... -count=1 -race     ok (22 packages)
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...     ok
golangci-lint run ./...          0 issues
make docs-check                  check passed — all generated docs current (829 metrics)
make grafana-check               25 tests OK; coverage 829/829 (726 panels); 51 manifests validated
```

`make grafana-check` could only pass post-commit — its final step is `git diff --exit-code`, which compares the worktree against the index, so it necessarily reported the (intended) uncommitted changes until they landed. Confirmed green against the pushed tree.

Alert behaviour was proved rather than asserted: `promtool test rules` over 11 scenarios (cold-tier persistent silent at 45m / firing at 55m, slow-tier silent at 15m / firing at 25m, single-failure-then-recovery silent throughout, and `OPNsenseEndpointErrors` still firing on sustained fast/medium errors and still not firing after a stopped burst — the #94 guard), backed by 11 new Python unit tests since promtool is not in CI.

### Outstanding — one item, and it needs a human

**#390's live verification on <host-1> has NOT been done.** The code will reach the box on its own (watchtower pulls `:main` hourly), but `--otlp.fast-export-interval` is still unset in `/opt/opnsense-exporter/docker-compose.yml`, so the fast lane is off in production and the two-lane split is unproven outside tests. Suggested config: keep `--otlp.export-interval=60s`, add `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_OTLP_FAST_EXPORT_INTERVAL: 15s`, then confirm fast-tier series arrive at 15s, cold series at 60s, and nothing is double-counted at the backend.

Also worth knowing: the **Grafana dashboard does not self-update**. `grafana/dashboard.json` and the four new alert manifests are regenerated and committed, but they still need pushing to `gc-gitsync-m7kni` / `gcx resources push` by hand.

### Pre-existing issue noticed, deliberately not fixed

`internal/telemetry/provider.go`'s early-return path on synthetic-`up`-gatherer failure leaks the constructed exporter. It predates this epic and construction failure is now fatal (so the process exits anyway), but it is real and worth a follow-up if that path ever becomes non-fatal.

## CI receipts — and one self-inflicted red on the intermediate commit

| commit | `ci-success` | note |
|---|---|---|
| `f159ad3` | **failure** | `Grafana artifacts up-to-date: failure` — every other job passed |
| `58a51e5` (head) | **success** | Tests & Linters, Race detector, Generated docs, Grafana artifacts, docker-build-verify, Coverage — all green |

**What went wrong, plainly:** `f159ad3` added `collector_snapshot_timestamp_seconds` and `collector_last_success_timestamp_seconds` to the docgen catalogue, and the Grafana coverage gate fails the build if any catalogue metric is not on a panel. The panels were still being written in a parallel lane at that moment, so I pushed a commit that could not pass its own gate. `main` was red for roughly 20 minutes until `58a51e5` landed the panels.

The gate did exactly its job — this is the coverage rule working as designed, catching a metric shipped without a dashboard. The sequencing was mine: a new catalogue metric and its panel have to land in the same commit, so splitting the epic into "code now, Grafana later" was the wrong cut. Worth remembering for the next multi-lane run in this repo.

No action outstanding from it: head is green and the two commits together are self-consistent.

Also confirmed green on head: `CodeQL`, `actionlint`, `zizmor`, `Docker Security`, `Scorecard`, `Trigger Documentation Sync`, and `Release Please`.

All ten children are closed by f159ad3 and 58a51e5, the epic checklist is fully ticked, and the full gate is green on the final integrated \`main\` with CI receipts recorded above.

Closing the epic. Two follow-ups are captured in the completion comment and are NOT blockers on this work: the fast OTLP lane (#390) is shipped but still switched off in production and wants a live check on <host-1>, and the regenerated Grafana dashboard/alert manifests still need pushing to the Grafana stack by hand.

## Wave 0: premise revalidation, frozen seams, and two corrections to the child issues

Revalidated all eight child premises against `main` at `52ef4b2` on 2026-07-25. **All eight still hold** — nothing was already fixed, nothing was disproven. Live evidence was captured from the dev box (`opnsense-devel`, OPNsense **26.7.r_35**, development channel) rather than inferred from GitHub master.

### Live evidence captured

`api/core/firmware/status` on the dev box serves 26 top-level keys, including every field #373 and #380 depend on:

| field | live value | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `connection` | `ok` | #373 confirmed present |
| `repository` | `ok` | #373 confirmed present |
| `download_size` | `37MiB` | **#380 is not capture-blocked** |
| `remove_packages` | `[]` (empty) | count reads 0; inner shape is source-derived |
| `upgrade_sets` | `[]` (empty) | count reads 0; inner shape is source-derived |

`api/diagnostics/traffic/interface` reports both #375 fields as populated numeric strings across all five interfaces, with genuine non-zero values (unknown-protocol up to `13852362`) and boot-attached markers of `1` versus `18` for the VLAN children — so both metrics have real live signal, and a genuine `"0"` occurs in practice.

### Correction 1 — #373's state vocabularies were incomplete

The issue lists connection states as `ok/unresolved/misconfigured/unauthenticated` and repository states as `ok/untrusted/revoked/unsigned/forbidden/incomplete`. **Both omit `error`**, which is the initial value each variable is assigned (`check.sh:54` and `check.sh:66`) and which persists when a failure matches none of the specific classifiers. The installed 26.7 `/usr/local/opnsense/scripts/firmware/check.sh` states the full closed sets in a header comment at lines 30-31:

- connection: `error`, `unauthenticated`, `misconfigured`, `unresolved`, `ok`
- repository: `error`, `untrusted`, `unsigned`, `revoked`, `incomplete`, `forbidden`, `ok`

The installed script is stronger evidence than GitHub master for what the supported releases actually serve, so the implementation uses these lists. Omitting `error` would have collapsed the most likely real-world failure state to `unknown`.

### Correction 2 — #378's "use the same error semantics as adjacent FRR decoders" is void

That instruction cannot be followed as written: **every** decoder in `opnsense/frr.go` swallows its second-stage decode error and returns `data, nil`, treating corruption as a disabled daemon — BFD at ~414 and ~456, BGP at ~583, OSPFv3 at ~805, database at ~1120. There is no error-surfacing pattern in the file to mirror. The fix therefore implements the issue's explicit acceptance criteria instead, and stays narrow: the OSPF overview decode is already guarded by `Response[0] != '['`, so a decode failure there is genuine corruption rather than a disabled daemon, and returns a contextual `APICallError` without setting `Present=true`. The `[`-array disabled path and empty payloads keep current behaviour exactly.

The four sibling swallowing sites are left alone deliberately — widening the fix was not in scope. They are a candidate follow-up issue.

### Decisions taken

- **#380 is in scope for this epic, not deferred.** Its premise was "capture the wire format first"; the format is now captured live. The parser is frozen against the installed 26.7 `FirmwareController.php:126-161`: comma-separated list, summed; unit is the first alphabetic character, `k`/`m`/`g`/`t`/`p` as powers of 1024, no letter means bytes. **We accept decimals; upstream's own regex is `(\d+)` and truncates the fraction.** We do not replicate that bug, so our value can exceed the GUI's displayed number — documented in the help text. Gating: no stored check emits nothing; a stored check with an empty field emits `0` (upstream leaves it empty when there is nothing to download, which is unambiguous); any unparseable item emits nothing at all rather than a fabricated `0`.
- **#379 is unblocked further than the issue assumed and is being tested live.** The dev box packaged `netbird-0.72.2` (not the 0.74.4 the issue asserted), `sessionExpiresAt` is absent from the live payload, and the box was unenrolled (`management.connected=false`, `peers.total=0`). Rob confirms 0.74.4 is available on the devel box and supplied an enrollment key, so the box is being enrolled and upgraded to 0.74.4 to test whether the field appears. Verdict deferred to that result rather than assumed. Note the `sessionExpiresAt` entry currently in `exemptions.json` under `netbirdStatus.knownExtraTopKeys` is **prospective, not observed** — the box does not serve it.
- **#377 gets real testbed provisioning, not just named blockers.** A second OPNsense VM is being built to establish genuine OSPF/OSPFv3 adjacency, Kea DHCPv6 prefix delegation is being configured on the existing box, and NetBird enrollment is in progress. Paths that still cannot be reached become named blockers with prune triggers, never an anonymous count.
- **Grafana artefacts land in-repo only.** Panels and rules are authored, regenerated and committed; the push to `gc-gitsync-m7kni` and `gcx resources push` stays a manual step.

### Frozen metric contract

| issue | metric | type | labels |
|---|---|---|---|
| #373 | `opnsense_firmware_update_check_success` | Gauge | — |
| #373 | `opnsense_firmware_update_check_state` | Gauge (=1) | `component`, `state` |
| #373 | `opnsense_firmware_remove_packages_count` | Gauge | — |
| #373 | `opnsense_firmware_upgrade_sets_count` | Gauge | — |
| #380 | `opnsense_firmware_pending_download_bytes` | Gauge | — |
| #374 | `opnsense_protocol_tcp_connection_drops_by_reason_total` | Counter | `reason` |
| #375 | `opnsense_interfaces_unknown_protocol_packets_total` | Counter | `interface`, `device`, `type` |
| #375 | `opnsense_interfaces_attach_or_statistics_reset_uptime_seconds` | Gauge | `interface`, `device`, `type` |

`component` is exactly `connection|repository`; `state` is the closed vocabulary above with anything unrecognised collapsed to `unknown`. `reason` is exactly `retransmit_timeout|persist_timeout|finwait2_timeout|keepalive`. Every new series that depends on state the box may not report is presence-gated: an absent wire field omits the series rather than emitting a zero. `remove_packages` and `upgrade_sets` are modelled with their full inner shapes (from `check.sh:256`/`262` and `374`/`385`/`397`) despite exporting counts only, because #376 begins reporting unexpected nested keys in this same epic and an under-modelled array would generate exactly the noise #376 exists to surface.

### Contract-tooling seam

#376 adds `UnknownPaths` for nested extras at depth ≥ 1 and **keeps `UnknownTopKeys` unchanged** for the root, so the existing bootgrid-envelope handling, the `knownExtraTopKeys` ledger and the existing report section keep working. Warning-level, never breaking. Dynamic-map keys normalise to `*` as a privacy requirement, not a formatting choice. #377 then adds `opnsense/testdata/schemas/coverage.json` with `required` versus `stateOptional` classes, and per-path unverified reporting; only unresolved `required` paths warn.

### Execution

Lanes run in parallel against the frozen seams above, one file owner each: A=#378, B=#376 then #377 (same files, so sequential), C=#373+#380, D=#374, E=#375. The three Grafana tab modules (`system.py`, `protocols.py`, `interfaces.py`) are disjoint. All generated artefacts — golden schemas, `exemptions.json`, docs, `dashboard.json`, alert manifests — are regenerated in a single wiring pass rather than per lane, and every commit lands from that pass.

## Epic complete — all eight children resolved, six commits on `main`

| # | outcome | SHA |
|---|---|---|
| #378 | fixed | [`9355aa4`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/9355aa4) |
| #374 | shipped | [`9fc10ba`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/9fc10ba) |
| #375 | shipped | [`3699176`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/3699176) |
| #373 + #380 | shipped | [`2d0769b`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/2d0769b) |
| #376 | shipped (report-only baseline) | [`53da29f`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/53da29f) |
| #377 | shipped | [`b171804`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/b171804) |
| #379 | **closed won't-do** — structural, not a version lag | — |

Metrics 818 → **826**. Dashboard coverage **826/826** with 719 panels. One new alert. All eight new metrics presence-gated so absent wire data omits a series rather than emitting a zero.

## Full gate, on the pushed tree

`go test ./...` exit 0 · `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` OK · `golangci-lint run ./...` **0 issues** · `make docs-check` "all generated docs current" · `make grafana-check` "validated 47 grafana-managed manifests: OK" · no conflict markers.

Rebased onto `34e0f04` (a Renovate Actions bump that landed mid-run, no file overlap) and the gate was re-run **after** the rebase rather than assumed.

Regeneration order matters and cost one iteration: `make rules` must run **before** the final `make docs`, because docgen pins alert counts into `grafana/README.md`. Correct order is schemas → docs → dashboard → rules → docs → docs-check.

## Live canary receipt (dev box, OPNsense 26.7.r_35)

**174 endpoints, 0 breaking type drift, 0 unexpected top-level keys, 0 probe errors.** Firmware missing-paths went **7 → 0** after the box-state ledger entries landed. One genuine new finding remains unexempted on purpose (#458, below).

## Corrections to the child issues, all evidence-backed

1. **#373's state vocabularies both omitted `error`** — the value each variable is initialised to (`check.sh:54`/`:66`) and the one that survives an unclassified failure. Following the issue literally would have collapsed the likeliest real-world failure into `unknown`. Implemented from the installed 26.7 `check.sh` header, which is better evidence than GitHub master for what supported releases serve.
2. **#378's "use the same error semantics as adjacent FRR decoders" was void** — all seven decoders in `frr.go` swallow their decode errors. There was no pattern to mirror.
3. **#380 was not capture-blocked.** `download_size` is live (`"37MiB"`), so it shipped in this epic rather than staying deferred. Upstream's own parser truncates decimals (`(\d+)`); ours does not, which is documented because our gauge can exceed the GUI's figure.
4. **#379's blocker is structural, not the version.** The field lands in netbird v0.75.0 (not 0.74.x, the current OPNsense ceiling) **and** setup-key peers can never carry a login-expiry deadline — live `HTTP 412 "this peer hasn't been added with the sso login"`. The os-netbird plugin enrols by setup key only, so the field is permanently absent for every plugin user. Implementing it would have added a permanently dead branch — the #284 failure mode this epic's own rules warn about. The recoverable half is #455.
5. **This epic's own frozen contract was wrong about nested-key severity**, and was corrected on evidence — see below.

## Things the work found that were not in scope

- **A real bug the new tooling caught within minutes of OSPFv3 coming up (#458).** `frrOSPFRouteRow` uses `json:"type"` for both route endpoints, but v3 serves no `type` at all — it splits the same information into `destinationType` + `pathType`. So `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_routes{type=""}` is emitted today and the v3 route-type breakdown is silently lost. Deliberately **not** exempted, so the canary keeps reporting it; silencing a live defect with the compat ledger would be misusing it.
- **The OSPFv3 blind spot is code, not lab (#459).** Both v3 endpoints are registered as envelope types whose sole field is `json.RawMessage` → `KindAny`, so the canary cannot verify their inner shape no matter what the box does. Rediscovered independently twice during this run, which is why it is now written into both the ledger and the `frr.go` banner.
- **The Kea IPv6 gap is root-caused.** The Proxmox **host** kernel is booted with `ipv6.disable=1`, so no LXC on it can ever run a DHCPv6 client. #227 concluded container privilege; that was wrong.
- **A split-brain on the dev box** — `cliVersion 0.74.4` against `daemonVersion 0.72.2`, a package upgrade without a service restart. Any version-gated conclusion drawn before the restart would have been wrong.

## Deliberate deviations, stated plainly

- **Nested-key detection ships REPORT-ONLY.** The baseline found **1003 unmodelled nested paths across 62 endpoints**. The frozen contract specified warning-level; that would have pinned the drift issue permanently open and trained everyone to ignore it — the exact risk #376 names. Triage is **#457**, and flipping the flag is its final step.
- **No second OPNsense VM.** A Debian 13 + FRR 10.3 peer produced identical coverage: the v3 payload is generated entirely by the dev box's own `ospf6d`, so the peer's vendor is invisible in the response, and the same guest doubles as the DHCPv6-PD client. The only available OPNsense media is an interactive DVD ISO. If a real second OPNsense is wanted for CARP/HA or cross-version testing, the ISO is staged and VMID 111+ is free.
- **Grafana artefacts are in-repo only.** The push to `gc-gitsync-m7kni` and `gcx resources push` for the new alert remain manual.

## Known-open, carried forward

#457 (nested baseline triage) · #458 (OSPFv3 route type — live defect) · #459 (envelope reflection) · #455 (netbird `daemonStatus` reaches no metric).

Testbed state that can regress coverage, made loud in the ledger rather than left to surprise someone: the NetBird second peer is hand-started and **not reboot-durable**; Kea v6 rows expire within the lease lifetime if VM 110 stops; `keaLeases4` is currently empty. VM 102 snapshot `pre_447_frr_kea` predates the OSPFv3 changes. A pre-existing netflow target (`127.0.0.1:2056`) contradicts the standing "leave targets empty" rule — not set by this work, flagged for a decision.

## Remote CI receipt

All checks green on the pushed tip [`b171804`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/b171804):

| workflow | result |
|---|---|
| CI (`ci-success`) | success |
| actionlint | success |
| zizmor | success |
| Docker Security | success |
| Scorecard | success |
| Trigger Documentation Sync | success |

That closes the epic's last completion-bar item — the full gate green on the integrated `main` with an exact remote receipt rather than a local-only assertion.

title: epic: expand OPNsense telemetry coverage and API contract assurance

body:
## Problem

Operators can discover invalid flags, unknown overrides, unreadable secret files, TLS mistakes, and conflicting receiver modes only by starting the exporter. Deployment systems lack a stable preflight command that validates effective configuration without binding ports or polling OPNsense.

## Evidence

- Startup validation covers many constraints, while the console exposes effective configuration only after process launch.
- The audit found executable deployment failures around secret readability and Compose health that a preflight could catch.
- No `--config-check`/validate subcommand exists.

## Operator value

A side-effect-free preflight makes systemd, containers, Kubernetes, and upgrade automation fail before replacing a working process.

## Scope

- Reuse the real parser/validation path and read referenced files without opening listeners, starting profilers, polling APIs, or exporting telemetry.
- Emit concise human output and a stable nonzero exit status; optionally provide redacted machine-readable output.
- Document which network reachability checks are intentionally excluded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid production-equivalent arguments return zero without binding any port or making network calls.
- [ ] Unknown collectors/overrides, conflicting modes, invalid durations, unreadable secret files, and TLS keypair errors return nonzero with actionable locations.
- [ ] Output never includes secret contents.
- [ ] Systemd/Compose/Kubernetes examples invoke the preflight where appropriate.
- [ ] Tests prove validation logic cannot drift between check and real startup.

## Dependencies and risks

- Land unknown-override validation and deployment secret fixes first or as frozen seams.
- Do not turn this into an active OPNsense connectivity probe; `/ready` already owns runtime reachability.

## Duplicate verdict

No current issue implements a preflight mode. The operator audit parked a broad check in favor of immediate permission fixes; this is the bounded follow-up.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.

- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

Delivered with #438 in `ed8fa848d69b1aa39acc5c0fbfc21426ae308f73` (pushed to `main`).

`--config.check` reuses the real startup resolver, reads referenced credential/TLS files, reports all validation failures with exit 1, redacts secrets, and performs no listener bind, poll, export, or reachability check. Systemd, Compose, and Kubernetes examples invoke it.

Verification:
- exact staged tree `go test ./...` — pass
- exact staged tree `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` — pass

body:
## Problem

OPNsense API credentials and TLS/sink secrets supplied through files are read at startup. Rotation requires an exporter restart, which resets in-memory log queues and can interrupt telemetry.

## Evidence

- Deployment guidance uses `*_FILE` secret paths but documents no reload signal or atomic rotation contract.
- The operator audit parked hot reload until the immediate unreadable-systemd-secret defect is fixed.
- The log pipeline is memory-buffered, so restart has a real delivery consequence.

## Operator value

Atomic reload supports routine credential rotation without avoidable scrape/log interruptions.

## Scope

- Define reload trigger (signal or authenticated/admin-safe mechanism), atomic validation/swap, and rollback on invalid new material.
- Cover API credentials, receiver TLS, and OTLP authentication only where the underlying clients can be safely rebuilt.
- Expose reload success/failure/last-success self metrics without secret values.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A valid file rotation swaps credentials without process restart or partial mixed configuration.
- [ ] Invalid/unreadable replacement leaves the previous working configuration active and reports failure.
- [ ] Concurrent polls/log exports pass race and fault-injection tests during reload.
- [ ] No secret value appears in logs, metrics, status pages, or errors.
- [ ] Systemd/Kubernetes rotation procedures and limitations are documented.

## Dependencies and risks

- Sequence after file-secret permissions/install guidance is correct.
- Some clients may require brief reconnects; document and measure them rather than promising zero packets lost.

## Duplicate verdict

No active issue tracks secret reload. The deployment audit explicitly parked it as a later operator enhancement.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
escoped from epic #452 by owner decision (2026-07-25).

Premise revalidated against `main` @ `58a51e5` and confirmed **still valid** — there is genuinely no reload mechanism. `rg -n "reload|SIGHUP|fsnotify|watch" internal/options/*.go main.go` returns only a cache comment and an unrelated collector-flag description string; zero reload code. `internal/logship/record.go`'s package doc confirms the queue is in-memory and at-most-once across restarts, so the "restart has a real delivery consequence" claim holds too.

Closing anyway, on scope rather than merit:

1. It is the most invasive of the epic's four P3 conveniences. Atomic swap-with-rollback has to reach into the OPNsense API client's auth, the receiver TLS material, and the OTLP sink's credentials — three separately rebuildable client paths, each with its own in-flight-request hazard.
2. Its own stated dependency has not landed. This issue says "sequence after file-secret permissions/install guidance is correct", and #437 is still open. Building rotation on top of a documented secret layout that the service user cannot currently read would bake in the wrong model.
3. Credential rotation is not a live operational need on the deployed instance today.

Left open, it reads as a commitment the epic is not making. Refile when #437 has settled the permission model and rotation is an actual requirement — the analysis above is the starting point and does not need redoing.

The other three P3 children (#443 fuzzing, #444 Helm, #446 config-check) remain in scope and are being built.

## Problem

NetFlow datagrams, syslog frames/structured data, and Zenarmor documents are untrusted network inputs with complex length, framing, timestamp, and nested-shape logic. The repository has extensive fixtures but no continuous Go fuzz targets for these parser boundaries.

## Evidence

- No `Fuzz*` test exists in the current Go tree.
- This audit found concrete malformed RFC5424 and TCP oversize edge cases despite the existing unit suite.
- NetFlow includes template/stateful decoding; syslog supports RFC3164/RFC5424 plus octet/newline framing; Zenarmor accepts multiple document families.

## Operator value

Fuzzing catches panics, unbounded allocation, hangs, integer mistakes, and parser disagreement before malformed traffic reaches production.

## Scope

- Add focused fuzz targets for stateless decode seams and bounded state-machine harnesses for NetFlow templates/TCP framing.
- Seed with existing real and regression fixtures.
- Run deterministic short fuzz smoke jobs in CI and a longer scheduled job with corpus retention.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fuzz targets cover NetFlow packet/template decode, RFC3164/RFC5424 envelopes, TCP framing, and Zenarmor document parsing.
- [ ] Each target asserts no panic/hang and enforces existing size/resource bounds.
- [ ] Current regression fixtures seed the corpus without sensitive payloads.
- [ ] CI has a bounded smoke budget; scheduled fuzzing retains minimized failures as safe fixtures.
- [ ] Race, unit, lint, and generation gates remain green.

## Dependencies and risks

- Do not commit raw production logs or addresses as corpus files.
- Keep stateful harnesses deterministic and cap memory/input sizes.

## Duplicate verdict

No prior tracker item or current fuzz target covers these network-input parsers.

body:
**Theme:** Least privilege / security ergonomics / troubleshooting  
**Priority:** P1 security ergonomics, otherwise P2  
**Confidence:** 0.90

### Evidence

- `docs/security.md:13-23` tells users to create a dedicated “read-only monitoring user.”
- The listed privilege table covers only 16 legacy GUI privileges (`docs/security.md:25-49`; duplicated at `README.md:131-158`) and then concedes that many newer collectors need unspecified extra permissions.
- The next warning admits those page-level ACLs include write endpoints and have no read-only variant (`docs/security.md:51-52`). “Read-only monitoring user” is therefore a materially misleading security description.
- The client error already carries endpoint and HTTP status (`opnsense/errors.go:5-15`), and the console reduces any observed 401/403 to a generic auth failure (`internal/webui/status.go:248-258`). Nothing maps a failed endpoint to the collector or privilege the operator should grant.
- OPNsense's first-party [API reference](https://docs.opnsense.org/development/api.html) says API access is authorised as the key's user and points operators to Effective Privileges. Its [ACL component documentation](https://docs.opnsense.org/development/components/acl.html) explains that ACL keys map to URI patterns and that modules contribute their own ACL definitions.

### Operator / security value

Lets operators grant the minimum available privilege set for the collectors they enable instead of trial-and-error 403s or falling back to a root/admin key. It also states honestly where OPNsense's ACL granularity still grants write capability.

### Scope

- Add a machine-readable map from exporter endpoint to collector, OPNsense core/plugin, and required ACL privilege.
- Generate documentation for the default collector set and opt-in/plugin collectors.
- Use the map to annotate 403 errors in logs and the operator console with the affected collector, endpoint, and likely missing privilege.
- Version and validate the map against supported OPNsense core/plugin ACL definitions and a least-privilege test user.

### Acceptance checklist

- [x] Every endpoint in the exporter's endpoint registry maps to a collector and an ACL status: known privilege, plugin/version-dependent, or explicitly unknown.
- [x] Generated docs distinguish default-on, opt-in, high-cardinality, and plugin-gated collectors.
- [x] The guide no longer calls the account truly read-only where the granted ACL URI patterns include write routes; it explains the residual capability plainly.
- [x] A 403 log/console entry names the collector, endpoint, and likely OPNsense privilege without exposing credentials.
- [x] Tests fail when a new endpoint or collector is added without an ACL classification.
- [x] The matrix is validated against current and previous supported OPNsense releases; plugin ACL sources and version caveats are recorded.
- [x] README links to the generated matrix instead of maintaining a second partial privilege table.

### Dependencies / risks

- Plugin ACL files live outside OPNsense core and can drift independently. Unknown mappings must remain explicit rather than guessed.
- OPNsense privilege names and URI patterns can change between releases; the source data must be versioned and the support window visible.
- Do not claim that a least-privilege set is harmless: some available ACL units necessarily include mutating endpoints.
- This likely benefits from the existing live-box canary infrastructure, but validation must remain read-only.

### Duplicate verdict

**No duplicate.** #222 added authentication-posture metrics, but did not map endpoints/collectors to OPNsense privileges or make 403 remediation actionable. Full-export ACL/least-privilege searches found only unrelated endpoint/canary work.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

Delivered in `d8a782421febe08598b09c4e4f1a72945011b1ed` and pushed to `main`.

- Added a complete 175-endpoint map with explicit `known`, `plugin-dependent`, or `unknown` status, collector/consumer ownership, privilege alternatives, wildcard scope, and pinned core/plugin provenance.
- Wired generation of the collector-to-ACL matrix into `make docs`; removed the duplicate README table.
- Annotated 401/403 logs and the operator console with endpoint, collector, ACL status, and likely privilege without including response bodies or credentials.

Verification: `go test ./opnsense ./internal/webui ./scripts/docgen -count=1`, `make docs-check`, and the full repository test/build/lint/docs/Grafana gate passed.

**Theme:** Maintainer routing / issue intake / contributor experience  
**Priority:** P1  
**Confidence:** 0.99

### Evidence

- `.github/CODEOWNERS:1` assigns every file to `@ihatemodels`.
- A live read-only GitHub permission query reports that account has `read`, not `write`, on this repository. GitHub's [CODEOWNERS documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners) requires code owners to have write access, so the only rule cannot assign a valid code owner.
- All three issue templates still default-assign the same inherited upstream account:
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md:1-7`
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/question.md:1-7`
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/enhancement.yaml:1-16`
- The bug template asks for OPNsense 21.1.7 and exporter 0.1.0 examples (`bug_report.md:14-18`) and does not ask for deployment mode, affected collector/receiver, redacted effective configuration, or relevant logs.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md:28-36` tells contributors to hand-edit nonexistent `docs/metrics.md`. The actual `docs/metrics/metrics.md` is generated and should be updated through `make docs`.
- `docs/development/contributing.md:95-109` tells contributors to update a removed “Changes from Upstream” README section. `:111-134` also describes `deploy/grafana/`, although Grafana artifacts live at repository root.
- The root `CONTRIBUTING.md:1-45` and site contributing page duplicate an incomplete gate. Neither gives contributors the actual blocking CI set: full tests, race, docs-check, Grafana builder tests/check, and container verification.

### Maintainer / contributor value

Restores real review ownership, stops issue templates routing work to an upstream read-only account, collects enough diagnostic context on first report, and gives contributors one accurate pre-PR path.

### Scope

- Set CODEOWNERS to a current write-capable maintainer/team or deliberately remove it.
- Remove inherited default assignees and modernise issue forms for the current project.
- Make the PR template generator-aware and match the real CI gate.
- Choose one canonical contribution guide; render/sync the other or reduce it to a stable pointer.
- Remove the obsolete fork-changelog instruction and repair the project map.

### Acceptance checklist

- [x] Every CODEOWNERS identity/team is verified to have write access, or CODEOWNERS is removed with an explicit rationale.
- [x] No issue template auto-assigns `ihatemodels`.
- [x] The bug form requests exporter version, OPNsense version, deployment method, affected collector/receiver, redacted effective config, relevant logs, expected/actual behavior, and reproduction steps.
- [x] Templates clearly warn against pasting API keys, secrets, tokens, or unredacted config.
- [x] The PR checklist directs contributors to run generators and then check generated artifacts; it never asks for hand edits to generated metrics/dashboard files.
- [x] The documented local gate matches all jobs feeding `ci-success`, including race and Grafana checks.
- [x] Root and site contribution guides cannot silently drift.
- [x] Template schema and CODEOWNERS validity are checked in CI.

### Dependencies / risks

- Required-review enforcement depends on branch-protection configuration outside the repository; a valid CODEOWNERS file alone does not enable required code-owner reviews.
- Avoid auto-assigning the owner merely to make the check green if that is not the desired issue-routing workflow.
- Preserve `CHANGELOG.md` as the sole changelog; do not recreate “Changes from Upstream.”

### Duplicate verdict

**No duplicate.** Full-export searches found no CODEOWNERS, `ihatemodels`, or template-maintenance issue. #151 concerns prose/doclint coverage, not invalid repository ownership or intake routing.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

**Theme:** Documentation contracts / example generation / public configuration truth  
**Priority:** P1 for current corrections, P2 for the prevention framework  
**Confidence:** 0.97

### Evidence

The current `make docs-check` passes while all of these contradictions are present:

- The code says an empty instance label defaults to the configured OPNsense address and hostname use is opt-in (`internal/options/exporter.go:20-35`). `docs/upgrading.md:32-37` and `:84-87` agree. `README.md:49-51` says the opposite: hostname is the default. This affects series identity, not cosmetic prose.
- `README.md:30-34` and `:124` say 818 metrics, while `README.md:173` links to “All 808 metrics.” The generator itself reports 818.
- `docs/getting-started.md:13-18` says the exporter is tested with 24.x and 25.x, while the canonical current/previous support policy is 26.1.x and 25.7 in `docs/compatibility.md:11-20`.
- `docs/development/release-process.md:51-77` documents image tags with a leading `v`. Live GHCR read-back succeeds for `:3.0.0` and fails for `:v3.0.0`; the Kubernetes manifest correctly documents no leading `v`.
- The canonical Kubernetes manifest uses `/-/healthy` probes and exposes optional syslog ports (`deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml:44-69`, `:125-142`). The copy embedded in `docs/deployment/kubernetes.md:41-141` still probes `/` and omits the receiver ports.
- `release-please-config.json:7-13` updates the version marker in both Kubernetes copies, but does not keep the rest of the duplicated YAML in sync.

### Operator / maintainer value

Prevents unexpected label churn, stale support expectations, wrong image pulls, and deployment behavior that changes depending on whether a user copies the docs or the repository manifest. It also turns `docs-check` into a semantic contract rather than only a generated-file freshness check.

### Scope

- Correct the current contradictions.
- Make canonical deployment artifacts the source for rendered documentation snippets, or replace inline copies with direct links plus small generated excerpts.
- Extend doc-generation/contract checks to public facts that are already derivable: metric count, collector count, instance-label default, image-tag convention, probe paths, and manifest version.
- Add targeted executable checks for release filenames/URLs, Compose syntax, and Kubernetes manifests rather than relying only on prose lint.

### Acceptance checklist

- [ ] README and generated configuration/upgrading docs agree that the address is the default instance label and hostname is opt-in.
- [ ] Every public metric/collector count is generated or checked against the registry; no hand-maintained 808/818 split remains.
- [ ] Getting Started links to or renders the canonical current/previous support policy rather than retaining historical version text.
- [ ] Release-process docs describe the actual no-leading-`v` image tags and current release artifact set.
- [ ] The documentation's Kubernetes example is generated from, included from, or automatically compared with `deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml`.
- [ ] The Kubernetes artifact passes schema validation and the documented Compose example passes `docker compose config`.
- [ ] A targeted test fails when a documented release filename does not exist in the GoReleaser artifact plan.
- [ ] `make docs-check` includes these contracts and remains read-only in check mode.

### Dependencies / risks

- Keep the README intentionally concise; do not recreate the removed “Changes from Upstream” inventory. `CHANGELOG.md` remains the changelog.
- Avoid a generic link checker as the sole fix: it will not catch semantically wrong but HTTP-200 examples, no-op flags, or a valid-looking duplicated manifest.
- Current OPNsense versions are time-sensitive. Prefer one canonical support declaration plus an explicit maintenance/update mechanism over several hard-coded copies.

### Duplicate verdict

**New systemic follow-up, with closed adjacent issues.** #75 fixed deterministic instance-label behaviour, but the README still contradicts it. #117 fixed stale collector/metric counts, but the 808 reference is outside the enforced token set. #99 repaired the old Kubernetes timeout/DNS example; #151 expanded doclint. None currently enforces executable, single-source deployment/public-fact contracts.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

**Theme:** Configuration UX / metric contract / dashboard and migration cleanup  
**Priority:** P1  
**Confidence:** 0.99

### Evidence

- After #336, serving `/metrics` is a pure replay from memory and makes no OPNsense API call (`internal/collector/collector.go:1284-1293`).
- The server still parses `X-Prometheus-Scrape-Timeout-Seconds`, creates a derived context, and passes it to the replay view (`internal/server/metrics.go:134-145`), even though the collector explicitly ignores the context.
- The public `--exporter.scrape-timeout-offset` flag still describes an API-collection deadline (`internal/options/exporter.go:37-45`) and remains wired through `main.go:1198-1204`. It no longer influences background polling.
- `opnsense_exporter_scrape_skips_total` still claims to report deadline/mutex pile-up (`internal/collector/collector.go:1105-1115`) but repository search finds no increment after its zero-value initialisation at `:1154-1155`.
- The generated Grafana dashboard continues to chart the inert counter and diagnoses “mutex pile-up in front of a slow firewall” (`grafana/build_dashboard.py:252-262`).
- Stale pre-scheduler guidance remains in:
  - `docs/configuration.md:148-175` and `:608-611`
  - `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml:13-20`
  - `docs/deployment/kubernetes.md:151-168`
  - `docs/deployment.md:54-56`
  - `docs/troubleshooting.md:47-66`
  - `docs/collectors/index.md:11-30`
  - `docs/index.md:84-85`
- #336's issue discussion explicitly noted that the skip counter stayed registered but stopped incrementing. The closing work did not retire the surface.

### Operator value

Removes a no-op configuration knob and a metric/dashboard signal that can never report the condition its help text describes. Rewrites tuning guidance around the real poll scheduler instead of the obsolete scrape fan-out model.

### Scope

- Decide and document compatibility policy for the dead flag and metric: deprecate in v3 and remove in the next major, or remove immediately only if project policy permits.
- Remove the unused request-header deadline plumbing once compatibility permits.
- Remove the inert skip metric or redefine it only if there is a real, measurable serving-admission condition.
- Replace the dashboard panel with poll freshness, poll failure, queue/concurrency, or serving-admission signals that actually move.
- Update all operator prose, diagrams, flag help, metric help, Kubernetes comments, and troubleshooting advice to the scheduler/snapshot model.

### Acceptance checklist

- [ ] A regression test proves that changing the Prometheus timeout header or scrape-timeout-offset cannot change OPNsense API polling.
- [ ] The dead flag has an explicit deprecation/removal path and a migration note in `docs/upgrading.md`.
- [ ] The inert metric is removed on the chosen compatibility schedule, or a test exercises a real increment path matching revised help text.
- [ ] The Grafana dashboard no longer presents a permanently-zero skip-rate diagnosis.
- [ ] `rg` finds no claim that `/metrics` performs collector/API fan-out or that the Prometheus scrape timeout bounds background OPNsense calls.
- [ ] `--opnsense.timeout`, request concurrency, and max poll duration guidance refer to poll deadlines/intervals rather than `scrape_timeout`.
- [ ] Generated metrics/config docs and the full Grafana/docs gates are green.

### Dependencies / risks

- Metric and flag removal is a public breaking change; a deprecation window is the safer default.
- Keep Prometheus's own HTTP scrape timeout in examples where useful for bounding the network request. Only the claim that it controls OPNsense collection is wrong.
- Do not rename every historical `scrape_*` metric in the same change; constrain scope to no-op/deceptive surfaces and clearly stale help.

### Duplicate verdict

**Required follow-up to closed #336, not a duplicate.** #122 fixed the old deadline-expired collection path and is superseded by the scheduler architecture. #336 intentionally left this counter registered but inert; this issue closes that acknowledged remainder.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.

- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.
