body:
**Theme:** Container deployment / health semantics / Compose secrets  
**Priority:** P1  
**Confidence:** 0.98

### Evidence

- The runtime image is distroless and contains only the exporter plus license files (`Dockerfile:37-54`). The project itself documents that it has no shell or package manager (`docs/security.md:190-198`).
- `docs/deployment/docker.md:126-140` nevertheless defines a healthcheck that executes `wget` inside the container. That command is not in the image.
- The same paragraph says the container “gets restarted” when the healthcheck fails. Docker's [HEALTHCHECK reference](https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/#healthcheck) says the check changes container health status; the [restart-policy documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/start-containers-automatically/) ties restart policies to container exit/stop, not an `unhealthy` status.
- `docs/deployment/docker.md:71-109` presents `docker secret create` and `external: true` as the default Docker Compose path, then relegates non-Swarm use to bind mounts. Docker's first-party [Compose secrets guide](https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/use-secrets/) uses top-level `secrets: ... file:` and per-service grants for regular Compose.
- The distroless design is intentional; the upstream [distroless project](https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/distroless) documents the absence of shells and other normal userland tools.

### Operator value

Stops users copying a healthcheck that can never become healthy, removes a false automatic-recovery promise, and gives non-Swarm Compose users a native secrets example.

### Scope

- Either add a native, static health-probe mode/tool that is actually present in the image, or remove the in-container HTTP healthcheck and document process restart semantics accurately.
- Use `/-/healthy`, not the operator-console root, for a real HTTP liveness probe.
- Make regular Compose `secrets.file` the primary local example; label external Docker secrets as Swarm-only.
- Exercise the published example with the built image in CI.

### Acceptance checklist

- [ ] A failing container test demonstrates that the current `wget` healthcheck cannot execute.
- [ ] Every command in the replacement healthcheck exists in the runtime image and reaches `/-/healthy`.
- [ ] CI starts the image using the documented Compose configuration and observes the expected healthy state, or the healthcheck is deliberately removed and the docs explain why.
- [ ] The docs state that `restart:` reacts to process exit, not merely Docker health status; any automatic unhealthy-container remediation names the required external mechanism.
- [ ] The non-Swarm example uses Compose `secrets.file`, passes `docker compose config`, and the non-root container can read both mounted secrets.
- [ ] Swarm external secrets and simple bind mounts are clearly marked as alternatives rather than conflated.

### Dependencies / risks

- Do not install `curl`, `wget`, or a shell merely to rescue the example; that weakens the deliberate distroless runtime.
- A new probe subcommand becomes a public interface and needs CLI tests and upgrade documentation.
- Docker Compose implementations can differ in how they realise local file secrets; test the minimum supported Compose version.

### Duplicate verdict

**No duplicate.** #292 discusses adding a private CA to a distroless image; #147 hardens Kubernetes. Neither covers a nonexistent healthcheck executable, Docker health/restart semantics, or Compose-vs-Swarm secret syntax.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
Delivered with #446 in `ed8fa848d69b1aa39acc5c0fbfc21426ae308f73` (pushed to `main`). The shared binary dispatch, Compose example, and Compose CI test make the two changes one executable deployment path.

The distroless image now uses `/opnsense-exporter health` against `/-/healthy`; plain Compose `secrets.file` is the primary example, and the docs distinguish health status from restart behavior.

Verification:
- old `wget` probe against the built image — exit 127, executable absent (expected failing reproduction)
- documented Compose secrets/config-check/native-health path — container reached `healthy`; UID 65532 read both secrets
- exact staged tree `go test ./...` — 23 packages pass

body:
**Theme:** Systemd deployment / supply-chain verification / secret permissions  
**Priority:** P1  
**Confidence:** 0.99

### Evidence

- `docs/deployment/systemd.md:14-23` and `:154-166` download `opnsense-exporter_linux_amd64` as a raw binary.
- GoReleaser actually emits `opnsense-exporter_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz` (`.goreleaser.yml:31-45`). A live request to the documented URL returned 404; the archive URL returned 200 and appears on the v3.0.0 release.
- The guide suggests separate key/secret files created by `sudo tee` and set to mode 0600 (`docs/deployment/systemd.md:58-72`). `docs/security.md:172-182` makes the broken ownership explicit: `root:root` 0600.
- The unit runs as `User=opnsense-exporter` (`docs/deployment/systemd.md:83-91`). The exporter process itself opens the paths (`internal/options/ops.go:82-97`, `internal/options/pyroscope.go:92-108`), so it cannot read root-owned 0600 credential files. `ReadOnlyPaths=` at `docs/deployment/systemd.md:115-116` does not grant Unix read permission.
- The release publishes `checksums.txt` and `checksums.txt.sigstore.json` (`.goreleaser.yml:43-64`), but the installation and upgrade instructions verify neither.

The root-only `EnvironmentFile=` at `docs/deployment/systemd.md:39-56` is not the defect: systemd reads that file before dropping to the service user. The defect is specifically the `*_FILE` credentials opened by the non-root exporter.

### Operator value

Turns the documented fresh install from a 404 followed by an unreadable-secret failure into a reproducible, verified service installation. It also gives operators a safe, atomic upgrade path.

### Scope

- Download and extract the real release archive for the selected OS/architecture.
- Verify archive checksum and the published Sigstore bundle before installation.
- Give only the exporter process read access to `OPS_API_KEY_FILE` and `OPS_API_SECRET_FILE` (for example, exporter-owned 0600 or root-owned/group-readable 0640).
- Make upgrades verify first, replace atomically, restart, and check service health.
- Smoke-test the commands copied from the documentation against a real release layout.

### Acceptance checklist

- [ ] A regression test proves the current documented filename is absent and the generated/documented filename matches `.goreleaser.yml`.
- [ ] The install instructions select the correct archive for at least Linux x86_64 and arm64 and run `opnsense-exporter --version` after extraction.
- [ ] The documented checksum and Sigstore verification commands succeed against a published release.
- [ ] A test executed as the `opnsense-exporter` user can read each documented `*_FILE` secret while an unrelated user cannot.
- [ ] The systemd unit starts with file-based credentials and reaches `/-/healthy`.
- [ ] The upgrade flow stages and verifies the new binary before stopping the current service, performs an atomic install, and verifies restart health.
- [ ] Both `docs/deployment/systemd.md` and `docs/security.md` use the same permission model.

### Dependencies / risks

- Exact `cosign verify-blob` identity constraints must match the repository's GitHub Actions signing identity; do not publish a verification command that merely checks a signature without constraining issuer/identity.
- Avoid making the entire `/etc/opnsense-exporter` directory group-readable just to expose two files.
- Preserve the hardened unit settings and non-root runtime.

### Duplicate verdict

**No duplicate in the full export.** #292 is limited to private CA trust in the distroless container; #293 concerns the release-please marker in the Kubernetes image tag. Neither covers release archive names, systemd file ownership, or signature verification.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

body:
**Theme:** Release integrity / license compliance  
**Priority:** P0 before another release  
**Confidence:** 0.99

### Evidence

- `Makefile:4-8` pins `GO_LICENSES_VERSION=v2.0.1`, but `Makefile:64-75` installs `github.com/google/go-licenses@v2.0.1`. v2 uses the semantic-import path `github.com/google/go-licenses/v2`.
- The live [Release Please run 30053718973](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/actions/runs/30053718973) failed only in `publish / notices`. Its exact error was:

  `invalid version: go.mod has post-v2 module path "github.com/google/go-licenses/v2" at revision v2.0.1`

- `.github/workflows/publish.yml:22-50` makes `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` a release asset, but normal CI never exercises `make notices`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml:18-183` covers tests, race, generated docs, Grafana, and a container build only.
- The container build did not catch the defect because `Dockerfile:28-35` independently installs the old `github.com/google/go-licenses@v1.6.0`. The two release paths have silently diverged.
- The live [v3.0.0 release](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/releases/tag/v3.0.0) contains binaries, checksums, a Sigstore bundle, provenance, and SBOMs, but no `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. The image and binary jobs succeeded, leaving a published partial release behind a red aggregate run.
- Upstream's v2 package is published under [`github.com/google/go-licenses/v2`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/google/go-licenses/v2).

### Operator / maintainer value

Restores the artifact the workflow promises, makes the already-published v3.0.0 release complete, and turns a release-only tool-resolution failure into a pre-merge failure.

### Scope

- Correct the v2 module/install path.
- Establish one source of truth for the go-licenses version and module path used by `make notices`, the image build, and Renovate.
- Exercise release tooling from a clean tool directory in CI; an existing `.tools/go-licenses` binary must not mask the test.
- Verify the required release asset set after a tagged publish.
- Backfill `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` on v3.0.0 once generated by the corrected path.
- Bring `docs/development/release-process.md:51-116` in line with the actual binary, image, SBOM, signature, provenance, and notices pipeline.

### Acceptance checklist

- [ ] A failing test or CI smoke step reproduces the current `v2.0.1` install failure from an empty tool directory.
- [ ] `make notices` installs and runs the v2 command successfully without relying on a cached binary.
- [ ] Makefile, Dockerfile/build args, and Renovate annotations cannot select different go-licenses versions or module paths unnoticed.
- [ ] A CI/release test asserts that a tagged release contains the agreed mandatory assets, including `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- [ ] The fixed notices file is attached to the existing v3.0.0 release and a scoped read-back confirms it.
- [ ] The release-process page documents the real artifacts and the no-leading-`v` image tag convention.
- [ ] The normal full gate remains green.

### Dependencies / risks

- Backfilling the release asset is a GitHub write and should happen only after the generated file has been reviewed.
- If v2 changes output semantics relative to v1.6.0, compare the generated notice set before standardising both paths.
- Do not commit generated dependency notices merely to make Renovate regenerate them; keep the release-time model and test the command itself.

### Duplicate verdict

**New regression, not a duplicate.** #135 added Renovate discovery for the pinned versions, but validated version detection rather than executable installation. The v2 bump exposed the untested semantic-import-path break. #135 is the direct predecessor and should be linked.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

body:
## Problem

The live Zenarmor companion dashboard is managed outside the repository's generator and lacks an OPNsense-instance contract. It can drift from exporter log fields, labels, navigation, and test gates.

## Evidence

- Live UID `opnsense-zenarmor` is not generated from the in-repo dashboard source.
- Queries select `opnsense_source="zenarmor"` and device/action fields but do not constrain a stable exporter instance.
- Several panels displayed generic `Value #A` legends, and exact DNS/SNI/JA3 queries took roughly 14 seconds during audit validation.
- The exact DNS, SNI, and JA3 queries did return live data; this issue must not treat the snapshot's transient No data as a proven schema defect.

## Operator value

Generated ownership provides drift tests, portable scoping, meaningful legends, and a place to profile expensive log queries without overstating current data gaps.

## Scope

- Import the dashboard definition into a generator or explicitly merge its unique content into the canonical Logs/Zenarmor tabs.
- Add stable instance/device/action variables and context-preserving links.
- Profile expensive top-k/range queries before changing them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The dashboard has one source-controlled generated owner and reproducible UID — the generated Zenarmor tab; companion UID retired and in the never-reuse list.
- [x] All panels are instance-safe and use the current structured log schema — enforced by `tests/test_zenarmor_tab.py`.
- [x] Legends, units, empty states, and descriptions are operator-readable — every merged panel has a written description; remaining key-column noise is filed as #471.
- [x] Known DNS/SNI/JA3 queries remain data-bearing on the live test window — all 10 merged queries returned series; two rendered as proof.
- [x] Query timings and any optimization decision are recorded — 986-2503 ms at a 3h window; decision is collapsed rows, no query changes.

## Dependencies and risks

- Depends on stable logship instance identity.
- Do not claim the three audited query families are broken; optimize only from measured behavior.

## Duplicate verdict

No repo issue covers ownership of the live Zenarmor companion. The malformed PromQL issue concerns a different generated metrics panel.

## Live verification

- Grafana Cloud stack `m7kni` was inspected read-only on 2026-07-25 using Grafana 13.2.0.
- The live main dashboard `opnsense-exporter` was GitSync-backed at version 2 with 711 elements and 100 variables.
- Live alerting contained 45 healthy rules in folder `opnsense-alerts`; 21,793 OPNsense series and 480 distinct `opnsense_*` metric names were present over the six-hour audit window.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Clean programme pause status

Queued under #453; no issue-specific implementation has started. No GitSync source, generated dashboard, repository file, or live Grafana resource was changed for this child.

The clean pause baseline is `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`: local `main`, `origin/main`, and remote main match, the worktree is clean, and all eight exact-SHA workflows are terminal-success. Resume after read-only reconciliation of #432–#434 retirement state and after #450/#451 freeze the shared UID, variable, and navigation contracts.

Parent receipt: https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/453#issuecomment-5085202867

Important: the zenarmor features should be within a tab in the existing comprehensive dashboard and not a dedicated panel. We should also utilise the metrics we are generating from the zenarmor data over logql type queries where possible (or we should ship recording rules to get the data from the log lines)

## Consequence of the owner's tab decision, recorded for #419

The owner's 2026-07-27 restatement — Zenarmor lives as a tab in the main dashboard, hidden
when no Zenarmor data exists, and should prefer the generated Zenarmor **metrics** over
LogQL where possible (shipping recording rules if the data only exists in log lines) —
changes #419's scope as well as this issue's:

- **There is no external Zenarmor destination to navigate to.** #419's planned
  main-to-Zenarmor drilldown is struck rather than deferred; an in-dashboard tab needs no
  link. The retired UID `opnsense-zenarmor` goes in #419's never-reuse list.
- The main dashboard **already has** a `Zenarmor` leaf tab whose rows are sentinel-gated,
  so "hides when no Zenarmor data exists" is satisfied by the existing mechanism. The work
  here is merging the companion's unique content into that tab and retiring the companion —
  not building the gating.

No implementation this run; this issue stays queued under #453.

## Delivered in [`59c4dfe`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/59c4dfe) — companion merged and retired

Per the owner's 2026-07-27 instruction, Zenarmor is a tab of the main dashboard, so the
question was not "how do we generate the companion" but **which of its 17 panels said
anything the generated tab did not**. Nine did.

### What moved, and what deliberately did not

| merged (unique) | not merged (already derived from metrics) |
| --- | --- |
| `Top DNS Queries`, `DNS Response Codes`, `Top DNS Domain Categories` | `Records / sec`, `Blocked (selected range)`, `Records by family` |
| `Top HTTP Hosts`, `Top URIs`, `Top User Agents`, `HTTP Status Codes` | `Top categories` (Flow Volume has it by category, from metrics) |
| `Top Applications` (app_name) | `Top JA3 client fingerprints`, `Top talkers`, `Raw records` |
| `Top TLS Server Names (SNI)`, `Destination Countries` — all-verdict counterparts to the existing blocked-only tables | |

Not merging the eight is the metrics-over-LogQL preference this issue asked for: the tab
already answers those from `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total`, which is cheaper than
counting log lines for the same number.

The nine were **rewritten, not copied**. Every selector goes through `loki_sel()` and every
`topk` carries `loki_grp()`. The companion had neither, and on a shared Loki tenant an
unscoped `topk` does not merge a second firewall's rows — it **drops** them, with nothing on
screen suggesting a second box exists (#413/#468).

### Three findings

- **The companion's `Device` picker cannot ever have worked.** Its query was a bare stream
  selector (`{opnsense_source="zenarmor"} | device_name!=""`), and `device_name` is
  structured metadata, not an indexed label: `label_values(..., device_name)` returns null,
  and the datasource's 44 label names do not include it (verified live). The replacement is
  a **textbox** `$zenarmor_client` taking a regex — honest about being un-enumerable, and it
  costs no cold-load query (#422). It sits in the controls menu (#470), since it applies to
  one tab of 41.
- **The web panels had to exclude the exporter's own ingest endpoint.** Zenarmor POSTs its
  records to us over HTTP, so unfiltered, our own `/zenarmor_*/_bulk` URI is the top host,
  the top URI and a large share of the status codes — the panels would have described this
  exporter rather than the network.
- **`promqlcheck` had a latent bug worse than the feature that exposed it.** Its variable
  type decoded `spec.query` as a query object, but a `TextVariable`'s `query` is a plain
  string — so ONE textbox made the whole document fail to decode and the tool validated
  **nothing**, reporting a json error instead of 975 targets. Now decoded per kind, with an
  unknown kind skipped rather than fatal, and a regression test.

### Live receipts

Published through GitSync
([`78dc3b1`](https://github.com/rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni/commit/78dc3b1)), which also
deletes `networking/opnsense-zenarmor.json`:

```text
opnsense-exporter    generation 6 -> 7 · 739 -> 749 elements · 106 -> 107 variables
                     checksum 6b8028e57acf8fd9 -> e15ee8a3e9f1f4ea
                     all 10 merged panel titles present · zenarmor_client TextVariable present
opnsense-zenarmor    gcx dashboards get -> 404 NotFound   (retired)
```

**Query timings, 3h window against the live Loki** (wall clock, ~800 ms of it fixed
per-request overhead measured in #422):

| panel | ms | series |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Top Applications | 2503 | 49 |
| DNS Response Codes | 2335 | 5 |
| Top DNS Queries | 2292 | 153 |
| Top DNS Domain Categories | 2161 | 33 |
| Top URIs | 2150 | 165 |
| Top User Agents | 1722 | 51 |
| Top HTTP Hosts | 1707 | 51 |
| Top TLS Server Names (SNI) | 1601 | 120 |
| Destination Countries | 1521 | 27 |
| HTTP Status Codes | 986 | 10 |

**Optimisation decision: the three new rows ship COLLAPSED, and nothing else is changed.**
All ten are data-bearing and none is pathological, but they are 2-3x the cost of a
Prometheus panel query on a 2.5-3.3M records/day stream, and #422 established that
cold-load cost is round-trip count. A collapsed row issues nothing until opened, which
makes the expensive half of this tab opt-in per visit rather than per load. The audit's
"roughly 14 seconds for two requests" is not reproduced at a 3h window; it is not called a
defect, in line with this issue's binding decision.

Two panels were rendered from the published dashboard as data-bearing proof: `Top DNS
Queries` (top row `profiles-prod-023.grafana.net`, 4396) and `Top Applications` (top row
`Domain Name Resolution`, 65925).

### One defect found by rendering, filed rather than absorbed

**#471** — every `loki_table()` renders its key column as the serialised label set
(`{app_name="STUN", service_instance_id="opnsense"}`) instead of a titled column per field.
It affects all **14** such tables, not only the six added here, so it belongs in the shared
helper with its own before/after rather than being patched into this change. The value and
the ordering are correct; only the presentation is wrong, which is why no test caught it.

### Criteria

- [x] One source-controlled generated owner and reproducible UID — the tab is generated; the
      companion UID is retired and now in `uids.RETIRED_UIDS`, so it can be neither linked
      nor recreated.
- [x] All panels instance-safe and on the current structured log schema — enforced by
      `tests/test_zenarmor_tab.py`, not asserted.
- [x] Legends, units, empty states and descriptions operator-readable — every panel carries a
      written description; the generic `Value #A` legends the audit found are gone. The
      remaining key-column noise is #471.
- [x] Known DNS/SNI/JA3 queries remain data-bearing on the live test window — table above.
- [x] Query timings and the optimisation decision recorded — table and decision above.

### Gate on `59c4dfe`

```text
go test ./...  ·  go vet ./...  ·  CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...   exit 0
go test -C tools/promqlcheck ./...                               exit 0
golangci-lint run ./...                                          0 issues
make docs-check  ·  make grafana-check                           passed
    191 grafana tests · 837/837 catalogue coverage · 749 panels / 41 tabs
    975 Prometheus targets + 102 variable queries + 10 annotation queries validated
7/7 workflows terminal-success on 59c4dfe
```

## Problem

The live `OPNsense SFP & Port Monitor` overlaps the canonical interface/SFP tab and presents expected copper/no-DOM ports as orange `NO DOM`. It also exposes a synthetic `none` interface choice.

## Evidence

- Live dashboard UID `ddfj9vprnpio74a` rendered useful SFP/link data but showed `NO DOM` as a warning-like state for copper hardware.
- The variable/results include `none`.
- The canonical generated dashboard already owns interface, line-rate, SFP, and optical telemetry.

## Operator value

A single portable view avoids duplicated maintenance and distinguishes unsupported telemetry from degraded hardware.

## Scope

- Compare unique SFP diagnostics and migrate valuable panels into the canonical generated source.
- Filter synthetic/empty interface values.
- Model no-DOM as neutral/unsupported, while retaining real alarm thresholds for DOM-capable optics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Copper/no-DOM ports render neutral rather than warning/failure.
- [ ] The `none` interface cannot be selected or displayed.
- [ ] Every retained panel has one generated owner with tested units and thresholds.
- [ ] The companion is retired or reduced to a linked specialized view with explicit ownership.
- [ ] Live visual validation covers copper and DOM-capable ports.

## Dependencies and risks

- Do not infer optical alarms for hardware that does not expose DOM.
- Coordinate with the generic bar-gauge threshold cleanup.

## Duplicate verdict

No existing issue reconciles the live companion with the generated SFP/interface tab.

## Live verification

- Grafana Cloud stack `m7kni` was inspected read-only on 2026-07-25 using Grafana 13.2.0.
- The live main dashboard `opnsense-exporter` was GitSync-backed at version 2 with 711 elements and 100 variables.
- Live alerting contained 45 healthy rules in folder `opnsense-alerts`; 21,793 OPNsense series and 480 distinct `opnsense_*` metric names were present over the six-hour audit window.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

## Programme pause status

The current programme baseline records this companion as already retired through GitSync. This run did not perform the required present-tense read-only verification of live absence, manager annotations, source ownership, and exact GitSync evidence, so the issue remains open and no acceptance checkbox is being claimed yet.

Next action is verification only. Do not recreate, overwrite, or retire the dashboard again. If current absence and ownership evidence match the baseline, update the checklist and close manually with that exact receipt; otherwise record the live contradiction before any change.

## Retirement verified — closing this issue

Reconciled against live state as epic #453 requires before any dashboard work. Retirement was already carried out through GitSync and is confirmed on both halves.

### How this was verified (read-only, both halves)

**Live stack** — `<host-36>`, 199 dashboards enumerated. Exactly two carry an OPNsense title or resource name:

| resource | title | folder | GitSync `sourcePath` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opnsense-exporter` | OPNsense Exporter | networking | `networking/opnsense-exporter.json` |
| `opnsense-zenarmor` | OPNsense Zenarmor — Network Activity & Threats | networking | `networking/opnsense-zenarmor.json` |

**GitSync source** — `rknightion/gc-gitsync-m7kni`, `origin/main` at `7dd8a4f03cdfda930f8f9c65b42f550b46022dcd`. `git ls-tree origin/main networking/` lists 17 entries; the three retired companions are absent, each removed by an explicit delete commit:

| dashboard | delete commit | committed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OPNsense Firewall Logs | `066d5a153fcb11006983dd82ed63a82e8666d74d` | 2026-07-25T17:07:33Z |
| OPNsense SFP & Port Monitor | `50e2ab9b10287899dfa5c8e7da32b08c4344dd7b` | 2026-07-25T18:50:36Z |
| OPNsense — Network Activity | `1b64eeeaa048af3fb29e649d0cd32fac282778cf` | 2026-07-25T18:56:00Z |

Both halves agree, so retirement is real and reconciled: absent from the GitSync source of truth **and** absent from the live stack. Nothing was recreated, re-retired, or overwritten.

**A trap for the next session:** the local clone at `~/repos/gc-gitsync-m7kni` is **14 commits behind `origin/main`** and carries untracked `dashboards/` and `resources/` directories. Its working tree is NOT evidence of live state and must never be pushed from as-is — `git fetch` and read `origin/main`. A first pass at this verification read the stale working tree and briefly concluded the retirements had never happened.

Note the GitSync history shows a migration attempt immediately before removal — `cd70db3 Save dashboard: migrate OPNsense SFP monitor to exporter metrics` — followed by the delete in `50e2ab9`. The migration was superseded by retirement rather than abandoned silently.

### Disposition

Retirement is the correct outcome. SFP and port monitoring duplicated canonical content, and the no-DOM concern this issue raised is now handled in the canonical dashboard's own interface tab rather than in a separate companion. The "no-DOM/unsupported hardware is neutral" rule stays binding on the canonical dashboard; it is not lost with this companion. No repository change was needed and none was made.

body:
## Problem

The live `OPNsense Network Activity` dashboard mixes exporter metrics with site-specific interface mappings and an external ktranslate NetFlow schema. Several panels are blank or misleading outside one firewall, while much of the content duplicates the canonical 711-panel dashboard.

## Evidence

- Queries hard-code `instance="opnsense"`, job names, device `<lan-ip-2>`, physical interfaces, and display names such as `AAISP` and `VIRGIN`.
- The dashboard queries `network_io_by_flow_bytes{job="integrations/ktranslate-netflow"}`, which is not emitted by this exporter.
- The live snapshot showed partial No data and gauge layouts that are difficult to interpret.

## Operator value

Clarifies which dashboard is supported, removes hidden personal topology assumptions, and prevents two diverging operational views from competing for ownership.

## Scope

- Inventory unique panels against the canonical dashboard.
- Move generally useful views into generated source with variables; explicitly mark or remove stack-local ktranslate content.
- Retire the companion if no unique portable value remains.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every retained panel has a documented datasource and portable variable contract.
- [ ] No source-controlled dashboard hard-codes Rob's firewall instance, IP, WAN names, or physical interfaces.
- [ ] Duplicate panels have one canonical owner and links replace copies where appropriate.
- [ ] The decision to rebuild or retire is recorded and reflected in GitSync.
- [ ] Live visual/query validation passes for the resulting state.

## Dependencies and risks

- Preserve stack-local dashboards outside this repo only when ownership is explicit.
- Do not make the exporter federate ktranslate metrics merely to keep this dashboard alive.

## Duplicate verdict

No tracker issue covers this live companion dashboard or its hard-coded topology.

## Live verification

- Grafana Cloud stack `m7kni` was inspected read-only on 2026-07-25 using Grafana 13.2.0.
- The live main dashboard `opnsense-exporter` was GitSync-backed at version 2 with 711 elements and 100 variables.
- Live alerting contained 45 healthy rules in folder `opnsense-alerts`; 21,793 OPNsense series and 480 distinct `opnsense_*` metric names were present over the six-hour audit window.

## Audit receipt

## Problem

Exporter/poller health is mixed into the 711-panel operational dashboard. There is no separate OPNsense exporter self-observability dashboard, even though self metrics describe a different subject: scheduling, retained data, API delivery, HTTP admission, log queues, rule evaluation, and process health.

## Evidence

- The live main dashboard contains Diagnostics, Log Shipping, and Recording Rules tabs but no separate exporter-health dashboard.
- Live Grafana search found companion operational/log dashboards but no OPNsense exporter self-observability dashboard.
- The live stack exposes 34 current self-metric names, while repository coverage gates exclude self metrics.
- Comparable live exporter dashboards (`ts2otel-exporter-health`, Meraki self-observability) demonstrate the operational split.

## Operator value

A focused dashboard makes it obvious whether a blank operational panel means the firewall, the poller, the sink, or Grafana is unhealthy. It also gives on-call responders a compact first stop.

## Scope

- Generate a separate dashboard from repository code with Runtime, Poll Scheduling, API/Collector Outcomes, Snapshot Freshness, Metrics Delivery, Log Shipping, HTTP Admission, Rules, and Build sections.
- Create a distinct generated recording/alert namespace or group layout for exporter self-health without duplicating operational firewall alerts.
- Keep only a compact exporter-health summary and link on the main dashboard.
- Use the generated self-metric inventory gate and per-instance identity contracts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A generated, version-controlled self-observability dashboard imports cleanly and is linked from the main dashboard.
- [ ] Every supported self-metric is covered or explicitly exempted with a reason.
- [ ] Panels distinguish poll attempt, retained-content age, sink delivery, queue pressure, and handler admission semantics.
- [ ] Rules are grouped/named so self-health and firewall-operational alerts cannot be confused.
- [ ] Multi-instance selection and disappearance behavior have deterministic tests.
- [ ] Repository generation gates and live visual/query validation pass.

## Dependencies and risks

- Sequence after stable logship instance identity and the self-metric inventory contract.
- Panel/rule fixes may land incrementally, but the dashboard must not duplicate ownership of the same generated artifacts across parallel lanes.

## Duplicate verdict

No dedicated artifact exists in the repository or live Grafana. Existing Diagnostics/Log Shipping tabs are operational-dashboard sections, not the requested separation.

## Live verification

- Grafana Cloud stack `m7kni` was inspected read-only on 2026-07-25 using Grafana 13.2.0.

## Clean programme pause status

Queued under #451; no issue-specific implementation has started. No metric/interface contract is frozen and there are no tests, source edits, generated dashboard/rule/runbook changes, live Grafana writes, or local half-changes for this child.

The clean pause baseline is `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`: local `main`, `origin/main`, and remote main match, the worktree is clean, and all eight exact-SHA workflows are terminal-success. Resume only after #450 reaches a clean disposition and after rereading this child and #451 in full. The #428/#429 priority mismatch and #419 navigation dependency remain explicit pre-implementation reconciliation items.

Parent receipt: https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/451#issuecomment-5085202800

## Inherited from #419: the UID is frozen, and one flag finishes #419's criterion 2

#419 froze this dashboard's UID ahead of it existing, per the owner's 2026-07-27
decision, and recorded it in the new registry `grafana/uids.py`:

```python
HEALTH_UID = "opnsense-exporter-health"   # exists=False — RESERVED
```

Two consequences for this issue, both enforced by tests today:

1. **`uids.dash_url()` raises on a reserved destination**, so nothing can link here
   until this dashboard is generated. That is deliberate: a link to a UID that 404s is
   the broken navigation #419's own criteria forbid.
2. **#419's acceptance criterion "a selected instance and time range survive navigation
   between main and self-observability dashboards" is carried by this issue.** To
   finish it, in the same commit that generates this dashboard:
   - set `exists=True` on the `HEALTH_UID` entry in `grafana/uids.py`;
   - add the main-to-self link (`uids.dashboard_link(...)` in
     `build_dashboard.add_navigation`) and the self-to-main link on this dashboard;
   - use the same UID as `metadata.name` for the generated manifest.

`grafana/tests/test_links.py::test_reserved_destinations_emit_no_link` fails today if a
link is emitted early, and stops applying the moment the flag flips — so the ordering
is enforced rather than remembered.

## Premise re-verified at `bf581a7`, and the design is now unblocked

Re-checked every blocker against current main (the audit baseline `52ef4b2` is ~100 commits behind). All three are still live and are exactly as epic #451 recorded:

| Blocker | Where | Still true |
|---|---|---|
| The builder can emit only ONE dashboard | `OUT` is a module-level literal (`build_dashboard.py:29`); `main()` writes exactly one manifest; `DASH_NAME` (`:872`) overrides only `metadata.name`, so a second invocation overwrites the same file | yes |
| Splitting content breaks `make grafana-check` | `coverage(b)` joins `b._exprs` for a single `Builder`, with no cross-dashboard aggregation — moving Diagnostics/Log Shipping panels out makes their metrics report MISSING on the main dashboard | yes |
| `organize_tabs` rejects any leaf set that is not its fixed one | builds `expected` from the module-level `TAB_GROUPS` and raises `dashboard leaf assignment mismatch` otherwise | yes |

Two figures in the body are stale and should not be trusted: the live rule count is **42 alerts + 14 recording** (the "45 healthy rules" was already wrong when written), and self-metric coverage is no longer excluded.

### What changed underneath this issue

**#428 landed in `bf581a7` and satisfies the "use the generated self-metric inventory gate" scope line outright.** `docs/metrics/self-metrics.md` is generated by AST-scanning the source (`scripts/docgen/selfmetrics.go`) and feeds `load_catalogue()`, so all 45 self-metrics are now gated — coverage went 838/838 to 869/869. The acceptance criterion "every supported self-metric is covered or explicitly exempted with a reason" is therefore already enforced by machinery; this issue inherits it rather than having to build it.

That also raises the stakes on the coverage blocker: with self-metrics now IN the catalogue, moving their panels to a second dashboard without fixing `coverage()` would red the build immediately rather than silently.

### Frozen design

**1. Make the coverage gate a union, not a per-Builder property.** This is the load-bearing change and it should land FIRST, on its own, while both dashboards still exist as one:

```python
def coverage(*builders) -> list:
    blob = "\n".join(expr for b in builders for expr in b._exprs)
```

`main()` then builds every dashboard and runs ONE gate over the union. A metric charted anywhere in the family counts as covered, which is the correct semantic — the gate asks "is this metric visible to an operator", not "is it on this particular file".

**2. Parameterise the single-dashboard assumptions.** `OUT`, `TAB_GROUPS` and the `metadata.name`/uid become per-dashboard values rather than module constants — a small `DashboardSpec` (uid, name, title, output path, tab groups, build function) that `main()` iterates. `organize_tabs` takes its expected leaf set from the spec it is organising instead of reading the module global. That turns "a second invocation overwrites the same file" into "each spec writes its own file", with the strict leaf-assignment check preserved per dashboard rather than weakened.

**3. The split.** Move **Diagnostics + Log Shipping** to the health dashboard. **Leave Recording Rules on the main dashboard** — those are precomputed *operational* signals (firewall, gateway, DNS rates and ratios), not exporter self-health, so they do not match this epic's own scope line ("not firewall domain health"). Flagged to the owner in #451 as an open scoping question; proceeding on that reading unless told otherwise, because the alternative moves firewall data onto a dashboard titled "exporter health".

**4. The link, and #419's reserved contract.** #419 is closed and deliberately left this hook: `HEALTH_UID = "opnsense-exporter-health"` is registered in `grafana/uids.py` with `exists=False`, and `test_links.py::test_reserved_destinations_emit_no_link` fails if a link is emitted before the destination exists. **Flipping `exists=True` must happen in the same commit that generates the dashboard**, never before. The main dashboard keeps a compact exporter-health summary row plus that link, per the scope line.

**5. Rule namespace.** Self-health alerts move to their own generated group/folder so they cannot be confused with firewall-operational ones. Note the ordering dependency with #430, which is in flight and is changing every rule's `runbook_url` to a per-rule anchor — sequence this after it lands to avoid both rewriting `build_rules.py`'s emit path at once.

### Sequencing

1. coverage union (independent, safe, unblocks everything else)
2. `DashboardSpec` refactor with the split still not performed — pure refactor, byte-identical `dashboard.json` output, which is exactly what `make grafana-check` proves
3. the actual split + `HEALTH_UID` flip + main-dashboard summary row, one commit
4. rule namespace, after #430

Step 2 producing a byte-identical artifact is the checkpoint worth insisting on: it separates "the machinery changed" from "the content moved", and `git diff --exit-code` on `dashboard.json` is already in `make grafana-check` to prove it.

## Steps 3 and 4 landed — #431 complete

| Step | SHA | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `076971a` | coverage union across builders |
| 2 | `474605f` | `DashboardSpec` + parameterised `organize_tabs`, byte-identical |
| 3 | `a486d0c` | the split: `dashboard-health.json`, cross-links, summary row, `HEALTH_UID` flip |
| 4 | `4a33aa5` | self-health alerts routed to their own Grafana folder |

Full gate green at both commits (`go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-test`, `make grafana-check`).

### The split

`dashboard-health.json`, uid `opnsense-exporter-health`, holds **Diagnostics + Log Shipping** — 49 panels, 2 tabs, deliberately flat (no domain layer: burying Diagnostics one click deeper on the dashboard an operator opens *because something is already wrong* would be a regression). No separate Overview tab either; Diagnostics already opens on scrape health.

The main dashboard keeps a three-tile **Exporter Health** row on Overview — failing collectors, stalest collector data, OPNsense API error rate — each linking through. That row is the tripwire the split would otherwise remove: a reader looking at a flat graph has no reason to suspect the collector stopped rather than the firewall going quiet.

**#419's remaining criterion is discharged.** `HEALTH_UID` flipped `exists=True` in `a486d0c`, the same commit that generates the dashboard, and both cross-links carry `${__url_time_range}` and `${opnsense_instance:queryparam}`.

### Three things the work turned up

**Two links were already pointing at a tab that moved.** `tabs/logs.py` linked to `Observability > Diagnostics` on the main dashboard. `test_links.py` now resolves every `dtab` against the **destination** dashboard's real layout instead of the source's, which is what caught them; `uids.to_tab()` gained a `uid` parameter so a health-dashboard tab module can link to its own tabs.

**`promqlcheck` rejected the second dashboard** as `unrecognized rule manifest kind "Dashboard"` — it routed arguments by position. It now routes by manifest `kind`, and errors if a run checked no dashboard at all.

**Roughly fifteen test modules would have silently stopped checking the 49 moved panels.** Panel descriptions, sentinel scoping, link context, threshold defaults and the coverage gate all asserted properties of "every panel we ship" via `build_all()`. All moved to the family. The sentinel contract and `dashboard-stats.json` went family-wide too — the contract governs tab-module authors and tab modules now build onto either dashboard, and the stats file already carried a family-wide metric count, so a primary-scoped tab count would have paired the two in one sentence and made it false.

### Recording rules: the owner's per-rule sort, and its result

Sorted per rule as instructed, not relocated as a tab. **All 14 bundled recording rules derive from firewall metrics (`opnsense_*`), none from exporter self-metrics (`opnsense_exporter_*`)**, so the self-observability set is empty and the Recording rules tab stays whole on the main dashboard.

That finding is now machinery rather than a comment: `tests/test_recording_rules.py` classifies each rule and fails if a self-metric-derived recording rule is charted on the main dashboard, with a control asserting the classifier discriminates (so it cannot pass by always returning False).

### Step 4 — alert folders

12 of 42 alerts are exporter-health and now generate into `opnsense-exporter-health-alerts`; the other 30 stay in `opnsense-alerts`. Membership is **declared** per rule, not inferred, because `OPNsenseExporterDown` and `OPNsenseExporterInstanceMissing` fire on `opnsense_up` — not an `opnsense_exporter_*` metric, but entirely a statement about the exporter. `is_self_health_expr()` is the mechanical cross-check: a rule built purely from self-metrics that forgets the flag fails the tests.

### Deployment, unchanged and still owner-gated

The alert manifests remain **not deployed**, now 58 of them across two folders. `build_rules.py` without `--stack` emits no routing labels, so pushing this output over rules created with `--stack` would strip their IRM routing labels — `grafana/README.md` states that at the push instructions now rather than leaving it as tribal knowledge.

The dashboards also need deploying: `dashboard-health.json` is new, and the main dashboard's summary row links to it, so importing only one leaves a link that 404s.

**Suggested title:** `grafana(alerts): generate complete per-rule runbooks and instance-aware summaries`

**Theme:** Runbook links, documentation drift, notification actionability

**Priority:** P2

**Confidence:** High

**Evidence**

- All 31 alerts receive the same `runbook_url`, `grafana/README.md#alerts` (`grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:339-340`).
- That target is a short inventory table, not remediation guidance (`grafana/README.md:124-167`).
- The source contains 31 alert definitions and 14 recording rules, but the README table has only 19 alert rows and the recording section names only 8 rules (`grafana/README.md:126-146,169-174`).
- Docgen pins only numeric counts; it does not generate the alert or recording inventory (`scripts/docgen/stats.go:45-77,93-100,134-137`).
- Twenty alert summaries omit `opnsense_instance`, including primary gateway, endpoint, service, certificate, VPN, CARP, and logship notifications. The label usually survives on domain metrics, but the human-facing summary is ambiguous across the supported multi-exporter mode.

**Operator value**

During an incident, the supplied link often does not even name the firing rule and never gives validation/remediation steps. Multi-firewall notifications can require opening the full label set before the affected box is identifiable.

**Scope**

- Generate an exact alert/recording inventory from `RULES`/`RECORDING`.
- Give every alert a stable rule-specific anchor or page with meaning, checks, likely causes, and recovery verification.

Wired into `make grafana-check`.

Reported by the tool: `validated 976 Prometheus targets, 103 variable queries, 10 annotation queries and 56 rule expressions`.

Node type routes on `model.datasource.type`, the same field Grafana routes on: `prometheus` is parsed, `__expr__` is skipped because a threshold/reduce node is a server-side expression rather than PromQL. **Anything else is a hard error, never a skip** — this tool has already shipped one bug of exactly that shape (the variable-kind decoder hit a `TextVariable`, validated *nothing*, and still exited 0), so an unrecognised kind, a missing `expr`, or an unknown datasource type all fail loudly.

Verified both failure paths independently rather than trusting the happy path: a corrupted copy of a **real** manifest (adjacent selectors, so the fixture has the shape the tool actually meets) and an unrecognised datasource type. Both exit 1 with the offending expression printed.

Rule expressions carry no Grafana template tokens today — I checked every manifest. Substitution is wired in anyway so a future rule using one doesn't regress.

Two figures in the body are stale, neither changing the substance:

- **The suite is 191 tests, not 16** (198 as of `4c529e3`). The last acceptance criterion should read "runs the builder suite exactly once" without the count.
- **45 expressions → 56** (42 alerts + 14 recording). The rule count was already wrong at audit time; `build_rules.py` had not changed since `52ef4b2`.

The double-run finding **is still accurate**: `grafana-test` is both its own CI step and a prerequisite of `grafana-check`, so the whole suite plus the Go tests still run twice per CI job.

## What remains

- [ ] Timeline tests for transient vs sustained endpoint errors across poll cadences
- [ ] Multi-instance tests: one missing exporter, one stalled log pipeline, whole-query No Data
- [ ] Manifest-contract assertions (severity, routing labels, `noDataState`, `execErrState`, pending duration, per-instance summaries, resolvable runbook anchors)
- [ ] Explicit modelling of Grafana-only MissingSeries/NoData behaviour
- [ ] CI runs the builder suite exactly once

Scoping note from the revalidation sweep: the manifest-contract half is a natural extension of `validate_manifests.py`'s existing structural-assertion style, but the timeline/MissingSeries half is genuinely net-new — `rg promtool` returns nothing repo-wide and there is no rule-evaluation harness of any kind to build on. Worth treating as two separate pieces of work.

Related: #427 shipped the MissingSeries *rule* in `4c529e3`, verified live. The behavioural test that would prove it in CI is the outstanding work here.

Partial delivery: the **manifest-contract half** landed in `55d3ce9`.

`validate_manifests.py` now contract-checks the Grafana-specific fields no PromQL syntax check can reach — `severity`, `execErrState`, a real Go duration in `for`, the `--stack` routing-label contract (`page` requires `domain`, is the string `"true"` not the JSON boolean, only rides `severity=critical`, never appears on a recording rule), `opnsense_instance` preservation in every `... by (...)` clause, `{{ $labels.X }}` tokens that name a label the query actually preserves, and `runbook_url` anchors resolved structurally against the real headings (no network request). 32 new tests in `grafana/tests/test_manifest_contract.py`, each mutation-checked by breaking the thing it asserts.

- [x] Every alert and recording expression syntax-checked from `RULES`/`RECORDING` — landed earlier in `7db33f3`
- [x] Manifest tests assert severity, stack routing labels, `noDataState`, `execErrState`, pending duration, per-instance labels/summaries, and resolvable runbook anchors

- [ ] Timeline tests covering transient vs sustained endpoint errors across poll cadences
- [ ] Multi-instance tests covering one missing exporter, one stalled log pipeline, whole-query No Data
- [ ] Grafana-only MissingSeries/NoData behaviour modelled explicitly

**Staying open for the behaviour harness**, which is genuinely net-new — `rg promtool` still returns nothing repo-wide and there is no rule-evaluation harness of any kind. Two stale figures in the body for the record: the suite is 198 tests, not 16, and the rule count is 42 alerts + 14 recording, not 45.

## Behaviour harness landed — `b5afdac`, #429 complete

All three remaining criteria are now covered, by a Python harness over the generated manifests rather than by promtool.

- [x] Timeline tests covering transient vs sustained endpoint errors across poll cadences
- [x] Multi-instance tests: one missing exporter, one stalled log pipeline, whole-query No Data
- [x] Grafana-only MissingSeries/NoData behaviour modelled explicitly

### Why not promtool, confirmed rather than assumed

promtool evaluates **Prometheus** rules; this project ships **Grafana-managed** ones, and every remaining criterion is about behaviour promtool has no concept of. The sister pollers were checked for prior art per the owner's note — `tailscale2otel` and `graph2otel` have none for this; their only overlap is `promqlcheck` testdata, the same tool already here.

### What shipped

`grafana/alerts/ruleeval.py` models the state machine — pending period, `noDataState`, `execErrState`, MissingSeries eviction — and `grafana/tests/test_rule_behaviour.py` runs the **42 generated manifests** through it. Reading the manifests rather than `build_rules.py`'s source dicts is deliberate: the manifest is what Grafana evaluates, so a bug in the emit path is in scope.

**It is explicitly not a PromQL evaluator.** It is fed query *results*. Reimplementing `increase()` and `unless` in Python would be a second, worse Prometheus whose disagreements with the real one would surface as confident wrong answers, and every interesting failure here is on the Grafana side of the query anyway.

Semantics were **fetched from the Grafana 13.1 / Grafana Cloud alerting docs**, not recalled — `alert-rule-evaluation`, `alert-rule-evaluation/stale-alert-instances`, `best-practices/missing-data`. The load-bearing one: a missing dimension holds its last state for **two** evaluation intervals, then resolves with `grafana_state_reason: MissingSeries`. That is a different thing from `NoData`, which is "no dimensions at all".

### The finding worth reading

**`OPNsenseExporterDown` has `noDataState: Alerting`, which reads like "page when a firewall goes away", and does not do that.** With any other firewall still reporting, the query still returns data, so the vanished one is a stale *series*: held two intervals, then resolved. Nothing pages. There is now a test saying so, sitting next to one showing `OPNsenseExporterInstanceMissing` does catch it — which is the concrete demonstration of why #427 was needed and is now regression-protected.

Other properties pinned, most as sweeps over every rule rather than one hand-picked example:

- a breach shorter than the pending period never fires; a sustained one fires **exactly** when the period elapses
- a flapping breach restarts the pending period rather than accumulating
- an errored evaluation does not resolve a firing instance (otherwise a datasource hiccup sends a resolved notification for a real outage)
- an inventory of which rules page on a whole-query No Data, so adding `noDataState: Alerting` is a decision rather than a slip

### Mutation-checking, including one test that was worthless

The two-interval hold test originally read the interval from `ruleeval.MISSING_SERIES_INTERVALS` — the constant it was meant to pin. Changing that constant to 3 left the test **green**, verified by doing exactly that. The number is now a literal with the doc reference beside it and the mutation fails as it should. An off-by-one in the pending comparison fails 47 subtests; removing the breach reset fails the flapping test.

Suite is 302 tests. Full gate green at `b5afdac`.

**Suggested title:** `grafana(alerts): detect a missing exporter instance when other instances still report`

**Theme:** No-data semantics, multi-instance behavior, critical paging

**Priority:** P1

**Confidence:** High

**Evidence**

- The alert query is the bare multi-dimensional vector `opnsense_up`, threshold `<1`, with `noDataState: Alerting` and a 15-minute pending period (`grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:35-44`; generated manifest `grafana/alerts/grafana-managed/opnsense-exporter-down.json:13-27,29-47`).
- The dashboard explicitly supports multiple exporters through `opnsense_instance` (`grafana/README.md:51-59`).
- Grafana distinguishes:
  - **No Data**: the rule returns no series at all.
  - **MissingSeries**: one dimension disappears while another still returns.
  Missing alert instances are retained briefly, then resolved/evicted rather than transitioned through the rule's `noDataState`. Official docs:
  - https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/alerting/guides/missing-data/
  - https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/alerting/fundamentals/alert-rule-evaluation/stale-alert-instances/
- Therefore, with exporters `edge-a` and `edge-b`, complete loss of `edge-a` while `edge-b` remains produces MissingSeries, not No Data. The critical rule silently loses the `edge-a` alert instance.

**Operator value**

A single firewall/exporter can disappear without the critical/page signal that the README promises. The blind spot becomes more likely as soon as the advertised multi-exporter mode is used.

**Scope**

- Add a per-`opnsense_instance` missing-series detector, either as a companion alert or a fleet-safe extension of the current rule.
- Preserve the existing `opnsense_up == 0` behavior for API unreachability.
- Preserve a useful `opnsense_instance` label and instance-naming summary.
- Document decommission/maintenance behavior.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A two-instance regression case proves that disappearance of only one instance reaches Pending/Alerting rather than `Normal (MissingSeries)` eviction.
- [ ] A total-fleet disappearance still alerts.
- [ ] `opnsense_up=0` for a reporting exporter still alerts after the existing reboot-tolerance window.
- [ ] A planned instance removal has an explicit operational path (silence/mute, expected-instance inventory, or a documented historical-baseline expiry).
- [ ] The generated manifest and README no longer imply that `noDataState: Alerting` alone covers every per-instance disappearance.

**Dependencies / decisions**

- Decide whether expected instances come from a static inventory or a historical `present_over_time(...) unless ...` baseline. A historical baseline is self-contained but deliberately alerts for some time after a decommission.
- Notification routing remains stack-owned.

**Risks**

- Dynamic missing-series detection can false-alert after a planned removal unless the baseline horizon and maintenance workflow are explicit.

**Duplicate verdict**

Not a duplicate. #95 addressed the removed portable rule and concluded the Grafana-managed variant covered exporter death. That conclusion is correct only for whole-query No Data, not one missing dimension. #372 verified current rule health/deployment, not this failure mode.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.

## What landed

`OPNsenseExporterInstanceMissing` (critical, `for: 10m`, `noDataState: Ok`):

```promql
max by (opnsense_instance) (present_over_time(opnsense_up[1h]))
  unless on(opnsense_instance) opnsense_up
```

**Decision on the dependency the issue flagged — historical baseline, not a static inventory.** A configured expected-instance list avoids alerting after a decommission, but it silently protects nothing when someone forgets to add a box, i.e. it fails open on exactly the event this rule exists to catch. The historical form is self-contained and a new exporter protects itself the moment it has been up an hour. The cost — up to 1h of alerting after a planned removal — is stated in both the rule description and the README rather than left for an operator to discover from a page.

**Division of responsibility with the existing rule, stated so neither drifts:** total fleet loss is No Data and stays with `OPNsenseExporterDown` (`noDataState: Alerting`). This rule keeps `noDataState: Ok` deliberately — when everything disappears its own query returns nothing too, and Alerting here would double-page one event.

## The aggregation is load-bearing, and only live verification found it

The first version was the obvious `present_over_time(opnsense_up[1h]) unless on(opnsense_instance) opnsense_up`. Run against the live stack, the mechanism probe returned **two** series for the single real instance — identical except one carried `service_version="59c4dfe"`, a label removed earlier the same day by #472 and still inside the 1h lookback.

`present_over_time` yields one series per distinct **label set**, not per instance. So any label churn in the lookback window — a version label changing, a relabel, a scrape-config edit — would have made one missing exporter raise one alert instance per historical label set, paging repeatedly for a single event. `max by (opnsense_instance)` collapses it. Pinned by `test_it_raises_one_alert_per_instance_not_per_historical_label_set`.

- [x] `opnsense_up=0` for a reporting exporter still alerts after the existing window — `OPNsenseExporterDown` untouched
- [x] Planned removal has an explicit operational path — documented decommission horizon (1h, self-resolving) in the rule description and README, with "silence it until then"
- [x] Generated manifest and README no longer imply `noDataState: Alerting` alone covers every per-instance disappearance — the README now opens the Alerts section by spelling out the No Data vs MissingSeries distinction

Against `grafanacloud-prom`, the real single-instance stack:

```
# no false positive on a healthy stack
max by (opnsense_instance) (present_over_time(opnsense_up[1h]))
  unless on(opnsense_instance) opnsense_up
=> (empty)

# mechanism: force the right-hand side empty to simulate the instance vanishing
max by (opnsense_instance) (present_over_time(opnsense_up[1h]))
  unless on(opnsense_instance) (opnsense_up unless on() vector(1))
=> {opnsense_instance="opnsense"} 1
```

Exactly one series, carrying the instance label, value 1 against a `gt 0` threshold — so it fires and names the box.

## Gate

`go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues, both modules), `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check` — all green. 198 Grafana tests. Rule inventory 41 → 42 alerts; the identity guard's expression count and the README's docgen-pinned count both moved with it.

Related: `7db33f3` landed the first acceptance criterion of #429, so this rule's expression is now syntax-checked in CI rather than only at deploy time.

body:
**Suggested title:** `server: instrument metrics-handler admission, latency, and gather failures`

**Theme:** Exporter serving-path self-observability

**Priority:** P3

**Confidence:** High

**Evidence**

- The handler enforces a 40-request admission cap and returns 503 on overflow (`internal/server/metrics.go:27-39,100-110`).
- Gather errors use `ContinueOnError` and are logged as warnings while a partial scrape is served (`internal/server/metrics.go:157-182`).
- The handler struct has no request/rejection/duration/gather-error collectors (`internal/server/metrics.go:62-80`), and there are no matching self-metrics elsewhere in the tree.
- #324 added the bound; #81 added partial-gather logging. Neither made those paths queryable.

**Operator value**

After recovery, there is no metric showing that admission rejected scrapes or that gather errors silently removed families from otherwise successful responses. Logs are the only evidence.

**Scope**

- Add bounded-label metrics for in-flight requests, completions/status, admission rejections, duration, and gather errors/partial responses.
- Add a small Diagnostics row and actionable warnings for sustained rejections or gather failures.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A forced 41st request increments an admission-rejection counter labelled with a bounded reason/status vocabulary.
- [ ] In-flight gauge and request duration are tested without unbounded path/client labels.
- [ ] A duplicate-series gather error increments a partial-gather counter while the handler still returns the intended partial response.
- [ ] Diagnostics displays saturation, rejections, and partial-gather activity.
- [ ] A warning rule is added only if it is actionable and does not duplicate the external scraper's target `up` alert.
- [ ] New metrics enter the self-metric coverage gate from `test(grafana): generate and gate the exporter self-metric inventory`.

**Dependencies / decisions**

- Best landed after or with `test(grafana): generate and gate the exporter self-metric inventory` so these metrics cannot become another manually uncovered family.

**Risks**

- Instrumenting `/metrics` from the same registry is self-referential: the in-flight gauge naturally includes the scrape collecting it. Document that and avoid metrics whose collection itself mutates cardinality.

**Duplicate verdict**

Not a duplicate. #324 bounded the path and #81 made gather failures survivable/logged; this is the missing observability follow-on.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

## Clean programme pause status

Queued under #451; no issue-specific implementation has started. No metric/interface contract is frozen and there are no tests, source edits, generated dashboard/rule/runbook changes, live Grafana writes, or local half-changes for this child.

The clean pause baseline is `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`: local `main`, `origin/main`, and remote main match, the worktree is clean, and all eight exact-SHA workflows are terminal-success. Resume only after #450 reaches a clean disposition and after rereading this child and #451 in full. The #428/#429 priority mismatch and #419 navigation dependency remain explicit pre-implementation reconciliation items.

Parent receipt: https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/451#issuecomment-5085202800

Implementation done locally, pending the wiring pass. Recording the one open decision and its answer here, since it was deliberately escalated rather than guessed.

## Metrics

Five, all on `internal/server/metrics.go`, all constant-named so `scripts/docgen/selfmetrics.go` can see them (#428 made an unresolvable name a hard build failure):

| Metric | Type | Bounded labels |
|---|---|---|
| `opnsense_exporter_server_metrics_requests_in_flight` | Gauge | — |
| `opnsense_exporter_server_metrics_requests_total` | Counter | `status` ∈ ok, bad_request, internal_error |
| `opnsense_exporter_server_metrics_request_duration_seconds` | Histogram | `status`, same three |
| `opnsense_exporter_server_metrics_requests_rejected_total` | Counter | `reason` ∈ in_flight_limit |
| `opnsense_exporter_server_metrics_gather_errors_total` | Counter | `reason` ∈ collector_error |

Every label value is pre-initialised to zero, so an absent series never has to be read as either "never happened" or "this build predates the label". A rejected request is counted on the rejection counter and NOT on `requests_total` — admission and completion are separate axes, and a test pins that they do not double-count.

Registered through `logship.SelfMetricsRegisterer(selfMetricsRegistry, instanceLabel)` — the same wrapper the annotation writer uses — so the family **carries `opnsense_instance`**. That was checked against `main.go`'s wiring before the dashboard selectors were written, specifically to avoid re-creating #466, where `opnsense_exporter_otlp_*` is filtered on a label it does not have and the panels are structurally always empty.

`promhttp.HandlerOpts.Registry` was deliberately left unwired. It auto-instruments the handler instance it is given, but `HandlerFor` is constructed fresh per request here (per-request collector-view filtering needs it), so its metrics would either double-register or measure a single request's lifetime. Cumulative counters have to live on the persistent handler struct.

The self-referential in-flight gauge is documented rather than worked around: it is incremented before `promhttp.HandlerFor` runs, so it always reads ≥1 in the very response that reports it. Any trick to hide that just moves the fencepost, and the alternatives touch collection — which is the one thing the issue's risk note says not to do.

## The alert-rule question, answered

The criterion says add a warning rule **only if it is actionable and does not duplicate the external scraper's target `up` alert**. The two candidates are not equivalent, and only one survives that test:

- **Admission rejections — NO rule.** A rejected scrape returns 503, which makes the scrape itself fail, which makes `up` go 0. `OPNsenseExporterDown` already covers it. A second rule would fire on the same event with a different name, which is precisely the duplication the criterion forbids. The rejection counter still earns its place as the panel that *explains* an `up` outage rather than as a second page.
- **Gather errors — YES, a warning rule.** This is the genuinely invisible case, and it is the reason #81 made partial gathers survivable in the first place: `ContinueOnError` drops the failing family and serves a **200** with the rest. `up` stays 1, the scrape looks healthy, and metrics have silently disappeared from an otherwise-green dashboard. Nothing else in the rule set can see that.

So: one warning rule on a sustained non-zero `rate(opnsense_exporter_server_metrics_gather_errors_total[...])`, warning severity rather than critical because the exporter is still serving and the correct response is investigation, not a page.

It is **not in this change** because `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py` is currently being rewritten by #430 (per-rule runbook anchors touch every rule's emit path), and two lanes rewriting that file at once is exactly the ownership collision #431 warns about. It lands immediately after #430.

body:
## Problem

The dashboard advertises multi-exporter selection, but several diagnostic queries aggregate without `opnsense_instance` and 24 tables hide the field. Some may intentionally present fleet totals; others may merge unrelated firewall rows into an ambiguous result.

## Evidence

- The source audit found multiple diagnostics aggregating away instance identity and 24 tables hiding the instance field.
- The current live stack exposes one logical instance, so visual inspection cannot distinguish intentional fleet aggregation from a latent two-instance bug.
- Missing-series alert behavior already demonstrates that single-instance testing is insufficient for fleet contracts.

## Operator value

A two-instance semantic audit makes All/multi-select behavior explicit and prevents data from different firewalls being presented as one interface, gateway, service, or diagnostic row.

## Scope

- Build a deterministic two-instance dashboard/query fixture with overlapping interface/service names.
- Classify each merged query/table as fleet aggregate, per-instance diagnostic, or intentionally hidden identity.
- File or implement only the bounded corrections proven ambiguous.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Every query that removes/hides instance identity has an explicit classification. **(111 merging panels + 24 identity-hiding tables = 119, classified; see the audit comment. Remaining criteria require implementation and are filed as #468.)**
- [x] Per-instance diagnostics retain identity through aggregation and table transforms.
- [x] Intentional fleet totals are labelled as such in title/description.
- [x] A semantic test catches cross-instance row merging for representative panels.
- [x] The final issue comment records corrected and accepted panels.

## Dependencies and risks

- Research first; do not blindly add instance labels to intentional fleet totals.
- Coordinate with Prometheus/Loki sentinel instance scoping.

## Duplicate verdict

No prior issue audits the current v2 dashboard with overlapping two-instance fixtures.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.
