Parent receipt: https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/450#issuecomment-5085202739

## 2026-07-26 compatibility reproduction

The exact historical v2beta1 artifact reproduces #22 on Grafana 12.4 with HTTP 422 and the reported interval-variable conflicts. Current schema v2 is unsupported by Grafana 11/12. The historical classic dashboard imports successfully through `/api/dashboards/db` and reads back on pinned Grafana 11.5.0 and 12.4.0 containers; all temporary containers were removed.

The supported direction is a generated bounded classic dashboard from shared query/panel sources, with explicit degradation: no TabsLayout and no conditional rendering. Do not copy or hand-maintain the 711-panel JSON. The exact bounded panel inventory must be frozen before TDD, then CI must POST/import and GET/read back stable UID/title/panel/variable contracts on both pinned versions. No implementation was started.

## Closed by [`8e49f4e`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/8e49f4e), with a CI fix in [`3f6ac71`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/3f6ac71)

### Criterion 1: the #22 failure reproduced EXACTLY, and the current artifact's failure is worse

First, a locating correction for anyone following the trail: the report is **not** the body of #22 — #22 is Renovate's Dependency Dashboard. It is a comment on it by **@ehnwebmaster**, 2026-03-20, and the file it names (`deploy/grafana/dashboard.json`) was deleted months ago.

That historical artifact still exists in git at [`da5a351`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/da5a351) (`apiVersion: dashboard.grafana.app/v2beta1`, 4 variables, the last an `IntervalVariable`). POSTed to a pinned `grafana/grafana:12.4.0` container's CRD route, it returns **HTTP 422** with the reporter's error, word for word:

```text
Dashboard.dashboard.grafana.app "opnsense-exporter-comprehensive" is invalid:
  [DashboardSpec.variables: Invalid value: incompatible list lengths (0 and 4),
   DashboardSpec.variables.3.kind: Invalid value: conflicting values "AdhocVariable" and "IntervalVariable",
   DashboardSpec.variables.3.kind: Invalid value: conflicting values "ConstantVariable" and "IntervalVariable",
   ...
```

So the report was real and is now fully attributed: a v2beta1 `IntervalVariable` that 12.4's schema could not disambiguate.

**The current artifact fails differently, and two of the three routes fail dishonestly.** All verified against pinned containers on 2026-07-27:

| Grafana | route | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 11.5.0 | `POST /api/dashboards/db` | **400** `Dashboard title cannot be empty` — v2 keeps the title under `spec`, so the error names a symptom and hides the cause |
| 12.4.0 | `POST /api/dashboards/db` | **200**, then the dashboard renders **0 panels, 0 variables**. The v2 body is stored verbatim and ignored |
| 12.4.0 | `POST /apis/dashboard.grafana.app/{v1beta1,v2alpha1,v2beta1}/...` | **400** `no kind "Dashboard" is registered for version "dashboard.grafana.app/v2"` |

The 12.4 classic-API case is the one worth carrying forward: **a silent success that produces an empty dashboard**. An operator has no error to search for. This corrects the 2026-07-26 reconciliation comment on this issue, which recorded the current artifact as reproducing #22's 422 — it does not; that 422 belongs to the historical file, and the current one has its own three distinct failures.

### Criterion 2: generated from shared sources

`grafana/build_compat.py` reads `grafana/dashboard.json` and emits `grafana/dashboard-compat.json` in classic schema. **Nothing is authored.** `make compat` regenerates; `make grafana-check` fails if it is stale, alongside `dashboard.json` itself. The "do not copy 711 panels into a second hand-edited source" constraint is not just respected but *checkable*: `test_it_is_derived_from_the_canonical_artifact` asserts every panel title and every query string in the compat file exists in the canonical one.

### Criterion 4: the bounded degradation, and why omission beats copying

Two things classic schema does not have:

1. **No TabsLayout.** Each tab's rows flatten in order, with the tab name prefixed onto the first row of the group so a reader can still tell where a row came from.
2. **No conditionalRendering — and this is the one that changes what an operator sees.** 31 of the 41 leaf tabs and 154 rows are gated on a feature sentinel, so a box without the CrowdSec plugin never sees a CrowdSec tab. Copied into classic they would be permanently visible and permanently empty, and **"No data" on a plugin you do not run is indistinguishable from a broken exporter**. So they are OMITTED.

The compat artifact therefore carries exactly the **unconditional** panels: **187 of the canonical 738**, in 60 rows across 10 sections — Overview, System & Resources, Services/Cron/DynDNS, Certificates, Interfaces, Gateways & WAN, Routing & Neighbors, Protocol Stats, Firewall & PF, Diagnostics. All 106 variables convert, including the ~100 hidden presence sentinels, which stay hidden.

**The boundary is computed, not listed.** It is derived at build time from the canonical artifact's own gating, so a tab that becomes gated leaves the compat build automatically and one that becomes unconditional joins it. There is no second inventory to drift. This is why the frozen-inventory step the 2026-07-26 comment called for is satisfied by a rule rather than a list.

### Criterion 3: CI imports and reads back on both declared versions

New `grafana-compat` job in `ci.yml`, inside the **required** `ci-success` gate. It regenerates the artifact first (verifying a stale committed file would pass while the generator is broken), then runs `grafana/verify_compat_import.sh`, which for each of 11.5.0 and 12.4.0 starts the container, POSTs to `/api/dashboards/db`, and **reads the dashboard back** to assert uid, title, panel count, variable count, that no panel type came back unknown, and that no panel lost its targets.

The read-back is not ceremony: **an accepted POST proves nothing**, because Grafana migrates `schemaVersion` on save and can store a panel it cannot render. Both legs green locally and in CI: 200 on import, **247 panels and 106 variables intact** on each (247 = 187 panels + 60 row headers).

**A real bug the CI run caught that local testing could not.** The job's first run failed with `curl: Argument list too long` (exit 126) before Grafana saw anything: the artifact is ~2 MB, which fits under macOS's `ARG_MAX` and not under Linux's, so `--data-binary "$body"` could only ever fail in CI. Fixed in `3f6ac71` by writing the body to a file. Two adjacent defects fixed with it: the read-back check used `$?` after a heredoc under `set -e`, so a genuine mismatch would have aborted before printing the summary and without testing the second version; and the script header pointed at a workflow file that does not exist.

Also from that run, and filed separately rather than absorbed: **#469**, `fuzz-smoke`'s `-timeout=45s` being consumed by build time, which failed the required check on `3f6ac71` for a reason unrelated to it. Fixed in `0a838db`.

### Local structural tests (run on every commit, no docker needed)

`grafana/tests/test_compat_dashboard.py`, 11 tests: classic schema with **no v2-only key or kind anywhere in the tree**; every panel type is one the converter maps deliberately (an unmapped viz group raises at build time rather than emitting a type Grafana 11 has never heard of); unique panel ids; every leaf keeps its targets; a Loki panel keeps the **Loki** datasource rather than the Prometheus default; the bounded set equals the recomputed unconditional set; no gated panel leaked in, compared on `(title, expr)` pairs so a reused title cannot cause a false failure; variables carry classic **integer** `refresh`/`hide` codes rather than v2 enum strings — which is the same class of defect #22 hit from the other direction; and the artifact declares its own provenance and degradation list.

### Criterion 5: #22

Reply posted linking this issue and naming the supported path. Left open: #22 is Renovate's dependency dashboard and closing it would be wrong.

### Not lowered, not over-promised

The canonical artifact is unchanged and Grafana 13 remains the target. The compat build claims **only** 11.5.0 and 12.4.0, the two versions CI actually imports into, and it uses uid `opnsense-exporter-compat` so it cannot overwrite the canonical dashboard.

### Docs

`docs/integration-dashboards.md` gains a compatibility section with the three-route failure table, `grafana/README.md` a full section covering the generator, the two degradations and the commands, and the README's Grafana-13 admonition now points 11/12 users at the compat file instead of leaving them at a dead end.

### Gate

```text
go test ./...            exit 0      CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...   exit 0
golangci-lint run ./...  0 issues    shellcheck (verify script)     0 findings
actionlint / zizmor      clean       grafana tests   144 passed, 986 subtests
make docs-check          passed      make grafana-check             passed
make compat-verify       passed on Grafana 11.5.0 and 12.4.0
```

All temporary containers removed; `docker ps -a` shows none left behind. Production Grafana untouched — every container was a local pinned image, and no dashboard was published.

## DESCOPED by owner decision — reverted in [`c89248a`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/c89248a)

The owner's call, verbatim: *"honestly we are okay with grafana 13 compatability only please given our use of dynamic dashboards!"*

So this issue closes as **not planned**. The compatibility dashboard was implemented and passing (`8e49f4e`, CI fix `3f6ac71`) before that decision arrived; it has been reverted rather than left in the tree, because a half-supported artifact is worse than none. Removed: `grafana/build_compat.py`, `grafana/dashboard-compat.json`, `grafana/tests/test_compat_dashboard.py`, `grafana/verify_compat_import.sh`, the `compat`/`compat-verify` make targets, the compat entry in the `grafana-check` staleness gate, and the `grafana-compat` job from the required CI gate.

The decision is consistent with what building it revealed: **classic schema cannot express `conditionalRendering`**, which is the dashboard's central behaviour, so 31 of the 41 leaf tabs and 154 rows had to be omitted — the artifact carried 187 of 738 panels and silently lacked IDS, HAProxy, VPN and DHCP. Maintaining an 18k-line generated artifact plus a docker-based required check for a build that omits three quarters of the dashboard is the wrong trade, and shipping it invites bug reports about missing tabs.

### What was kept, and why

The **reproduction** stays in the docs, because it cost real container runs and it protects users from misfiling a version problem as an exporter bug. `README.md`, `grafana/README.md` and `docs/integration-dashboards.md` now state that there is deliberately no schema-v1 build, and what an older Grafana actually does:

| Grafana | route | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 11.5.0 | `POST /api/dashboards/db` | **400** `Dashboard title cannot be empty` — v2 keeps the title under `spec`, so the error names a symptom rather than the cause |
| 12.4.0 | `POST /api/dashboards/db` | **200**, then the dashboard renders **0 panels and 0 variables**. The v2 body is stored verbatim and ignored, with no error anywhere |
| 12.4.0 | `POST /apis/dashboard.grafana.app/...` | **400** `no kind "Dashboard" is registered for version "dashboard.grafana.app/v2"` |

The 12.4 silent-empty case is the one worth having written down: an operator has no error to search for.

### Findings preserved for the record

- **The #22 report is a comment on Renovate's dependency dashboard, not an issue body** — easy to lose, which is why it sat. Its exact 422 (`conflicting values "AdhocVariable" and "IntervalVariable"`) reproduces byte-for-byte from the historical `deploy/grafana/dashboard.json` at [`da5a351`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/da5a351) against a pinned `grafana/grafana:12.4.0`. It was a real v2beta1 `IntervalVariable` schema defect, now moot: the current artifact has no interval variables.
- **A correction to this issue's own 2026-07-26 reconciliation comment**, which recorded the *current* artifact as reproducing that 422. It does not — the 422 belongs to the deleted historical file, and the current artifact has the three distinct failures tabled above.
- **#469 came out of this work and stands on its own** (fixed in `0a838db`): `fuzz-smoke`'s `-timeout` was being consumed by build time, failing the required check for reasons unrelated to the commit under test. Untouched by the revert.
- **A portability trap, for anyone writing a similar check later:** the ~2 MB artifact could not be POSTed via `curl --data-binary "$body"`. That fits under macOS's `ARG_MAX` and not under Linux's, so it passed locally and failed only in CI with `Argument list too long` — which reads exactly like a datasource rejection and is not one.

### #22

@ehnwebmaster has been replied to twice: first pointing at the compatibility artifact, then **corrected** once this decision landed, so the public thread now says Grafana 13+ and does not point at a file that no longer exists. #22 itself stays open — it is Renovate's dependency dashboard.

### Verified end state

```text
go test ./...            exit 0     CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...   exit 0
golangci-lint run ./...  0 issues   actionlint (ci.yml)            clean
grafana tests            133 passed, 506 subtests
make docs-check          passed     make grafana-check             passed
```

No `compat` reference remains in the Makefile, CI, tests or docs; `git grep` for the artifact is empty. All temporary Grafana containers from the earlier verification were removed.

title: feat(grafana): provide a Grafana 11 and 12 compatibility dashboard

body:
## Problem

The generated dashboard has no dashboard links or panel data links. Responders must manually reselect instance, time range, interface/device, and log filters when moving between operational metrics, self-observability, companion log views, and runbooks.

## Evidence

- The dashboard builder hard-codes empty link arrays and the generated dashboard contains zero links.
- The audited estate has separate main, firewall-log, SFP, Network Activity, Zenarmor, and future self-observability destinations.
- Grafana supports dashboard/data links with time range and template-variable propagation.

## Operator value

One-click, context-preserving navigation shortens diagnosis and prevents responders from comparing different instances or time windows by accident.

## Scope

- Define stable dashboard UIDs and a generated link helper.
- Add main-to-self, self-to-main, metrics-to-logs, alert-to-runbook, and relevant companion drilldowns.
- Preserve `from`, `to`, selected instance, interface/device, and safe action/source filters where destinations support them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Links are generated from one source of truth and covered by schema/unit tests.
- [ ] A selected instance and time range survive navigation between main and self-observability dashboards. **(half met — registry + URL builder in place; the link itself is carried by #431, one `exists=True` flag)**
- [x] At least firewall, flow, interface, gateway/HA, and logship panels have useful scoped drilldowns.
- [x] Missing optional companion dashboards degrade to documented links or are omitted without broken navigation.
- [ ] ~~Live browser validation proves links resolve and retain context.~~ **WON'T-DO** by owner decision 2026-07-27 (same call as #422's browser half); substituted with generated-URL unit tests + live UID resolution.

## Dependencies and risks

- Freeze destination UIDs and variable names before parallel implementation.
- Do not embed stack-specific hostnames or datasource UIDs in source.

## Duplicate verdict

No existing issue adds links. The source-only audit parked it until current Grafana link semantics and live navigation were verified; both were checked in this audit.

## Live verification

- Grafana Cloud stack `m7kni` was inspected read-only on 2026-07-25 using Grafana 13.2.0.
- The live main dashboard `opnsense-exporter` was GitSync-backed at version 2 with 711 elements and 100 variables.
- Live alerting contained 45 healthy rules in folder `opnsense-alerts`; 21,793 OPNsense series and 480 distinct `opnsense_*` metric names were present over the six-hour audit window.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

## Clean programme pause status

Queued under #450; no issue-specific implementation has started. There are no RED tests, source edits, generated-artifact changes, live Grafana writes, or local half-changes for this child.

The clean pause baseline is `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`: local `main`, `origin/main`, and remote main match, the worktree is clean, and all eight exact-SHA workflows are terminal-success. Resume only in the #450 dependency order after rereading the child and parent in full and revalidating the premise and ownership.

Parent receipt: https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/450#issuecomment-5085202739

## 2026-07-26 live reconciliation

Live ownership and UID contracts are now known:

- main: `opnsense-exporter`
- reserved self-observability destination: `opnsense-exporter-health`
- Zenarmor companion: `opnsense-zenarmor`
- retired UIDs `rovp4pp`, `opnsense-network-activity`, and `ddfj9vprnpio74a` all return 404 and must remain omitted.

Use explicit relative dashboard URLs with `${__url_time_range}`, `${opnsense_instance:queryparam}`, and `${datasource:queryparam}`; do not propagate hidden sentinels or blindly propagate `device` because its contract differs on the Zenarmor dashboard. Main-to-self waits for #431; main-to-Zenarmor waits for #435. No links were implemented, so the issue remains open at a clean cross-epic seam.

## Owner decision 2026-07-27: the UID freeze is authorized now, and the Zenarmor destination is gone

Recorded so the next session does not re-litigate it.

> "for 419 I think we can likely freeze the IDs now of the generated self o11y and
> operational o11y dashboards. The zenarmor dash in 435 in the latest comment advises
> zenarmor features/o11y should entirely be in our main deployed dashboard as a dedicated
> tab (that hides when no zenarmor data exists of course!)"

This resolves both blockers this issue was parked on, though not in the same way:

- **Self-observability (`opnsense-exporter-health`, #431):** the UID may be frozen now,
  ahead of the dashboard existing. What must NOT happen is emitting a link to it before
  #431 lands — a link to a UID that 404s is exactly the "broken navigation" this issue's
  own acceptance criteria forbid. So the registry needs an explicit exists/reserved flag,
  and the main-to-self link is generated only when the destination is generated.
- **Zenarmor (`opnsense-zenarmor`, #435):** there is no longer an external destination to
  link to. Zenarmor becomes a tab in the main dashboard, gated on a Zenarmor presence
  sentinel — which the dashboard already has (`Zenarmor` is one of the 41 leaf tabs, and
  its rows are already sentinel-gated). So the main-to-Zenarmor drilldown is struck from
  scope, replaced by nothing: an in-dashboard tab needs no link. The retired UID stays in
  the never-reuse list.

### Still to do (nothing was implemented this run)

1. A frozen UID registry as the single source of truth: `opnsense-exporter` (live),
   `opnsense-exporter-health` (reserved, not yet generated), and the three retired UIDs
   `rovp4pp`, `opnsense-network-activity`, `ddfj9vprnpio74a` recorded as never-reuse — all
   three 404 today, per this issue's earlier live reconciliation.
2. A URL builder using `${__url_time_range}`, `${opnsense_instance:queryparam}` and
   `${datasource:queryparam}`. Do not propagate hidden sentinels, and do not blindly
   propagate `device`: its contract differs per destination.
3. Panel data links for the firewall, flow, interface, gateway/HA and logship panels.
4. **#421 depends on this.** Annotation text is the only place Grafana carries a link from
   an annotation, and #421's "links preserve time and instance context" criterion is
   deliberately waiting for this builder rather than hand-rolling a second URL format.

## Delivered in [`6100ad6`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/6100ad6) — four of five criteria met, the fifth is carried by #431

### What landed

`grafana/uids.py` is the single source of truth for every destination and every URL. No
call site types a UID or a URL any more.

| criterion | state |
| --- | --- |
| Links generated from one source of truth, covered by tests | **met** — 19 cases in `tests/test_links.py` |
| Instance + time range survive navigation between main and self-observability | **half met** — see below, carried by #431 |
| Firewall, flow, interface, gateway/HA and logship panels have scoped drilldowns | **met** |
| Missing optional companions degrade or are omitted without broken navigation | **met** |
| Live browser validation | **won't-do** by the owner's #422 decision; substituted, see below |

### The UID freeze, and the one flag that finishes criterion 2

- `opnsense-exporter` — live.
- `opnsense-exporter-health` — **frozen and RESERVED**, `exists=False`. `dash_url()`
  raises on it, so the main-to-self link cannot be emitted until the dashboard is
  generated. **This is what #431 has to do to finish criterion 2:** flip `exists=True`
  in `grafana/uids.py` in the same commit that generates the dashboard, and add the
  link. `test_reserved_destinations_emit_no_link` fails today if anyone links it early,
  and stops applying the moment the flag flips. Recorded on #431 too, so it is not
  carried only here.
- Retired `rovp4pp`, `opnsense-network-activity`, `ddfj9vprnpio74a` — never-reuse, and a
  test asserts none of the three appears anywhere in the generated manifest.
- The Zenarmor companion is deliberately **not** a destination: per the owner's
  2026-07-27 decision Zenarmor becomes a tab here (#435), and an in-dashboard tab needs
  no link.

### Why the URL is spelled out instead of using `keepTime` / `includeVars`

`includeVars` would propagate all ~100 hidden presence sentinels, and a panel data link
has no such booleans at all — its only input is the URL. One explicit shape serves both
and is testable: `${__url_time_range}`, `${opnsense_instance:queryparam}`,
`${datasource:queryparam}`, plus `${loki_datasource:queryparam}` for log-facing targets.

### Two things that were checked rather than assumed

- **Flow's `interface` label is description space.** Live values on 2026-07-27 were
  `AAISP, CAM, IOT, LAN, MGMT, VIRGIN` — the same set `opnsense_interfaces_link_state`
  carries — plus unresolved device names and the synthetic `locally-originated` /
  `__other__` keys. So flow drilldowns set `$interface`, not `$device`. Guessing here
  is the #98 trap: the two label spaces are disjoint, and the wrong one navigates to a
  selection matching nothing while looking like it worked.
- **Tab deep-linking uses `dtab` / `<domain>-dtab`,** with slugs that are the tab title
  with space runs collapsed to hyphens (case and punctuation preserved, hence
  percent-encoding — `Firewall & PF` would otherwise truncate the query string). Read
  out of Grafana's own `TabsLayoutManager` / `getSlugForRowOrTab`. **Caveat stated
  rather than hidden:** the deployed stack reports 13.2.0 and there is no matching OSS
  tag to pin against, so this is source-verified, not verified against the running
  build. It degrades safely — a Grafana that ignores `dtab`, or a tab hidden by its
  presence sentinel, opens the dashboard on its default tab with the time range and
  instance still correct. Nothing 404s.

### Drilldowns

Field links (click a series) re-scope the dashboard: `$interface` on interfaces, flow
and the firewall log-entries panel; `$device` on the eight pf traffic panels. Panel
links jump to the tab that answers the next question, carrying instance and window:
interfaces → firewall / flow / log-derived events / gateways, firewall → interfaces /
log-derived events, flow → interfaces / firewall, gateways + CARP → log-derived events /
raw syslog / HA sync, log shipping → syslog / diagnostics.

The alert rules' `runbook_url` now comes from the same registry as the dashboard's
"Alert runbooks" link, so an alert notification and the dashboard cannot point at two
different pages.

### New executable contracts (`grafana/tests/test_links.py`)

1. A destination must be registered **and exist** — a reserved UID is unwritable.
2. Retired UIDs must appear nowhere in the manifest.
3. Every internal link must carry time, instance and datasource.
4. No stack-specific hostname or datasource UID may be embedded.
5. A `var-` parameter must name a declared, **non-hidden** variable — sentinels are
   presence probes, not navigation context.
6. A field link may only template a label its own panel's queries return. Without this,
   `${__field.labels.interface}` on a panel that never keeps `interface` navigates with
   an empty variable and looks fine.

body:
## Problem

The PF packet families are emitted as OpenTelemetry counters, so Prometheus exposes `_total` names, while the metric catalogue, generated dashboard, and recording rules reference unsuffixed names and describe them as gauges. The panels and rules therefore return no data despite live counter series being present.

## Evidence

- All eight PF packet descriptors are constructed with `CounterValue` in the collector.
- The live panel 106 query using an unsuffixed PF packet name returned no series; the same query with `_total` returned data.
- The live recording rule `instance:opnsense_firewall_block_packets:rate5m` returned no series.
- OpenTelemetry's Prometheus compatibility guidance and exporter specification require `_total` on counters.

## Operator value

This restores eight currently blank operational views and prevents generated documentation from lying about counter semantics.

## Scope

- Choose the canonical contract: retain counters and update every consumer to `_total`, unless a migration analysis proves the instruments were intended to be gauges.
- Update catalogue types, dashboards, recordings, alerts, examples, and contract tests atomically.
- Add a cross-surface test that derives the Prometheus export name from instrument type.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A failing test proves current generated consumers reference names the supported live Prometheus backend does not expose.
- [x] All eight PF packet series have one consistent instrument type and Prometheus name.
- [x] Panel 106 and every dependent panel/recording query return live data after deployment. **Verified read-only at the query level: the renamed series returns 36 live series and the corrected recording-rule expression 18 rows, while the pre-fix unsuffixed name returns empty. Rendered-panel confirmation still belongs to the GitSync publication step.**
- [x] The recording rule emits instance-labelled series and downstream alerts remain correct.
- [x] Generated metric docs state Counter and explain `_total`/`rate` use.
- [x] Full repository gates pass. **Live Grafana read-back is outstanding** — the dashboard is GitSync-owned and no publication was authorized in this run, so it belongs to the publication step (same reason the panel checkbox above is unticked).

## Dependencies and risks

- Treat this as one atomic contract migration; partial updates will swap one no-data state for another.
- Avoid a duplicate alias unless a time-bounded compatibility need is demonstrated.

## Duplicate verdict

No prior issue captures this cross-surface mismatch. #303 rebuilt the dashboard and #372 validated rule health, but live query evaluation exposes the surviving defect.

## Live verification

- Grafana Cloud stack `m7kni` was inspected read-only on 2026-07-25 using Grafana 13.2.0.
- The live main dashboard `opnsense-exporter` was GitSync-backed at version 2 with 711 elements and 100 variables.
- Live alerting contained 45 healthy rules in folder `opnsense-alerts`; 21,793 OPNsense series and 480 distinct `opnsense_*` metric names were present over the six-hour audit window.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

The P0 contract migration landed atomically, no alias, per the decision already recorded on this issue.

### Premise revalidated first — with one correction

The body said the generated consumers "reference names the supported live Prometheus backend does not expose", which is right, but the earlier framing that the eight names were *impossible* was not: they **are** real exported descriptors, just unsuffixed. The precise defect, as this issue's 2026-07-26 reconciliation comment already stated, is that OTLP-to-Prometheus canonicalization appends `_total` to every monotonic sum, so the two export paths disagree and only the direct `/metrics` path ever showed the unsuffixed name. That is the version implemented.

### What changed

All eight descriptors renamed to `opnsense_firewall_{in,out}_{ipv4,ipv6}_{pass,block}_packets_total`. Consumers updated in the same commit: the eight `grafana/tabs/firewall.py` expressions, the `$device` template-variable query in `grafana/build_dashboard.py`, and the four names in the `instance:opnsense_firewall_block_packets:rate5m` recording-rule source.

**A second, independent bug fixed at the root.** `docs/metrics/metrics.md` documented all eight packet metrics as **Gauge** despite `CounterValue` emission. Cause: the sixteen pf pass/block metrics were emitted through a `map[*prometheus.Desc]int64` loop whose desc argument was the loop variable, which defeats `scripts/docgen`'s static per-field type attribution and silently fell through to its `_total`-suffix heuristic. Each metric now emits via its own explicit `c.<field>` selector, so the catalogue types all sixteen as Counter *because resolution succeeds*, not because the suffix now happens to be present. `TestMetricTypesFromEmission` and `TestMetricTypeSuffixFallback` both still pass unmodified.

**Four invented metric names removed from hand-written docs.** `docs/metrics/overview.md` and `docs/integration-dashboards.md` referenced `opnsense_firewall_{ipv4,ipv6}_{pass,block}_packets_total` — direction dropped entirely, names that never existed in any form — plus `opnsense_firewall_states_{current,limit}`, which are really `opnsense_firewall_pf_states_{current,limit}`. Neither file is generated and no lint covered them, so nothing would have caught these.

### The executable guards (acceptance criteria 1 and the scope's cross-surface test)

Both were observed failing first, for the right reason and with no false positives.

`TestFirewallCollector_CounterMetricsEndInTotal` (Go) gathers the collector and asserts every counter-typed family ends in `_total`. RED output named exactly the eight targets:

```text
firewall_test.go:275: counter metric "opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_packets" is emitted with CounterValue but its name does not end in _total
    ... (8 total)
--- FAIL: TestFirewallCollector_CounterMetricsEndInTotal (0.00s)
```

`grafana/tests/test_metric_counter_total_suffix.py` derives instrument type from the generated catalogue and asserts no Counter-typed metric referenced by `grafana/dashboard.json` or `grafana/alerts/grafana-managed/*.json` lacks the suffix. RED listed the same eight. Neither `tools/promqlcheck` (syntax only) nor `docgen`'s doclint (flag/env tokens only) could have caught this class.

### Gate — all green on the completing tree

```text
go test ./...                                        exit 0
go test -race ./internal/collector/... ./internal/logship/...   exit 0
go vet ./...                                         clean
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...                         ok
golangci-lint run ./...                              0 issues
make docs-check                                      passed — 831 metrics (Gauges 550, Counters 281)
make grafana-check                                   passed — 831/831 coverage, 731 panels, 968 PromQL targets, 44 grafana tests, 54 manifests
```

Catalogue type census moved 8 metrics Gauge→Counter (558/273 → 550/281), which is the docs half of the defect being corrected.

### Actions — all 8 workflows terminal-success for the exact SHA

CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, Release Please, Trigger Documentation Sync.

### Breaking change recorded

`docs/upgrading.md` v4.0 section documents the rename and why direct-scrape consumers are the only ones affected. The commit is `!`-marked with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

### Deviation and follow-up: nine more metrics have this exact defect

Building the guard surfaced nine further Counters that do not end in `_total` and are consumed with `rate()` today — `opnsense_ipsec_phase{1,2}_{bytes,packets}_{in,out}` and `opnsense_vnstat_total_bytes`. They are the same live-blank class, but out of this issue's scope, which enumerates the eight firewall descriptors. Rather than silently absorb or silently ignore them they are carried in an explicitly commented `KNOWN_PRE_EXISTING_VIOLATIONS` set in the new guard, and filed as **#464** with the requirement that closing it empties and deletes that set. `opnsense_vnstat_total_bytes` needs a naming decision there, not a mechanical suffix.

### Live read-back not performed

Acceptance criterion 3 asks that panel 106 and dependents return live data *after deployment*. The dashboard is GitSync-owned and no dashboard publication was authorized in this run, so that check remains outstanding and belongs to the publication step, not to this commit. Panel numbering has also shifted since the audit: the four pass/block-packets panels are ids 113-116 in current source, and today's id 106 is an unrelated SFP panel added by #456.

## Live read-back complete — the outstanding acceptance criterion is now met

The receipt above left acceptance criterion 3 ("Panel 106 and every dependent panel/recording query return live data after deployment") outstanding, on the grounds that it needed a dashboard publication. **It did not.** The OTLP path already canonicalizes counters to `_total`, so the names this commit now generates are exactly the ones the live backend has been exposing all along — which is verifiable read-only, today, with no publication and no deployment of the new binary.

Read-only queries against `grafanacloud-prom`:

```text
count(opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_packets_total)   -> 36        the name the commit now generates
count(opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_packets)         -> (empty)   the name it generated before
```

And the corrected recording-rule source expression:

```text
count(sum by (opnsense_instance, interface) (
  rate(opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_block_packets_total[5m]) + rate(opnsense_firewall_out_ipv4_block_packets_total[5m]) +
  rate(opnsense_firewall_in_ipv6_block_packets_total[5m]) + rate(opnsense_firewall_out_ipv6_block_packets_total[5m])))
  -> 18
```

18 instance/interface rows, matching the count recorded in this issue's 2026-07-26 reconciliation. The evidence is symmetric and unambiguous: the pre-fix generated queries return nothing against live data, the post-fix ones return the full series set. The four pass/block-packets panels and the `instance:opnsense_firewall_block_packets:rate5m` recording rule will therefore return data as soon as the regenerated dashboard and rules are published.

Ticking criterion 3, with one honest limit: this verifies the **queries** against live data, not a **rendered panel**. Dashboard publication is GitSync-owned and was not authorized in this run, so a visual confirmation still belongs to the publication step. That is a weaker claim than "a human looked at the panel" and a much stronger one than "the JSON regenerated".

**Theme:** documentation integrity / dynamic-rendering contract

**Priority and confidence:** P2, certain

### Evidence

- Runtime source and its build guard correctly implement the closed #114 decision:
  - `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py:31-59` detects DHCP service/metric presence rather than nonzero lease count.
  - `grafana/build_dashboard.py:521-542` explicitly rejects DHCP sentinels containing `>0`.
- The authoring guide still prescribes value-based DHCP queries at `grafana/tabs/AUTHORING.md:163-165`, including `query_result(...leases_total > 0)`.
- `grafana/README.md:39-49` still says some sections are gated on whether data/leases exist and describes Kea visibility in terms of leases, which can be read as the behavior #114 removed.
- Sentinel definitions are spread across feature modules, while the documentation table is maintained manually. There are now 97 generated sentinels from 98 source registrations; the duplicate `has_netflow` registration is currently silently deduplicated, so drift is difficult to notice in review.
- Issues 2 and 3 will need to change the identity selector in almost every sentinel, multiplying the drift risk.

### Operational value

The current guide instructs the next contributor to reintroduce a fixed bug: a healthy DHCP service with zero leases would disappear. Generating or checking the table from the same source as the dashboard makes the conditional-rendering contract reviewable and keeps zero-valued-series semantics intact.

### Scope

- Represent each sentinel with structured metadata sufficient for both generation and documentation:
  - variable name;
  - datasource;
  - feature/row it gates;
  - query;
  - instance-scope mode;
  - reason or empty-state semantics.
- Generate the sentinel reference section in `grafana/tabs/AUTHORING.md`, or validate a marked hand-written table against the manifest.
- Correct README language to distinguish:
  - metric/series presence;
  - a valid zero value;
  - absent/disabled collection.
- Keep the DHCP `>0` build guard as a focused invariant.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No authoring documentation recommends `leases_total > 0` for DHCP feature visibility.
- [ ] README states that a running/present DHCP collector remains visible with zero active leases.
- [ ] Every generated hidden sentinel appears exactly once in the structured documentation inventory.
- [ ] Datasource, query, and instance-scope mode in docs match generated JSON.
- [ ] Adding, removing, or changing a sentinel without updating the manifest/generated docs fails `grafana-check`.
- [ ] The #114 zero-value regression guard remains covered.
- [ ] Dashboard generation, documentation checks, and the full repository gate pass.

### Dependencies and risks

- Land after issues 2 and 3, or implement the shared sentinel manifest as their seam, to avoid documenting known-global queries immediately before changing them.
- Keep prose explanations hand-authored where useful; generate the mechanical inventory, not all surrounding guidance.

### Duplicate verdict

Not a duplicate. Closed #114 fixed dashboard behavior, but its old query remains in current authoring documentation. Closed #303 did not make sentinel documentation self-validating.

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.

## 2026-07-26 live reconciliation

Current main generates 97 sentinels from 98 registrations; the difference is the silently duplicated `has_netflow` name. The manual authoring inventory documents only 38 and still contains stale identity/zero-value guidance.

The recommended single owner is `build_dashboard.py`: emit a structured `grafana/sentinel-contract.json` and a marked generated section in `grafana/tabs/AUTHORING.md`, with `make grafana-check` detecting drift. This follows #413/#414 and preserves the #114 series-presence rather than positive-value rule. No implementation was started.

## Delivered in [`fd94cbd`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/fd94cbd3267fbe98c9b0e90f5b8f803a865afa90)

All 7 workflows for the exact SHA are terminal-success. `Trigger Documentation Sync` was legitimately not triggered — its `paths` filter covers `docs/**`, `zensical.toml` and `scripts/docgen/**`, and this change writes under `grafana/` only.

### The issue's premise had moved, and where

Two acceptance criteria were **already satisfied** before this started, verified by grep before touching anything and then left alone rather than re-done: no doc recommends a `leases_total > 0` presence query (`AUTHORING.md`'s old ~40-row hand-written table was already deleted, because it had drifted into prescribing queries `build_dashboard.py` actively fails the build on — the #114 fix landed in code and never reached the doc), and `grafana/README.md` already states that a zero-lease DHCP backend stays visible.

One fact in this issue's **most recent** comment is also now stale: it records `has_netflow` being silently deduped. `d55384c` made `Builder._claim_sentinel_name` **raise** on a duplicate, so silent dedup no longer exists.

The issue's "reason or empty-state semantics" field was written against the old raw-query model. It maps onto the structured model's `presence` field (`existence` vs `value`) — stated explicitly rather than silently substituted.

### Design

`grafana/sentinel_contract.py` reads the same `Builder` instance `build_all()` already produces and derives three things:

- **scope** — straight from the registry `d55384c` introduced.
- **presence** — `value` iff the built query contains a `> 0` comparison, which only `nonzero=True` can produce. This reuses the exact discriminator `build_dashboard.py`'s own DHCP guard relies on, rather than inventing a second one that could disagree with it.
- **gates** — a recursive walk of the assembled tab tree **after** `organize_tabs()` applies, collecting every `Domain > Leaf > Row` path whose `conditionalRendering` references the sentinel. A sentinel can legitimately gate several points and all are reported.

Output is a machine-readable `grafana/sentinel-contract.json` plus a marked generated section in `AUTHORING.md`, and `grafana-check`'s staleness gate now covers both.

**Owned by `build_dashboard.py`, not `scripts/docgen`:** the registry is a Python `Builder` object, so the Go pipeline would have to re-parse the JSON and duplicate the classification. The existing `git diff --exit-code` pattern already does this kind of staleness gating, so extending its file list was the minimal seam — no new CI job.

The markers use a **`sentinelgen:`** prefix rather than `docgen:`, because `docgen` only processes markers it names in code and an unclaimed `docgen:` marker would falsely imply Go-pipeline ownership.

### Derivation, not enumeration — proven within the hour

The generator reported **98** Prometheus sentinels (95 collector, 1 self_labeled, 2 target_join, 0 global) plus 2 Loki, the moment `f0f1a26`'s CARP sentinel existed — **with no test, fixture or count to update.** It had been 97 when the lane started. A hand-maintained table would have been wrong before it was committed, which is the whole argument for generating this.

`has_carp_vips` is confirmed as the sole `value`-tested sentinel; every DHCP presence sentinel and both Loki sentinels are `existence`-tested, each asserted by a dedicated test.

### RED, and proven load-bearing

```text
FAIL: test_authoring_md_generated_section_is_not_stale
AssertionError: -1 not greater than or equal to 0 : sentinelgen begin marker missing from AUTHORING.md
FAIL: test_sentinel_contract_json_is_not_stale
AssertionError: .../grafana/sentinel-contract.json does not exist — run `make dashboard`
Ran 12 tests ... FAILED (failures=2)
```

The gate was then verified non-vacuous by hand-tampering with the committed JSON: it failed with a full diff, and regenerating restored green.

### Gate

```text
go test ./...        exit 0        go vet / build     clean
golangci-lint       0 issues      make docs-check    passed — 833 metrics (550 gauges / 283 counters)
make grafana-check  passed — 833/833 coverage, 737 panels, 971 targets + 101 variables, 113 grafana tests, 56 manifests
```

Grafana tests 101 → **113**. `dashboard.json` and the alert manifests regenerated byte-identical: this change adds documentation and a gate, not dashboard content.

### One follow-up worth knowing about

`Builder.sentinel(reason=...)` for `scope="global"` is validated but **not persisted** — `builder.py` discards it after the raise-check. Inert today, since there are zero `global` sentinels, but if one is ever added its stated reason will not reach the generated contract until `builder.py` stores it. Recorded here rather than fixed, because `builder.py` was owned by a concurrent lane.

`Builder.ts()` already accepts field overrides (`grafana/builder.py:179-207`), so these can be fixed either by unit-specific overrides/axes or by splitting panels when the scales make a combined chart misleading.

The current axis and tooltip label byte rates as unitless event rates. Large byte values also flatten lower-volume request/datagram series, hiding the relationship an operator is meant to inspect. Correct units make spikes and saturation evidence interpretable.

The body cited 374/641/654 and the reconciliation comment corrected those to 384/653/666. **Both were stale by the time this landed**, because #418 and #406 each added panels and ids are assigned by build order. Observed ids at implementation time: **384** (syslog, unchanged), **655** (flow, not 653), **668** (zenarmor, not 666). They will shift again on the next panel addition. Anyone verifying this should search by title, never by id.

### The three splits

| was | now | series | unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "Dropped / Truncated Rates" (`short`) | "Dropped / Truncated Message Rate (msgs/sec)" | `opnsense_syslog_dropped_total`, `opnsense_syslog_truncated_messages_total` | `short` |
| | "Truncated Bytes Rate (bytes/sec)" | `opnsense_syslog_truncated_bytes_total` | `Bps` |
| "NetFlow Ingest (datagrams/sec)" (`short`) | "NetFlow Ingest (datagrams/sec)" | `opnsense_flow_netflow_datagrams_total` | `short` |
| | "NetFlow Ingest Bytes (bytes/sec)" | `opnsense_flow_netflow_bytes_received_total` | `Bps` |
| "Zenarmor Bulk Ingest (rate)" (`short`) | "Zenarmor Bulk Ingest Requests (requests/sec)" | `opnsense_exporter_logs_zenarmor_bulk_requests_total` | `reqps` |
| | "Zenarmor Bulk Ingest Bytes (bytes/sec)" | `opnsense_exporter_logs_zenarmor_bulk_bytes_total` | `Bps` |

Event-series units are not invented — each matches the token its sibling panels in the same tab already use. `reqps` for Zenarmor bulk was the one debatable choice and it is kept deliberately: these are literally Elasticsearch `_bulk` HTTP requests, and falling back to `short` for consistency with neighbouring panels would discard exactly the denominator information this issue exists to make explicit.

Titles, legends and descriptions now state the quantity and its denominator, so a byte rate cannot be misread as an event rate. Legend text changed on four series (`"dropped {{...}}"` → `"dropped msgs/s {{...}}"`); that is `legendFormat`, i.e. presentation, not the PromQL.

### Presentation only — queries provably untouched

Every original raw expression string is byte-identical, asserted by exact-string `assertIn` against the builder's recorded expressions for all six affected series. That is a stronger guarantee than review: a future edit cannot quietly re-mix the units or alter semantics while still satisfying the presentation contract.

### RED first, verbatim

```text
test_syslog_dropped_truncated_rates_split_into_message_and_byte_panels ... FAIL
test_netflow_ingest_rate_splits_into_datagram_and_byte_panels ... FAIL
test_zenarmor_bulk_ingest_rate_splits_into_request_and_byte_panels ... FAIL

AssertionError: no panel titled Dropped / Truncated Message Rate (msgs/sec)
AssertionError: True is not false   (flow: bytes_received leaked into the datagram-only query set)
AssertionError: no panel titled Zenarmor Bulk Ingest Requests (requests/sec)

Ran 3 tests in 0.051s
FAILED (failures=3)
```

### Contracts landed hours earlier, all still green

The Loki-scoping and sentinel-scoping guards from `d55384c` (#413/#414) both pass unchanged — these are pure Prometheus panels, so no `loki_sel()` interaction arose, and no exemption was added anywhere. Catalogue coverage stayed **832/832**: splitting a panel orphaned no metric.

### Gate — green on the completing tree

```text
go test ./...                    exit 0
go vet ./...                     clean
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...     ok
make docs-check                  passed — 832 metrics (Gauges 550, Counters 282)
make grafana-check               passed — 832/832 coverage, 736 panels, 970 PromQL targets, 64 grafana tests, 54 manifests
```

Panels **733 → 736** (+1 per split), tabs unchanged at 41, grafana tests **61 → 64**. `grafana/alerts/grafana-managed/` regenerated with **zero diff**, confirming no alert or recording rule is affected.

### Actions — all 7 workflows terminal-success for the exact SHA

CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, Release Please.

**Seven, not the usual eight, and that is correct rather than a missing run.** `Trigger Documentation Sync` has a `paths` filter on `docs/**`, `zensical.toml` and `scripts/docgen/**`; this commit touched only `grafana/`, so the workflow was legitimately not triggered. Verified against the workflow definition and the commit's file list rather than assumed — noting it because a successor comparing run counts across this session's commits would otherwise read it as a gap.

body:
**Theme:** visual semantics / false alert coloring

**Priority and confidence:** P2, certain

### Evidence

- `grafana/builder.py:262-280` gives every bar gauge the same implicit thresholds when a caller omits them:

  ```text
  green: base
  yellow: 70
  red: 90
  ```

- There are now 39 generated bar gauges: 37 carry the implicit 70/90 defaults and 2 carry explicit semantic ratio thresholds currently carry that exact threshold set.
- The defaults are valid for some 0–100 utilization panels, but many panels are counts, bytes, versions, or categorical/status values. Concrete examples:
  - Panel 367, **Signature Database Versions**, unit `short` (`grafana/tabs/clamav.py:51-56`): a version value greater than 90 renders red.
  - Panel 560, **eve Log File Sizes**, unit `bytes` (`grafana/tabs/ids.py:71-76`): more than 90 bytes renders red.
  - Panel 129, **PF Memory Limits by Pool**.
  - Panel 143, **NAT Rules**.
  - Panel 149, **Largest Tables**.
- Similar false severity coloring reaches DHCP inventory, ARP/NDP counts, socket counts, Tor status, and other panels where 70/90 has no operational meaning.
- Panels that genuinely own a threshold can already pass one explicitly; `grafana/tabs/recording_rules.py:115-133` is a working example.

### Operational value

Red and yellow encode urgency. Applying them to version numbers and arbitrary counts creates false incidents and trains users to ignore color. Thresholds should communicate a known boundary, not be a builder decoration.

### Scope

- Change `Builder.bargauge()` so omitted thresholds produce neutral/continuous coloring with no synthetic severity boundary.
- Audit all 39 current callers:
  - retain explicit thresholds only for normalized percentage/utilization values with a defensible boundary;
  - remove severity thresholds from counts, bytes, versions, and categorical/status panels;
  - document the meaning where a threshold is retained.
- Add builder and generated-panel tests that distinguish explicit semantic thresholds from no-threshold panels.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Builder.bargauge()` does not inject 70/90 thresholds when `thresholds` is omitted.
- [ ] Signature Database Versions and eve Log File Sizes no longer turn yellow/red at numeric 70/90.
- [ ] Each retained threshold is explicit in its caller and matches the field’s scale and unit.
- [ ] Percentage/utilization panels that require thresholds retain them after the default is removed.
- [ ] Tests cover one neutral count/bytes panel and one explicit utilization panel.
- [ ] Generated JSON and dashboard statistics are regenerated without unrelated changes.
- [ ] Full dashboard and repository gates pass.

### Dependencies and risks

- Removing implicit thresholds affects 37 implicitly-thresholded panels at once. Review the generated diff by panel title and unit, not as one undifferentiated JSON change.
- Preserve useful explicit thresholds; this is not a request to remove severity coloring globally.

### Duplicate verdict

Not a duplicate. Closed #303 called for a broad visual audit, but the current builder still injects these thresholds into every bar gauge. Closed #97/#112 concern table field-unit behavior, not bar-gauge threshold semantics.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

AssertionError: False is not true : 'Arbitrary Counts' (unit=short) got a severity boundary
it never asked for: [{'color': 'green', 'value': None}, {'color': 'yellow', 'value': 70}, {'color': 'red', 'value': 90}]
AssertionError: {'PF Memory Limits by Pool': [...90}]} != {}   (34 more offenders, truncated)

Two of the ten tests passed pre-fix, and the lane flagged that honestly: the disk-usage assertion passed **coincidentally**, because the synthetic default happened to equal the value that panel wanted. The trap is that the next `gauge()` caller with a `short` or `bytes` value inherits a boundary it never asked for, which is precisely how these 35 bar gauges came about.

### Gate

```text
go test ./...          exit 0        go vet / build      clean
golangci-lint          0 issues      make docs-check     passed — 832 metrics
make grafana-check     passed — 832/832 coverage, 736 panels, 93 grafana tests
```

Panel count, tab count, catalogue coverage and metric census all unchanged — this is a pure presentation change. `dashboard-stats.json`, the alert manifests and every `docs/` file regenerated with **no diff**.

`AUTHORING.md` needed no correction this time: its `bargauge()` line never claimed a 70/90 default. Checked rather than assumed, since two stale docs had already been found earlier in the run.

body:
**Theme:** conditional rendering / multi-instance navigation

**Priority and confidence:** P1, high

### Evidence

- The dashboard has 95 hidden Prometheus feature sentinels. One (`has_logs`) is already selected-instance scoped; the remaining 94 are unscoped.
- Representative generated queries:

  ```text
  has_temperature       label_values(opnsense_temperature_celsius, __name__)
  has_flow              label_values({__name__=~"opnsense_flow_.+"}, __name__)
  has_zenarmor_metrics  label_values(opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total, __name__)
  has_recording_rules   label_values({__name__=~"instance:opnsense_.+"}, __name__)
  has_logs              label_values(opnsense_exporter_logs_queue_capacity{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}, __name__)
  has_go_runtime        label_values(go_goroutines{job=~"opnsense.*"}, __name__)
  ```

- `grafana/builder.py:485-515` accepts a raw sentinel query and refreshes it on dashboard load, but does not apply an instance matcher.
- Optional tabs and rows use these values through `grafana/builder.py:540-590`.
- Normal panel queries use `sel()` and are scoped by the visible variable (`grafana/builder.py:33-36`), so conditional navigation and displayed panels can disagree.
- Example failure: if firewall A has no SMART metrics and firewall B does, selecting only A can still expose the SMART tab/row because `has_smart` searches the datasource globally.

### Operational value

Conditional rendering is part of the dashboard’s diagnostic story: it is supposed to remove irrelevant features. Global sentinels make the navigation lie in multi-appliance deployments, produce empty panels after a tab appears, and make absence on the selected appliance harder to distinguish from a collection problem.

### Scope

- Make instance scoping the default for collector-metric Prometheus sentinels.
- Provide structured sentinel definitions rather than arbitrary unclassified query strings, with an explicit scope mode such as:
  - collector metric: `opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"`;
  - exporter self metric: documented mapping to the exporter identity label;
  - process/runtime metric: explicit global or job-scoped exception.
- Handle regex metric-name sentinels and recording-rule sentinels without losing their existing feature detection.
- Add tests that require every hidden sentinel to declare its identity/scope behavior.
- Confirm zero-valued but present metrics still expose their feature; do not regress the DHCP zero-lease fix.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every collector-metric sentinel filters on `opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"`.
- [ ] Recording-rule sentinels preserve the selected instance when the recording series carries that label.
- [ ] Exporter self/process sentinels (`has_logs`, `has_go_runtime`, or successors) have explicit, tested identity rules rather than silently remaining global.
- [ ] Selecting an appliance without a feature hides that feature even when another appliance exposes it.
- [ ] Selecting multiple appliances exposes the union of their available features.
- [ ] Presence tests remain based on series existence, not value greater than zero.
- [ ] A generated-dashboard test inventories all Prometheus sentinels and rejects undeclared scope.
- [ ] Existing dashboard and repository gates pass.

### Dependencies and risks

- `has_logs` already carries `opnsense_instance`. Runtime and OTLP self-metrics require the separately tested scrape-target join identity rule recorded in the latest issue comment.
- Some Grafana `label_values()` forms accept a selector rather than a metric plus matcher. The builder should own those shapes so callers cannot accidentally bypass scoping.
- Coordinate the shared identity contract with `fix(grafana): scope Loki panels and sentinels to the selected instance`.

### Duplicate verdict

Not a duplicate. Closed #303 included dynamic rendering and multi-exporter work, but 94 of the 95 current Prometheus sentinels are still unscoped. Closed #114 corrected DHCP value-based hiding; this issue preserves that decision and fixes a separate fleet-scope defect.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

## Clean programme pause status

Queued under #450; no issue-specific implementation has started. There are no RED tests, source edits, generated-artifact changes, live Grafana writes, or local half-changes for this child.

The clean pause baseline is `18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f`: local `main`, `origin/main`, and remote main match, the worktree is clean, and all eight exact-SHA workflows are terminal-success. Resume only in the #450 dependency order after rereading the child and parent in full and revalidating the premise and ownership.

Parent receipt: https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/450#issuecomment-5085202739

## 2026-07-26 live reconciliation

Current main has 95 Prometheus sentinels. `has_logs` is already correctly scoped by `opnsense_instance`; the remaining 94 are unscoped. Collector, recording-rule, and labelled exporter-self sentinels use `opnsense_instance`. Runtime and OTLP self-metrics have no native appliance label; the evidence-backed portable path is a co-scrape target join with `opnsense_up` on `(job, instance)`, not an invented global exception.

The source also registers `has_netflow` twice with different meanings; `Builder.sentinel()` silently keeps the first. The structured sentinel model must reject duplicate names and the flow-receiver sentinel needs its own name. No implementation was started.

## Delivered in [`d55384c`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/d55384c6a7047a99a799fbd4d722234f40afe127)

#413 and #414 landed as **one commit**. They modify the same helper (`grafana/builder.py`) and the same 38 tab modules, and a guard for either half would be red while the other was in flight, so splitting would have meant committing a knowingly-failing intermediate state. #413's own comment also required the identity mapping to be frozen with #414 before implementation, which is the same coupling seen from the other side.

All 8 workflows for the exact SHA are terminal-success: CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, Release Please, Trigger Documentation Sync.

### RED first, both guards, verbatim

`grafana/tests/test_sentinel_scoping.py`:

```text
FAIL: test_sentinels_carry_the_instance_matcher_unless_exempt
: 94 sentinel(s) are fleet-wide instead of scoped to $opnsense_instance:
  has_acme -> label_values(opnsense_acme_certificates_total, __name__)
  has_captiveportal -> query_result(opnsense_captiveportal_zones_total > 0)
  [...92 more...]
FAIL: test_every_prometheus_sentinel_declares_a_known_scope_mode
: 95 sentinel(s) declare no scope mode
```

`grafana/tests/test_loki_scoping.py`:

```text
FAIL: test_every_logql_stream_selector_is_scoped_to_an_appliance
: 11 LogQL target(s) query the whole fleet's logs:
  panel 'Raw syslog stream' ref A -> {opnsense_source="syslog"}
  panel 'Top Blocked Servers' ref A -> {opnsense_source="zenarmor", opnsense_action="block"}
  [...7 more panels...]
  sentinel 'has_syslog_logs' -> {opnsense_source="syslog"}
  sentinel 'has_zenarmor_logs' -> {opnsense_source="zenarmor"}
FAIL: test_the_shared_seam_is_what_produced_the_matcher
: LogQL target(s) not built through loki_sel()
```

94 unscoped of 95 unique names, and exactly the 9 panels plus 2 sentinels — matching both issues' audits precisely. The 96th call site was the silently-deduped `has_netflow` (see below).

### The unscoped style is now unwritable, not merely detectable

`sentinel()` is structured and **keyword-only**, so the old positional raw-query form does not fail a test — it raises `TypeError` and `make dashboard` exits non-zero. That is a stronger contract than a guard, because a contributor cannot land the mistake even with tests skipped. Duplicate sentinel names now raise instead of being silently dropped.

Scope modes, all 97 sentinels declared: **collector 94, self_labeled 1, target_join 2, global 0.**

`target_join` is what makes "this metric has no appliance label" stop being a reason for a global exception. `has_go_runtime` (`go_goroutines`) and `has_otlp` (`opnsense_exporter_otlp_enabled`) both join to `opnsense_up` on `(job, instance)` — the portable path #414's reconciliation comment demanded instead of an invented global exception. `has_otlp` was not in either audit but is the identical case, verified against `main.go` rather than assumed.

**`GLOBAL_SENTINEL_ALLOWLIST` and `LOKI_SCOPE_EXCEPTIONS` both ship EMPTY**, and each guard asserts its allowlist holds no stale entry. Nothing needed an exception.

All 97 sentinel inner expressions were additionally parsed through the PromQL parser from #412 — which otherwise never sees variable queries, since it walks only panel targets.

### `loki_sel()` — filter before aggregation, asserted positionally

```python
LOKI_INSTANCE_SEL = 'service_instance_id=~"$opnsense_instance"'

def loki_sel(matchers: str = "") -> str:
    inner = LOKI_INSTANCE_SEL + (("," + matchers) if matchers else "")
    return f"{{{inner}}}"
```

"Top Blocked Servers", before and after:

```diff
- topk(20, sum by (server_name) (count_over_time({opnsense_source="zenarmor", opnsense_action="block"} | server_name!="" [$__auto])))
+ topk(20, sum by (server_name) (count_over_time({service_instance_id=~"$opnsense_instance",opnsense_source="zenarmor", opnsense_action="block"} | server_name!="" [$__auto])))
```

The matcher sits inside the stream selector, so it precedes the `|` line filter, the `[$__auto]` range, the `sum by` and the `topk` — the ranking sees only the selected appliance. A guard asserts this **by position** (matcher index before the first `|` and first `[`), not merely by presence, so a future author cannot satisfy it by appending a filter after the aggregation. Multi-select and All stay regex-based.

**The label choice was verified against the live stack before any code was written**, because getting it wrong would blank nine panels that currently show data. A real syslog stream's complete label set is `opnsense_action`, `opnsense_source`, `opnsense_subsystem`, `service_instance_id`, `service_name`; `service_instance_id="opnsense"` and Prometheus `opnsense_instance="opnsense"` are the same value space. `opnsense_instance` is **not** a Loki label — filtering LogQL on it would have matched nothing.

### One presence-test rule, stated once and cross-referenced

> Use existence when the series only appears if the feature is deployed; use a value test only when the series is emitted unconditionally.

Value-gated sentinels went 3 → 1.

- `has_trafficshaper` → existence. The collector is silent on 404 *and* when pipes and queues are both empty, so `> 0` was redundant — and actively wrong in one state: queues-with-no-pipes exports `pipes_total=0` alongside real queue data, so the whole tab was hidden while holding data.
- `has_captiveportal` → existence. Silent on 404, so the series exists only where the plugin is installed; `> 0` was a value-gate on an installed feature, the #114 shape exactly.
- `has_carp_vips` → **keeps** `nonzero=True`, scoped. CARP status is core rather than a plugin, so `vips_total` is emitted on every readable box, including a literal 0. Existence conveys nothing there, which makes the value test the only available presence test rather than a gate bolted on top of one. Its call site carries a comment saying so and telling future readers not to convert it for consistency.

#414's "presence tests remain based on series existence" is about not regressing #114 — it is not a mandate to convert a metric every box emits. Both call sites cross-reference each other so whichever a reader lands on first points at the contrasting case.

### Three latent bugs surfaced and fixed

**1. `has_netflow` was registered twice with different queries, and the shadowed one was the intended one.** `netflow.py` queried `opnsense_netflow_active` (OPNsense's own netflow-export config); `flow.py` queried `opnsense_flow_netflow_datagrams_total` (this exporter's receiver). Module order runs netflow first, so `sentinel()`'s silent dedupe made flow.py's call a no-op.

The instruction to verify no `conditionalRendering` depended on the shadowed meaning is what found the real damage: **flow.py's three rows — NetFlow Receiver, NetFlow Repairs & Topology, and their `present=` usages — were gated on the wrong metric entirely.** They describe our receiver, and flow.py's own comment says so, so the intent was unambiguous. Renamed to `has_flow_netflow` and re-pointed. Those rows now correctly hide on a box that exports netflow without this exporter receiving it, where previously they appeared and were empty. A reference-integrity sweep confirms 99 `conditionalRendering` references with zero dangling and zero orphaned.

**2. `has_trafficshaper` hid a tab holding real data** whenever queues existed but pipes did not (above).

**3. `AUTHORING.md` prescribed queries a build gate rejects.** Its sentinel table told authors to write lease-count `> 0` queries for `has_dnsmasq`/`has_kea`/`has_dhcpv4_isc` that `build_dashboard.py` actively fails the build on — the #114 fix landed in code and never reached the doc. The table was deleted rather than patched: a prescriptive doc contradicting a live gate is worse than no doc. It is replaced by the structured API and its scope modes.

### Routed out, not fixed: #466

The four OTLP delivery panels are structurally always empty — `opnsense_exporter_otlp_*` carries no `opnsense_instance` (`telemetry.Start` gets the **raw** registry at `main.go:1016`, unlike `logship` which wraps at `main.go:896`), while `sel_pipeline()` is a pure alias of `sel()` and filters on that absent label. Worse, the comment beside them **inverted the conclusion**, claiming `sel_pipeline` was bare and that `sel()` would be the thing that emptied them — so the next reader would have reproduced the bug.

The panels and `sel_pipeline` are byte-identical to before; only the misleading comment was corrected, now naming **#466** as owner with "do not fix here". `AUTHORING.md` carries the same correction. These are Prometheus panel targets, which neither new guard inspects, so no exemption was needed.

### Gate — green on the completing tree

```text
go test ./...                    exit 0

body:
**Theme:** multi-instance correctness / tenant isolation within the dashboard

**Priority and confidence:** P1, high

### Evidence

- The visible instance variable is multi-select with an All regex and is intended to control the dashboard (`grafana/build_dashboard.py:134-143`).
- Log shipping records the resolved exporter instance as resource attribute `service.instance.id`; it is indexed as Loki label `service_instance_id` by default (`docs/log-shipping.md:227-250`, `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go:388-407`).
- Every generated Loki query omits that label:

  | Panel | Title | Current selector |
  | ---: | --- | --- |
  | 388 | Raw syslog stream | `{opnsense_source="syslog"}` |
  | 389 | Syslog lines/s by subsystem | `{opnsense_source="syslog"}` |
  | 671 | Raw Zenarmor Records | `{opnsense_source="zenarmor"}` |
  | 672 | Records/s by Family | `{opnsense_source="zenarmor"}` |
  | 673 | Blocked/s by Family | `{opnsense_source="zenarmor", opnsense_action="block"}` |
  | 674 | Top Blocked Servers | Zenarmor selector without instance |
  | 675 | Top Talkers by Bytes | Zenarmor flow selector without instance |
  | 676 | Blocked by Country | Zenarmor block selector without instance |
  | 677 | Top JA3 Fingerprints | Zenarmor TLS selector without instance |

- The Loki sentinels are global too:
  - `has_syslog_logs`: `label_values({opnsense_source="syslog"}, opnsense_source)`
  - `has_zenarmor_logs`: `label_values({opnsense_source="zenarmor"}, opnsense_source)`
- Source locations are `grafana/tabs/syslog.py:11-15,55-59`, `grafana/tabs/zenarmor.py:27-29,106-152`, and the Loki helpers in `grafana/builder.py:390-472`.
- Result: selecting appliance A can still show logs and feature rows produced only by appliance B, and aggregate panels can merge records from all exporters.

### Operational value

The dashboard’s main filter currently gives a false sense of scope. In a fleet, an operator investigating one firewall can read raw logs or top-talker/block aggregates from another firewall. The same leak makes a log-only row appear when the selected appliance has no matching data.

### Scope

- Extend the shared Loki selector/helper path to add:

  ```logql
  service_instance_id=~"$opnsense_instance"
  ```

- Use that helper for all syslog and Zenarmor panel queries, including unwrap/top-k queries.
- Add the same matcher to both Loki sentinel queries.
- Preserve multi-select and All behavior through regex matching.
- Keep the label indexed; do not move instance filtering into a line parser.
- Add generated-artifact tests that inventory Loki targets and Loki sentinels and require an explicit instance-scope declaration.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 9 Loki panel selectors include `service_instance_id=~"$opnsense_instance"`.
- [ ] Both Loki feature sentinels include the same matcher.
- [ ] Selecting one instance returns only that instance’s syslog and Zenarmor records.
- [ ] Multi-select and All continue to work as regex selections.
- [ ] Top-k, count/rate, and unwrap panels aggregate only after the instance filter is applied.
- [ ] A generated-dashboard test fails if a future Loki panel or sentinel omits instance scope without an explicit documented exception.
- [ ] Existing Grafana generation, coverage, and repository gates pass.

### Dependencies and risks

- This relies on the documented default indexed label `service_instance_id`. If users can remove it from `indexed_resource_attributes`, the dashboard should state that requirement in the Loki datasource/log-shipping setup documentation.
- Freeze the identity mapping with `fix(grafana): scope Prometheus feature sentinels to the selected instance` before implementation: UI variable `opnsense_instance`, Prometheus label `opnsense_instance`, Loki label `service_instance_id`.

### Duplicate verdict

Not a duplicate. Closed #301 introduced mixed Prometheus/Loki syslog and Zenarmor panels and the current Loki helper, but the shipped selectors remain fleet-global. Closed #303 mentioned multi-exporter identity broadly; it did not close this concrete Loki selector gap.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

`sentinel()` is structured and **keyword-only**, so the old positional raw-query form does not fail a test — it raises `TypeError` and `make dashboard` exits non-zero. LOKI_INSTANCE_SEL = 'service_instance_id=~"$opnsense_instance"'

def loki_sel(matchers: str = "") -> str:

Its call site carries a comment saying so and telling future readers not to convert it for consistency.

**Theme:** correctness / CI guard

**Priority and confidence:** P1, certain

### Evidence

- `grafana/tabs/zenarmor.py:43-50` builds the panel expression with:

  ```python
  sel("opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total") + '{action="block"}'
  ```

- `sel()` already creates a complete vector selector, including the selected-instance matcher (`grafana/builder.py:33-36`). The generated expression for panel 665, **Zenarmor Blocks by Category (rate)**, therefore contains two adjacent selectors:

  ```promql

    sum by (category) (
      rate(opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}{action="block"}[$__rate_interval])
    )
  )
  ```

- `promtool --experimental promql format` rejects it with:

  1:155: parse error: unexpected "{" in aggregation
  ```

- The same module already demonstrates the correct API at `grafana/tabs/zenarmor.py:78-79`, passing `action="block"` into `sel()` as an additional matcher.

- The syntax audit covered 947 generated Prometheus panel expressions; this was the only parser failure.

### Operational value

The affected panel cannot execute against Prometheus. More importantly, a malformed query can currently be generated, committed, and released while every dashboard CI gate remains green. A parser-backed gate turns this from a render-time failure into a precise build failure naming the panel and query.

### Scope

- Pass the `action="block"` matcher through `sel()` instead of appending a second selector.
- Add a generated-dashboard validator that:
  - walks Prometheus panel targets only;
  - normalizes known Grafana macros and template variables to parser-safe values;
  - parses every expression with a real Prometheus parser;
  - reports panel ID, title, ref ID, and the rejected expression.
- Wire the validator into `grafana-check` and CI.
- Add a focused regression assertion for panel 665 so a parser normalization change cannot conceal this exact defect.

- [x] Panel 665 contains one selector with both `opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"` and `action="block"` matchers.
- [x] The expression parses successfully with the Prometheus parser used by CI.
- [x] Every generated Prometheus panel target is included in the syntax gate; Loki targets are not parsed as PromQL.
- [x] A deliberately malformed fixture fails with panel ID, title, ref ID, and parser error in the test output.
- [x] Grafana unit tests, generation/coverage checks, and the full repository gate pass.
- [x] `grafana/dashboard.json` and `grafana/dashboard-stats.json` are regenerated with no unrelated churn.

### Dependencies and risks

- Pin or explicitly install the parser version in CI. Grafana macros such as `$__rate_interval` and regex variables require a small, documented normalization layer before parser invocation.
