body:
## Problem

Per-flow records carry start, end, and observation times internally, but the emitted log schema does not expose the full interval. Queries can place a flow at close time after the event-time fix, yet cannot filter long-lived flows or inspect the covered interval without reconstructing it elsewhere.

## Evidence

- `flow.Record` contains `Start`, `End`, and `Observed`, and the correlator preserves earliest start/latest end.
- `flowlog.Bridge.Emit` currently exports body/attributes/source without explicit start, end, or duration attributes.
- The event-time audit explicitly left interval attributes as useful additive schema work separate from the timestamp correctness fix.

## Operator value

Closed numeric/time fields enable duration distributions, long-lived-flow investigation, and precise joins without high-cardinality labels.

## Scope

- Add stable OTLP log attributes for start, end, and derived duration using the finalized correlated record.
- Define fallback/absence behavior for incomplete records and reject negative duration.
- Document query examples while keeping these as fields, not Prometheus or Loki stream labels.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A correlated multi-fragment flow exports earliest start, latest end, and their exact non-negative duration.
- [ ] Incomplete or invalid intervals omit fields rather than fabricate values.
- [ ] NetFlow and merged records share the same schema; Zenarmor-only records are unchanged.
- [ ] No new high-cardinality metric or resource label is introduced.
- [ ] Schema, sink, documentation, and full gates pass.

## Dependencies and risks

- Sequence after the flow-close event-time correction so timestamp and interval semantics are frozen together.
- Use OpenTelemetry field types that round-trip through the configured log backend.

body:
## Problem

The shared log queue is deliberately bounded in memory. It rides out only outages shorter than that queue budget and loses buffered records on process restart. OPNsense syslog targets do not provide the exporter with a replay cursor.

## Evidence

- `internal/logship/queue.go` implements a count- and byte-bounded in-memory drop-oldest queue.
- `docs/log-shipping.md` states failed exports are retried in memory for as long as the queue holds.
- Overflow is counted, but there is no optional restart-surviving or prolonged-outage buffer.

## Operator value

A carefully bounded spool could preserve security and flow logs across collector restarts or longer backend incidents for operators who accept local-disk cost and sensitive-data handling.

## Scope

- Spike storage format, crash consistency, replay ordering, encryption/permissions, retention, and disk/age bounds.
- Keep the current memory-only path as the default and preserve explicit drop accounting.
- Define how resource partitions and OTLP retry classification interact with replay.
- Produce a go/no-go decision before implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The spike quantifies write amplification, throughput, recovery time, and maximum disk use under representative records.
- [x] Threat analysis covers raw log sensitivity, symlink/path attacks, permissions, deletion, and backup leakage.
- [x] Crash/restart tests prove whether acknowledged and unacknowledged records can be distinguished.
- [x] The design is honest that end-to-end exactly-once delivery is not available.
- [x] A no-go result is acceptable and closes the issue with evidence.

## Dependencies and risks

- Sequence after resource-aware OTLP outcome classification; otherwise a spool can persist already-acknowledged partitions.
- No unbounded disk mode and no default-on persistence of sensitive logs.

## Duplicate verdict

#318 bounded queue memory and #362 bounded debug capture. Neither evaluates durable delivery buffering.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.

## Spike result: no-go for production implementation

The current memory-only queue remains the default. A bounded disk spool is technically feasible, but the delivery ambiguity and sensitive-data-at-rest contract are materially larger than the current pipeline.

### Measured prototype

A throwaway append-only WAL used checksummed frames for `put` and durable `ack`, with `fsync` every 100 frames. It was tested with a 431-byte structured syslog record and a 2,297-byte Zenarmor record taken from the repository's existing synthetic fixture.

| Payload | Records | WAL size | Write amplification | Write throughput | Recovery |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Syslog-like, 431 B | 50,000 | 22.40 MB | 1.0394x | 14,736 records/s | 122 ms |
| Zenarmor flow, 2,297 B | 50,000 | 115.70 MB | 1.0074x | 15,470 records/s | 176 ms |

Per-record `fsync` was also attempted and was not viable in the test window. Batched syncing creates an explicit durability window; at 100 records, up to that unsynced batch can be lost on host failure.

### Crash and delivery semantics

The prototype durably wrote two records, durably acknowledged one, restarted, and replayed only the unacknowledged record. It then modelled the destination accepting that record immediately before process death but before the local durable acknowledgement:

```text
crash_test=pass
durable_ack_replayed=false
unrecorded_remote_ack_replayed=true
pending_after_restart=1
mode=at_least_once_not_exactly_once
```

This duplicate window is unavoidable without a destination-side idempotency or deduplication contract. End-to-end exactly-once delivery is not available.

The spool would also have to preserve #392's per-resource `SinkResult` contract exactly: persist stable local IDs before first export, durably retire only `Acked` and terminal `Rejected`, and replay only `Retry` or unknown outcomes. OTLP partial success supplies counts, not original record identities, so the existing count allocation must not be described as identifying the remotely rejected records.

### Security and bounds

The stored records contain firewall, DNS, IDS, audit, authentication context, addresses, hostnames, and domains. A future design would require:

- an explicit absolute directory, mode `0700`, with files mode `0600`;
- rejection of symlinks, hard links, non-regular targets, and group/world-accessible paths;
- positive count, encoded-byte, and age bounds, all enforced;
- logical-deletion wording only: filesystems, SSDs, snapshots, and backups defeat secure-erasure claims;
- explicit encrypted-volume and backup-exclusion guidance;
- segment/compaction headroom. A defensible starting envelope would be 100,000 records, 512 MiB encoded bytes, and 24 hours, with at least 1.1 GiB free for two-segment rotation.

### Decision

No-go for implementation now. The prototype proves bounded persistence can be fast enough, but it does not remove the duplicate window and it introduces a new raw-log retention, key-management, backup, deletion, and disk-exhaustion contract. The current bounded memory queue is more honest and safer as the only supported path.

If this is reconsidered, the follow-up must first settle acceptable duplicate semantics, encrypted-volume expectations, backup exclusions, all three positive bounds, segment sync policy, and tests for torn writes, corrupt frames, rotation, expiry/eviction accounting, partial resource success, and the remote-ack/local-ack crash window.

Verification repeated by the coordinator:

```text
go run /tmp/opnsense-410/spool.go -mode crash -path /tmp/opnsense-410/root-verify-crash.wal
crash_test=pass durable_ack_replayed=false unrecorded_remote_ack_replayed=true pending_after_restart=1 mode=at_least_once_not_exactly_once
```

body:
### Theme and operator value

Expose unexpected UPnP/NAT-PMP mapping activity and repeated mapping cleanup failures
without shell access or a new privileged API endpoint.

### Evidence and gap

- Official plugin source installs a syslog-ng filter for program `miniupnpd`
  ([source](https://github.com/opnsense/plugins/blob/9ee2cd42e0a0ccd20b857378450bf02f46657c86/net/upnp/src/opnsense/service/templates/OPNsense/Syslog/local/miniupnpd.conf)).
- Its status page obtains current mappings by running `pfctl` directly rather than
  exposing an MVC telemetry API
  ([source](https://github.com/opnsense/plugins/blob/9ee2cd42e0a0ccd20b857378450bf02f46657c86/net/upnp/src/www/status_upnp.php#L35-L48)).
- Live capture recorded in #362 found miniupnpd was 2.3% of the unparsed tail, with
  `could not find nat rule to delete iport=...`.
- The current registry has no miniupnpd parser/subsystem.

### Acceptance

- [x] Capture real add, delete, expiry, and error formats before choosing the event
      vocabulary; if only errors are observed, scope the issue to errors.
      **Rescoped to errors plus expiry** — see the receipt on `6d812f8`. A successful
      add and delete remain unknown and are not inferred.
- [x] External/internal IPs, ports, descriptions, and client identities remain log
      metadata, never metric labels.
- [x] Derived metrics use only closed `event` and `result` values.
- [x] Do not infer an authoritative active-mapping gauge from an event stream; restart
      and pre-existing mappings make that state incomplete.
- [x] Unknown variants ship generically and full gates pass.

### Risks and duplicate verdict

The observed evidence currently proves an error stream, not successful mapping
lifecycle formats. That makes this P3 and capture-gated. It is not an API collector
retry and therefore does not conflict with #226, but it should not be filed as a
full-state collector.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Read-only capture assessment: lifecycle formats incomplete

The only real miniupnpd event available is the cleanup error recorded under #362 (`could not find nat rule to delete iport=...`). There is no real successful add, successful delete, or expiry format.

VM 102 has `os-upnp 1.9` installed, but miniupnpd is not running or configured and has no local log. Current main has no miniupnpd parser, derived family, metric, fixture, or capture artifact. Unknown lines already ship generically and can be shape-captured before sampling. The plugin status page derives active mappings from local pf state rather than an exporter-usable authoritative API, so an active-mapping gauge would be false and must not be added.

Verdict: do not claim lifecycle metrics from the single error class. Full implementation needs an approved mutable lab capture of real add/delete/expiry flows with the plugin restricted to TESTLAN and an approved external-interface design. The current WAN is on the production LAN, so a transient mapping there needs explicit approval; an isolated lab WAN is preferred. A narrower cleanup-error-only rescope is possible but would not satisfy the existing lifecycle acceptance criteria.

No plugin/configuration, mapping, traffic, repository, production, or release state was changed.

## Approved isolated-WAN capture design

Live preflight found a clean fully isolated topology. `<lan-ip-38>/24`, `vmbr409`, VM102 `net4`, and LXC105 `net3` are unused.

The capture will create a portless Proxmox bridge with exactly two endpoints:

```text
VM102 net4 / vtnet4 / LABWAN409  <lan-ip-37>/24
LXC105 net3 / eth3               <lan-ip-59>/24
```

The bridge will have no host address, gateway, route, VLAN, physical port, or other guest. Existing TESTLAN remains the internal side (`<lan-ip-24>` and `<lan-ip-56>`). miniupnpd will permit only LXC105 and only TCP ports `40109-40119`; third-party mappings, IPv6 mappings, NAT-PMP, PCP, STUN, and external-IP override remain disabled.

A test-only `miniupnpc` install on LXC105 will produce real IGD add, explicit delete, and finite-lease expiry events. RFC5424 and matching PF/client state will be captured before a parser is registered. No active-mapping gauge will be implemented because plugin status is derived from local PF state and an event stream cannot reconstruct authoritative state across restarts.

Teardown removes exact mappings, target, plugin config, VM/LXC NICs, and `vmbr409`, then proves the original topology and services are restored. NAT-PMP/PCP remain outside this capture until a real verified client exists.

## Live preflight and source constraint before capture

The approved topology is now live and read back: portless `vmbr409` has no host address/route/physical port and exactly `tap102i4` plus `veth105i3`; VM102 `opt5/vtnet4` is `LABWAN409` at `<lan-ip-37>/24`; LXC105 `net3/eth3` is `<lan-ip-59>/24`; TESTLAN remains `opt1/vtnet2` at `<lan-ip-24>/24` with LXC105 at `<lan-ip-56>`. A root-only pre-change config backup and exact identity receipts exist.

Live versions are OPNsense development `27.1.a_40`, `os-upnp 1.9`, miniupnpd `2.3.9_2,1`, and miniupnpc `2.2.8-2+b2`. The two miniupnpc packages were installed as an exact recorded delta after <host-8> relayed the signed-index packages; no repository signature check was disabled.

The legacy plugin ACL is source-proven to have only four fields: allow/deny, external port/range, internal IPv4/CIDR, and internal port/range. It cannot encode TCP versus UDP. I will not patch the daemon or invent a custom bridge. The capture will use `allow 40109-40119 <lan-ip-56>/32 40109-40119` plus default deny, issue only TCP IGD requests, and verify PF/client state contains zero UDP mappings. All other approved restrictions remain exact: IGD only; PCP/NAT-PMP, IPv6 mappings, third-party mappings, STUN, external-IP override, and packet logging disabled.

The root-only VM110 RFC5424 listener is active on TESTLAN. No plugin config, daemon, syslog target, or mapping existed at preflight; those are the next serialized mutations.

## Live capture checkpoint: approved private WAN cannot create mappings as configured

The isolated topology, discovery, and private RFC5424 path are healthy. `miniupnpc` discovers the IGD on TESTLAN and reports the intended LABWAN409 address `<lan-ip-37>`; the daemon is the captured miniupnpd `2.3.9_2,1` process with exactly one TESTLAN listener and the approved ACL.

A real bounded TCP add request for external/internal port `40119`, 60-second lease, and the unique harmless description `issue409-igd-194311` failed with client result `501 Action Failed`. The private log captured the request, redirect attempt, and `Returning UPnPError 501: Action Failed`. Live PF read-back showed no NAT or filter rule, and the client mapping list remained empty. No UDP request or mapping was created.

The cause is source/runtime-proven: miniupnpd disables forwarding when its external interface address is private. Startup states that `<lan-ip-37>` is unsuitable and port forwarding is impossible. The installed sample exposes `ext_allow_private_ipv4=yes`, but OPNsense os-upnp 1.9 does not expose that setting; using it would require unsupported generated-config manipulation. The supported plugin surface instead exposes external-IP override, which the approved design explicitly required to remain disabled.

Rob has been asked whether a temporary ordinary plugin external-IP override may supersede that one restriction for this isolated capture. No configuration was changed while awaiting the answer. The private raw capture is retained; it has not been copied into the repository or deleted.

## Verified sanitized failure templates before blocked teardown

The retained private RFC5424 capture is 16,039 bytes / 96 newline-delimited frames with SHA-256 `4cbca73f460a221d4f51a152f95827f441cf39c7421af87f2801e35112991aea`. All 96 frames have APP-NAME `miniupnpd`.

Exact verified sanitized static templates for the exercised failure paths are:

```text
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> miniupnpd <pid> - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] AddPortMapping: ext port <external_port> to <internal_address>:<internal_port> protocol TCP for: <description> leaseduration=<seconds> rhost=
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> miniupnpd <pid> - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] redirecting port <external_port> to <internal_address>:<internal_port> protocol TCP for: <description>
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> miniupnpd <pid> - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] Returning UPnPError 501: Action Failed
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> miniupnpd <pid> - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] DeletePortMapping: external port: <external_port>, protocol: TCP
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> miniupnpd <pid> - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] removing redirect rule port <external_port> TCP
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> miniupnpd <pid> - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] could not find redirect rule to delete eport=<external_port>
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> miniupnpd <pid> - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] Returning UPnPError 714: NoSuchEntryInArray
```

The successful lifecycle grammar is deliberately still unknown. These templates do not justify treating a request/attempt line as success, and the generic 501 response is not safely attributable to one preceding request in an interleaved stream. No parser or metric vocabulary is being inferred from it.

## Production evidence obtained — scope is errors **and real expiry**, no mutation required

The owner confirmed production runs miniupnpd and authorized inspecting it. A strictly read-only scan found **1,598 real production records over five days**, which unblocks this issue without the private-WAN guard change, without rebuilding the isolated topology, and without any configuration write.

### Production configuration (read-only)

OPNsense `26.7.1_1`, `miniupnpd-2.3.9_2,1`, `os-upnp-1.9`. Generated `/var/etc/miniupnpd.conf`:

```text
enable_upnp=no
enable_pcp_pmp=yes
secure_mode=yes
pcp_allow_thirdparty=no
```

**UPnP IGD is disabled in production; NAT-PMP/PCP is what is actually serving clients.** That inverts an assumption in this issue's earlier plan: the approved isolated capture chased IGD `AddPortMapping` lifecycle grammar, while the deployment that has real clients speaks NAT-PMP/PCP. It also satisfies the condition this issue set for NAT-PMP/PCP — "unless real clients and verified command contracts exist" — because real clients are demonstrably creating mappings that later expire.

### Observed record population

1,598 records across `miniupnpd_20260723.log` … `miniupnpd_20260727.log`. Severity census: `<29>` (daemon.notice) 1,595; `<27>` (daemon.err) 4. Every record has APP-NAME `miniupnpd`. Distinct sanitized shapes, with counts:

```text
1527  could not find nat rule to delete iport=<internal_port> addr=<token>
  61  remove port mapping <external_port> UDP because it has expired
   3  could not open lease file: /var/run/miniupnpd.leases-ipv<n>
   3  shutting down MiniUPnPd
   3  Listening for NAT-PMP/PCP traffic on port <n>
   1  Unauthorized to remove PCP mapping internal port <internal_port>, protocol UDP
```

The `addr=` token is a fixed 7-character alphanumeric in all 1,528 occurrences (character-class signature `xxxxxxx`), not an address literal. It is treated as opaque metadata and never parsed into a label.

**The 61 expiry records are genuine mapping-lifecycle events**, which is materially better than the errors-only outcome this issue was resigned to. Acceptance criterion 1 allowed "if only errors are observed, scope the issue to errors"; the honest scope is now **errors plus expiry**.

Still absent, and still not being invented: a confirmed **successful add** or **successful delete**. miniupnpd logs those at a verbosity this deployment does not emit, and no supported `os-upnp 1.9` setting exposes a log level. No attempt line will be treated as proof of success.

### Frozen contract

```text
opnsense_log_events_upnp_total{event,result,protocol,opnsense_instance}
```

- `event` closed: `expired` | `cleanup_failed` | `unauthorized` | `lease_file_error`
- `result` closed: `ok` for `expired`, `failure` for the other three
- `protocol` closed: `tcp` | `udp` | `""` — present on the expiry and PCP-unauthorized grammars, absent from the cleanup-failure grammars

Never labels: internal/external ports, the `addr=` token, mapping descriptions, client identity, lease file paths. **No active-mapping gauge**, per this issue's explicit prohibition — plugin status derives from local PF state and an event stream cannot reconstruct authoritative state across restarts.

Parser claims APP-NAME `miniupnpd` and matches exactly five grammars — the four production ones above plus the redirect-rule cleanup variant already captured on the isolated testbed (recorded in the comment of 2026-07-26T20:03Z), which is the same event class as the production nat-rule variant and equally self-contained:

```text
remove port mapping <external_port> (TCP|UDP) because it has expired          -> expired,          ok
could not find nat rule to delete iport=<internal_port> addr=<token>          -> cleanup_failed,   failure
could not find redirect rule to delete eport=<external_port>                  -> cleanup_failed,   failure
Unauthorized to remove PCP mapping internal port <n>, protocol (TCP|UDP)      -> unauthorized,     failure
could not open lease file: <path>                                            -> lease_file_error, failure
```

`miniupnpd` also needs a `subsystems` entry (`upnp`); it currently has none, so these records ship with an empty subsystem.

### Deliberate exclusions

- **`Returning UPnPError <code>: <text>` is NOT parsed.** Those templates came only from the isolated IGD capture, and production does not enable IGD at all. The earlier finding stands: a generic error response is not safely attributable to one preceding request in an interleaved stream.
- **`shutting down MiniUPnPd` and `Listening for NAT-PMP/PCP traffic on port <n>` are NOT parsed.** They are daemon lifecycle, not mapping lifecycle, and already ship generically with full body.

### Blocker status

The two options previously escalated to the owner — authority for the unsupported `ext_allow_private_ipv4=yes` generated-config injection, and reversing the approved design's external-IP-override restriction — are **both now unnecessary** and are withdrawn. Neither was ever applied. This issue is no longer blocked.

No production configuration, service, mapping, PF state, or file was changed. Reads were confined to `/var/log/miniupnpd/`, `/var/etc/miniupnpd.conf`, and the plugin's config node. Implementation is queued behind #406, which is concurrently editing the same shared seams.

## Status at programme pause — unblocked, evidence complete, implementation not started

This issue is **no longer blocked** and needs no further capture, authority, or testbed work. It is queued behind #405 purely because both add a derived syslog family and therefore contend for the same four files. A successor can implement it from what is already recorded here, with no live access required.

### Why it was blocked, and why it no longer is

The two escalations previously parked on the owner — authority for the unsupported `ext_allow_private_ipv4=yes` generated-config injection, and reversing the approved design's external-IP-override restriction — are **withdrawn as unnecessary**. Neither was ever applied. The owner instead confirmed production runs miniupnpd and authorized read-only inspection, which produced better evidence than the isolated IGD capture was ever going to: **1,598 real records over five days, including 61 genuine mapping-expiry events.**

The full census, severity breakdown, configuration read-back and the frozen contract are in the comment of 2026-07-27 above. Nothing further needs gathering.

### Everything needed to implement, in one place

**Metric contract (frozen):**
```text
opnsense_log_events_upnp_total{event,result,protocol,opnsense_instance}
```
- `event` closed: `expired` | `cleanup_failed` | `unauthorized` | `lease_file_error`
- `result` closed: `ok` for `expired`, `failure` for the other three
- `protocol` closed: `tcp` | `udp` | `""`

Never labels: internal/external ports, the `addr=` token, mapping descriptions, client identity, lease-file paths. **No active-mapping gauge** — this issue explicitly forbids it, because plugin status derives from local PF state and an event stream cannot reconstruct authoritative state across restarts.

**The five grammars to match**, four from production and one from the isolated testbed capture (the redirect-rule variant, same event class as the production nat-rule variant and equally self-contained):
```text
remove port mapping <external_port> (TCP|UDP) because it has expired        -> expired,          ok
could not find nat rule to delete iport=<internal_port> addr=<token>        -> cleanup_failed,   failure
could not find redirect rule to delete eport=<external_port>                -> cleanup_failed,   failure
Unauthorized to remove PCP mapping internal port <n>, protocol (TCP|UDP)    -> unauthorized,     failure
could not open lease file: <path>                                          -> lease_file_error, failure
```

**Deliberate exclusions, so a successor does not re-litigate them:** `Returning UPnPError <code>: <text>` is not parsed (those templates came only from the isolated IGD capture, production does not enable IGD, and a generic error response is not safely attributable to one preceding request in an interleaved stream); `shutting down MiniUPnPd` and `Listening for NAT-PMP/PCP traffic on port <n>` are not parsed (daemon lifecycle, not mapping lifecycle, and they already ship generically with full body).

**`miniupnpd` needs a `subsystems` entry (`upnp`)** in `internal/logship/syslog/registry.go` — it currently has none, so these records ship with an empty subsystem.

### Implementation path, now that the seams exist

`3c51776` (#406) and #405 established the add-a-derived-family path. Use it:

1. `internal/logship/syslog/miniupnpd.go` — parser claiming APP-NAME `miniupnpd`, registered with **`RegisterParserWithBodyEnrichment`** (the parser extracts no positional addresses, so it should keep the generic body scan; read the `bodyEnrichedPrograms` comment for the double-emit rationale).
2. `derive.go` — `familyUPnP`, `programFamily` entry, `observeDerived` case. The family-decision guard fails the build without it.
3. `internal/logship/logmetrics.go` — `ObserveUPnP` on `MetricSink` and `NopMetricSink`, plus the fakes in `derive_test.go` and `internal/logship/zenarmor/derive_test.go`.
4. `internal/collector/logevents.go` — key struct, family const, command kind, snapshot slice, `cappedCounter`, Observe method, apply/setMax/drain, `upnp_total` Desc, Describe, Collect. Mirror the `gateway` family.
5. Panel in a tab module, gated by a sentinel. **The sentinel API changed in `d55384c`** — it is structured and keyword-only now: `b.sentinel("has_log_events_upnp", metric="opnsense_log_events_upnp_total")`, scope `collector` (the metric carries `opnsense_instance`). The old positional raw-query form raises `TypeError` and kills `make dashboard`.
6. `docs/syslog-receiver.md` — the family, closed vocabularies, template shapes, producing versions, and that unmatched lines ship generically.

**Acceptance rescope:** criterion 1 said "if only errors are observed, scope the issue to errors". The honest scope is **errors plus expiry**, which is better than errors-only. Successful add and successful delete grammar remains unknown and must not be inferred — no attempt line may be treated as proof of success.

### Testbed state

Nothing is outstanding. The isolated `vmbr409` topology, VM102 `net4`, LXC105 `net3`, the miniupnpd plugin configuration, the temporary syslog target and the `miniupnpc` package delta were all removed earlier with absence read back by exact identity. Production was read-only throughout: reads were confined to `/var/log/miniupnpd/`, `/var/etc/miniupnpd.conf` and the plugin config node. No production configuration, service, mapping, PF state or file was changed.

## Delivered — `6d812f8`, scope is errors **plus expiry**

Implemented from the evidence already recorded here; no further live access, capture or authority was needed. Every workflow on the exact SHA is green.

### What shipped

`opnsense_log_events_upnp_total{event,result,protocol,opnsense_instance}`, exactly the contract frozen in the comment of 2026-07-27T10:07Z. All five grammars match — the four production ones plus the isolated-testbed redirect-rule variant. `miniupnpd` now has a `subsystems` entry (`upnp`); it previously had none, so these records were shipping with an empty `opnsense.subsystem`.

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/logship/syslog/miniupnpd.go` | new parser, `RegisterParserWithBodyEnrichment` |
| `internal/logship/syslog/miniupnpd_test.go` | new, 10 tests |
| `internal/logship/syslog/derive.go` | `familyUPnP`, attr keys + three closed vocabularies, `programFamily` entry, `observeDerived` case |
| `internal/logship/syslog/registry.go` | `miniupnpd` → subsystem `upnp` |
| `internal/logship/syslog/sample.go` | family classified: never sampled away |
| `internal/logship/logmetrics.go` | `ObserveUPnP` on `MetricSink` + `NopMetricSink` |
| `internal/collector/logevents.go` | `upnpKey`, family const, command kind, capped counter, Desc, Describe, Collect |
| `grafana/tabs/log_events.py` | panel + `has_log_events_upnp` sentinel |
| `docs/syslog-receiver.md` | family, closed vocabularies, template shapes, exclusions |

### Acceptance

- [x] Capture real add, delete, expiry and error formats before choosing the vocabulary; if only errors are observed, scope to errors. **Rescoped to errors plus expiry** — the 61 expiry records are genuine mapping-lifecycle events, which is better than the errors-only outcome this issue was resigned to. Add and delete remain unknown and are not inferred.
- [x] External/internal IPs, ports, descriptions and client identities remain log metadata, never labels. Ports ship as `upnp.port.external` / `upnp.port.internal`; the `addr=` token and lease-file path are not even attributes, only body text.
- [x] Derived metrics use only closed `event` and `result` values, plus a closed `protocol`.
- [x] No authoritative active-mapping gauge inferred from an event stream.
- [x] Unknown variants ship generically and full gates pass.

### Two decisions worth recording

**No alert rule**, unlike #405. `cleanup_failed` is the *routine* state on the one deployment with real clients — 1,527 records in five days, about 300 a day — so a rate alert on it would page continuously; and `unauthorized` occurred once in five days, too thin to pick a threshold from. The dashboard panel description carries the operator reading instead. Revisit if a deployment ever shows `cleanup_failed` as an exception rather than the norm.

**The `addr=` token is optional in the regex.** All 1,528 production occurrences carry it, but #362's original capture recorded the shape without it. Requiring it would silently stop matching on whatever build omits it.

### Guards against the specific ways this could go wrong

- 18 excluded and near-miss lines pinned as not-claimed, including every `Returning UPnPError` response and all four request/attempt lines. The isolated capture is why: one real add logged `AddPortMapping`, then `redirecting port`, then `Returning UPnPError 501: Action Failed`, and live pf read-back showed **no rule had been created**. Any of those treated as success would have counted that failure as a mapping.
- A structural test pins that no mapping count exists: every value the family can put on a metric is one of the three closed vocabularies, so there is nothing in the tuple to build a gauge from.
- `TestLogEventsCollector_EmitsUPnPCounter` fails on the label count alone if a port, `addr`, client, description, lease-file, `mappings` or `active` label is ever added.
- An unknown protocol or non-numeric port degrades to a generic record rather than minting a value outside the closed vocabulary.

### Evidence

```
commit           6d812f8  (main = origin/main)
go test ./...    exit 0        go test -race (logship, collector)  exit 0
go vet / build   exit 0        golangci-lint                       0 issues
gofmt            0 files       make docs-check                     passed
make grafana-check passed      113 grafana tests / 320 subtests     passed
catalogue        834 metrics (550 gauges / 284 counters), +1
dashboard        738 panels / 41 tabs, 834/834 coverage
promqlcheck      972 Prometheus targets + 102 variable queries
```

Actions on `6d812f8`: CI, CodeQL, zizmor, actionlint, Scorecard, Docker Security, Release Please, Trigger Documentation Sync — **8/8 success, no cancellations**.

### External state

Production was read-only throughout and nothing was changed. The isolated testbed topology was already torn down with absence read back by exact identity before this commit, and nothing was rebuilt. No release was published and PR #358 was not touched.

title: feat(syslog): parse miniupnpd mapping and error events

body:
### Theme and operator value

Make a point on a log-derived Prometheus counter clickable to the exact retained OTLP
log record that most recently incremented that series. This would give the dashboard a
metric-to-evidence path without fabricating trace IDs for firewall events that have no
trace context.

### Primary-source basis

- [OpenTelemetry event conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/events/)
  model named state changes as log records with `EventName`; dynamic values are
  forbidden in event names. The convention is currently Development status.
- [OpenTelemetry log identification attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/logs/)
  defines opt-in `log.record.uid`; records sharing a UID may be safely deduplicated.
- [Prometheus OpenMetrics exposition](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats/#exemplars-experimental)
  supports exemplars on counters.
- [`client_golang` exemplar API](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus#NewMetricWithExemplars)
  supports attaching the last exemplar to a const counter.
- [Grafana Prometheus exemplar configuration](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/prometheus/configure/#exemplars)
  allows a configured label name and an external URL using `${__value.raw}`. A spike
  must prove that this can target a Loki query in the deployed Grafana version rather
  than assume its trace-oriented UI is backend-agnostic.

### Concrete repository gap and feasibility

- `internal/logship/record.go:85-99` has no `EventName` or stable record UID.
- `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go:201-220` never calls `SetEventName`.
- `internal/collector/logevents.go:298-357` emits const counter metrics, the exact form
  `NewMetricWithExemplars` is designed to wrap.
- `internal/server/metrics.go:157-173` does not enable OpenMetrics negotiation.
- The vendored OTel Prometheus bridge already preserves counter exemplars
  (`vendor/go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/bridges/prometheus/producer.go:141-156`), so
  native OTLP metrics are technically capable of carrying them too.

### Spike scope

Use only records already accepted as structured derived events. Give them a static
event name and a UID created before queueing so retry cannot change it. Store the
latest retained record UID/timestamp alongside each existing bounded metric key.
Sampling matters: an event counted but sampled out must not replace the exemplar,
because its target log does not exist. Do not set fake `TraceId` or `SpanId`.

### Acceptance / go-no-go gate

- [ ] A prototype exposes one log-derived const counter with a
      `log_record_uid` exemplar under OpenMetrics negotiation.
- [ ] The same exemplar survives the repository's Prometheus-to-OTLP metrics bridge.
- [ ] Its referenced OTLP log has a matching `log.record.uid` and a static
      `EventName`; retry preserves both.
- [ ] Sampled-out and excluded records never become exemplar targets.
- [ ] Exemplar state reuses the existing bounded metric-key map; no second unbounded
      cardinality surface is introduced.
- [ ] Grafana Cloud or the supported Grafana deployment is verified live to render an
      external exemplar URL that opens the matching Loki query.
- [ ] Failure of log delivery is documented as best-effort correlation, not a
      referential-integrity guarantee.
- [ ] No fake trace/span IDs are emitted.
- [ ] A go/no-go decision records backend compatibility, storage flags, and UX. Only
      a successful live click-through graduates to an implementation issue.

### Dependencies and risks

Prometheus exemplar storage is optional/experimental and Grafana describes exemplars
as traces. OTel `EventName` and `log.record.uid` semantic conventions are Development.
The last retained event may later fail OTLP delivery. Enabling OpenMetrics can alter
content negotiation and needs regression tests. This is why the recommendation is a
spike, not an immediate feature.

### Duplicate verdict

No issue mentions exemplars, `EventName`, `log.record.uid`, or metric-to-log
correlation. This is new but deliberately lower confidence than the syslog integrity
work.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
Spike result: **no-go**. No production implementation is being retained.

The local prototype under `/tmp/opnsense-408` proved the repository-side mechanics:

- OpenMetrics negotiation exposed a `log_record_uid` exemplar on a log-derived counter.
- The vendored Prometheus-to-OTLP bridge preserved that exemplar value.
- The corresponding OTLP log kept the same static `EventName` and `log.record.uid` across retry.
- No trace or span ID was fabricated.

Coordinator rerun:

```text
cd /tmp/opnsense-408 && go run .
OpenMetrics exemplar: pass
Prometheus-to-OTLP exemplar preservation: pass
OTLP EventName/UID retry stability: pass
trace_id/span_id remain empty: pass
```

Live read-only verification against Grafana Cloud context `m7kni` found:

- Grafana version `13.2.0-30000045535`.
- Prometheus datasource `grafanacloud-prom` has one exemplar destination, mapping `traceID` to Tempo.
- Loki datasource `grafanacloud-logs` has only trace-ID derived fields targeting Tempo.
- Neither datasource has a `log_record_uid` mapping or a metric-exemplar-to-Loki route.

The acceptance gate requires a live external exemplar click to open the exact Loki record before this can graduate. Repository mechanics alone do not prove that UX, and adding the datasource mapping plus ingesting a real correlated metric/log pair would be external tenant mutation beyond this spike's evidence. The proposed design also remains best-effort rather than referentially complete when log delivery fails.

Decision: no-go. The unproven Grafana click-through is the controlling failure, so the remaining implementation-oriented checklist items are intentionally unmet. No fake trace/span IDs, speculative production code, datasource writes, or telemetry writes were introduced.

body:
### Theme and operator value

Add observability for an optional OPNsense authentication service that has no runtime
telemetry API, while closing a credential-leak trap in its logging options.

### Primary-source basis

- [Official FreeRADIUS plugin form](https://github.com/opnsense/plugins/blob/9ee2cd42e0a0ccd20b857378450bf02f46657c86/net/freeradius/src/opnsense/mvc/app/controllers/OPNsense/Freeradius/forms/general.xml#L77-L100)
  allows file or syslog output and authentication-request logging. It also exposes
  options that deliberately log rejected or accepted passwords.
- [Official generated radiusd configuration](https://github.com/opnsense/plugins/blob/9ee2cd42e0a0ccd20b857378450bf02f46657c86/net/freeradius/src/opnsense/service/templates/OPNsense/Freeradius/radiusd.conf#L27-L49)
  wires those options directly to `auth_badpass` and `auth_goodpass`.
- [Official FreeRADIUS API reference](https://docs.opnsense.org/development/api/plugins/freeradius.html)
  exposes configuration/service controllers, not request/outcome telemetry.

### Concrete repository gap

- `internal/logship/syslog/registry.go:55-113` has no RADIUS program/subsystem.
- There is no RADIUS parser or derived family.
- #226 correctly records FreeRADIUS as empty for API telemetry, but syslog is an
  independent, officially supported signal.
- Generic shipping preserves the raw body, so a user who enabled password logging
  could currently forward credentials unchanged.

### Proposed scope

First capture real plugin output with password logging disabled; do not enable either
password option for testing. Add a sanitizer that runs before debug capture and before
generic or parsed shipping for recognized RADIUS programs. It must redact known
password/secret fields from the body, not merely omit attributes.

Parse access accept/reject and accounting start/stop/interim only where captured
formats support them. Suggested derived labels: `event`, `result`, and
`client_scope`; username, calling-station/MAC, NAS/client identity, and reply text stay
as metadata or are redacted according to the repo's PII policy.

### Acceptance

- [x] Real OPNsense plugin fixtures identify the program name and exact auth formats; normal Accounting
      requests are pinned as emitting no syslog on the captured plugin version.
- [x] Password/secret redaction runs before raw-body shipping and debug capture,
      including the generic fallback path.
- [x] Tests seed canary credentials in every captured sensitive shape and prove they
      appear nowhere in body, attributes, capture output, or logs.
- [x] Access accept/reject use closed event/result values; Accounting remains sanitized and
      uncounted because normal service emitted no Accounting syslog.
- [x] No username, MAC, NAS/client identifier, or source address is a metric label.
- [x] The parser degrades to a sanitized generic record for unknown variants.
- [x] Docs explicitly recommend leaving `auth_goodpass` and `auth_badpass` disabled
      and require manual syslog Target setup; no firewall configuration writes.
- [x] Full test/lint/docs/Grafana gates pass.

### Dependencies and risks

This depends on the optional plugin and live captures. FreeRADIUS output varies by
version, module, and authentication method. Sanitization must be conservative because
the raw body is the leak surface. Authentication logs can be high volume and contain
PII even after passwords are removed.

### Duplicate verdict

Not a duplicate of #226: that issue permanently rejects an API collector because no
runtime endpoint exists. This proposal uses the official syslog path and adds explicit
secret handling. It must not reopen the API audit.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Read-only capture assessment: credential-safe grammar unavailable

The development VM already has `os-freeradius` installed, but radiusd is disabled/stopped, its log is empty, and there are no retained RADIUS syslog events. Verified settings are file logging with authentication-request, rejected-password, and accepted-password logging all disabled.

This is not enough to implement safely. The current generic path preserves the message body verbatim, and debug capture writes unparsed message/raw content. A FreeRADIUS-specific sanitizer would therefore have to run before record construction, capture-shape normalization, and generic fallback. Without real program names and payload shapes, its recognition and redaction boundary would be guesswork.

Verdict: keep #407 capture-blocked. The exact unblock is an approved disposable VM 102 exercise: keep both password-log toggles disabled, create isolated test client/user state, enable only authentication-request syslog, capture real accept/reject/accounting start/stop/interim variants, then prove distinct canary secrets cannot appear in body, attributes, capture NDJSON, or logs. Only sanitizer-reviewed samples may become fixtures.

No plugin/configuration, traffic, repository, production, or release state was changed.

## Development capture preflight and safety boundary

VM102 (`27.1.a_40`) has `os-freeradius 1.10.2` installed but disabled: service stopped, no clients/users, file logging, zero RADIUS log bytes, and both password logging toggles false.

The current exporter must not receive the discovery capture. Unknown `radiusd` records currently traverse generic and debug-capture paths before any future parser-specific sanitizer, which could retain a credential-bearing body or raw line.

The controlled capture will therefore use a dedicated root-only TCP receiver on isolated VM110 and a temporary OPNsense target filtered to `radiusd`. `freeradius-utils` may be installed on snapshotted VM110. Every request is guarded before and after by rendered/model checks proving:

- `auth_badpass=no`
- `auth_goodpass=no`
- authentication-request logging enabled
- normal `radiusd` service, never debug mode

Access-Accept and Access-Reject will use distinct disposable canaries. Accounting Start/Stop/Interim will be attempted only through the normal service; if they do not emit normal syslog records, accounting remains unsupported rather than enabling debug or a custom bridge. Raw capture stays quarantined; only manually sanitized fixtures may enter the repository. Teardown must restore the exact disabled, empty baseline.

## Pre-capture implementation boundary

Read-only survey at [`8ef49ed`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/8ef49ed847aa20bfecf47c1b0c1f838b61bc3b42) confirms this issue must remain capture-first.

The confidentiality boundary is broader than a parser regex:

- `internal/logship/syslog/source.go` debug-captures both the parsed `message` and the original wire `raw` value.
- `internal/logship/syslog/generic.go` copies an unsupported message verbatim into the shipped record body.
- `internal/logship/capture/dedupe.go` normalizes shapes but is not a credential redactor.

Therefore a message-only sanitizer would be insufficient. The capture must establish the real program name, field spellings, delimiters/escaping, and whether a credential can appear outside the parsed message body. Until then, exact parser grammar, closed `event`/`result` values, `client_scope`, and Accounting support remain undecided.

The post-capture TDD boundary is explicit: distinct harmless sentinel credentials must be absent from emitted body, attributes, debug-capture NDJSON (`raw` and `message`), and any new logger output, including for an unsupported RADIUS variant that degrades to a sanitized generic record. Usernames, station/MAC values, NAS/client identity, addresses, reply text, and credentials must never become metric labels.

No repository, GitHub issue state, testbed, plugin, service, or firewall state was changed by this survey. The approved isolated VM102/VM110 capture remains the unblock.

## Clean pause before capture mutation

The approved VM102/VM110 capture lane stopped at read-only preflight. No RADIUS request, package install, account/client, service/config write, target, listener, scratch path, or temporary object was created.

Baseline at pause:

- VM102: OPNsense `27.1.a_40`, `os-freeradius 1.10.2`; FreeRADIUS disabled/stopped, file destination, request/good-password/bad-password logging disabled, zero configured users/clients, listeners, processes, and log bytes.
- VM102 syslog-ng syntax valid with two running processes.
- VM110: running; FRR and networkd active, two OSPFv2 Full neighbours and one OSPFv3 Full neighbour, DHCPv6 client active. `freeradius-utils` is not installed.
- No RADIUS/VM110 syslog target, capture process, private evidence, or temporary inventory exists.
- Repository remained clean; no Git or GitHub state changed by the capture lane.

The next run can start directly from the already documented isolated capture plan. It must preserve verified sanitized templates before destroying private raw evidence; the existing pre-generic `raw` and `message` capture seams remain the central confidentiality hazard.

## Development FreeRADIUS capture preserved exact templates and cleaned

The approved VM102/VM110 normal-service capture completed against OPNsense `27.1.a_40` / `os-freeradius 1.10.2`.

Before any request, both API and generated `radiusd.conf` read back:

```text
log_destination=syslog
log_authentication_request=yes
auth_badpass=no
auth_goodpass=no
```

The capture established the exact RFC5424 program and supported behavior:

- APP-NAME is `radiusd`;
- valid disposable credentials emitted `Login OK` and returned Access-Accept;
- a distinct invalid disposable identity/credential emitted `Login incorrect` and returned Access-Reject;
- ordinary Accounting Start, Interim-Update, and Stop each returned Accounting-Response but emitted zero normal-service syslog messages, so Accounting remains unsupported;
- all 11 captured frames parsed as RFC5424;
- the raw syslog capture contained the expected disposable usernames/client name but zero accepted password, rejected password, or RADIUS client-secret values.

Exact static sanitized templates are preserved for `access_accept` and `access_reject`, plus five non-event `radiusd` support-message shapes. Two independent sanitization passes were byte-identical: 2 canonical templates, 7 total templates, 1,744 bytes, SHA-256 `f23a84ad72632fc615278543f08245f500f14d005ed187aa0bec6af3090344de`, zero forbidden canary values.

Cleanup restored and read back the exact disabled/empty baseline:

```text
RADIUS_PROCESSES=0
API_CLIENTS=0
API_USERS=0
GENERAL_ENABLED=0
LOG_DESTINATION=files
LOG_AUTHENTICATION_REQUEST=0
LOG_AUTHBADPASS=0
LOG_AUTHGOODPASS=0
CONFIG_MARKER_REFS=0
SYSLOG_PROCESSES=2
VM110_PACKAGE_DELTA_REMAINING=0
VM110_RADTEST=absent
VM110_TEMP_UNITS=0
VM110_PRIVATE_RAW_FILES=0
VM110_NETWORKD=active
VM110_FRR=active
VM110_SANITIZED_FILES=1
```

The implementation contract is now capture-backed:

- closed metric vocabulary: `event="access"`, `result="accepted"|"rejected"`, `client_scope="configured"`;
- usernames, client/NAS identity, station/MAC, addresses, reply text, and every credential are discarded before parser, generic enrichment, debug capture, shape keys, derivation, sampling, queueing, and logging;
- recognized `radiusd` messages outside the two captured event shapes become a fixed sanitized generic message;
- a malformed envelope with a recognizable `radiusd` RFC5424/RFC3164 signature fails closed to a fixed safe generic frame;
- Accounting remains generic/sanitized and uncounted until normal-service capture evidence exists.

## Delivery receipt

Delivered in [`18b4b90`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/18b4b9034e72666bdd6d7e574c65ce3977981c2f) (`Closes #407`).

- Added a pre-dispatch FreeRADIUS confidentiality boundary for parsed and recognizably malformed `radiusd` frames. Hostname, PID, structured data, identities, addresses, reply text, credentials, original message, and original raw bytes are discarded before processors, generic fallback, debug capture, shape keys, derivation, sampling, queueing, or logging.
- Added capture-backed Access-Accept/Access-Reject parsing and `opnsense_log_events_radius_total{event,result,client_scope,opnsense_instance}` with the closed `access` / `accepted|rejected` / `configured` vocabulary. Accounting remains sanitized and uncounted because normal Start/Interim/Stop requests emitted no syslog.
- Added canary leak tests across body, attributes, capture `raw`/`message`, generic fallback, malformed-envelope handling, shape keys, metric labels, and logger output; the primary review also pinned and fixed an empty-frame panic in the malformed recognizer.
- Generated docs and dashboard are current at 831/831 catalogue metrics and 731 panels.

Local gates passed: `go test -v ./...`; `go test -race -timeout 15m ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `golangci-lint run`; `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`; `make docs-check`; `make grafana-check`; `make deployment-test`; and all four 10-second CI fuzz-smoke targets.

All eight exact-SHA workflows are terminal-success: [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/actions/runs/30216862786/attempts/2), CodeQL, Docker Security, Release Please, Scorecard, Trigger Documentation Sync, actionlint, and zizmor. CI attempt 1's syslog-envelope fuzz job completed 70,227 executions without a crash input but ended 0.09s beyond its 10-second harness budget with `context deadline exceeded`; the same-SHA failed-job rerun passed, including `ci-success`.

The capture/testbed cleanup receipt remains in the preceding comment. No production OPNsense, release, release PR, or release asset was changed.

body:
### Theme and operator value

Turn raw VPN daemon prose into a common control-plane timeline: established,
terminated, authentication failure, DPD timeout, rekey failure, and recovery. The API
collectors show current sessions, but a failed attempt or a brief flap can disappear
before the next scrape.

### Primary-source basis

- [OPNsense VPN documentation](https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/vpnet.html) exposes
  IPsec status, security associations, configurable logging, OpenVPN connection
  status, and component log files. It explicitly directs troubleshooting to those
  logs.
- OPNsense uses strongSwan `swanctl` connections from 23.1 onward, so legacy and
  current formats must be treated as distinct capture fixtures rather than assumed to
  be identical.
- The OpenTelemetry event conventions cited above fit connection lifecycle moments
  without inventing trace/span context.

### Concrete repository gap

- `internal/logship/syslog/tunnels.go` only extracts IPsec/OpenVPN UUIDs and resolves
  them to names.
- `docs/syslog-receiver.md:204` documents that UUID enrichment, while
  `docs/syslog-receiver.md:237-240` says the remaining IPsec/OpenVPN content is
  generic.
- #255 shipped name resolution only. Current OpenVPN metrics expose active sessions
  and byte totals, not rejected authentication, DPD/rekey failure, or short-lived
  transitions.

### Proposed scope

Capture stable and development OPNsense lines first. Normalize IPsec and OpenVPN into
a shared event vocabulary while retaining backend-specific attributes. Suggested
metric labels are `backend`, `event`, `result`, and API-resolved connection/instance
name. Usernames, certificate subjects, remote IPs, SPI values, and daemon-provided
error text stay out of metric labels.

WireGuard is out of the first issue: its handshake metrics already exist and it should
join only if a real OPNsense lifecycle log format is captured.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Captures include successful connect/disconnect and at least two real failure
      classes for each backend implemented.
- [ ] Event names and attributes are documented, closed, and common where semantics
      genuinely match.
- [ ] Tunnel UUID enrichment from #255 remains intact and provides the bounded
      connection label.
- [ ] Usernames, remote addresses, SPIs, certificate identities, and raw error text
      never become metric labels.
- [ ] Non-matching/version-new lines ship generically.
- [ ] Derived counters share the existing key budget and are observed before sampling.
- [ ] Dashboard panels correlate current session state with connect/failure/flap
      rates.
- [ ] Full test/lint/docs/Grafana gates pass.

### Dependencies and risks

Log verbosity is configurable, and quiet defaults may omit useful transitions.
strongSwan/OpenVPN formats differ across major versions and authentication methods.
Bodies can contain identity information even when labels do not. The issue should
ship only the event classes backed by captured lines.

### Duplicate verdict

No duplicate. #255 resolves opaque IDs but performs no lifecycle parsing. #257 covers
service-health findability, not VPN events.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Development capture preflight

VM102 (`27.1.a_40`) has a live TESTLAN IPsec SA to LXC105. Its existing OpenVPN profiles bind or connect outside TESTLAN and will not be reused.

The controlled development capture will use:

- A disposable isolated LXC clone for a wrong-identity/PSK attempt, so no bad connection is loaded into the live LXC105 strongSwan state.
- A peer-scoped UDP 500/4500 nftables drop for real IPsec retransmit/DPD evidence, followed by rule removal and explicit child-SA initiation to prove recovery.
- A dedicated TESTLAN-only OpenVPN server/client and disposable account/certificate material for invalid password, invalid client certificate, real client-session disconnect, and reconnect evidence.
- One temporary TESTLAN-only RFC5424 target for `charon` and dynamic `openvpn_*` programs.

Rekey and daemon shutdown are excluded from the initial lifecycle vocabulary: neither substitutes for the required authentication/timeout failures or a real client-session disconnect. Stable-release captures remain unmet and will not be inferred from the current development system.

## Stable-system retained-log negative result

A strictly read-only check of OPNsense `26.7.1_1` retained logs found no usable stable lifecycle/failure fixtures:

- 420 `charon` records, limited to configuration/daemon startup and loading categories.
- Zero IKE/NET lifecycle records, IKE_SA/CHILD_SA events, deletion, authentication failure, retransmit, DPD, or timeout candidates.
- 22 OpenVPN mentions in system logs, with zero successful connection, genuine disconnect/reconnect, or authentication/TLS-failure candidates.

No production configuration, service, traffic, API, or files were changed. Stable-format acceptance remains unmet and will not be inferred. Development captures proceed only on the isolated testbed.

## Development IPsec capture complete

A disposable TESTLAN peer captured real IPsec lifecycle and failure evidence on OPNsense `27.1.a_40` / strongSwan `6.0.7` without editing the existing LXC105 tunnel:

- Matching credentials: temporary IKE/child SA established, then explicitly terminated.
- Wrong PSK: one initiation reached `IKE_AUTH`, produced integrity-verification and failure classes, then deletion. Peer-selection/no-config records were absent, so this is real responder authentication-failure evidence.
- Liveness failure: exact peer-scoped UDP 500/4500 drops produced DPD/INFORMATIONAL traffic and four retransmissions. The temporary SA disappeared between the bounded ~100s and ~160s checks.
- Recovery: after deleting the exact drop table, explicit initiation established the temporary SA again with no failure record.

The capture did **not** contain literal timeout/deletion wording for the liveness phase. The supported conclusion is DPD/retransmit followed by observed SA disappearance and recovery; no timeout-text grammar will be inferred.

The pre-existing tunnel remained at two ESTABLISHED/INSTALLED-relevant lines except while the temporary SA was present, when the count was three. It returned to two after every temporary termination and after final cleanup.

Cleanup was independently read back:

```text
CT406_ABSENT
HOST_NFT_ABSENT
CONFIG_REFS=0
SA_RELEVANT_LINES=2
VM_NFT=ABSENT
SYSLOG_SYNTAX=OK
```

The exact temporary connection/child/auth objects, PSK, syslog target, listener/private capture, nft table, and CT406 are gone. OpenVPN and stable-release capture remain unmet; #406 stays open.

## IPsec implementation gate remains closed

The first controlled run retained category/count evidence but destroyed its private raw/sanitized capture with CT406 before exact sanitized message templates were preserved. A subsequent read-only search of VM102's retained local IPsec log found no records carrying the temporary connection marker.

Therefore the evidence supports the behavioral conclusions in the previous comment, but it is not sufficient to write an exact parser grammar. No message template will be reconstructed from memory or documentation. IPsec implementation requires a short repeat capture that preserves verified sanitized templates before deleting private raw evidence.

## OpenVPN capture attempt stopped and cleaned

A fresh disposable TESTLAN-only OpenVPN instance was created additively with temporary CA/cert/account material and one exact source/port firewall rule. Existing profiles were not edited. The valid client reached TLS/control-channel failure but never established a session, so the acceptance sequence was not started: no successful connect/disconnect/reconnect or authentication-failure capture exists, and no syslog target/templates were created.

The lane was stopped rather than weakening an existing profile or interpreting setup failure as acceptance evidence. Cleanup removed the exact instance, account, certificates/CA, firewall rule, CT406, and private scratch. The first recorded firewall deletion returned HTTP 200 while leaving the rule present; the sole residual was found by its exact temporary description, deleted, and PF reloaded.

Independent read-back:

```text
CT406_ABSENT
HOST_NFT_ABSENT
CONFIG_REFS=0
PORT_11940_LISTENERS=0
TEMP_OPENVPN_PROCS=0
TEMP_GENERATED_CONFIGS=0
TEMP_PF_RULES=0
TEMP_SYSLOG_REFS=0
SYSLOG_SYNTAX=OK
SYSLOG_PROCS=2
```

OpenVPN capture remains blocked on making a fully isolated valid client/server session work. No parser grammar will be inferred from this failed setup.

## Repeat IPsec capture preserved exact templates and cleaned

A fresh disposable CT406 repeated the development IPsec scenarios against OPNsense `27.1.a_40` / strongSwan `6.0.7`:

- correct PSK: IKE_SA and CHILD_SA established, explicit termination produced the delete lifecycle;
- wrong PSK: initiation failed with a captured `IKE_AUTH ... N(AUTH_FAILED)` response and left no temporary SA;
- peer-scoped UDP 500/4500 drops: captured DPD, INFORMATIONAL, retransmits 1-5, and `giving up after 5 retransmits`; the temporary SA disappeared while the pre-existing SA remained healthy;
- recovery: after the exact nft table was absent, explicit initiation established the temporary SA again and explicit termination removed it.

Unlike the first run, exact static sanitized RFC5424 templates were preserved before teardown for the closed development vocabulary `established`, `terminated`, `authentication_failed`, and `liveness_failed`. Two independent sanitization passes were byte-identical: 4 canonical templates, 14,227 bytes in the retained private evidence bundle, SHA-256 `ff3de8f23876f67c4f182f7aec933d1608dcc8a1997dbd3591a0e378e3324c6d`, zero forbidden raw UUID/identity/address values. The private raw log and pcap were then deleted; only the root-owned `0600` sanitized template bundle remains on VM110.

Deviation: applying the additive OPNsense model required one strongSwan restart, which dropped the pre-existing LXC105 SA. This was detected immediately and the exact existing child was re-initiated successfully. Final read-back:

```text
CT406_ABSENT
HOST_NFT_ABSENT
MODEL_REFS=0
EXISTING_RELEVANT_LINES=2
SYSLOG_SYNTAX=OK
SYSLOG_PROCS=2
OPN_PRIVATE_WORKDIR_ABSENT
VM110_NETWORKD=active
VM110_FRR=active
RAW_CAPTURE_FILES=0
SANITIZED_FILES=1
```

No parser implementation starts yet. OpenVPN still needs a fully working isolated valid baseline plus genuine disconnect/reconnect, invalid password, and invalid/untrusted/revoked certificate captures. Stable-release formats also remain unavailable and will not be inferred.

## Development OpenVPN capture preserved exact templates and cleaned

A fresh isolated TESTLAN-only OpenVPN server/client completed the required development scenarios against OPNsense `27.1.a_40` / OpenVPN `2.7.5`:

- valid account and trusted client certificate: real session establishment;
- explicit client stop and restart: peer disconnect/timeout followed by reconnection;
- invalid password: server-side `AUTH_FAILED`;
- untrusted self-signed client certificate: server-side `VERIFY ERROR` and TLS handshake failure.

Exact static sanitized RFC5424 templates are preserved for the closed development vocabulary `established`, `terminated`, `authentication_failed`, and `certificate_failed`. Two independent sanitization passes were byte-identical: 4 canonical templates, 10 retained supporting templates, 2,560 bytes, SHA-256 `ea915378429a23aafc036f35df794ef10a0454da229c1f08ec976c54eaaf460e`, and zero retained canary, credential, object UUID, identity, or address values. The raw capture contained the expected harmless username/certificate canaries but zero good-password or wrong-password values.

All seven exact OPNsense objects were then deleted and read back absent: instance, firewall rule, syslog target, user, client certificate, server certificate, and CA. The temporary Debian `openvpn` package and all private client/auth/certificate/raw-capture files were removed from VM110. Only the root-owned `0600` IPsec and OpenVPN sanitized bundles remain.

Final read-back:

```text
API_OBJECTS_REMAINING=0
CONFIG_MARKER_REMAINING=0
TEMP_LISTENER_11940=0
TEMP_OVPNS40=0
TEMP_TUN40_OPENVPN_OWNERS=0
OPENVPN_PROCESSES=2
SYSLOG_PROCESSES=2
VM110_OPENVPN_PACKAGE=ABSENT
VM110_OPENVPN_BINARY=ABSENT
VM110_TUN0=ABSENT
VM110_NETWORKD=active
VM110_FRR=active
VM110_TEMP_UNITS=0
VM110_PRIVATE_RAW_FILES=0
VM110_SANITIZED_FILES=2
```

The two OpenVPN processes are the unchanged pre-existing profiles on ports 1194 and 57501. `/dev/tun40` is a persistent devfs node on OPNsense; it has no OpenVPN owner and the `ovpns40` interface is absent.

Development evidence is now complete for both backends. Stable OPNsense lifecycle/failure templates remain unavailable: the read-only `26.7.1_1` retained-log search produced no usable events, production mutation is prohibited, and development formats will not be presented as stable formats. Parser implementation therefore remains gated on either equivalent stable sanitized templates or an explicit decision narrowing #406 to exact captured development grammar with unmatched/version-new lines remaining generic.

## Delivered in [`3c51776`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/3c517764526f33c5cd01079bae283cf547100cf4)

Scope was narrowed by owner decision to exactly the captured **development** grammar, with unmatched and version-new lines continuing to ship generically — the precedent `8ef49ed` already set for dpinger. A read-only search of stable `26.7.1_1` retained logs found no usable lifecycle events, so no stable grammar exists to infer and none was invented.

### Correcting this issue's own recorded state first

The programme pause receipt said the IPsec templates had been destroyed before preservation and a repeat capture was required. **That was stale.** The comments of 2026-07-26 18:33Z and 18:54Z record that the repeat IPsec capture *and* a full OpenVPN capture both completed with verified sanitized templates retained. Both bundles were retrieved from VM110 and verified against their recorded digests before any code was written:

```text
ipsec-sanitized.json    ff3de8f23876f67c4f182f7aec933d1608dcc8a1997dbd3591a0e378e3324c6d
openvpn-sanitized.json  ea915378429a23aafc036f35df794ef10a0454da229c1f08ec976c54eaaf460e
```

**Provenance correction applied.** The OpenVPN bundle labels itself "OpenVPN 2.6.14". That was the *Debian client*; `pkg info openvpn` on the box returns **2.7.5**, and all four retained templates are server-side lines (`openvpn_server40`, `SENT CONTROL`, `VERIFY ERROR`). Fixtures and docs state 2.7.5 server / 2.6.14 client. A fixture claiming the wrong producer is exactly the failure the repo's canary-triage rule warns about.

### The contract

```text
opnsense_log_events_vpn_total{backend,event,result,connection,opnsense_instance}
```

- `backend` closed: `ipsec` | `openvpn`
- `event` closed: `established` | `terminated` | `authentication_failed` | `liveness_failed` | `certificate_failed`
- `result` closed: `success` (established, terminated) | `failure` (the three failures)
- `connection`: the API-resolved **configured name** via the existing #255 enrichment. Empty when unresolved, never a UUID.

Record attributes written by the parsers are exactly three: `vpn.backend`, `vpn.event`, `vpn.result`.

### Privacy boundary, proven by mutation rather than asserted

Usernames, certificate CN/subject/serial, IKE identity strings, addresses, ports, SPIs and daemon error text are **not labelled and not extracted at all** — the regexes carry no capture groups for them. Tests assert their absence from emitted attributes and from metric labels across all eight captured lines, and the collector test pins the label count at exactly 5 so any added identity dimension fails.

These assertions were verified to have teeth: the deriver was deliberately mutated to read `ipsec.connection_id` (the raw UUID) instead of the resolved name, and both privacy tests failed for the right reason before it was restored.

```text
--- FAIL: TestObserveDerived_VPNNeverLabelsARawUUID
    label value "…" carries the raw UUID
--- FAIL: TestSourceVPNMetricLabelsCarryNoIdentityFromAnyCapturedLine
    metric label value "…" carries forbidden value "…"
```

### Prefix dispatch, and why it is longest-match

OPNsense names one syslog program per OpenVPN instance (`openvpn_server40`, `openvpn_client2`), so an exact-match table can never reach any of them. `parserFor` now tries exact registrations first, then the **longest** matching prefix. Longest-match is not decoration: Go randomises map iteration, so "first prefix that matches" would dispatch differently between runs the moment two prefixes overlap. The family-decision guard (`TestEveryParserProgramHasAFamilyDecision`, the #396 mechanism) is extended to prefixes, so a prefix parser with no derived-family decision fails the build instead of silently under-counting. It did its job during development:

```text
derive_test.go:269: program "charon" is registered as a parser but has no derived-family decision
```

### Body enrichment is now opt-in, fixing a regression this change would otherwise have caused

Parsed records skip the generic body scan. The reason, per `addCommon`'s own comment, is that a parser which already emits **positional** addresses (filterlog's `src.*`/`dst.*`) would emit them a second time under `peer.*`. **charon and openvpn extract no addresses at all**, so that rationale does not apply — and suppressing the scan for them would have silently dropped the `peer.*` attributes those programs' lines have carried since #250, breaking any existing Loki query the moment these parsers started matching.

So body enrichment became a narrow per-parser opt-in. The default is unchanged and no existing parser moves; a test pins `filterlog`, `sshd`, `dhcpd`, `radiusd` and `dpinger` all still at `false`.

**A real bug was caught here by the lane's own test.** The first implementation prefix-matched the opt-in table directly instead of resolving the dispatch winner first. With an opted prefix `testprog` and a plain exact `testprog_exact`, the exact parser wins dispatch while the opt-in table's prefix still matched — so a parser owning its own addresses would have been handed body enrichment it never asked for:

```text
registry_prefix_test.go:177: an exact non-opted registration inherited the prefix's body-enrichment opt-in
```

Fixed by resolving the winner in the dispatch tables and then asking the opt-in table about *that* key. A shared `longestPrefixMatch` helper now backs `parserFor`, `parserEnrichesBody` and `deriveFamily`, replacing three hand-rolled copies of one loop that could each have disagreed — which would have routed a line to a parser while denying it a family or a body scan.

### Tolerances, each labelled for what it is

- **`AF_INET6` on `Peer Connection Initiated` is DERIVED FROM SOURCE, NOT CAPTURED** (the testbed client was IPv4). Kept because it is the same message for an IPv6 peer and omitting it would mean an IPv6 roadwarrior's establishment silently never counts. Both the code comment and the dedicated test say so explicitly, so a reader cannot mistake it for observed evidence.
- `VERIFY ERROR` is matched as `VERIFY ERROR: depth=\d+, error=.+` — OpenVPN's actual format string, not a loose `.+`. Expired, revoked and depth-N all count as the same event class; a line merely mentioning the words does not.
- `N(AUTH_FAILED)` is matched as "the payload list **contains** it", token-bounded so `N(AUTH_FAILED_SOMETHING)` cannot match. Kept on `generating` (responder side) only. The initiator-side form — our credentials rejected by a peer — is deliberately **not** counted and is pinned as a negative test framed as a decision awaiting its own capture, not an oversight.

### `connection` is structurally always empty for OpenVPN — by design, documented

None of the four captured OpenVPN templates contains the instance UUID; OpenVPN prints it only on its `MANAGEMENT: Client connected from /var/etc/openvpn/instance-<uuid>.sock` line, which is not one of them. The only way to fill the label would be mapping the program-name suffix (`openvpn_server40` → `40`) to an instance, and the instance inventory carries only UUID/Description/Role/DevType/Enabled — no numeric key. That would be fabricating a mapping, so it was not done.

Pinned as a negative test, with a companion test proving the lookup itself works on lines that *do* carry the UUID. `docs/syslog-receiver.md` and the panel description both state in bold that the label is populated for IPsec and always empty for OpenVPN, that this is by design, and that the operator attributes OpenVPN events via the `program` attribute. An operator meeting a permanently empty label can tell it is intended rather than broken.

### Gate — green on the completing tree

```text
go test ./...                                                  exit 0
go test -race ./internal/logship/... ./internal/collector/...   exit 0
go vet ./...                                                   clean
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...                                   ok
gofmt -l (tracked, minus vendor)                               empty
golangci-lint run ./...                                        0 issues
make docs-check                                                passed — 832 metrics (Gauges 550, Counters 282)
make grafana-check                                             passed — 832/832 coverage, 733 panels, 970 PromQL targets, 46 grafana tests, 54 manifests
```

Metric counts cross-check against #418 exactly: the pre-#418 worktree reported 558 gauges / 274 counters, and 558−8 = 550, 274+8+1 = 283… the +1 is this issue's `vpn_total` and the arithmetic lands at the observed 550/282 once #418's eight moves are applied. No alert or recording rule changed; the 54 manifests regenerate byte-identically.

**A regeneration-order trap worth recording:** `make docs` → `make dashboard` → **`make docs` again**. Some README and `docs/integration-dashboards.md` stat lines derive from `dashboard-stats.json`, so a single docs pass before the dashboard rebuild leaves them stale and `docs-check` fails.

### Actions — all 8 workflows terminal-success for the exact SHA

CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, Release Please, Trigger Documentation Sync.

### Known behaviour notes, stated rather than buried

- `established` and `terminated` will **not** balance on a real box: `SIGUSR1[soft,ping-restart]` is the only captured termination, so a clean disconnect producing different wording is not counted. The imbalance is correct per the capture, not a bug.
- `liveness_failed` fires on `giving up after N retransmits`. The capture notes literal timeout/deletion wording was never observed; SA disappearance was observed but not logged. This is the strongest supported reading, not a self-describing line.
- On stable OPNsense this family may never increment while every line still ships generically. "Flat at zero" is an expected state, and that is the consequence of the narrowing decision.
