body:
### Theme and operator value

Record the transitions that explain a failover, not just the state visible at the next
scrape. Existing CARP and gateway gauges can miss a short flap entirely and do not
retain why a node demoted. Event counters make Prometheus alerting possible; structured
OTLP events provide the incident timeline and cause.

### Primary-source basis

- [OPNsense CARP status documentation](https://docs.opnsense.org/development/backend/carp.html)
  defines interface-down, announcement-send, pfsync, and service-health demotion
  causes and gives exact syslog examples for `carp demoted ... due to service
  disruption` and `carp promoted ... due to service recovery`.
- [OPNsense high availability](https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/hacarp.html) explains
  that CARP state is the mechanism that moves service between firewall nodes.
- [OPNsense gateways](https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/gateways.html) documents dpinger
  monitoring and gateway switching/failover behavior.
- Current OPNsense source routes `MASTER|BACKUP|INIT` CARP events through devd
  (`src/etc/devd/carp.conf:6-10` at upstream core
  `5c7830d6979ec4e0ee93ea8b12a20d7173c19c3c`).
- [OpenTelemetry event conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/events/)
  explicitly identify state changes and point-in-time outcomes as events; names must
  be low-cardinality and contain no dynamic values.

### Concrete repository gap

- Current metrics expose `opnsense_carp_demotion`,
  `opnsense_carp_vip_status`, gateway RTT/loss, and
  `opnsense_gateways_status` (`docs/metrics/metrics.md:104-110,393-409`) but only as
  scrape-time state.
- `internal/logship/syslog/registry.go:88-100` maps FRR and `dpinger` to coarse
  subsystems but registers no structured parser for them.
- `docs/syslog-receiver.md:237-240` confirms FRR, IPsec, OpenVPN, and catch-all
  programs still ship generically.
- The six current derived families in `internal/logship/syslog/derive.go:26-60` do not
  include gateway or HA continuity events.

### Proposed scope

Start with a capture gate. The official CARP demotion/promote lines are usable
fixtures, but dpinger alarm/recovery grammar must be captured from current stable and
development OPNsense before code is written.

Emit a closed event vocabulary such as:

- `opnsense.carp.demoted`
- `opnsense.carp.promoted`
- `opnsense.carp.state_changed`
- `opnsense.gateway.alarm_started`
- `opnsense.gateway.alarm_cleared`

Keep cause, service list, thresholds, loss, and latency as log attributes. Derived
metric labels should be limited to `component`, `event`, `reason_class`, and a
config/API-resolved gateway or interface name. Never put monitor IPs, raw service
lists, or message text in metric labels.

### Acceptance

- [x] Real dpinger alarm and recovery lines are captured before its parser is written;
      fixtures state the OPNsense versions that produced them.
- [ ] Official CARP demotion/recovery examples and captured MASTER/BACKUP/INIT lines
      parse into documented, closed event names.
- [x] Non-matching variants ship generically; parsing failure never drops a line.
- [ ] Cause and affected service/interface/gateway remain structured log metadata.
- [x] New derived counter labels are closed or configuration-derived and share the
      existing per-family key budget.
- [x] A flap that begins and clears between two API scrapes still increments both
      transition counters.
- [ ] Grafana shows present state beside event rate/reason; Prometheus rules alert on
      repeated flaps and unexpected demotions.
- [x] No FRR adjacency parser is included without a real adjacency-change capture.
- [x] Full test/lint/docs/Grafana gates pass.

### Dependencies and risks

dpinger wording and CARP program names may differ by OPNsense/FreeBSD version.
Reload/startup chatter can look like a state transition. Gateway names need
config-derived enrichment to stay bounded and useful. Counter alerts must use rates,
not absolute cumulative totals.

### Duplicate verdict

#257 only made these programs findable by subsystem/severity and explicitly deferred
an FRR adjacency parser until a real `AdjChg` line exists. #230 was the superseded
diagnostics-log polling lane. Neither preserves CARP/gateway transitions or derives
metrics. This proposal extends the shipped syslog architecture without reopening the
discarded polling transport.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Development capture preflight

Current VM102 (`27.1.a_40`) has two live `dpinger` workers on non-isolated LAN/WAN DHCP gateways. Those gateways will not be disturbed. CARP transition capture remains blocked because there is no second OPNsense node; the existing TESTLAN VIP is not evidence of a real `MASTER`/`BACKUP` transition.

A safe gateway alarm/clear capture is available on isolated TESTLAN:

1. Add a temporary, non-default TESTLAN gateway whose gateway and monitor are LXC105 (`<lan-ip-56>`). No route may reference it.
2. Capture RFC5424 `dpinger` output through a temporary TESTLAN-only TCP target.
3. On LXC105 only, temporarily drop ICMP echo requests from VM102 to produce the alarm.
4. Remove the dedicated nftables rule to produce the clear.
5. Remove the temporary gateway and target.

The run must prove the original gateways remain online and unchanged and CARP demotion remains zero. Stable-release format evidence is still unavailable; the retained 26.1 snapshot is not being represented as a current supported stable release.

## Stable-system retained-log evidence

A strictly read-only check of OPNsense `26.7.1_1` retained gateway/system logs found:

- 288 real `dpinger` records.
- 31 records using the stable alarm-status grammar:
  `dpinger: <gateway> (IP: <address> Alarm: <state> - <reason> RTT: <ms> ms ... Loss: <percent> %)`
- 19 records with a `down` state; all 31 contain a loss state.
- Zero clear, recovery, or explicit transition lines.

This supplies a real stable alarm fixture but does not satisfy the required alarm/clear pair or between-scrapes transition proof. Production was not triggered or modified; only retained logs were read. Development alarm/clear capture remains scheduled on isolated TESTLAN. CARP transitions remain capture-blocked without a second OPNsense node.

## Development dpinger capture complete

A temporary non-default, route-free TESTLAN gateway and dpinger-only RFC5424/TCP target on OPNsense `27.1.a_40` produced a real alarm and clear:

```text
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> dpinger <pid> - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] MONITOR: <gateway> (Addr: <address> Alarm: none -> down RTT: <milliseconds> ms RTTd: <milliseconds> ms Loss: <percent> %)
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> dpinger <pid> - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] MONITOR: <gateway> (Addr: <address> Alarm: down -> none RTT: <milliseconds> ms RTTd: <milliseconds> ms Loss: <percent> %)
```

Timeline:

- API scrape A: `16:14:20Z`, gateway Online.
- Scoped ICMP drop applied: `16:14:21Z`.
- Alarm record: `16:14:24Z`.
- Drop removed: `16:15:16Z`.
- Clear record: `16:15:26Z`.
- API scrape B: `16:16:15Z`, gateway Online.

Both transitions occurred between the normal API scrapes, proving the operator gap. The LXC rule dropped 32 packets and matched only VM102 TESTLAN echo requests. The private capture contained four temporary-gateway records; raw data was deleted after deriving the sanitized grammar.

Cleanup was independently read back: temporary gateway/target/config references absent, destination count zero, nft table/listener/scratch absent, original LAN/WAN gateways still the only dpinger processes and Online, CARP demotion zero, syslog healthy.

Implementation may now proceed for dpinger. #405 remains open: real CARP `MASTER`/`BACKUP`/`INIT` transitions still require the parked second node, and stable retained evidence still lacks a real recovery line.

## dpinger implementation checkpoint

Commit [`8ef49ed`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/8ef49ed847aa20bfecf47c1b0c1f838b61bc3b42) implements the evidence-backed gateway half of this issue.

- Parses only the OPNsense `27.1.a_40` capture forms `none -> down` and `down -> none`; unsupported or malformed `dpinger` lines remain generic records.
- Adds `opnsense_log_events_gateway_total{event,gateway,opnsense_instance}` with closed `event` values and the configured monitor name under the existing per-family key budget. Address, state, RTT, loss, sequence ID, and message text are not labels.
- Adds a Gateways & WAN transition-rate panel beside current gateway state.
- Adds `OPNsenseGatewayAlarmFlapping`, warning on three or more `alarm_started` transitions for one gateway in 15 minutes.
- Includes no FRR adjacency parser and makes no CARP claims.

Verification passed on the completing tree:

```text
go test ./...
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...
golangci-lint run ./...
make docs-check
make grafana-check
```

The generated catalogue covers 830/830 metrics, the dashboard has 730 panels, all 41 Grafana tests passed, and all 54 alert/recording-rule manifests validated.

#405 remains open. Real CARP `MASTER`/`BACKUP`/`INIT` transition capture still requires the parked second OPNsense node, so CARP parsing and unexpected-demotion alerting were not inferred or implemented.

## Authority blocker: #449 versus #460

The remaining CARP acceptance cannot proceed without a genuine HA peer. The binding #449 comment says: “Explicitly parked: standing up a second OPNsense devel box to produce a real CARP HA pair.” The later #460 body says: “Rob has confirmed he wants one” and explicitly scopes a second isolated OPNsense VM on `vmbr9`.

Those instructions conflict. Rob has been asked whether #460 supersedes #449. Recommendation: accept #460 as the controlled isolated path, then capture real MASTER/BACKUP/INIT transitions and only implement the evidence-backed #405 slice. Until Rob confirms, owner is Rob and the unblock condition is explicit authority to provision/mutate the second OPNsense VM under #460’s containment requirements.

No second VM or HA/CARP state has been created or changed.

## CARP transition evidence obtained — no second OPNsense node required

The remaining CARP acceptance is **unblocked by retained-log evidence alone**. A strictly read-only scan of the development box's retained system logs found **44 real kernel CARP records covering all three states**, produced by genuine historical events. No second VM was provisioned, no configuration was written, and no CARP state was forced.

### What was found

Box: OPNsense `27.1.a_40` (FreeBSD 15), single CARP VIP on the isolated TESTLAN bridge, `net.inet.carp.log=1` (the FreeBSD default).

Two distinct kernel grammars, program (APP-NAME) `kernel`:

```text
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> kernel - - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] <<kpri>>[<kuptime>] carp: <vhid>@<device>: INIT -> BACKUP (initialization complete)
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> kernel - - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] <<kpri>>[<kuptime>] carp: <vhid>@<device>: BACKUP -> MASTER (master timed out)
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> kernel - - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] <<kpri>>[<kuptime>] carp: <vhid>@<device>: MASTER -> INIT (hardware interface up)
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> kernel - - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] <<kpri>>[<kuptime>] carp: demoted by <delta> to <total> (pfsync bulk start)
<PRI>1 <timestamp> <host> kernel - - [meta sequenceId="<sequence>"] <<kpri>>[<kuptime>] carp: demoted by -<delta> to <total> (pfsync bulk fail)
```

Observed counts: `INIT -> BACKUP` 10, `BACKUP -> MASTER` 10, `MASTER -> INIT` 2, `demoted by <positive>` 11, `demoted by <negative>` 11.

**All three of `MASTER`, `BACKUP` and `INIT` appear as real observed transition endpoints.** The demotion pair supplies the "why a node demoted" data this issue said the gauges do not retain: a signed delta, a resulting total, and a cause.

Two load-bearing details for the parser:

1. The RFC5424 MSG field carries a **kernel prefix before `carp:`** — verbatim shape `<6>[754] carp: ...`, where `<6>` is the kernel's own priority and `[754]` its monotonic counter. A regex anchored directly on `carp:` will not match. The prefix must be tolerated and treated as optional.
2. The transition grammar originates in FreeBSD's `carp.c` `CARP_LOG` call in `carp_set_state`, so it is kernel-derived rather than OPNsense-derived. Records span 2026-07-12 through 2026-07-26T20:45:31+01:00 — the newest is on the current release, so this is current-generation evidence, not a stale snapshot.

### A second, config-derived source (recorded, not being parsed)

OPNsense's own CARP syshook also logs 22 real records under APP-NAME `opnsense`:

```text
/usr/local/etc/rc.syshook.d/carp/20-openvpn: Carp cluster member "<vip description> (<vip address>) (<vhid>@<device>)" has resumed the state "MASTER" for vhid <vhid>
```
(`MASTER` 10, `BACKUP` 10, `INIT` 2.)

This carries the admin's own VIP *description*, which would be an attractive bounded label. It is deliberately **not** being parsed in this slice: APP-NAME `opnsense` is a catch-all for every `log_msg()` call on the box, so claiming it for a parser puts an unbounded variety of unrelated lines through a CARP matcher, and the message is prefixed by whichever syshook script happened to emit it. The kernel source is authoritative, complete for all three states, and narrowly scoped. Recorded here so the option is not lost.

### Production has no CARP at all

Read-only check of production OPNsense `26.7.1_1`: **0 configured CARP VIPs and 0 retained kernel `carp:` records**, with `net.inet.carp.log=1`. There is therefore no stable-release CARP evidence to obtain, and none will be inferred. This matches the precedent already set by the shipped dpinger parser in `8ef49ed`, which parses captured development grammar only and ships unmatched lines generically.

### Frozen contract for the implementation slice

```text
opnsense_log_events_carp_total{event,from,to,interface,vhid,opnsense_instance}
```

- `event` closed: `state_changed` | `demoted` | `promoted`. A signed demotion delta decides the latter two — positive is `demoted`, negative is `promoted`.
- `from` / `to` closed and lowercased: `master` | `backup` | `init`, empty on a demotion record.
- `interface` is the OS device; `vhid` the configured VHID. Both empty on a demotion record, which names neither.
- The **cause** (`initialization complete`, `master timed out`, `hardware interface up`, `pfsync bulk start`, `pfsync bulk fail`) stays **structured log metadata and never a metric label** — it is an open-ended kernel string across FreeBSD versions, and bucketing it into a `reason_class` would be inventing a taxonomy no capture supports.
- Parser claims APP-NAME `kernel` and must return no-match for every non-CARP kernel line, of which there are many.

### Consequence for #460

The owner authorized building the second OPNsense VM to obtain this evidence. **That build is not needed for #405 and will not be done here** — the transition grammar already existed in retained logs, so the cheaper read-only path was taken instead.

#460 is a genuinely different requirement and remains open on its own terms: it covers *API payload* coverage (the five `hasync` metrics, `carp_vip_status` observed as `BACKUP` on a real peer, `remote_version_match` observed as `0`, and the unfalsifiable `hasyncVersion` `missingOK` exemption). None of that is reachable from syslog, and none of it is in scope for epic #449.

### State

No repository, configuration, service, CARP, or VM state was changed to obtain this evidence. Implementation is queued behind #406, which is concurrently editing the same shared seams (`registry.go`, `derive.go`, `logmetrics.go`, `logevents.go`); landing both at once would put two owners on one file.

## Delivered in [`f0f1a26`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/f0f1a26a115e527d11585d21f8c92fc8682db9e9) — all 8 workflows terminal-success

The CARP half is complete. The dpinger half shipped in `8ef49ed`. **No second OPNsense VM was built**, and none was needed.

### The blocker was not real

This issue had been parked on "genuine CARP transitions require the parked second node", and the owner had authorized building the #460 VM to get them. Investigating before provisioning found the evidence already existed: **44 real kernel CARP records in the development box's retained logs, covering all three states**, because `net.inet.carp.log` defaults to `1`. No configuration was written and no VM was created to obtain them.

`INIT -> BACKUP` ×10, `BACKUP -> MASTER` ×10, `MASTER -> INIT` ×2, plus 11 positive and 11 negative demotion records. Newest 2026-07-26T20:45:31+01:00 on OPNsense `27.1.a_40` — current-generation, not a stale snapshot.

**#460 remains valid on its own terms.** It covers *API payload* coverage — the five `hasync` metrics, `carp_vip_status` observed as `BACKUP` on a real peer, `remote_version_match` observed as `0`, and the unfalsifiable `hasyncVersion` `missingOK` exemption. None of that is reachable from syslog.

### Contract

```text
opnsense_log_events_carp_total{event,from,to,interface,vhid,opnsense_instance}
```

`event` closed: `state_changed` | `demoted` | `promoted`, the sign of the demotion delta deciding the latter two, with zero staying `demoted` since nothing was raised. `from`/`to` closed and lowercased through an **explicit map rather than `ToLower`**, so the vocabulary stays closed even if the regex is later loosened. States are anchored to the three literals rather than `\w+`, so an unknown future kernel state ships generically instead of minting a label value.

### The kernel prefix, which would have broken a naive parser

The RFC5424 MSG field is `<6>[754] carp: 9@vtnet2: INIT -> BACKUP (initialization complete)`. A regex anchored on `carp:` matches nothing. Both halves of the prefix are independently optional — proven by a real captured line from this repo's own `debugcapture_test.go` fixtures that carries the counter without the priority.

### Cause is metadata, never a label — four tests

`carp.reason`, `carp.demotion.delta` and `carp.demotion.total` are record attributes. The reason is an open-ended kernel string across FreeBSD versions, so bucketing it into a `reason_class` would invent a taxonomy no capture supports.

One test uses the **documented** service-disruption and service-recovery reasons plus an invented one, commented as *documentation-derived reasons inside a captured shape, not a new shape* — pinning the free-text property so any future attempt to close the reason into a vocabulary breaks there. The collector test asserts exactly 6 labels and explicitly rejects `reason`, `reason_class`, `cause`, `delta`, `total` and `demotion`.

### Claiming APP-NAME `kernel` — the standing risk, and its guard

A `kernel` parser sees every kernel line on the box. `parseCARP` declines everything that is not one of the two CARP shapes, and **23 unrelated kernel lines are pinned as not-claimed** — link state, ARP, ZFS, `carp0:` interface events, and near-misses like `BACKUP -> DEMOTED` and `demoted by two`.

That guard's RED came from a **deliberate mutation** of the fallthrough to `return rec, true`, not from test-before-implementation: a correctly-anchored regex already declines these, so no honest ordering yields a natural RED. All 23 fired under the mutation, which was then reverted. Disclosed as a deviation rather than presented as TDD.

### Alert thresholds, both moved off the obvious value

**`OPNsenseCARPUnexpectedDemotion` fires above 3 in 15 minutes, not above 0.** The evidence window recorded **11 `demoted by 240 (pfsync bulk start)`** records — demotion during pfsync bulk transfer is *routine cluster operation*, so `> 0` would page on a healthy cluster doing exactly what it should. One bulk cycle produces one `demoted` and one `promoted`, so the rate is effectively a bulk-cycle counter and four in fifteen minutes is churn. The reasoning and the observed counts are in a comment at the rule so nobody re-tightens it for sensitivity.

**`OPNsenseCARPStateFlapping` fires above 3, diverging from dpinger's above-2.** A boot is `INIT -> BACKUP -> MASTER` (two changes) and one failover is a single change, so four-or-more sits above one planned event. The divergence and its justification are recorded at the rule, because dpinger's threshold is calibrated for a different event shape and the inconsistency would otherwise read as an oversight.

### Production has no CARP at all

Read-only check of OPNsense `26.7.1_1`: **0 configured CARP VIPs, 0 retained kernel `carp:` records**, with `net.inet.carp.log=1`. There is no stable-release evidence to obtain and none was inferred — the same disposition the dpinger parser took.

The OPNsense syshook also logs 22 real records under APP-NAME `opnsense` carrying the admin's own VIP description, which would be an attractive bounded label. It is deliberately **not** parsed: `opnsense` is a catch-all for every `log_msg()` on the box. Recorded in `carp.go` and the docs so the option is not lost.

### Gate

```text
go test ./...                                                exit 0
go test -race ./internal/logship/... ./internal/collector/... exit 0
go vet / build / gofmt / golangci-lint                        clean, 0 issues
make docs-check                                              passed — 833 metrics (550 gauges / 283 counters)
make grafana-check                                           passed — 833/833 coverage, 737 panels, 971 targets + 101 variables, 101 grafana tests, 56 manifests
```

Every delta matched prediction exactly: +1 metric (a counter), +1 panel, +2 manifests, gauges unchanged.

### An integration finding worth recording

The regeneration order in this repo is **`make docs` → `make dashboard` → `make rules` → `make docs`**. This change was the first to add an alert rule, and it exposed that the final docs pass must follow `make rules`: some README and `docs/` stat lines derive from the alert and recording-rule counts as well as from `dashboard-stats.json`, so running docs before rules left `docs-check` failing. The order used earlier in this run happened to work only because no rule counts had moved.

body:
## Problem

Real OPNsense RFC5424 fixtures contain syslog-ng `meta.sequenceId`, which may make otherwise silent message gaps observable. Its reset, destination, reconnect, wrap, duplicate, and UDP reordering behavior must be validated live before the exporter treats a jump as loss.

## Evidence

- `internal/logship/syslog/envelope_test.go` contains a real `[meta sequenceId="590250"]` record, while `envelope.go` discards structured data.
- syslog-ng documents `${SEQNUM}` as a per-destination sequence that survives reloads and resets on restart.
- The receiver currently has no sequence field or transport-aware bounded state.

## Operator value

If validated, this can quantify gaps on UDP and detect truncation or discontinuity on TCP/TLS without exposing sender-controlled identity labels.

## Scope

- Capture contiguous, reconnect, reload, restart, duplicate, backward, wrap, and UDP reorder behavior in the actual OPNsense target configuration.
- Design bounded state keyed only by a safe, fixed stream identity such as listener/transport.
- If semantics hold, follow with closed-label missing/discontinuity counters and dashboard/alert coverage.
- Keep observed-time correction in the separate stage-correct freshness issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Live evidence records sequence scope and behavior for TCP, TLS, and UDP where enabled.
- [x] The analysis distinguishes proven missing sequence numbers from restart/reset/reorder cases.
- [x] A go/no-go decision and bounded state design are recorded.
- [x] Any implementation uses only a closed `transport` and `kind` vocabulary and never peer/hostname/sequence labels.
- [x] Arbitrary RFC5424 structured data remains excluded.

## Dependencies and risks

- Research first; do not ship counters from fixture inference alone.
- A hostile allowed sender must not create unbounded state or inflate arbitrary labelled series.

## Duplicate verdict

No matching issue exists. #260 rejected auto-configuration and #362 bounds debug capture; neither covers passive sequence-integrity research.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Read-only capture assessment: no-go for gap telemetry

VM 102 has genuine RFC5424 `meta.sequenceId` records but no configured remote syslog target (`target_count=0`), so there is no UDP/TCP/TLS receiver-path evidence.

The retained local firewall stream disproves the unsafe destination-wide assumption. On 2026-07-26 it contained 1,610 sequence-bearing records with first=1, last=4, min=1, max=18, 1,304 adjacent +1 steps and 305 backwards steps. `sequenceId=1` and `2` each occurred under 304 distinct PIDs. This is per-emitter reset/reuse evidence, not packet loss.

Current code also drops structured data and does not carry transport through the listener callback. The existing debug capture is not an evidence collector for this question because successfully parsed known records are deliberately not written.

Verdict: do not implement missing/reset/reorder counters from this evidence. The unmet requirement is an approved raw testbed capture, one target at a time over UDP, TCP, and TLS, recording transport plus connection/reload/restart lifecycle outside the exporter. Only then can sequence scope and a bounded state machine be decided. If IDs prove per-emitter or per-connection, the correct result is no loss counter.

No repository, testbed, production, or GitHub state other than this comment was changed.

## Live capture result: no-go for bounded sequence-gap telemetry

A controlled metadata-only capture ran on development OPNsense `27.1.a_40` / syslog-ng 4.12.0 over isolated TESTLAN. One temporary RFC5424 destination was used at a time.

| Transport | Frames | RFC5424 + sequence | Observed behavior |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| UDP | 1,194 | 1,194 | Reload stayed contiguous; two ordinary backward/reset transitions occurred. |
| TCP | 1,668 | 1,668 | Forced close/EOF/reconnect produced a backward/reset transition between connection generations. Reload stayed contiguous. |
| mutual TLS | 1,171 | 1,171 | Two authenticated connections; reload stayed contiguous. Reconnect and restart shared one boundary, so attribution is inconclusive. |

Receivers persisted only timestamps, fixed transport/lifecycle values, frame length/hash, RFC5424 validity, `meta.sequenceId`, and an in-memory-key HMAC pseudonym. They retained no message body, peer/address, hostname, arbitrary structured data, certificate material, or HMAC key. No stage reached its 8-minute, 12 MiB, or 100,000-frame cap.

### Decision

Do not implement sequence-gap counters:

- TCP reconnect contradicts a destination-wide `lastSeq` state.
- Per-connection or per-emitter state would require dynamic identity keys that the receiver does not expose safely and an allowed sender could inflate.
- UDP backward/reset observations mean a discontinuity cannot be distinguished from reordering/reset and therefore cannot be labelled as loss.
- The exercised `configctl syslog restart` did not replace the observed PID, so restart/reset semantics remain unproved.
- Wrap remains source-documented (`INT32_MAX` to 1), but practical capture is unavailable and does not rescue the unsafe identity model.

Arbitrary structured data remains excluded. No production function is being added from this research result.

### Cleanup and safety receipt

All temporary destinations and both TLS Trust sets were deleted; VM102 reports zero `issue-404` references and healthy syslog. The metadata-only LXC scratch directory was deleted. Coordinator readback found the final TLS receiver still listening despite the lane's initial cleanup report; PID 206141 was verified as the exact issue-404 receiver, terminated, and port 15516 was then confirmed closed.

During the first TLS setup attempt, an invalid pipeline printed a one-day test-only server private key into the tool transcript. It had never been used by a listener or destination. That certificate/CA/key set was immediately revoked and deleted and treated as compromised. The successful TLS run used an entirely fresh set transferred only by mode-0700/0600 file-copy operations; it was deleted after capture. No production credential was involved.

body:
## Problem

The flow pipeline can hold records briefly to learn parent/child VLAN relationships, but the production pair-gap distribution, peak occupancy, and value of subnet-evidence relabelling have not been measured. Changing the hold or relabel policy without that evidence risks either missed attribution or unnecessary memory.

## Evidence

- #357 left an order-independent subnet-evidence relabel alternative unfiled.
- #360 added the capture needed to measure it and started a live capture, but no later issue records pair-gap distribution, peak hold occupancy, or trunk records with subnet evidence and no child copy.

## Operator value

A bounded production measurement can justify a smaller/larger hold window, prove the current policy sufficient, or identify safe relabelling opportunities without guessing from synthetic traffic.

## Scope

- Analyse the existing privacy-preserving capture before changing code.
- Measure parent-child pair gaps, peak held-record/byte occupancy, and records with subnet evidence but no child copy.
- Only propose relabelling when evidence is strong; never drop uncertain records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The measurement method, capture window, sample counts, and privacy properties are recorded on the issue.
- [x] Pair-gap percentiles and peak hold occupancy are reported.
- [x] The count of subnet-evidence-without-child-copy cases is reported.
- [x] If that count is zero, the implementation idea is closed as unnecessary. **Not applicable — the count is 247,105, not zero, so the idea is justified and is implemented by #465.**
- [x] Any follow-on code issue states exact thresholds and pins order-independence tests.

## Dependencies and risks

- Evidence first. This issue does not authorize production behavior changes.
- Do not add address/subnet values as Prometheus labels or durable public fixtures.

## Duplicate verdict

Untracked measurement follow-up from #357/#360; no later issue records the result.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Capture assessment blocked by a biased retained sample

The real capture started under #360 was found on <host-1> and analysed read-only. It cannot satisfy this issue because the live deployment no longer has the recorded `all`/50 GiB capture configuration.

Verified current configuration:

```text
OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_FLOW_NETFLOW_DEBUG_CAPTURE=unidentified
OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_LOGS_DEBUG_CAPTURE_MAX_BYTES=256MiB
```

The bounded snapshot contained:

- 10 captured NetFlow v9 datagrams, 22,022 bytes of NDJSON;
- 210 decoded records and 0 decode errors;
- a 28h54m window;
- only `unknown_field` captures.

No topology-proven parent/child pair was present, so pair-gap p50/p95/p99/max are undefined, not zero. A 2-second sample-local hold model peaked at 21 candidate records and 1,670,038 bytes of record volume, but this is not a production occupancy or allocation measurement.

There were 39 trunk-ingress records with an endpoint in a VLAN-child prefix and no captured child copy. That number must not be used to justify relabelling: `unidentified` mode systematically excludes ordinary datagrams and captured no pair population.

Coordinator reproduction:

```text
go test -overlay=/tmp/opnsense-403/overlay.json ./cmd/flowanon -run '^TestAnalyze403$' -v
PASS
capture_frames=10 decoded=10 decode_errors=0 records=210 payload_bytes=13960
pair_hits=0 p50_gap_s=n/a p95_gap_s=n/a p99_gap_s=n/a max_gap_s=n/a
hold_model=2s unique-instance peak_records=21 peak_record_volume_bytes=1670038
subnet_evidence trunk_candidates=39 without_child_copy=39 child_prefixes=3
```

The raw base64 payloads retain real addresses and traffic patterns. They remain in temporary local storage only; no payload, address, or tuple was printed or committed.

This issue remains open. No hold-size change or subnet-evidence relabelling is justified by the retained sample. The unmet requirement is an explicitly approved, bounded, multi-hour `all` capture window, followed by the same analysis over its complete datagram population.

## Development capture started

A real all-datagram NetFlow capture is running on the <host-1> exporter for the VLAN-hold research.

- Capture ID: `issue-403-20260726T152015Z`
- Started: `2026-07-26T15:20:15Z`
- Automatic stop: `2026-08-02T15:20:15Z` (analysis may stop it earlier)
- Application capture cap: `50 GiB` (below the approved `100 GiB` maximum)
- Free-space safety floor: `200 GiB`
- Initial evidence: 1,186 captured datagrams; queue drops, capture buffer-full drops, cap drops, and write errors all zero
- Initial capture size: 3,046,803 bytes; free space: 1,282,167,340 KiB

A persistent 15-minute guard stops the window and restores the exact prior Compose configuration if the deadline or size/free-space bounds are reached, the container/metrics fail, configuration drifts, or any queue/capture write failure appears. The raw capture remains private on <host-1> and will not be committed.

Topology evidence checkpoint (read-only; capture remains active):

- Wrote a root-owned `0600` private topology snapshot beside the capture at `2026-07-26T18:03Z`.
- Snapshot scope is deliberately narrow: 15 interface-overview rows, 16 interface-config rows, 34 interface-statistic rows, 3 VLAN rows and the 10-entry active NetFlow ifIndex override. Unrelated API configuration was excluded.
- Snapshot integrity: 21,394 bytes, SHA-256 `98a1ec5fdec3228cc9391c95d09281388f2f8f605121b95c91ccf0ef4aaa7dbc`.
- Historical Prometheus label-set checks at capture start and the resumption guard boundary were identical: normalized `{device,interface,ifindex}` SHA-256 `2050f8b2cd0353d420bbb4aae9cb849f0174a008642b0110eade5914aa996134`, 17 series at both boundaries.

The historical check proves the ifIndex mapping stayed stable across the observed window. It does not by itself prove that current VLAN prefixes/parents were unchanged at capture start; the offline analysis will treat that separately and will record a blocker rather than infer historical topology from a current-only API snapshot. No raw address, subnet, tuple or payload was posted here.

## Measurement complete — all four acceptance criteria answered, and the answer is decisive

Analysis ran against the guarded production capture at 18h34m52s elapsed rather than the full seven days, which the capture design explicitly permitted ("analysis may stop it earlier"). The sample is large enough that every requested statistic is tight, and the result is unambiguous, so extending it to 2026-08-02 would have bought nothing while keeping production deviating from baseline.

### Method and privacy properties

A single throwaway Go test in package `flow` — deliberately **not committed**, per this issue's "evidence first, no behaviour change" scope. It:

1. parsed the real `topology-snapshot.json` (SHA-256 `98a1ec5fdec3228cc9391c95d09281388f2f8f605121b95c91ccf0ef4aaa7dbc`, unchanged from the value recorded at capture time) into an `ifTopology` double — VLAN parent/child from `vlan_settings`, per-child IPv4/IPv6 prefixes from `interface_config` (IPv6 filtered to non-link-local/deprecated/tentative), ifIndex→device from `netflow_ifindex_map`. WAN resolution was stubbed: none of the questions touch egress direction, so `EgressCorrected=0` is expected, not a finding;
2. streamed all 21 NDJSON files through one shared `netflow.Decoder` (keeping the v9 template cache warm) and **one real `Repairer(20000, 10000)`**, driving `repairWith` per record and `Release` per datagram exactly as `Processor.ObserveDatagram` does — so the occupancy figures are the real hold buffer's, not a model's;
3. built a separate full-capture-lifetime `instanceKey → occurrences` map, independent of the Repairer's TTL and capacity bounds, to find every pair regardless of whether the live Repairer still remembered it;
4. read the Repairer's internal `held`/`seen`/`vlanDropped` state directly (same package) for exact mechanism attribution.

Privacy: only aggregates are reported. Entities appear as `trunk_A`, `child_1..3`, assigned in sorted real-name order. An automated scan for IPv4, IPv6, MAC and known real device/VLAN-name patterns over the final output found no matches. Neither input was ever copied into the repository. Both local copies have since been deleted (receipt below).

### 1. Sample

290,147 datagram entries, **0** malformed or truncated lines, **0** decode errors (mine and the capture's own), 4 entries carrying a non-empty `unidentified` field. **6,177,984 records** decoded; the capture's own `records` metadata summed to 6,163,731, and the 195-record delta is fully explained by my decoder's cold-start template cache rather than any drift. One exporter. All NetFlow v9. Window **2026-07-26T15:20:22Z → 2026-07-27T09:55:14Z = 18h34m52s**. 604,049,967 bytes on disk, 402,014,252 raw datagram bytes.

Filename order matched received order at every file-rotation boundary, but **5,519 of 290,147 lines (1.9%) were out of order against their immediate neighbour** — filename order is a safe proxy at file granularity, not at record granularity. Worth knowing for any future analysis tool.

### 2. Pair population — emphatically non-zero

5,724,461 distinct instance keys; 447,497 seen in ≥2 distinct datagrams. Classified against real topology:

- **372,109 genuine trunk↔VLAN-child duplicates**
- 71,676 same-device repeats (the inter-VLAN double-hook shape, where both copies read in=trunk out=child)
- 1,398 same-key on unrelated interfaces — correctly **not** treated as duplicates
- 2,314 keys seen in >2 datagrams (excluded from the gap breakdown, still resolved by the live Repairer)

Multiplicity: `{1: 5,276,964, 2: 445,183, 3: 2,288, 4: 19, 5: 6, 6: 1}`. The `moreSpecific()` "neither side more specific" edge case occurred **0** times.

The earlier `unidentified`-mode sample reported `pair_hits=0` and undefined percentiles. That was a property of the biased capture mode, not of the traffic — this confirms it.

### 3. Pair gap

n = 372,109.

| statistic | ms |
| --- | --- |
| min | 0.0 |
| p50 | 953.7 |
| p90 | 4,056.1 |
| p95 | 5,712.9 |
| p99 | 31,172.8 |
| p99.9 | 68,059.3 |
| **max** | **108,481.2** |
| mean | 2,090.1 |

Trunk copy first: **283,578 (76.2%)**; child first: 88,531; simultaneous: 0. The repair-stage comment's claim of trunk-first in 12/12 of an earlier sample holds directionally but is far from absolute at scale.

**The current 2,000 ms `vlanHoldWindow` covers 70.8% of pairs. 29.2% (108,678) exceed it.**

### 4. Observed hold peak — from the real Repairer

- **Peak concurrent held records: 2,115** against the production `maxHeld` of 10,000 — **78.8% headroom**, `HoldOverflow = 0`. The hold buffer is comfortably sized for the current window.
- Peak held **record volume: 8,593,511,107 bytes**. To be precise about what that is: it is the sum of the *traffic byte counters* of the records held at that instant, **not memory footprint**. Memory is bounded by the 2,115-record peak and is small. A long-lived flow simply carries a large counter.
- Final stats: `VLANDuplicatesDropped 450,495 · EgressCorrected 0 · VLANChildPreferred 184,815 · HeldEntries 0 · HoldOverflow 0 · DedupeEntries 11,245 · DedupeEvicted 5,713,216 · DedupeCapped 0`.
- Mechanism split: **A (802.1Q tag) = 0**, B (hold contest) = 266,914, C (instance table) = 183,581. That reconciles exactly: 372,109 + 71,676 single-drop pairs + 6,710 extra drops from the 2,314 complex keys = 450,495. Mechanism A remaining dead confirms the earlier finding that this exporter never sets the VLAN tag.

### 5. Subnet-evidence-without-child-copy — 247,105, not zero

902,925 trunk-touching records matched exactly one VLAN child prefix (a further 5,914 matched ≥2 and were excluded as ambiguous). Of those, **247,105 had no child copy anywhere in the entire capture**:

| child | missing child copy | child copy present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| child_1 | 65,157 | 226,535 |
| child_2 | 7,230 | 9,839 |
| child_3 | 174,718 | 419,446 |

**This closes acceptance criterion 4 in the affirmative direction:** the count is not zero, so the implementation idea is *not* closed as unnecessary. These records cannot be fixed by any hold window of any size — there is no second copy to prefer.

### 6. Would order-independent subnet evidence have worked? Yes, unanimously

Over all 372,109 genuine pairs: **agree with the hold contest's winner 362,678 · disagree 0 · ambiguous (0 or ≥2 matching child prefixes) 9,431.**

Zero disagreements. Subnet evidence resolves on first sight with no wall-clock wait, so it eliminates the arrival-order dependency instead of racing it. The 9,431 ambiguous cases mean the hold must be **retained as a fallback**, not replaced.

### 7. Threshold recommendation — do not enlarge the window

The distribution is heavy-tailed (114x from p50 to max), so a safety-factor-over-max rule would demand an unusable multi-minute window. Two measurements say the window is the wrong lever:

- Occupancy scales with window length; the measured 2s peak of 2,115 linearly extrapolates to roughly 32,000 at a p99-covering ~31s window, far past the 10,000 cap — and past the cap `releaseOldestHeld` degrades records to first-seen-wins, which is the very failure being fixed. *(Extrapolation, not measurement — flagged as such.)*
- The observed max gap (108,481 ms) is **90% of the 120,000 ms dedupe TTL**. A window pushed into the tail runs into entries already expiring, which double-counts rather than misattributes.

**Recommendation: keep `vlanHoldWindow` at 2 s and add order-independent subnet-evidence attribution ahead of it**, retaining the hold for the 9,431 ambiguous cases.

### A correctness defect found while measuring

`Repairer.admit()`'s mechanism C — the `r.seen[key]` branch — **never calls `moreSpecific()`**. It returns `RepairDrop` for any proven duplicate unconditionally, so the first-admitted copy is permanently the reference. Verified directly against `internal/flow/repair.go`, not inferred from data.

Consequence: when a gap exceeds the hold window, the trunk copy is held, released, inserted into `seen`, and the arriving child copy is then dropped — attributing the flow to the trunk. **All 108,678 above-window pairs were trunk-first**, so this is systematic rather than a coin flip.

### Disposition

All four measurable acceptance criteria are answered and recorded. The fifth required a follow-on code issue stating exact thresholds and pinning order-independence tests — filed as **#465**, which carries the full distribution, the occupancy argument, the mechanism-C defect, and explicit order-independence acceptance tests.

This issue authorized no behaviour change and none was made. Closing.

## Capture stopped early, baseline restored, apparatus fully torn down

Stopped deliberately at 18h34m52s rather than running to the 2026-08-02 deadline: the measurement is complete and decisive, so continuing to hold production away from its baseline configuration bought nothing.

### How it was stopped

Via the guard's **own** tested `finish()` code path, not an improvised teardown — the deadline in `/var/lib/opnsense-exporter-issue403/active` was brought forward and `opnsense-exporter-issue403-monitor.service` was started exactly as its timer would. **The `finished` receipt therefore records `reason=deadline_reached`, which is literally true but would mislead without this note: the stop was operator-initiated because analysis was complete, not a bound being hit.** No size, free-space, container, drift, or queue-loss condition ever tripped; the last two healthy checks logged 615,907,729 and 625,198,810 bytes with ~1.28 TB free.

```text
capture_id=issue-403-20260726T152015Z
stopped_at=2026-07-27T10:32:27Z
reason=deadline_reached
```

### Restoration, verified rather than assumed

- `docker-compose.yml` is **byte-identical** to `docker-compose.yml.bak.PRE-issue-403-20260726T152015Z` (`cmp -s`).
- Container environment back to baseline, read from the live container: `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_FLOW_NETFLOW_DEBUG_CAPTURE=unidentified`, `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_LOGS_DEBUG_CAPTURE_MAX_BYTES=256MiB`, `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_LOGS_DEBUG_CAPTURE_DIR=/capture`.
- Container running, restarted 2026-07-27T10:32:27Z; `/metrics` returns HTTP 200.
- Teardown refused to proceed unless compose matched the backup first — an explicit guard, since API/command acceptance is not proof.

### Teardown by exact identity, with absence read back

Inventoried before deletion, then verified absent after:

| object | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/opt/opnsense-exporter/capture/issue-403-20260726T152015Z` | 628,291,533 bytes, 26 files | absent |
| `docker-compose.yml.bak.PRE-issue-403-20260726T152015Z` | present | absent |
| `/var/lib/opnsense-exporter-issue403/` | `active.bak`, `finished` | absent |
| `/usr/local/sbin/opnsense-exporter-issue403-monitor` | present | absent |
| `opnsense-exporter-issue403-monitor.timer` / `.service` units | present, enabled | absent, `systemctl list-unit-files` matches 0 |
| `/var/lib/systemd/timers/stamp-…-issue403-monitor.timer` | present | absent |

A filesystem-wide sweep for `*issue403*` / `*issue-403*` now returns only unrelated Go compiler test files inside Docker layers (`issue40301.go` and similar match the glob by prefix). `/opt` free space recovered to 1,279,519,036 KiB.

### Private data destroyed

The raw capture held real production addresses and traffic tuples. It is deleted on <host-1>, and the local temporary copies used for offline analysis — the capture tree and the topology snapshot — are deleted too, verified absent. Nothing was ever committed to the repository, and the throwaway analysis harness was deliberately not committed either.

**Consequence, stated plainly:** these numbers cannot be re-derived without a fresh approved capture. That is why the full distribution, occupancy figures, mechanism attribution and per-child breakdowns are written out in the measurement comment above and carried into **#465** rather than left as a pointer to a file that no longer exists.

### Disposition

Every acceptance criterion is met: method/window/counts/privacy recorded, pair-gap percentiles and peak hold occupancy reported, the subnet-evidence-without-child-copy count reported as **247,105** (so the implementation idea is justified, not closed as unnecessary), and the follow-on code issue **#465** filed with exact measured thresholds and explicit order-independence acceptance tests.

This issue authorized evidence only and no behaviour change was made. `main` is untouched by #403. Closing.

### Problem and value

The queue is bounded by both count and bytes, but the near-capacity alert watches

error panels/alerts incorrectly say every failed attempt loses records even

metrics, reasons, and labels.

The result is a green-looking queue while byte eviction is active, noisy/false
loss language during recoverable retries, and an operator guide that no longer
describes the code.

### Evidence

  1% while byte occupancy reaches budget.
- `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:167-172`: near-capacity alert uses count ratio
  only.
- `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:160-166`: sink-error alert says failed attempts
  mean records are being lost.

body:
**Priority/confidence:** P2, certain.

### Problem and value

Connection-cap refusals and TLS handshake failures happen before a record
exists. They are logged but never counted, so a capacity attack, stalled TLS
client, invalid client certificate, or mTLS configuration mismatch is
invisible to `/metrics` and cannot be alerted on. High-rate cap refusals also
emit one warning per connection without rate limiting.

### Evidence

- `internal/logship/syslog/listener.go:333-340`: plaintext cap refusal logs and
  closes only.
- `internal/logship/syslog/listener.go:381-388`: TLS cap refusal logs and closes
  only.
- `internal/logship/syslog/listener.go:411-442`: deadline setup/clear failures
  and TLS handshake failure return false without a receiver metric; handshake
  failure is debug-only.
- `internal/logship/syslog/source.go:27-42`: closed rejection vocabulary has
  only `peer`, `oversized`, `filtered`, and `sampled`.
- `internal/logship/recvmetrics.go:34-85`: the shared receiver metric already
  supports pre-initialized closed reasons.
- #328 acceptance explicitly required “Handshake timeout and rejection metrics
  are explicit.” The timeout shipped; the rejection metrics did not.

### Implementation scope

- Add closed reasons for connection-cap and TLS-handshake rejection. A bounded
  split between timeout and authentication/configuration failure is reasonable
  if it is code-derived; never put peer/certificate/error text in labels.
- Count TCP and TLS cap refusals.
- Count TLS timeout, failed authentication, and local deadline setup/clear
  failures at the right stage.
- Rate-limit refusal logs with a bounded key set.
- Add dashboard/alert/docs coverage after `fix(logship): give every self-metric stable instance identity` supplies stable instance
  identity.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Plain TCP and TLS cap refusals increment a pre-initialized closed reason.
- [ ] TLS timeout and invalid/missing-client-certificate failures are counted.
- [ ] Local deadline setup/clear failure is observable.
- [ ] No peer address, certificate identity, or raw error becomes a metric
      label.
- [ ] Repeated refusals cannot flood logs unboundedly.
- [ ] Focused cap, stalled-handshake, and mTLS tests assert exact counts.
- [ ] Dashboard/docs expose the new reasons.

### Duplicate verdict

This is incomplete #328 acceptance, not a novel broad security finding.
Recommendation: reopen #328 and finish the unchecked contract, or file one
narrow corrective issue explicitly linked to #328 if closed issues are treated
as immutable.

body:
**Priority/confidence:** P2, certain.

### Problem and value

The stateful splitter skips and counts oversized octet-counted frames, but a
newline-delimited frame larger than the scanner buffer causes terminal
`bufio.Scanner: token too long`. The connection closes, no `oversized`
rejection is counted, and the next valid frame on that connection never
arrives. A nominally valid 64 KiB frame can also fail because the scanner buffer
must hold its delimiter or octet-count prefix in addition to the payload.

This is exactly the failure mode the framing comments and #248 acceptance said
must not happen.

### Evidence

- `internal/logship/syslog/framing.go:8-12`: 64 KiB is the advertised per-frame
  cap and scanner errors are acknowledged as terminal.
- `internal/logship/syslog/framing.go:41-53,109-118`: newline framing has no
  oversized state; it requests more data until a newline/EOF appears.
- `internal/logship/syslog/framing.go:88-106,128-187`: only an
  octet-count-declared oversize enters the counted stateful skip path.
- `internal/logship/syslog/listener.go:468-471`: scanner maximum buffer is
  exactly `maxMessageBytes`.
- `internal/logship/syslog/listener.go:507-511`: scanner error is debug-logged
  and the connection closes; no rejection metric increments.
- `internal/logship/syslog/framing_test.go:72-108` and
  `listener_test.go:150-172`: oversize tests are octet-counted only.
- #248 acceptance required “oversized frame skips-and-counts rather than
  killing the connection.”

### Implementation scope

Replace the newline Scanner path with a bounded reader/state machine that can
discard through newline and recover the next frame, or otherwise give framing
logic explicit payload-plus-delimiter headroom while classifying and draining
oversize input. Keep memory bounded and preserve fragmented-read behavior.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] A newline-framed payload above 64 KiB increments
      `logs_rejected_total{source="syslog",reason="oversized"}` exactly once.
- [x] The same TCP/TLS connection delivers the next valid frame.
- [x] Payload boundary cases `cap-1`, `cap`, and `cap+1` are pinned for LF,
      CRLF, and octet-counted framing, including prefix/delimiter overhead.
- [x] Fragmented and one-byte-at-a-time reads recover correctly.
- [x] Existing octet-counted oversized behavior remains counted and
      connection-safe.
- [x] No unbounded allocation is introduced.

### Duplicate verdict

Do not file this as another broad receiver feature. It is a narrow regression
against a specific #248 acceptance item. Prefer a focused bug referencing #248
(or reopen #248 if the tracker convention favors repairing incomplete
acceptance in place).

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
Delivered in `b64a7902e982c6619fa47a115349f9c55da88079` and pushed to `main`.

Newline and octet-counted framing now share the 64 KiB payload limit. Oversized newline input is discarded through its terminator, counted once, and the same TCP connection resumes at the next valid frame. Scanner headroom covers legal payloads plus framing bytes.

Verification: boundary, fragmented-read, oversized-recovery, and live same-connection tests passed; the syslog package passed under `-race`; full Phase 1 repository gate passed.

body:
**Priority/confidence:** P2, certain; small implementation.

### Problem and value

An RFC5424 frame whose structured-data element starts with `[` but never closes
is accepted as a valid record with an empty message. The normal “parse error
ships original raw bytes” path never runs, so the original content is lost.

### Evidence

- `internal/logship/syslog/envelope.go:156-187`: the inner loop reaches
  `i == len(b)` when no `]` is present.
- `internal/logship/syslog/envelope.go:188-193`: only `i > len(b)` is treated as
  truncated; `i == len(b)` returns valid “SD only, no MSG.”
- `internal/logship/syslog/envelope.go:148-153`: `ParseEnvelope` accepts the
  empty message.
- `internal/logship/syslog/source.go:200-220`: raw fallback runs only when
  `ParseEnvelope` returns an error.
- `internal/logship/syslog/envelope_test.go:125-150`: malformed cases omit
  unclosed structured data.
- `internal/logship/syslog/envelope_test.go:153-164`: coverage includes only
  valid escaped `]`.

### Implementation scope

Track whether each bracketed element encountered a real closing `]`. Return
`errTruncated` on EOF before closure or a dangling escape, while preserving the
valid RFC5424 case where a correctly closed structured-data element ends
exactly at EOF with no MSG.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Unclosed RFC5424 structured data returns a parse error.
- [x] A dangling structured-data escape returns a parse error.
- [x] The receiver then emits the exact original raw line and increments
      `parse_errors{stage="envelope"}`.
- [x] Correct SD-only input, nil SD, multiple elements, and escaped `\]`, `\"`,
      and `\\` remain valid.
- [x] Fuzz/no-panic coverage includes bracket/escape truncation.

### Duplicate verdict

New. No archived issue covers truncated RFC5424 structured data.

**Priority/confidence:** P1 for multi-box deployments, certain.

### Problem and value

The collector metrics use `opnsense_instance`; the logship self-metrics do not.
Dashboard selectors therefore cannot honor the instance variable and aggregate
multiple exporters together. The cursor alert takes `max by (source)`, so one
healthy or future-dated box masks a stalled box with the same source.

This is already documented in code as a known limitation, but there is no issue
that fixes it. It makes the Log Shipping and Zenarmor operational views
misleading as soon as more than one OPNsense exporter is present.

### Evidence

- `internal/logship/metrics.go:33-45,80-96`: pipeline metrics have source/reason
  labels but no stable instance label.
- `internal/logship/recvmetrics.go:28-69`: shared receiver parse/reject metrics
  carry only source plus stage/reason.
- `grafana/builder.py:518-522`: `sel_pipeline` deliberately omits the dashboard
  instance matcher because these metrics lack `opnsense_instance`.
- `grafana/tabs/logs.py:13-16`: the whole Log Shipping tab uses that workaround.
- `grafana/tabs/zenarmor.py:12-16`: the source explicitly says these metrics
  aggregate across exporter instances.
- `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:182-188`: `max by (source)` drops every instance
  identity and can cross-mask.
- #301 called this a “latent bug” and shipped a selector workaround; it did not
  add identity to the metric family.
- `logship.Start` already receives `instance` at
  `internal/logship/pipeline.go:69-75`, so the value is available.

### Implementation scope

- Apply a stable `opnsense_instance` const label to every
  `opnsense_exporter_logs_*` metric, including pipeline, receiver, Zenarmor
  receiver, enrichment, and debug-capture metrics.
- Prefer one wrapped registerer or one shared constructor seam so new
  self-metrics cannot omit it.
- Preserve shared `CounterVec` reuse across receivers and zero
  pre-initialization.
- Make dashboard selectors honor `$opnsense_instance`.
- Group alerts by instance and source; never aggregate a liveness verdict across
  boxes.
- Verify both scraped Prometheus and the OTLP metrics bridge use the same label.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `opnsense_exporter_logs_*` series carries
      `opnsense_instance` in scrape and OTLP ingestion.
- [ ] Selecting one dashboard instance excludes all other exporters' logship
      self-metrics.
- [ ] A healthy box cannot mask a stalled box's source-freshness alert.
- [ ] Alert summaries identify the affected instance and source.
- [ ] Two receivers still share their parse/reject collectors without duplicate
      registration.
- [ ] Healthy zero-series pre-initialization remains intact.
- [ ] A catalogue/contract test fails when a new logship self-metric omits the
      instance label.

### Duplicate verdict

New. #301 deliberately worked around and documented the missing label; it did
not remediate it.

body:
**Priority/confidence:** P1, high confidence.

### Problem and value

`logs_last_event_timestamp_seconds` is documented and alerted as the last event
shipped, but it is advanced immediately after queue admission using the
source-origin timestamp. It can move before export acknowledgement, regress on
out-of-order input, and be pushed into the future by a sender-controlled syslog
timestamp. OTLP `ObservedTimestamp` is then assigned at export attempt time, so
it changes on retry instead of recording when the exporter first observed the
event.

The current stalled-source alert can therefore look healthy while the sink is
backed up, and an admitted syslog sender can suppress it with a future
timestamp. Old/out-of-order events can also create false stalls.

### Evidence

- `internal/logship/push.go:78-99`: after enqueue succeeds, the gauge is set
  directly to `Record.Timestamp`, before sink export.
- `internal/logship/pipeline.go:258-281`: poll sources likewise update it after
  enqueue, using the newest origin timestamp in that poll.
- `internal/logship/pipeline.go:331-340`: actual acknowledgement occurs later.
- `internal/logship/metrics.go:117-120`: help says “most recent event shipped.”
- `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go:188-208`: `ObservedTimestamp` is `time.Now()` at
  each `Emit` attempt.
- `grafana/tabs/logs.py:66-72` and
  `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:182-188`: dashboard and alert interpret the
  gauge as shipped/source liveness.
- `internal/options/logs_syslog.go:32-52`: when syslog is enabled, UDP listens on
  all interfaces by default and an empty peer allowlist accepts any sender;
  origin timestamps are therefore not a trustworthy process-health clock.
- OpenTelemetry defines `Timestamp` as origin-clock event time and
  `ObservedTimestamp` as collection-system observation time that should be set
  once:
  [logs timestamp fields](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/#field-timestamp).

### Implementation scope

- Add an observed/received timestamp to `Record` or `Entry`, stamped once when
  the exporter accepts the event and preserved through queueing and retries.
- Split the ambiguous metric into stage-specific names:
  `logs_last_received_timestamp_seconds{source}` using the exporter clock and
  `logs_last_exported_timestamp_seconds{source}` on acknowledgement.
- If origin-event freshness remains useful, expose it under an explicit name
  and monotonic/max policy; never use it as process/source health.
- Set OTLP `ObservedTimestamp` from the preserved receive time, not each export
  attempt.
- Update dashboard panels, alerts, metric help, and prose. Sequence the alert
  update with `fix(logship): give every self-metric stable instance identity` so one instance cannot mask another.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A future origin timestamp cannot suppress source-receive or
      export-freshness alerts.
- [ ] Out-of-order and zero origin timestamps cannot regress process-clock
      freshness metrics.
- [ ] `ObservedTimestamp` is stamped once at collection and remains byte-for-byte
      stable across retries.
- [ ] Receive freshness advances only when input is admitted.
- [ ] Export freshness advances only for acknowledged delivery outcomes.
- [ ] Queued, failed, terminally dropped, and retried records have focused
      stage-semantic tests.
- [ ] Metric names, help, dashboard descriptions, alert descriptions, and docs
      describe the same stages.
- [ ] The old gauge has an explicit compatibility/deprecation decision.

### Duplicate verdict

New. #290 made `logs_shipped_total` acknowledgement-based but did not change
the last-event gauge or OTLP observed-time semantics. #301 built the current
alert on the misleading gauge.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
Core timestamp semantics landed in `adabcad01e4622203dc4fee6074fefe4c95f7b22` (`Refs #394`).

`Entry.Received` is stamped once at admission and preserved through retry; OTLP `ObservedTimestamp` uses it. The ambiguous old gauge is removed and replaced by exporter-clock received/exported gauges, with exported freshness advancing only for acknowledged entries. Focused queued, retry, rejection, zero/future/out-of-order, and acknowledgement tests are green.

This issue remains open for #400, which owns the generated Grafana selectors/panels/alerts and final operational documentation reconciliation.

Completed by e0b497db91960573305392c0ab6271e7ee900d73, on top of the stage-correct metric implementation in adabcad.

The dashboard, alert rules, and operator guide now consume logs_last_received_timestamp_seconds as exporter-clock queue admission and logs_last_exported_timestamp_seconds as exporter-clock sink acknowledgement. No operational surface reads source event time as liveness, and the removed last_event metric has no remaining dashboard or alert reference.

Verification: the focused Grafana tests, generated manifest validation, make docs-check, and make grafana-check all passed.

body:
**Priority/confidence:** P1, high confidence.

### Problem and value

The `MetricSink` contract says receiver calls must be non-blocking, but the
concrete store takes one global mutex. A Prometheus scrape holds that same mutex
while copying every live tuple from all seven metric families. Syslog UDP calls
the sink synchronously on the socket-read goroutine.

At default cardinality this can pause the read loop while tens of thousands of
map entries are copied. With `--logs.max-metric-keys=0`, the pause is unbounded
by configuration. UDP datagrams lost from the kernel socket during that pause
never reach the pipeline queue, so no existing drop/reject counter can account
for them.

### Evidence

- `internal/logship/logmetrics.go:30-31`: `MetricSink` implementations must be
  non-blocking because calls run on receiver read goroutines.
- `internal/logship/syslog/source.go:194-200,262-265`: syslog calls
  `observeDerived` synchronously from `handle`.
- `internal/logship/syslog/listener.go:285-306`: `serveUDP` calls the handler
  directly in the socket read loop.
- `internal/collector/logevents.go:66-89`: all seven families share one mutex.
- `internal/collector/logevents.go:123-169`: every `Observe*` takes that mutex.
- `internal/collector/logevents.go:286-320`: scrape `Update` takes the same mutex
  and copies every family's entire live map before unlock.
- `internal/collector/logevents.go:60-80`: default is 5,000 keys per family and
  zero disables the cap.
- The `Update` comment at `internal/collector/logevents.go:298-301` only proves
  metric channel emission occurs after unlock; the full map copy still happens
  under lock.

### Implementation scope

Preferred direction: a bounded, non-blocking observation handoff with one
consumer owning the maps. Make each observation report whether it was accepted.
Sampling may drop a raw line only after the corresponding derived observation
was accepted. A full handoff must therefore keep the raw record, increment a
closed-label observation-drop/pressure counter, and avoid inventing a
successfully-counted result.

A different design is acceptable if it gives the receiver call a deterministic
upper bound and cannot wait behind a scrape. Merely sharding the current mutex
reduces contention but does not satisfy the stated non-blocking contract.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every syslog and Zenarmor derived-metric observation has a deterministic,
      non-blocking receiver-side path even while scrape collection is stalled.
- [ ] Handoff saturation is counted with a closed, code-defined label set.
- [ ] Syslog sampling never drops a record whose derived observation was not
      accepted.
- [ ] Normal-load totals remain exact, including cardinality-overflow totals.
- [ ] A focused concurrency test stalls scrape/snapshot work and proves
      receiver-side observation returns immediately.
- [ ] A benchmark records steady-state observation cost and allocation count.
- [ ] `go test -race` covers the store, syslog sampling path, and Zenarmor
      derivation.

### Dependencies and risks

The return value is load-bearing for sampling. An asynchronous queue that
silently drops observations would turn a receiver-protection fix into metric
loss and permit sampled raw lines to disappear uncounted.

### Duplicate verdict

New. #311/#326 bounded attacker-controlled tuple growth. They did not remove
scrape/receiver lock contention or make kernel-level UDP loss observable.
#286 benchmarks enrichment, not the derived-metric sink.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
Completed by e0b497db91960573305392c0ab6271e7ee900d73.

The derived-metric store now uses a bounded 65,536-command non-blocking handoff with one map-owning goroutine. Receiver admission reports success, handoff saturation increments opnsense_log_events_observation_dropped_total{reason="handoff_full"}, and syslog retains a sample-eligible raw record when its derived observation was refused.

Verification:
- focused concurrency and saturation tests passed, including 500 repeated saturation runs
- race tests passed for collector, syslog, and Zenarmor paths
- steady-state benchmark: 31.79 ns/op, 0 B/op, 0 allocs/op with every timed observation accepted
- go test ./..., CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./..., golangci-lint run ./..., make docs-check, and make grafana-check passed
- the metric is visible on the Log-derived Events dashboard tab and covered by the operations-surface guard

body:
**Priority/confidence:** P1, high confidence. The cross-resource replay is
certain from control flow. The partial-success behavior is confirmed against
the pinned exporter and current OTLP contract.

### Problem and value

One logical pipeline batch is split among resource-specific logger providers.
Those providers are flushed one by one, but any error causes the pipeline to
retry the original whole batch. This can duplicate already-acknowledged
partitions. A populated OTLP partial-success response is also surfaced as an
error by the pinned exporter, so the same generic retry resends accepted
records even though OTLP explicitly forbids retrying that request. Permanent
HTTP/gRPC failures are retried as though transient.

For log/SIEM data this is a data-integrity bug, not harmless retry noise:
duplicate firewall/security events inflate downstream counts, while the
exporter's own `shipped`/`dropped` metrics can claim an entire logical batch was
lost even when some records were accepted one or more times.

### Evidence

- `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go:117-149`: each resource provider buffers its
  own records; `export` removes that buffer before calling the shared exporter.
- `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go:183-234`: `Emit` builds a `touched` map and
  flushes every provider in nondeterministic map order, joining errors into one
  undifferentiated result.
- `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go:225-227`: the comment explicitly says every
  non-nil result means whole-batch retry.
- `internal/logship/pipeline.go:331-368`: every non-nil sink error retries the
  original `[]Entry`; no acknowledged subset or error class exists.
- `internal/logship/delivery_test.go:85-110`: delivery tests cover only an
  all-or-nothing transient failure.
- `internal/logship/sink_otlp_test.go:144-174`: resource partitioning is
  tested, but no test makes one partition succeed and a sibling fail.
- `go.mod:13-20`: OTLP logs are pinned at `v0.20.0`.
- `vendor/.../otlploghttp/client.go:212-275`: HTTP partial success becomes an
  export error; only 429/502/503/504 are internally retryable.
- `vendor/.../otlploggrpc/client.go:171-187,258-285`: gRPC partial success
  becomes an export error and status codes are classified before return.
- OTLP requires clients not to retry populated partial-success responses,
  requires non-retryable errors to be dropped and counted, and permits HTTP
  retry only for 429/502/503/504:
  [OTLP response and failure rules](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otlp/#otlpgrpc-response).

### Concrete failure cases

1. Resource A flushes successfully, resource B fails after exporter retries.
   `Emit` returns an error; the pipeline resends A and B. A is duplicated.
2. One resource request accepts 90 records and rejects 10 using
   `partial_success`. The pinned exporter returns an error. The pipeline retries
   all 100, contrary to OTLP, duplicating accepted records on every attempt.
3. The endpoint returns HTTP 400 or gRPC `Unauthenticated`. The OTLP exporter
   correctly does not retry internally, then the outer pipeline repeats the
   permanent request up to `--logs.ship-max-attempts` (default 10).

### Implementation scope

- Replace the `Sink.Emit(...) error` all-or-nothing seam with an outcome that can
  distinguish acknowledged entries/partitions, retryable entries/partitions,
  and terminally rejected counts.
- Flush resource partitions in deterministic `resourceKey` order and retry only
  the unacknowledged retryable partition(s).
- Treat populated OTLP partial success as terminal for that exact request: do
  not resend it; count accepted and rejected quantities without pretending the
  protocol identifies which individual records were rejected.
- Treat permanent HTTP/gRPC responses as one terminal attempt. Preserve bounded
  retry for genuinely transient failures.
- Add a supported error-classification seam. The Go exporter currently keeps
  its typed partial-success and HTTP retry marker under `internal/`; do not
  parse error strings. This may require a small transport wrapper, an upstream
  public type/capability, or a narrower OTLP client seam.
- Keep stdout behavior simple and explicitly all-or-nothing.
- Update delivery-contract prose and self-metric help.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] If partition A is acknowledged and sibling B fails, retry sends B only;
      A is never emitted twice.
- [ ] HTTP and gRPC populated partial-success responses are never retried.
- [ ] Partial-success accepted/rejected counts reconcile exactly once in
      self-metrics.
- [ ] HTTP 400 and gRPC `InvalidArgument`/`Unauthenticated` are terminal and
      counted without repeated wire attempts.
- [ ] Transient HTTP 429/502/503/504 and retryable gRPC failures remain bounded
      and recover without loss.
- [ ] Partition flush order is deterministic and tested.
- [ ] `logs_shipped_total`, `logs_dropped_total`, and
      `logs_ship_errors_total` reconcile the logical records without counting
      acknowledged records as dropped.
- [ ] No implementation relies on matching vendor error text.
- [ ] Focused HTTP, gRPC, multi-resource, shutdown, and retry tests pass under
      `-race`.

### Dependencies and risks

This changes the `Sink`/pipeline seam and must land before prose/alert cleanup.
The main risk is replacing duplicate delivery with silent undercounting.
Partial success reports a rejected count, not record identities, so acceptance
must be count-accurate without claiming per-record knowledge the protocol does
not supply.

### Duplicate verdict

New. #290 removed the unobservable asynchronous SDK queue and established
synchronous acknowledgement, but it retained a single generic error for the
whole logical batch. #325 bounded poison-batch retries; it did not classify
OTLP outcomes or preserve already-acknowledged resource partitions.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
Delivered in `adabcad01e4622203dc4fee6074fefe4c95f7b22` (pushed to `main`).

The sink now returns acknowledged, retryable, and terminally rejected entry sets. Resource partitions flush deterministically; acknowledged siblings are removed before retry; populated HTTP/gRPC partial success and permanent protocol failures are terminal; and transient failures retain bounded retry. Self-metrics reconcile each logical record exactly once.

Verification:
- real HTTP 503 → 200 recovery test — retry succeeds without loss
- real gRPC `Unavailable` → success test — retry succeeds without loss
- HTTP 400 and gRPC `InvalidArgument`/`Unauthenticated` tests — one terminal wire attempt
- multi-resource sibling failure test — acknowledged partition never resent
- partial-success tests — accepted/rejected counts reconciled once
- `go test -race ./internal/logship -count=1` — pass
- `go test ./...` — pass
- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` — pass
- `golangci-lint run ./...` — 0 issues
- `make docs-check` — pass
