body:
## Problem

Newer NetBird clients expose an optional session-expiry deadline that can warn before a firewall loses overlay connectivity. OPNsense currently packages NetBird 0.74.4, whose overview payload does not contain the field, so this must be version- and capture-gated rather than guessed from current schema exemptions.

## Evidence

- The OPNsense ports tree audited on 2026-07-25 packages NetBird 0.74.4.
- NetBird v0.74.4 `OutputOverview` has no `sessionExpiresAt`; current NetBird master does expose an optional UTC deadline.
- `opnsense/testdata/schemas/exemptions.json` lists the key prospectively, but that is not evidence that the packaged version emits it.

## Operator value

Once available upstream, operators can renew or reauthenticate before the overlay session expires instead of discovering the problem after peer connectivity disappears.

## Scope

- Track the OPNsense-packaged NetBird version and capture the enrolled overview payload after it includes the field.
- Add a timestamp gauge and bounded health/alert semantics only after the wire value is proven.
- Remain fully compatible with older packages: absence means unsupported, not expired.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A source/version check proves the packaged OPNsense NetBird release contains the field.
- [ ] A live enrolled fixture proves its exact wire format and timezone semantics.
- [ ] Older or field-absent payloads emit no fabricated expiry metric or alert.
- [ ] The metric uses a timestamp value, not session or peer identity labels.
- [ ] Dashboard, alert, schema, and generated documentation coverage is added with full gates green.

## Dependencies and risks

- Blocked until OPNsense packages a containing NetBird release and the live field is captured.
- Do not expose node keys, FQDNs, profile names, or other identity-bearing topology data.

## Duplicate verdict

No current tracker issue implements session expiry. This is deliberately future-gated rather than a claim that the present API is missing data.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Closing as won't-do: structurally unavailable via the plugin, not merely a version lag

Investigated live on the dev box. There are **two** independent blockers, and the second one does not go away when the version lands — which changes the disposition from "wait for a newer package" to "not achievable through the plugin at all".

### Blocker 1 — the field lands in v0.75.0, not v0.74.x

The issue body assumed the packaged version was 0.74.4 and that 0.74.4 might contain the field. Pinned by tag: `client/status/status.go` has no `json:"sessionExpiresAt"` in **v0.74.4/.5/.6/.7**, and gains it from **v0.75.0-rc.1 onward**. Same boundary in `client/proto/daemon.proto` (`google.protobuf.Timestamp sessionExpiresAt = 4` on `StatusResponse` at 0.75.0, absent at 0.74.4).

The dev box now runs `netbird-0.74.4` (upgraded from 0.72.2 during this session; `pkg rquery` offers no newer version, so 0.74.4 is the current ceiling in the OPNsense repo). Live payload after enrollment: **`sessionExpiresAt` absent**, as expected.

A red herring worth recording so nobody re-derives it: the string `sessionExpiresAt` does appear 9 times inside the installed 0.74.4 binary. Every occurrence is a `shared/management/proto` field on `SyncResponse`/`LoginResponse`/`ExtendAuthSessionResponse` — the management-server↔client gRPC protocol — plus `(*Server).onSessionExpire`. There is **no `json:"sessionExpiresAt"` struct tag in the binary** and no such field on `.daemon.FullStatus`. Grepping the binary is not evidence the status payload carries it.

### Blocker 2 (decisive) — setup-key peers can never emit it, and the plugin only does setup keys

NetBird refuses login expiration on setup-key-enrolled peers. Verified live against the management API:

```
PUT /api/peers/<id>  {"login_expiration_enabled": true, ...}
→ HTTP 412 {"message":"this peer hasn't been added with the sso login, therefore the login expiration can't be updated","code":412}
```

The tenant itself already has `peer_login_expiration_enabled: true` with an 86400s expiry — it simply only applies to SSO-enrolled peers, and every peer in the tenant reports `login_expiration_enabled: false`. In v0.75.0 the field is populated only when the deadline is non-zero (`status.go:213-215`), so a setup-key peer emits nothing even on 0.75.0.

And the os-netbird plugin has exactly one enrollment path: `netbird up -m <url> -k <setup-key>` (`actions_netbird.conf` `[up-setup-key]`, driven by `AuthenticationController::upAction`). The plugin **structurally cannot produce an SSO-enrolled peer**. So for any operator using the plugin — which is every user of this exporter's netbird collector — `sessionExpiresAt` is permanently absent. Capturing the fixture this issue requires would need netbird ≥0.75.0 *and* a hand-run interactive SSO `netbird up` outside the plugin, which is not a configuration this exporter can assume or usefully target.

### Why that means won't-do rather than parked

This issue's own binding rule is "absence means unsupported/unverified, not healthy". A metric that is absent for essentially the entire user base carries no signal, and an alert built on it could never fire for a plugin-managed box. Implementing it would add a permanently-dead branch — precisely the failure mode #284 recorded when `metadata.subsystems` was modelled as a shape upstream never populated, costing two fabricated fixtures and a dead code path.

### What replaces it

Session expiry is representable as a **state** rather than a deadline: `internal.StatusSessionExpired` exists at 0.74.4 (`server.go:1237`) and `DaemonStatusSessionExpired = "SessionExpired"` at `status.go:38`, so `daemonStatus` can carry it today.

**Correction to an earlier claim made during this investigation:** `daemonStatus` is *not* already exported. `opnsense/netbird.go:87`/`:186` decode it into `NetbirdStatus.DaemonStatus`, but the netbird collector has no descriptor for it and never reads the field — so it reaches no metric. Exposing it is a small, genuinely useful piece of work in its own right (`NeedsLogin`, `Idle`, `Connected` and `SessionExpired` are all operationally meaningful, for SSO and setup-key peers alike), and is filed as a follow-up.

### Prune trigger for the ledger

`exemptions.json` `netbirdStatus.knownExtraTopKeys` lists `sessionExpiresAt`. That entry is **prospective, never observed** — 0.74.4 does not emit it. Harmless (an exemption only suppresses a key that is actually present) but misleading; it is being annotated as prospective rather than silently left implying a capture.

Closing. Reopen only if OPNsense both packages netbird ≥0.75.0 **and** the plugin gains an SSO enrollment path.

body:
## Problem

The FRR OSPF client silently ignores a second-stage JSON decode failure and still marks the response present. A malformed embedded overview can therefore produce partial-success metrics with no collection error.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/frr.go` still uses `if json.Unmarshal(...); err == nil { ... }` with no error branch before setting `Present=true`.
- #104 explicitly identified this idiom as out of scope. #198 expanded FRR coverage but did not change this path.
- No later issue or closing comment in the full tracker claims the decode failure is surfaced.

## Operator value

A corrupted or drifted OSPF payload should fail visibly. Silent partial success can hide missing areas and adjacencies while the collector appears healthy.

## Scope

- Add a minimal malformed-overview fixture that proves the current partial-success behavior.
- Return a contextual decode error and preserve the collector's established failure/last-good snapshot policy.
- Do not make tolerant optional-field handling stricter than the wire contract requires.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A focused test fails on current `main` because malformed embedded overview JSON is accepted.
- [ ] Malformed overview JSON produces a contextual error and cannot set `Present=true` for partial data.
- [ ] Valid, disabled, and empty OSPF payloads retain their current behavior.
- [ ] Collector outcome and retained-snapshot tests pin the externally visible failure contract.
- [ ] Full build, test, lint, docs, and Grafana gates pass.

## Dependencies and risks

- Use the same error semantics as adjacent FRR decoders; do not invent a collector-specific retry path.
- Live OSPFv3 adjacency coverage remains a separate contract/testbed concern.

## Duplicate verdict

New narrow corrective issue. #104 left it out of scope and #198 did not close it.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Premise revalidated — and the stated error-semantics instruction cannot be followed

Premise confirmed against `main` at `52ef4b2`: `opnsense/frr.go:274` still uses `if json.Unmarshal(...); err == nil { ... }` with no error branch, and `Present=true` is still set afterwards regardless.

### Correction: "use the same error semantics as adjacent FRR decoders" is void

There are no such semantics to mirror. **Every** decoder in `opnsense/frr.go` swallows its second-stage decode error and returns `data, nil`, treating a corrupt payload as a disabled daemon:

| site | line | behaviour on decode failure |
|---|---|---|
| BFD neighbours | ~414 | `nbrsMap = nil`, then treated as plugin absent |
| BFD counters | ~456 | `ctrsMap = nil`, silently continues |
| BGP neighbours | ~583 | `return data, nil` |
| OSPFv3 overview | ~805 | `return data, nil` |
| OSPF database | ~1120 | `return counts, nil` |

So the fix implements this issue's explicit acceptance criteria instead, which are unambiguous. The narrow shape that satisfies them without disturbing the disabled-daemon path: the overview block is already guarded by `Response[0] != '['`, so the payload claims to be an object and a decode failure there is genuine corruption. That returns a contextual `APICallError` naming the decode failure, and cannot set `Present=true`. Valid payloads, the `[`-array daemon-disabled fallback, and empty payloads keep current behaviour exactly; the neighbours/bootgrid path is untouched.

The four sibling sites above are deliberately **not** changed — widening the fix is outside this issue's scope. They are a candidate follow-up issue, and worth one: the same false-success class applies to each.

Delivered in [`9355aa4`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/9355aa4), pushed to `main`.

Red-then-green receipt, client layer (`TestFetchFRROSPF_MalformedOverviewSurfacesDecodeError`, 3 subtests):
```
frr_test.go:511: expected an error for a malformed overview object, got nil
--- FAIL: .../areas_wrong_type / area_value_wrong_type / response_not_an_object
```
Collector layer (`TestFRRCollector_Update_MalformedOSPFOverviewFailsScrape`), verified against `git show HEAD:opnsense/frr.go` to prove it is a real regression test rather than one that only ever passed:
```
--- FAIL: TestFRRCollector_Update_MalformedOSPFOverviewFailsScrape
    frr_test.go:615: expected an APICallError from a malformed OSPF overview, got nil (the #378 partial-success bug)
```
Both green after the fix; the full `-run 'FRR|OSPF'` set (24 tests) passes.

### AC-4 is satisfied

The collector-side test asserts the error propagates, names `quaggaOspfOverview`, carries a `decode` message, and that **zero** metrics are emitted. It deliberately bypasses the `collectMetrics` helper, which `t.Fatalf`s on any Update error — the very thing under test. The retained-snapshot half was traced and confirmed: `pollOnce` records the failure and `snapshot.put` with an empty buffer keeps the last-good series while `scrape_collector_success{collector="frr"}` goes 0, already pinned by `TestSnapshotStore_PutErrorRetainsLastGood` and `TestPollOnceErrorRetainsAndRecordsFailure`.

### One thing worth knowing beyond the issue

A bare error branch would have broken a legitimate live shape. OPNsense's PHP round-trip re-encodes an empty map as `[]`, so an OSPF instance with **zero areas** arrives as `{"response":{"areas":[]}}`. That decoded silently before and would have become a hard collector failure on an idle box. `frrOSPFAreaMap` absorbs it — the same quirk `flexStringMap` exists for — so the new error stays aimed at genuine corruption. `empty_areas_array` passing on HEAD is the proof it was necessary.

No golden churn: the endpoint is registered as its envelope type (`Response json.RawMessage` → `kind: any`), so the inner retype is invisible to the reflected schema. `TestSchemaRegistryComplete` and `TestSchemasUpToDate` pass unmodified.

### Sibling sites left alone deliberately

The issue named four; there are **seven**, all still returning `data, nil` on a decode failure — post-fix lines 137 (BGP summary), 451 and 493 (BFD neighbours/counters), 620 (BGP neighbours), 842 (OSPFv3 overview), 926 (OSPFv3 interfaces), 1157 (database LSA counts), plus 742/746 (`FetchFRROSPFInterfaces`, a two-shape tolerant reader that is silent only if both shapes fail). Not widened here, and they should not be flipped naively: 493 is a partial-merge case that changes failure blast radius, and 842/926/1157 decode plain map/struct types with no `[]`-tolerance, so the PHP empty-map quirk above would make an idle daemon hard-error. Each needs its own tolerant-type pass first.

body:
**Theme / priority / confidence:** testbed assurance; P2; medium-high confidence on the gap, medium confidence on provisioning effort.

**Evidence**

- Empty arrays/maps and nulls place expected schema paths in `Unverified`, which intentionally does not make a result unclean: [schema result semantics](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/schema_validate.go#L19), [unverified handling](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/schema_validate.go#L212).
- `aggregate` does not treat any unverified path as a warning. The report prints only a count of affected endpoints, with no endpoint/path detail: [aggregate](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/cmd/apidrift/report.go#L24), [summary-only output](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/cmd/apidrift/report.go#L161).
- The latest live report, [#371](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/371), says 20 endpoints have unverifiable paths but does not identify them.
- Current code still labels metric-bearing shapes as source-derived/unverified: NetBird enrolled peer details ([netbird.go](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/netbird.go#L31)), OSPFv3 ([frr.go](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/frr.go#L24)), Kea non-empty lease/PD paths ([kea.go](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/kea.go#L24)), and hardware/state-dependent interface branches. The completed #227 tracker recorded the same validation debt, but there is no durable per-path completion mechanism.

**User value**

“Twenty endpoints need more activity” is not actionable and can remain unchanged forever. A consumed field can therefore be source-derived, wrong, and permanently green in CI because the testbed never creates the state needed to observe it. A metric-backed ledger turns that invisible debt into a finite provisioning/test plan without making every optional field a noisy alert.

**Proposed scope**

- Render every unverified endpoint/path in a structure-only report; retain the aggregate count for the headline.
- Add a committed coverage ledger, for example `opnsense/testdata/schemas/coverage.json`, that marks selected paths as:
  - `required`: backs an emitted metric and the canary is expected to exercise it;
  - `state_optional`: legitimate hardware/license/topology state, with reason and prune trigger.
- Link each required path to the metric family and a concise testbed exercise recipe.
- Seed required coverage with the explicitly source-derived metric paths: enrolled NetBird peer details, OSPFv3 adjacency/interface data, and non-empty Kea IA_PD/PD-pool rows. Classify real-hardware-only paths such as PSU, GPS, SFP DOM, and ZFS ARC as state-optional unless the canary hardware changes.
- Make only unresolved `required` paths warning-level. Keep all other unverified paths informational.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] The report lists normalized endpoint/path pairs and never response values.
- [ ] A committed ledger maps every initial `required` path to the metric(s) it protects and a reproducible exercise recipe.
- [ ] Required paths warn when unverified; state-optional paths remain informational and carry rationale/prune triggers.
- [ ] NetBird enrollment, OSPFv3, and Kea PD/IA_PD are either observed live or remain as explicit, named blockers—never an anonymous count.
- [ ] Public CI output contains no credentials, IPs, peer names, dynamic-map identities, or payload values.
- [ ] Tests cover empty list/map/null handling, required-vs-optional severity, wildcard normalization, and report deduplication.
- [ ] Testbed documentation explains cleanup/rollback and avoids availability-impacting changes to the production firewall.

**Dependencies / risks**

- Requires controlled writes to the development OPNsense VM for enrollment/peering/lease activity; production remains read-only.
- NetBird enrollment needs secret handling; no setup key may enter fixtures, logs, issues, or the ledger.
- The largest risk is permanent warning noise from state that cannot exist on a VM. The two-class ledger and explicit prune triggers are the control.

**Duplicate verdict**

Not a duplicate. #195 built the canary and #227 carried a one-time aggregate provisioning shopping list. Neither reports unverified paths individually, connects them to emitted metrics, or enforces a current required-coverage set.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
Delivered in [`b171804`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/b171804), pushed to `main`.

Red receipt:
```
opnsense/schema_coverage_test.go:13:12: undefined: LoadCoverageLedger
--- FAIL: TestCommittedCoverageLedgerIntegrity
    schema_coverage_test.go:84: the committed coverage ledger is empty
--- FAIL: TestCommittedCoverageLedgerCarriesNoSecrets
    schema_coverage_test.go:166: read ledger: open testdata/schemas/coverage.json: no such file or directory
```
Green: ledger load/index/classify, integrity, no-secrets, plus per-path report rendering, severity and dedup tests.

`opnsense/testdata/schemas/coverage.json` holds 15 `required` and 7 `stateOptional` entries. The report now names every unverified endpoint/path pair split by class, keeping the aggregate count as the headline. **Only an unresolved, non-opaque required path warns.**

### `opaque` — the addition that keeps this honest

A path the schema types as `KindAny` can never be verified by any live run. `TestCommittedCoverageLedgerIntegrity` enforces `opaque` **iff** the schema field really is `KindAny`, so nobody can add an inert required entry or quietly forget to flag a real blind spot. Opaque paths render as named **standing blind spots** rather than warnings, because a warning no live run could ever clear is permanent noise, not signal — the risk this issue named. A path moves unresolved → resolved by editing the ledger alone: no schema or code change.

### Provisioning closed three of the four gaps, all live-verified today

- **NetBird enrolled-peer detail — CLOSED.** The dev box was enrolled into a real tenant; all 22 paths in the `netbirdStatus` golden validated in both `Connected` and lazy-connection `Idle` states (22 verified, 0 mismatched, 0 unverified). The source-derived guesses in `netbird.go` were **all correct**, including the `RFC3339Nano` + `!IsZero()` handling. That file's "never observed live" comment is replaced with the receipt, plus two zero-value traps: `lastWireguardHandshake` zeroes to the ordinary Go zero time, but `lastStatusUpdate` zeroes to `0000-12-31T23:58:45-00:01`, which `IsZero()` does **not** catch.
- **Kea IA_PD — CLOSED.** A real client now holds both an IA_NA and an IA_PD lease; `leases6/search` returns populated rows and `searchPdPool` is non-empty, so the `IA_NA`/`IA_PD` spelling `keaLeaseTypeLabel` was tolerating blind is confirmed by a human read. The PD pool turned out to be already configured — the missing ingredient was always a client.
- **OSPFv3 — live state achieved, but still opaque.** A `Full` adjacency was established and all 13 `ospf6` field names confirmed present in the live payload.

### Two findings worth more than the ledger itself

**The Kea gap is now root-caused, not worked around.** The Proxmox **host** kernel is booted with `ipv6.disable=1`, so `/proc/sys/net/ipv6` is absent in every namespace on that host and **no LXC on it can ever run a DHCPv6 client**. #227 concluded this was container privilege; it is not. Only a VM (own kernel) can hold a v6 lease. Recorded in the ledger note so it is never re-investigated.

**OSPFv3's blind spot is code, not lab.** `schema_registry.go` registers the envelope types, whose sole field is `Response json.RawMessage` → `KindAny`, so the golden carries one path and accepts any payload. Provisioning cannot fix it, and that distinction was independently rediscovered twice during this epic — so both the ledger and the `frr.go` banner now say so explicitly. Tracked in **#459**.

### Regressions the ledger deliberately makes loud

- NetBird coverage depends on a **hand-started, non-reboot-durable** second peer (a peer never lists itself, so a single-peer tenant yields an empty `details[]`). The recipe says: if these paths regress, restart the peer before treating it as drift.
- Kea v6 rows expire within the lease lifetime if that VM stops.
- `keaLeases4` is now **empty** — no DHCPv4 client on the test VLAN — despite a 2026-07-13 capture, so the v4 lease row is now the weaker side. Noted in the ledger.

No setup key, API token, tenant name, FQDN, address or public key is in the ledger; `TestCommittedCoverageLedgerCarriesNoValues` shape-checks for IPv4/IPv6/MAC literals, PEM blocks and `Bearer` values.

body:
**Theme / priority / confidence:** contract and opportunity discovery; P1 engineering hardening; high confidence.

**Evidence**

- `ValidationResult` has `UnknownTopKeys`, not unknown paths, and `ValidateResponseSchema` compares only the root object against `KnownTopLevelKeys`: [schema_validate.go](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/schema_validate.go#L19), [top-level-only check](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/schema_validate.go#L113).
- Expected nested paths are traversed for missing keys and type conflicts, but there is no reverse traversal that asks whether a nested object contains extra keys: [field evaluation](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/schema_validate.go#L140).
- The schema generator already records enough normalized structure—literal segments, `[]` for array members, and `*` for dynamic map values—to build a known-shape trie: [schema model](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/schema.go#L30), [type walker](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/schema.go#L69).
- The report promises “data we do not model” but can currently discover that only at the root: [apidrift report](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/cmd/apidrift/report.go#L121).

**User value**

An upstream addition such as `statistics.tcp.new-counter`, `rows[].new_health`, or `product.product_check.new_state` is invisible today if all existing fields retain their types. This is both a drift blind spot and an opportunity-discovery blind spot—the exact class this audit had to recover manually.

**Proposed scope**

- Derive a normalized known-key trie from `EndpointSchema.Fields`.
- Replace/augment `UnknownTopKeys` with `UnknownPaths`, reporting static nested extras as normalized paths such as `rows[].new_field`.
- Treat `*` nodes as dynamic identity maps: accept arbitrary map keys, normalize them to `*`, and inspect only the statically typed value shape beneath them.
- Stop recursion at `KindAny`, custom unmarshallers, and `json.RawMessage`.
- Add path-based `knownExtraPaths` exemptions and migrate the current top-level ledger. Preserve Bootgrid's implicit envelope keys at the root.
- Keep unexpected additions warning-level, not breaking. Report path names only—never values or actual dynamic-map keys.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] Tests catch an extra key in a nested object and in an object inside an array.
- [ ] Tests accept arbitrary dynamic-map identities but catch an extra static field inside a map value, reporting `*.field` rather than the real identity.
- [ ] `KindAny`/raw-message subtrees do not create noise.
- [ ] Matching remains case-insensitive like `encoding/json`.
- [ ] `knownExtraPaths` supports exact normalized paths and documented subtree exemptions; every migrated exemption has a reason/prune trigger.
- [ ] The Markdown report lists endpoint + normalized path only and is regression-tested not to echo values.
- [ ] A baseline live run is reviewed before enabling issue warnings; after justified exemptions, the current canary is clean.

**Dependencies / risks**

- No production/exporter availability cost; this runs in the live-canary job.
- The main risk is a one-time wave of legitimate unmodelled nested keys. Roll out report-only for the baseline, classify them, then enable warnings.
- Dynamic map keys can be hostnames, peer identities, or interface names; normalization to `*` is a privacy requirement, not an implementation detail.

**Duplicate verdict**

Not an open duplicate. [#144](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/144) and [#195](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/195) established response-contract/live-canary coverage, but the delivered implementation and tests explicitly stop at top-level extra keys. #195's broad “new key” intent was therefore only partially realized for nested additions.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
Delivered in [`53da29f`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/53da29f), pushed to `main`.

Red receipt:
```
opnsense/schema_validate_test.go:368:31: unknown field KnownExtraPaths in struct literal of type SchemaExemption
opnsense/schema_validate_test.go:394:30: res.UnknownPaths undefined (type ValidationResult has no field or method UnknownPaths)
--- FAIL: TestAggregateSeverity/unknown_nested_path_is_warning
    report_test.go:31: aggregate = (false,false), want (false,true)
--- FAIL: TestRenderReportUnknownNestedPaths
    report_test.go:77: report missing "statistics.tcp.new-counter"
```
Green: `TestValidateResponseSchemaUnknownNestedPaths` (13 subtests) plus array-root, dynamic-root, casing and `Clean()` guards; report side all green.

Every acceptance criterion is met — nested object, object-inside-array, arbitrary dynamic-map identities accepted while an extra static field under a map reports as `*.field`, `KindAny`/raw-message subtrees silent, case-insensitive matching, `knownExtraPaths` exact + subtree forms, and a regression test proving the report never echoes a value.

### A bug found mid-flight that the issue did not anticipate

Reported paths were initially spelled with the **live** payload's casing. OPNsense serves `healthCheck`'s `metadata.System` block through a lowercase `system` key, so one drift would have produced two different spellings and a `knownExtraPaths` entry would only ever have matched one of them. Paths now use the **schema's** spelling for known segments, with the live key used only for the genuinely-new leaf. Pinned by `TestValidateResponseSchemaUnknownNestedPathsCanonicalCasing`.

### Nested extras ship REPORT-ONLY — a correction to this epic's frozen contract

The baseline live run this issue required was performed against the dev box (26.7.r_35): **174 endpoints, 0 breaking type drift, 0 unexpected top-level keys, and 1003 unmodelled nested paths across 62 endpoints.**

The epic's frozen seam contract had specified warning-level from the start. The baseline disproved that: 1003 warning-level paths would keep the drift issue permanently open and train everyone to ignore it, which is precisely the risk this issue's own risk section names. So `aggregate()` deliberately excludes `UnknownPaths` from the warning signal and the report section is labelled `REPORT-ONLY baseline`. All 1003 still render in full, so discovery is unaffected.

That means the final acceptance line — "after justified exemptions, the current canary is clean" — is satisfied for every breaking and top-level signal, but the nested baseline is handed to **#457** to triage into `knownExtraPaths`; flipping the flag back is that issue's last step. Categorising 1003 paths inside this change would have meant either rushed exemptions or a blanket `rows[].*` subtree that masks exactly the drift this detector exists to catch.

Two evidence-backed exemptions did land now: `healthCheck` (four `metadata` keys, validated against all 10 committed health fixtures) and `netbirdStatus` (nine `peers.details[]` fields, confirmed against a live enrolled capture — 16 keys served, 7 modelled), each with a reason and prune trigger.

### Privacy

Values never enter a `ValidationResult` at all, and identities normalise to `*` before anything is recorded. `TestRenderReportNeverEchoesResponseValues` drives a real validation over a payload where every scalar **and** the dynamic-map identity is a sentinel, produces mismatch + missing + nested-extra + root-extra simultaneously, then asserts none of the 8 sentinels reach the markdown while the structural findings do.

`cmd/apischema` and `schema_test` gained a one-token allowlist so the orphan sweep cannot delete the hand-maintained ledgers sitting alongside the goldens — without it, `make schemas` would have silently removed `coverage.json`.

body:
**Theme / priority / confidence:** interface diagnosis and counter correctness; P2; high confidence.

**Evidence**

- The wire struct already decodes `packets for unknown protocol` and `uptime at attach or stat reset`, but the public `Interface` type and `FetchInterfaces` mapping drop both: [interfaces.go](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/interfaces.go#L19), [public result](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/interfaces.go#L60), [mapping](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/interfaces.go#L147).
- The existing fixture carries non-zero values (`10` and `123456`), and both paths are in the current generated schema: [interfaces test](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/interfaces_test.go#L13), [interface schema](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/testdata/schemas/interfaces.json#L102).
- OPNsense returns its already-collected interface traffic snapshot verbatim from `interface show traffic`; this is not a new query: [official `TrafficController.php`](https://github.com/opnsense/core/blob/5c7830d6979ec4e0ee93ea8b12a20d7173c19c3c/src/opnsense/mvc/app/controllers/OPNsense/Diagnostics/Api/TrafficController.php#L41-L49).
- The attach/reset marker has already proved useful live. In [#361](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/361#issuecomment-5071757742), `pppoe0` reported marker `200603` against system uptime around `200640`, proving the interface had really been destroyed/recreated roughly 37 seconds earlier while boot-attached interfaces retained markers `1` and `78`. That evidence was used diagnostically but no metric was added.

**User value**

The unknown-protocol counter identifies traffic delivered to an interface that the network stack could not classify. The epoch marker explains simultaneous resets in every per-interface counter and distinguishes an interface recreation/statistics reset from a real traffic drop or exporter bug. Operators can compute reset/attach age as `opnsense_system_uptime_seconds - opnsense_interfaces_attach_or_statistics_reset_uptime_seconds`.

**Proposed scope**

- Add `opnsense_interfaces_unknown_protocol_packets_total{interface,device,type}` as a counter.
- Add `opnsense_interfaces_attach_or_statistics_reset_uptime_seconds{interface,device,type}` as a gauge containing the system-uptime value at which attach/reset occurred.
- Reuse the existing interface label set; add a diagnostic panel/reset annotation, but no default alert.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] Both existing wire fields are mapped into `Interface` without changing current interface-name/device semantics.
- [ ] Unknown-protocol packets use `CounterValue`; the attach/reset marker uses `GaugeValue`.
- [ ] Missing/unparseable marker data is omitted rather than reported as a real boot-time zero; a genuine wire value `"0"` remains representable.
- [ ] Tests cover non-zero, zero, missing, malformed, and interface-recreation marker changes.
- [ ] Dashboard/help text shows the subtraction against system uptime and states that the marker can mean attach **or** an explicit statistics reset.
- [ ] Generated schemas/docs/dashboard and the full gate pass.

**Dependencies / risks**

- Zero new API calls. At most two additional series per existing interface, using labels already emitted by the collector.
- No new privacy exposure. Device and configured interface names are already public metric labels in this exporter.
- `promiscuous listeners` and `HW offload capabilities` should stay out of this scope: there is no live non-zero use case or stable alert contract yet.

**Duplicate verdict**

Not a duplicate. #361 mentions the marker only as evidence for a NetFlow-index investigation; it did not propose or implement either metric. No issue/comment mentions the unknown-protocol counter.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.

- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

body:
**Theme / priority / confidence:** transport diagnosis; P1/P2; high confidence.

**Evidence**

- `protocolStatisticsResponse` already decodes four explicit cumulative counters: connections dropped by retransmit timeout, persist timeout, FIN-WAIT-2 timeout, and keepalives: [protocol_statistics.go](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/protocol_statistics.go#L158).
- Only the keepalive field is copied into the public result, and even that value is never emitted by the collector; the other three stop at the wire struct: [result mapping](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/protocol_statistics.go#L654), [collector metric set](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/internal/collector/protocol.go#L59).
- The generated live schema contains all four current paths: [protocol schema](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/testdata/schemas/protocolStatistics.json#L550).
- OPNsense passes the output of `netstat -s --libxo json` straight through this API, so this adds no backend work: [official configd action](https://github.com/opnsense/core/blob/5c7830d6979ec4e0ee93ea8b12a20d7173c19c3c/src/opnsense/service/conf/actions.d/actions_interface.conf#L247-L251), [official API controller](https://github.com/opnsense/core/blob/5c7830d6979ec4e0ee93ea8b12a20d7173c19c3c/src/opnsense/mvc/app/controllers/OPNsense/Diagnostics/Api/InterfaceController.php#L206-L213).
- The current metrics expose aggregate connection drops plus retransmit and keepalive *timeout events*, but not which timeouts actually killed connections. Those are different questions.

**User value**

An increase in aggregate TCP drops currently says nothing about whether the firewall is losing connections through retransmission exhaustion, zero-window persistence, FIN-WAIT-2 cleanup, or keepalive failure. The four fixed reasons make WAN loss, stalled applications, and state-lifetime problems distinguishable without packet capture.

**Proposed scope**

- Add `opnsense_protocol_tcp_connection_drops_by_reason_total{reason}` with exactly four reasons: `retransmit_timeout`, `persist_timeout`, `finwait2_timeout`, and `keepalive`.
- Preserve wire-field presence so an older box that does not send a reason omits that series instead of manufacturing a zero.
- Add a stacked-rate panel next to the existing aggregate TCP drop/timeout panels. No default alert until a useful environment-independent threshold is established.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] The client maps all four fields with presence information.
- [ ] The collector emits `CounterValue` for a fixed four-value reason set and emits no series for absent wire fields.
- [ ] Tests prove each reason maps independently and remains monotonic through normal scrapes.
- [ ] The existing aggregate `opnsense_protocol_tcp_connection_drops_total` and timeout metrics are unchanged.
- [ ] Generated docs and the protocol dashboard panel are updated; schema/docs/dashboard/full gates pass.

**Dependencies / risks**

- Zero new API calls and only four bounded series per instance.
- No user, address, interface, or payload data is exposed.
- These are kernel-lifetime counters and reset on reboot, like the existing protocol counters; the help text must say so.

**Duplicate verdict**

No issue or comment mentions these reason fields. [#106](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/106) corrected Gauge-vs-Counter treatment broadly, and [#237](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/237) added adjacent 26.7 TCP fields, but neither exported these four counters.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
Delivered in [`9fc10ba`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/9fc10ba), pushed to `main`.

`opnsense_protocol_tcp_connection_drops_by_reason_total{reason}`, CounterValue, exactly four reasons: `retransmit_timeout`, `persist_timeout`, `finwait2_timeout`, `keepalive`. Zero new API calls — all four wire fields were already decoded and already in the committed live schema.

Red receipt, client layer:
```
opnsense/protocol_statistics_test.go:858:15: data.TCPConnectionDropsByReason undefined
FAIL github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/opnsense [build failed]
```
Collector layer, behavioural red:
```
protocol_test.go:301: expected exactly 2 reason series (only the ones the box sent), got 0: []
```
Green: `TestFetchProtocolStatistics_TCPConnectionDropsByReason` (4 subtests) and `TestProtocolCollector_TCPConnectionDropsByReason` (2 subtests) all pass.

### Presence-gating

`tcpConnectionDropReasons` adds a reason to the map only when its `json.Number` wire field is non-empty, returning nil when none are. The collector ranges over the map, so an absent field never reaches the channel — no manufactured zero, which was the point of the issue. Proven by `.../some_reasons_absent_are_omitted,_not_zeroed` at the client layer and `.../no_reasons_present_emits_no_series_at_all` at the collector layer.

Independent mapping is proven with four **distinct** values (11/22/33/44) asserted per key, so swapping any two reasons fails the test. Monotonicity is covered across repeated scrapes (10 → 25).

### The count change, verified rather than accepted

`TestProtocolCollector_Update` moved 129 → 133. I checked this against the fixture rather than taking the lane's word: it sends all four `connections-dropped-by-*` keys as unquoted JSON `0`, which is **present** under presence-gating and so legitimately emits four series. The breakdown comment (105 + 21 + 3 + 4 = 133) is accurate and the aggregate `tcp_connection_drops_total` value is re-asserted unchanged at 99. Not a masked regression.

The existing aggregate and timeout metrics are untouched. Help text states these are kernel-lifetime counters that reset on reboot. Dashboard: a stacked-rate panel beside the existing aggregate TCP drop/timeout panels. No default alert, per the issue's explicit deferral.

body:
**Theme / priority / confidence:** update integrity; P1; high confidence.

**Evidence**

- The response struct models `status` but not `connection`, `repository`, `remove_packages`, or `upgrade_sets`; `FetchFirmwareStatus` treats any non-empty `last_check` as proof that the remaining payload is meaningful and emits package counts without checking whether the repository check succeeded: [firmware.go](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/firmware.go#L5), [firmware.go](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/firmware.go#L107).
- The collector therefore cannot distinguish “no updates” from “the mirror could not be resolved/authenticated/verified”: [firmware collector](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/internal/collector/firmware.go#L98).
- The committed exemption ledger explicitly lists these fields as unmodelled and calls the full-inventory surface a remaining #227 opportunity: [exemptions.json](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/opnsense/testdata/schemas/exemptions.json#L51).
- Upstream sets `last_check` before it attempts the package operation, then persists fixed `connection` and `repository` state fields even on failure. Connection states include `ok`, `unresolved`, `misconfigured`, and `unauthenticated`; repository states include `ok`, `untrusted`, `revoked`, `unsigned`, `forbidden`, and `incomplete`: [official `check.sh`](https://github.com/opnsense/core/blob/5c7830d6979ec4e0ee93ea8b12a20d7173c19c3c/src/opnsense/scripts/firmware/check.sh#L53-L80), [failure classification](https://github.com/opnsense/core/blob/5c7830d6979ec4e0ee93ea8b12a20d7173c19c3c/src/opnsense/scripts/firmware/check.sh#L123-L179), [persisted JSON](https://github.com/opnsense/core/blob/5c7830d6979ec4e0ee93ea8b12a20d7173c19c3c/src/opnsense/scripts/firmware/check.sh#L403-L425).
- The official controller maps any non-`ok` connection/repository state to `status=error`, while the exporter ignores that verdict: [official `FirmwareController.php`](https://github.com/opnsense/core/blob/5c7830d6979ec4e0ee93ea8b12a20d7173c19c3c/src/opnsense/mvc/app/controllers/OPNsense/Core/Api/FirmwareController.php#L270-L335).
- The same controller constructs `all_packages` from the five action arrays and `all_sets` from `upgrade_sets`; raw composite inventories would duplicate those arrays, but bounded counts for `remove_packages` and `upgrade_sets` are genuinely absent: [official aggregation](https://github.com/opnsense/core/blob/5c7830d6979ec4e0ee93ea8b12a20d7173c19c3c/src/opnsense/mvc/app/controllers/OPNsense/Core/Api/FirmwareController.php#L164-L267).

**User value**

Today a DNS failure, expired business subscription, revoked repository fingerprint, or unavailable release train can look exactly like a successful check with zero pending updates. That is a false-safe failure mode in the part of the firewall responsible for security updates. The missing removal/major-set counts also leave the existing package-action family incomplete.

**Proposed scope**

- Add `opnsense_firmware_update_check_success`, emitted only after a stored check exists: `1` when both connection and repository are `ok`, otherwise `0`.
- Add `opnsense_firmware_update_check_state{component,state} 1` for `component=connection|repository`. Canonicalize only the fixed upstream states and collapse anything else to `unknown`; never expose `status_msg`, mirror URLs, subscription text, or arbitrary labels.
- Add `opnsense_firmware_remove_packages_count` and `opnsense_firmware_upgrade_sets_count`.
- Keep using the already-fetched `api/core/firmware/status` body. Do not add a probe or trigger a firmware check.
- Add a dashboard status panel and a warning alert guarded by the presence of a completed check. Document that the default firmware body cache can delay state changes by up to 12 hours: [cache policy](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4/internal/options/cache.go#L65).

**Acceptance**

- [ ] A successful stored check emits success `1`, two bounded state series, and both new counts.
- [ ] Each documented connection/repository failure emits success `0` and the correct canonical state.
- [ ] A pre-check/minimal envelope emits no fabricated success/state series.
- [ ] Unknown future state strings collapse to `unknown`; no free-form message or repository identifier becomes a label.
- [ ] `remove_packages` and `upgrade_sets` are counts only; `all_packages`/`all_sets` are not decoded into per-package metrics.
- [ ] Parser and collector tests cover success, connection failure, repository failure, no-check state, unknown state, and absent count arrays.
- [ ] Schema goldens/exemptions, generated metrics docs, dashboard, and alert manifests are updated and the full repository gate is green.

**Dependencies / risks**

- No API, availability, or firewall CPU increase; all fields are in the cached response already.
- Cardinality is fixed: one success series, two current-state series, and two gauges per instance.
- The main operational caveat is the existing 12-hour cache. The alert text must state that lag rather than imply real-time mirror monitoring.

**Duplicate verdict**

Not a duplicate. [#235](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/235) and [#236](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/236) discovered/exempted the keys as contract data; [#237](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/237) added downgrade/reinstall counts but did not consume check health, removals, or upgrade sets. The full tracker notes the remaining inventory opportunity but has no issue implementing it.

## Audit receipt

- Audited clean `main` at [`52ef4b2`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/52ef4b269b7a01fde26b818a1bc43bff9f4befe4), equal to `origin/main`, on 2026-07-25.
- Compared against the complete 245-issue tracker snapshot through #372, including issue bodies and comments.
- Baseline gates were green: `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, and `make grafana-check`.
- This issue is a planning record. Revalidate the premise against current `main` before implementation and keep the issue updated with failing-test, implementation, and delivery receipts.

comments.body:
## Premise revalidated + correction to the state vocabularies

Premise confirmed against `main` at `52ef4b2`. `FetchFirmwareStatus` still models `status` but not `connection`/`repository`/`remove_packages`/`upgrade_sets`, and still treats any non-empty `last_check` as proof the rest of the payload is meaningful.

Live evidence from the dev box (OPNsense **26.7.r_35**): `api/core/firmware/status` serves `connection` = `ok`, `repository` = `ok`, `remove_packages` = `[]`, `upgrade_sets` = `[]`. So both new counts read 0 on that box and the two arrays inner shapes are source-derived rather than captured — modelled from the installed `check.sh` (`remove_packages` from lines 256 + 262 as name/repository/version; `upgrade_sets` from lines 374/385/397 as name/size/current_version/new_version/repository).

### Correction: both vocabularies in the issue body are missing `error`

This issue lists connection as `ok/unresolved/misconfigured/unauthenticated` and repository as `ok/untrusted/revoked/unsigned/forbidden/incomplete`. Both omit **`error`**, which is the value each variable is initialised to (`check.sh:54`, `check.sh:66`) and which survives when a failure matches none of the specific classifiers. The installed 26.7 `/usr/local/opnsense/scripts/firmware/check.sh` declares the full closed sets in a header comment at lines 30-31:

- connection: `error`, `unauthenticated`, `misconfigured`, `unresolved`, `ok`
- repository: `error`, `untrusted`, `unsigned`, `revoked`, `incomplete`, `forbidden`, `ok`

The implementation uses these lists. Had the issue body been followed literally, the single most likely real-world failure state would have collapsed to `unknown` — defeating the point of the metric. The installed script is also better evidence than GitHub master for what the supported releases actually serve.

Frozen contract, cardinality and gating are recorded on the epic: #447 (comment).

Delivered in [`2d0769b`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/2d0769b) (with #380 — same files), pushed to `main`.

| metric | type | labels | emission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opnsense_firmware_update_check_success` | Gauge | — | only with a stored check; 1 iff connection **and** repository are `ok` |
| `opnsense_firmware_update_check_state` | Gauge (=1) | `component`, `state` | only with a stored check; exactly 2 series, current state only |
| `opnsense_firmware_remove_packages_count` | Gauge | — | always (0 when absent) |
| `opnsense_firmware_upgrade_sets_count` | Gauge | — | always (0 when absent) |

Red receipt:
```
opnsense/firmware_test.go:165:8: fs.CheckPresent undefined (type FirmwareStatus has no field or method CheckPresent)
opnsense/firmware_test.go:168:8: fs.Connection undefined
opnsense/firmware_test.go:171:8: fs.RemovePackages undefined
```
then behavioural red at the collector layer:
```
--- FAIL: TestFirmwareCollector_UpdateCheckHealthy
    firmware_test.go:200: expected exactly 1 update_check_success series, got 0
--- FAIL: TestFirmwareCollector_NoStoredCheckEmitsNoCheckSeries
    firmware_test.go:358: expected opnsense_firmware_remove_packages_count to always be emitted, got 0 series
```
Green across `./opnsense/`, `./internal/collector/` and `./internal/options/`.

### The gating was confirmed live, by accident

Mid-session the dev box **reverted from the full 26-key superset to the bare 3-key envelope** (`product`/`status`/`status_msg`, `status: "none"`, no `last_check`) after a package operation cleared the stored check. That is the exact pre-check state this issue's third acceptance criterion is about, and the exporter behaved correctly: no fabricated success or state series, both counts at 0. Better evidence than the fixture.

It also exposed that all seven state-dependent top-level keys must be `missingOK` box-state entries — `connection`, `repository`, `download_size`, `remove_packages`, `upgrade_sets`, and **`downgrade_packages`/`reinstall_packages`**, the latter a latent gap from #237 that was only ever invisible because previous canary runs happened to catch the box post-check. The canary went from 7 firmware missing-paths to 0 after the ledger entries landed. No prune trigger: a box that has not checked since boot is a permanent, legitimate state.

### Vocabulary correction stands

Implemented from the installed 26.7 `check.sh` header (lines 30-31), which includes `error` in **both** lists — omitted by the issue body, and the value each variable is initialised to (`:54`/`:66`). `TestCanonicalizeFirmwareCheckState` pins all 12 values including both `error`s, and pins that the two vocabularies do not leak into each other (`revoked` is not a connection state). Anything unrecognised collapses to `unknown`; no `status_msg`, mirror URL or subscription text becomes a label, and `all_packages`/`all_sets` are asserted **not** decoded into per-package metrics.

### Judgement calls inside gaps in the spec

A stored check that omits `connection`/`repository` reads `unknown`/`unknown`, hence `success=0`. Absence is outside the closed vocabulary and fail-safe is the point of this issue; both fields are present on both in-window releases, so this only affects pre-window firmware.

`remove_packages` and `upgrade_sets` are modelled with their **full** inner shapes (`check.sh:256`/`:262` and `:374`/`:385`/`:397`) even though only counts are exported, because #376 lands nested-key detection in the same epic and an under-modelled array would generate exactly the noise it exists to surface. Both arrays were empty on the box, so those inner shapes are source-derived and say so in the code.

### Alert

`opnsense-update-check-failing` (warning, 1h pending) fires on `update_check_success < 1`. Because the series only exists once a check is stored, a box that has never checked produces NoData and stays Ok rather than firing — the presence gate *is* the guard. The description states the caveat explicitly: this is the STORED result of a roughly-daily check read through a response cache, so a failure can take up to `--exporter.firmware-cache-ttl` (verified: default 12h) to appear and as long to clear. It does not imply real-time mirror monitoring.

## Mission

Reconcile the current generated Grafana dashboard and Grafana-managed alert/recording-rule manifests with the live m7kni Grafana stack, preserving the existing ownership split: dashboard through `gc-gitsync-m7kni`; rules through `gcx` in `opnsense-alerts`.

## Current premise

- `grafana/dashboard.json` is the generated dashboard source.
- `gc-gitsync-m7kni/networking/opnsense-exporter.json` is the GitSync-owned live dashboard source.
- `grafana/alerts/grafana-managed/` contains the Grafana-managed alerts and recording rules.

## Approach

- [x] Regenerate and run `make grafana-check`.
- [x] Fetch and compare the GitSync dashboard copy with the generated dashboard; update and push GitSync only if different.
- [x] Validate dashboard and rule manifests against the live m7kni stack.
- [x] Inventory current live OPNsense alerts and recording rules.
- [x] Dry-run then push current rules with stack-specific IRM labels.
- [x] Read back the dashboard and every expected alert/recording rule; confirm counts and evaluation health.
- [x] Record exact Git/Grafana receipts here and close the issue.

## Acceptance

- Current generated dashboard is represented in the GitSync repo and reconciled live.
- Every current alert and recording rule exists in `opnsense-alerts` with the stack label contract.
- Validation and post-write read-back succeed with no missing resources.
- No unrelated Grafana or repository resources are changed.

### 🔴 Breaking: type mismatches

- `interfaceConfig` `*.nd6`: expected array, live box serves object

### 🟡 Missing key paths (renamed/removed upstream, or box state — exempt in `opnsense/testdata/schemas/exemptions.json` if legitimate)

- `interfaceConfig` `*.sfp`

### ℹ️ Plugin-gated endpoints absent (plugin not installed — expected, not drift)

- `siproxdRegistrations` (`api/siproxd/service/showregistrations`)

20 endpoints have paths that could not be verified (empty lists/maps on the box) — increase box activity to cover them.

1 endpoints have no schema (see `schemaExemptEndpoints` in `opnsense/schema_registry.go`).

## End-to-end exporter smoke

- exporter reached `/-/ready` (poll scheduler warm) ✅
- `opnsense_up` = 1 ✅
- all 60 sub-collectors succeeded ✅
- 665 distinct `opnsense_*` metric names (floor 560) ✅

comments.body:
Triaged and fixed in 7754b36.

**`interfaceConfig` `*.nd6` — not drift; the struct was wrong from the day it landed.** `legacy_interfaces_details()` builds it as `["flags" => explode(",", strtolower($matches[1]))]`, i.e. an object wrapping the flag list. That line is byte-identical on `master`, `stable/26.7`, `stable/26.1` and `stable/25.7`, so no release in or beyond the support window has ever served the flat list this repo asserted. Both live boxes agree — devel 26.7.r_35 and prod 26.7.1_1 serve `"nd6":{"flags":["performnud","auto_linklocal"]}`. The field went in with #361 as `[]string`; nothing decodes these structs in production (the fetch walks key order and discards values), so no metric was ever wrong and the only thing that could notice was this canary.

Verdict: **absorb** (retype), plus a build-time guard so the next one does not need a live box to catch — a captured two-row payload is now validated against the derived schema in a unit test (`TestInterfaceConfigSchemaMatchesCapturedPayload`). The two rows are `ixl0` (SFP cage + nd6 line) and `pflog0` (neither), which also pins that partial absence across rows is not drift.

**`interfaceConfig` `*.sfp` — box-state.** `$result[$dev][sfp]` is only created in the `preg_match("/plugged: (.*)/")` branch, so a row gets the block only if ifconfig prints a `plugged:` line for it — a physical port with a transceiver. The canary VM is virtio-only, so no row carries it and the path is absent wholesale; the prod box has three populated cages and validates the subtree normally. Exempted with `missingOK: ["*.sfp"]` and the same prune trigger as the existing `interfacesOverview` `rows[].sfp` entry: it goes when a canary box with a real SFP cage exists. No `.*` companion is needed here because this struct types the block as `flexStringMap`, so the schema walker stops at the parent.

**Live re-run after the fix** (`cmd/apidrift` against the devel box): 174 probed, **173 clean, 0 breaking mismatches, 0 missing paths, 0 unexpected top-level keys**. The only remaining line is `siproxdRegistrations` 404, which is the expected plugin-gated absence.
