title: OPNsense live-box canary drift

body:
## Two label spaces describe the same interface and cannot be joined

#366 shipped `opnsense_netflow_capture_expected{interface}` and established, with live measurement, that it cannot detect a single dead `ng_netflow` hook: `ng_netflow` fills one side of every flow from a FIB lookup, so records captured on the LAN hook also name the egress WAN. On the reference box `netflow_pppoe0` had processed zero packets while 92% of all volume was attributed to `AAISP`, which is that interface.

The thing that **does** see a dead hook is already exported: `opnsense_netflow_cache_packets_total{interface}`, one series per `ng_netflow` node, straight from the box. `netflow_pppoe0` reads 0 there right now, correctly, while its peers climb.

The two cannot be joined in PromQL, because `interface` means different things on each:

| metric | `interface` value | source |
|---|---|---|
| `opnsense_netflow_cache_*` | kernel **device** — `pppoe0`, `ixl0_vlan25` | `flowctl` node names |
| `opnsense_netflow_capture_*` | configured **description** — `AAISP`, `CAM` | netflow config model option-dict `value` |
| `opnsense_flow_*` | configured **description** | ifIndex map `Name` |

So "configured to capture on AAISP, and the `pppoe0` node has been frozen at zero for an hour" is currently a manual, two-panel, eyeball correlation. It is the highest-value netflow health signal there is and nothing can express it in one query.

The correspondence is not missing — the exporter already builds it. The ifIndex map holds `index → device → name` and renders it on the operator console's ifIndex tab. It just is not on any metric.

## Options

1. **Add a `device` label to `opnsense_netflow_capture_expected`.** Cheapest join. Risk: the device is only known when the flow lane's ifIndex map exists, so the series shape would depend on whether a different subsystem is enabled — a metric whose labels appear and disappear is worse than no join.
2. **Emit a dedicated mapping metric**, e.g. `opnsense_flow_interface_info{device,interface,ifindex} 1`, the standard info-metric join pattern. Bounded (~17 series), stable shape, and both spaces join through it with `group_left`. Also makes the ifIndex map queryable, which today only the console shows.
3. **Relabel the cache metrics into description space.** Rejected on sight: breaks every existing query and dashboard, and `#98` deliberately put them in device space.

Option 2 looks right. It costs one small series family and needs no change to either existing metric.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The device ↔ description ↔ ifIndex correspondence is queryable as a metric
- [ ] A single PromQL expression can state "interface configured for capture whose own `ng_netflow` node has been at zero for longer than the active timeout"
- [ ] Existing `opnsense_netflow_cache_*` and `opnsense_flow_*` label spaces are unchanged
- [ ] The join is on a Grafana panel, and `docs/flow.md` replaces its current "the two cannot be joined directly" paragraph with the query

comments.body:
Shipped in ff5b9c7 — option 2, as the issue recommended.

**`opnsense_flow_interface_info{device,interface,ifindex}`**, value always 1, one series per resolved ifIndex (17 on the test box, bounded by the interface count). Published by the flow collector from the ifIndex map that already existed, so the correspondence stops being console-only. Neither existing label space changed.

Two behaviours worth knowing, both documented in `docs/flow.md`:

- `interface` is unique only across **assigned** interfaces. OPNsense gives every unassigned device the same `Unassigned Interface` placeholder, so a `group_left` whose *left* side carried that value would trip the many-to-one uniqueness rule. Nothing worth joining does — the capture config lists assigned interfaces only — and an error there beats a plausible wrong device.
- For the first seconds after a restart the series exist with an empty `interface`: the enumeration and the interface metadata are separate fetches and the map publishes as soon as the enumeration lands (the #365 cold-start behaviour). Observed live, not theorised.

## The query

It grew a clause beyond what the issue asked for, because the three-clause version has a false positive: a node frozen at zero is *also* what a legitimately idle interface looks like. pf settles it, and is already in device space:

```promql
max by (opnsense_instance, interface, device) (
  (opnsense_netflow_capture_expected == 1)
    * on (opnsense_instance, interface) group_left (device) opnsense_flow_interface_info
)
and on (opnsense_instance, device) max by (opnsense_instance, device) (
  label_join(increase(opnsense_netflow_cache_packets_total[45m]), "device", "", "interface") == 0
)
and on (opnsense_instance, device) max by (opnsense_instance, device) (
  label_join(increase(opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_bytes_total[45m]), "device", "", "interface") > 0
)
and on (opnsense_instance) (opnsense_netflow_capture_active_timeout_seconds < 2700)
```

Clause 4 is the honesty check on the window: "exported nothing" means nothing until the active timeout has passed, so the query withdraws itself if the box is configured above 45m rather than letting `[45m]` quietly become a lie. The box reads 1800s live, so it clears. `label_join`, not `label_replace`, because both the cache and pf families put a device in their `interface` label and a `$1` capture reference gets eaten by Grafana variable interpolation — that one would have shipped broken and rendered empty.

## Verification

Not asserted — measured:

- The full four-clause expression, run against the reference box's live data (`opnsense_interfaces_info` standing in for the not-yet-deployed metric, same device/description pairing), returned **exactly one row: `{interface="AAISP", device="pppoe0"}`** — the dead hook from #366 that previously needed a packet capture to find. Healthy interfaces: none returned.
- A local exporter run against the test box published all 17 series with the triple intact (`vtnet0`/`LAN`/1 … `wg1`/`Unassigned Interface`/15, plus `""`/`locally-originated`/0).
- Generated PromQL parsed with `promtool check rules`; `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check` (coverage 818/818), `go test ./...` and `golangci-lint` all clean.

## Acceptance

- [x] The device ↔ description ↔ ifIndex correspondence is queryable as a metric
- [x] A single PromQL expression states the fault (and now distinguishes a dead hook from an idle interface)
- [x] `opnsense_netflow_cache_*` and `opnsense_flow_*` label spaces unchanged
- [x] On a Grafana panel — NetFlow → **Hook Liveness** row: the map as a table plus the join; `docs/flow.md` replaces the "cannot be joined directly" paragraph with the query

No alert rule shipped, consistent with #366's deliberate no-verdict stance — but unlike #366 this expression is conclusive, so it is now a reasonable candidate if you want one. The dashboard still needs the manual push to `gc-gitsync-m7kni`.

title: netflow: make the device/description label spaces joinable so a dead ng_netflow hook is one query

body:
## The counter #365 added is still not visible on a live box

`ProcessorStats.RecordsUnmapped` is populated — `internal/flow/processor.go:141-143` increments `p.noIfaceMap` for every record whose ifIndexes both resolved to nothing — and `Stats()` returns it at `processor.go:225`. Nothing consumes it. `internal/collector/flow.go:706-724` publishes `RecordsEmitted`, `RecordsDropped`, `RecordsNoAddr` and `RecordsHeld` from the same struct and simply omits this one field.

So the counter exists, is correct, and is unreadable.

This matters right now because #365 just moved that increment **out** of the `if m != nil` guard specifically so the cold-start window — the one period where nothing can be labelled — stops being silent. That fix is verified working: on `012ff0d`, five minutes after a restart, the empty-label bucket is entirely absent where the pre-fix baseline held 4212.27 MB / 94.7% ([evidence](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/issues/365#issuecomment-5072520494)). But the metric that would have *told* an operator that window happened, and how many records it swallowed, does not exist. The fix is invisible from outside the process.

That is the same failure shape #365 existed to fix, one layer up: a quantity is being counted where nobody can see it, which for observability purposes is the same as not counting it.

## It is not the same thing as `ifindex_unmapped_total`

`opnsense_flow_ifindex_unmapped_total` already exists and reads 0 on the live box. It is a different quantity and cannot substitute:

| | counts | fires when the map is nil? |
|---|---|---|
| `opnsense_flow_ifindex_unmapped_total` | `IfMap.Iface` **lookups** that resolved to no interface — two per record, and it is attached to the map object | **No.** `IfMap.Iface` returns early on a nil receiver without touching the counter, deliberately (#365 acceptance item 4). |
| `RecordsUnmapped` (unpublished) | **records** where neither ifIndex resolved, including every record processed before the first map is published | **Yes — that is the point.** |

During cold start the first reads 0 and the second is the only thing counting. They also differ in unit (lookups vs records) even once a map exists, so they are complementary rather than redundant.

## Not part of the accounting identity

`RecordsIn = RecordsEmitted + RecordsDropped + RecordsNoAddr + RecordsHeld`, per the doc comment at `processor.go:68-75`. `RecordsUnmapped` is deliberately **outside** it: an unmapped record still emits, with an empty interface label, because dropping loses data and an empty label is honest. So this must not be published as a `reason` on `netflow_records_dropped_total` — it is not a drop, and folding it in there would break the funnel arithmetic that panel's description promises (`decoded = emitted + dropped`). It needs to be its own series.

## Proposed shape

A standalone counter, `opnsense_flow_netflow_records_unmapped_total`, no labels, published from zero like the other self-metrics so a healthy lane reads a flat zero rather than nothing at all. It belongs on the existing "NetFlow ifIndex Map" panel next to `ifindex_unmapped_total`, since the two together distinguish "the map is missing" from "the map is wrong".

## Acceptance

- [ ] `ProcessorStats.RecordsUnmapped` is published as a counter, from zero, with a test that fails if it is dropped again
- [ ] The metric is distinguishable from `ifindex_unmapped_total` in its help text — an operator must not read them as the same number
- [ ] It is NOT folded into `netflow_records_dropped_total`; the funnel identity stays intact
- [ ] On a Grafana panel (the coverage gate requires it regardless)
- [ ] `docs/flow.md` explains what a non-zero value means and that these records still counted, with an empty label

comments.body:
Done in `70c9b2b`.

- [x] Published as `opnsense_flow_netflow_records_unmapped_total`, a counter, from zero. `TestFlowCollector_PublishesRecordsUnmapped` fails if the emit is removed or wired to the wrong field — both mutations were run and both were caught.
- [x] Help text states the distinction against `ifindex_unmapped_total` explicitly (lookups against a map that exists vs records, and which of the two fires while the map is nil).
- [x] Not folded into `records_dropped_total`. `TestFlowCollector_UnmappedIsNotADropReason` pins that no `unmapped` reason appears and that the drop counters stay at zero in a fixture where 7 records went unmapped, so the funnel identity is intact.
- [x] On the existing "NetFlow ifIndex Map" panel next to the lookup counter, with the panel description rewritten to lead on the fact that the two series are not the same number. Coverage gate: 813/813.
- [x] `docs/flow.md` gained a bullet in the guards list covering what a non-zero value means, that those records still counted with an empty label, and why it is not a drop reason.

Gate green: `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check`.

### Regeneration-order note

The documented order is `make dashboard` then `make docs`, because `make docs` re-pins counts out of `dashboard-stats.json`. That is right for a panel-only change but insufficient when a **new metric** is introduced: the coverage gate's catalogue is parsed out of `docs/metrics/metrics.md` (`grafana/build_dashboard.py:373`), which `make docs` writes. So a new metric needs a fixpoint — `make docs` (metric enters the catalogue), `make dashboard` (coverage sees it, stats update), `make docs` (counts re-pinned). Running only the documented two-step leaves `dashboard-stats.json` claiming 812 metrics against a docs tree that says 813, and `make grafana-check` fails on `git diff --exit-code`. Hit and resolved here.

title: flow: RecordsUnmapped is counted but never published, so the cold-start window #365 fixed is still invisible

body:
## A netflow node can lose its interface hook and keep looking healthy

Observed for real on the reference box on 2026-07-24. A PPPoE WAN was bounced; `pppoe0` was destroyed and recreated. The ng_netflow node for it survived the churn but its `ifaceN` hook did not:

```
netflow_ixl1     Num hooks: 3    export9, out2, iface2      <- healthy
netflow_pppoe0   Num hooks: 1    export9                    <- exports nothing
```

The node existed. The export ksocket was connected. `configctl netflow status` reported the service running. `api/diagnostics/netflow/getconfig` still listed `opt7` as a selected capture interface. Nothing anywhere said the box had stopped capturing its primary WAN — the one carrying ~91% of inbound volume — and it stayed that way until `configctl netflow restart` reattached it as `iface15`.

**From the exporter's side this is indistinguishable from an idle interface.** No records arrive for that ifIndex, which is exactly what a quiet link looks like. Every existing counter reads healthy, because nothing is malformed, nothing is unmapped, and nothing is dropped — there is simply an absence, and absence is what the metrics cannot currently speak about.

## Why the exporter can detect it when the firewall doesn't

The set of interfaces that *should* be producing records is knowable. `api/diagnostics/netflow/getconfig` returns it directly — verified live, HTTP 200, 1,002 bytes:

```json
{"netflow": {"capture": {"interfaces": {
  "opt7": {"value": "AAISP", "selected": 1},
  "opt4": {"value": "CAM",   "selected": 1},
  "opt2": {"value": "IOT",   "selected": 1},
  "lan":  {"value": "LAN",   "selected": 1},
  ...
}}}}
```

`selected: 1` is the capture set; `opt1` (tailscale) and `opt5` (zenoverlay) are `0` on this box. Crossed with the ifIndex map the exporter already builds, that yields a list of interfaces from which records are expected — and the receiver already knows which ifIndexes have actually been seen.

The endpoint is **not currently registered** in `opnsense/client.go`, so this is genuinely unbuilt.

## Proposed shape

A per-interface gauge along the lines of `opnsense_flow_netflow_capture_expected{interface}`, paired with the time since a record was last seen for it. An interface that is configured for capture and has produced nothing for well past its active-flow timeout is the signal. The exact metric shape is open — the important part is that "configured to export, exporting nothing" becomes expressible at all.

### Things to get right

- **This must not fire on a genuinely idle interface.** A guest VLAN with nothing on it is legitimately silent for hours. Whatever the threshold, it has to be long enough that quiet is not an alarm, and the metric should expose the raw "seconds since last record" so an operator picks their own threshold rather than inheriting ours.
- **Cardinality is bounded** — one series per configured capture interface, a closed set from the firewall's own config, so this does not inherit the unauthenticated-socket cardinality problem the record path has.
- **Do not alert on it at startup.** Every interface is silent before the first record arrives; the metric needs to distinguish "never seen since boot" from "seen, then stopped".
- **The endpoint is plugin-independent but netflow-specific.** It should degrade quietly (no metrics, no errors) on a box where the netflow reporting feature is not configured, in the same way the plugin-gated collectors do.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `api/diagnostics/netflow/getconfig` registered, with a `Fetch*` returning the selected capture interfaces
- [ ] The expected-vs-seen comparison is exposed as a metric, with seconds-since-last-record rather than a baked-in verdict
- [ ] Silent-at-startup and genuinely-idle interfaces do not present as faults
- [ ] Schema-registry entry + `make schemas`; the response is config, so caching is permissible under the usual rule — confirm it carries no live status before adding it
- [ ] `docs/flow.md` explains what the signal means and what it cannot tell you

comments.body:
Done in `0f83056`. One finding below changes what this metric can honestly claim, so read that before relying on it.

## Acceptance

- [x] `api/diagnostics/netflow/getconfig` registered (`netflowGetConfig`, endpoint count 174 → 175) with `FetchNetflowCaptureConfig()` returning the selected capture set plus the two flow timeouts.
- [x] Exposed as `opnsense_netflow_capture_expected{interface}` (1 selected / 0 listed-but-not-selected) paired with `opnsense_netflow_capture_last_record_seconds{interface}` — a raw age, no baked-in verdict, no alert rule.
- [x] Silent-at-startup and genuinely-idle do not present as faults. A never-seen interface has **no age series at all** rather than a large number, pinned by `TestNetflowCollector_NeverSeenInterfaceHasNoLastRecordSeries`. Also shipped `opnsense_netflow_capture_active_timeout_seconds` / `_inactive_timeout_seconds` so the threshold is derived from the box's own 1800s/15s rather than guessed.
- [x] Schema registry entry + `make schemas`, structure-only golden. Caching: **confirmed clean, deliberately not applied** — see below.
- [x] `docs/flow.md` gained a section covering what the signal means and, more importantly, what it cannot tell you.

## The finding: a fresh age does not prove the hook is alive

The proposed design rests on "no records for interface X ⇒ X is not being captured". That inference does not hold, and it fails on exactly this box.

`ng_netflow` stamps the capturing hook's index on **one** side of a flow and fills the **other** side from a FIB lookup. So a record captured on the LAN hook also names the egress WAN. An interface can be named continuously while its own capture hook produces nothing.

Measured live 2026-07-24, not inferred:

```
# ngctl msg netflow_pppoe0: info
Args:   { Inactive timeout=15 Active timeout=1800 }          <- no packet/byte counters at all

# ngctl msg netflow_ixl0: info
Args:   { IPv4 bytes=65132219225 IPv4 packets=62450645 ... }
```

`netflow_pppoe0` had processed **nothing**. Over the same window the exporter attributed **10,991 MB — 92.4% of all volume** — to `AAISP`, which is ifIndex 15 = `pppoe0`. Every one of those records was captured by `netflow_ixl0` and the VLAN nodes and named the WAN from a route lookup.

Note the node is in the shape this issue calls healthy — 3 hooks, `iface15` and `out15` both attached to `pppoe0`:

```
netflow_pppoe0  Num hooks: 3
  export9   -> ksocket_netflow_pppoe0
  out15     -> pppoe0:upper
  iface15   -> pppoe0:lower
```

The reason it still captures nothing is that the netgraph node named `pppoe0` is type **`pppoe`** — the PPPoE session/framing node on `ixl2` — not the IP-layer interface. The IP interface is the `iface` node `ng0` (which `ifconfig` presents as `pppoe0`, carrying <pub-ip-2>). The netflow node is hooked to the framing node, so no IP packets ever reach it. **So "3 hooks = healthy, 1 hook = broken" is not a sound test either** — this box is at 3 hooks and capturing zero.

### What this means for the shipped metric

It **does** catch: the receiver losing its feed, the export target going wrong, netflow stopped box-wide, an interface dropping out of the capture set — anything where *nothing* names the interface.

It does **not** catch a single hook dying behind other nodes' FIB lookups, which is the motivating incident. Had this metric existed during that hour it would have read healthy for AAISP.

Rather than ship a metric that quietly implies a guarantee it does not provide, the limitation is stated in the metric help text, the panel description and `docs/flow.md`, each pointing at the thing that *does* see it: `opnsense_netflow_cache_packets_total{interface="<device>"}`, one series per `ng_netflow` node, already shipped. A node pinned at zero while its peers climb is the firewall's own account of a dead hook — `netflow_pppoe0` reads 0 there right now, correctly.

The two label spaces cannot be joined directly: cache metrics are keyed by kernel **device** (`pppoe0`), capture metrics by configured **description** (`AAISP`). The console's ifIndex tab prints the correspondence. Making that join automatic is worth a follow-up; I did not widen scope here.

## Caching — confirmed clean, still not applied

`getconfigAction` returns `$mdlNetflow->getNodes()`, the stored model straight out of `config.xml`. No counters, no live status: it passes the "wholly slow-moving GET body" test outright.

It is still **not** given a body TTL. The netflow collector is on the **fast** tier, and `TestBodyCachedEndpointsPollSlowerThanTheirTTL` forbids a body TTL on any fast-tier collector, on the grounds that fast-tier data is by definition not slow-moving. That guard reasons about the *collector*, and here the tier is set by the collector's other three endpoints, which are genuinely live. Subverting a guard built for exactly this shape to save one PHP call every 15s is a bad trade, so the endpoint is uncached and the reasoning is in the commit message.

## Payload notes for whoever touches this next

Serialization is **not** uniform — a struct that assumes it is will not decode this:

- `capture.interfaces`, `egress_only`, `version`, `targets` are `{value, selected}` option dicts, keyed by ident (`opt7`) with the **description** in `value` (`AAISP`). The description is what every flow metric labels with, so it is the only key the two can be joined on.
- `collect.enable` is a `BooleanField` and comes back as a **bare string** `"0"`, not an option dict.
- `activeTimeout` / `inactiveTimeout` are **strings**, not JSON numbers.
- A box with netflow never configured still answers 200: the `InterfaceField` enumerates every interface with `selected: 0`. That is "nothing is expected to export", not an error and not an absent feature — `TestFetchNetflowCaptureConfig_UnconfiguredBoxIsNotAnError` pins it.

## Gate

`go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check` — all green. Mutation-checked: omitting unselected interfaces, returning the getconfig error instead of warning, and emitting never-seen interfaces as a number are each caught by a distinct test, as are dropping the Zenarmor source filter and letting the interface cap freeze a known interface's timestamp.

title: flow: detect an interface configured for netflow capture that is exporting nothing (a lost ifaceN hook reads as an idle link)

body:
## 4.2 GB landed with an empty interface label and nothing counted it

Observed live immediately after deploying #364, on a container that had been up ~2 minutes:

```
(empty)              4212.27 MB   94.7%
AAISP                 115.04 MB    2.6%
LAN                   114.93 MB    2.6%
```

Every ifIndex health metric read clean throughout:

```
opnsense_flow_ifindex_conflicts             0
opnsense_flow_ifindex_source_disagreements  0   (both reasons)
opnsense_flow_ifindex_unmapped_total        0
```

Sampling twice 45s apart shows the empty bucket is **frozen** while the real ones grow — so the labels are correct now and this is entirely a **cold-start artifact**, not ongoing:

```
sample 1:  (empty)=4212.27  AAISP=1216.23  LAN=208.02
sample 2:  (empty)=4212.27  AAISP=1776.55  LAN=240.70
```

## Cause

`internal/flow/processor.go:129`:

```go
if m != nil {
    rec.In = m.Iface(nr.InIfIndex)
    rec.Out = m.Iface(nr.OutIfIndex)
    if rec.In.Device == "" && rec.Out.Device == "" {
        p.noIfaceMap.Add(1)
    }
}
```

The counter increment is **inside** the nil guard. With no map published yet, the whole block is skipped: `rec.In`/`rec.Out` stay zero (empty label), and nothing is counted. `IfMap.Iface` has the same shape — it returns early on a nil receiver without touching the counter, which is correct for that method but leaves the caller as the only place the fact can be recorded.

So a nil map is completely silent: no label, no count, no signal of any kind. It is indistinguishable from a quiet network, which is the failure mode this pipeline's counters exist to make impossible.

## Why the window got wider

Pre-#361 the map was published as soon as the interface metadata arrived. #361 made publishing conditional on a non-empty `IfaceOrder` — correctly, since a map built from an empty enumeration resolves nothing — but the rebuild runs on a **60-second** ticker (`ifIndexRefreshInterval`), and the first tick fires before the enrichment refresher has completed its first fetch. So the loop skips, and the next attempt is a full minute later.

On a WAN doing ~28 MB/s that is gigabytes of traffic attributed to nothing, once per restart, on every deployment.

## Fix

Two parts, both small:

1. **Count it.** Move the increment out of the nil guard so a nil map is recorded as an unmapped record. It genuinely is one. Without this the alarm cannot fire during the exact window it is most needed.
2. **Shorten the window.** Retry the first map build on a short interval until the first successful publish, then settle to the normal 60s. The map should be live within a second or two of the enrichment snapshot landing, not up to a minute after.

Deliberately NOT changing: records with no map still **emit** with an empty label rather than being dropped. Dropping loses data, and an empty label is honest — it is the silence that was the bug, not the label.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A record processed with a nil ifIndex map increments the unmapped counter, with a test
- [ ] The first map publish happens within seconds of the enrichment snapshot having an ordering, not on the next 60s tick
- [ ] A restart on a busy box leaves at most a small fraction of a scrape interval in the empty bucket, verified live
- [ ] `IfMap.Iface`'s nil-receiver behaviour stays allocation-free and non-counting; the caller owns this

## The kernel index is directly available for every device; the rank heuristic should go

#363 shipped a reconstruction that back-fills devices with no API-stated index into the free slots in attach order. It is correct on the reference box — validated 16/16 against live `ifinfo` — but it rests on a premise that is **false**:

> only a configured interface can be destroyed and recreated at runtime; the devices with no stated index are unassigned ports and kernel pseudo-devices which attach at boot and never churn

They do churn. A recreated device reclaims the **lowest free** index (FreeBSD `ifindex_alloc`) while being re-appended to the tail of the attach list, so an unstated device that churns and returns to a low index gets back-filled into a slot far too high, shifting everything between.

Device types that churn at runtime **and** never appear in `api/diagnostics/traffic/interface`:

| device | churns because | absent because |
|---|---|---|
| **`pfsync0`** | `configd interface pfsync.configure` | never a config interface — and holds index **10** here, mid-range, so its misplacement shifts six devices |
| `wgN` | destroyed/recreated on every WireGuard apply | unassigned by default |
| `ovpnc*` / `ovpns*` | recreated on instance restart | unassigned by default |
| `zen0`, `tailscale0` | recreated on service restart | unassigned on a stock install (assigned on this box, which is why the heuristic survives here) |
| unassigned VLAN / LAGG / bridge / GIF / GRE / VXLAN | each destroy+recreate on apply | configured under Other Types, never assigned |
| assigned-but-**disabled** interfaces | same as their type | dropped by `traffic/interface`'s `enable => true` filter |

So: correct today, one WireGuard restart or one unassigned-VLAN apply away from being silently wrong, with nothing to distinguish that from working. It should be replaced rather than tuned.

## The direct source

**`api/diagnostics/interface/get_interface_statistics`** — plain GET, 8.8 KB, no params. Handler is configd `[show.interfaces]` → `netstat -i -n -W -b -d --libxo json`. Each interface's AF_LINK row carries `network` as the literal `<Link#N>`, and **N is the kernel `if_index`**. Source: `usr.bin/netstat/if.c`, `snprintf(linknum, ..., "<Link#%d>", sdl->sdl_index)`.

Verified live, HTTP 200, **16/16 devices including `pfsync0`**, with the post-bounce inversion right:

```
ixl0 1   ixl1 2   ixl2 3   ixl3 4   igb0 5   igb1 6   lo0 7   enc0 8
pflog0 9   pfsync0 10   ixl0_vlan100 11   ixl0_vlan25 12   ixl0_vlan50 13
zen0 14   pppoe0 15   tailscale0 16
```

Sorting by index and ranking reproduces `ifinfo` byte-for-byte. It is also *more* reachable than what we already call: it has an ACL entry (`page-diagnostics-netstat`), whereas `get_interface_config` has none and is admin-only.

## Why rank, not the index itself

`ifinfo` walks the ifmib table by row number, and the row number **is** the kernel index (`/usr/ports/opnsense/ifinfo/files/ifinfo.c` — `for (i = 1; i <= maxifno; i++)`, `continue` on `ENOENT`). It does not sort; the table is already index-ordered and sparse. `rc.d/netflow` and `parse.py` both count **position** in that output and both ignore the printed `index:` field.

So ifIndex is the **rank over live indices**, and rank equals index only while the space is dense. A permanent removal leaves a gap and they diverge — which is exactly what the existing `stated_index` guard detects.

## Plan

1. Register `api/diagnostics/interface/get_interface_statistics`; fetch `name → N` from rows whose `network` matches `^<Link#(\d+)>$`, ignoring the per-address rows.
2. Sort by N, ifIndex = 1-based rank. One endpoint, one fetch — which also removes the cross-endpoint race the current two-fetch scheme has.
3. Delete `reconstructIfinfoOrder` and its attach-order fill.
4. Keep `traffic/interface` as the **independent** `stated_index` guard, unchanged. It stays a genuinely separate derivation (`ifinfo` via PHP vs `netstat` via libxo). Do not promote it to a derivation input.

### Guards, keeping the refuse-and-hold discipline

- Zero `<Link#>` rows → refuse. A netstat/libxo format change fails exactly this way.
- A device with two different N, or two devices with the same N → refuse.
- **Count cross-check** against the device count from `get_interface_config` (16 = 16 here). A mismatch means a source is missing a device. Note the `interfaces_info`/`export` endpoints return 15 — `parseIfInfo()` has a hardcoded `if ($if == 'pfsync0') { continue; }` — so never cross-check against those.
- On any refusal: keep the last good map, let `ifindex_map_age_seconds` rise. No fallback to attach order or to the rank heuristic.

### Known residual, not fixable through the API

The `ifaceN` hook name is frozen when netflow is *configured*, not when a flow is exported. Between an interface churning and OPNsense reconfiguring netflow, a freshly-derived map is right about `ifinfo` and wrong about the hooks actually wired. That window is what the disagreement guard is for. (Observed for real this session: after a PPPoE reconnect `netflow_pppoe0` kept its node but lost its `ifaceN` hook entirely and captured nothing until `configctl netflow restart`.)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Ordering derives from `get_interface_statistics` ranks; `reconstructIfinfoOrder` deleted
- [ ] `<Link#N>` parsing ignores per-address rows and tolerates unexpected rows
- [ ] Fixture from this box's live payload asserts all 16 including `pfsync0` at 10 and the post-bounce `pppoe0` at 15
- [ ] Each guard refuses and keeps the last good map, with a test
- [ ] `traffic/interface` remains the independent cross-check, not an input
- [ ] Schema-registry entry + `make schemas`; endpoint NOT cached (it carries live counters)
- [ ] `docs/flow.md` names the real source and drops the attach-order-correction description

## The ordering source drifts from `ifinfo` after an interface is recreated

#361 moved the ifIndex enumeration onto `api/diagnostics/interface/get_interface_config`, on the evidence that its JSON key order reproduced `ifinfo` order exactly — 16/16 devices on the reference box. That was true when measured. It is not invariant.

Bouncing WAN1 broke it within minutes. Live, right now:

```
ifinfo:       ... zen0(14)  pppoe0(15)  tailscale0(16)      <- sorted by KERNEL INDEX
ifconfig -l:  ... zen0      tailscale0  pppoe0              <- ATTACH order, pppoe0 last
```

`get_interface_config` follows `ifconfig -l`. `interfaces_info` follows `ifconfig -l`. **`rc.d/netflow` and `scripts/netflow/lib/parse.py` both count `ifinfo`.** So every API source is in attach order and the thing that names the netgraph hook is in kernel-index order, and the two coincide only until something is destroyed and recreated.

`pppoe0` reclaims kernel index 15 (the lowest free one) but is re-appended to the end of the ifnet list. `ifinfo` re-sorts it back to position 15; the API does not.

This is the same class of bug #361 fixed, with a different trigger: #361's source dropped a device, this one reorders two.

### Corrections to what #361 concluded

Two things stated there are now known to be wrong, and both were stated confidently:

- **"`get_interface_config` reproduces `ifinfo` order exactly"** — it reproduces it while the index space is dense and nothing has been recreated. It is attach order, which is a different thing that happened to agree.
- **"A reconnect does not renumber anything"** (`f2bae6e`) — true of `ifinfo` and therefore of the netflow hook names, which is what that comment was about, but NOT true of the API ordering the exporter actually consumes. The correction corrected the wrong half.

### The guard worked, which is the one good part

`opnsense_flow_ifindex_source_disagreements{reason="stated_index"}` went to **2** the moment the two sources diverged, naming exactly `pppoe0` and `tailscale0`. `ifindex_conflicts` also reads 2, i.e. the operator pins are winning over a derivation that is genuinely wrong. On this box the labels are therefore still correct — but only because the pins are set. An unpinned box would now be mislabelling its primary WAN.

That is the guard doing precisely its job. It caught the exporter's own new source being wrong, on the first real event after deployment.

### What the fix has to be

`ifinfo` sorts by kernel index, so its position is the **rank of the device once all devices are ordered by kernel index** — not the kernel index itself (a gap from a permanent removal makes rank and index differ, which is the case the existing guard already models).

The obstacle is that no API endpoint carries the kernel index for every device:

| endpoint | devices | has index? |
|---|---|---|
| `api/diagnostics/interface/get_interface_config` | all 16 | no |
| `api/interfaces/overview/interfaces_info` | 15 (omits pfsync0) | no |
| `api/diagnostics/traffic/interface` | 8 (configured only) | **yes** |

The 8 that carry an index are exactly the configured interfaces, which are also exactly the ones that can be labelled and the ones that get destroyed and recreated. The unconfigured remainder (`ixl2`, `ixl3`, `igb0`, `igb1`, `enc0`, `pflog0`, `pfsync0`) are attached at boot and never churn, so their attach order and index order do not drift apart in practice.

So a workable reconstruction is: take the full device list for membership, apply the known kernel indices, and rank. Whether that is sound enough to trust unpinned, or whether this should instead surface loudly and lean on the guard plus pins, is the open design question — do not just implement the ranking without deciding that.

Worth checking before designing: whether any other endpoint exposes a per-device index for unassigned interfaces.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Decide and record whether the enumeration can be reconstructed from the API alone, or whether an unreconstructable case must degrade to "keep last good map + guard fires" rather than guess
- [ ] The reference box's post-bounce state is a regression fixture: `get_interface_config` in attach order with `pppoe0` last, `traffic/interface` stating 15 for it, asserting the map still resolves 15 to `pppoe0`
- [ ] `stated_index` disagreements go to 0 on this box without pins
- [ ] `docs/flow.md` corrected: the endpoint's key order is attach order, not `ifinfo` order, and the two diverge on a recreate
- [ ] The `f2bae6e` comments claiming a reconnect changes nothing are re-corrected — it changes nothing about `ifinfo`, but it does reorder every API source

## Ground truth: the hook is `iface15`, so `ifinfo` wins and the API source is definitively wrong

The bounce had left `netflow_pppoe0` detached — the node existed with only its `export9` ksocket hook and no `ifaceN` at all, so WAN1 was not being captured. `configctl netflow restart` reattached it, and that re-ran `rc.d/netflow`'s counter against the CURRENT `ifinfo`:

```
BEFORE                                    AFTER
netflow_pppoe0        hooks=NONE          netflow_pppoe0        hooks=iface15
netflow_ixl0          hooks=iface1        netflow_ixl0          hooks=iface1
netflow_ixl1          hooks=iface2        netflow_ixl1          hooks=iface2
netflow_ixl0_vlan100  hooks=iface11       netflow_ixl0_vlan100  hooks=iface11
netflow_ixl0_vlan25   hooks=iface12       netflow_ixl0_vlan25   hooks=iface12
netflow_ixl0_vlan50   hooks=iface13       netflow_ixl0_vlan50   hooks=iface13
```

**`iface15`.** At the moment that ran, `ifinfo` had `pppoe0` at position 15 and every API endpoint had it at 16. The hook name is the mapping that actually arrives in the records, so this settles it as measurement rather than inference:

- **`ifinfo` order is authoritative.** Kernel-index order.
- **`get_interface_config` key order is wrong** whenever it diverges, and it diverges after any recreate.

Records arriving now carry ifIndex 15 for the PPPoE WAN while the shipped derivation resolves 15 to `tailscale0`. On this box the pins mask it; unpinned, it would be mislabelling the WAN outright — with `ifindex_source_disagreements{reason="stated_index"}` at 2 as the only signal.

## Side note worth recording: a recreate can silently detach the netflow hook

This is a firewall-side behaviour, not an exporter bug, but it changes what "no data" means. After the PPPoE reconnect the `netflow_pppoe0` node survived while its `ifaceN` hook did not, so ng_netflow kept a node that captured nothing. Nothing on the box reports that state — the service is "running", the node is present, and the export socket is connected.

From the exporter's side it looks identical to a quiet WAN. Worth considering whether the exporter can distinguish "this interface is configured for netflow capture but is exporting nothing" from "this interface is idle" — `api/diagnostics/netflow/getconfig` already lists the selected capture interfaces, so the set of interfaces that *should* be producing records is knowable. That would be a separate issue if it is worth having; noting it here so the observation is not lost.

## A reconstruction that works, validated against the currently-diverged box

Tested against the live post-bounce state, where `get_interface_config` and `ifinfo` genuinely disagree:

```
1. Take the full device set and attach order from get_interface_config.
2. Place every device whose kernel index traffic/interface states at that index.
3. Fill the remaining slots, in attach order, with the devices that have no stated index.
4. Consistency check. If it fails, keep the last good map and let the guard fire.
```

Result on the diverged data:

```
reconstructed: ixl0 ixl1 ixl2 ixl3 igb0 igb1 lo0 enc0 pflog0 pfsync0 ixl0_vlan100 ixl0_vlan25 ixl0_vlan50 zen0 pppoe0 tailscale0
ifinfo truth : ixl0 ixl1 ixl2 ixl3 igb0 igb1 lo0 enc0 pflog0 pfsync0 ixl0_vlan100 ixl0_vlan25 ixl0_vlan50 zen0 pppoe0 tailscale0
MATCH

naive attach order gets wrong:
  pos 15: attach=tailscale0  truth=pppoe0
  pos 16: attach=pppoe0      truth=tailscale0
```

Step 3 lands `ixl2 ixl3 igb0 igb1 lo0 enc0 pflog0 pfsync0` in free slots `3..10`, which is exactly where `ifinfo` has them. It works because the devices with no stated index are the unconfigured ones, and those attach at boot and never churn — so their attach order is still their index order. The devices that DO churn are configured by definition, so they always carry a stated index.

### Why it is sound, and precisely where it is not

The step-3 fill assumes the index space is **dense**. That is the case it can solve, and it solves it exactly.

With a gap — an interface removed permanently — `ifinfo` position and kernel index stop being equal for everything above the gap, and step 2 would place a known device one slot too high. The consistency check catches this rather than guessing: a stated index outside `1..N`, a collision on a slot, or a mismatch between the number of unplaced devices and the number of free slots all mean the reconstruction cannot be trusted.

**On failure it must keep the last good map and let `ifindex_map_age_seconds` rise, exactly as the fetch-failure path already does.** It must NOT fall back to raw attach order — that is the current bug. This is the same rule #361 established: a wrong interface label is worse than a missing one.

That gives a clean contract worth stating in the code: *this reconstruction is exact while the kernel index space is dense, and refuses rather than guesses when it is not.* The `stated_index` guard remains the detector for the sparse case, and would fire for every device above the gap at once.

### Still open

Whether a single endpoint exposes a kernel index for ALL devices, which would make step 3 unnecessary and the sparse case solvable by ranking. Under investigation. If one exists, prefer it — this reconstruction is a workaround for a missing field, and should be described that way in the code rather than presented as the natural approach.

body:
## What happened

While winding down the #360 NetFlow capture window on the reference box, the shared debug-capture dir had **31 MB of syslog captures across 29 rotated files** built up over roughly a day. All of it is `kind="unparsed"`.

Aggregated over the whole set — 60,073 entries:

| share | program | dominant message |
|---|---|---|
| 51.0% | `kernel` | `arpresolve: can't allocate llinfo for 86.31.203.x` |
| 19.1% | `/usr/sbin/cron` | `(nobody) MAIL (mailed 37 bytes of output but got status 0x000...)` — 11,485 times |
| 7.6% | `unbound` | `dnsbl_module: updating blocklist.` |
| 3.8% | `kea-dhcp6` | `DHCPSRV_MEMFILE_LFC...` / `ALLOC_ENGINE_V...` |
| 2.4% | `dhclient` | `DHCPDISCOVER on ixl1 to 255.255.255.255 port 67` |
| 2.3% | `miniupnpd` | `could not find nat rule to delete iport=...` |

Three message shapes account for over 70% of the file.

## Why this is a problem, not just untidy

`internal/logship/syslog/source.go:222-233` captures on `!parsed`, and its comment calls that "exactly the signal we do not model". The intent is right. The definition is too broad: a firewall's syslog is overwhelmingly programs with **no dedicated parser** — parsers exist for audit/sshd/DHCP/HAProxy/Suricata (#249–#257) and everything else falls through. So the capture fires on the majority of all lines rather than on anything novel.

**The real harm is the shared byte cap.** `--logs.debug-capture.max-bytes` governs the whole directory and **stops when reached, keeping the oldest**. So the syslog firehose fills the cap with `arpresolve` and `cron MAIL`, and from that point on nothing else can be written — including:

- the NetFlow lane's `--flow.netflow.debug-capture=unidentified`, which is bounded by design (a couple of datagrams at startup and nothing after), and
- the Zenarmor lane's `unknown_family` / `unhandled_endpoint` / `parse_error`, which produced **zero** entries over the same period.

The two captures that are genuinely "we do not model this" get starved by the one that is not. At ~31 MB/day the 256MiB default is exhausted in roughly eight days, silently, and the failure looks exactly like "nothing unrecognised has arrived".

## Proposed fix

Dedupe the syslog unparsed capture by **message shape**, not by line. First occurrence of a shape always writes; repeats stay quiet for a window.

The pattern already exists in this repo and is proven: `noticeLimiter` in `internal/flow/netflow/capture.go` — 15-minute interval, bounded key count, everything past the bound folds to one shared key so memory stays flat and the log still says something is happening. Reuse that shape rather than inventing a second one.

Shape key wants to be `(program, normalised message)` where normalisation collapses the variable parts — the `arpresolve` lines differ only by a trailing IP and a bracketed counter, and the `cron MAIL` lines only by a byte count. Digits-to-placeholder is probably enough; it does not need to be clever, it needs to stop 11,485 identical facts becoming 11,485 entries.

Two things to preserve:

- **Never drop an uncounted line.** The existing capture is deliberately written *before* any sample drop. A deduped capture must still count what it suppressed, so a metric shows the real rate even when the file shows one example.
- **First occurrence always writes.** The point is to see a novel line the moment it appears.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Repeated syslog `unparsed` shapes are captured once per window, not once per line
- [ ] The suppressed count is observable (metric), so the file being small is not mistaken for the lane being quiet
- [ ] A first-occurrence shape is always written
- [ ] Key count is bounded, with a fold, so an attacker-controlled or runaway program cannot grow the map without limit
- [ ] Re-run against the reference box: the 70% held by three shapes collapses to a handful of entries
- [ ] Zenarmor and NetFlow captures are unaffected — they are already bounded and must not be regressed into the same window logic without cause

## Note on the immediate state

The 31 MB was deleted from the reference box (the captures existed for #331, which is closed). Zenarmor and NetFlow-unidentified capture stay on because both are bounded; syslog capture stays off there until this lands, so it cannot starve them.

```
  -> "<#>[#] arpresolve: can't allocate llinfo for #.#.#.#"
"(nobody) MAIL (mailed 37 bytes of output but got status 0x00000000)"
  -> "(nobody) MAIL (mailed # bytes of output but got status #)"
"dnsbl_module: updating blocklist."   -> unchanged
```

Keys are bounded at 256 and fold past that, because a shape is derived from input nobody controls. Suppression happens on the caller's goroutine **before** the channel, so the count stays exact even when the writer is behind or already stopped at the cap.

`CaptureShape` is a second path rather than a change to `Capture`. The NetFlow and Zenarmor lanes must not be windowed — both are bounded by design and a window would cost them samples they need to be complete — and a regression test pins that so nobody routes them through it later.

Mutation-checked: forcing `ShapeLimiter.Allow` to always return true fails five tests, including the end-to-end syslog one (`records = 51, want 2`) and the concurrency test (`a single shape was allowed 800 times across 8 goroutines, want 1`).

### The invariant that mattered most

Dedupe affects the debug **capture** only, never what ships. Three identical unparseable lines still produce three emitted records and one capture entry, and there is a test holding that line. The existing "capture before any sample drop" ordering is also preserved.

### Docs

`docs/log-shipping.md` hand-enumerated the drop reasons in prose **outside** the docgen markers, so `make docs-check` passed with the list already incomplete. Added `duplicate_shape` and a short section explaining why this one lane is deduplicated and the other two deliberately are not. Worth noting the trap recurring: generated-doc checks do not cover prose, so any hand-written enumeration of a code-defined set goes stale silently.

### Gate

```
go test ./...                        all packages ok
go test -race ./internal/logship/... ok
golangci-lint run ./...              0 issues
make docs-check                      check passed
make grafana-check                   validated 46 manifests
```

### Left open on the reference box

The acceptance item "re-run against the reference box and watch the three shapes collapse" needs the new image to deploy. The 31 MB was already deleted; syslog and Zenarmor capture stay enabled there, which is now safe because this is what makes the syslog lane bounded.

title: logship: the syslog unparsed debug capture is a firehose, and it starves the bounded captures sharing its byte cap

body:
Found while enabling the NetFlow receiver on the reference box for the #360 capture window. The receiver had never been enabled there — `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_ENABLE_NETFLOW` was set, but that is the *collector* (netflow plugin status via the API), not the receiver, so nothing had ever listened on 2055 while ng_netflow exported to it. Everything in #346/#357 was validated against the replay fixture, never against live traffic.

Two separate problems. The second is confirmed in code; the first is measured but not yet explained.

## 1. The two lanes disagree about which interface the traffic is on

Both lanes running, same process, counters started together at container start. Totals agree to within 0.2%, attribution does not agree at all.

| source | top interface | share | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| `netflow` | `tailscale` | 93.3% | 38,611 MB |
| `zenarmor` | `LAN` | 91.5% | 38,671 MB |

Full breakdown at the same instant:

```
--- source=netflow  total=38611.3 MB
    tailscale               36008.25 MB   93.3%
    LAN                      2057.14 MB    5.3%
    (empty)                   339.64 MB    0.9%
    zenoverlay                101.89 MB    0.3%
    Loopback                   90.84 MB    0.2%
    VIRGIN                      5.78 MB    0.0%
    locally-originated          4.54 MB    0.0%
    IOT                         1.78 MB    0.0%

--- source=zenarmor  total=38670.9 MB
    LAN                     35403.07 MB   91.5%
    ixl0                     1872.36 MB    4.8%
    IOT                      1365.92 MB    3.5%
    MGMT                       28.95 MB    0.1%
    CAM                         0.54 MB    0.0%
    ixl0_vlan50                 0.02 MB    0.0%
    ixl0_vlan100                0.01 MB    0.0%
```

The near-identical totals are the point: both lanes are measuring the same traffic, so this is an attribution fault rather than two sources seeing different things.

`docs/flow.md` documents a *deliberate* difference — the NetFlow lane's `interface` names the WAN-facing side (egress for outbound, ingress for inbound, `internal/flow/processor.go:346-357`) while Zenarmor keeps naming the VLAN child. That explains LAN traffic being attributed to a WAN. It does not explain `tailscale`, which is not a WAN, taking 93% of the volume.

Supporting state at the same instant:

```
opnsense_flow_ifindex_entries      16
opnsense_flow_ifindex_conflicts     0
opnsense_flow_ifindex_unmapped_total 0
opnsense_flow_netflow_datagrams_total{result="peer_rejected"} 0
```

`conflicts` is 0 only because no `--flow.netflow.ifindex-map` pins are set, so it proves nothing here.

### Candidate causes, none yet verified

- **Positional ifIndex mismatch.** ng_netflow's ifIndex is a 1-based counter over `ifinfo` output, and the map is derived from the API rather than from `ifinfo` itself — the hazard `docs/flow.md` already calls out and that `--flow.netflow.ifindex-map` exists to override. A systematic offset would relabel everything consistently, which fits the shape of what is observed. Decisive test is reading the real mapping off the firewall with `ngctl list | grep netflow.` and diffing it against `BuildIfMap`'s output.
- **A genuine tailscale-heavy workload.** Has to be ruled out rather than assumed, but it does not fit: Zenarmor sees the same byte total and puts it on LAN.
- **The WAN-facing-side rule selecting the wrong side** when both ends resolve, independently of whether the indices are right.

### Why the empty 0.9% is its own puzzle

`interfaceLabel` (`internal/flow/processor.go:346-357`) returns `""` only when *both* `In.Label()` and `Out.Label()` are empty. `Iface.Label()` (`internal/flow/record.go:129-134`) is empty only when both `Name` and `Device` are empty, which is the zero `Iface` — and `IfMap.Iface` (`internal/flow/ifmap.go:216-226`) returns the zero value only on a miss, which it counts. So 339 MB on an empty label with `ifindex_unmapped_total` at 0 should not be reachable.

Two ways out, and problem 2 below makes the first likely:

- the counter is resetting and hiding the misses;
- an entry in `byIndex` was built with an empty `Device` *and* an empty `Name`, which yields an empty label through the mapped path without ever counting as unmapped. `BuildIfMap` (`internal/flow/ifmap.go:101`) does not reject such an entry.

## 2. `ifindex_unmapped_total` is a counter that resets every 60 seconds

Confirmed by reading the code, not inferred from the metric.

`unmapped` is an `atomic.Uint64` field on `IfMap` (`internal/flow/ifmap.go:70`). `BuildIfMap` returns a brand-new `*IfMap` (`internal/flow/ifmap.go:101-107`), so the counter starts at zero on every build. `main.go` replaces the map wholesale every `ifIndexRefreshInterval` = 60s (`main.go:85`, `proc.SetIfMap(flow.BuildIfMap(...))`).

So `opnsense_flow_netflow_ifindex_unmapped_total` can only ever report unmapped lookups since the last rebuild. It is a Prometheus `_total` that goes backwards once a minute, which breaks `rate()` and `increase()` on it as well as making the raw value meaningless.

It is worse than one-minute granularity in practice. Sampled every 10s for 110s on the live box:

```
14:38:40 entries 16 map_age_seconds 3.186148303 unmapped_total 0
14:38:50 entries 16 map_age_seconds 3.186148303 unmapped_total 0
...
14:40:21 entries 16 map_age_seconds 3.185323329 unmapped_total 0
```

`map_age_seconds` sits at a near-constant ~3.19s because the flow collector's poll and the map rebuild are both on 60s tickers started at roughly the same instant. The snapshot therefore samples the map about 3 seconds after every rebuild, so the metric reflects roughly 3 seconds of lookups out of every 60 and is structurally close to blind.

This matters beyond the metric being wrong. `docs/flow.md` sells this counter as the alarm for the positional-renumbering hazard — "a rising rate after a network change means the enumeration shifted" — and as written it cannot rise.

### Fix direction

Move the counter off the map instance so it survives a rebuild. `Processor` already outlives the map and is the natural owner; `IfMap.Iface` would report the miss to it rather than counting internally. `IfMapStats.UnmappedLookups` should then come from the owner, not from the map.

Whatever shape it takes, a regression test must rebuild the map and assert the counter did not go backwards — that is the property that was missing.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `ifindex_unmapped_total` is monotonic across an ifIndex map rebuild, with a test that rebuilds and asserts it
- [ ] The real ng_netflow enumeration is read off the box (`ngctl list | grep netflow.`) and diffed against `BuildIfMap`'s derived map, and the result is recorded here either way
- [ ] The `tailscale` vs `LAN` disagreement is explained, and either fixed or documented as correct with the reasoning
- [ ] An `IfMap` entry that would produce an empty label is either impossible by construction or counted, so an empty `interface` always has a matching counter
- [ ] `docs/flow.md` updated if any documented behaviour turns out to be wrong

## Evidence to hand

The #360 capture is running on the reference box now (`--flow.netflow.debug-capture=all`, 50GiB cap, `/opt/opnsense-exporter/capture/netflow/`). It carries the raw ifIndex values as exported, so it settles the enumeration question offline without needing the live box again.

Refs #346, #357, #360.
