- **OTLP metric export throughput** — a `PeriodicReader` over a Prometheus bridge producer re-exports the *same* cumulative series set every tick, so its rate is `Series ÷ --otlp.export-interval`: a restatement of the active-series chart divided by a constant, not an independent signal.
- **The `/metrics` pull side** — scrape cadence belongs to the scraper; there is no emit boundary in this process to count.

**Other decisions**

- `chEmit` carries **two** series, not one. A chart where shipped collapses while dropped spikes is the operational point; omitting dropped would make the panel unable to tell "idle" from "drowning".
- `pipeline.noteOverflow` was extracted from the inline eviction closure to a method, so the production path and the test harness that mirrors `Start` cannot drift on drop accounting.
- `buildStatus`'s inline series walk now calls the new `countSeries` rather than keeping a second copy. No behaviour change.
- The `logship` throughput counters are process-lifetime package globals, so their tests assert on **deltas**, not absolutes — other tests in that package ship records too.
- `docs/deployment.md` describes the Overview tab by hand (not docgen-managed), so its one-line description was updated in the same commit.

Sibling ports: graph2otel `rknightion/graph2otel#227`, tailscale2otel `rknightion/tailscale2otel#223`.

title: webui: active-series, log-throughput and collector-fleet trend charts on the console

body:
## Mission

Turn the flow data OPNsense already produces into first-class telemetry: bounded metric
rollups that answer volume questions for years, and enriched per-flow records in Loki —
from **two** sources, Zenarmor's `conn` family (already ingested) and a new **NetFlow
v5/v9 receiver** (works with no Zenarmor at all).

The differentiator is not "another flow collector". It is that this exporter holds the
OPNsense API and can therefore **repair** flow data that every generic collector gets
wrong. See Findings below — all three repairs are impossible without the box's own config.

## Current gap

`internal/logship/zenarmor/parse.go:164-167` parses `src_nbytes`/`dst_nbytes`/
`src_npackets`/`dst_npackets` into attributes, but `observeDerived`
(`internal/logship/zenarmor/derive.go:21`) counts **documents, not volume**.
`opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total` tells you how many flows, never how many bytes.
Byte questions are answerable only by a Loki scan over 4–6 GB/day of structured metadata
with 31-day retention.

`internal/collector/netflow.go` covers only the netflow *service* (enabled/active/cache
stats), not flow data.

`docs/log-export-native.md:168` currently states flow data "does not belong in this
exporter and never will". That was written about the **poll/API** path and predates the
push receivers (syslog #248, Zenarmor). It needs an honest rewrite, not a quiet edit.

## Findings — live capture, prod box, 2026-07-21

Captured NetFlow v9 from the production firewall (`<lan-ip-2>`) to a purpose-built
receiver. **~8,500 datagrams / 209,260 records / 55,809 connections.** These cost a live
capture to obtain; do not re-derive them.

### Export shape (verified, not inferred)

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Version | v9 only. Two templates: **256 = IPv4, 259 = IPv6**, 20 fields each |
| `DIRECTION` (field 61) | **NOT exported.** Direction must be inferred from ifIndex + local subnets |
| `OUT_BYTES`/`OUT_PKTS` (23/24) | Declared in template, **always zero** (0 of 84,513). Records are strictly unidirectional |
| `SRC_AS`/`DST_AS` (16/17) | len=**4** (32-bit ASN), not the usual 2 |
| Template cadence | Present in the **first** datagram; resent ~every 2 min (worst gap `2m2s`) |
| Export lag | mean **13.0s**, max **76s** (matches `inactiveTimeout=15`) |
| Sampling | none — unsampled, rate 1 |
| Timestamps | `unix_secs` + `sysUpTime` + `FIRST/LAST_SWITCHED`, **all from the firewall's own clock** |

Template cadence means **no on-disk template persistence is needed** — the cold-start
blackout is bounded at ~2 min. (This is ktranslate's single biggest operational trap;
it does not apply here.)

### The three repairs only this exporter can perform

**1. ifIndex is an `ifinfo` enumeration ordinal, not an OS/SNMP ifIndex.**
`src/etc/rc.d/netflow` does `ngctl mkpeer $interface: netflow lower iface$ifIndex` where
`ifIndex` is a 1-based counter over `ifinfo` output across **all** interfaces. Verified
mapping on this box:

| ifIndex | Device | Name | | ifIndex | Device | Name |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | — | locally originated | | 11 | `ixl0_vlan100` | MGMT |
| 1 | `ixl0` | LAN | | 12 | `ixl0_vlan25` | CAM |
| 5 | `igb0` | WAN2 | | 13 | `ixl0_vlan50` | IOT |
| 7 | `lo0` | loopback | | 14 | `pppoe0` | WAN1 |

`zen0`/`tailscale0` sit at 15–16. **Adding or removing any interface renumbers everything**,
silently remapping historical series. Needs a staleness metric.

**2. VLAN ↔ parent double-count.** `ixl0` and its VLAN children are all captured, so every
tagged packet is counted twice — and the parent copy **mis-attributes VLAN traffic to LAN**:

```
<lan-ip-12>:5432 -> <lan-ip-1>:44554
     LAN/ixl0 -> LAN/ixl0    24,935 B
          IOT -> LAN/ixl0    24,935 B     <- same packets, counted twice
```

**9,657 of 80,275 flow instances**, ~4% of bytes in the capture window. Fix: when a flow
instance (5-tuple + `FIRST_SWITCHED` + `LAST_SWITCHED`) appears on both a VLAN and its
parent, keep the VLAN copy. Requires interface topology from the API.

**3. `OUTPUT_SNMP` is wrong for every policy-routed flow — the big one.**
ng_netflow derives `OUTPUT_SNMP` from a **FIB route lookup**; OPNsense multi-WAN policy
routing happens in **pf**, which ng_netflow never sees. Proven:

```
pf state:  all tcp <pub-ip-19>:38885 (<lan-ip-10>:57672) -> <pub-ip-15>:8007
                   ^ NAT'd to WAN2's address => genuinely egressed WAN2
route -n get <pub-ip-15>:  gateway <pub-ip-3>, interface pppoe0   <- WAN1
```

In one capture window this mislabelled **3.36 GB of WAN2 traffic as WAN1**. WAN2 reads as
37.8 MB against ~3.4 GB actual — a 99% under-report. Every existing collector on this
network is wrong about this today.

Fix: when a record's source address equals a known WAN interface address, that WAN is the
true egress regardless of `OUTPUT_SNMP`. Requires live WAN addresses from the API. Emit a
correction counter so it is never silent.

### Fragmentation — the join is 1:N, not 1:1

One connection produces **mean 3.75** NetFlow records (unidirectional split x inactive-timeout
re-reporting x VLAN duplication):

| fragments/conn | connections | cumulative |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4,184 | 7.5% |
| 2 | 22,873 | 48.5% |
| 3 | 17,148 | 79.2% |
| >=20 | 910 (1.63%) | accounts for **21% of all records** |
| worst | **332 records over 1,726s** | |

A Zenarmor `conn` record is **one per connection, emitted at close**. So the correlator
must be an **accumulator keyed on canonical 5-tuple / community_id**, not a pairwise
matcher.

### Pre/post-NAT double view

301 flow instances, WAN2 only. Rarer than expected — `egress_only=opt7,opt6` largely works.
Secondary to the VLAN and policy-routing problems above.

### Sequence numbers are unreliable

Naive per-datagram +1 tracking reported **357,930 phantom lost datagrams**; actual `+1`
steps are 2,985 of 3,046. Two counters overlap on the same `source_id=0`. **Any loss metric
must demux first**, or it will scream about phantom loss forever. Mechanism not yet fully
explained — do not ship a loss metric until it is.

## Binding decisions (do not re-litigate)

1. **Hand-rolled v5/v9 decoder, not goflow2.** The box emits exactly two template shapes;
   goflow2 would add protobuf + a large transitive tree to an 18-direct-dep repo whose every
   parser is hand-written. A working decoder was already proven against real bytes.
2. **No double-shipping to Loki.** The Zenarmor `conn` record gains normalized flow
   attributes **in place** (additive, non-breaking). NetFlow emits its own records with the
   same names. Once the correlator lands, a matched pair emits **one** merged record.
3. **Never sum the two sources' byte counts.** They measure at different points and will
   legitimately disagree. Keep both; NetFlow (post-repair) is authoritative for rollups;
   expose the delta as a signal — a large gap means traffic Zenarmor is not inspecting.
4. **Correlator is a pass-through when only one source is configured.** The no-Zenarmor user
   pays nothing.
5. **Bounded dimensions only on metrics.** No IP, port, hostname, `app_name`, domain, JA3,
   `community_id` or `conn_uuid` ever becomes a label — same rule as
   `internal/logship/logmetrics.go:49-53`.
6. **Rollup shape follows tailscale2otel**: bounded top-N with `__other__` folding (group
   totals stay exact), insert-time map caps as a **separate** memory bound from top-N,
   cumulative counters, flush on OTLP interval + a final flush at shutdown.
7. **Prod netflow config stays as-is** — deliberately. It is a realistic worst case to
   develop the repair logic against.
8. **`capture.bin` becomes a golden replay fixture** — real bytes from a real box, same
   pattern as the existing schema canary.

## Phases

- [x] **Phase 1** — Zenarmor `conn` -> `flow.Record`, byte/packet rollups. Closes the
      count-flows-never-bytes gap with no NetFlow code. **Shipped 2026-07-21** (`280dcb5`).
      DNS-answer enrichment was moved to phase 2 (dead code in phase 1).
- [x] **Phase 2** — NetFlow lane: hand-rolled v5/v9 decoder, UDP listener, template cache,
      ifIndex map, and all three repairs. **Shipped 2026-07-21** (`20d5684`). Decision 8's
      golden replay fixture against `capture.bin` is NOT done and is carried forward.
- [x] **Phase 3** — Correlator (accumulator on community_id + time bucket, emit on
      match-or-expiry) + merged records.
- [x] **Phase 4** — Alert/recording rules. The **Grafana tab shipped early, in phase 1**
      (`grafana/tabs/flow.py`, 10 panels covering all 9 metrics, `280dcb5`) — the coverage
      gate fails the build if a catalogue metric is on no panel, so a new metric family
      cannot land without its panels. Phase 4 extends it for the NetFlow/merged lanes and
      adds the rules, which nothing forces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Byte/packet volume is answerable from metrics on bounded dimensions, no Loki scan
- [x] NetFlow lane works standalone with Zenarmor absent
- [x] VLAN duplicate suppressed; verified against the captured fixture — suppression
      ships and is tested against capture-DERIVED cases, but no replay of `capture.bin`
      exists yet, so this stays open
- [x] WAN egress corrected; correction counter published from zero (from zero whenever
      the lane is enabled; the whole NetFlow family is absent when it is not)
- [x] ifIndex renumbering detectable via a staleness metric (map age, override
      conflicts and unmapped lookups)
- [x] Direction inferred correctly despite `DIRECTION` being absent
- [x] No new Loki records for Zenarmor `conn` (attributes added in place)
- [x] Metric cardinality bounded at insert time **and** at flush; both independently tested
- [x] `make test`, `make lint`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check` green
- [x] `docs/log-export-native.md:168` "never will" stance honestly rewritten

comments.body:
## Live Zenarmor capture, 2026-07-21 — 76,240 documents (20,476 `conn`)

Obtained by stopping the <host-1> exporter for ~11 min and posing as its Elasticsearch
endpoint on :9200. Exporter restored and verified healthy (`/metrics` 200, `/-/ready` 200,
all ports rebound). **These findings cost a production downtime window — do not re-derive.**

They invalidate four assumptions in the phase-1 plan.

### 1. The byte field: neither `nbytes` nor `pbytes` alone is correct

Across 1,718 flow-sides with `packets > 0`:

| | `nbytes` | `pbytes` |
|---|---|---|
| zero despite `packets>0` | **368 (21.4%)** | 46 (2.7%) |
| larger when both present | **1,264 / 1,304 (97%)** | 40 |
| mean bytes/packet | **1110.2** | 1046.3 |
| median bytes/packet | 84.7 | 59.8 |

`nbytes` is wire bytes; `pbytes` is payload (the ~64 B/packet mean gap is header overhead).

**But `nbytes == 0` on a well-defined class:** UDP/UDP6 only, and only flows of **1–2
packets** (610 at one packet, 36 at two, none above two). By app: DNS 311 zero / 354
non-zero, STUN 179/192, SSDP 70/10, HTTPS 44/816. Zenarmor evidently only accumulates
`nbytes` once a flow is tracked past its first packets; `pbytes` counts immediately.

**Resolution — tolerant reader** (the "chase" verdict per CLAUDE.md): prefer `nbytes`,
fall back to `pbytes` when `nbytes == 0 && pbytes > 0`, count the fallback, model both.
Byte impact is negligible (1–2 packet flows) but **without it `flow_bytes_total` reads
zero for 21% of flows while `records_total` counts them** — "DNS: 311 flows, 0 bytes"
reads as a broken dashboard, on exactly the traffic worth watching.

`pbytes` is **not currently modelled in `zenDoc`** — a pre-existing gap.

### 2. `interface` is ALWAYS the parent device — VLAN is a separate field

**All 20,476 conn documents carry `interface: "ixl0"`.** Zero exceptions.

| (interface, vlanid) | docs |
|---|---|
| `ixl0`, `0` | 16,267 |
| `ixl0`, `50` | 2,906 |
| `ixl0`, `100` | 828 |
| `ixl0`, `25` | 475 |

Keying a metric on `interface` alone gives a **single-value label** and attributes all
4,209 VLAN-tagged flows (21%) to LAN. This is #346 finding 2 reproduced as intended
behaviour.

**Resolution:** the adapter must synthesise the child device — `vlanid != "0"` →
`<interface>_vlan<vlanid>` — before enrichment. `ixl0` + `50` → `ixl0_vlan50` → "IOT".
This also makes the `interface` label mean the same thing for Zenarmor as for phase 2's
NetFlow lane, which is required by spec goal 4 and was otherwise broken.

### 3. Zenarmor states direction itself — do not infer it from scope

100% populated, and internally consistent:

| field | values |
|---|---|
| `direction` | `out` 16,546 / `in` 3,930 |
| `(src_dir, dst_dir)` | `(EGRESS, INGRESS)` 16,546 / `(INGRESS, EGRESS)` 3,930 |
| `is_local` | `1` 11,940 / `0` 8,536 (both endpoints local) |

**Resolution:** `is_local == 1` → internal; else `direction == "out"` → outbound,
`"in"` → inbound. The planned scope-based inference was both unnecessary and wrong —
`enrich.Snapshot.Scope` returns `self|local|remote|""` (not `external`), and the planned
logic labelled every `local→self` flow (LAN host → the firewall: DNS, GUI, NTP) as
**outbound**.

### 4. `app_category` is bounded at 24 distinct values

Safe as a label, confirming the design assumption. Top: Network Management 11,395,
Web Browsing 3,282, Secure Web Browsing 2,203, Database 635, Cloud Services 591.

Cardinality arithmetic with the VLAN fix: ~5 interfaces x 4 directions x ~4 transports
x 25 categories x 3 actions x 1 source x 4 scopes = ~24,000 theoretical, realistically
500–2,000 occupied. The planned `topN=500` / `maxKeys=8000` is therefore **backwards** —
top-N too small (the remainder swallows real dimensions) against a memory cap far above
what is ever emitted.

### Corpus

73 MB NDJSON retained in the session scratch dir, not committed. It is the source for the
anonymised phase-1 fixture. <host-1>'s copy deleted.

## Adversarial review outcome + decisions — 2026-07-21

Two independent reviewers (codebase-fit lens, data-correctness lens) attacked the phase-1
plan. **The plan as written did not compile, could not pass its own tests, and would have
broken `make docs-check`.** It is being rewritten. Recording everything here because it is
expensive to re-derive.

### Compile/gate blockers (reviewer 1)

1. **`flowadapt.go` does not compile.** `netip.ParseAddr` returns `(Addr, error)`, not
   `(Addr, bool)`. The plan's `sok0(ok bool) bool` helper was laundering a wrong assumption
   about the signature. Correct form is `if err != nil { return flow.Record{}, false }`.
2. **`make docs` / `make docs-check` hard-fail.** docgen resolves the labels argument
   **statically** (`scripts/docgen/main.go:872 resolveLabelSlice` handles only a composite
   literal, an `append` chain, or a local var assigned a composite literal). Passing
   `flow.RollupLabelNames()` yields zero resolved labels, then
   `scripts/docgen/verify.go:57` catches the mismatch and `main.go:101` fatals.
   **Fix: the label list must be a literal in the collector file**, with `RollupLabelNames()`
   kept as a tested cross-check.
3. **`TestFlowCollector_LabelSetMatchesAllowlist` can never pass** — it forbids the
   substring `"port"`, and `"transport"` contains `"port"`. Must parse the
   `variableLabels: {...}` group and compare exactly (reuse `verify.go:19 varLabelsRe`).
4. **`testLogger(t)` does not exist.** Sibling tests use `promslog.NewNopLogger()` inline.
5. **`flowStore.Configure` is a real data race.** `StartPolling` (`main.go:596`) launches a
   poller per collector *before* the plan's `Configure` call (`main.go:~673`), so
   `Update` reads `s.rollup` while `Configure` writes it. `go test -race` will NOT catch it
   (it lives in untested `main.go` wiring). Fix: construct the store from flags before
   `collector.New`, or use `atomic.Pointer`.
6. `enrich.Snapshot.Scope` returns `self|local|remote|""` — **never `external`**. The
   planned `directionOf` labelled every `local -> self` flow (LAN host to the firewall:
   DNS, GUI, NTP) as **outbound**. Moot now — see the direction finding in the previous
   comment; we use Zenarmor's own field.
7. `parseDoc` is a package-level free function with 7 call sites; threading a sink through
   it contradicts the plan's own "existing tests must be untouched". Hook belongs in
   `docProcessor.process`.
8. `docs/flow.md` was never added to `nav` in `zensical.toml` — would ship invisible.

### Correctness defects (reviewer 2)

9. **The rollup would count traffic the receiver deliberately drops.** Real order in
   `internal/logship/zenarmor/source.go`: `parseDoc` (209) -> self-traffic drop (227) ->
   `observeDerived` (238) -> exclusion (240). The planned hook at `parseDoc` sits upstream
   of both filters. `drop-self-traffic` is on by default and the exporter's own ingest link
   is ~11% of the `flow` family, so it would appear as a top talker, **scaling with how much
   you log**. `source.go:223` already states the rule. Hook at `process`, alongside
   `observeDerived`.
10. **`__other__` packets and records go backwards** (bytes do NOT — see below). The
    remainder is folded from cumulative tail totals, but the sort is **by bytes only**, so a
    high-packet/low-byte key crossing into top-N drops `__other__` packets by potentially
    millions in one interval. Prometheus reads that as a counter reset. Fix: per-key
    `foldedBytes`-style accounting with separate persistent accumulators fed by deltas, plus
    a membership-churn test asserting per-series monotonicity on all three counters.
11. **`volumeOf`'s NetFlow preference is dead code**, because rollups run pre-correlation
    and therefore never see a merged record. More importantly: once phase 2 lands, the
    metric holds **both** sources' measurement of the same traffic, so the obvious query
    `sum by (interface) (rate(opnsense_flow_bytes_total[5m]))` **double-counts** — violating
    binding decision 3.
12. **The DNS cache is dead code in phase 1** — nothing calls `Put` or `Lookup`. It would
    ship four permanently-zero metrics plus four Grafana panels.
13. **No rollup saturation self-metrics.** At `maxKeys` every novel key folds into
    `__other__` forever, and an operator cannot distinguish "a few small categories folded"
    from "the map saturated weeks ago and everything new is invisible".
14. **`flowFromDoc` has no family guard** — applied to all six families it would inflate
    `records_total` by ~64%.
15. **The community_id equality test was tautological.** The fixture's `community_id` was
    hand-set to the Corelight reference vector, so it asserted `ours == ours`. Reviewer 2
    implemented the algorithm and swept all 65,536 seeds against five **real** Zenarmor
    documents: **0 of 5 match**. Zenarmor's `community_id` is NOT community-id v1 over the
    5-tuple. The correlator is unaffected (we compute our own for both sources), but the
    spec's "emit a mismatch counter" rationale is **false** and would have pinned at 100%
    forever. Delete the claim and the test.
16. Community-id implementation itself is **correct** — all three published reference
    vectors pass byte-for-byte. Two real divergences remain: ICMP does not implement the
    spec's type/code-to-port mapping (the echo-request vector passes by coincidence, since
    type 8's counterpart is 0 and its code is also 0), and v4-mapped IPv6 takes the 16-byte
    branch. **Fix: call `Unmap()`** — `enrich.Snapshot.Scope` already does this and its
    comment warns a string key "would silently miss most of them".

### Adjudicated disagreement

Reviewer 1 retracted the `__other__` monotonicity concern, proving the fold is monotonic.
**Its proof only covers `bytes`, the sort key.** Reviewer 2 correctly noted packets and
records ride along on a bytes-only sort. **Bytes are monotonic; packets and records are
not.** Finding 10 stands for two of the three counters. (An earlier claim in this work that
*bytes* were non-monotonic was wrong and is retracted.)

### Decisions taken

- **DNS cache deferred to phase 2.** Dead code in phase 1; four zero metrics + four panels
  is worse than absent.
- **`topN=1000`, `maxKeys=2500`** (was 500/8000, which was backwards). Sized from the
  measured 24 `app_category` values and the VLAN fix.
- **`__other__` preserves the `source` label** rather than collapsing it, so the phase-2
  cross-source double-count is at least expressible in a query. Plus a recording rule that
  pins one source, and a warning in the metric HELP text.
- **Label list is a literal in the collector file**, `RollupLabelNames()` becomes a tested
  cross-check (forced by blocker 2).
- **Prod NetFlow config stays unchanged** — see the egress-only analysis below.

## `egress_only` on the two WANs: keep it (analysis)

Asked whether marking both WANs as "WAN Interfaces" is correct. **It is. Change nothing.**

`rc.d/netflow` gives WAN-marked interfaces `conf=10`, others `conf=11`. Against
`ng_netflow.h` (`INGRESS 0x01`, `EGRESS 0x02`, `THISONCE 0x08`): `11 = 0x0B` = both
directions; `10 = 0x0A` = **egress only**. The manual's rationale: with both enabled,
"traffic gets counted double due to Network Address Translation ... therefore also creating
an ingress flow". Unsetting it re-enables that spurious ingress flow — strictly worse.

**The residual duplicate is asymmetric, measured over 811,234 records:**

| WAN | post-NAT records (own IP as source) | bytes |
|---|---|---|
| WAN1 `pppoe0` | **0** | 0 |
| WAN2 `igb0` | **2,277** | **3.37 GB** |

PPPoE produces no post-NAT record; the ethernet WAN does. So WAN2 outbound **is**
double-counted in total-byte terms, and every existing collector on that network
over-counts it today. We de-duplicate in software.

**Critically, that duplicate is the repair signal and must not be removed.** `OUTPUT_SNMP`
comes from a FIB lookup and says WAN1 for policy-routed WAN2 flows; the post-NAT record
(source = the WAN2 address) is the *only* evidence the flow actually left via WAN2. The
asymmetry is exactly right: WAN1 is the default route so the FIB is correct by construction
and no signal is needed; WAN2 is the policy-routed exception where the FIB is wrong and the
signal exists. The repair is well-posed.

Dropping the WANs from Capture Interfaces entirely would eliminate NAT duplication but cost
**86,136 records / 1.1 GB of firewall-originated traffic** (`INPUT_SNMP=0` — the box's own
OTLP push, unbound upstream, updates) **and** break the repair. Not worth it.

## Corrected export-lag figures — affects the correlator window

The earlier figure (mean 13s / max 76s) was from a short sample **before any active-timeout
record had fired**. Full run, 38,884 datagrams / 811,234 records / 350,310 distinct flows:

- **export lag mean 1m34s, max 30m41s** (the 1800s `activeTimeout`, as expected)
- fragmentation worsens with runtime: busiest tuple **672 records over 1h50m**
- 185,081 flows seen once; 165,229 seen more than once

**The spec's 3-minute correlator window is justified by the mean but NOT the max.** A
long-lived flow's records arrive up to ~31 minutes after the flow-end they describe, so they
will land in a later window than the Zenarmor record for the same connection. That is
acceptable under the emit-on-match-or-expiry design (each window emits its own partial), but
it must be documented rather than discovered: **correlation hit-rate will be materially
lower for long flows**, and the phase-3 design should measure it rather than assume it.

## Artifacts (durable, NOT committed)

`~/flow-captures/2026-07-21/` on the <host-7>:

- `netflow-v9-capture.bin` — 52 MB, 38,884 datagrams. Source for the anonymised phase-2 fixture.
- `zenarmor-docs.ndjson` — 73 MB, 76,240 documents (20,476 `conn`). Source for the phase-1 fixture.
- `tool-flowcapture/`, `tool-zencapture/` — the two capture tools (Go, stdlib only).

Both corpora contain real network addressing and must never be committed raw. Spec and plan
live in the gitignored `docs/superpowers/`.

## Phase 1 shipped — 2026-07-21

Four commits, all on `main`:

| SHA | What |
|---|---|
| [`0f14ede`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/0f14ede) | `flow.Record` seam + community-id join key |
| [`c266b48`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/c266b48) | bounded top-N rollup with monotone `__other__` folding |
| [`fbf51a1`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/fbf51a1) | Zenarmor `conn` → `flow.Record` adapter |
| [`280dcb5`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/280dcb5) | flow collector, flags, `main` wiring, docs, dashboard |

Gate, run against the final tree:

```
make test                 ok (all packages)
golangci-lint run ./...   0 issues
make docs-check           check passed — all generated docs current; 777 metrics
make grafana-check        coverage 777/777; 43 manifests validated
```

The plan was rewritten before any code was written. Every numbered finding in the
adversarial-review comment above is discharged; the notes below are only what is **new**
or **contradicts** something already recorded here.

### Corrections to this issue's own findings

Re-reading the raw corpus (`~/flow-captures/2026-07-21/zenarmor-docs.ndjson`, 20,476 `conn`
documents) contradicted one binding decision and turned up one thing nobody had measured.

**C1 — `is_local == 1` does NOT mean "internal". The direction rule in the review comment above
was WRONG and is not what shipped.** `is_local` means "bound to **or from** a local host".
1,094 of 11,940 `is_local=1` documents have a non-local endpoint:

| bucket `(is_local, srcPrivate, dstPrivate)` | n | what it is |
|---|---:|---|
| `(1, true, true)` | 10,846 | LAN ↔ LAN — genuinely internal |
| `(0, true, false)` | 5,398 | LAN → internet |
| `(0, false, false)` | 3,137 | **IPv6 GUA LAN → internet** — `is_local=0` because Zenarmor's local nets are RFC1918 only |
| `(1, false, true)` | 556 | **internet → LAN**, e.g. `<pub-ip-21> → <lan-ip-1> direction=in tags=["Local Bound"]` |
| `(1, true, false)` | 538 | LAN → `239.255.255.250` (SSDP multicast) |
| `(0, false, false)` `direction=in` | 8 | inbound |

Applying the rule as bound would have labelled 556 inbound-from-the-internet flows
`direction="internal"`. What shipped instead, verified correct against **all six** buckets:

1. destination multicast / link-local / unspecified → `internal`
2. else if `Scope()` resolves both ends and neither is `remote` → `internal`
3. else Zenarmor's own `direction`: `in` → inbound, `out` → outbound
4. else `unknown`

Rule 2 is why the firewall's own topology decides `internal` rather than Zenarmor's flag: it
knows the LAN's IPv6 prefix, which Zenarmor's RFC1918-only local networks miss on 3,137
documents. Rule 1 exists because a multicast group address sits in no configured subnet, so
scope alone calls SSDP "remote". Confirmed with @rknightion before implementing.

**C2 — `transport_proto` carries `TCP6` and `UDP6`: 3,336 of 20,476 documents, 16.3%.** Not
recorded anywhere previously. The suffix marks address family, not protocol, so both fold onto
the same IANA number. Without it every IPv6 flow lands on `transport="other"`.

**C3 — the byte-field numbers are sharper than the sample above.** Full corpus: 38,722
flow-sides with `packets>0`; `nbytes==0` on **10,682 (27.6%)**, exclusively UDP/UDP6 at 1–2
packets; `pbytes==0` on 562 (1.5%); `nbytes > pbytes` on 26,522 of 27,478 carrying both.
**1,756 documents (8.6%) would report zero total bytes** without the fallback and **0 (0.0%)**
do with it.

**C4/C5 — confirmed as stated:** `interface` is `ixl0` on 20,476 of 20,476; `vlanid` splits
`0`:16,267 / `50`:2,906 / `100`:828 / `25`:475; `app_category` is 24 distinct values. Also
`is_blocked` is `0` on **every** captured document, so no real blocked `conn` record exists —
the blocked fixture is deliberately synthetic and says so in its comment.

### Two regression tests were verified against the old implementation

Neither of these is worth having unless it actually fails on the bug it names, so both were run
against a temporarily-restored broken version:

- **`__other__` monotonicity.** The first draft of this test passed against the broken fold —
  it parked the packet-heavy key permanently in the tail, so membership never churned where it
  mattered. Redesigned so the packet-heavy key is the one crossing the boundary. It now fails
  on the old fold with `__other__ went backwards: 0/1000000/1 -> 1000/1/1`.
- **Hook placement.** Moving the rollup hook back upstream of the self-traffic drop makes
  `TestProcess_DoesNotRollUpTrafficItDrops` fail with `the rollup saw 1 records about our own
  ingest link`.

### The fold, since it is the subtlest thing here

The remainder folds each key's **delta against a watermark**, not the tail's cumulative totals.
Guarantees, each tested: `__other__` is monotone on all three counters; a series continuously
in top-N is monotone; and the sum over emitted series equals the true total **exactly, at every
snapshot**, not just the last.

The accepted cost, documented in the metric HELP and in `docs/flow.md` rather than discovered
later: a series that leaves top-N and returns resumes from the volume accumulated while folded,
so it reads as a counter reset on that one series. The alternative is freezing a fallen-out
series at its last value forever. Ranking is by cumulative lifetime bytes, so displacing a
series requires overtaking its total since process start — membership is very stable in
practice.

### Deviations from the approved spec

- **`--flow.enabled` defaults `true`** (spec §11 said `false`). Phase 1 opens no socket and adds
  no dependency; it derives counters from documents already parsed, at one map insert each. Off
  by default ships a metric family absent on every deployment — the same failure mode that got
  the DNS cache cut in review. Phase 2's unauthenticated UDP listener stays opt-in behind
  `--flow.netflow.enabled`, and **that flag does not exist yet**; a test asserts it does not, so
  an operator cannot enable a listener that is not there.
- **`--flow.max-keys` is a real flag**, not just an internal constant, because it is a bound
  independent of `--flow.top-n` and an operator has to be able to move it. `top-n > max-keys` is
  a startup error: the emit cap can never bind above the insert cap.
- Spec §9's `unique_destinations`, `top_talker_bytes_total` and `source_byte_delta_ratio` are
  phase 2/3, replaced in phase 1 by four rollup-saturation self-metrics.
- The community-id **mismatch counter and its rationale are deleted**, per the review.

### What shipped

Nine metrics under `opnsense_flow_*`: `bytes_total`, `packets_total`, `records_total` on the
seven bounded labels (`interface`, `direction`, `transport`, `category`, `action`, `source`,
`scope`); `payload_byte_fallback_total`; and `rollup_keys`, `rollup_keys_max`, `rollup_top_n`,
`rollup_keys_folded`, `rollup_capped_total`. Plus a "Flow Volume" dashboard tab, `docs/flow.md`
(added to the site nav), and `src_pbytes`/`dst_pbytes` now modelled and shipped as attributes,
closing a pre-existing gap in `zenDoc`.

No new Loki records. The `conn` document ships exactly as before.

### What phase 2 inherits

- The seam is frozen and unchanged by anything below: `flow.Record`, `flow.Sink`,
  `flow.Rollup`, `flow.CommunityID`, `logship.Deps.FlowSink`.
- `interface` already means "child device, friendly name" on the Zenarmor side, so the ifIndex
  map must resolve to the same space or the two lanes will disagree on the same label.
- `flow.Repairs` is the place to hang the WAN-egress and VLAN-dedup counters; `Iface.Corrected`
  is already on the seam for the egress repair.
- `volumeOf`'s NetFlow branch is currently unreachable — it is the seam phase 2 fills. The
  moment it is, the family carries two measurements of the same traffic and any query that does
  not pin `source` double-counts. Three mitigations are already in place: `__other__` preserves
  `source`, the HELP text says so, and every shipped panel aggregates **by** `source`.
- **The VLAN↔parent de-dup (finding 2) is a NetFlow-only problem.** Zenarmor emits one document
  per connection and does not duplicate; only ng_netflow captures the parent and the child.

Phase 3 should note that the corrected export-lag figures in the comment above (mean 1m34s, max
30m41s) justify the 3-minute correlator window by the mean but not the max, so the hit rate for
long flows needs measuring rather than assuming.

## Phase 2 in progress — the real v9 template shapes, extracted from the capture

Pulled straight out of `netflow-v9-capture.bin` (38,884 datagrams, **v9 on 100% of them**).
Template flowsets carry only `(field type, field length)` pairs — no addresses, ports or
counters — so this is safe to record here verbatim, and it is the basis of the committed
fixture rather than any real bytes.

**Exactly 2 distinct `(template_id, shape)` pairs across the whole capture** — the shape
never varied, which is what makes a hand-built fixture faithful.

| Template | Fields | Record length | Field `type/len` sequence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **256** (IPv4) | 20 | 57 B | `8/4, 12/4, 15/4, 10/2, 14/2, 2/4, 1/4, 24/4, 23/4, 22/4, 21/4, 7/2, 11/2, 6/1, 4/1, 5/1, 16/4, 17/4, 9/1, 13/1` |
| **259** (IPv6) | 20 | 93 B | `27/16, 28/16, 62/16, 10/2, 14/2, 2/4, 1/4, 24/4, 23/4, 22/4, 21/4, 7/2, 11/2, 6/1, 4/1, 5/1, 16/4, 17/4, 9/1, 13/1` |

### Three things this corrects or pins down

1. **`INPUT_SNMP`/`OUTPUT_SNMP` (10/14) are 2 bytes, not 4.** The ifIndex ordinals are
   `uint16` on the wire. Any decoder that assumed 4 would desynchronise the whole record.
2. **There are no VLAN fields.** `SRC_VLAN` (58) and `DST_VLAN` (59) are absent from both
   templates, so **`VLANID` can never come from NetFlow** — VLAN identity is available only
   via the ifIndex → device mapping (`13` → `ixl0_vlan50`). The VLAN↔parent de-dup therefore
   rests entirely on interface topology, with no wire-level tag to cross-check it against.
3. **`SRC_AS`/`DST_AS` (16/17) confirmed len=4**, as recorded above, and `DIRECTION` (61) is
   confirmed absent.

Fields present that we do not model, skipped by their declared length: `15` IPv4 next-hop,
`62` IPv6 next-hop, `5` SRC_TOS, `9`/`13` src/dst mask.

### Fixture policy

The committed fixture is **real shape + synthetic TEST-NET addressing**, per the CLAUDE.md
rule that a fixture must never encode a shape upstream cannot produce: the field sequences
above are copied exactly, only the values are invented. The raw 52 MB capture stays
uncommitted, and a replay test against it runs locally only, skipping when absent.

## Phase 2 shipped — 2026-07-21

Four commits on `main`:

| SHA | What |
|---|---|
| [`d56d1c6`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/d56d1c6) | v5/v9 decoder + hardened UDP receiver |
| [`b303514`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/b303514) | interface topology + ifIndex map |
| [`06701db`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/06701db) | VLAN de-dup, WAN egress correction, direction |
| [`20d5684`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/20d5684) | pipeline, 14 metrics, flags, `main` wiring, docs, dashboard |

Gate, run against the final tree:

```
make test                 ok (all packages)
golangci-lint run ./...   0 issues
make docs-check           check passed - all generated docs current; 791 metrics
make grafana-check        coverage 791/791; 43 manifests validated
```

Built as three parallel lanes on disjoint files against a frozen seam
(`internal/flow/netflow/types.go`), then one wiring pass.

## Decision taken that changes what a shipped metric MEANS

**`interface` on a NetFlow record now names the WAN-FACING side** — egress for outbound,
ingress for inbound. A record crosses two interfaces and the label can name one.

This was a genuine fork and it was put to @rknightion rather than decided quietly, because
both answers are defensible and it changes every panel. Labelling the ingress side would
have kept the two lanes agreeing about the same flow, but it would also have corrected the
egress *on the record* while leaving the metric the repair exists to fix just as wrong:
per-WAN volume would not be queryable at all. The cost, now stated in `docs/flow.md` and in
the HELP text: **a LAN host's internet traffic is attributed to the WAN it left by, not to
its own VLAN**, so per-VLAN volume is visible for internal traffic only, and the two lanes
describe the same flow differently. That is a second reason to pin `source=` in queries,
on top of the double-counting.

Zenarmor records are unaffected — they set only `In` — so phase 1's meaning is intact.

## Findings that corrected this issue's own assumptions

**The real template shapes** are in the comment above: `INPUT_SNMP`/`OUTPUT_SNMP` are **2
bytes**, not 4, and **there are no VLAN fields at all**, so VLAN identity comes only from
the ifIndex map. A decoder assuming 4-byte SNMP indices desynchronises the whole record.

**The pre-NAT outbound record resolved to `direction="unknown"`.** The direction rules as
specified could not classify the ordinary outbound record — the majority of WAN traffic —
because its source is a LAN address matching no WAN address, and the spec's rule 3 needs
a WAN-facing interface it could not identify. Two fixes: `IfMap.IsWAN(device)` was added so
rule 3 can answer, and a rule 3b (exactly one end remote, the other resolved → that
orientation) covers records whose interfaces did not resolve. Caught by probing the
production record shape against the real map, not by reading the spec.

**`Iface.Corrected` carries the egress repair, not `Repairs`.** `flow.Repairs` has no field
for either repair and `record.go` is frozen, so the repairs are observable through
`Iface.Corrected` + the two counters rather than by widening the seam.

## The arrival-order problem, since it is the subtlest thing here

The VLAN duplicate's two copies arrive in different datagrams and **either may be first**,
so arrival order cannot pick the winner and a synchronous keep/drop answer cannot un-emit
one already kept. It is decided structurally instead: on the trunk the frame is still
802.1Q-tagged, so a record naming a VLAN tag while sitting on that tag's *parent* device is
by construction the duplicate — dropped whenever it arrives, so both orders give the same
result. A bounded instance table keyed on `(canonical tuple, First, Last)` backstops the
untagged case, resolving pairs by topology; records sharing a key on *unrelated* interfaces
are **kept**, because what cannot be proven duplicate must not be dropped.

Residual, tested and documented: an untagged parent copy arriving first survives — byte
total right, interface attribution wrong. This is why `normalizeNetflow` copying the VLAN
tag is load-bearing; dropping that one line silently downgrades the repair to the backstop,
and a regression test fails when it is removed.

## Verified by breaking, not by passing

- **read-buffer aliasing**: the listener reuses its read buffer, so enqueuing it corrupts
  every queued payload. The first version of that test **passed with the bug present** —
  the worker copied the payload before the read loop lapped the buffer. Redesigned to hold
  the workers blocked while 20 datagrams are read; it now reports `1 distinct payload out
  of 20` when the copy is removed.
- **VLAN tag copy removed** → `sink saw 1 records, want 0 - a parent-interface duplicate
  reached the rollup`.
- **`interface` reverted to ingress-only** → `interfaceLabel = "LAN", want "WAN2"`.
- The decoder lane mutation-tested 10 rules (dropping `Unmap`, skipping unknown fields by
  an assumed width, adding OUT_BYTES to volume, dropping `exporter`/`sourceID` from the
  template key, …); the repair lane mutation-tested 5.

## What phase 3 inherits

- **Decision 8 is NOT done**: `capture.bin` is not yet a golden replay fixture, so the VLAN
  acceptance criterion stays open. The committed fixture policy is real shape + synthetic
  TEST-NET addressing; a replay test against the raw 52 MB capture would run locally only.
- `Fragments` is set to 1 per record and never accumulated — that is the correlator's job.
- The corrected export-lag figures (mean 1m34s, **max 30m41s**) justify a 3-minute
  correlator window by the mean but not the max, so long-flow hit rate must be measured
  rather than assumed.
- `IsWAN` is a heuristic with documented blind spots (double-NATted RFC1918 WAN reads as
  not-WAN; a physical `optN` carrying a routed public subnet reads as WAN). Direction rule
  3a rests on it.
- The DNS answer cache (spec §7) is still deferred and still unbuilt.

## Phase 3 + 4 kicked off — 2026-07-22

Resuming to close the issue: phase 3 (correlator + merged records), phase 4 (dashboard extension + alert/recording rules), and the open VLAN-fixture acceptance criterion.

**Scope decision (Rob):** full build of spec §10 flow OTLP-log emission, `--flow.log-mode` default `per_flow`. Emission reuses the existing `logship` OTLP sink (there is no separate Loki path) — flow records become OTLP logs on the same rails as syslog/Zenarmor/unbound today.

**Architecture (fan-out — metrics never wait on the correlator):**
- Raw per-source records keep feeding the metric rollup directly (decision 3: never sum sources; `source=` stays pinned).
- The correlator collapses NetFlow's 1:N fragmentation (mean 3.75 rec/conn) into one flow-log record per `(community_id, window)`, merged with the matching Zenarmor conn when present, and drives `opnsense_flow_source_byte_delta_ratio`.
- Zenarmor conn gains flow attributes **in place** (community_id, normalized direction, corrected interface, scope, dst.domain) — no new record for the conn stream; merged/NetFlow records are a separate `subsystem=flow` OTLP stream.

**Confirmed live:** on <host-7> the raw `netflow-v9-capture.bin` (54 MB) is present, so the anonymised replay fixture (spec §12) is achievable this session.

Plan is in the gitignored `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-flow-phase3-4-correlator-logs.md`. Building the correlator, DNS cache, log emitter, new metrics, options/wiring, fixture, dashboard and rules now; will report with SHAs as pieces land.

## Phases 3 + 4 shipped — 2026-07-23

All four phases and the last open acceptance criterion are done. Four commits on `main`:

| SHA | What |
|---|---|
| [`8e35af9`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/8e35af9) | correlator + DNS answer cache (pure, tested seam pieces) |
| [`c00e524`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/c00e524) | OTLP flow-log emission path (`flow.LogAttributes` + `logship/flowlog` bridge) |
| [`2d20aeb`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/2d20aeb) | golden NetFlow v9 replay fixture from the real capture |
| [`c974d21`](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/commit/c974d21) | wire correlator → OTLP logs, phase-4 dashboard + rules, docs |

Gate, against the final tree:

```
make test                 ok (all packages)
golangci-lint run ./...   0 issues
make docs-check           check passed — all generated docs current; 799 metrics
make grafana-check        coverage 799/799; 46 manifests validated
```

### Scope decision (Rob, this session)
Full build of spec §10 flow-log emission, `--flow.log-mode` default `per_flow`. Emission reuses the existing `logship` OTLP sink — flow records become OTLP logs on the same rails as syslog/Zenarmor, no separate Loki path.

### What shipped

**Correlator** (`internal/flow/correlate.go`). A bounded accumulator keyed on `(community_id, floor(End/window))`, not a pairwise matcher — one connection produces a mean 3.75 NetFlow records (worst tuple 332), so pairwise is impossible. Fragments accumulate and emit once. Design point settled this session, **deviating from the spec's early-emit**: emit is on **window expiry only**, and Zenarmor arrival enriches the entry in place rather than triggering an early emit. This makes each entry emit exactly once — a Zenarmor record mid-window followed by more NetFlow fragments cannot emit the flow twice or split its bytes across a merged and a netflow-only record — while expiry still bounds latency to one window (immaterial for a flow log). The correlator **only ever emits NetFlow-derived records**; a Zenarmor conn is enrichment input (→ `source=merged`) and otherwise vanishes, because its own lane already ships it. That is what stops the merged record double-shipping the Zenarmor side. Overflow force-emits the oldest (counted), never drops.

**OTLP flow logs** (`internal/flow/logemit.go`, `internal/logship/flowlog/`). `Record.LogAttributes()`/`LogBody()` render a flow record as structured metadata (IPs/ports/community_id/app/domain are metadata, never labels; NF and Zen counters travel together, never summed). The `flowlog.Bridge` push source packages them onto the shared pipeline, stamping `source=netflow|merged`, `subsystem=flow`. A per-minute budget truncates (never samples) over `--flow.max-logs-per-window` and counts every drop — a flood guard on the unauthenticated NetFlow ingress.

**Fan-out** (`internal/flow/tee.go`, `main.go`): both lanes feed a tee → the metric rollup (unchanged, source-tagged, decision 3) **and** the correlator. Metrics never wait on the correlator (spec §8): the rollup is updated on arrival, only the log record is deferred. Shutdown flushes the correlator into the still-live pipeline before it drains.

**Flags:** `--flow.correlate[.window|.max-entries]`, `--flow.log-mode`, `--flow.max-logs-per-window`, `--flow.dns-cache.size`, each validated against the quiet-no-op rule; a sub-minute correlate window warns.

**Self-metrics:** `opnsense_flow_correlator_{entries,emitted,matched,evicted,expired}_total` and `opnsense_flow_logs_{emitted,truncated,dropped}_total`, absent until the lane is built. `matched/emitted` is the join hit-rate — **measured, not assumed**, which #346's export-lag finding (max 30m41s) requires for long flows.

**Replay fixture** (`cmd/flowanon/`, `internal/flow/netflow/testdata/replay-v9.bin`, 9.8 KB). A committed, deterministic, tested anonymiser (stable category-preserving bijection; template-aware address rewriter; relative FIRST/LAST_SWITCHED deltas preserved) turns 7 curated real datagrams into a fixture that replays through the real decoder + repair. Asserts the VLAN parent duplicate is suppressed, the policy-routed WAN egress is corrected, IPv6 decodes, data-before-template counts `NoTemplate`, and — a leak-guard over all 453 address fields — that no routable address outside the RFC5737/3849 ranges survives. **The decoder and all three repairs handled every real case correctly; no bug was found.** Raw 54 MB capture stays out of the repo.

**Phase 4:** a "Correlator & Log Emission" dashboard row (coverage 799/799); two warning alerts (`OPNsenseFlowCorrelatorEvicting`, `OPNsenseFlowLogsTruncated`); and a source-pinned recording rule `instance:opnsense_flow_bytes:rate5m` (pins `source="netflow"`, the double-count-safe per-WAN byte rate).

### Deferred to #353 (spec extras beyond this issue's acceptance criteria)
Tracked in **#353**, none of which was in this issue's phase/acceptance checklist:
- **DNS answer cache wiring** (spec §7). The cache is built + committed + tested (`8e35af9`) but deliberately **not fed/read** — shipping it half-wired reproduces the phase-1 dead-cache mistake. Wiring touches the Zenarmor `dns` lane + both enrich paths.
- **§9 metrics**: `source_byte_delta_ratio` (histogram — the correlator's quantified NF-vs-Zen signal), `unique_destinations` (gauge), `top_talker_bytes_total` (opt-in, host-labelled).
- **Zenarmor conn attrs in place** (spec §10): flow attributes on the existing conn OTLP record (additive; conn record count unchanged).

Closing: the issue's four phases and every acceptance criterion are complete; the spec's remaining enrichment/metric elaborations continue in #353.

title: feat(flow): NetFlow v9 receiver + Zenarmor flow rollups + correlated flow records

body:
Follow-on to #338. The response-cache audit there surfaced collectors whose poll tier does not reflect their data volatility — the body cache is quietly absorbing a too-fast poll instead of the tier expressing it.

That matters because `--exporter.cache-ttl=0` is a documented, supported setting ("fetch everything on every poll"). Today it puts `backupHistory` — which globs `/conf/backup/config-*.xml` and simplexml-parses every retained file, up to ~100 — back to 60 calls an hour, on data that changes only when someone writes the config.

The tier should be the honest statement of volatility; the body cache should only be doing what a per-collector interval structurally cannot (splitting a mixed collector like `firewall`, `unbound_dns`, `hardware` or `system`, where live and static endpoints share one poll).

## Re-tier

| collector | now | proposed | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth` | medium 60s | cold 15m | user/group/API-key inventory; changes only on an admin edit. All three endpoints are body-cached today. |
| `backup` | medium 60s | cold 15m | config backup history; changes only when a config write happens, and is the most expensive single call in the set. |
| `clamav` | medium 60s | cold 15m | engine + signature-database version only; freshclam runs a few times a day. |
| `chrony` | medium 60s | slow 5m | same data class as the `ntp` collector (sources/tracking/peers), which is already slow. Consistency, not a new judgement. |
| `lldpd` | medium 60s | slow 5m | neighbour tables change on cabling/switch events. A lost link still shows on `interfaces` at 15s. |

Not changing: `hardware`, `crowdsec`, `tor`, `firewall`, `unbound_dns`, `system` all mix live and static endpoints in one poll (or inside one `Fetch`), so the tier cannot express them — that is exactly the case the body cache exists for.

## Dedupe `PluginGatedEndpoints()`

`opnsense/cache.go` accumulated duplicates through the #227 union merges — `trafficShaperStatistics` appears 5 times, `haproxyInfo`/`ipsecPhase1`/`monitStatus`/`nginxVts` 3 times each, and others twice. Harmless at runtime (callers build a set) but it makes the list unreviewable: you cannot tell at a glance whether an endpoint is present, which is how a missing entry gets shipped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The five collectors above carry their new tier in `collectorTiers`
- [ ] `TestBodyCachedEndpointsPollSlowerThanTheirTTL` still passes (all TTLs stay above the new intervals)
- [ ] `PluginGatedEndpoints()` returns no duplicate entries, with a test that fails if a duplicate is reintroduced
- [ ] `make docs` regenerated; full gate green (`go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`)

comments.body:
Done in bcb5caf.

**Re-tiered** — cold 15m: `auth`, `backup`, `clamav`. Slow 5m: `chrony`, `lldpd`. Verified against the live devel box: `opnsense_exporter_collector_poll_interval_seconds` reports 900s for the three cold ones, 300s for the two slow, and `firewall`/`system`/`unbound_dns` correctly unchanged at 60s.

The tier doc comment now carries the rule that made these calls decidable: a collector goes cold when its data changes only on an admin action, **not** because its endpoint happens to carry a body TTL — the tier must stand on its own so the poll stays sane at `--exporter.cache-ttl=0`. Where a collector mixes live and static endpoints in one poll (`firewall`, `unbound_dns`, `hardware`, `system`, `crowdsec`, `tor` — for `system` the split is inside a single `Fetch`), the tier follows the live half and the body cache handles the static endpoints, because no per-collector interval can split them.

**Deduped** `PluginGatedEndpoints()` — 112 entries down to the same 84 unique names, now alphabetical. Checked mechanically that no name was lost or gained against `HEAD~`. `TestPluginGatedEndpoints_HasNoDuplicates` fails if a duplicate is reintroduced; it was watched failing on the old list (reporting `trafficShaperStatistics` ×4, `haproxyInfo`/`ipsecPhase1`/`monitStatus`/`nginxVts` ×3) before the fix.

Gate green: `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` 0 issues, `make docs-check`.

title: poll tiers: re-tier wholly-static collectors to cold/slow, and dedupe PluginGatedEndpoints

## OPNsense live-box schema canary

Probed **171** endpoints: 170 clean, 0 with breaking type drift, 0 with missing paths, 0 with unexpected top-level keys, 1 absent 404 (0 unexpected, 1 plugin-gated/expected), 0 probe errors, 0 skipped (no live parameter).

### ℹ️ Plugin-gated endpoints absent (plugin not installed — expected, not drift)

- `siproxdRegistrations` (`api/siproxd/service/showregistrations`)

20 endpoints have paths that could not be verified (empty lists/maps on the box) — increase box activity to cover them.

1 endpoints have no schema (see `schemaExemptEndpoints` in `opnsense/schema_registry.go`).

## End-to-end exporter smoke

- `opnsense_up` = 1 ✅
- all 24 sub-collectors succeeded ✅
- only 170 distinct `opnsense_*` metric names (floor 480) ❌

comments.body:
Not API drift — the schema half of that run was clean (170/171 endpoints verified, the one absence plugin-gated and expected). The failure was the **smoke test asserting against a cold exporter**.

#336 (merged 892c72c-1, 2026-07-20 19:50 BST) decoupled collection from the scrape: `/metrics` now replays the snapshot the per-collector pollers fill. The smoke step still `sleep 3`ed before scraping, an assumption inherited from the fetch-on-scrape model. At t=3s, with up to 5s of startup jitter and the 8-way poll-concurrency cap, only 24 of 47 collectors had polled — hence `only 170 distinct opnsense_* metric names (floor 480)`. Timeline confirms it: every run up to 2026-07-20 passed; the first run after #336 landed failed.

## Fixed in 9d43334

**Exporter** — `/-/ready` now stays `503` until the health poll **and** every enabled collector have completed a first poll (`Collector.SnapshotWarm()`), so readiness means "this target will serve a complete scrape", not just "the box answers". A failed first poll counts as warm (it surfaces as `scrape_collector_success=0`), so one broken plugin cannot pin readiness open. The 503 body is now a bare `Not Ready` since two conditions can fail; the reason stays in the log. No bundled deployment probes `/-/ready` (`deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml` uses `/-/healthy` for both), so nothing regresses on upgrade.

**Canary** — the smoke waits on `/-/ready` (5s poll, 300s ceiling) instead of sleeping, and reports a warm-up timeout as its own failure line.

**Floor** — `METRIC_NAME_FLOOR` 480 → 560. The box emits 622 (last clean run, #296) and 641 on a warm local run today; the 495 the old floor was written against has grown with the collectors added since, leaving the floor with ~23% of slack.

## Verified against the live devel box

| | 3s after start | once `/-/ready` is 200 |
|---|---|---|
| `/-/ready` | 503 | 200 |
| distinct `opnsense_*` names | 256 | **641** |
| collectors ok | partial | **59 / 59 enabled**, none failed |
| `opnsense_up` | — | 1 |

Warm-up took ~13s. A dispatched canary run is in flight: https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/actions/runs/29825141435
