## Summary

Every labelled error counter in `internal/logship` disappears from `/metrics` entirely when nothing has gone wrong, because a Prometheus `CounterVec` emits **no series until its first increment**. A healthy exporter therefore publishes *nothing* for its own error metrics, and every restart resets them back to invisible.

Observed live: `opnsense_exporter_logs_rejected_total` vanished at 23:01 when the container restarted. It had carried `reason="peer"` and `reason="unhandled_endpoint"` from earlier; after the restart nothing had been rejected, so the metric family was simply absent until something failed. It looks exactly like broken instrumentation.

Current state on a healthy live box:

| Metric | Type | Present when healthy? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `logs_ship_errors_total` | `Counter` | **yes**, reads `0` |
| `logs_resource_capped_total` | `Counter` | **yes**, reads `0` |
| `logs_rejected_total` | `CounterVec` | no |
| `logs_parse_errors_total` | `CounterVec` | no |
| `logs_dropped_total` | `CounterVec` | no |
| `logs_poll_errors_total` | `CounterVec` | no |
| `logs_possible_gap_total` | `CounterVec` | no |
| `logs_enrich_misses_total` | `CounterVec` | no |

The unlabelled counters behave correctly. Only the vectors are affected.

## Why it matters

`rate(opnsense_exporter_logs_parse_errors_total[5m])` returns **no data**, not `0`. So:

- The Log Shipping tab's error panels render "No data" rather than a flat zero line — indistinguishable from a broken query or a dead exporter, which is precisely the distinction those panels exist to make.
- An alert on any of them evaluates to NoData rather than 0. `noDataState` then decides the outcome, which is not what the rule author meant.
- After every deploy the metrics silently disappear again until the first failure, so "no series" means both "healthy" and "never observed" with no way to tell them apart.

This is the same class of defect as the Zenarmor dashboard's Blocked stat reading "No data" when it meant "nothing was blocked" (fixed there with `noValue: "0"`) — except here the honest fix belongs in the exporter, not in every panel that touches the metric.

## Change

Pre-initialise the known label combinations at registration, which is Prometheus' own documented advice ("initialize the metrics you know about"). Every label set involved is **closed and code-defined**, so there is no cardinality risk:

- `logs_rejected_total{source,reason}` — reasons are per-receiver and fixed: syslog `peer,oversized`; zenarmor `peer,oversized,unhandled_endpoint,unknown_family,filtered,self_traffic`. `NewReceiverMetrics` would take the receiver's reason set.
- `logs_parse_errors_total{source,stage}` — `envelope,filterlog,document`.
- `logs_dropped_total{source,reason}` — `overflow`.
- `logs_poll_errors_total{source}` / `logs_possible_gap_total{source}` — sources are known when the pipeline registers them.
- `logs_enrich_misses_total{table}` — `rules,interfaces,leases,services`.

Total added series is on the order of a dozen zeroes.

**Do not** pre-initialise anything whose label values come off the wire. The rule is the same one that keeps `program` out of the Loki index: only closed, code-defined sets. If a reason can be attacker-influenced or discovered at runtime, it must stay lazily created.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `CounterVec` above emits its known label combinations at `0` from startup, before any event
- [ ] A test asserts the metrics are present-and-zero on a freshly constructed pipeline/receiver
- [ ] Reason/stage/table vocabularies live in one place per counter, so a new reason cannot be added without also being pre-initialised
- [ ] No pre-initialisation of any label value sourced from received data
- [ ] Log Shipping dashboard error panels show a flat zero on a healthy box rather than "No data"

Found while diagnosing an apparent metric outage that turned out to be a restart plus an empty vector.

comments.body:
## Vocabulary correction before implementing

Premise confirmed and unchanged: a `CounterVec` emits no series until its first increment, so healthy reads as invisible. Pre-initialisation goes ahead.

The label vocabularies in the issue body are wrong though. Checked every production call site — six of them don't match.

| Metric / label | Issue said | Actually in the code |
|---|---|---|
| `logs_rejected_total` reason (syslog) | `peer`, `oversized` | `peer`, `oversized`, `filtered`, `sampled` (`filtered` at `internal/logship/syslog/source.go:132`, `sampled` at `source.go:145`) |
| `logs_rejected_total` reason (zenarmor) | `peer`, `oversized`, `unhandled_endpoint`, `unknown_family`, `filtered`, `self_traffic` | `peer`, `auth`, `unhandled_endpoint`, `body`, `unknown_family`, `filtered`, `self_traffic`. There is no `oversized` on the zenarmor path at all; `auth` (`server.go:130`) and `body` (`server.go:303`) were missed |
| `logs_parse_errors_total` stage | `envelope`, `filterlog`, `document` | syslog: `envelope` only. zenarmor: `bulk` and `document`. `filterlog` is a parser name registered via `RegisterParser`, not a stage — nothing ever calls `ParseError("filterlog")`. `bulk` (`server.go:324`) was missed |
| `logs_enrich_misses_total` table | `rules`, `interfaces`, `leases`, `services` | `rules` is the only reachable value, one production call site at `internal/logship/syslog/filterlog.go:129`. `interfaces`/`leases`/`tunnels` are tables for `RefreshErrors` and `LastRefresh` but never for `Misses`. `services` isn't a table at all |
| `logs_possible_gap_total` source | "sources are known when the pipeline registers them", implying all of them | `unbound` only, one call site at `internal/logship/unbound.go:93`. It exists for bounded-window sources; a cursor-based source can never gap |
| `logs_dropped_total` reason | `overflow` | right |

The rule that decided all of the above: pre-initialise exactly the label combinations the code can actually produce, and nothing else. A series that can never be non-zero isn't an honest zero - it claims we're watching something we aren't. That's why `possible_gap` gets `unbound` only and `misses` gets `rules` only, rather than the fuller sets the issue asked for.

One design decision: the receiver reason sets get pre-initialised in full regardless of config, so `logs_rejected_total{source="syslog",reason="sampled"}` reads 0 even when `--logs.syslog.sample` is off. The vocabulary is a property of the code, not of the config. Conditioning it on config would put the exact ambiguity this issue is closing straight back, just at a different point: a flag flip would make series appear and disappear.

Knock-on for the acceptance criteria: the `possible_gap` criterion ("sources are known when the pipeline registers them") is replaced by an optional source interface letting a source declare it can report gaps, matching the existing `StatefulSource`/`IntervalSource` idiom. `unbound` is the only implementer today.

Done in 9f64c66.

Pre-initialises every affected `CounterVec` to zero at registration, using the corrected vocabularies from the comment above. `logs_enrich_refresh_errors_total` is fixed too — it wasn't listed in the issue but is a `CounterVec` with the identical defect.

Two things worth recording beyond the acceptance criteria:

**Timestamp gauges are deliberately left lazy.** A pre-initialised zero on `logs_last_event_timestamp_seconds` or `logs_enrich_last_refresh_timestamp_seconds` reads as 1970, so `time() - LastRefresh` would report a 56-year-old cache instead of "not refreshed yet". Absent is the honest answer there; present-at-zero is not.

**The enforcement is an AST test, not a convention.** `TestReceiverVocabulariesMatchCallSites` (`internal/logship/vocab_test.go`) parses the receiver packages and diffs the reasons/stages actually reachable against the declared vocabulary, in the spirit of `opnsense/contract_postendpoints_test.go`. It fails in **both** directions: a call site missing from the vocabulary (the #280 bug returning), and a vocabulary entry no call site can produce (a zero that can never move). `TestTablesMatchTickCallSites` does the same for enrichment tables, and `TestReceiversPassTheirVocabularyToNewReceiverMetrics` catches a receiver declaring a vocabulary and then passing `ReceiverVocab{}`.

All assertions go through `registry.Gather`, not `WithLabelValues` — reading a vec child *creates* it, so a test built on it would have passed against the unfixed code. Verified by mutation: disabling `preInit` fails the pre-init tests, adding an undeclared `Reject("brand_new_reason")` fails the vocab test, and declaring an unreachable miss table fails the dead-vocabulary check.

Acceptance criteria:

- [x] Every `CounterVec` emits its known label combinations at 0 from startup
- [x] A test asserts present-and-zero on a freshly constructed pipeline/receiver
- [x] Vocabularies live in one place per counter, enforced against call sites
- [x] No pre-initialisation of any label value sourced from received data
- [x] Dashboard error panels show a flat zero — no panel change needed; the series now exist, and `make grafana-check` still passes 765/765

Gate: `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check` all green. No metric names changed, so the docs/dashboard counts are unaffected.

title: Labelled counters vanish when healthy, so rate() returns no-data instead of zero

body:
## Summary

Zenarmor streams ~4-6 GB/day and a large share of it is traffic the operator already knows about and will never investigate. On the live box, **`<host-1>` alone is 57k of 78k records (~73%)** — it is the observability host, so it spends its life talking to `otlp-gateway-prod-gb-south-1.grafana.net` and `profiles-prod-023.grafana.net`. Those two are the top TLS SNI *and* the top DNS query. Every top-N panel is dominated by the monitoring stack monitoring itself.

There is no way to cut that today short of turning off a whole family.

## Two different problems — worth not conflating

**1. Self-referential traffic (#278).** Records describing the `_bulk` connection that delivers the records. Tautological: it exists only because we are measuring. Should be dropped in code, default on, and should NOT be counted either — `logs_zenarmor_bulk_requests_total` already measures that connection exactly, and far better. Tracked separately in #278.

**2. Real-but-boring traffic (this issue).** <host-1> → Grafana Cloud is genuine network activity. It is high-volume and uninteresting *today*. That is not the same as being uninformative, which is the whole point below.

## Why the syslog precedent does not transfer

`--logs.syslog.sample` gets this right via `sampleKeep` (`internal/logship/syslog/sample.go`): a line that `observeDerived` did not count is **never** dropped, so sampling only ever removes the redundant raw copy of something a counter already captured — and every block/reject survives regardless.

That contract works for syslog because `opnsense_log_events_firewall_total` carries `action`, `interface` and `rule` — most of the line's value survives in the counter.

**It does not work for Zenarmor.** `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total` carries only family / action / category / interface / rcode / severity / status_class — deliberately, for cardinality. No `server_name`, no `query`, no `device_name`. So dropping a Zenarmor line after counting it still destroys the thing the SIEM dashboard exists to show. **Zenarmor exclusion is lossy in a way syslog sampling is not, and the design should say so out loud rather than inherit the syslog framing.**

## Proposal

A repeatable field matcher, evaluated against the record's attributes, dropping the whole record:

```
--logs.zenarmor.exclude='server_name=~.*\.grafana\.net'
--logs.zenarmor.exclude='query=~.*\.grafana\.net'
```

Contracts:

- **Default off.** No implicit blind spots.
- **Counted** — `logs_dropped_total{source="zenarmor", reason="excluded"}`, ideally labelled by rule, so the blind spot is visible on a dashboard rather than inferred from a config file.
- **Metrics still derived before the drop**, so the low-cardinality counters stay complete and the *shape* of excluded traffic outlives both the exclusion and Loki's 31-day retention.
- **Validated at startup** against the known attribute keys — a typo'd field name must error, not silently match nothing. Same reasoning as the existing strict `--logs.zenarmor.families` validation: a filter that silently does nothing looks exactly like a quiet network.

Open design question for the implementer: single `field=regex` per entry (simple, mirrors `--logs.syslog.exclude-programs`) versus AND-ing several fields in one rule (needed to express "<host-1>'s Grafana traffic" precisely rather than "all Grafana traffic from anywhere"). Recommend starting with the simple form and only adding AND if a real rule needs it.

## Recommendation on the Grafana Cloud case specifically

**Do not ship a default rule for it, and prefer filtering Grafana-side for now.** <host-1> is the most privileged host on the network, and "high-volume encrypted egress to a cloud endpoint" is precisely the shape exfiltration takes. Dropping it at ingest to save bytes means the one host worth watching most closely becomes the one we log least — and unlike a query-time filter, that decision is unrecoverable after the fact.

The knob is still worth building: the operator who wants it should have it, per deployment. This issue is for the mechanism, not for a default.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--logs.zenarmor.exclude` drops matching records, default off, repeatable
- [ ] Drops are counted with a reason label and surfaced on the Log Shipping dashboard
- [ ] Derived counters are unaffected by exclusion (metric observed before the drop)
- [ ] An unknown field name is a startup error, not a silent no-op
- [ ] `docs/zenarmor-receiver.md` documents the mechanism AND states plainly that exclusion loses forensic detail the counters cannot replace

Related: #278 (self-traffic, a separate and unconditional case), #276 (the receiver).

comments.body:
Done in d31296f.

```
--logs.zenarmor.exclude='server_name=~.*\.grafana\.net'
--logs.zenarmor.exclude='query=~.*\.grafana\.net'
```

Repeatable, default off, field-scoped, OR-ed. Went with the simple `FIELD=~REGEX` form per your recommendation — no AND. Only `=~` exists (`^x$` says exact), leaving `=` and `!=` unclaimed so they can be added later without redefining what a bare `=` already meant. Env form is one rule per **line** — kingpin splits cumulative env values on newline, not comma, so a regex containing `a{1,3}` survives.

### Deviation from the issue: the metric

The issue asked for `logs_dropped_total{source="zenarmor", reason="excluded"}`. **That can't be built as written** — `logs_dropped_total` is pipeline-owned (queue overflow) and a receiver can't reach it; every configured receiver drop (`filtered`, `self_traffic`) goes on `logs_rejected_total`. So exclusions are counted on both:

```
opnsense_exporter_logs_rejected_total{source="zenarmor", reason="excluded"}     12
opnsense_exporter_logs_zenarmor_excluded_total{rule="server_name=~.*\\.grafana\\.net"}  9
opnsense_exporter_logs_zenarmor_excluded_total{rule="query=~.*\\.grafana\\.net"}        3
```

The first keeps accounting consistent with the other configured drops; the second is the "ideally labelled by rule" bit — the aggregate alone can't distinguish a rule that drops nothing from one quietly eating the stream. Rule cardinality is bounded by config, so both are pre-initialised to 0 per #280. New panel on the Log Shipping tab.

### On the framing

Took the issue's point that this shouldn't inherit the syslog framing, and said so in the docs rather than only in the code: sampling is safe because `opnsense_log_events_firewall_total` carries most of the line's value, whereas `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total` has no `server_name`, `query` or `device_name`. Derived counters *are* observed before the drop (so the shape outlives both the exclusion and Loki's retention), but the record itself is gone for good and can't be recovered the way a query-time filter can. `docs/zenarmor-receiver.md` states that plainly, and carries your recommendation on the Grafana Cloud case verbatim: **no default rule, prefer filtering Grafana-side**, because <host-1> is the most privileged host on the network and that traffic shape is exactly what exfiltration looks like.

### Validation

Field names are checked at startup against the receiver's attribute vocabulary, and the error names the near-miss:

```
logs.zenarmor.exclude: unknown field "servername" in rule "servername=~.*\\.grafana\\.net"
(did you mean server_name?). A rule naming a field the receiver never sets would silently
match nothing, so this is refused at startup. Valid fields: alertinfo.category, ...
```

The vocabulary is enforced against `parse.go`'s real `set()`/`setInt()` call sites by an AST test, in both directions. Worth noting: building that scan turned up two shapes a grep misses — `rcode` is assigned directly (`attrs[attrRCode] = ...`) rather than via `set()`, and `set(logship.AttrSubsystem, ...)` is a qualified constant. Both are now resolved, and an unknown qualified constant fails the test loudly rather than silently shrinking the vocabulary.

`opnsense.subsystem` and `opnsense.action` are in the vocabulary because they're genuinely on the record and matchable. Excluding on either is a bad idea and the docs say so, but that's the operator's call to make explicitly rather than something to hide by pretending the field doesn't exist.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] `--logs.zenarmor.exclude` drops matching records, default off, repeatable
- [x] Drops counted with a reason label and surfaced on the Log Shipping dashboard
- [x] Derived counters unaffected by exclusion (metric observed before the drop)
- [x] An unknown field name is a startup error, not a silent no-op
- [x] `docs/zenarmor-receiver.md` documents the mechanism AND states plainly that exclusion loses forensic detail the counters cannot replace

Verified against the built binary, not just unit tests: typo'd field and invalid regex each abort startup; a valid pair of rules publishes both counters at zero; a `_bulk` POST of two TLS records drops only the `grafana.net` one, attributes it to the right rule, and ships the other. Gate green: `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check`.

One unrelated thing that surfaced while smoke-testing: when the firewall is unreachable, the collector short-circuits the whole sub-collector fan-out, so the `opnsense_log_events_*` derived counters disappear from `/metrics` even though log shipping is still running and still counting. Pre-existing and out of scope here, but it's the same class as #280 — a counter describing log traffic vanishing because an unrelated API scrape failed. Say the word and I'll file it.

title: Let operators exclude known-boring Zenarmor traffic from the log stream

body:
## Summary

Zenarmor inspects the traffic on the link the exporter's Elasticsearch receiver listens on, so it reports **the connection that is delivering its own records to us**. We then ship those records, which generates more of them.

Measured on the live box within an hour of enabling the receiver (#276):

| Family | To exporter `:9200` | Total | Share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web` | 6,194 | 8,135 | **76%** |
| `flow` | 5,808 | 54,079 | 11% |
| **combined** | **~12,000/hour** | ~78,000/hour | **~15%** |

At the measured ~4-6 GB/day that is roughly **600-900 MB/day of Loki volume describing our own ingest**. The `web` family is effectively unusable without filtering: its top hosts/URIs/user-agents are all `POST /zenarmor_<uuid>_<family>_write/_bulk` from `go-elasticsearch/8.19.3`.

Not affected: syslog `:5847` and metrics `:9098` produce no such records.

## It converges, but it does not go away

Each `_bulk` POST yields ~1 `web` record plus its `flow` record, and those ride along in a *later* bulk carrying many records — so this is self-sustaining, not exponential. It settles at a constant ~1 web record per bulk request rather than running away. Worth stating plainly so nobody reads "feedback loop" as an emergency.

## Why fix it in the exporter

Every deployment of this receiver hits it, on any network, with no way for an operator to see why their `web` family is nonsense. It is self-referential by construction: a receiver reporting on the connection carrying its own reports is never information.

The `--logs.zenarmor.families` help already says to prefer cutting at the Zenarmor end, and that remains true for *volume* — but this specific traffic cannot be cut there without also excluding the exporter host from inspection generally, which an operator may well want for other reasons.

## Suggested change

Drop records whose destination is our own ingest endpoint. The receiver knows both its listen port and the streaming peer, so `ip_dst_port == <our listen port>` combined with the record's source being the configured peer identifies it precisely. Behind a flag, defaulted on:

```
--logs.zenarmor.drop-self-traffic  (default true)
```

Worth confirming against a container deployment first: the receiver binds `0.0.0.0:9200` and sees `ip_dst_saddr` as the host's LAN address (`<lan-ip-1>`), not its own container IP, so matching on destination *address* is unreliable where matching on destination *port* is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Records describing the exporter's own ingest connection are dropped before shipping
- [ ] Behaviour is flagged, defaulted on, and documented in `docs/zenarmor-receiver.md`
- [ ] Dropped records are counted (so the drop is visible rather than silent)
- [ ] A test covers the container case (destination address is the host, not the container)
- [ ] Once fixed, remove the `| uri!~"/zenarmor_.*/_bulk"` workaround from the `opnsense-zenarmor` dashboard's web panels (`gc-gitsync-m7kni`)

Found while validating #276 against live data.

comments.body:
Broadened into #279, which proposes a general `--logs.zenarmor.exclude` mechanism for operator-defined noise.

Keeping this issue separate on purpose — the two have opposite defaults and different justifications:

- **This one (#278)** is self-referential traffic: records about the connection carrying the records. It exists only because we are measuring, so it should drop by default and should NOT be counted either (`logs_zenarmor_bulk_requests_total` already measures that connection precisely).
- **#279** is real traffic the operator finds boring. Default off, counted, and lossy by admission.

If #279 lands first, this can be expressed as a built-in rule in the same engine — but its no-count semantics are the exception, not the norm, so it may well be cleaner standalone.

## Verified live

<host-1> picked up `b454b0e` and the fix is doing exactly what it was measured to do.

- **`rate(logs_rejected_total{reason="self_traffic"})` = 5.54/s** against **`rate(bulk_requests_total)` = 2.79/s** — a ratio of **1.99**, not the ~1 predicted. Each `_bulk` POST generates *two* self-records, not one: a `web` record for the HTTP request and a `flow` record for the TCP connection underneath it. The filter catches both.
- **Zero `/zenarmor_*/_bulk` records reaching Loki in the last minute** (down from ~150/min).
- **Top URIs in the web family are now real traffic** — `/inform`, `/api/states`, `/ng-client/share.php` — where they were 100% our own ingest before.
- The stream is otherwise untouched: **2,038 Zenarmor records/minute** still shipping.
- Drops as a share of everything: 534 dropped vs 3,107 shipped shortly after start = **14.7%**, against the ~15% measured before the fix existed.

The container-safe design held: the record's destination is the host's `<lan-ip-1>` while the exporter is inside a container that has never heard of that address, and the filter fires anyway because it matches on the sending peer plus the bound port and never on the destination address.

One correction to this issue's own text for the record: it estimated "~1 web record per bulk". The real figure is ~2 records per bulk across two families. The volume estimate (~15%) was right.

body:
## The bug

`internal/logship/syslog/derive.go:85` reads the attribute `http.status_code`:

```go
sink.ObserveHAProxy(event, attrs["haproxy.backend"], attrs["haproxy.server"], attrs["haproxy.state"], statusClass(attrs["http.status_code"]))
```

But `internal/logship/syslog/haproxy.go:209` sets it under a different key:

```go
set("http.response.status_code", m[12])
```

So the lookup always misses, `statusClass("")` always returns `""`, and the `status_class` label on `opnsense_exporter_log_events_haproxy_total` has been **empty for every HAProxy line since the metric shipped**. The 2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx bucketing the label exists to provide has never worked.

## Why it went unnoticed

It fails silently and in the safe direction — an empty label looks like "no HTTP status on this line", which is a legitimate case the code explicitly supports (`logmetrics.go:26`: `statusClass is "2xx"/"3xx"/"4xx"/"5xx" or "" when the line carries no HTTP status`). So the metric looks plausible rather than broken. The existing `derive_test.go` builds its attribute map by hand and uses the *reader's* key, so it agrees with the bug rather than catching it.

## Found by

Adversarial review during the Zenarmor receiver work (#276). The Zenarmor package guards against exactly this failure mode by declaring shared attribute keys as consts used by both the parser and the deriver, so the two sides cannot drift.

## Fix

Make `derive.go` read `http.response.status_code`, and add a regression test that drives a **real HAProxy log line through the parser** and asserts a non-empty `status_class` reaches the sink — rather than hand-building the attribute map, which is what let the two keys drift apart in the first place. Consider hoisting the shared keys to consts, as `internal/logship/zenarmor` does.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `derive.go` reads the key `haproxy.go` actually writes
- [ ] Regression test drives a real HAProxy line end-to-end (parser → deriver → sink) and asserts `status_class` is `2xx`/`4xx`/etc, not `""`
- [ ] Test fails against the current code and passes after the fix
- [ ] `make test` + `golangci-lint run ./...` green
title: fix(logship): HAProxy status_class label is always empty (attribute key mismatch)

body:
## What and why

Zenarmor is the last significant data source on the firewall the exporter doesn't touch. Its syslog export is licence-gated above the Home tier, so the only Zenarmor data reaching Loki today is `zenarmor_servicelog` — engine diagnostics tailed off disk by Alloy at ~62 lines/sec. That's noise. The per-flow connection records, per-query DNS, TLS/SNI, HTTP metadata and threat alerts never leave the box.

Zenarmor exposes an **additional streaming destination**: "Stream Reporting Data to External Elasticsearch". It's available on Home, it mirrors rather than replaces the local reporting DB, and it speaks the ES `_bulk` API. If the exporter poses as an Elasticsearch node it receives that stream and can ship it as enriched OTLP logs plus derived counters.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-zenarmor-receiver-design.md` (local scratch, gitignored).

## Proven on the live box (spike, 2026-07-16)

73-second capture against the prod firewall, 2,824 real documents, 250 bulk requests:

- **Works on the Home tier.** The `"remote elasticsearch not available on free plan"` string in the binary guards the *install-time full-offload wizard*, a different (and irreversible) feature.
- **Streaming mirrors.** `ipdrstreamer` is a writer fan-out (`writer.Manager` → `[]pool.Writer`) over the same `.ipdr` files. Local ES + GUI reporting untouched; streamed docs are byte-identical to the local ES docs.
- **`ipdrstreamer` links the official `github.com/elastic/go-elasticsearch`.** The 7.14+ product check is enforced — every response MUST carry `X-Elastic-Product: Elasticsearch` or the client hard-refuses. Report version 8.11.3 (Zenarmor supports 8.9.x–8.17.1).
- **Records arrive at flow close, near-real-time, no backfill.** `start_time` can be hours stale on long-lived flows — never use it to reason about arrival.
- **Volume:** ~39 docs/sec → ~2.5–3.3M docs/day, **~4–6 GB/day raw JSON**. conn 61.4%, dns 25.7%, tls 9.9%, http 3.0%, alert ~0, sip 0.

## Scope

New `internal/logship/zenarmor` implementing `logship.PushSource`. Seven ES endpoints, all observed rather than guessed: `GET /`, `GET /_cat/indices`, `GET /_cat/aliases`, `PUT /<index>`, `DELETE /<alias>`, `POST /_aliases`, `POST /<alias>/_bulk`. Rollover-alias pattern — bulk targets the `_write` alias, never the dated index.

Family → subsystem: `conn`→`flow`, `dns`→`dns`, `tls`→`tls`, `http`→`web`, `alert`→`ids`, `sip`→`voip`.

Three cross-cutting changes come with it:

1. **Metric hoist (breaking).** `syslog/metrics.go:21` registers `logs_parse_errors_total` / `logs_rejected_total` with source-neutral names and no `source` label via `MustRegister` on the shared registry. A second receiver **panics at startup**. Hoist both to `logship/metrics.go` with a `source` label. Ships `feat!`.
2. **`opnsense.action` as a third index label.** Binary `pass`|`block`, normalised across all five lanes, hoisted to the OTLP resource. Mapping is an explicit allowlist — **unknown verbs leave it unset**, never guessed (filterlog's `action` is a raw wire passthrough, `filterlog.go:89`).
3. **`ObserveZenarmor` on `MetricSink`** — derived counters on bounded dimensions only.

## Decisions taken (do not re-litigate)

- **All six families, raw** — Loki as SIEM; volume accepted.
- **Raw AND counters**, not either/or — raw to Loki for forensics, counters to Prometheus for alerting and to outlive the 31d Loki retention.
- **Keep `opnsense.*` + self-serve promotion.** Native-only OTel promotion has no slot for "log category"; the self-serve API is a low barrier.
- **Reuse the coarse subsystem vocabulary** so `{opnsense_subsystem="ids"}` crosses sources.
- **Sensitive data is the point.** DNS queries, URIs, JA3, MACs are desired. The only hard constraint is Prometheus cardinality.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `internal/logship/zenarmor` implements `logship.PushSource`, registered via `init()`
- [ ] All seven ES endpoints served; `X-Elastic-Product: Elasticsearch` on **every** response
- [ ] In-memory index registry: 404 before create, 200 after — idempotent across restarts, robust to either handshake path
- [ ] Unhandled endpoints answer `200 {}` **and** increment `logs_rejected_total{source="zenarmor",reason="unhandled_endpoint"}` (drift signal, not silent outage)
- [ ] All six families parsed to `logship.Record`; family routed off the URL path
- [ ] Full document preserved in `Record.Body`; per-flow fields in structured metadata, never on the resource
- [ ] `logs_parse_errors_total` / `logs_rejected_total` hoisted to `logship` with a `source` label
- [ ] `logship.AttrAction` = `opnsense.action`, binary `pass`|`block`, hoisted by the sink
- [ ] All five lanes map to `opnsense.action` via explicit allowlist; unknown → unset, with a table test proving it
- [ ] `ObserveZenarmor` counters on bounded dims only — no IP/port/hostname/MAC/ja3/session_id/community_id/conn_uuid/app_name/uri/query
- [ ] Receiver self-o11y: bulk requests, docs per family, bytes, parse errors, rejections, unhandled hits
- [ ] `--logs.zenarmor.*` flags, off by default, requires `--logs.enabled`
- [ ] Enrichment never calls `miss` (flows are overwhelmingly external — would refresh on every internet-bound flow)
- [ ] Nothing on the receive path makes a network call
- [ ] Tests use **real documents from the 2,824-doc capture**, inline per convention
- [ ] `make test` + `golangci-lint run ./...` + `make docs-check` + `make grafana-check` all green
- [ ] Grafana panels for new metrics (coverage gate enforces)
- [ ] Docs page + `make docs` regenerated

## Follow-ups (not this issue)

- **Adaptive Logs exemption.** Adaptive Logs is active and sampling the tenant. Sampling forensic data defeats the SIEM goal. `gcx logs adaptive exemptions` 401s — the access policy lacks `adaptive-logs:admin`.
- **Tenant `otlp_config`** needs `opnsense.action` adding (3rd promoted key; cap 30; PUT fully replaces — GET-merge-PUT).
- **DNS overlap guard** vs `--logs.unbound.enabled` (both ship per-query DNS; unbound lane not currently running). Precedent: `logs_syslog.go:233`.
- **Retire `zenarmor_servicelog`** Alloy noise.
- **31d Loki retention** is the real ceiling on Loki-as-SIEM.

comments.body:
## Progress: cross-cutting seams landed (3/9 tasks)

Plan written, self-reviewed, then adversarially reviewed by a fresh Opus agent — which found 4 critical and 9 major defects, including one real bug I would otherwise have shipped (see below). Plan corrected before any code was written.

**Landed:**

- `c990cc7` **feat(logship)!: source-label the receiver self-metrics** — the startup-panic fix. `logs_parse_errors_total`/`logs_rejected_total` hoisted into `logship` as a shared source-bound `ReceiverMetrics`, registering via `Register`+`AlreadyRegisteredError` so several receivers share one registry. BREAKING: both metrics gain a `source` label; `sum by (stage)`/`sum by (reason)` unaffected.
- `19d407b` **feat(logship): add opnsense.action** — binary `pass`/`block`, hoisted onto the OTLP resource for Loki promotion. Also counts the sink's resource-cap degrade path (`logs_resource_capped_total`), which drops a record's `opnsense.*` labels while still shipping it — silent label loss that made label-scoped queries under-report. That path was previously commented "unreachable"; `action` takes the key count from ~25 to ~44 of 64, so it is not unreachable any more.
- `1060108` **feat(logship): map every lane's disposition onto opnsense.action** — filterlog, unbound, suricata, crowdsec and ids.

**Adversarial-review findings worth recording:**

- **`main.go:632` gates enrichment on `syslogEnabled && syslogCfg.Enrich`** — the only thing setting `deps.Cache`/`deps.Miss`. A zenarmor-only box would fall back to a cold cache and every enrichment lookup would miss *forever, silently*, with `--logs.zenarmor.enrich` defaulting to `true`. Fixed in Task 8.
- **`ids.go:191` is a fifth action-bearing lane** the design missed. `--logs.ids.enabled` + `--logs.zenarmor.enabled` is legal, so omitting it would leave IDS blocks out of `{opnsense_action="block"}`. Now included.
- **`crowdsec.go:242` is `d.Action`, not `d.Type`**; crowdsec has two record builders and only the *decision* one gets a disposition (an alert is an observation).
- Cleared as false alarms: no import cycle; no existing test asserts the old unlabelled metric output; `sum by (stage)` genuinely survives.

**Deviation from the design, consciously:** the spec said to settle Zenarmor's handshake tail with a second live capture. Instead the receiver keeps an in-memory index registry (404 before create, 200 after) and behaves like a real ES — correct under *either* path Zenarmor takes, and no second production mutation.

Gate green on every commit: `go test ./...` + `golangci-lint run ./...`.

Remaining: `ObserveZenarmor` + collector (4), the zenarmor package (5-7), options/main wiring (8), docs + Grafana panels (9).

## Shipped — 8 commits, `c990cc7`..`9e217a8`

Gate green on every commit: `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `make docs-check`, `make grafana-check` (765/765 catalogue metrics covered). 55 tests in the new package.

| commit | |
|---|---|
| `c990cc7` | `feat(logship)!` source-label the receiver self-metrics — the startup-panic fix |
| `19d407b` | `opnsense.action` + count the sink's resource-cap degrade path |
| `1060108` | map every lane's disposition onto `opnsense.action` |
| `a632f14` | `ObserveZenarmor` + `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total` |
| `02edcdc` | the receiver itself |
| `6d0cbae` | `--logs.zenarmor.*` + the enrichment-gate fix |
| `e312922` | HAProxy `status_class` fix (#277) |
| `9e217a8` | docs + dashboard panels |

## Correction to this issue's body

**The metric is `opnsense_log_events_zenarmor_total`, not `opnsense_exporter_log_events_zenarmor_total`.** There are two namespaces: collector metrics use `opnsense_*` (`internal/collector/collector.go:19`), self-metrics use `opnsense_exporter_*`. The issue body, the design and the plan all had this wrong; the code and docs are right.

## What real bugs this turned up

- **`main.go:632` enrichment gate** — asked only about syslog, so a zenarmor-only box would miss every enrichment lookup forever, silently, while `--logs.zenarmor.enrich` defaulted to true. Fixed in `6d0cbae` with a regression test on the predicate.
- **HAProxy `status_class` empty since it shipped** (#277) — `derive.go` read `http.status_code`, `haproxy.go` wrote `http.response.status_code`. Both now share a const. Every other family's parser/deriver key pairs were cross-checked; no siblings.
- **The sink's resource-cap degrade path was silent** — it drops a record's `opnsense.*` labels while still shipping it, so label-scoped queries under-report with nothing saying so. Its comment claimed the cap was "unreachable"; `action` takes the key count from ~25 to ~44 of 64. Now counted and warned once.

## Things the design got wrong, found against real payloads

- `domain_category` does not exist. dns sends `domain_categories` (an **array**); tls/http send `category` (a string). Reading one key would have left the label silently empty on two of six families.
- Only `conn` carries `end_time` — dns, tls and http have `start_time` only.
- HTTP status is `status_msg`, not `status`.
- `is_blocked` is decoded as `*int`: absent leaves `opnsense.action` **unset** rather than claiming `pass`, so a document that never stated a verdict cannot corrupt `{opnsense_action="pass"}`.

## Remaining follow-ups (not blocking, not done)

1. **Adaptive Logs is sampling this tenant.** Sampling forensic data defeats the SIEM goal. `gcx logs adaptive exemptions` 401s — the access policy needs `adaptive-logs:admin`. **This one matters most.**
2. **Tenant `otlp_config` needs `opnsense.action` adding** or the third label is emitted but not indexed. Deliberately not done automatically: `PUT` fully replaces (GET-merge-PUT), it takes ~2 business days to apply, and a botched replace would drop the two existing promotions.
3. DNS overlap guard vs `--logs.unbound.enabled` (latent — that lane isn't running).
4. Retire the `zenarmor_servicelog` Alloy noise (~62 lines/sec of engine diagnostics).

## Follow-up 2 done: `opnsense.action` submitted for promotion

Self-serve config request **`3838c86f`**, `HTTP 200`, status **pending** — expect it applied within ~2 business days, after which `{opnsense_action="block"}` becomes a stream selection rather than a scan.

GET-merge-PUT, as required, since the PUT replaces the whole `otlp_config` subtree:

```yaml
otlp_config:
  resource_attributes:
    attributes_config:
      - action: index_label
        attributes: [opnsense.subsystem, opnsense.source, opnsense.action]
```

Verified after the write:

- **The two existing promotions survived** (`opnsense.subsystem`, `opnsense.source`) — the actual risk of a full-replace PUT.
- **`retention_period: 31d` and `max_query_lookback` are untouched.** Worth recording: "PUT fully replaces" means the `otlp_config` **subtree only**, not the whole limits block. GET-merge-PUT is still mandatory *within* otlp_config — a PUT listing only `opnsense.action` would silently drop the other two.
- `ignore_defaults` left unset, so Loki's distributor defaults (`service.name`, `service.instance.id`) stay promoted. Three of the 30-attribute cap used.

Until it applies, `opnsense.action` is emitted on the resource but lands in structured metadata — so it is filterable with `| opnsense_action="block"` today, just not indexed. Nothing is lost in the meantime.

Adaptive Logs (follow-up 1) is with @rknightion.

## Live and validated end to end

Zenarmor is now streaming to <host-1> (`http://<lan-ip-1>:9200`). First hour, measured rather than assumed:

- **76,225 records / ~49 per second / 139 MB** across 4,732 `_bulk` requests
- **Zero parse errors, zero drops, `logs_resource_capped_total 0`**, queue steady at 0/4096
- 77,863 lines in Loki over the same window, so nothing is lost in flight
- The one `logs_rejected_total{reason="peer",source="zenarmor"}` is my own test curl being correctly refused by the allowlist

Every trap the design called out held up against real payloads: `domain_categories[0]` → `domain_category`, `resp_code` → `rcode`, `is_blocked: 0` → `action=pass`. Enrichment is adding what Zenarmor doesn't know (`ixl0` → `interface_name: LAN`, `src_scope`, `dst_service`) on top of what it does (device vendor/OS/MAC/hostname).

**`opnsense.action` promotion has applied** (request `3838c86f`) — much faster than the ~2 business days quoted. `{opnsense_action="block"}` is a real stream selector now, not a scan. Follow-up 2 is done.

**Adaptive Logs** — handled separately; it is not currently dropping Zenarmor (Loki's count matches what we shipped). Follow-up 1 is done.

## Two findings

**Nothing is ever blocked.** Every stream and all 76 counter series are `action="pass"`; there is no `block` stream. Not a bug — `is_blocked` is read faithfully — but either nothing has tripped a policy, or the policies are effectively report-only. Worth knowing, because it makes block-oriented panels look broken when they are honest.

**The receiver observes its own ingest** — filed as #278. Zenarmor inspects the link our `:9200` listener sits on, so it reports the `_bulk` POSTs delivering its own records: 76% of the `web` family, 11% of `flow`, **~15% of all volume** (~12k records/hour, ~600-900 MB/day). It converges rather than running away, but the `web` family is unusable without filtering.

## Dashboard

A Loki SIEM dashboard now covers what the metrics deliberately cannot — which domain, which device, which application: `opnsense-zenarmor` in `gc-gitsync-m7kni` (`6d87efa`), 17 panels over DNS / TLS / Web / Applications, plus raw records. Hand-authored rather than generated: this repo's `grafana/` builder is Prometheus-only, and its README already says log panels belong in a separate dashboard.

## End-to-end exporter smoke

- `opnsense_up` = 1 ✅
- all 59 sub-collectors succeeded ✅
- 617 distinct `opnsense_*` metric names (floor 480) ✅

Triaged in dfd73ee. **All 7 findings are box state — zero upstream drift, zero code changes.**

| Finding | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `healthCheck` `subsystems` | box state | exempted |
| `ipsecSad` `rows[].addtime_diff` | box state | **not** exempted — fix the testbed |
| `ipsecSad` `rows[].addtime_hard` | box state | **not** exempted |
| `ipsecSad` `rows[].addtime_soft` | box state | **not** exempted |
| `ipsecSad` `rows[].reqid` | box state | **not** exempted |
| `ipsecSad` `rows[].state` | box state | **not** exempted (also unconsumed) |
| `nginxVts` `cacheZones` | box state | exempted |
| `siproxdRegistrations` absent | plugin-gated | correct as reported, no action |

**`healthCheck subsystems`** — `SystemController::statusAction()` assigns `$response['subsystems']` only inside `if ($statuses)`, so a box where nothing is reporting omits the key. The blob is identical on `master`, `stable/26.1` and `stable/25.7` (`ea83f28a`) and untouched since 2025-01-21 — there is no drift here at all. #235 flagged it, #243 didn't, and this run flagged it again purely because the box's health flipped. Exempted.

**`nginxVts cacheZones`** — vts writes the key, calls `display_set_cache()`, then rewinds the buffer wholesale if nothing was written, so the key vanishes when its shm holds no cache node (and the shm resets on every nginx reload). The box *has* a cache configured (`settings/get` → `/var/nginx/cache/heavy`) but has served nothing through it. Exempted, with a prune trigger pointing at the testbed rather than a release.

**`ipsecSad` — deliberately NOT exempted.** The box has zero live kernel SAs: the single row is the synthetic `No SAD entries.` placeholder that `FetchIPsecSAD` already discards (`src="No"`, `dst="SAD"`, `nat="ntries"`), corroborated by `search_phase1` reporting the test tunnel `connected: false`. Four of those five fields back exported series (`ipsec_sa_age_seconds`, `_lifetime_hard_seconds`, `_lifetime_soft_seconds`, and `reqid` as a label), so exempting them would permanently blind the canary to real drift on consumed fields. **This is a testbed regression** — the traffgen LXC's strongSwan tunnel is down; #243 had `ipsecSad` clean.

### Two things this triage turned up

**1. The 26.1.11 health model is built on a false premise → #284.** Chasing `healthCheck subsystems` showed that upstream *never* populates `metadata.subsystems` — it is set to `[]` at line 79 and never written again; the only per-subsystem map is the top-level one. So what `0bda657` modelled as two *generations* are two *box states* of one unchanged endpoint, and two fixtures encode a shape no OPNsense build emits. Not a live bug (`AllSubsystems()` merges both and top-level wins), but the model is wrong and misleads triage. Filed as #284; the wrong ledger note is corrected in this commit.

**2. The verdict taxonomy has a gap.** CLAUDE.md mandates exactly one of absorb/chase/drop/opportunity, but **all four presuppose upstream drift**. The ledger already carries five box-state entries (`dechwPowerStatus`, `vnstatGetJsonData`, `interfacesOverview rows[].sfp`, `systemResources memory.arc`, `ipsecSad rows[].nat`) that fit none of them, and box state is now the majority class — 7/7 here and 7/7 in #243. Worth adding a fifth verdict, **box-state**: *the box has nothing to report; exempt with a prune trigger, or fix the testbed — never a code change*. Without it, triage gets pushed toward force-fitting "drop" onto a live tunnel that merely fell over. Happy to do that CLAUDE.md edit if you want it.

**Testbed follow-ups** (both would restore real coverage rather than mask it): bring the traffgen LXC's strongSwan tunnel back up, and point it at a cached nginx location so the vts cache zone materialises. An optional `cmd/apidrift` hardening would make the ipsecSad class self-healing: `FetchIPsecSAD` already drops the placeholder row, but the probe doesn't, so "no SAs" surfaces as 5×Missing instead of Unverified.

body:
## Summary

`service.version` is promoted from the OTel resource to a **`service_version` label on every metric series** (see the `telemetry` package — the build-info catalog doc notes "the service version is promoted from the resource as `service_version`"). Per the OTel→Prometheus compatibility spec this is a deviation: version belongs on an **info metric** (`target_info` from the resource, or the existing `*_build_info` gauge), **never as a label on every series**.

## Why it matters (even though this repo doesn't visibly break)

Only `service.name`(+`service.namespace`)→`job` and `service.instance.id`→`instance` are meant to become labels; every other resource attribute — including `service.version` — goes to `target_info` by the spec. Putting version on every series means **each new build mints a whole new series set**; during the query-lookback window after a redeploy, the old-version and new-version series coexist, and any `sum`-style panel adds both → a transient multiplier.

This repo runs **stable release tags**, so it rarely restarts onto a *different* version and the artifact stays invisible — but it's the same anti-pattern, and it inflates active-series cardinality by the number of versions ever seen. (It surfaced loudly in the sibling `graph2otel`, which runs the `:main` per-commit build — see rknightion/graph2otel#104, which has the full OTLP→Prometheus spec analysis.)

## Change

- Keep `service.version` on the OTel **resource** (semconv-correct → flows to `target_info`).
- Stop promoting it to a per-series label; rely on the existing `*_build_info{version=...}` gauge (and/or `target_info`) for version, joined via `group_left` where a panel needs it.
- Audit dashboards/alerts for any query that aggregates over or filters on `service_version` and repoint them at the info metric.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `service_version` no longer appears as a label on ordinary metric series (only on `target_info` / `*_build_info`)
- [ ] Version remains queryable via the build-info gauge (+ a documented `group_left` example)
- [ ] Dashboards/alerts updated if any referenced `service_version`
- [ ] Note the OTLP→Prometheus resource-attribute convention in the telemetry package docs

Cross-repo consistency with rknightion/graph2otel#104 (which carries the detailed spec citations).

comments.body:
## Verified against the live tenant — the conclusion holds, the stated mechanism does not

Checked the premise before implementing. Summary: **the label really is there, but not for the reason this issue gives, and the fix is not in this repo.**

### The label is real (confirmed)

```
opnsense_gateways_status{
  address="<pub-ip-1>", default_gateway="true", instance="opnsense",
  job="opnsense-exporter", name="AAISP_PPPOE", opnsense_instance="opnsense",
  service_instance_id="opnsense", service_name="opnsense-exporter",
  service_version="0896994"
}
```

`service_version` is on ordinary series, not just `build_info`. So the core complaint stands.

### But this repo never promotes it

The issue points at the `telemetry` package and quotes a build-info catalog doc saying "the service version is promoted from the resource as `service_version`". **That string does not exist in this repo** — not in the tree, not anywhere in history (`git log -S`). It came across from rknightion/graph2otel#104.

What the code actually does is already what this issue asks for:

- `internal/telemetry/resource.go:31` puts `service.version` on the **OTLP resource** and nowhere else.
- `internal/telemetry/provider.go` exports via the Prometheus bridge producer. Resource attributes go to `ResourceMetrics.resource`; they are never merged into datapoint attributes.
- There is no code path in this repo that writes a `service_version` label.

Proof it is not us: `tailscale2otel`, a completely separate codebase pushing OTLP to the same tenant, shows the identical label set.

```
tailscale2otel_dedup_evictions_total{
  ..., service_instance_id="<host-1>", service_name="tailscale2otel", service_version="4ab2311"
}
```

### The actual mechanism: a Grafana Cloud default, not self-serve

Per [OTLP format considerations → Metrics](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/send-data/otlp/otlp-format-considerations/#metrics), Grafana Cloud **automatically promotes** a fixed list of resource attributes to labels on every series, and `service.version` is on it:

> `service.instance.id`, `service.name`, `service.namespace`, `service.version`, `cloud.availability_zone`, `cloud.region`, `container.name`, `deployment.environment`, …

> To disable this option or to update this list, contact Grafana Labs Support.

**Not configurable self-serve** — unlike the Loki `otlp_config` promotion list (#276). That matters, because it means acceptance criterion 1 and the "keep `service.version` on the resource" instruction in this issue are **mutually incompatible on Grafana Cloud without a support request**: anything named `service.version` on the resource gets promoted. Pick one.

### The impact assessment was backwards

The issue says:

> This repo runs **stable release tags**, so it rarely restarts onto a *different* version and the artifact stays invisible

That is not what is deployed. <host-1> runs `ghcr.io/rknightion/opnsense-exporter:main` under watchtower, so the version is a git short SHA and turns over on **every commit**:

- **19 distinct `service_version` values in 30 days**
- **12,332 active series** on `job="opnsense-exporter"`

So the artifact is not invisible here — it is more pronounced than in the sibling repo the analysis came from.

Worth naming the sharpest edge, which the issue does not: without the version label a restart is a plain counter reset on one series, and `rate()` handles resets correctly. **With** it, a restart mints a brand-new series instead, so `sum(rate(...))` adds a decaying old series to a rising new one and transiently over-reports — ~19 times a month, for the lookback window each time. The label makes restart handling worse, not just noisier.

### What is already satisfied

- **AC2 (version stays queryable):** yes. `opnsense_exporter_build_info{version, goversion, opnsense_instance}` exists and is already what the dashboard's Build Info panel reads. `target_info` also already carries `service_version`, so Grafana's documented join works today:
  ```promql
  opnsense_gateways_status * on(job, instance) group_left(service_version) target_info
  ```
- **AC3 (dashboards/alerts):** nothing to do. No query in `grafana/` references `service_version`.

### Options

1. **Support request** — ask Grafana to drop `service.version` from the promote list for the tenant. Keeps semconv, keeps `target_info`, removes the per-series label, and fixes graph2otel#104 and tailscale2otel at the same time. Tenant-wide.
2. **Stop putting `service.version` on our resource** — in our control, no ticket, but it also disappears from `target_info` and deviates from semconv. Version stays available via `build_info`.
3. **Accept and document** — leave it, note the convention and the join.

Independently of the above: pinning <host-1> to release tags rather than `:main` would cut the churn from ~19/month to roughly per-release, which is where most of the actual cost is.

Not implementing anything yet — the choice between 1 and 2 is a real fork and 1 has cross-repo blast radius. Parking for a decision.

Closed as **accept + document** (`eee3006`), per the analysis above: the promotion is a Grafana Cloud gateway default, not something this exporter does or can prevent, so there was no code fix to make here. Filing a support request to alter the tenant's promote list was considered and declined — the churn is not worth it, and <host-1> deliberately stays on `:main` for per-commit deploys.

What landed:

- **`internal/telemetry/resource.go`** — the const block now states the OTLP→Prometheus convention (`service.name`→`job`, `service.instance.id`→`instance`, everything else to `target_info`), that version is exposed Prometheus-natively on `build_info`, and that Grafana Cloud deviates by promoting `service.version` to every series. It explicitly warns not to read a `service_version` label in a Grafana Cloud query as evidence this package emits one, and says to check a second app on the tenant first — which is the trap this issue fell into.
- **`docs/configuration.md`** — new "Resource attributes and `service_version`" section under OTLP metrics export, covering the same ground plus the one real consequence for per-commit deploys, and both ways to read the version back.

On the acceptance criteria as written:

- **AC1** — not done, deliberately. It is unachievable from this repo while `service.version` stays on the resource, which the same issue also requires.
- **AC2** — already true. `opnsense_exporter_build_info{version, goversion, opnsense_instance}` exists and the dashboard's Build Info panel already reads it. The `group_left` example is documented and verified live:
  ```promql
  opnsense_up * on(job, instance) group_left(service_version) target_info
  ```
- **AC3** — nothing to do; no query in `grafana/` referenced `service_version`.
- **AC4** — done, in both the package and the configuration page.

One correction worth carrying to rknightion/graph2otel#104, which this issue was derived from: the analysis there attributes the label to the application's own telemetry code. That is wrong for this repo and, given `tailscale2otel` shows the identical label set on the same tenant with an unrelated codebase, likely wrong there too. Grafana Cloud promotes `service.version` by default for any OTLP source. Whatever #104 concludes, it is not a code bug.

Gate: build, `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `make docs-check` all green.

title: Don't promote service.version to a per-series metric label (OTLP→Prometheus: version belongs on target_info/build_info)

Follow-up to #268. Make Pyroscope push the full profile-type set by default, matching the same change on tailscale2otel.

## Changes

- [x] All standard profile types on by default: cpu, alloc/inuse memory, goroutines, **and mutex/block** (previously mutex/block were opt-in via `--pyroscope.enable-mutex-block`).
- [x] Add **goroutine-leak** profiling (`ProfileGoroutineLeak`), which needs the Go `goroutineleakprofile` runtime experiment. Wire `GOEXPERIMENT=goroutineleakprofile` into every build path (Makefile, Dockerfile, GoReleaser). Verified it cross-compiles cleanly across the full release matrix (linux/darwin/windows/freebsd/openbsd × amd64/arm64).
- [x] Runtime guard: `profileTypes` appends `goroutineleak` only when `pprof.Lookup("goroutineleak") != nil`, so a binary built without the experiment cleanly omits it instead of pushing an empty/erroring profile.
- [x] **Breaking:** rename the operator escape hatch `--pyroscope.enable-mutex-block` (default off) → `--pyroscope.disable-mutex-block` (default off = contention profiling ON), following the repo `disable-*` convention for default-on features. Env `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_PYROSCOPE_DISABLE_MUTEX_BLOCK`.
- [x] Runtime mutex/block sampling knobs applied by default (skipped when disabled).
- [x] Tests updated (availability-guard aware); docs regenerated.

## Overhead note

mutex/block: negligible for this I/O-bound, per-scrape workload — mutex only costs on contended unlocks; block adds a per-blocking-event timestamp read (real cost only in channel-hot loops, which this is not). goroutine-leak: a short periodic STW at each upload interval, cheap for the exporter's modest goroutine count. Operators who want the contention profiles off can set `--pyroscope.disable-mutex-block`.

comments.body: Shipped in fec8915. All profile types default-on (cpu/memory/goroutines/mutex/block + goroutine-leak via GOEXPERIMENT); `--pyroscope.enable-mutex-block`→`--pyroscope.disable-mutex-block` (breaking). Full gate green in both build modes; release matrix cross-compiles with the experiment.
Correction: the opnsense commit SHA is `f5ab4d8` (my previous comment mistakenly pasted the tailscale2otel SHA). Change and gate status stand as described.

title: Pyroscope: collect all profile types by default, incl. goroutine-leak (GOEXPERIMENT)

body:
Goroutine profiles are absent on the <host-1> deployment, whereas tailscale2otel (same pyroscope-go SDK) reports them.

## Root cause

In `internal/profiling/profiling.go`, `pyroscope.ProfileGoroutines` is bundled into the `enableMutexBlock` branch alongside the mutex/block profiles, so it is only pushed when `--pyroscope.enable-mutex-block` is set (default `false`). <host-1> runs the default, so no goroutine profile ever gets uploaded.

That bundling is wrong. Goroutine profiling is a plain stack snapshot with essentially zero overhead and needs **no** runtime knob. Only mutex and block profiling need the process-global `runtime.SetMutexProfileFraction` / `runtime.SetBlockProfileRate` rates — which is the actual reason those two are gated. tailscale2otel keeps `ProfileGoroutines` in its always-on base set for exactly this reason.

## Fix

- [ ] Move `ProfileGoroutines` into the always-collected base set in `profileTypes()`; leave mutex/block gated behind `EnableMutexBlock`.
- [ ] Reword the `--pyroscope.enable-mutex-block` flag help + comments (goroutine is no longer gated by it) — "mutex/block profiling", not "goroutine/mutex/block".
- [ ] Update `profiling_test.go` (default set now includes goroutines).
- [ ] `make docs` to regen the flag tables + fix the architecture.md profiling prose.

No config change needed on <host-1> — the default set will start emitting goroutine profiles after this ships.

comments.body:
Fixed in 31d2aa7 (pushed to `main`).

`ProfileGoroutines` moved into the always-collected base set in `profileTypes()`; mutex/block stay gated behind `--pyroscope.enable-mutex-block`. Flag help + architecture.md prose reworded, `profiling_test.go` updated (default set now asserts goroutines present and mutex/block absent). Full gate green: `go test ./...`, golangci-lint, `make docs-check`.

No <host-1> config change needed — the default profile set now emits goroutine profiles, so they'll appear once the new image is deployed.

body:
Follow-up from the semconv-alignment research on the syslog log pipeline. Implementing the high-value, spec-Stable subset; holding the Development-stage and breaking-heavy items.

## Done (this change)
**A — fix retired pre-1.0 HTTP names in `haproxy.go`** → semconv Stable:
- `http.status_code` → `http.response.status_code`
- `http.method` → `http.request.method`
- `http.target` → `url.path`
- `http.version` → `network.protocol.version` (value stripped of the `HTTP/` prefix)

**B — namespace the two custom OTLP resource keys** (collision-safety; enables clean Loki index-label promotion):
- `source` → `opnsense.source`
- `subsystem` → `opnsense.subsystem`

**C — cheap Stable/standard additions:**
- `network.type` (ipv4/ipv6) alongside `ip.version` (filterlog)
- `network.transport` (tcp/udp only) alongside `protocol` (filterlog)
- `user.name` dual-emitted alongside `auth.user` (sshd), `config_user`/`audit.user` (audit)
- `SeverityText` now set on OTLP log records alongside the numeric severity

## Follow-up (separate, operator action)
- **D** — promote `opnsense.subsystem` (+`opnsense.source`) to Loki index labels via the tenant `otlp_config` **after** this ships and redeploys (promoting before the rename is live would match nothing).

## Deliberately held (documented, not done)
- `src.ip`→`source.address` family: semantically right but Development-stability and highest-volume lane → dual-emit at most, later.
- Firewall-as-`host`-entity (OTel Entities model): experimental + trips Loki resource→label promotion. Roadmap.
- Metric name changes: none — Prometheus-first naming is compliant.
- Suricata underscore names / `peer.*` / `direction`: correctly custom, left alone.

Log-attribute keys are not part of the docgen/metrics catalogue, so no generated-doc churn.

Shipped and verified live on <host-1> (image `1ea8afd`).

**A–C done** — verified on real Loki data: firewall line now carries `opnsense_subsystem=firewall`, `opnsense_source=syslog` (bare `subsystem`/`source` absent), `severity_text=WARN`, `network_type=ipv4`, `network_transport=tcp`.

Unit tests passed (parser and sink tested separately); only querying live Loki after deploy caught it. Fixed by exporting `logship.AttrSubsystem` as the single source of truth.
