body:
Fast-follow from #230. The generic `diagnostics/log` reader's row timestamps are naive local-time strings with no offset, and the backend interprets `validFrom` in the box's local timezone. The diaglog source currently reads them as UTC (house convention) — correct on UTC boxes; on a box behind UTC it only causes redundant rescans (deduped), but on a box AHEAD of UTC it can skip events immediately after a cursor advance.

Fix sketch (from the #230 implementation notes): compute the box's true offset via the existing `dstAbbrevOffset`/`absUnixFromAbbrev` machinery in `opnsense/system_resources.go` (fed by `systemTime`), and apply it when converting row timestamps and building `validFrom`.

Acceptance: a simulated +02:00 box neither skips nor duplicates events across a cursor advance; UTC boxes unchanged; documented behavior updated in docs/log-shipping.md.

body:
## Why

The cross-version payload build (#236) captured live payloads from a 26.1.11 stable box and the 26.7 devel box. Several metric-worthy keys surfaced that the #227 audit (run 2026-07-12 against then-current sources) could not have caught: they exist only in the 26.1.11/26.7 payloads, and the `firmwareInfo` keys were additionally invisible until #236's `ForceAttemptHTTP2` fix made that endpoint probeable at all. Every surface below is an **already-fetched endpoint** — zero new API cost, struct extensions only. All keys are already acknowledged in `opnsense/testdata/schemas/exemptions.json` as `knownExtraTopKeys` (canary-quiet); implementing a surface means modeling the keys, removing its exemption entry, and running `make schemas`.

## Surfaces

### 1. tailscale — health warnings (the standout)

`tailscaleStatus` now serves `Health` — an array of live warning strings from the local client (e.g. update available, derp unreachable, key expiry). Proposed: `opnsense_tailscale_health_warnings` gauge (count only — the strings are unbounded text, never a label). `TUN` (bool) could fold into an existing info-style series if one exists; skip `TailscaleIPs`/`CurrentTailnet`/`ClientVersion` (info data, no operational signal).

### 2. firmware — inventory + remediation counts

`firmware` (core/firmware/status) now serves `all_packages` / `all_sets` (full available inventory) plus `downgrade_packages` / `reinstall_packages` alongside the `new_packages` / `upgrade_packages` we already count. Proposed: `downgrade_packages_count` + `reinstall_packages_count` gauges as siblings of the existing `new_packages_count` / `upgrade_packages_count` (`internal/collector/firmware.go:56-60`); optionally `available_packages_count` from `all_packages`. Note the endpoint serves a **state-dependent superset** (keys appear after a firmware check runs) — decode as pointers or tolerate absence; the response is cached (`--exporter.cache-ttl`, #193), so no extra API cost either way.

### 3. protocolStatistics — new tcp counters

- `statistics.tcp.syncookies.{sent-cookies,received-cookies,failed-cookies,spurious-cookies}` — the syncache cookie counters that moved out of `syncache.*` in 26.7 (typo fixed upstream: `receivd`→`received`). Never emitted before; 4 counters.
- `statistics.tcp.ecn.{sent-ect0-packets,sent-ect1-packets}` — send-side ECN, twins of the received-* counters we already emit.
- `statistics.tcp.ecn.{ace-ce-syn,ace-ect0-syn,ace-ect1-syn,ace-nonect-syn}` — FreeBSD 15 AccECN handshake counters (decoded already, unexported).
- `statistics.tcp.received-acks-for-data-{not-yet-sent,never-been-sent,being-too-old}` — the 26.7 three-way split of the legacy `received-acks-for-unsent-data` (which fed no metric).

All `json.Number`, all CounterValue. Present only on newer releases — absent keys must read as not-present, not zero-forever counters (pointer or presence check per the #236 pattern).

### 4. mbuf — buffer-exhaustion families

`memoryStatistics`/`systemMbuf` (26.1.11+) added `jumbo9-*`, `jumbo16-*` pool families, `packet-{count,free,failures,sleeps}`, `sendfile-*`, `sfbufs-{alloc-failed,alloc-wait}`. The operationally useful subset is the **failures/sleeps counters** (allocation pressure) and `sfbufs-alloc-failed`; the pool gauges mirror the existing jumbo-page set. Suggest failures/sleeps first, pool gauges only if the dashboard wants them.

### 5. pf — translate counter (verification only)

`pfStatsInfo` gained `info.counters.translate` (total+rate). `Counters` is already a `map[string]pfStatsCounterEntry` iterated into metrics (`opnsense/pf_statistics.go:25`), so this **flows through with zero code change** — the checkbox here is to verify the series appears on a ≥26.7 box and add it to the dashboard/alert consideration.

### 6. unbound — base-stat additions that work on default 26.7

New keys in the **non-extended** `data.total.num.*` set (so they populate even with `extended-statistics: no`, unlike everything gated in #236): `queries_wait_limit`, `queries_discard_timeout`, `queries_replyaddr_limit`, `dns_error_reports` (RFC 9567 error reporting), `requestlist.current.replies`, and the `total.num.dnscrypt.*` group. Proposed: counters for the four query-drop/limit counters and `dns_error_reports`; skip dnscrypt (nobody runs it via OPNsense) and `requestlist.current.replies` unless free.

## Binding notes

- All version-dependent: fields absent on older boxes must be presence-handled so counters don't emit as eternal zeros (#236 / #90 pattern — `ExtendedPresent` in `opnsense/unbound_dns.go` is the template for group-level gating; individual counters can use pointers).
- Zero new endpoints → no `defaultEndpoints`/contract/capture changes; only struct + collector + `make schemas` (remove the corresponding `knownExtraTopKeys` exemptions as each surface is modeled) + `make docs` + dashboard coverage (step 9).
- Aggregate only — no per-warning/per-package/per-IP label series (tracker #227 binding notes apply).

## Acceptance

- [ ] tailscale `health_warnings` gauge
- [ ] firmware downgrade/reinstall (± available) package count gauges
- [ ] tcp syncookies + sent-ect + acks-split (± AccECN) counters, presence-safe
- [ ] mbuf failures/sleeps counters for the new families, presence-safe
- [ ] pf `translate` counter verified flowing + dashboard consideration
- [ ] unbound base-stat drop/limit counters + `dns_error_reports`, presence-safe
- [ ] exemptions removed for every key modeled; `make schemas`; live canary stays 107/107 clean
- [ ] `make docs` + dashboard coverage gate green

Refs #227 (tracker), #236 (source of the captures and the tolerant-reader/presence patterns).

comments.body: Landed in f80174f. All six surfaces implemented: `opnsense_tailscale_health_warnings` (count only — warning strings never exported), firmware `downgrade`/`reinstall` package counts, protocol `tcp_ecn_packets_total{direction,mark}` (which also fixes a latent gap — the received-side ECN counters were decoded but never wired), `tcp_ecn_accecn_handshakes_total{mark}` (26.1.11+), `tcp_syncookies_total{result}` and `tcp_received_acks_for_data_total{reason}` (26.7+, presence-gated so they are absent-not-zero on 26.1), mbuf `sfbufs` alloc failures/sleeps folded into the existing maps, and the unbound base-stat drop/limit counters + `dns_error_reports_total` + `request_list_current{scope="replies"}` (populate even with extended-statistics off). pf `translate` confirmed already flowing with zero code change. Exemptions removed for every modelled key. Per-version presence/absence covered by table tests on every surface. Full gate green; dashboard coverage 654/654.

body:
## Why

The live-box canary (#195) filed its first genuine drift report (#235): OPNsense 26.7 (devel channel, GA imminent) reshapes several payloads the exporter consumes. Users upgrade slowly — the installed base will span 26.1 and 26.7 (and stragglers on 25.7) for a year or more, and fleets are mixed. So every fix must be **additive**: one binary parses all supported shapes, no configuration, no version sniffing.

This issue scopes the cross-version support build and tracks the triage of every #235 finding.

## Policy (binding for this and future drift)

1. **Support window: current stable + previous stable** (today 26.1 + 25.7; once 26.7 GAs: 26.7 + 26.1), best-effort older. Compat shims are pruned when a version leaves the window.
2. **Tolerant-reader pattern** — the `health_check.go` template: old and new fields side by side in the response struct, accessor methods resolve across shapes, per-version fixtures in table tests. Never replace a shape; add alongside.
3. **Feature-detect by payload shape, never by version number.** The version belongs in an info metric, not in control flow.
4. **`opnsense/testdata/schemas/exemptions.json` is the compat ledger.** The canary probes the 26.7 box, so every legacy (≤26.1) field we keep reports as "missing" there — each gets a `missingOK` exemption whose note names the shape generation and the prune trigger (e.g. `legacy ≤26.1 shape — prune when 26.1 leaves the support window`).
5. **Triage taxonomy** for every canary finding: **absorb** (retype → flex types, usually already handled) / **chase** (data moved → tolerant reader) / **drop** (data removed upstream → metric absent on new versions, CHANGELOG note) / **opportunity** (new data → roadmap #227, not a bug).

## Triage of #235

| Endpoint / finding | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `unboundDNSStatus` `data.*` restructured (`num`, `mem`, `msg`, `rrset`, `infra`, `key`, `unwanted`, `dnscrypt_*` gone; `thread0..N`/`total`/`time` remain) | **chase** | tolerant reader over both layouts; ~40 metric mappings affected |
| `healthCheck` legacy top-level + `metadata.*` subsystem fields missing on 26.7 | **chase (done)** — code already tolerant | verify with a real 26.7 fixture; exempt legacy paths |
| `memoryStatistics` + `systemMbuf` `mbuf-statistics.jumbop-*`, `mbuf-and-cluster`, `mbuf-max`, `percentage` gone | **drop** (confirm vs rename first) | keep fields for ≤26.1; exempt; CHANGELOG note |
| `ndpTable` `[].expire`, `[].type` gone | **drop** (labels go empty on 26.7) | keep fields; exempt |
| `pfStatsInfo` `current-entries.rate` gone; `pfStatisticsByInterface` `interfaces.*.interface` gone | **drop** (confirm) | keep fields; exempt |
| `protocolStatistics` tcp `ecn.*`, `received-acks-for-unsent-data`, `syncache.*cookies` gone | **drop or chase** — check for renames (upstream fixed the `receivd` typo?) | per investigation |
| `keaSubnets4` `rows[].%interface` gone | **drop or chase** (label source) | per investigation |
| New top-level keys: `interfaces.time`, `ipsecPools.leases`, `keaLeases4/6.interfaces+stats`, `nginxVts` server-info, `tailscaleStatus` extras | **opportunity** | `knownExtraTopKeys` exemptions to quiet the canary; metric candidates → #227 |
| `firmwareInfo` malformed chunked encoding (HTTP 0) | **investigate** | box-side bug vs transient; upstream report if real; prober tolerance if needed |

Ground truth for chase-vs-drop verdicts comes from structure captures on both boxes (26.7 test box + 26.1 prod box) — in progress.

## Deliverables

- [x] `unboundDNSStatus` tolerant reader: 26.1 and 26.7 fixtures both parse, all existing unbound metrics still populated on both shapes (where the data exists), tests per fixture
- [x] `healthCheck` 26.7 fixture test proving `GetMetadataSystemStatus` / subsystem health still resolve
- [x] exemptions ledger updated: every kept-legacy path exempted with a generation + prune note; every confirmed-new top-level key in `knownExtraTopKeys`
- [x] dropped-data CHANGELOG/docs note: which metrics/labels go absent on 26.7+
- [x] `docs/compatibility.md`: support-window policy + version/metric availability notes, wired into nav
- [x] CLAUDE.md: canary-drift triage recipe (taxonomy + exemption ledger rules)
- [x] `firmwareInfo` probe error root-caused; workaround or upstream report
- [x] `make schemas` regenerated; full gate green; `cmd/apidrift` against the 26.7 test box reports clean (or expected-only warnings); #235 closes on next scheduled canary run

## Non-goals

- New metrics from the new 26.7 keys (kea `stats`, `ipsecPools.leases`, nginx server info, tailscale extras) — those are #227 roadmap candidates.
- 25.7-specific regression testing (best-effort; no 25.7 box exists).

comments.body:
## Baseline captured from a live 26.1.11 box — major reframe of the #235 triage

Read-only structure capture of all 15 affected endpoints from an OPNsense **26.1.11_6** (current stable) box, compared against our structs/goldens. Key finding: **most of the "26.7 drift" is already live on 26.1.11** — our structs lag current stable, so these aren't future-proofing fixes, they're fixing metrics that are silently wrong/absent for current-stable users today. (The live canary never ran against 26.1 — the box moved to the devel channel the same day the canary shipped, so #235 was the first structural validation anywhere.)

### Already true on 26.1.11 (fix benefits current users NOW)

| Endpoint | Reality on 26.1.11 | Verdict update |
|---|---|---|
| `systemMbuf` / `memoryStatistics` | `jumbop-current/cache/total/max` → **renamed** `jumbo-count/cache/total/max` (+ new `jumbo-page-size`); `jumbop-failures`/`jumbop-sleeps` still exist; `mbuf-max`, `percentage`, `mbuf-and-cluster` gone; `mbuf-current/cache/total/failures/sleeps` present; big new families (`jumbo9-*`, `jumbo16-*`, `packet-*`, `sendfile-*`, `sfbufs-*`) | **chase (rename)** — jumbop gauges are reading zero on current stable; new families → #227 opportunity |
| `ndpTable` | rows carry only `intf`, `intf_description`, `ip`, `mac`, `manufacturer` — `expire`/`type` gone | **drop confirmed** (labels empty on ≥26.1.11; keep fields for older boxes) |
| `pfStatsInfo` | `current-entries` has only `total` — `rate` gone | **drop confirmed** — `Rate` reads zero on current stable |
| `pfStatisticsByInterface` | per-if keys are `cleared`, `in4/6_pass/block_{bytes,packets}`, `out…` — no `interface` key | **drop confirmed** |
| `protocolStatistics` | tcp `ecn.*` **renamed**: `ce-packets`→`received-ce-packets`, `ect0/1-packets`→`received-ect0/1-packets`, plus new `sent-ect0/1-packets`, `ace-*`, `congestion-reductions`, `handshakes`; `received-acks-for-unsent-data` gone; syncache `receivd-cookies`/`sent-cookies` still present on 26.1.11 | **chase (rename)** — ecn counters read zero on current stable |
| `keaLeases4/6` | top-level `interfaces` + `stats` keys already present | knownExtraTopKeys (not 26.7-new) |
| `interfaces` | top-level `time` key already present | knownExtraTopKeys |
| `tailscaleStatus` | `AuthURL`, `Health`, `TailscaleIPs`, `CertDomains`, etc. all already present | knownExtraTopKeys (never modeled) |
| `healthCheck` | top level is only `metadata` (`metadata.subsystems` = `[]`, `metadata.system.status` = number) | tolerant reader already handles it; legacy paths → missingOK |
| `firmwareInfo` | serves cleanly (≈350 KB) | 26.7 chunked-encoding failure is version-specific, not size |

### Still genuinely 26.7-specific (pending the 26.7 capture)

- `unboundDNSStatus`: 26.1.11 has BOTH the aggregated sections (`data.num/mem/msg/rrset/infra/key/unwanted/dnscrypt_*`) AND `data.thread0..N` + `data.histogram[]` + `data.total/time`. On 26.7 the aggregated sections vanish — need the 26.7 structure to see what survives (worst case most unbound detail metrics become drops rather than chases).
- syncache `receivd-cookies`/`sent-cookies` (present on 26.1.11, flagged missing on 26.7 — possibly the `receivd` typo got fixed upstream).
- `keaSubnets4` `rows[].%interface` (prod box runs no Kea v4 — cannot confirm from this baseline).
- `firmwareInfo` malformed chunked encoding.

Triage table in the issue body will be corrected as part of the build; priority of the rename chases (mbuf, ecn) is bumped since they affect current stable.

## firmwareInfo probe failure root-caused (not box flakiness)

lighttpd 1.4.84 on OPNsense 26.7 with `server.stream-response-body = 2` deterministically truncates the ~380 KB `core/firmware/info` response over **HTTP/1.1** chunked encoding (reproducible: `curl --http1.1` fails 3/3 at a fixed per-path byte offset; HTTP/2 succeeds 5/5). No server-side log — a pure connection-level cutoff.

Why only our canary hit it: `cmd/apidrift` and `cmd/apicapture` construct `http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: ...}` without `ForceAttemptHTTP2`, and Go silently disables HTTP/2 auto-negotiation whenever a custom `TLSClientConfig` is set without that flag — so both tools were speaking HTTP/1.1. The production client (`opnsense/client.go`) already sets `ForceAttemptHTTP2: true` and is unaffected; the only field exposure would be an intermediate proxy forcing the exporter onto HTTP/1.1.

Fix in flight: `ForceAttemptHTTP2: true` in both tools' transports (+ a conservative single retry in the prober for genuinely transient cases). Possibly worth an upstream OPNsense/lighttpd report — the truncation would bite any plain HTTP/1.1 API consumer of large endpoints; parking that pending Rob's call.

Also confirmed by the same investigation: tcp syncache cookie counters weren't removed in 26.7 — they moved to a new `statistics.tcp.syncookies.*` section (typo fixed upstream), and `received-acks-for-unsent-data` split into three finer counters. Neither ever fed an exporter metric (decoded-only), so no user-visible impact; ledger notes corrected accordingly.

## Shipped — all deliverables complete

Eight commits on main (`bd06b50`…`965f6fb`), closed by `965f6fb`:

**Wave 1 — fixes for current-stable users (26.1.11):** mbuf jumbo-page rename resolution (`bd06b50`), tcp ECN counter rename resolution (`1b78b94`), metadata.subsystems health detail (`0bda657`).

**Wave 2 — 26.7 + infrastructure:** unbound extended-statistics presence gating (`f25dae2`), subtree-prefix exemptions + the full compat ledger (`e207e3f`), ForceAttemptHTTP2 + transport retry for the canary tools (`0ba9482`), docs/compatibility.md + CLAUDE.md triage recipe (`feafbc6`), canary metric floor adjustment (`965f6fb`).

**Verification evidence:**
- Live canary against the 26.7 devel box: **107/107 endpoints clean** — zero breaking drift, zero missing paths, zero unexpected keys, zero probe errors (was 91 clean + 40 warnings + 1 probe error in #235).
- End-to-end exporter smoke against the same box: `opnsense_up=1`, **47/47 collectors green**, 495 metric names (the 12-name drop vs before is the unbound extended series correctly gated off instead of fabricated as zeros).
- Full gate green: build, entire test suite, golangci-lint (0 issues), `make docs-check`.

#235 closes automatically on the next clean scheduled canary run (06:47 UTC).

**Parked, awaiting Rob's call:** upstream report to OPNsense/lighttpd about the HTTP/1.1 stream-response-body truncation (bites any plain HTTP/1.1 consumer of large endpoints). **Known gap:** the test box currently has zero Kea leases, so the 26.7 per-lease row shape is unverified — the daily canary will flag it if it drifted; a traffgen kick would close it sooner. New-data opportunities (kea stats, firmware inventory, tailscale/nginx metadata, syncookies) noted for #227.

title: OPNsense live-box canary drift

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (#227), logs/events lane. Companion to #228 — the honest "when NOT to use the exporter" page. Source-verified against the syslog-ng templates/model, IDS suricata.yaml, Netflow model, and the beats/telegraf plugin models.

## What
A docs-site page: **the native log-export recipe** for OPNsense → Grafana Cloud (or any Loki), and the decision matrix between native paths and the exporter's log shipping.

## Content (research already done — write it up)
1. **Native syslog recipe**: one syslog-ng Target (System > Settings > Logging), TCP or TLS (client-cert supported), RFC5424 on, program filter (applications list incl. `filterlog`, `suricata`, `audit`, `dpinger`, `openvpn`, `kea-*`, `captiveportal`, plugin programs like `squid-*`) → **Grafana Alloy off-box** `loki.source.syslog` → `loki.process` routing on APP-NAME → `loki.write`. Link the community filterlog pipelines (rudimartinsen.com, roguesecurity.dev incl. geoIP). Note: run NO agent on the firewall — os-beats is Filebeat→Elasticsearch-only, os-telegraf has no Loki output, hand-installed Alloy/Vector are unsupported on OPNsense.
2. **Suricata**: the `syslog_eve` toggle ships full EVE alert JSON via syslog (alerts only; shares program/facility with engine logs — demux stage needed). Fastlog `syslog` toggle as the lightweight alternative.
3. **NetFlow**: native v5/v9 export (Reporting > NetFlow, samplicate fan-out to multiple collectors) → a flow pipeline (goflow2/akvorado/ntopng). Flow data does not belong in the exporter; the API only exposes pre-aggregated Insight data.
4. **Decision matrix**: native syslog wins on volume (enterprise filterlog rates), zero exporter state, and raw fidelity; exporter log shipping (#228+) wins on parsed/enriched records (rule labels, eve objects, audit fields, DNS block enrichment), no listener infra, pull-based single agent, and CrowdSec (which has NO syslog path). Rule: **pick one path per log type** — enabling both double-ships.
5. **Known gaps of the native path** (why the exporter lane exists): filterlog CSV is headerless with rule md5s only (no labels, OS ifnames); audit is one prose line (no structured fields); unbound per-query enrichment is DuckDB/API-only; captive portal sessions/VPN session tables are API-only.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Docs page added (make docs / doclint clean), linked from the log-shipping docs of #228
- [ ] Closing commit references this issue

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue). `docs/log-export-native.md`: syslog-ng Target → Alloy → Loki recipe (verified against current Alloy docs — loki.source.syslog listener, TLS, app-name routing via loki.process/stage.match, community filterlog pipelines linked), Suricata `syslog_eve` vs fastlog split with the shared-program-name demux gotcha, NetFlow v5/v9 native-only (no per-flow API exists or will), the per-log-type decision matrix (firewall/IDS/audit/gateway-CARP-portal-DHCP/unbound/crowdsec) with the binding pick-ONE-path rule, and the native path's known gaps. Cross-linked both ways with docs/log-shipping.md; nav wired. docs gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (#227), logs/events lane. Depends on the log-shipping foundation (#228); pairs with metrics issue #209. Source-verified against `OverviewController.php` + `stats.py`/`logger.py`.

## What
Opt-in pi-hole-style DNS query log to Loki: per-query records with block/policy enrichment unavailable anywhere else (syslog only has raw unbound daemon lines).

## Endpoint
`GET api/unbound/overview/search_queries` → DuckDB rows: `uuid`, `time` (epoch s), `client` (hostname-substituted where known), `family`, `type` (qtype), `domain`, `action` (Pass/Block/Drop), `source` (Recursion/Local/Local-data/Cache), `rcode`, `blocklist`, `dnssec_status` (+ controller adds category/policy).

## Hard limitations — the issue exists to encode these honestly
- **Weak cursor**: the time-range form requires `client`+`timeStart`+`timeEnd` together; without a client filter you only ever get latest-1000 (time DESC). Cursor = last seen `time` + `uuid` dedupe for same-second. At >100 qps, 1000 rows ≈ 10s of traffic → **sampling loss on busy resolvers is accepted and documented**; `logs_possible_gap_total` fires when a full page contains no previously-seen uuid.
- **Heavy backend**: each call spawns python+pandas+duckdb (~1s CPU on the box). Opt-in (`--logs.unbound.enabled`, default false), poll floor 15s.
- Requires Unbound reporting/statistics enabled; DuckDB retention is bounded — no historical backfill.
- Volume: homelab 5–100 qps is fine; enterprise resolvers should not enable this.

## Loki mapping
Structured metadata: `client, domain, qtype, action, source, rcode, blocklist, dnssec_status`. Body = compact JSON. Domains/clients NEVER become labels.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Enable reporting + DNSBL; capture `search_queries` shape (uuid format, hostname substitution, blocklist field) at known qps; measure poll cost
- [ ] Verify latest-1000 ordering and same-second uuid dedupe assumptions

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unbound query Source (opt-in) with time+uuid cursor and gap accounting; fixtures; self-metrics; docs with the sampling caveat front and center

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue). `unboundSource` behind `--logs.unbound.enabled` (default off, 15s floor). Confirmed live that `search_queries` without a client filter is a fixed newest-1000 window with `uuid` always null — so the cursor is lastTime + a same-second content-fingerprint dedup ring, window overflow counts the new `opnsense_exporter_logs_possible_gap_total{source}` self-metric (the deferred #228 metric, added additively to metrics.go) while still shipping visible rows, and the accepted-loss caveat is in the flag help + docs. Cold start seeds without emitting. Attribute note: Unbound's own `source` field ships as `query_source` — the pipeline reserves and strips the `source` key, which would have silently dropped it. Domains/client IPs are structured metadata only. New core POST endpoint (contract count 23) with captureRequests parity. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (#227), logs/events lane. Depends on the log-shipping foundation (#228); pairs with metrics issue #205. Source-verified against the crowdsec plugin controllers + `actions_crowdsec.conf`.

## What
Ship CrowdSec **alert and decision records** to Loki as security events. We already export counts; this adds the records — and there is NO native syslog path for them (the plugin registers no syslog scope; alerts live only in the LAPI).

## Endpoints (GET, os-crowdsec gated)
- `api/crowdsec/alerts/search` → `cscli alerts list -l 0 -o json` (full dump per call), controller-flattened rows: `id`, `value` (scope:ip), `reason` (scenario), `country`, `as`, `decisions` summary, `created`
- `api/crowdsec/decisions/search` → rows: `id`, `value`, `type` (ban/captcha), `scenario`, `duration`, `expiration`

## Cursor
None server-side — `id` is monotonic; diff client-side (ship ids > last seen). Easy and reliable; survives restarts with the state file.

## Volume / cost
Few–dozens of events/day; one cscli exec (full dump) per poll — fine at 60s. Endpoints already registered in `defaultEndpoints()` for the metrics collectors — reuse.

## Loki mapping
Structured metadata: `scenario, value, country, as, decision_type, duration`. Body = compact JSON.

## Caveat
Controller strips the rich LAPI fields (events, meta) — scenario/ip/country/duration is what's available; note it and move on. LAPI-down returns `{"message":"unable to retrieve data"}` HTTP-200 — reuse the nil-envelope handling from `opnsense/crowdsec.go`.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Trigger a decision (e.g. cscli decisions add) and capture both payloads; confirm id monotonicity assumptions

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CrowdSec Source with id-diff cursor; fixtures; self-metrics; docs; dashboard panel

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue). `crowdsecSource` behind `--logs.crowdsec.enabled` (default off, 60s poll floor): ships alert + decision records via the EXISTING crowdsecAlerts/crowdsecDecisions endpoints (no new keys). Cursor is a plain id-diff per kind (both server ids are monotonic), persisted via StatefulSource; cold start ships the current active set once. Live-verified correction to the issue: decision rows carry `action`/`expiration` (a remaining-duration string like "693h46m29s", not the guessed type/duration) and no absolute timestamp — stamped at emit. Body = compact JSON; attributes = scenario/value/country/as (+ decision_type/duration). Plugin-absent/daemon-down degrade silently. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (#227), logs/events lane. Depends on the log-shipping foundation issue; pairs with the metrics issue #203. Source-verified against `queryAlertLog.py` + IDS ServiceController.

## What
Ship full structured Suricata EVE **alert records** to Loki (the metrics issue #203 only ships aggregate gauges).

## Endpoint
`POST api/ids/service/query_alerts` — reverse-reads eve.json(.N), returns complete eve records that contain an `alert` key: `timestamp` (µs precision), `flow_id`, `in_iface`, `src_ip/src_port/dest_ip/dest_port`, `proto`, flattened `alert` (signature text), `alert_sid`, `alert_action`, app-layer metadata, plus `filepos` (byte offset) + `fileid`.

## Cursor
`(fileid, filepos)` is fragile across rotation (rename shifts fileids). Use the record **timestamp as the true cursor** with `flow_id + alert_sid` dedupe; treat filepos as an optimization only. (Upstream itself resumes by filepos in `get_alert_info` — offsets are line starts.)

## Native alternative — must be documented
The IDS model has `syslog_eve` (ships the identical EVE JSON via syslog, alerts only, metadata + community-id) and `syslog` (fastlog lines) toggles. Users on the syslog→Alloy path should flip `syslog_eve` instead; this source is opt-in for zero-listener setups. Beware: syslog EVE shares program `suricata`/local5 with engine logs (demux needed there — not our problem on the API path).

## Loki mapping
Structured metadata: `alert_sid, alert_action, src_ip, dest_ip, in_iface, proto, signature`. Body = compact JSON of the eve record. Never label by SID/IP.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Row field shapes with Suricata enabled + triggered alerts (timestamp format, filepos/fileid across an eve rotation)
- [ ] Response when IDS installed-but-disabled (200-empty vs error → error-handling decision; IDS is core so NOT PluginGatedEndpoints)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] IDS Source with timestamp cursor + flow_id/sid dedup ring; POST contract entry (shared with #203)
- [ ] Fixtures; self-metrics; docs incl. the syslog_eve alternative; dashboard panel

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue). `idsSource` behind `--logs.ids.enabled` (default off, 30s floor), reusing the existing `idsQueryAlerts` POST contract — no new endpoint. Body is the byte-for-byte compact EVE record (RawMessage decode, unmodelled fields included); attributes are alert_sid/alert_action/src_ip/dest_ip/in_iface/proto/signature (structured metadata, never labels); severity warn for blocked. Cursor is the record's own timestamp (filepos/fileid deliberately never consulted — they shift across rotation) with a flow_id+sid dedupe ring bounded to the cursor boundary. Window overflow (full 500-row read whose oldest row is still newer than the cursor) ships a synthetic `gap_detected` Warn record — queryable in Loki — rather than dropping silently. docs/log-shipping.md gained the IDS section incl. the syslog_eve native alternative. Full gate green.

title: feat(logs): IDS source — ship full Suricata EVE alert records

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (#227), logs/events lane. Depends on the log-shipping foundation issue. Source-verified against `LogController.php` (magic __call), `queryLog.py`, `log_matcher.py`, and the syslog-ng scope templates.

## What
One generic collector over `POST api/diagnostics/log/<module>/<scope>` = the whole event backbone. ~25 core + ~20 plugin scopes; records come back PARSED: `timestamp` (ISO, ms precision on RFC5424 files), `facility`, `severity`, `process_name`, `pid`, `line`.

This single source delivers, via scope selection:
- **audit** — config changes (`user X changed configuration to <revision> in <URI> <description>` from `Config::auditLogChange()`) + GUI login success/failure + sudo/sshd. Parse the config-change line into structured fields (username, revision, URI) with a small regex.
- **gateways** — dpinger latency alarms + gateway state transitions (no event API exists for these)
- **system** — kernel lines incl. CARP MASTER/BACKUP transitions
- **configd** — service lifecycle events
- **portalauth** — captive portal logon/logoff (the connect/disconnect feed; no dedicated event API)
- **kea / dnsmasq / dhcpd** — real DHCP lease events (DHCPACK etc.) — better than snapshot-diffing lease tables
- plus ipsec, openvpn, wireguard, suricata (daemon), resolver, monit, ntpd, and ~20 plugin scopes (haproxy, postfix, squid_access, named, nginx, routing_frr, ...)

## Cursor
`validFrom` (epoch) bounds the reverse scan; poll with `validFrom = last_seen_ts` and dedupe the boundary second client-side (ms precision keeps dupes bounded). Survives restarts.

## Config
`--logs.scopes` (list of module/scope pairs) — default to the high-signal event scopes: `core/audit, core/gateways, core/portalauth, core/system, core/configd`. Each scope = one configd exec per poll; 5–10 scopes @30s is cheap.

## Caveats
- POST (searchBase) → `postEndpoints` + golden-count bump. Page cap 9999.
- Do NOT use `.../live` SSE: it tails with `tail -f` (not `-F`) and **silently stalls after rotation** (keepalives continue, data stops).
- Native syslog ships all of these raw — the API adds parsing + pull-based collection with no listener. The docs must position this honestly (see native-recipe issue).

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Enumerate available module/scope pairs on 26.1; `validFrom` precision; server-side severity filtering?
- [ ] Capture audit config-change lines for the regex; kea DHCPACK lines; portalauth login lines

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Generic scope Source + validFrom cursor + boundary dedupe; scope allowlist flag
- [ ] Audit-line structured parsing; fixtures per scope
- [ ] Contract-manifest POST entry; self-metrics; docs; dashboard panel

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue). `diaglogSource` multiplexes every `module/scope` pair in `--logs.scopes` (default `core/audit,core/gateways,core/portalauth,core/system,core/configd` — kea/dnsmasq/dhcpd/plugin scopes addable without code changes) behind `--logs.diaglog.enabled`. Cursor mechanics verified live + against queryLog.py: `validFrom` is an INCLUSIVE epoch-seconds lower bound on a reverse scan (boundary record deduped client-side), rowCount server-clamps at 9999, 5-page/scope/poll cap with logged truncation, fresh scopes bootstrap to now. Audit config-change lines parse into `config_user`/`config_revision`/`config_uri`. The `/live` SSE variant confirmed architecturally broken for ingestion (tail -f of a resolved-once path — stalls on rotation), matching the landmines page. Known limitation documented in docs/log-shipping.md: naive local-time row timestamps are read as UTC (house convention) — tz correction filed as a fast-follow. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (#227), logs/events lane. Depends on the log-shipping foundation issue. Source-verified against `read_log.py` + `FirewallController.php`.

## What
Flagship log source: ship parsed, **rule-label-enriched** firewall events to Loki.

## Endpoint
`GET api/diagnostics/firewall/log?limit=N&digest=<md5>` → configd `filter read log` → `read_log.py`.

Record: full parsed filterlog — `rulenr, rid, interface, reason, action (pass|block|rdr|nat|binat), dir, ipversion`, proto fields, `src/dst/srcport/dstport`, tcpflags — plus `__timestamp__`, `__digest__` (md5 of raw line), and **`label`** (human rule description resolved from `rid` via /tmp/rules.debug). That label enrichment is the whole reason to use the API instead of native filterlog syslog (which ships headerless CSV with only rule md5s).

## Cursor — the good one
Pass `digest=<last seen>`: the backend reverse-reads the rotation-aware filter logs and stops at the digest; returns newest-first including the digest row (drop it client-side). Lossless unless >`limit` rows arrive between polls; `limit` default 1000, poll 10–30s. Persist digest via `--logs.state-file` for restart resume.

## Loki mapping
Structured metadata: `action, interface, dir, proto, src, dst, srcport, dstport, rid, rulenr, label`. Body = raw line. Never promote IPs/ports to labels.

## Caveats to document
- Filter log records a flow's FIRST packet only — event stream, not flow accounting.
- Enterprise boxes logging pass-rules (100s–1000s events/s) will melt API polling — recommend native syslog + Alloy pipeline for that class (see native-recipe docs issue); the exporter path targets homelab/SMB volumes.
- Do NOT use `stream_log` (SSE): it drops everything past 10 lines per 100ms window by design (`read_log.py:207-214`).
- qfeeds `search_events` is a filtered 300s-stale subset of this feed — qfeeds blocks appear here natively with their rule label; never build that endpoint.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Digest behavior when the digest has rotated out (full window? duplicate bound?)
- [ ] rows==limit without digest hit — infer-gap handling
- [ ] Poll cost at 5s/10s (configd spawn + rules.debug parse per poll)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Firewall `Source` with digest cursor + dedup ring; endpoint + query-param client support registered
- [ ] Label enrichment fields verified against live payloads; fixtures
- [ ] Self-metrics wired; docs (incl. volume guidance); dashboard panel for shipped/dropped

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue). `firewallSource` behind `--logs.firewall.enabled` (default off, 10s floor). Digest-cursor tailing of `diagnostics/firewall/log`: prime-at-newest first poll (ships nothing — honest resume-from-now), oldest-first shipping below the 1000-row cap, fixed digest ring for rotation-overlap dedup, cursor-not-in-batch → resume-from-newest + rate-limited gap warning (bounded, visible loss). StatefulSource persists the digest; a resumed cursor polls immediately. The server-resolved rule `label` ships as an attribute — the enrichment syslog cannot provide; IPs/ports/rids are structured metadata, never labels; body is compact JSON; block→Warn. New core GET `firewallLog` (query params built per-call so the live feed is never cached). Live-verified end-to-end on the dev box: prime shipped 0, next poll shipped 37 new rows with an advanced cursor and correct enrichment. docs/log-shipping.md gained the firewall section with volume guidance (enterprise pass-logging → native syslog per the decision matrix). Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (#227), logs/events lane. Architecture spike — research complete (repo internals + otel-go status + Loki OTLP ingestion verified); this issue is the foundation the per-source issues (firewall, diagnostics-log, IDS, crowdsec, unbound) build on.

## What
An opt-in background log/event pipeline in the exporter: poll structured events from the OPNsense API (with per-source cursors) and ship them to Loki — high-cardinality data that must never become metrics (per-flow firewall events, IDS alerts, audit lines).

## Sink decision
- **Primary: OTLP logs** (`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log` + `sdk/log` + otlploghttp/grpc). One sink covers both the Grafana Cloud OTLP gateway (`/otlp/v1/logs` → Loki) and self-hosted Loki 3.x native OTLP ingest. Reuses the existing `--otlp.*` transport family (endpoint/protocol/headers/TLS/mTLS/Grafana-Cloud shortcut) — needs a small refactor so transport config resolves without `--otlp.enabled` (metrics stay gated by that; logs gated by `--logs.enabled`), and the `/v1/logs` gateway-path fix analogous to #80's `/v1/metrics`.
- Honest caveat: the Go logs signal is pre-1.0 (`sdk/log` v0.20.0 beside the v1.44 line we vendor). Confine SDK imports to one package, pin + Renovate. Acceptable for an opt-in feature.
- **Secondary: `--logs.sink=stdout`** — one JSON line per event; k8s/container log collection ships it. ~50 lines; great debug path.
- **Rejected: Loki-native push client** — `grafana/loki-client-go` unmaintained, loki module graph unimportable for vendored builds, promtail EOL 2026-03; Loki 3.x takes OTLP directly so native push buys nothing.

## Collection model
New package `internal/logship` (peer of `internal/telemetry`), never a `CollectorInstance` — long-lived background loop, not scrape-time:
- Per-source poller goroutines implementing `Source{Name(); Poll(ctx) ([]Record, error)}`; all requests via the existing client choke point (retries, gzip, body cap, redaction, RequestObserver self-metrics for free). New endpoints registered in `defaultEndpoints()` (canary coverage); POSTs into `postEndpoints` + golden count.
- Client extension needed: query-param support (firewall log takes `?limit=&digest=`).
- Cursors per source (digest / validFrom / timestamp+dedup); in-memory by default (stateless; restart = resume from now), optional `--logs.state-file` (atomic JSON) for resume. Dedup ring per source absorbs rotation overlap.
- Bounded queue (default 4096) between pollers and emitter; drop-oldest + counter (we own the queue because the SDK BatchProcessor drops silently).
- Lifecycle: `logship.Start` returns `stop func(ctx)` like `telemetry.Start`; wired into the #161 graceful shutdown (drain HTTP → stop pollers → flush sink bounded → stop OTLP metrics). Lazy connect — dead endpoint never blocks startup.
- **SSE rejected as transport**: `stream_log` is lossy by design (throttle drops >10 lines/100ms incl. boundary), generic `/live` stalls silently on rotation (`tail -f` not `-F`). Polling-with-cursor wins on loss + reconnect; SSE at most a phase-3 firewall optimization always paired with digest catch-up.

## Loki label model (cardinality discipline)
- Resource attrs → labels: `service.name` (reuse `--otlp.service-name`), `service.instance.id` (= instanceLabel).
- Record attr `source` ∈ {firewall, ids, audit, ...} — structured metadata by default, promotable to a label via Grafana Cloud self-serve API / otlp_config.
- Everything high-cardinality (IPs, ports, SIDs, domains) = structured metadata / body, NEVER labels. Body = raw line (firewall/backend) or compact JSON (IDS); timestamp = the record's own.

## Config surface (`internal/options/logs.go`, mirrors otlp.go)
`--logs.enabled` (false) · `--logs.sink` (otlp|stdout) · `--logs.poll-interval` (10s, floor 5s) · `--logs.buffer-size` (4096) · `--logs.batch-max` (1000) · `--logs.state-file` ("") · per-source `--logs.<source>.enabled`. Env vars per `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_` convention; flags flow through docgen tables.

## Self-metrics (+ dashboard coverage-gate panels)
`opnsense_exporter_logs_shipped_total{source}` · `logs_dropped_total{source,reason}` · `logs_ship_errors_total` · `logs_poll_errors_total{source}` · `logs_last_event_timestamp_seconds{source}` (cursor lag) · `logs_queue_length`/`_capacity` · optional `logs_possible_gap_total{source}`.

## Delivery semantics (stated honestly in docs)
Within a run: at-least-once (cursor + dedup ring) degrading to counted-lossy under backpressure. Across restarts: at-most-once by default; state file → best-effort resume. Never exactly-once. Multi-replica = double-shipping — document one logs-enabled instance per firewall. Double-shipping vs native syslog: pick one path per log type (see the native-recipe docs issue).

## Phases
- **P0**: dev-box (#195) validation — digest-across-rotation behavior, truncation detection, queryAlerts field shapes + disabled-IDS response, log-scope inventory + validFrom precision, poll cost at 5s/10s, end-to-end Grafana Cloud OTLP logs check.
- **P1 (this issue)**: logship core + firewall source + OTLP/stdout sinks + options + self-metrics + docs + sync-vendor.
- **P2**: IDS + diagnostics-log sources, state file, gap metric. **P3 (demand)**: SSE optimization, crowdsec source, per-source intervals.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] P0 dev-box answers recorded here
- [ ] `internal/logship` + Sink(otlp,stdout) + options family + graceful-shutdown wiring
- [ ] Self-metrics + dashboard panels; docs page incl. delivery semantics + double-ship guidance
- [ ] `make sync-vendor` (3 otel log modules); full gate green

comments.body: Landed in 0a27446. `internal/logship`: poll → bounded drop-oldest queue (counted) → emitter → sink, all opt-in behind `--logs.enabled` (+ sink/poll-interval/buffer/batch/state-file flags). OTLP-logs sink reuses the `--otlp.*` transport via a new `OTLPTransport()` resolver that is NOT gated on `--otlp.enabled` (metrics gating unchanged), with the `/v1/logs` gateway path fix; stdout sink ships one compact JSON line per entry. Loki labels fixed at `service.name` + `service.instance.id`; `source` is a promotable record attribute; reserved keys are stripped off source records defensively. Delivery: at-least-once within a run, at-most-once across restarts (optional atomic state file, time-based save cadence), never exactly-once. The `Source`/`StatefulSource`/`IntervalSource` contract + `RegisterSource` factory idiom are frozen — #229–#233 code against them, each lane in disjoint files. Self-metrics + Log Shipping dashboard tab + docs/log-shipping.md. otel logs SDK v0.20.0 vendored, confined to sink_otlp.go. Scope note: the firewall source is #229 (parallel-build split) — this issue is the foundation only, zero OPNsense endpoints added.

title: feat(logs): log-shipping foundation — internal/logship pipeline with OTLP + stdout sinks (opt-in)

body:
## Mission
Roadmap of every metrics-worthy OPNsense API surface the exporter does not yet cover, plus an SSH spike for API-absent telemetry. One issue per surface; this tracker orchestrates them.

## Methodology (2026-07-12, reproducible)
Ran our own `tools/opnsense_api_contract/extract.py` (the apicontract parser) against fresh master clones of opnsense/core + opnsense/plugins: **2,404 endpoints across 93 modules**, diffed against our 107 covered paths → 741 uncovered metrics-plausible endpoints. 12 parallel research passes then read the actual PHP controllers, configd actions, and backend scripts for every candidate (no guessing from endpoint names), cross-checked against our existing collectors, and produced per-surface verdicts. A final straggler sweep covered the heuristic's blind spots and every dashboard-widget data source. Two independent passes converged on the same finds (unbound totals, relayd, dechw/dmidecode, tor) — good confidence in coverage.

## The roadmap

### High value / low cost — extend payloads we ALREADY fetch (zero new API cost)
- [x] #218 core — export ALL system-status subsystems (incl. disk space)
- [x] #219 monit — per-check resource telemetry (only disk-%-usage source in the exporter; blocked on payload capture)
- [x] #214 interfaces — LAGG member state, SFP/DOM optics, bridge membership
- [x] #212 openvpn — per-session traffic counters
- [x] #200 nginx — VTS cache zones / latency counters / reload timestamp (+1 small endpoint for bans)
- [x] #201 haproxy — show-stat latency/health fields (+1 endpoint for stick tables)
- [x] #208 kea — lease state/type, PD pools, pool utilization (mostly struct extensions)
- [x] #237 cross-surface — struct extensions from new 26.1.11/26.7 payload keys (tailscale health warnings, firmware inventory counts, tcp syncookies, mbuf exhaustion counters, pf translate, unbound base-stat drops) — added 2026-07-13 from the #236 live captures; keys post-date the 2026-07-12 audit

### New collectors — core subsystems
- [x] #203 ids — Suricata (largest uncovered core subsystem, 0/43 endpoints today)
- [x] #220 core — backup freshness + ZFS boot environments
- [x] #221 firewall — GeoIP freshness (+ optional NAT counts)
- [x] #222 auth — user/group/API-key posture counts
- [x] #223 hostdiscovery — persistent host inventory (hostwatch)
- [x] #207 captiveportal — voucher inventory
- [x] #213 ipsec — kernel SAD/SPD tables, lease detail, dirty flag
- [x] #209 unbound — DNSBL/qstats totals (opt-in; heavy backend)

### New collectors — plugins (all 404-gated)
- [x] #197 frr — BGP neighbor session detail (flap counters)
- [x] #198 frr — OSPF interface + OSPFv3 parity
- [x] #199 frr — route-table/LSDB volume gauges (opt-in)
- [x] #211 netbird — connectivity + per-peer telemetry
- [x] #204 clamav — signature DB freshness
- [x] #205 crowdsec — hub component health
- [x] #216 lldpd — neighbor table (topology sensor)
- [x] #215 vnstat — persistent traffic accounting (opt-in)
- [x] #217 hardware — dmidecode DMI info + dechw PSU status
- [x] #202 relayd — LB virtual server/table/host health
- [x] #206 tor — circuit/stream telemetry (opt-in)


### Logs / events lane (added 2026-07-12 — comprehensive observability beyond metrics)
Research: API event-source inventory + native-syslog baseline + shipping-architecture spike (three passes, source-verified). Key structural findings: the generic `api/diagnostics/log/<module>/<scope>` reader (~45 scopes) is the event backbone (audit/config-change, dpinger/gateway, CARP, portal-auth, DHCP daemon events — none have dedicated event APIs); the firewall log endpoint has a purpose-built md5-digest cursor AND rule-label enrichment syslog cannot provide; the SSE streams are disqualified as transport (stream_log drops lines by design; /live stalls on rotation); sink = OTLP logs reusing the existing `--otlp.*` transport (Grafana Cloud gateway + Loki 3.x both ingest OTLP natively).

- [x] #228 log-shipping foundation — internal/logship pipeline, OTLP + stdout sinks (opt-in)
- [x] #229 firewall log source — digest cursor + rule-label enrichment (flagship)
- [x] #230 generic diagnostics-log source — audit, gateways, CARP, portalauth, DHCP scopes
- [x] #231 IDS source — full Suricata EVE alert records
- [x] #232 crowdsec source — alert/decision records (no native syslog path exists)
- [x] #233 unbound source — per-query DNS log (opt-in, sampling caveats)
- [x] #234 docs: native syslog/NetFlow recipe + exporter-vs-native decision matrix

Binding notes for this lane: pick one path per log type (native syslog vs exporter — never both, double-ships); Loki labels fixed at service_name + service_instance_id (+ optionally `source`) — IPs/ports/SIDs/domains are structured metadata, never labels; delivery semantics are at-least-once within a run / at-most-once across restarts (state file optional), never exactly-once; NetFlow stays native (v5/v9 export) — the API has only pre-aggregated Insight data.

### Fixes / meta
- [x] #210 fix(unbound): migrate off deprecated isBlockListEnabled before OPNsense 26.7 (**time-sensitive**)
- [x] #226 docs: do-not-scrape landmines + confirmed-empty modules
- [x] #224 minor extension candidates (ntpd GPS, chrony NTS, siproxd, shaper last-match)
- [x] #225 spike: SSH channel for API-absent telemetry (ZFS pool health, CARP demotion, disk I/O)

## Binding notes (don't re-litigate)
- Per-plugin `service/status` endpoints are NOT worth collectors — `api/core/service/search` (covered) already exports running state for every registered plugin daemon. Verified against `plugins.inc.d/*.inc` across the fleet. See #226 for the full confirmed-empty list.
- Aggregate in the collector; never per-prefix / per-circuit / per-IP / per-domain / per-voucher-code label series. Sensitive material (voucher codes = usernames, otp_seed, API keys, MaxMind URL with license key, .onion hostnames) must never appear in labels — narrow structs, error-path redaction.
- Windowed backends (unbound qstats 7-day retention, IDS query_alerts saturation) are gauges, never counters.
- Every new plugin endpoint goes in `PluginGatedEndpoints()`; core endpoints must NOT (a cached 404 on a core route would mask real drift). POST endpoints need `postEndpoints` + golden-count bump — only IDS needs this so far; everything else proposed is GET.

## Dev-box (#195) shopping list — aggregate across all issues
os-frr (bgpd+ospfd+ospf6d+bfdd, peered with a companion FRR instance), os-nginx (vhost+upstream+proxy_cache+autoblock), os-haproxy (stick-table + http backend ×2 servers), os-relayd, IDS with ET Open + triggered alerts + rotated eve.json, os-clamav + freshclam run, os-crowdsec (collections, one tainted), os-tor (control port + hidden service), voucher auth server + group, Kea DHCPv6 + PD pool + PD client, unbound stats + DNSBL policy, os-netbird enrolled, IPsec tunnel (NAT-T + road-warrior), OpenVPN server + client, LACP lagg + SFP DOM NIC + bridge, os-vnstat (1+ day), os-lldpd on an LLDP switch, os-dmidecode, monit with one check of each type, hostdiscovery enabled, a GeoIP alias, user with expiry/OTP/API key, one NAT rule of each type, ZFS boot environments, SSH spike fixtures (zpool -j?, iostat, sysctls, non-wheel shell behavior).

## Operating rules
- Validate payload shapes on the dev box before coding structs where an issue says so (monit, ospf6, netbird, clamav strings, lldp text, siproxd).
- Progress lives here: tick checkboxes as issues close; each closing commit uses `Closes #NN`; post a phase comment when a cluster lands.
- If context runs out mid-effort, a successor resumes from this tracker + the per-issue bodies alone.

comments.body:
Orchestration run started 2026-07-13. Decisions confirmed with Rob:

- **Scope: everything, phased** — all metrics lanes, the logs lane (#228–#234), spike #225, docs.
- **Dev box: full provisioning authorized.** Proxmox snapshot `pre_roadmap_227` taken first. Prod box strictly read-only (GETs only).
- **Unverifiable payloads** (netbird enrollment, dechw, possibly tor): code tolerantly from OPNsense source, land with a validation caveat on the issue.
- LLDP is capturable after all — the dev box LAN side is bridged to a real LLDP-serving switch, and the prod box sees LLDP **and** SFP/DOM optics (live fibre transceivers) → prod read-only captures feed #214/#216.
- Dev box is **not ZFS** (`bectl list` → `libbe_init failed`) — #220's boot-environment shape comes from source + a prod read-only check.

Wave plan: **P** provisioning/captures (prod read-only; dev-box core config; dev-box plugin installs) → **A** payload extensions (#210 first, time-sensitive) → **B** new core collectors → **C** plugin collectors → **D** logs lane (#228 foundation design-gated before source fan-out) → **E** #224/#225/#226 + final sweep.

Contention sequencing (binding for this run): #210 → #209 → #237-unbound; #218 before #220/#237 (shared `tabs/system.py`); #237 firewall panels coordinated with #221; frr issues #197–#199 built by one lane.

Per-issue closes follow the standard flow: one squash commit to main per issue with `Closes #NN`, closing comment with SHA, checkbox ticked here, phase comment per wave.
Worth checking if this reproduces with a fresh install — some package managers cache broken versions.

## Roadmap complete — all 38 checkboxes done (2026-07-13)

Every issue on this tracker is implemented, closed by a `Closes #NN` commit on main, and carries a closing comment with the design rationale. Executed in one orchestrated session: provisioning agents built real payloads on the dev box first (plugin installs, a triggered IDS alert, BGP/OSPF peering from the traffgen LXC, heavy nginx/haproxy/relayd topologies, LLDP unblocked at the hypervisor), then one coding lane per issue in isolated worktrees, integrated one squash-commit at a time with the full local gate on every merge.

**The delta:** 571 → 736+ metrics · 107 → 173 endpoints (24 POST) · 47 → 62 collectors · 30 → 38 dashboard tabs · plus the new `internal/logship` subsystem (opt-in `--logs.*`: OTLP-logs/stdout sinks over the existing `--otlp.*` transport; firewall digest-cursor, generic diaglog, IDS EVE, crowdsec and unbound sources; docs for the native path + decision matrix).

**Verified:** full local gate green on every merge (build, tests, schemas, docs-check, dashboard coverage); final live smoke against the dev box with all opt-ins enabled: `opnsense_up 1`, **56/56 enabled collectors scraping with zero failures**.

**Open threads:**
- #238 (fast-follow): diaglog `validFrom` timezone correction for non-UTC boxes.
- Source-derived shapes awaiting live validation by the daily canary or user reports: OSPFv3 (#198 — flagged in a code banner), netbird enrolled/per-peer (#211), dechw PSU-OK (#217), ntpd GPS fix (#224), kea per-row IA_PD values (#208 — LXC has no IPv6).
- Grafana: dashboard JSON regenerates via gitsync; the new alert manifests need a `gcx resources push` when convenient.
- release-please will propose a large release PR covering ~35 feat commits (remember the close+reopen trick to fire ci-success).

Leaving this tracker open for Rob to close after reviewing.

title: API-surface roadmap: full endpoint-universe audit → new metrics coverage (tracker)

body:
Companion to the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). The audit found several endpoints that LOOK like harmless status reads but mutate state or have unacceptable side effects. Recording them so no future collector work "discovers" them the hard way. Deliverable: a short "do not scrape" section in the docs site (probably under development/architecture notes) + this list kept in the issue for the record.

## Never-scrape endpoints (verified in source)
| endpoint | why |
|---|---|
| `api/iperf/instance/query` (GET!) | If the iperf-manager socket is absent, `send_command()` runs configd `iperf restart`/`start` — a GET that starts a service and rewrites pf anchor rules. Also: only returns manually-launched one-shot test results, purged after 1h. |
| `api/redis/service/resetdb` (GET!) | **Flushes the Redis database.** |
| `api/haproxy/maintenance/*` (all) | Look like status reads; respond only to POST AND fire `configdRun('template reload OPNsense/HAProxy')` on every call — config regeneration per scrape. Server state data is redundant with `show stat` anyway. |
| `api/hwprobe/service/report` | Runs `hw-probe -all -upload` — uploads the hardware profile to linux-hardware.org. |
| `api/tailscale/status/net` | Runs `tailscale netcheck` — an active multi-second network probe, plain-text output. |
| `api/diagnostics/carp_status` (POST) | A **setter** (enable/disable/maintenance CARP) despite the read-sounding name. |
| `api/unbound/diagnostics/dumpcache` | Dumps the entire unbound message cache — enormous payload. |
| `api/diagnostics/traffic/_top` | iftop-style sampling capture per call (up to 10s) + unbounded per-host cardinality. |
| `api/nginx/bans/get` | Inherited getAction returns the ENTIRE nginx model for two fields — use `searchban`. |

## Also recorded (won't-do, with reasons)
- A "watched plugin services" collector fanning out to per-plugin `service/status` endpoints: **do not build** — every relevant plugin registers in `api/core/service/search`, which we already export as `opnsense_services_status{name}`. Only exception found: os-beats (no plugins.inc.d file) — too thin to justify a collector.
- `hostdiscovery/service/search` silently falls back to ARP+NDP (`source: "arp-ndp"`) when the daemon is off — emission must be source-aware (see the hostdiscovery issue).
- Modules confirmed to have NO telemetry beyond config CRUD + service status (running state already covered by the services collector): caddy, bind, dnscrypt-proxy, freeradius, radsecproxy, turnserver, sslh, shadowsocks, stunnel, tinc, openconnect, zerotier (runtime data exists only in a UI controller, not the API), postfix (no queue stats in the API), squid/proxy (cachemgr not bridged), cicap, ftpproxy, rspamd (own controller not bridged; can self-export Prometheus), maltrail, wazuhagent, telegraf, netdata, collectd, zabbix agent/proxy, nodeexporter, muninnode, nrpe, netsnmp, ntopng, cloudflared, qemuguestagent, puppetagent, tftp, wol, dhcrelay, radvd, tayga, ndpproxy, ndproxy, mdnsrepeater, udpbroadcastrelay, dnsmasq (fully covered), dyndns (fully covered), trafficshaper (fully covered), routes/routing (gateway status redundant with covered searchGateway), trust CRL (no expiry fields; per-CA OCSP text parsing not worth it), kea HA + statistics (simply not exposed by the OPNsense API).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Do-not-scrape list added to the docs site
- [ ] Closing commit references this issue

comments.body:
Additional landmines found by the logs/events research pass (add to the docs page):

| endpoint | why |
|---|---|
| `api/diagnostics/firewall/stream_log` (SSE) | **Lossy by design**: the streamer throttles to 10 lines per 100ms window and silently drops the rest, including the window-boundary line (`read_log.py:207-214`). Never use as an ingestion transport — the paged `?digest=` endpoint is the lossless path. |
| `api/diagnostics/log/<module>/<scope>/live` (SSE) | Tails with `tail -f` (not `-F`) — **silently stalls after log rotation** while keepalives continue flowing. Poll with `validFrom` instead. |
| `api/qfeeds/settings/search_events` | Filtered, 300s-configd-cached, port-only re-parse of the filter log restricted to qfeeds tables — strictly a stale subset of the firewall log endpoint (where qfeeds blocks appear natively with their rule label). |
| `api/unbound/overview/search_queries` without a client filter | Only ever returns latest-1000 (the client+timeStart+timeEnd form is the sole time-range mode) — naive polling silently samples on busy resolvers. See #233 for the accepted-loss design. |

Landed in 1341145. Hand-written page at `docs/development/api-landmines.md`, wired into the Development nav: all 9 side-effecting never-scrape endpoints from the audit, the 4 lossy/sampling-transport rows added by the 2026-07-13 logs/events comment (stream_log SSE throttle-drop, log `/live` SSE rotation stall, qfeeds `search_events` stale subset, unbound `search_queries` latest-1000 sampling → #233), the watched-plugin-services won't-build rationale, and the full confirmed-empty module list — framed explicitly as never-re-audit. `make docs`/`docs-check` green.

title: docs: record do-not-scrape API landmines and confirmed-empty modules from the API-surface audit

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Full spike research done against the 2404-endpoint API universe + OPNsense core/plugins source; API-absence claims verified per item.

## Motivation
The REST surface is close to exhausted for metrics-worthy data. A handful of genuinely valuable FreeBSD-level signals have **no API endpoint at all**. An opt-in, read-only SSH channel with a small compiled-in command allowlist could collect them.

**Scope-shrinking findings**: (a) most classic candidates turned out API-exposed and already scraped — pfctl stats, dummynet shaper stats, netstat -s, temperatures, mbuf/netisr/sockets/bpf, SMART, NTP, activity; `pfctl -vvsq` is an ALTQ/pfSense-ism that doesn't apply. (b) OPNsense ships an os-node_exporter plugin whose FreeBSD build covers devstat (disk I/O), interrupts, and ZFS ARC — the honest first recommendation for users who only want those. (c) SFP/DOM optics appear to be available from the already-scraped `interfaces_info` payload (#214) — prefer the API route.

## Genuinely SSH-only inventory (verified)
| command | data | value |
|---|---|---|
| `zpool list -Hp -o name,size,alloc,free,frag,cap,health` + `zpool status -x` (or `-j` JSON on OpenZFS ≥2.3) | pool health/capacity/fragmentation/error counts, scrub state | **High** — OPNsense defaults to ZFS; degraded mirror / cksum errors on an appliance SSD is the "firewall about to die" signal. No API, no node_exporter equivalent. |
| `sysctl -n net.inet.carp.demotion dev.cpu.0.freq kstat.zfs.misc.arcstats.{hits,misses,size,c_max}` (one exec) | CARP self-demotion (silent-failover cause), CPU freq/throttling, ARC hit ratio | **High for HA pairs**; cheapest possible win (~10ms, unprivileged) |
| `iostat -x -I -d` | cumulative per-device I/O totals-since-boot (proper counters) | Moderate — overlaps node_exporter devstat; keep for the single-agent story |
| NIC driver sysctl trees (`dev.ix.0.*` missed_packets etc.) | invisible packet loss | High value but per-driver parsing matrix + queue cardinality — defer indefinitely |

## Architecture (sketch)
- `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` + knownhosts (no CGO, fits static build; `make sync-vendor`).
- New `internal/sshrunner`: dial once, persistent connection + keepalives, one session per command per scrape, semaphore 2-3, per-command timeout. Hang optional runner off `opnsense.Client` (nil when disabled) so SSH collectors use the same `init()`/CollectorInstance pattern; `client.SSH() == nil` → silent return (mirrors plugin-absent).
- **Allowlist is structural, not configurational**: command strings are compiled-in constants keyed by CommandID; no flag can add or alter a command.
- SSH down ≠ firewall down: never fold into the main up metric. Self-metrics: `opnsense_exporter_ssh_connected`, `_ssh_reconnects_total`, `_ssh_commands_total{command,status}` + duration.
- Parser fragility (no apicontract canary for CLI output): prefer machine formats (`zpool -Hp`/`-j`, `sysctl -n`), tolerant parsers, golden fixtures per FreeBSD version; unparseable = collector error, never a wrong number.
- Config (`internal/options/ssh.go`): `--opnsense.ssh.enabled` (default false), host/port/user, `key-file` (+passphrase-file; `*_FILE` convention), `known-hosts-file` or pinned `host-key` (required by default), explicit insecure-skip flag mirroring `ops.insecure`, per-command timeout. Key auth ONLY — no password support at all.
- OPNsense side: dedicated unprivileged user ("System: Shell account access", NOT wheel) — every MVP command runs unprivileged. Document optional forced-command/restricted `authorized_keys` hardening. Docs must state the residual risk plainly: the exporter holds a shell credential to the firewall.
- Precedent: czerwonk/junos_exporter (fixed read-only SSH commands, key auth, reused connections); treydock/ssh_exporter shows the anti-pattern to avoid (user-configurable command strings).

## Phased plan
- **Phase 1 (MVP)**: ZFS pool health; sysctl bundle (carp.demotion, cpu freq, ARC); iostat disk I/O counters.
- **Phase 2**: SFP/DOM via `ifconfig -v` ONLY if the API route (#214) falls through.
- **Skip**: everything API-covered, vmstat -i (node_exporter), NIC driver trees, ipfw tables, gstat/jails.

## Open questions for the dev box (#195)
- [ ] `zpool status -j`/`list -j` available on 26.1/FreeBSD 14.x? (JSON → trivial stable parsing)
- [ ] Default shell for a non-wheel user (csh?); clean non-interactive exec (no profile noise)? Force `sh -c`?
- [ ] sshd `MaxSessions` default; GUI-user group requirements
- [ ] Fixtures: `iostat -x -I -d`; `net.inet.carp.demotion` on a non-CARP box (0 vs ENOENT?); `dev.cpu.0.freq` presence under virtualization
- [ ] Measure end-to-end added scrape latency for the 3 MVP commands (expect <100ms on LAN)

## Acceptance criteria (spike → implementation gate)
- [ ] Dev-box questions answered; go/no-go decision recorded here
- [ ] If go: separate implementation issues per phase-1 collector

comments.body:
Spike executed 2026-07-13 on the dev box (FreeBSD 15.1 / OPNsense 26.7-devel). **Verdict: no-go on an exporter-embedded SSH channel** — recommendation is a documentation-only close (details below). The decisive finding is not parsing fragility but the privilege model.

## The killer finding: OPNsense has no unprivileged shell tier

From `/usr/local/etc/inc/auth.inc`: any user **without** the full-admin `page-all` privilege is hard-forced to shell `/usr/sbin/nologin` and group `nobody`, regardless of GUI shell selection (`$user_shell = $is_admin && !empty($user['shell']) ? $user['shell'] : '/usr/sbin/nologin'`). There is no "shell access" privilege distinct from full admin. And the generated `sshd_config` (`plugins.inc.d/openssh.inc:171`) unconditionally hardcodes `AllowGroups wheel`. So **every credential that can run one SSH command is a full-admin/root-equivalent credential.** The issue's sketch (dedicated non-wheel read-only user) describes a tier that does not exist in stock OPNsense; faking it requires out-of-band sshd_config.d drop-ins + boot-hook user creation — unmanaged by config.xml, not upgrade-safe, unshippable as a default.

## Evidence on the candidate commands

- `zpool status -j` works (OpenZFS 2.4.2) and returns valid JSON even with zero pools (`{"pools":{}}`); gotcha: `zpool list -j` with zero pools emits **empty stdout**, rc=0 — parsers must treat that as no-pools, not an error.
- `sysctl net.inet.carp.demotion` (=0) and the `kstat.zfs.misc.arcstats.*` OIDs are always present. `dev.cpu.0.freq` is **absent under virtualization** (no cpufreq driver on KVM) — real-hardware-only signal.
- `iostat -x -I -d` gives true cumulative counters but has no JSON mode — a fixed-column parser with no contract-canary safety net, and it duplicates `os-node_exporter`'s devstat coverage anyway.

## Costing summary

(a) exporter dials SSH: root-equivalent credential unavoidable; new dependency + reconnect state machine + un-canaried parsers; unlocks only 2 metrics beyond node_exporter. (b) recommend os-node_exporter: free, covers devstat/interrupts/ARC, misses zpool health + carp demotion. (c) upstream REST endpoint contribution: structurally correct, not on our timeline. (d) **on-box textfile-collector recipe: zero blast radius, zero new credential — a ~10-line root cron writing a Prometheus textfile that os-node_exporter's textfile collector picks up; covers exactly the two SSH-only signals (zpool health, carp demotion).**

## Recommendation (proceeding as the stated default)

Close as no-go for exporter-embedded SSH. Deliverable: a docs page recommending os-node_exporter for devstat/interrupts/ARC plus the documented textfile-collector recipe for ZFS pool health + CARP demotion; optionally an upstream feature request for a `diagnostics` REST endpoint covering both. No product code, no new dependency.

No changes were made to any box — every command was read-only.

Doc-only close landed in c622632: `docs/development/api-absent-telemetry.md` (Development nav, next to API Landmines). Records the wheel-only privilege-model finding as the permanent reason there is no exporter-embedded SSH channel, recommends os-node_exporter for devstat/interrupts/ZFS ARC, and gives the copy-paste root-cron + textfile-collector recipe for the two genuinely API-absent signals (ZFS pool health incl. the zero-pools JSON gotcha, CARP demotion), plus the cron-must-go-via-Services→Cron gotcha. The optional upstream feature request (a diagnostics REST endpoint for zpool status + carp demotion) is left as a suggestion in the page.

Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Grab-bag of WEAK-verdict candidates from the audit — none justifies its own collector; all are validate-first riders to pick up opportunistically when touching the relevant files. Recorded so they aren't re-discovered.

## 1. ntpd — GPS refclock status (unique find, no lane owned ntpd)
`api/ntpd/service/gps` (GET, core; empty `gps:{}` without a GPS refclock): `{sentence, ok, sat, alt, lat, lon}` from `ntpq -c clockvar`. Same backend script as our covered ntp status — share one fetch rather than a second configd call. Proposed: `opnsense_ntp_gps_ok`, `opnsense_ntp_gps_satellites` gauges; skip lat/lon (privacy). Not validatable without GPS hardware — implement empty-tolerant, mark experimental.

## 2. chrony — NTS authdata (extend existing collector)
`api/chrony/service/chronyauthdata` (GET, os-chrony gated): raw `chronyc authdata` text — NTS key state per source (mode, KeyID, cookies held, key age). Only meaningful on NTS configs; needs text-table parsing like the existing chrony endpoints. Candidates: `opnsense_chrony_nts_cookies{source}`, `opnsense_chrony_nts_key_age_seconds{source}`. Do only if a user asks for NTS visibility.

## 3. siproxd — SIP registration count (validate-first)
`api/siproxd/service/showregistrations` (GET, os-siproxd gated): configd literally `cat`s `/var/lib/siproxd/siproxd_registrations` — unstructured, possibly partially binary, refreshed only every ~300s by the daemon. Candidate: `opnsense_siproxd_registrations` gauge (no per-user labels — PII). **Blocked on a dev-box capture proving the file is line-parseable; if binary-ish, close as not-feasible.**

## 4. trafficshaper — rule last-match timestamp
The covered `service/statistics` payload carries rule `accessed_epoch` we drop. Candidate: `opnsense_trafficshaper_rule_last_match_timestamp_seconds`. Genuinely weak; only as a rider.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each item either implemented as a rider on other work, or closed with a "validated infeasible / not wanted" note

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue). Implemented 3 of 4 candidates: `opnsense_ntp_gps_ok`/`_gps_satellites` (core ntpd/service/gps; marked experimental — the populated fix shape is source-derived since no GPS hardware exists on any available box, and lat/lon are deliberately never decoded), `opnsense_siproxd_registrations` (new plugin-gated collector; the registration file's 4-line colon-delimited format validated via the pfSense package that parses the identical file; count only, no per-user labels), and `opnsense_trafficshaper_rule_last_match_timestamp_seconds` (rider on the already-fetched accessed_epoch, omitted when 0 = never matched). Chrony NTS authdata skipped per this issue's own verdict ("only if a user asks") — reopen that sub-item if someone does. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source: core hostwatch daemon (Deciso 2025) — `hostdiscovery/service/search` → configd `hostwatch dump_full` → `list_hosts.py` (read-only sqlite + OUI lookup).

## Value
Persistent inventory of every host ever seen per interface (MAC, IP, OUI vendor, first/last-seen) — unlike ARP/NDP tables we already scrape, entries survive cache expiry and reboots. Host-count-per-interface and new-device signals: rogue-device detection, network growth.

## Endpoint
| path | method | payload |
|---|---|---|
| `api/hostdiscovery/service/search` | GET | rows: `source` ("discovery" when hostwatch enabled; **"arp-ndp" fallback otherwise — duplicates our arp/ndp collectors, skip emission or expose as label**), `interface_name`, `ether_address`, `ip_address`, `organization_name` (OUI), `first_seen`, `last_seen` (ISO8601) |

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_hostdiscovery_hosts{interface}` gauge
- `opnsense_hostdiscovery_hosts_recent{interface}` gauge (last_seen within e.g. 15m, client-side)
- NO per-host series by default (MAC/IP labels = unbounded). If ever wanted: separate opt-in flag.

## Implementation notes
- GET, no contract change. **Core endpoint — must NOT go in `PluginGatedEndpoints()`** (per CLAUDE.md rule); old OPNsense releases will 404 → tolerate as "feature absent" the FetchACMECertificates way, or version-gate.
- `dump_full` does per-host OUI lookups — moderate cost on large networks; `last_seen` live → no response-cache. Default-on with `exporter.disable-hostdiscovery`.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Enable Interfaces → Host discovery on the 26.1 box; confirm endpoint exists on 26.1 (2025 vintage), row shape + timestamp format, and the disabled-daemon arp-ndp fallback payload

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetch + collector + flag; 404-tolerant handling WITHOUT plugin-gating; tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue). `opnsense_hostdiscovery_hosts{interface,source}` + `_hosts_recent` (15-minute last_seen window) aggregated from `GET hostdiscovery/service/search`. Hostdiscovery confirmed core (not plugin) via OPNsense source, so it is excluded from PluginGatedEndpoints() while a 404 still degrades to feature-absent for pre-Nov-2025 releases. The `source` label carries the arp-ndp fallback (hostwatch disabled) as its own visible value instead of conflating or dropping it; fallback rows never count as recent (empty last_seen). No per-host series. Flag `--exporter.disable-hostdiscovery` (default on); panels in Routing & Neighbors. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source: `Auth/Api/UserController.php`, `GroupController.php`, `Auth/User.xml`.

## Value
Security-posture drift: an unexpected new admin, a pile of API keys, or an expired-but-still-enabled account is worth a dashboard tile. Cheap config reads.

## Endpoints (GET, core)
| path | payload |
|---|---|
| `api/auth/user/search` | rows: `name`, `disabled`, `scope`, `expires` (date string `m/d/Y`), `otp_seed`, `pwd_changed_at`, `is_admin` (computed 0/1), + sensitive fields |
| `api/auth/user/search_api_key` | rows: `username`, `key`, `id` (no expiry) |
| `api/auth/group/search` | group config rows |

## Proposed metrics (aggregates ONLY — per-user labels are PII + cardinality)
- `opnsense_auth_users{disabled="true|false"}` gauge; `opnsense_auth_admin_users`; `opnsense_auth_users_expired` (expires in the past); `opnsense_auth_users_with_otp` (non-empty otp_seed); `opnsense_auth_api_keys`; `opnsense_auth_groups`

## Implementation notes
- All GET, slow-moving → response-cache. Default-on.
- SECURITY: rows contain `otp_seed`, `authorizedkeys`, API `key` material — define narrow Go structs (the `caRow` precedent) and add `otp_seed`/`key` to error-path redaction.
- `user/search` computes privileges per row server-side — fine at homelab counts; note for LDAP-imported user lists.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] User with past expiry, one with OTP, one API key; confirm `expires` format

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetches + metrics with sensitive fields excluded; tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Landed in 97c4ac5. New auth collector over `auth/user/search`, `auth/user/search_api_key`, `auth/group/search` (core GETs, response-cached). Aggregates only: `opnsense_auth_users{disabled}`, `_admin_users`, `_users_expired`, `_users_with_otp`, `_api_keys`, `_groups` — zero per-user/key/group labels. Sensitivity is structural: `otp_seed` collapses to a bool inside a custom UnmarshalJSON (the seed never persists as a field), API-key/group rows decode as `[]struct{}` so key/username/member values are never bound at all, and `otp_seed` joined the error-path redaction regex (verified by test). `expires` confirmed live as the literal m/d/Y string. Flag `--exporter.disable-auth` (default on); Local Auth row on the System tab. Full gate green.

Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source: `Firewall/Api/AliasController.php::getGeoIPAction` → `geoip.py` (cached stats file), NAT controllers (plain searchBase over MVC config).

## Part 1 — GeoIP database freshness (MODERATE)
`api/firewall/alias/get_geo_i_p` (GET, core): `alias.geoip` = `usages` (# geoip aliases), `subscription`, `address_count`, `file_count`, `timestamp` (ISO or null, last DB update) — plus the geoip config node whose `url` can embed the MaxMind license key.

- GeoIP aliases silently stop matching when the DB stops updating (expired key, download failure) — this is the direct health signal.
- SECURITY: never capture the `url` field (narrow struct, `caRow` pattern); consider error-path redaction.
- Cheap (cached stats file); slow-moving → response-cache; default-on.

## Part 2 — NAT rule inventory counts (WEAK — implementer's call, fine to drop)
`api/firewall/{source_nat,d_nat,one_to_one,npt}/search_rule` (GET): config rows with `enabled`.
- `opnsense_firewall_nat_rules{type, enabled}` gauge (8 series max). 4 extra GETs for pure config counts → response-cached, and consider opt-in.
- Caveats: sees only MVC-managed NAT rules (legacy pre-migration rules invisible); NAT rule *stats* are impossible (verified: `rule_stats.py` is filter-rules-only, `pfctl -sr -v`).

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] GeoIP alias with a free MaxMind key (populated shape) + never-configured shape (`timestamp: null`)
- [ ] One NAT rule of each type, one disabled

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GeoIP fetch + metrics with the url field excluded; NAT counts if kept; tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

GeoIP freshness: `opnsense_firewall_geoip_alias_usages`/`_addresses`/`_files` + `_last_update_timestamp_seconds` (emitted only once the DB has downloaded — never epoch 0), default-on and response-cached. The MaxMind/ipinfo `url` (embeds the license key) is structurally undecodable — no struct field exists, golden schema has no url path, and a planted-key test asserts nothing leaks.
