body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source: `Core/Api/BackupController.php`, `SnapshotsController.php` → `bectl.py`.

## Part 1 — config backup history health (STRONG)
`api/core/backup/backups/this` (GET, core): `items[]` newest-first with `time` (epoch string), `description`, `username`, `filesize`. Answers "is my config actually being backed up, and how stale is the newest backup?" — silent backup failure is invisible today.

- `opnsense_backup_last_timestamp_seconds` gauge; `opnsense_backup_count` gauge; `opnsense_backup_last_size_bytes` gauge. No per-backup labels.
- Cost: controller globs `/conf/backup/config-*.xml` and simplexml-parses every file per call (default retention 60) — not free → slow-moving payload, ideal response-cache candidate; default-on with caching.

## Part 2 — ZFS boot environments (MODERATE)
`api/core/snapshots/search` (GET): bootgrid rows `uuid, name, active ("N","R","NR","-"), size (human string), created (epoch float)`. `api/core/snapshots/is_supported` (GET): `{"supported": bool}`. Boot environments are the rollback safety net — are pre-upgrade snapshots actually being made?

- `opnsense_snapshots_supported` gauge 0/1; `opnsense_snapshots_total` gauge; `opnsense_snapshots_active_created_timestamp_seconds` gauge (row whose `active` contains "N"). Skip `size` (human-formatted string).
- UFS boxes: `bectl` fails → empty rowset / supported:false — handle gracefully. Cheap exec; slow-moving → cache candidate.

## Implementation notes
Both GET, core, not gated, no contract changes. One "core housekeeping" collector or fold into an existing core collector.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Confirm `time` epoch-string shape on backups; ZFS box: create/clone a BE to see `active` flag combos; validate UFS empty shape if possible

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetches + metrics + cache wiring; tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Prod read-only capture (2026-07-13) — shape corrections for implementation: `core/snapshots/search` rows also carry `mountpoint` and `created_str` (not in the issue body), `created` is a plain **int** (not float), and observed `active` values are `NR` and `-` (no bare `N`/`R` sample captured). `core/backup/backups/this` returned **100** items (retention exceeds the assumed 60 default) with `time` as an epoch **string with decimals** ("1783886416.55") and `filesize` int. `core/snapshots/is_supported` → `{"supported":true}` on prod (ZFS). The dev box is UFS — use it to capture the unsupported/absent shape. Raw captures: session scratchpad `captures/prod/` (ephemeral — shapes recorded here are the durable copy).

Landed in 96174f0. Two new default-on core collectors: `backup` (`opnsense_backup_last_timestamp_seconds`/`_count`/`_last_size_bytes` from `core/backup/backups/this`, newest picked by max(time) rather than item order) and `snapshots` (`opnsense_snapshots_supported`/`_total`/`_active_created_timestamp_seconds` from `core/snapshots/{search,is_supported}`). Incorporated the prod-capture corrections: `time` handled as a quoted-decimal epoch string, `created` as int, `mountpoint`/`created_str` modeled. UFS behavior verified live on the dev box: both endpoints answer 200 with `supported:false`/empty rows (never 404) → `supported=0` and no timestamp series, not zeros. All three endpoints joined the response cache (slow-moving reads — the backup controller parses every retained XML per call). Flags `--exporter.disable-backup`/`--exporter.disable-snapshots`; full gate green, coverage 609/609.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source: `Monit/Api/StatusController.php` proxies monit httpd `_status?format=xml` verbatim; monit 5.x XML schema.

## Value
We fetch monit's full XML status but parse only name/type/status/monitor. The same document carries per-check resource data: filesystem usage %, process cpu/mem/uptime, host ping/port response times, system load/memory/swap. **This is the only disk-usage-percent source in the whole exporter today.** Zero new API cost.

## Fields available per check type (single-vs-array quirk already handled in `opnsense/monit.go`)
- type 0 filesystem: `block.percent/usage/total`, `inode.percent`
- type 3 process: `pid`, `uptime`, `threads`, `children`, `memory.percent/kilobyte`, `cpu.percent`
- type 4 host: `icmp.responsetime`, `port[].responsetime` (+portnumber, protocol)
- type 5 system: `system.load.avg01/05/15`, `system.cpu.user/system/wait`, `system.memory.percent/kilobyte`, `system.swap.percent`
- type 8 network: link counters — duplicate our interface metrics; lean: drop

## Proposed metrics (all `{name}`, plus `{port,protocol}` on port checks)
- `opnsense_monit_filesystem_usage_percent`, `_filesystem_inode_usage_percent`
- `opnsense_monit_process_cpu_percent`, `_process_memory_bytes`, `_process_uptime_seconds`, `_process_threads`
- `opnsense_monit_host_icmp_response_seconds`, `_port_response_seconds`
- `opnsense_monit_system_load{period=1m|5m|15m}`, `_system_memory_percent`, `_system_swap_percent`

## Implementation notes
- Live data — the endpoint isn't response-cached today; keep it that way. Cardinality bounded by configured checks. Cost unchanged (same single GET).
- **BLOCKER**: `opnsense/monit.go:19-24` documents that the `result:"ok"` shape is unvalidated — dev-box payload capture required before coding. Emit only fields present per check type.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Monit enabled with one check of each type: system, filesystem, process, remote host (ICMP + port), network interface, program
- [ ] Capture `/api/monit/status/get/xml` raw JSON — ground truth for simplexml number-vs-string encoding

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Struct extension + metrics; fixtures from real payloads; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Landed (see the commit referencing this issue). 12 new gauges from the existing single `monit/status/get/xml` GET — filesystem block/inode %, process cpu/mem/uptime/threads, host icmp + per-port response times, system load/memory/swap/cpu{mode}. Pointer-typed absence (no fabricated zeros), the `-1` not-yet-computed cpu sentinel dropped, system CPU decoded as a mode map (FreeBSD reports user/system/nice/hardirq). Validated against the live one-check-of-each-type capture; not-running prod shape unchanged. Coverage 674/674; full gate green.

Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source: `src/core/.../library/OPNsense/System/Status/*.php`.

## Value
We already scrape `api/core/system/status` but only surface overall + CrashReporter + Firewall. The `subsystems` map carries per-subsystem detail we throw away — including **DiskSpaceStatus** (disk full!), RootLockStatus, LiveMediaStatus, UnboundBlocklistStatus, and the *Override misconfig statuses. Disk-space alone justifies this. **Zero new API cost.**

## Endpoint (covered — collector extension only)
`api/core/system/status`. 17 subsystem classes in core (CaptivePortal, ConfigdProxyOverride, CrashReporter, DiskSpace, DnsmasqOverride, Firewall, HostDiscovery, IDSOverride, IPsecOverride, LiveMedia, MonitOverride, OpensshOverride, ResolvConfOverride, RootLock, SystemBooting, UnboundBlocklist, UnboundOverride); plugins can add more. Keys = lowercased class names minus "Status".

## Proposed metric
- `opnsense_system_subsystem_status_code{subsystem}` gauge — SystemStatusCode int (2=OK, 1=NOTICE, 0=WARNING, -1=ERROR), one series per subsystem **present in the response**. A healthy box omits healthy subsystems → series appear/disappear; document absence == healthy (same convention as `firewallIsHealthy`, `internal/collector/collector.go:672`).

## Implementation notes
- `opnsense/health_check.go` already decodes the dynamic `subsystems` map — the collector just never emits it. Purely additive; keep existing crashreporter/firewall gauges for compat. Bounded cardinality (~20 keys, only unhealthy present).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Collector emits the new gauge; tests with a populated-fixture; `make docs` + dashboard panel + alert-rule candidate (disk space)

comments.body: Landed in 7ea8cb9 (+ docs-count fixup ce7cfcb). `opnsense_system_subsystem_status_code{subsystem}` now surfaces every health-check subsystem OPNsense reports — disk space, root lock, and every plugin override — not just firewall/crashreporter, at zero extra API cost. `HealthCheckResponse.AllSubsystems()` unions the 26.1 top-level map and the 26.1.11 metadata-only shape (top-level wins, matching existing precedence); an absent series means healthy, same convention as the existing gauges, with a per-scrape reset so recovered subsystems disappear. Fixture-driven tests now cover populated multi-subsystem maps on both generation shapes (previously only near-empty maps were validated). Added a Subsystem Health dashboard row and an `OPNsenseDiskSpaceLow` grafana-managed alert (fires after 10m below OK). Full gate green; dashboard coverage 577/577.

Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified; also confirmed via the dashboard-widget sweep (`DecHW.js` reads exactly pwr1/pwr2).

## Value
Fleet inventory (which appliance model/BIOS runs where — join target for every other metric) and, on Deciso DEC appliances, dual-PSU health: a dead redundant PSU is otherwise silent until the second one fails.

## Endpoints (GET, both plugin-gated)
| path | gated | payload |
|---|---|---|
| `api/dmidecode/service/get` | os-dmidecode | `{status, system{Manufacturer, "Product Name", Version, "Serial Number", Family}, bios{Vendor, Version, "Release Date"}}` — configd greps `dmidecode -q -t system|bios` into ini form |
| `api/dechw/info/power_status` | os-dec-hw | `{status: "OK"|"failed", pwr1: 0|1, pwr2: 0|1}` — GPIO via `gpioctl`; `status:"failed"` when no GPIO device (e.g. installed on non-Deciso hardware). NOTE: two research passes disagreed on the route (`power_status` vs `powerstatus`) — verify the actual action name on the dev box / in the manifest. |

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_hardware_dmi_info{manufacturer,product,version,serial,family,bios_vendor,bios_version,bios_release}` =1 (single series; flag: serial in a label — confirm Rob is happy or make it opt-out)
- `opnsense_dechw_power_status{psu="1"|"2"}` gauge 0/1 (emit only when top-level `status == "OK"`)

## Implementation notes
- Both into `PluginGatedEndpoints()`. dmidecode is maximally slow-moving → prime response-cache candidate; dechw PSU state is live — never cache. `status:"failed"` = no data, not an error. One bundled hardware issue, two small collectors (or one collector, two fetches). GET-only, no contract change.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-dmidecode anywhere (validate ini keys with spaces survive PHP parse; VM shows "To be filled by O.E.M.")
- [ ] dechw needs real DEC hardware — if unavailable, code defensively from the script (pwr1/pwr2 integers) and mark unvalidated

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetches + metrics + cache wiring; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` + tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box captures (2026-07-13): package name is `os-dec-hw` (not os-dechw). Real route is `dechw/info/power_status` (source method `powerStatusAction`; router is case-insensitive). On non-Deciso hardware it returns `{"status":"failed"}` with NO pwr1/pwr2 keys at all — emit PSU series only when status is OK. dmidecode capture (`captures/dmidecode/`) has the clean QEMU DMI shape ("Not Specified" serial etc.).

Landed in 27c3509. New plugin-gated `hardware` collector: `opnsense_hardware_dmi_info` (DMI identity labels from `dmidecode/service/get`, response-cached — slow-moving) and `opnsense_hardware_psu_status{psu}` (0/1 from `dechw/info/power_status`, never cached — live GPIO). Three-state dechw handling per the capture comment: plugin absent (404) and hardware absent (`{"status":"failed"}`, no pwr keys) both yield no PSU series; pointer-typed pwr fields so a single-PSU variant cannot fabricate a bogus series. Flag `--exporter.disable-hardware` (default on); Hardware Identity table + PSU state-timeline rows on the System tab. Fixture set covers QEMU DMI (live capture), source-derived Deciso-OK PSU, hardware-absent and plugin-absent. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `net/lldpd` plugin (configd runs `lldpcli show neighbors`, plain text — no `-f json`).

## Value
LLDP neighbors turn the exporter into a topology sensor — alert when a firewall port stops seeing the expected switch/port; catches miscabling and switch-replacement drift.

## Endpoint
| path | method | gated? | payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api/lldpd/service/neighbor` | GET | os-lldpd | `{"response": "<text>"}` — raw `lldpcli show neighbors`: per-neighbor blocks with `Interface:`, ChassisID, SysName, SysDescr, MgmtIP, PortID, PortDescr, TTL |

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_lldp_neighbors{interface}` gauge
- `opnsense_lldp_neighbor_info{interface,chassis_name,port_id,port_descr}` =1 (omit SysDescr/MgmtIP from labels)

## Implementation notes
- Plugin-gated → `PluginGatedEndpoints()`. GET, no contract change. One lldpcli exec per scrape — cheap.
- Free-text payload — needs a lenient block parser (lldpcli output can drift between releases): skip unparseable blocks, never error the collector. Default-on behind `exporter.disable-lldpd`.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-lldpd attached to an LLDP-speaking switch; capture raw response text for parser fixtures (incl. a multi-neighbor port if possible)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetch + text parser + metrics; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` + tests with real fixtures; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Prod read-only capture (2026-07-13): os-lldpd is active on prod — real `lldpcli` free-text with 4 neighbor blocks, including **one port (ixl0) with TWO neighbors** (the multi-neighbor case) and one block (ixl2) whose `Interface:` line carries **no `alias:` token at all** — the parser needs a fixture for that variant, not just the happy path. Raw capture: session scratchpad `captures/prod/lldpd-neighbor.json` (ephemeral); the dev box (LAN bridged to a real switch) is the second live source.

Dev-box LLDP result (2026-07-13): structurally-valid EMPTY neighbor response captured (`captures/lldpd/neighbor_none.json` — useful as the empty fixture). Zero neighbors is root-caused to the Proxmox host: vmbr0 `group_fwd_mask=0x0`, and Linux bridges drop the reserved 802.1D multicast range (LLDP dst <mac-11>) between ports by default — NOT an OPNsense/lldpd issue, unfixable from the box. Fix would be `echo 16384 > /sys/class/net/vmbr0/bridge/group_fwd_mask` on the hypervisor (shared infra — needs Rob's call; parked). The 2026-07-13 PROD capture (4 real neighbor blocks incl. multi-neighbor port and missing-alias variant) is the populated ground truth for the parser.

Landed in 8fa19ab. New plugin-gated `lldpd` collector: `opnsense_lldp_neighbors{interface}` and `opnsense_lldp_neighbor_info{interface,chassis_name,port_id,port_descr}` (SysDescr/MgmtIP deliberately excluded — unbounded free text). The lenient lldpcli text parser is fixture-tested against the prod capture (multi-neighbor port + the missing-alias variant), the dev-box empty shape, and the post-hypervisor-fix populated dev-box capture (RID/Time/ifalias/Unknown TLVs all tolerated); malformed blocks are skipped with a warning, never failing the scrape. Flag `--exporter.disable-lldpd` (default on); panels in the Routing & Neighbors tab. The dev-box LLDP path is now live end-to-end (<host-8> vmbr0 group_fwd_mask fix, persisted), so the daily canary exercises this collector with real neighbors. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `net/vnstat` plugin.

## Value
vnstat's DB survives reboots and exporter restarts, so its day/month totals are the right source for ISP data-cap tracking — `increase()` over interface byte counters loses data on reboots/counter resets.

## Endpoints (GET, os-vnstat gated)
| path | payload |
|---|---|
| `api/vnstat/service/interface_list` | `{"interfaces": [...]}` — vnstat DB ∩ configured devices |
| `api/vnstat/service/get_json_data?iface=<if>` | `vnstat --json`: `interfaces[0].traffic.total{rx,tx}` (bytes) + `day`/`month`/`year` arrays `{date{...},rx,tx}` |

(`hourly|daily|monthly|yearly` endpoints are raw CLI text — do not use; `service/status` redundant with services collector.)

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_vnstat_total_bytes{interface,direction=rx|tx}` counter (cumulative since DB creation; resets only on resetdb)
- `opnsense_vnstat_current_day_bytes{interface,direction}` gauge
- `opnsense_vnstat_current_month_bytes{interface,direction}` gauge

## Implementation notes
- **Opt-in `exporter.enable-vnstat`**: 1 list call + 1 configd `vnstat --json` exec per interface per scrape.
- Both endpoints into `PluginGatedEndpoints()`. Don't cache success. The `?iface=` query-param GET form is novel for our client — check how the contract canary treats a parameterized GET. Skip `fiveminute`/`hour` arrays (Prometheus has that resolution natively).

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-vnstat, ≥1 day accumulation; capture `get_json_data` raw JSON (jsonversion, array ordering, date-matching fields)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Opt-in flag + fetch fan-out + metrics; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` + tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box captures (2026-07-13, `captures/vnstat/`): real non-sparse data (day+month rows with non-zero rx/tx) via the `?iface=` GET form. Collector expectation note: `interface_list` returns EVERY interface in vnstat's DB (enc0, tailscale0, vlans, all vtnets), not just the plugin-configured set.

Landed in 8c71d6d. New opt-in vnstat collector (`--exporter.enable-vnstat`, default off — one `interface_list` call plus one `get_json_data?iface=` call per interface per scrape). `opnsense_vnstat_total_bytes` is a counter (resets only on `vnstat --resetdb`, a legitimate counter reset); `current_day`/`current_month` are gauges (calendar resets), all `{interface,direction}`. Exports every device vnstat's own DB tracks (confirmed live to include enc0/tailscale0 — bounded by box topology; the plugin's selected-set config exposes only unmappable logical names, so no third endpoint). Current day/month buckets matched via vnstat's `updated.date`, not array order (regression-tested). Only `interface_list` joined the 404 negative-cache — the per-iface query string never matches the fixed-path cache key. Interfaces-tab row behind a `has_vnstat` sentinel. Full gate green.

Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `legacy_interfaces_details()` in `src/core/src/etc/inc/interfaces.lib.inc` (backing the covered `interfaces_info` endpoint).

## Value
LAGG failover is invisible today — a lagg that dropped from 2 active ports to 1 keeps passing traffic and no metric moves. SFP DOM (module temp, voltage, per-lane RX power/TX bias) is the canonical early-warning for dying optics. **Both are already in a response body we fetch every scrape and discard** — zero new API cost.

## Endpoint (covered — struct extension only)
`api/interfaces/overview/interfaces_info` rows additionally carry:
- `sfp`: `plugged`, `vendor`, `part_number`, `serial_number`, `temperature` ("NN.NN C"), `voltage`, `lane_<n>_rx_power` (dBm string), `lane_<n>_tx_bias` (mA string)
- `laggproto`, `lagghash`, `laggstatistics` (`active ports`, `flapping`), `laggport` map (per-member `flags` + `state`: active/collecting/distributing for LACP)
- bridge `members` map; `tunnel` proto/src/dst; wireless `channel`/`ssid`

## Proposed metrics (extend `interfaces` subsystem; join key `device`)
- `opnsense_interfaces_lagg_active_ports{device}` gauge; `opnsense_interfaces_lagg_flapping_total{device}` counter
- `opnsense_interfaces_lagg_port_active{device,member}` gauge 0/1; `_collecting`/`_distributing` gauges (LACP only, emit when present)
- `opnsense_interfaces_lagg_info{device,protocol,hash}` =1
- `opnsense_interfaces_sfp_info{device,vendor,part_number,serial_number}` =1
- `opnsense_interfaces_sfp_temperature_celsius{device}` / `_voltage_volts{device}` gauges
- `opnsense_interfaces_sfp_lane_rx_power_dbm{device,lane}` / `_lane_tx_bias_milliamps{device,lane}` gauges (lane ≤4)
- `opnsense_interfaces_bridge_member{device,member}` =1

## Implementation notes
- No new endpoint, no contract change, no extra scrape cost — widen `interfaceOverviewRow` in `opnsense/interfaces.go`, emit from the interfaces collector. Values are strings with unit tails ("45.32 C", "-2.32 dBm (0.59 mW)") — tolerant float parsing; absent fields → no series (never zeros). Default-on.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] LACP lagg with ≥2 members; SFP/SFP+ NIC with DOM-capable transceiver (Intel ix/ixl or Chelsio — igc/em won't show `plugged:`); a bridge
- [ ] Capture raw `interfaces_info` JSON to pin sfp string formats and `laggport.state` contents

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Struct extension + metrics; tests + fixtures; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Prod read-only capture (2026-07-13) — scoping notes: prod has **no LAGG and no bridge interfaces**, and its two SFPs (ixl0/ixl2) are **copper RJ45 UBNT modules** — the SFP block populates `plugged`/`vendor`/`part_number`/`serial_number`/`manufacturing_date` but **no DOM fields** (temperature/voltage/lane rx power/tx bias all absent; copper modules never carry DOM). DOM series must degrade to **absent series, never zeros**. LAGG/bridge/DOM-populated shapes come from OPNsense source (+ a possible dev-box lagg/bridge capture, pending provisioning). Raw capture: session scratchpad `captures/prod/interfaces-overview.json` (ephemeral).

Landed in e62ddb8. Widened `interfaceOverviewRow` to capture laggproto/lagghash/laggstatistics/laggport, bridge `members`, and the `sfp` block (modeled as a string map since DOM lane keys are dynamically named — this also collapses the golden schema to one wildcard path). 12 new `opnsense_interfaces_*` series: lagg info/active-ports/flapping/per-port state (LACP collecting+distributing emitted only when a `state=` clause exists), bridge membership, SFP identity, and per-module temperature/voltage + per-lane RX power/TX bias DOM gauges. Confirmed against the 2026-07-13 prod capture: copper RJ45 SFPs (UBNT UF-RJ45-1G on ixl0/ixl2) populate identity only and DOM series degrade to absent, never zero. No lagg/bridge exists on prod or the dev VM, so those fixtures are source-derived from `legacy_interfaces_details()` in `interfaces.lib.inc` (cited inline) and ledger-exempted as hardware-dependent. New LAGG / Bridge / SFP Optics dashboard row; full gate green, coverage 589/589.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against core ipsec controllers + `list_sad.py`/`list_spd.py`/`list_leases.py`.

## Value
We export vici-level phase1/phase2 traffic and lease-pool aggregates. The kernel view (`setkey`) adds what vici can't: installed SA/policy counts (catching "tunnel up but no SA/policy installed"), SA age vs hard/soft lifetime (rekey health), NAT-T detection. Plus a free "uncommitted ipsec changes" flag.

## Endpoints (all GET, core — NOT plugin-gated, no contract changes)
| path | payload |
|---|---|
| `api/ipsec/sad/search` | per SA (from `setkey -D`): `src`, `dst`, `nat` (NAT-T), `satype`, `spi`, `mode`, `bytes_*`, `addtime_diff` (age s), `addtime_hard/soft` (lifetimes s), `state`, joined with `ikeid`/`phase1desc`/`phase2desc` |
| `api/ipsec/spd/search` | per policy (from `setkey -DP`): `src/dst/ports`, `dir` (in/out/fwd), `proto`, `mode`, `reqid`, + ikeid/descs |
| `api/ipsec/leases/search` | per lease (swanctl --list-pools --leases): `pool`, `address`, `online`, `user` |
| `api/ipsec/legacy_subsystem/status` | `{enabled, isDirty}` — pure PHP, no exec |

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_ipsec_sad_entries` gauge `{satype, ikeid, phase1desc}` — **never label by SPI** (churns every rekey; known backlog item)
- `opnsense_ipsec_sa_age_seconds` / `_sa_lifetime_hard_seconds` / `_soft_seconds` gauges `{ikeid, phase2desc}` (max/min per reqid group) — "time to rekey" alerting
- `opnsense_ipsec_sad_nat_traversal` gauge `{ikeid}`
- `opnsense_ipsec_spd_policies` gauge `{direction}` — zero policies while phase2 claims connected = broken
- `opnsense_ipsec_lease_online` gauge `{pool, user}` — opt-in (user = unbounded road-warrior identity); pool aggregates stay default-on
- `opnsense_ipsec_config_dirty` + `opnsense_ipsec_legacy_enabled` gauges — effectively free
- Skip per-SA byte counters (redundant with vici bytes we export; non-monotonic across rekeys when aggregated)

## Implementation notes
- `sad/spd` = one setkey exec each (moderate); `leases/search` re-runs the same swanctl call as covered `leases/pools` — fetch once and feed both if possible. No response caching (live). Rides existing `exporter.disable-ipsec`; lease-user detail behind an opt-in.
- Parsing quirk: numeric-looking strings int-cast by the script except `spi`; nulls where empty.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] One established tunnel (one behind NAT for the `nat` field; one road-warrior client for named leases); confirm `addtime_*` key names and SPD record shape

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetches + metrics + opt-in lease detail; tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue on main). Kernel `setkey` view + mode-cfg leases + dirty flag: `sad_entries{satype,ikeid,phase1desc}`, per-reqid `sa_age_seconds`/`sa_lifetime_hard_seconds`/`sa_lifetime_soft_seconds` (max-age/min-lifetime grouping; SPI never a label — reqid anchors the series because the live box returns null ikeid/phaseNdesc from the join and reqid is rekey-stable), `sad_nat_traversal{ikeid}`, `spd_policies{direction}`, `config_dirty`, `legacy_enabled`, and opt-in `lease_online{pool,user}` behind `--exporter.enable-ipsec-lease-details` (pool aggregates always-on, fed from the existing leases/pools payload — its `knownExtraTopKeys` exemption is gone). Three new core GET endpoints, never cached. Validated against the real established tunnel on the dev box (addtime keys, SPD shape, reqid int-vs-string split, hex spi, the "No SAD entries." placeholder discarded); NAT-T key carries a missingOK note (no NAT'd peer available). Per-SA byte counters skipped as redundant with vici. Full gate green; coverage 683/683.

Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against core `ovpn_status.py` (`status 3` per instance socket).

## Value
Our openvpn collector counts sessions but drops the traffic data the payload already carries. Closes the long-standing OpenVPN per-user visibility gap with **zero new endpoints**.

## Endpoint (covered — struct extension only)
`api/openvpn/service/search_sessions` (GET, core) rows additionally carry: `bytes_received`, `bytes_sent`, `connected_since__time_t_` (note double-underscore from the upstream field mangling), `common_name`, `username`, `client_id`, `data_channel_cipher`; client-role instances also get instance-level bytes + `timestamp`.

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_openvpn_session_received_bytes_total` / `_transmitted_bytes_total` counters `{description, common_name/username, real_address, virtual_address}` — cumulative per-connection, resets on reconnect (fine for counters). Behind the existing `--exporter.enable-openvpn-details` flag (same label surface as today's sessions gauge).
- `opnsense_openvpn_session_connected_since_timestamp_seconds` gauge, same labels.
- Default-on aggregates (no username label): `opnsense_openvpn_instance_received_bytes_total`/`_transmitted_bytes_total{description}` summed over sessions.

## Not proposed
`search_routes` re-runs the same configd `openvpn connections` fan-out (per-socket unix conns with 5s timeouts) — doubles the subsystem's scrape cost for a marginal routing-table count. Skip unless someone asks.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] OpenVPN server with 1+ connected client (ideally also a client-role instance); confirm field names post-mangling and byte-counter types (strings?)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Struct fields + metrics (details flag + aggregates); tests + fixtures; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Landed in 5f6a9ce. Extended `FetchOpenVPNSessions` to decode `bytes_received`, `bytes_sent`, `connected_since__time_t_` and `common_name` from the existing `search_sessions` payload — zero new endpoints. Per-session `opnsense_openvpn_session_received_bytes_total`/`_transmitted_bytes_total` (counters) and `opnsense_openvpn_session_connected_since_timestamp_seconds` (gauge) sit behind the existing `--exporter.enable-openvpn-details` flag with the same label surface as the sessions gauge; the identity label prefers the TLS common name over OpenVPN's literal `UNDEF` for cert-only sessions. Default-on `opnsense_openvpn_instance_received_bytes_total`/`_transmitted_bytes_total` aggregate per instance description with no per-client labels. Field shapes verified live on the 26.7-devel box (byte counters and the timestamp arrive as quoted numeric strings; `common_name` is null for user/pass sessions). `search_routes` intentionally skipped per the issue. Docs, golden schema and three new VPN-tab dashboard panels regenerated; coverage gate 576/576.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `net/netbird` plugin (`netbird status --json` via configd).

## Value
NetBird is the one VPN plugin with a rich, fully-JSON runtime API we don't touch: management/signal-plane connectivity, relay availability, per-peer connection type (P2P vs relayed), transfer counters, latency, handshake age — the direct analogue of our existing tailscale collector.

## Endpoints (GET, os-netbird gated)
| path | payload |
|---|---|
| `api/netbird/status/status` | netbird CLI JSON: `management.connected`, `signal.connected`, `relays.total/available`, `peers.total/connected`, `peers.details[]` (`fqdn`, `status`, `connectionType`, `direct`, `lastWireguardHandshake`, `transferReceived/Sent`, `latency`, ...), `cliVersion`/`daemonVersion`. Empty `[]` when daemon down. |
| `api/netbird/service/status` | standard running/stopped |

(`status/get` is an empty in-memory model — useless; settings/authentication are config.)

## Proposed metrics (`opnsense_netbird_*`)
- Default-on aggregates: `management_connected`, `signal_connected` gauges 0/1; `relays_total`/`relays_available`; `peers_total`/`peers_connected`; `service_running`; `info{cli_version,daemon_version}` =1
- Opt-in per-peer (`exporter.enable-netbird-details`, mirroring openvpn-details): `peer_connected{fqdn}`, `peer_direct{fqdn}`, `peer_received_bytes_total`/`peer_transmitted_bytes_total` counters, `peer_last_handshake_timestamp_seconds`, `peer_latency_seconds`

## Implementation notes
- Both GET → no contract change; both into `PluginGatedEndpoints()`. Live counters — never cache success. One configd exec per scrape, cheap. Empty-array (daemon down) → running=0 + skip peers, not a scrape error.
- New collector + `exporter.disable-netbird`.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-netbird enrolled (netbird.io free tier or self-hosted) with ≥1 peer
- [ ] Validate JSON casing (`connectionType` vs older `conectionType` typo), `latency` units (Go time.Duration → integer ns?), `lastWireguardHandshake` format

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetch + collector + flags; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` + tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box captures (2026-07-13, `captures/netbird/`): both unenrolled shapes captured — daemon DOWN returns a bare `[]` (not an object!) from status/status; daemon up + unenrolled returns `daemonStatus:"NeedsLogin"`, management/signal `connected:false`, `peers.total:0`, versions populated (0.72.2). `status/get` confirmed useless (`{"Netbird":[]}`). No enrollment was performed — enrolled-shape fields come from plugin source per the code-tolerantly policy.

Landed in 06c02f6. New plugin-gated netbird collector mirroring tailscale: default-on management/signal connectivity, relay totals, peer counts, `service_running`, and a `version_info` gauge — all absent (never zeroed) in the daemon-down state, where `status/status` returns a bare `[]` (confirmed live; decoded via RawMessage so the object schema keeps field-level drift detection). Opt-in `--exporter.enable-netbird-details` adds per-peer connected/direct/traffic/handshake/latency labeled by fqdn only — no IP labels. Validation caveat per the agreed policy: connectivity/counts/versions live-verified on the unenrolled dev box; per-peer and relay fields are source-derived from netbird's own `client/status/status.go` (the exact struct the plugin relays verbatim) and flagged in the exemptions ledger so a daemon-down canary probe is triaged as the documented fallback, not drift. New NetBird dashboard tab. Full gate green.

body:
Forward-compat fix surfaced by the API-surface audit (see tracker issue).

## Problem
`OverviewController::isBlockListEnabledAction()` in OPNsense core master carries `/* XXX deprecated and to be removed for 26.7 */`. Our `FetchUnboundBlockListStatus()` (feeds `opnsense_unbound_blocklist_enabled`) scrapes `api/unbound/overview/isBlockListEnabled` and will start 404ing on 26.7 boxes. Since it's a core endpoint, that 404 would surface as a real scrape error, not plugin-absent.

## Fix
Replacement: `api/unbound/overview/get_policies` (GET, core) — returns the dnsbl `blocklist` node, one entry per policy with an `enabled` flag. Derive `blocklist_enabled = any(policy.enabled)` — exactly the deprecated endpoint's logic (`array_filter($nodes, fn($v) => $v['enabled'])`). Cheap config read, slow-moving → response-cache candidate.

- Keep `opnsense_unbound_blocklist_enabled` emitting identically (no metric change).
- Optional bonus: `opnsense_unbound_blocklist_policies{enabled}` count gauge.
- Decide: drop `unboundBlocklistStatus` outright, or keep as fallback during a transition (26.1 boxes have both). Do NOT treat 404 as plugin-absent — core endpoint.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Capture `get_policies` payload with 0, 1-enabled, and all-disabled policies

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Endpoint swapped (or dual-path), metric unchanged, tests + fixtures updated, `make docs`

comments.body: Landed in a849c38. Migrated `opnsense_unbound_blocklist_enabled` off the deprecated `isBlockListEnabled` endpoint onto `api/unbound/overview/get_policies`, verified against a live 26.7-devel box (empty policy set returns `[]` — the PHP empty-array quirk) and OPNsense core source on both master and stable/26.1 (`getPoliciesAction()` is core on both, so no legacy dual-path needed). Metric semantics unchanged: still any-enabled across dnsbl policies, matching the old endpoint's server-side `array_filter` logic. Tolerant JSON handling for map-vs-empty-array and string `"1"`/`"0"` booleans (the `subsystemMap` pattern). The endpoint is a slow-moving config read so it joined the response cache. Skipped the optional `blocklist_policies` count gauge to keep the fix minimal — #209 covers further unbound DNSBL metrics. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against core Unbound overview/diagnostics controllers (`stats.py` over `/var/unbound/data/unbound.duckdb`, `logger.py` retention). Independently confirmed by two research lanes.

## Value
Our unbound collector has ~60 series from `unbound-control stats` but **zero DNSBL visibility** — blocks happen in OPNsense's python dnsbl module, not unbound's counters. `overview/totals` is the only API reporting blocked vs passed vs local vs resolved outcomes plus loaded blocklist size — the pi-hole-style headline numbers.

## Endpoints
| path | method | payload |
|---|---|---|
| `api/unbound/overview/totals/{max}` | GET | `{total, blocklist_size, passed, resolved{total,pcnt}, blocked{total,pcnt}, local{total,pcnt}, start_time, top{}, top_blocked{}}` — call with `{max}=1` to shrink the top-N maps we ignore |
| `api/unbound/overview/is_enabled` | GET | `{"enabled": "0"/"1"}` — whether query-stats logging (`general.stats`) is on; cheap config read |
| `api/unbound/diagnostics/listlocalzones` / `listlocaldata` / `listinsecure` | GET | optional rider: local zone/data/insecure-domain counts via unbound-control |

## CRITICAL — gauges, not counters
`logger.py` truncates the query table to the last 7 days (hourly DELETE) and `qstats reset` truncates everything: totals are rolling-window aggregates that can decrease. Counters would produce phantom resets.

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_unbound_dnsbl_blocklist_size` gauge
- `opnsense_unbound_qstats_queries_7d{result=passed|blocked|local|resolved}` gauge + `opnsense_unbound_qstats_queries_total_7d` gauge
- `opnsense_unbound_qstats_start_time_seconds` gauge (detects DB resets)
- `opnsense_unbound_qstats_enabled` gauge
- Do NOT export `top`/`top_blocked` (unbounded domain cardinality)
- Rider (WEAK, optional): `opnsense_unbound_local_zones{type}`, `_local_data_records`, `_insecure_domains` gauges — slow-moving, ideal response-cache candidates

## Implementation notes
- GET only, core, not gated. **Expensive backend**: configd spawns python+pandas+DuckDB per `totals` call (~1s) → **opt-in `exporter.enable-unbound-qstats`**. Gate the heavy call on `is_enabled` (the #90 lesson: stats off → emit only `qstats_enabled 0`, never zero-valued gauges).
- Skips recorded: `overview/_rolling` (history — Prometheus derives rates), `search_queries` (per-query rows), `dumpcache` (entire message cache), `reset`/`test_blocklist` (mutations).

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Enable Unbound statistics + one DNSBL policy; generate blocked + passed queries; capture `totals/1` (pcnt formatting, start_time type, empty-DB shape) and stats-disabled behavior

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Opt-in flag + fetches + metrics; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Landed in 0289a3d. New opt-in flag `--exporter.enable-unbound-qstats` (default off — `overview/totals` spawns configd→python→DuckDB at ~1s/call, and the totals call is skipped entirely when `is_enabled` reports stats logging off). Adds `opnsense_unbound_dns_qstats_enabled`, `_dnsbl_blocklist_size`, `_qstats_queries_7d{result}`, `_qstats_queries_total_7d`, `_qstats_start_time_seconds`, `_local_zones{type}`, `_local_data_records`, `_insecure_domains` — all gauges per the rolling-window/resettable backend. `top`/`top_blocked` deliberately unmodelled (unbounded per-domain cardinality), ledger-exempted. Validated against live dev-box captures (real DNSBL policy, real blocked/passed queries) plus a synthetic empty-DB fixture. Five new endpoints (count 113); the three slow-moving diagnostics reads joined the response cache. Dashboard row added to the Unbound tab; full gate green.

Reopened by decision 2026-07-31 as #587. The cardinality rejection here predates the bounded-inventory primitive (#474: hard key cap, time-based retirement, refusal counter), which now handles an equally open set (Zenarmor device names). New scope: default-on (opt-out), 512-key configurable cap. This issue's reasoning was sound for its time and is superseded, not refuted.

Reopened and shipped as #587, landed in `4439d18`.

**This issue's rejection was correct at the time.** It ruled out `top`/`top_blocked` domain leaderboards as unbounded cardinality, and had the endpoint deliberately called with `{max}=1` to shrink them. With no way to bound the key space, that was the right call.

**What changed is the premise, not the judgement.** The bounded-inventory primitive now exists (#474): a hard key cap, time-based retirement, and a `cardinality_capped_total{family}` refusal counter that makes churn-out visible instead of silent. It is already carrying an equally open, adversarial-adjacent key space — Zenarmor device names, including Plex-generated DNS names — at a 512-key cap.

So the leaderboards now ship under that primitive at a 512-key cap, with the endpoint's `{max}` raised from 1 to the same 512 (the two are one constant, because `{max}` binds to the backend's SQL `LIMIT` and a separately configurable cap above it would be inert while looking adjustable).

The residual risk this issue was right to worry about has not vanished — DNS-tunnelling or random-subdomain traffic can still churn genuinely-top entries out of a capped inventory. What is different is that it is now **counted and panelled** rather than unbounded and invisible.

Full detail on #587.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against core Kea controllers (`get_kea_leases.py`, `KeaDhcpv6.xml`).

## Value
We emit Kea lease totals and configured pool sizes but not lease *health*: declined/expired leases (state != 0) indicate address conflicts or DHCPDECLINE storms; IA_NA vs IA_PD breakdown + PD pool capacity give the only visibility into IPv6 prefix-delegation exhaustion; per-subnet lease counts turn `dhcp4_pool_size` into a real utilization ratio.

## Endpoints
| path | method | status | payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api/kea/leases4/search`, `leases6/search` | GET | covered — extend structs | per record: `type` (v6: IA_NA/IA_PD), `state` (0=active, 1=declined, 2=expired-reclaimed), plus a top-level `stats{active, inactive, total}` object our `keaLeaseResponse` currently drops |
| `api/kea/dhcpv6/search_pd_pool` | GET | NEW | config rows `{subnet, prefix, prefix_len, delegated_len}`; capacity = 2^(delegated_len − prefix_len). Cheap config read. |
| `api/kea/dhcpv4|dhcpv6/search_subnet` | GET | covered | used for client-side CIDR matching (lease records carry no subnet id) |

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_kea_dhcp4_leases_by_state{state}` gauge (+ dhcp6 twin) — ≤3 states
- `opnsense_kea_dhcp6_leases_by_type{type}` gauge (IA_NA/IA_PD)
- `opnsense_kea_dhcp6_pd_pool_size{subnet,prefix}` gauge — PD-utilization denominator vs IA_PD count
- `opnsense_kea_dhcp4_pool_used{subnet}` gauge (+ v6 twin) — client-side CIDR match of lease addresses into subnets; joins with existing `dhcp4_pool_size{subnet}`

## Rider — isc-dhcp online aggregate (WEAK, optional)
The legacy plugin's lease rows (already parsed) carry ARP-derived `status: online|offline`; add `opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_online_total` (+v6). No new endpoints. Deprecated plugin — do only while touching these files.

## Implementation notes
- Lease-derived metrics are free (struct additions to already-fetched responses). `search_pd_pool`: new GET, core (NOT plugin-gated), slow-moving → response-cache candidate. Default-on in the existing kea collector.
- Recorded negative findings: OPNsense exposes neither Kea's statistics API (`statistic-get-all`) nor Kea HA runtime state (`status-get`) — pool utilization must be computed client-side; HA health is impossible from the REST surface today.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Kea DHCPv6 with subnet + PD pool + a PD-requesting client (IA_PD rows; `search_pd_pool` row field rendering)
- [ ] Confirm `stats` object shape on `leases4/search`; `state` parses (declined hard to simulate — parse-only OK)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Struct extensions + new endpoint + count bump; metrics; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box confirmation for the first acceptance checkbox: the top-level `stats` object on `kea/leases4/search` and `leases6/search` is confirmed live on OPNsense 26.7 (and on 26.1.11 stable) — shape `stats: {active, inactive, total}`, all JSON **numbers** (not numeric strings), alongside a top-level `interfaces` array. Captured 2026-07-13 during the #236 cross-version work; both keys are currently acknowledged as `knownExtraTopKeys` in `opnsense/testdata/schemas/exemptions.json` — remove those entries when this issue models them. Caveat: the box held zero leases at capture time, so per-row `type`/`state` fields remain unverified (parse-only per the issue body is still the right call); the stats values were all 0 but the key shape is solid.

Landed in b68eadb. Models the confirmed `stats{active,inactive,total}` + `interfaces` keys on the lease searches (both `knownExtraTopKeys` exemptions dropped) and adds: `opnsense_kea_dhcp{4,6}_leases_by_state{state}` and `opnsense_kea_dhcp6_leases_by_type{type}` from per-row fields; `opnsense_kea_dhcp6_pd_pool_size{subnet,prefix}` via the new core `kea/dhcpv6/searchPdPool` endpoint (camelCase form confirmed live — the underscore form also answers, but source uses searchPdPool); and `opnsense_kea_dhcp{4,6}_pool_used{subnet}` from a client-side CIDR join (IA_PD leases excluded, tracked by the PD pool metric). Empty lease tables emit no state/type series. Per-row `type`/`state` and the PD pool row shape are source-derived (get_kea_leases.py, KeaDhcpv6.xml) since the box held zero leases at capture time — tolerant parse-only, flagged in code; the daily live canary will verify once real leases exist. The optional isc-dhcp rider was skipped (different file surface — can be a follow-up if wanted). Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against core captiveportal voucher controller (direct SQLite reads).

## Value
We already export sessions per zone; vouchers are the other operational half of a guest portal. "How many unused vouchers are left" is a real run-out alert; expired-voucher buildup indicates cleanup needed.

## Endpoints (all core GET, not gated)
| path | payload |
|---|---|
| `api/captiveportal/voucher/list_providers` | array of auth-server names with type `voucher` (usually 0–1) |
| `api/captiveportal/voucher/list_voucher_groups/{provider}` | array of group names |
| `api/captiveportal/voucher/list_vouchers/{provider}/{group}` | rows `{username, validity, expirytime, starttime, endtime, state ∈ valid|unused|expired}`. **`username` IS the voucher code — must never appear in a label.** |

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_captiveportal_vouchers{provider, group, state}` gauge
- optional `opnsense_captiveportal_voucher_group_next_expiry_seconds{provider, group}` gauge (min positive expirytime across unused/valid)

## Implementation notes
- Fan-out 1 + P + Σgroups GETs (P almost always ≤1). SQLite reads — cheap. A group can hold up to 10,000 rows → aggregate immediately. Boxes without a voucher server: empty provider list after one cheap GET → fold into existing captiveportal collector default-on (or opt-in if preferred).
- Path-param GETs — no contract-manifest POST change. Not plugin-gated.
- `session/list` duplicates covered `session/search` (same configd call) — skip; `access/*` are client-self-service.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] Voucher auth server + generated group; burn one voucher, let one expire; capture `list_vouchers` payload; confirm empty-provider behavior

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetch fan-out + metrics; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Landed (commit referencing this issue). `opnsense_captiveportal_vouchers{provider,group,state}` (zero-filled valid/unused/expired) + `voucher_group_next_expiry_seconds{provider,group}` (absolute epoch per the existing certificates/qfeeds convention; only when a hard expirytime exists — the common validity-from-first-use case emits nothing). Fan-out over the three core GETs with immediate aggregation (a 10k-voucher group never sits in memory row-by-row). Voucher codes are structurally undecodable — the row struct has no username field, enforced by a reflection test, and fixtures deliberately include codes to prove they are ignored. Bonus infrastructure: `cmd/apidrift` now resolves path-parameterized endpoints (provider/group) from live data, so the daily canary probes these routes properly instead of forever reporting 404-absent. Full gate green; coverage 693/693.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `security/tor` plugin (`tor_diag` Ruby script → control port `GETINFO`).

## Value
A wedged Tor stays "running" with zero built circuits — circuit counts by build status and stream counts by status are the actual health signal, unavailable from service status.

## Endpoints (all GET, os-tor gated)
| path | payload |
|---|---|
| `api/tor/service/circuits` | `{"response": {<circuit_id>: {status (LAUNCHED/BUILT/EXTENDED/FAILED/CLOSED), hosts[], flags{BUILD_FLAGS, PURPOSE, TIME_CREATED}}}}` |
| `api/tor/service/streams` | `{"response": [{stream_id, stream_status (NEW/SUCCEEDED/DETACHED/CLOSED...), circuit_id, destination_host, destination_port}]}` |
| `api/tor/service/get_hidden_services` | `{"response": {<service_name>: "<hostname>.onion" or "not available"}}` — slow-moving |

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_tor_circuits{status}` gauge (aggregate counts; NEVER per-circuit series — ids churn)
- `opnsense_tor_circuits_by_purpose{purpose}` gauge (optional)
- `opnsense_tor_streams{status}` gauge — do NOT label by destination (user-traffic PII + unbounded cardinality)
- `opnsense_tor_hidden_services` gauge + `opnsense_tor_hidden_service_hostname_available{service}` gauge 0/1 — service NAME only, never the .onion hostname (sensitive)

## Implementation notes
- All three into `PluginGatedEndpoints()`. GETs, no contract change. Circuits/streams live (no caching); hidden services cacheable.
- **Control port is optional config**: `tor_diag` returns `{"error": ...}` when the control port isn't set up with a password — treat an `error` key as "no data", not scrape failure.
- Two configd execs (Ruby, dials control port) per scrape + setup dependency → **opt-in `exporter.enable-tor`**.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-tor, control port + password set, one hidden service; capture circuits/streams with live traffic and the no-control-port error shape
- [ ] Verify whether empty HashedControlPassword still authenticates

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetches + collector + opt-in flag; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` + tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box captures (2026-07-13, `captures/tor/`): control port + hashed password configured; circuits/streams captured but bootstrap incomplete (stuck at PROGRESS=5 "Connecting to a relay" — looks like lab egress restriction, so only ONEHOP/internal circuits and NEW-status streams). **Parser landmine found in a real payload**: one streams row has misaligned fields (`{"stream_id":"NEW","stream_status":"0",...}`) — the GETINFO text parsing must defend against column shift. Plugin behavior note: default `SOCKSPolicy reject *` silently drops everything until an explicit SocksACL accept rule exists. Hidden service not provisioned.

Landed in 18da737. New opt-in tor collector (`--exporter.enable-tor`, default off — two extra configd execs per scrape). Aggregate-only gauges: `control_port_up`, `circuits{status}`, `circuits_by_purpose{purpose}`, `streams{status}`, `hidden_services`, `hidden_service_hostname_available{service}`. Sensitive-material handling is structural: destination hosts/ports, circuit/stream IDs and `.onion` hostnames are never parsed into any Go field at all, so they cannot reach labels or error logs. Every status/purpose is vocabulary-checked against torspec's closed set (unknown → `other`) — which also makes the decoder immune to the upstream `tor_diag` bug root-caused during this work: its whitespace-flattened `each_slice(4)` parsing desyncs every row after an unexpected token count (the dev-box misaligned capture is kept as a permanent regression fixture; the analogous circuits `hosts[]` shift is dodged the same way). `{"response":null}` (control port down/bad password) is distinguished from empty (up, idle) so `control_port_up` is honest. Three GET endpoints, plugin-gated; hidden-services body cached, circuits/streams never. New Tor dashboard tab. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `security/crowdsec` plugin (each endpoint = one configd exec of `cscli <thing> list -o json`).

## Value
We already export alert/decision/bouncer/machine counts. The gap is hub hygiene: per-component `status` (enabled / tainted / update-available) for collections, scenarios, parsers, postoverflows, appsec configs/rules — a real upgrade-health signal — plus engine version for fleet dashboards.

## Endpoints (all GET, all os-crowdsec gated)
| path | payload |
|---|---|
| `api/crowdsec/collections/search`, `scenarios/search`, `parsers/search`, `postoverflows/search`, `appsecconfigs/search`, `appsecrules/search` | bootgrid rows `{name, status, local_version, local_path, description}` |
| `api/crowdsec/version/get` | raw multi-line text of `cscli version` (NOT json) |

## Proposed metrics (extend existing crowdsec collector, same `exporter.disable-crowdsec` flag)
- `opnsense_crowdsec_hub_items{component, status}` gauge — count per component per status. Aggregate by status; NEVER per-item name labels (a collection pulls in 50–200 scenarios/parsers).
- `opnsense_crowdsec_version_info{version}` gauge =1 (first version token from the text)

## Implementation notes
- All GET → no contract-manifest changes. All 7 endpoint names into `PluginGatedEndpoints()`.
- Slow-moving (changes on hub update only) → response-cache the successful GETs too; 6–7 cscli execs per scrape is the main cost, near-free with `--exporter.cache-ttl`.
- LAPI down → controllers return `{"message":"unable to retrieve data"}` HTTP-200 — reuse the nil-`Total` envelope handling in `opnsense/crowdsec.go`.
- `status` string vocabulary needs live confirmation — pass through but normalise commas.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-crowdsec with collections installed; taint one item (edit a local scenario file), leave one outdated; capture status strings
- [ ] Capture `cscli version` format; confirm appsec endpoints return empty-but-valid with no appsec configured

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetches + metrics; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` + cache list + tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box captures (2026-07-13, `captures/crowdsec/`): 6 hub collections live; **tainted vocabulary confirmed live** — a locally-modified scenario reports status `"enabled,tainted"` with `local_version` = `"?"`. `version_get` returns raw multi-line `cscli version` TEXT, not JSON (v1.7.8_1). appsec search endpoints return valid empty bootgrids when nothing is configured.

Landed in 8d7fca5. Extends the crowdsec collector with `opnsense_crowdsec_hub_items{component,status}` — installed hub items aggregated by component (collection/scenario/parser/postoverflow/appsec_config/appsec_rule) and normalized status string — plus `opnsense_crowdsec_version_info{version}`. Status strings are comma-token-normalized rather than enumerated: the live-confirmed `"enabled,tainted"` (with `local_version:"?"`) collapses consistently and unknown future tokens (e.g. `update-available`) pass through. `version/get` is raw multi-line cscli TEXT (confirmed live, not JSON) — added a `*[]byte` raw-bytes bypass to the client (first raw-text endpoint) and a `schemaExemptEndpoints` registry so the schema canary does not JSON-parse it; parse failure omits the metric, never fails the scrape. Six new POST bootgrid endpoints (contract manifest now 22 POSTs) + one GET, all plugin-gated; version body positively cached. New Hub Component Health + Engine Version dashboard rows. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `security/clamav` plugin (`versions.sh` scraping `clamconf`).

## Value
Stale ClamAV signatures are a silent failure mode (freshclam broken, mirror unreachable). DB version + built-date + total signatures enable "signatures older than 48h" alerting. Running state is already covered by the services collector; this adds freshness.

## Endpoint
| path | method | gated? | payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api/clamav/service/version` | GET | os-clamav | `{"version": {"clamav": "<clamd version>", "main": "version 62, sigs: N, built on <date>…", "daily": "…", "bytecode": "…", "signatures": "<total>"}}` — free-text strings assembled by a fragile sed/cut pipeline; `.cvd`/`.cld` variants map to the same keys; empty `{}` when clamconf output doesn't parse (freshclam never ran). |

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_clamav_signature_db_version{db=main|daily|bytecode}` gauge
- `opnsense_clamav_signature_db_built_timestamp_seconds{db}` gauge (the point of the exercise)
- `opnsense_clamav_signatures` gauge (DB size, not a counter)
- `opnsense_clamav_version_info{version}` info gauge =1

## Implementation notes
- GET, plugin-gated → 404 = absent (FetchACMECertificates pattern) + `clamavVersion` in `PluginGatedEndpoints()`.
- Slow-moving (changes a few times/day) → ideal response-cache candidate; default-on with caching.
- Parse defensively; emit nothing on parse failure rather than garbage.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-clamav + one freshclam run; capture exact `version` strings (date format, bare-digit `signatures`) — the metric set hinges on these
- [ ] Capture the never-ran shape (empty `{}`)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetch + collector + flag; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` + tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box captures (2026-07-13, `captures/clamav/`): both the post-freshclam real shape AND the never-ran shape. Parser notes: numeric fields arrive as strings with a LEADING SPACE (`"signatures":" 3642597"`, never-ran = `" 0"`); daily/main/bytecode are free-text version strings with embedded build dates (`" version 28059, sigs: 355490, built on Mon Jul 13 07:25:07 2026"`).

Landed in e22020e. New plugin-gated `clamav` collector against `api/clamav/service/version`: `opnsense_clamav_version_info{version}`, `_signatures`, `_signature_db_version{db}` and `_signature_db_built_timestamp_seconds{db}` for daily/main/bytecode. Confirmed against both dev-box captures + a live probe: leading-space numeric strings trimmed, the never-ran shape (db keys absent, `signatures=" 0"`) yields no db series, malformed free-text/dates degrade gracefully (version kept, timestamp omitted) and never fail the scrape, PHP empty-array payloads tolerated. 404 negative-cached via PluginGatedEndpoints, success body in the response cache. Flag `--exporter.disable-clamav` (default on); new ClamAV dashboard tab. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against core `OPNsense/IDS` controllers + backing scripts (`queryAlertLog.py`, `listAlertLogs.py`, `listInstallableRulesets.py`, `lib/rulecache.py`).

## Value
Suricata is the single most operator-relevant subsystem we don't cover at all (0 of 43 endpoints). Targets: "IDS silently died", "rules haven't updated in a week", alert-rate visibility. **IDS is CORE, not a plugin** — endpoints do NOT 404 when unconfigured (status returns `disabled`, data endpoints return empty structures) → do NOT add these to `PluginGatedEndpoints()`.

## Endpoints
| path | method | payload |
|---|---|---|
| `api/ids/service/status` | GET | `{"status":"running|stopped|disabled"}` |
| `api/ids/service/get_alert_logs` | GET | per eve log (incl. rotated `.N`): `{filename, size (bytes), modified ("Y/m/d G:i" local string), sequence}` |
| `api/ids/service/query_alerts` | POST (form) | bootgrid, newest-first eve alert rows: `timestamp, alert_sid, alert_action, alert (signature), src_ip, dest_ip, in_iface, proto`. **`total` saturates at rowCount+1** (script breaks out of the reverse read early) — not a full count. Severity not available. |
| `api/ids/settings/get` | GET | full model; useful: `general.enabled`, `general.ips`, `general.promisc`, `general.interfaces`. Can be large with many per-rule overrides. |
| `api/ids/settings/list_rulesets` | GET | per ruleset: `filename, description, enabled, modified_local ("Y/m/d G:i" or null = never downloaded)` |
| `api/ids/settings/search_installed_rules` | POST (form) | bootgrid over SQLite rule cache: `total_rows` from count(*) — cheap steady-state; first call after a rule update rebuilds the cache (potentially seconds). Supports metadata filters (e.g. `action=drop`). |

## Proposed metrics (`opnsense_ids_*`)
- `opnsense_ids_status` tri-state gauge; `opnsense_ids_ips_mode_enabled` / `opnsense_ids_promiscuous_mode_enabled` gauges 0/1
- `opnsense_ids_alert_log_size_bytes{filename}` gauge + `opnsense_ids_alert_log_files` gauge
- `opnsense_ids_recent_alerts{action=allowed|blocked}` gauge — alerts inside a lookback window (flag, default 15m) counted from `query_alerts` with a capped rowCount (e.g. 500); document the floor semantics when saturated. Gauge by design — a true counter is impossible from this API without unbounded reads.
- `opnsense_ids_ruleset_enabled{ruleset}` gauge + `opnsense_ids_ruleset_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{ruleset}` gauge (parse best-effort, skip null)
- `opnsense_ids_installed_rules_total` gauge (rowCount=1, read `total_rows`)

## Implementation notes
- POSTs (`query_alerts`, `search_installed_rules`) → `postEndpoints` in `opnsense/contract.go` + golden-count bump.
- One collector: status/settings/rulesets default-on; alert-activity part opt-in (`exporter.enable-ids-alerts`) given per-scrape eve-log reverse reads.
- `settings/get` + `list_rulesets` are slow-moving → response-cache candidates.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] IDS enabled on an interface with an ET Open ruleset; trigger alerts (`curl http://testmyids.com`); let eve.json rotate
- [ ] Verify `query_alerts` row shape (timestamp format `2026-07-12T10:11:12.123456+0200`), `total` saturation, `modified_local` format, `settings/get` size with policies, `disabled` status when unconfigured

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetchers + collector + flags; contract-manifest POST entries + count bump
- [ ] `make docs` + dashboard panels (likely a new IDS tab)

comments.body: Dev-box provisioning (2026-07-13): IDS enabled on TESTLAN (pcap=vtnet2), 3 ET Open rulesets downloaded, and a REAL alert triggered and captured via `query_alerts` (`GPL ATTACK_RESPONSE id check returned root`, sid 2100498, alert_action "allowed"). Captures in the session scratchpad `captures/ids/`: service_status, get_alert_logs (eve.json entry), query_alerts, settings_get, list_rulesets (68 total / 3 enabled+downloaded with `modified_local`), search_installed_rules (SQLite bootgrid rows). #231 shares the same query_alerts shape.

Landed in 1be18bf. New core IDS/IPS (Suricata) collector — never plugin-gated (endpoints answer disabled/empty rather than 404). Default-on (`--exporter.disable-ids`): `opnsense_ids_status` (tri-state 1/0/-1), `ips_mode_enabled` (read tolerantly across the ≤26.1 `general.ips` boolean and the 26.7 `general.mode` pcap/netmap/divert selector, exemption-tracked), `promiscuous_mode_enabled`, `alert_log_files` + `alert_log_size_bytes{filename}`, `ruleset_enabled{ruleset}` + `ruleset_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{ruleset}`, `installed_rules_total`. body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `net/relayd` plugin (`StatusController::sumAction` → `relayctl show summary`).

## Value
For boxes using os-relayd as a load balancer this is the only API window into whether backends are actually alive: per-host up/down plus relayd's own availability % from health checks, per table, per virtual server. Niche plugin (HAProxy is the recommended LB) but the one runtime surface it has is complete and cheap.

## Endpoint
| path | method | gated? | payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api/relayd/status/sum` | GET | os-relayd | `rows[]`: per virtual server `{id, type: redirect|relay, name, status, listen_address, ...}`, nested `tables{id → {name, status, hosts{id → {name (address), avlblty (availability %), status (up/down/unknown/"stopped"/"-"), ...}}}}`. Disabled hosts back-filled from config with `avlblty: null`. Top level `{"result": "ok"|"failed"}` — "failed" when relayd stopped. Always call WITHOUT the `wait` param (`wait=1` sleeps up to 10s server-side). |

## Proposed metrics
- `opnsense_relayd_virtualserver_status{name,type}` gauge (map conservatively: only known-good strings → 1)
- `opnsense_relayd_table_active{virtualserver,table}` gauge
- `opnsense_relayd_host_up{virtualserver,table,host,address}` gauge
- `opnsense_relayd_host_availability_percent{virtualserver,table,host,address}` gauge (omit when null; strip `%`)

## Implementation notes
- GET → no contract change. Add `relaydStatusSum` to `defaultEndpoints()` + `PluginGatedEndpoints()`. New collector, `exporter.disable-relayd` default-on (trivial cost, 404-cached when absent). `result:"failed"` = "present but no data", not an error. Never cache success. Cardinality: LB topology, small. `service/status` + `settings/*` add nothing (services collector covers running state).

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-relayd with one redirect + 2-host table (one dead); capture status strings, `avlblty` format, stopped-service shape vs plugin-absent 404

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetch + collector + disable flag wiring; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` + tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box baseline (2026-07-13, `captures/relayd/`): fetch-layer gotchas confirmed live — settings search nodeTypes are `host`/`table`/`tablecheck`/`virtualserver`/`protocol` (NOT relay/redirect), set/get take the nodeType as a URL path segment, and the `settings/set` response wrapper reports `"result":"failed"` even on success (trust the paired `"status":"ok"` / a follow-up GET instead). relayd correctly stays STOPPED with configtest "no actions, nothing to do" until a real topology exists — populated `status/sum` capture comes with the heavy-topology provisioning pass.

Dev-box heavy-topology captures (2026-07-13, `captures/relayd/`): real topology (table with 2 hosts, TCP tablecheck, redirect virtualserver) — `status_sum_populated.json` shows virtualserver `active`, table `active (2 hosts)`, both hosts `up` @100.00% availability, plus populated settings searches. Confirms the earlier fetch-layer note: `settings/set` returns `{"result":"failed","status":"ok"}` even on success — trust `status`. Also for the record: the redirect was inert until a `firewall/filter/apply` picked up the `rdr-anchor "relayd/*"` line.

Landed (commit referencing this issue). New plugin-gated relayd collector reading `relayd/status/sum`: `virtualserver_status{name,type}`, `table_active{virtualserver,table}`, `host_up{virtualserver,table,host,address}`, `host_availability_percent`. State mapping is source-verified against OpenBSD relayctl.c — `active*`/`up` → 1, everything else including unknown future strings → 0; availability omitted (not zeroed) until relayd has checked the host; internal `:port` suffixes stripped so table labels match GUI names. Plugin-absent (404) and present-but-stopped (`result:"failed"`) both emit nothing. The settings search endpoints were deliberately NOT added — status/sum already embeds all names (confirmed vs StatusController source). Flag `--exporter.disable-relayd` (default on); new Relayd dashboard tab. Fixtures are the real populated topology captures + stopped shape. Full gate green.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `net/haproxy` plugin (StatisticsController → queryStats.php over `/var/run/haproxy.socket`).

## Part 1 — stick-table occupancy (1 new endpoint)
| path | method | gated? | payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api/haproxy/statistics/tables` | GET | os-haproxy | `show table` parsed: array of `{"table": <name>, "type": ip|integer|string|binary, "size": "204800", "used": "1"}` (all strings). Service stopped → `null` body (same tolerance as existing haproxy fetch). |

- `opnsense_haproxy_stick_table_size{table,type}` gauge; `opnsense_haproxy_stick_table_used{table,type}` gauge

A stick table at capacity silently stops tracking entries → rate limiting degrades with no other signal. Completes the statistics-controller trio we already scrape (counters, info). Add `haproxyTables` to `defaultEndpoints()` + `PluginGatedEndpoints()`; fetch concurrently with the existing calls; never cache success.

## Part 2 — extend counters/info parsing (zero new endpoints)
`show stat` rows we already fetch carry unparsed columns: `qtime/ctime/rtime/ttime` (avg queue/connect/response/total times over last 1024 reqs), `chkdown` (UP→DOWN transitions), `lastchg`, `slim`, `req_tot`, `lbtot`, `cli_abrt`/`srv_abrt`; `show info` carries `Maxconn`, `SslCurrConns`.

Proposed (curated):
- `opnsense_haproxy_backend_{queue,connect,response,total}_time_avg_seconds` gauges `{backend}` + same four for servers `{backend,server}` (ms→s)
- `opnsense_haproxy_server_check_downs_total` counter `{backend,server}`; `opnsense_haproxy_server_last_state_change_seconds` gauge
- `opnsense_haproxy_frontend_requests_total` counter `{frontend}`; `opnsense_haproxy_frontend_session_limit` gauge (saturation vs existing `scur`)
- `opnsense_haproxy_backend_selected_total` counter `{backend}`; `opnsense_haproxy_backend_aborts_total` counter `{backend, side=client|server}`
- `opnsense_haproxy_connection_limit` gauge; optionally `opnsense_haproxy_ssl_current_connections` gauge

Follow the #164 empty-string rule: tcp-mode proxies leave these cells empty — omit the series, never fabricate 0.

## Warning recorded for posterity
The `maintenance/*` controller endpoints look like status reads but are POST-only AND fire `configdRun('template reload ...')` on every call — config-regenerating side effect per scrape. Never scrape anything in that controller. No cert-expiry data exists in this module (cert expiry = trust collector).

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-haproxy: frontend with `stick-table type ip size 100k` + traffic so `used > 0`; confirm parsed key names
- [ ] HTTP-mode backend with 2 servers; kill one to see `chkdown`/`lastchg` move; confirm tcp-mode empty cells

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] tables fetch + struct extension + metrics; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` entry
- [ ] `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box heavy-topology captures (2026-07-13, `captures/haproxy/`): frontend with `stick-table type ip size 100k` + backend with 2 real servers and HTTP healthchecks. `stats_tables.json` shows `used:1`; `stats_counters_populated.json` has real `qtime/ctime/rtime/ttime` + per-server `stot`; `stats_counters_chkdown.json` captures a live DOWN transition (`chkdown:1`, `status:DOWN`) from killing one backend. CRUD API matched source 1:1.

Landed (commit referencing this issue). Part 1: plugin-gated `haproxy/statistics/tables` with `stick_table_{size,used}{table,type}` — table-level occupancy only, fetched concurrently with counters/info and tolerated absent on older builds. Part 2 (no new endpoints): backend+server qtime/ctime/rtime/ttime as gauges (rolling averages, ms→s), `server_check_downs_total` (chkdown) + `server_last_state_change_seconds` (lastchg), frontend `requests_total` + `session_limit`, backend `selected_total` + `aborts_total{side}`, and `connection_limit`/`ssl_current_connections` from show info (the real key is CurrSslConns, not the issue's SslCurrConns guess). Empty CSV cells omit series per the existing #164 rule. Regression fixtures are the real dev-box captures including the live UP→DOWN transition. Full gate green; coverage 715/715.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against `www/nginx` plugin (vts.php, BansController, vts.conf template, ngx_autoblock.php).

## Part 1 — extend the VTS collector (zero new API calls)
We scrape `api/nginx/service/vts` but decode only a subset. The same payload carries:
- `cacheZones.<zone>`: `maxSize`, `usedSize`, `inBytes`, `outBytes`, `responses{miss,bypass,expired,stale,updating,revalidated,hit,scarce}` — one per configured `proxy_cache_path` (zone names are cache_path uuids without dashes)
- `serverZones.<zone>.responses` cache-status counters (same 8 keys) alongside the 1xx–5xx we already read
- `serverZones.<zone>.requestMsecCounter` and `upstreamZones.<up>[i].requestMsecCounter`/`responseMsecCounter` — cumulative latency counters (we only export the `responseMsec` moving average today)
- top-level `loadMsec` (config-load timestamp → reload detection), `nginxVersion`

Proposed (extend `opnsense/nginx.go` + `internal/collector/nginx.go`):
- `opnsense_nginx_cache_zone_max_bytes` / `_used_bytes` gauges `{zone}`; `_bytes_in_total` / `_bytes_out_total` counters `{zone}`; `_responses_total` counter `{zone, cache_status}`
- `opnsense_nginx_server_zone_cache_responses_total` counter `{zone, cache_status}`
- `opnsense_nginx_server_zone_request_seconds_total` counter `{zone}` (cumulative in source → MUST be counter; true per-vhost avg latency via rate()/rate())
- `opnsense_nginx_upstream_server_request_seconds_total` / `_response_seconds_total` counters `{upstream, server}`
- `opnsense_nginx_config_load_timestamp_seconds` gauge

No new endpoint, no contract change, no new flag; gating/404 handling already in place. Emit cache metrics only when maps present (older vts / no cache configured).

## Part 2 — autoblock ban count (1 new endpoint)
| path | method | gated? | payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api/nginx/bans/searchban` | GET/POST (searchBase) | os-nginx | paged rows of the `ban` ArrayField: `{ip, time (unix ban timestamp)}` + `total`. Runtime state despite living in config: rows created by the autoblock cron, TTL-expired. |

- `opnsense_nginx_bans` gauge (from `total`; no per-IP labels — unbounded)
- optional `opnsense_nginx_ban_last_timestamp_seconds` gauge (max `time`)
- Avoid `bans/get` (returns the entire nginx model). If POST is used, add to `postEndpoints` + bump golden count; validate on dev box whether plain GET returns the full rowset. Add `nginxBans` to `PluginGatedEndpoints()`.

## Explicit skips (recorded here so they aren't re-litigated)
`settings/*` (config CRUD, no runtime fields), `settings/testconfig` (runs `nginx -t` per call), `logs/*` (paged log readers — Loki territory; `tls_handshakes` is an unbounded fingerprint-log dump).

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-nginx: HTTP server + upstream + `cache_path` with proxy_cache on a location; drive traffic
- [ ] Confirm `cacheZones` key shape (uuid zone names — relabel via settings lookup or keep raw?)
- [ ] Confirm `requestMsecCounter`/`responseMsecCounter` exist in the shipped vts build; re-verify fields we already decode
- [ ] Seed an autoblock ban; capture `searchban` GET vs POST shape

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] VTS struct/collector extension + bans fetch; metrics above
- [ ] Contract-manifest updates if POST chosen; `PluginGatedEndpoints()` for bans
- [ ] `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box heavy-topology captures (2026-07-13, `captures/nginx/`): vhost + 2-server upstream + proxy_cache zone + live autoblock ban. `vts_populated.json` has cache hit=20/miss=3, per-upstream-server `requestMsecCounter`/`responseMsecCounter`; `bans_populated.json` has a real ban row `{ip,time}`. Provisioning-side gotchas for the record: `addhttpserver` POST body key is `httpserver` (not `http_server`); `upstream_server.priority` maps to nginx `weight=` and 0 silently breaks the generated config.

Landed (commit referencing this issue). VTS extensions: cache-zone size/used gauges + bytes and responses{zone,cache_status} counters, server-zone cache-status counters (presence-gated on the vts build actually reporting cache status — no fabricated zeros), request-time totals, per-upstream-server request/response second totals, and `config_load_timestamp_seconds` from loadMsec (exemption dropped). New plugin-gated GET `nginx/bans/searchban` — confirmed GET live — with bans count + last-ban timestamp; banned IPs never become labels. The responses object is modeled as three distinct struct shapes (server/cache/upstream) so golden schemas never claim fields a zone type cannot send — no false drift noise. Fixtures are the real heavy-topology captures. Full gate green; coverage 731/731.

body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against OPNsense plugins master.

## Value
Route-table size by protocol is the classic "did my routes disappear / did something start leaking" trend signal — catches redistribution accidents and neighbor loss even when sessions look up. LSDB size trends catch LSA storms.

## Endpoints (all GET, os-frr gated; bootgrid search endpoints accept GET query params `?current=1&rowCount=-1` → zero contract-manifest changes)
| path | payload |
|---|---|
| `api/quagga/diagnostics/search_generalroute4` / `search_generalroute6` | zebra RIB (`show ip[v6] route json`), flattened one row **per nexthop** (`prefix`, `protocol`, `selected`, `installed`, `distance`, `metric`, `interfaceName`) — dedupe by `prefix` for a route count |
| `api/quagga/diagnostics/search_ospfroute` / `search_ospfv3route` | OSPF route tables, per-nexthop rows with `type`/`network`/`cost`/`area` |
| `api/quagga/diagnostics/ospfdatabase` | `show ip ospf database json`: per-area LSA lists by type |
| `api/quagga/diagnostics/search_ospfv3database` | per-LSA rows with `dbname` (scope), `areaId`, `interface` |

## Proposed metrics — aggregates ONLY, computed in the collector; never per-prefix/per-LSA series
- `opnsense_frr_route_count` gauge `{af=ipv4|ipv6, protocol}` (distinct prefixes; protocol set is FRR-fixed)
- `opnsense_frr_route_nexthop_count` gauge `{af, protocol}` (ECMP width; optional)
- `opnsense_frr_ospf_route_count` gauge `{type}`; `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_route_count` gauge
- `opnsense_frr_ospf_lsa_count` gauge `{area, lsa_type}`; `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_lsa_count` gauge `{scope}`

## Implementation notes
- **Opt-in `exporter.enable-frr-routes`** (default-off): payload size scales with route count and the PHP flattens the whole table per request — harmless on a homelab RIB, expensive with a full BGP feed. `search_bgproute4/6` deliberately EXCLUDED (catastrophic with a real BGP table; RIB size per AF already covered by `opnsense_frr_bgp_rib_entries`).
- Up to 6 extra vtysh execs per scrape when enabled. All names into `PluginGatedEndpoints()`. No success caching.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] FRR lab + static routes + `redistribute connected` so tables have multiple protocols
- [ ] Verify generalroute `protocol` values and ECMP row multiplication (confirms dedupe-by-prefix)
- [ ] Confirm `ospfdatabase` JSON key names per LSA type

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Opt-in flag + wiring test; fetchers; aggregation in collector
- [ ] `PluginGatedEndpoints()` entries + tests; `make docs` + dashboard panels

comments.body: Dev-box captures (2026-07-13, `captures/frr/`): RIB/LSDB populated with protocol diversity via `redistribute connected` both sides — `search_generalroute4.json` (+v6), `search_ospfroute.json`, `ospfdatabase.json`; 48 rows spanning kernel/connected/local/ospf/bgp. Shapes matched the issue expectations.

Landed in c846f42 (shared FRR lane), opt-in via `--exporter.enable-frr-routes` (default off). Zebra RIB volumes `route_count{af,protocol}` (prefix-deduped) + `route_nexthop_count` (ECMP width), OSPF/OSPFv3 route-table counts by type, and LSDB volumes `ospf_lsa_count{area,lsa_type}` / `ospfv3_lsa_count{scope}` — aggregates only, never per-prefix/per-LSA. `search_bgproute4/6` excluded per the issue. Deviation worth noting: skipped the `?current=1&rowCount=-1` query string — OPNsense's searchRecordsetBase defaults rowCount to 9999 on a bare GET, which let all six endpoints register cleanly on PluginGatedEndpoints() without the query-vs-cache-key mismatch vnstat hit. Verified against the real 48-row multi-protocol RIB capture. Full gate green.
