body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against OPNsense plugins master (`net/frr` DiagnosticsController → vtysh JSON via configd).

## Value
We see OSPF per-area and per-neighbor but not per-interface (where cost, DR/BDR role and adjacency counts live), and we have zero OSPFv3 visibility — an IPv6-routed site is blind. Brings ospf6d up to par with ospfd coverage.

## Endpoints
| path | method | gated? | payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api/quagga/diagnostics/ospfinterface` | GET | os-frr | `show ip ospf interface json`. FRR ≥8 wraps per-iface objects in `"interfaces":{}` (older FRR top-level — decode both). Per iface: `ifUp`, `ospfEnabled`, `area`, `networkType`, `cost`, `state` (DR/Backup/DROther/...), `priority`, `nbrCount`, `nbrAdjacentCount`, `mtuBytes`, `bandwidthMbit`. |
| `api/quagga/diagnostics/ospfv3overview` | GET | os-frr | `show ipv6 ospf6 json`: `routerId`, `running`, spf timers, `areas{<id>}` with area-scoped LSA counts. Exact key names uncertain — capture on dev box before coding structs. |
| `api/quagga/diagnostics/ospfv3interface` | GET | os-frr | `show ipv6 ospf6 interface json`: per iface `status`, `type`, `area`, `cost`, `priority`, `state`, DR/BDR, `numberOfInterfaceScopedLsa`, `pendingLsaLsUpdateCount`, `pendingLsaLsAckCount`. Note: the API exposes NO OSPFv3 neighbor endpoint — interface state is the best available proxy. |

## Proposed metrics (per-interface = bounded by NIC count)
- `opnsense_frr_ospf_interface_up` gauge `{interface, area}`; `_cost` gauge; `_neighbors` gauge; `_neighbors_adjacent` gauge; `_state` enum-style gauge `{interface, state}` (fixed set: DR/BDR/DROther/PointToPoint/Waiting/Down)
- `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_interface_up` / `_cost` / `_state` — same shape for ospf6
- `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_area_lsa_count` gauge `{area}` (v3 parity with existing `ospf_area_lsa_count`)
- `opnsense_frr_ospfv3_interface_pending_lsa` gauge `{interface, queue=update|ack}` (flooding backlog)

## Implementation notes
- 3 GETs, no contract change; +3 vtysh execs per scrape. Default-on (matches existing OSPF coverage; small payloads). All three names into `PluginGatedEndpoints()`.
- Daemon disabled → configd returns `[]` — reuse existing array-fallback tolerance. Timer config fields deliberately excluded.

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] ospfd + ospf6d enabled with one interface each and a neighbor (companion FRR) so nbr counts/DR election are non-trivial
- [ ] Capture all three JSON payloads + with each daemon disabled
- [ ] Pin exact ospf6 overview/interface key names (least-certain payload here)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetchers + endpoint registrations + count bump
- [ ] Metrics emitted; absent fields → no series
- [ ] `PluginGatedEndpoints()` entries + tests
- [ ] `make docs` + dashboard panels

Per the run policy: OSPFv3 field shapes come from FRR/plugin source, tolerant, with the captured empty shape as the absent fixture.

Landed in c846f42 (shared FRR lane). OSPF: `interface_up/cost/neighbors/neighbors_adjacent{interface,area}` + enum-style `interface_state{interface,state}` — verified live at Full/DR on FRR 10.3's interfaces-wrapped shape (legacy flat shape decoded tolerantly). OSPFv3 parity (`ospf6d`): overview/interface fetches + up/cost/state, area LSA counts and pending update/ack queues — **unverified against a live v3 adjacency** (the lab LXC has no IPv6 stack; only the disabled/empty shape was captured), field names grounded in FRR ospf6d C source and flagged in a verification banner in opnsense/frr.go per the code-tolerantly policy. body:
Part of the API-surface roadmap (see tracker issue). Source-verified against OPNsense plugins master (`net/frr`, `DiagnosticsController.php` → `vtysh -c 'show ... json'` via configd).

## Value
`bgpsummary` (covered) tells you a peer is down; `bgpneighbors` tells you how often and why. `connectionsEstablished`/`connectionsDropped` are the canonical BGP flap counters, per-message-type counters separate keepalive noise from UPDATE churn, and `lastResetTimerMsecs` lets you alert on "peer reset recently" even if it re-established between scrapes.

## Endpoint
| path | method | gated? | payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api/quagga/diagnostics/bgpneighbors` | GET | os-frr (404 when absent) | `{"response": {<peerIP>: {...}}}` — raw `show bgp neighbors json`. Per peer: `bgpState`, `remoteAs`, `bgpTimerUpMsec`, `connectionsEstablished`, `connectionsDropped`, `lastResetTimerMsecs`, `lastResetDueTo` (free string), `messageStats{...Sent/Recv, depthInq, depthOutq}`, `addressFamilyInfo{<af>:{acceptedPrefixCounter,...}}`. Empty `[]` when bgpd disabled. |

## Proposed metrics (per-peer; same cardinality class as existing `bgp_peer_up`)
- `opnsense_frr_bgp_peer_connections_established_total` counter `{peer}`
- `opnsense_frr_bgp_peer_connections_dropped_total` counter `{peer}`
- `opnsense_frr_bgp_peer_messages_by_type_total` counter `{peer, type=open|update|keepalive|notification|route_refresh|capability, direction=sent|received}` (distinct name from the existing aggregate `bgp_peer_messages_*_total`)
- `opnsense_frr_bgp_peer_last_reset_seconds` gauge `{peer}` (`lastResetTimerMsecs/1000`; `lastResetDueTo` goes in a log line, NOT a label — unbounded values)
- `opnsense_frr_bgp_peer_prefixes_accepted` gauge `{peer, af}` (post-policy; complements existing pre-policy `bgp_peer_prefixes_received`; reuse `frrAFLabel()`)
- `opnsense_frr_bgp_peer_queue_depth` gauge `{peer, direction=in|out}`

## Implementation notes
- GET → no `postEndpoints`/contract-manifest change. Add `quaggaBgpNeighbors` to `PluginGatedEndpoints()`.
- +1 configd/vtysh exec per scrape — cheap; default-on, fold into the existing `frr` collector.
- No success-body caching (live counters). Decode defensively — FRR renames fields across versions (hazard already documented in `opnsense/frr.go`).

## Dev-box validation (#195)
- [ ] os-frr installed, bgpd enabled, peered with a companion FRR instance (second VM/container); one peer Established
- [ ] Bounce the session once so `connectionsDropped`/`lastReset*` are non-zero
- [ ] Capture JSON for Established + Active/Idle peers, and with bgpd disabled (expect `[]`)
- [ ] Same lab session should re-validate the existing unverified shapes in `opnsense/frr.go` (see its VERIFICATION banner)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `FetchFRRBGPNeighbors` (or extended `FetchFRRBGP`) + endpoint registered, count bumped
- [ ] Metrics above emitted, omitting series when fields absent

body:
## Mission

Close the payload-shape blind spot in our OPNsense API drift detection by standing up a
**development-channel OPNsense VM** and turning the response-contract layer into a real
live-box canary.

## Where we are today (assessment, 2026-07-12)

**1. Endpoint-manifest canary — `cmd/apicontract` + `tools/opnsense_api_contract/extract.py`
(`.github/workflows/api-contract.yml`). Healthy.**

- Clones `opnsense/core` + `opnsense/plugins` at `master` **and** the latest `stable/*` branch,
  runs OPNsense's own docs parser (pinned by SHA, Renovate-bumped) over the PHP API controllers,
  and diffs the result against our 107-endpoint manifest (derived from `defaultEndpoints()`, so
  it cannot drift from the live client).
- Missing path = hard failure + opens/updates the `api-drift` issue. GET-we-issue that source no
  longer advertises = warning, files the issue, does not fail.
- `master` **is** OPNsense's development branch, so this already gives us pre-release visibility
  for endpoint renames and verb changes. A dev box adds nothing here.
- Guardrails are good: `--min 200` floor, pytest fixture guarding docs-lib churn, per-controller
  fault isolation, label+title issue dedupe, auto-close when clean.
- Run history is green; no open `api-drift` issues.

**2. Response-shape contracts — `opnsense/response_contract.go` / `TestResponseContracts`. Weak.**

- Covers **5 of 107 endpoints** (`healthCheck`, `gatewaysStatus`, `pfStates`, `unboundDNSStatus`,
  `firmware`).
- Validates against **committed fixtures**, not a live box. So it fails when *we* change a struct;
  it can never fail because *OPNsense* changed a payload. A fixture captured from 26.1 passes
  forever even after 26.7 reshapes the JSON. It is a regression guard, not a canary.

**3. `cmd/apicapture` / `make capture`.** Manual, local, writes to a gitignored dir. Nothing
scheduled ever touches a real box.

### The gap

The source-diff canary sees **paths and verbs only**. Every OPNsense change that has actually bitten
this exporter was a *payload* change at an unchanged path and verb:

- 26.1 moving per-subsystem health into a top-level `subsystems` map
- `metadata.system.status` becoming the string `"ERROR"`
- the status-`"2"` enum issue still in the backlog

All structurally invisible to the canary, and the layer that would catch them covers 4.7% of the
surface against frozen fixtures.

Secondary gaps:

- The four **exempt endpoints** (`firmware`, `firmwareInfo`, `keaLeases4`, `keaLeases6`) have
  **zero** automated coverage of any kind — the code comments in `cmd/apicontract/main.go` admit
  this. `firmware` is now cached for 12h, which raises the blast radius.
- The parser cannot say anything about **plugin-gated endpoints** on a real box (200 vs 404), nor
  about auth/permission changes or HTTP-status changes.

## Scope

### Phase 0 — cheap wins, no VM needed

- [x] Endpoint-manifest canary moved from weekly (Mon 06:17 UTC) to **daily** 06:17 UTC.
- [ ] Confirm the daily schedule fires and stays green for a week (no new noise, no rate-limit
      trouble cloning core+plugins twice a day).

### Phase 1 — stand up the dev box

- [ ] OPNsense VM on the homelab, switched to the **Development** release channel (tracks `master`,
      i.e. the same ref the endpoint canary already diffs — so the two layers line up).
- [ ] Install the plugins the exporter has collectors for, so plugin-gated endpoints are actually
      exercised rather than silently 404ing. (Deliberate setup work; without it those endpoints
      stay uncovered.)
- [ ] API key/secret issued for a read-only account; reachable from CI over the tailnet.

Setup instructions: see the comment below.

### Phase 2 — generic schema canary (the real payoff)

- [ ] **Auto-derive** the expected schema per endpoint by reflecting over the existing `json` tags
      on our response structs, rather than hand-writing 107 validators. Emit a committed golden
      schema per endpoint: **key paths + value types only, no values**.
- [ ] Scheduled CI job: join the tailnet (`tailscale/github-action`), run `apicapture` against the
      devel box for all 107 endpoints, diff the live payload structure against the golden schema.
      New key / vanished key / type change → drift report → reuse the **existing `api-drift` issue
      machinery** (label, dedupe, auto-close) rather than inventing a second channel.
- [ ] This covers the four exempt endpoints too — the only coverage they will ever have.

### Phase 3 — end-to-end smoke

- [ ] Point the actual exporter at the devel box; assert **zero fetch errors** and metric count
      above a baseline. Cheap, high signal, and would have caught the 26.1 health regression on
      day one.

## Constraints / decisions already made

- **Captures must never land in the repo with values.** They contain host/network data. Golden
  schemas are structure-only (key paths + types); raw captures stay in the gitignored scratch dir.
  This repo is public — treat it as a leak vector.
- **Reuse the `api-drift` issue machinery**, do not build a parallel reporting path.
- Do **not** hand-write per-endpoint validators at 107x. Reflect over the struct tags.
- The endpoint-manifest canary stays as-is. It is not the problem and the dev box does not replace it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A payload-shape change on the devel box (new/renamed/retyped key) on **any** of the 107
      endpoints produces an `api-drift` issue within 24h.
- [ ] The four exempt endpoints are covered by the schema canary.
- [ ] No response values (host/network data) are committed to the repo.
- [ ] The endpoint-manifest canary still runs daily and green.

## Dev-box setup instructions (Phase 1)

### 1. VM

Grab an image from https://opnsense.org/download/ — pick the **VGA** flavour (`amd64`, `vga`) for a
VM; it gives a console you can drive and then the web UI over HTTPS. (`dvd` also works; `nano` and
`serial` are for embedded/serial-console boxes and aren't what you want here.)

Sizing: 2 vCPU / 4 GB RAM / 20 GB disk is comfortable for a lab box that will have most plugins
installed. Two NICs (WAN + LAN) — the installer expects to assign both; a second NIC on an isolated
bridge is fine, it doesn't have to route anything real.

Install, then **default credentials are `root` / `opnsense`** — change the password immediately.

Refs:
- Install guide: https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/install.html
- Hardware sizing: https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/hardware.html

### 2. Switch to the Development channel

**System → Firmware → Settings → Release Type → `Development`**, then run an update
(**System → Firmware → Updates → Check for updates**).

This is the key step. The Development channel tracks **`master` on GitHub** — the same ref our
endpoint-manifest canary already diffs — so the two layers line up: the canary tells us an endpoint
moved, the dev box tells us a payload reshaped, both ahead of the stable release.

Docs are blunt about it: *"Please leave this setting on 'Production', unless you fully understand the
implications of switching."* That's exactly what we want here and it's why this must be a
throwaway lab VM, never anything on the live path.

Refs:
- Firmware settings: https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/firmware.html
- Updates: https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/updates.html

To keep it current, either leave auto-update off and let a cron on the host run
`opnsense-update -a && /usr/local/etc/rc.reboot`, or just refresh it by hand periodically — a stale
devel box is a canary that has quietly stopped singing, so it's worth a reminder either way.

### 3. Install the plugins the exporter has collectors for

Without these the plugin-gated endpoints just 404 and we cover nothing. From
**System → Firmware → Plugins**, install the `os-*` plugins backing the endpoints in
`PluginGatedEndpoints()` (`opnsense/cache.go`):

`os-acme-client`, `os-apcupsd`, `os-chrony`, `os-collectd`, `os-crowdsec`, `os-dnsmasq` (if not
core on the devel build), `os-ddclient` (dyndns), `os-haproxy`, `os-kea` (if not core), `os-monit`,
`os-nginx`, `os-nut`, `os-frr` (quagga/bfd/bgp/ospf), `os-qfeeds`, `os-tailscale`,
`os-wireguard` (if not core), `os-smart`.

Then actually *configure* enough of each to make it return a non-empty body — an installed-but-empty
plugin returns a valid-but-degenerate payload, which validates a schema we can't trust. Chrony wants
a source, HAProxy wants a backend, and so on. This is the genuinely tedious part of the phase and
it's worth doing properly once.

### 4. API credentials

**System → Access → Users →** create a user (e.g. `exporter-canary`), give it a read-only group with
the effective privileges the exporter needs, then **+** under *API keys* to generate a key/secret
pair. It downloads as an `apikey.txt`. Feed it to `cmd/apicapture` the same way the exporter takes
it — `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_OPS_API_KEY` / `_SECRET`, or the `OPS_API_KEY_FILE` / `OPS_API_SECRET_FILE`
file-based secrets, which `apicapture` already resolves via `internal/options`.

Ref: https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/how-tos/api.html

Local smoke test before wiring any CI:

```
make capture   # cmd/apicapture, writes to the gitignored opnsense/testdata/captures/
```

### 5. Reachability from CI

The box lives on the tailnet. Have the workflow join with `tailscale/github-action` using an
ephemeral, tagged auth key (or an OAuth client scoped to a tag), and ACL that tag to reach only the
dev box on 443. Do **not** put the box on the public internet, and do **not** put the API secret
anywhere but repo secrets.

### 6. Then Phase 2

Once `make capture` returns clean payloads for all 107 endpoints from the box, the generic schema
canary in Phase 2 has something to diff against.

The API-surface roadmap (#227) is now the main consumer of this dev box. Its tracker body carries an aggregated shopping list of plugins/configs to enable for payload validation (FRR lab, IDS + ET Open, os-nginx with proxy_cache, haproxy stick tables, Kea PD pools, monit checks of every type, LACP lagg + SFP DOM NIC, etc.). Several roadmap issues are explicitly blocked on dev-box payload captures before structs get coded: #219 (monit), #198 (ospf6 JSON keys), #211 (netbird), #204 (clamav version strings), #216 (lldp text fixtures).

## Phase 1 done: the devel box is up and exercising every collector

The VM is built and configured. Headline: **47/47 collectors green, 513/571 catalogue metrics emitting, zero fetch errors, zero failed collectors** on a full scrape with every opt-in flag enabled.

That is the number that matters for this issue. The whole point of the box is that a payload-shape change upstream should break a *test*, and a collector that never returns data can't do that. 513 of the 571 metrics in the catalogue now have live values coming off a real firewall rather than a hand-written fixture.

### What it took beyond "install OPNsense"

Standing the box up was the easy part. Getting collectors to emit non-empty data meant actually *using* the features:

- **A second machine.** ARP, NDP, DHCP leases, pf states, netflow, unbound stats and firewall rule hits are all zero on a firewall with nothing behind it. There is now a small container on an isolated segment running a per-minute loop (DNS, HTTP, ICMP, inter-VLAN) so those collectors always have something to report.
- **Loopback VPN topologies.** Two WireGuard instances peer with *each other* over localhost — real handshakes, real transfer counters. Likewise an OpenVPN server plus an OpenVPN client connecting back to it, which yields a genuine connected session with byte counts. IPsec has a full connection/child/pool/PSK config, so the config-side endpoints return data even though no tunnel completes (no peer).
- **Fake hardware.** The UPS collectors need a UPS. There is now a `dummy-ups` driver behind a local NUT server, and a small hand-written apcupsd NIS server, so both UPS collectors return plausible readings.
- **Every plugin installed *and configured*.** Installing `os-haproxy` gets you a 200 with an empty body; you only get real counters once a frontend, backend and server exist. Same for nginx (needs a server block plus traffic before VTS reports zones), FRR (needs BGP/OSPF/BFD neighbours), CrowdSec, chrony, monit, ACME, ddclient, captive portal and the traffic shaper.

### What is still missing, and why

The remaining 58 metrics need things a single VM structurally cannot produce:

| Group | Count | Blocker |
|---|---|---|
| IPsec phase 2 | 16 | Needs a peer that completes phase 2 |
| SMART | 12 | Virtual disk; also hit what looks like an upstream `os-smart` bug (below) |
| QFeeds | 8 | Commercial feed licence |
| Tailscale peers | 5 | Needs a tailnet join |
| HA sync | 5 | Needs a second box |
| FRR uptimes/adjacency | 3 | Needs established neighbours |
| ZFS ARC, temperature | 2 | Do not exist on this VM |

Most of these are reachable later (a second VM would unlock IPsec phase 2, HA sync and FRR in one go — worth doing, but it is not blocking the schema canary).

### Findings the box produced on day one

It has already earned its keep as a bug-finder, which is a good sign for the premise of this issue:

1. **`api/smart/service/list` returns `{"message":"Unable to run list action"}`** on a SCSI/virtio disk, while `configctl smart list` and `smartctl --scan` both enumerate the device fine. Looks like a genuine upstream `os-smart` bug rather than anything on our side. Worth reporting.
2. **`upsc` in nut 2.8.5 segfaults**, which makes the NUT API return an empty body — so `opnsense_nut_*` would be silently absent on any box running that build. Worked around locally with a shim; the exporter handles the empty response gracefully, which is the right behaviour, but it is worth knowing the metric can vanish for reasons that have nothing to do with us.
3. **Pointing the netflow collector's target at the box itself creates a feedback loop.** `samplicate` fans its own packets back into flowd; it wrote a 51 GB log and pinned two cores in about half an hour. Not an exporter bug, but a sharp edge for anyone configuring netflow, and a reminder that the flowd log is deleted-but-open until you kill the daemons.

### Next

Phase 2 (the generic schema canary) is unblocked. The box is on the stable channel for now, deliberately — the plan was always to max out collector coverage first, then switch the release type to Development so the box tracks the same `master` the endpoint canary already diffs. That switch is a one-liner and comes next, along with the CI wiring to reach the box from a workflow run.

## Update: IPsec phase 2 solved without a second firewall — **534/571**

Coverage is now **534/571 catalogue metrics, 47/47 collectors, zero errors**. Two of the blockers in the table above turned out not to be blockers.

### IPsec phase 2 (was: "needs a peer that completes phase 2")

It does need a peer — but the peer can be the traffic-generator container, not a second firewall. strongSwan runs in the (unprivileged) container as the **initiator**; the firewall is the **responder**, handing out a virtual IP from an address pool. The child SA comes up INSTALLED with real SPIs, and pushing traffic across it gives genuine non-zero byte and packet counters rather than an established-but-idle tunnel.

Two things make it work, and they are the bits worth writing down:

- XFRM is network-namespace-aware, so an unprivileged container **can** drive IPsec — but only if the **host** has the modules loaded (`esp4`, `ah4`, `xfrm_user`, `af_key`, `tunnel4`). Without them the container fails in a way that looks like a config error.
- `start_action = start` in the initiator's config means the tunnel re-establishes itself on boot, so this survives a restart rather than needing a manual kick.

The same pattern generalises to any other "needs a real peer" collector.

### A note on `search_phase2` that is worth knowing

While chasing this I briefly thought the exporter was broken, and the reason is a sharp edge in the API: **`api/ipsec/sessions/search_phase2` returns zero rows unless you pass the connection's `id`**. The controller does `$selected_conn = $this->request->getPost('id', ...)` and then guards on `if (!empty($data[$selected_conn]))`, so an id-less call always yields an empty result set — not an error, just silently nothing.

We already get this right (`FetchIPsecPhase2` posts `{"id": ikeId}` per phase-1 row, and a JSON body is honoured). But it is exactly the kind of endpoint where a plausible-looking refactor — "why are we doing an N+1 here, let's just fetch them all" — would produce an empty result that looks like "no tunnels" rather than a failure. Worth a comment in the code, and a good argument for the schema canary this issue is about: a fixture-based test would never have caught it, because the fixture would have been captured with the id.

### Tailscale

The box is on the tailnet under a CI tag, so the peer metrics are populated and CI can reach it. That unblocks the workflow wiring.

### Remaining 37

SMART (12, blocked on the upstream `os-smart` bug noted earlier), QFeeds (8, licence), HA sync (5) and FRR uptimes/adjacency (3) — the last two would both fall to a **second VM**, which is now the obvious next win. The rest are things that do not exist on a VM (ZFS ARC, temperature sensors).

## Phases 2+3 shipped: the live canary is running end to end

The generic schema canary and the end-to-end smoke are implemented, wired into CI, and proven: [run 29204638183](https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/actions/runs/29204638183) joined the tailnet, probed all 107 endpoints on the box — now on the **Development channel (26.7 series)** — ran the full exporter against it (47/47 collectors, 507 metric names, zero fetch errors), and filed its findings as #235 through the api-drift machinery. That closes the acceptance criteria.

### What landed

- **Golden schemas derived by reflection** (`opnsense/schema.go` + `schema_registry.go`): every endpoint maps to the struct its fetch decodes, and `make schemas` emits one committed structure-only golden per endpoint — key paths + JSON types, no values. `TestSchemaRegistryComplete` pins the registry to the manifest; `TestSchemasUpToDate` fails CI when a struct change leaves goldens stale. The four manifest-canary-exempt endpoints (`firmware`, `firmwareInfo`, `keaLeases4/6`) are asserted schema-covered — their only automated coverage, as this issue demanded.
- **`cmd/apidrift`**: probes every endpoint with the client's own request shapes (POST bodies included; `smartInfo`/`ipsecPhase2` resolve their parameters from live data first), validates structure, and reports through the same drift/warnings step-output + label/title issue machinery as the endpoint canary. Type mismatch on a consumed path = breaking (fails the job); missing path / new top-level key / vanished endpoint = warning (files the issue, job stays green). `exemptions.json` acknowledges box-state variance (drive-type-dependent SMART fields, no-ZFS `memory.arc`, the widget block) so state never reads as drift.
- **`.github/workflows/live-canary.yml`**: daily 06:47 UTC. Ephemeral tagged tailnet node → apidrift → build + run the actual exporter asserting `opnsense_up`, per-collector success and a metric-name floor. One report, one issue title, distinct from the endpoint canary's.

### It caught real drift on day one

First run against 26.7, before any schedule existed (now recorded in #235):

- **The health payload reshaped again**: top level is now just `metadata`, `subsystems` moved inside it, and `metadata.system.status` became a JSON number. The exporter still scrapes green — the exact silent false-OK failure mode this issue was opened about. The smoke can't see it; the schema layer does.
- **Counters retyped string→number** across `protocolStatistics` and `systemResources`. Our `json.Number` fields absorb both, so no breakage — and chasing it taught the canary the distinction (a `numeric` kind: number or numeric string both valid, anything else still fails).
- **Unbound stats restructured**, mbuf fields renamed/dropped, ndp lost `expire`/`type`, pf-stats lost its `rate` sub-fields, kea subnets lost `%interface`, kea leases grew `interfaces`/`stats` blocks, `firmwareInfo` intermittently serves malformed chunked encoding. All warning-level, all per-path in #235. Triage of which fields we chase vs drop is follow-on exporter work under the #227 roadmap, not canary work.

### Plumbing that had to happen (kept generic here)

Two network-layer gotchas ate three workflow runs, both now handled: the tailnet policy needed an accept rule for the CI tag to reach the box on 443 (deny-by-default grants — the join succeeds either way, which is misleading), and the firewall itself needed the tailscale interface assigned with a pass rule for 443, since an unassigned interface is default-deny regardless of tailnet policy. The runner also keeps its own DNS (`--accept-dns=false`) because the tailnet's forced resolver isn't reachable from the CI tag and GitHub API calls die after the join. apidrift now fails fast (single pre-flight probe) instead of burning 107 timeouts when the path is broken.

### Acceptance criteria

- Payload-shape change on any of the 107 endpoints → api-drift issue within 24h: **done** — the machinery filed #235 on its first successful run; the schedule keeps it current daily.
- Four exempt endpoints covered by the schema canary: **done**, test-enforced.
- No response values committed: **done** — goldens and reports are structure-only; raw captures stay runner-local and are never uploaded.
- Endpoint-manifest canary daily and green: schedule merged; first daily run fires tomorrow 06:17 UTC. Its failure mode is its own issue machinery, so nothing to babysit.

Adding a collector now has one extra step (registry entry + `make schemas`), documented in CLAUDE.md alongside the postEndpoints/plugin-gating steps.

All phases delivered: endpoint-manifest canary daily (phase 0), devel box built and on the Development channel (phase 1), reflected golden schemas + cmd/apidrift live canary (phase 2), end-to-end exporter smoke (phase 3). Proven by run 29204638183 → #235. Follow-on work (triage of the 26.7 payload changes, second VM for HA/FRR) is tracked under #227 and #235, not here.

body:
Follow-up to #193, which added the per-endpoint TTL response cache (GET-only, success-only, opt-in per endpoint) and wired it to the two firmware endpoints.

A survey of all ~107 endpoints in `defaultEndpoints()` classified the rest. **These findings are a first-pass survey and each candidate must be re-verified against the actual decoded struct + emitted metrics before being cached** — the failure mode (freezing a counter and inventing flat `rate()` plateaus, or making a dead thing look alive) is worse than the saving.

## Tranche 1 — near-zero staleness risk, no new machinery

Pure GETs, already supported by the cache as built:

| Endpoint | Path | What it returns | Proposed TTL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cpuType` | `api/diagnostics/cpu_usage/getCPUType` | CPU model/cores/threads — immutable until reboot | 12h |
| `systemInformation` | `api/diagnostics/system/system_information` | hostname + OPNsense/FreeBSD/OpenSSL versions | 1h |
| `certificates` | `api/trust/cert/search` | leaf cert inventory + validity windows | 1h |
| `caCertificates` | `api/trust/ca/search` | CA validity windows | 1h |
| `acmeCertificates` | `api/acmeclient/certificates/search` | ACME cert list + renewal status | 1h |

Cert expiry is alerted on a days-to-weeks horizon, so an hour of staleness is invisible. `acmeCertificates` carries a renewal-failure `statusCode` — do not go beyond 1h there.

## Tranche 2 — negative caching (arguably the biggest win)

A large group of endpoints **404 permanently** on boxes without the relevant plugin, yet are re-called every single scrape: `acmeCertificates`, `dyndnsAccounts`, `qfeedsStats`, `smartList`, `ipsecPools`, `captivePortalZones`, plus every `FetchServiceStatusOptional` caller (`opnsense/service_status.go:45-47`).

Caching the "feature absent" 404 for a long TTL removes a fixed per-scrape cost on every box that doesn't run those plugins, at essentially zero staleness risk — plugin install is an admin action. Needs a small extension: the cache currently stores successful responses only.

## Tranche 3 — config-only endpoints that are POST (needs body-keyed cache)

`firewallRules` (`api/firewall/filter/search_rule`), `cronJobs`, `openVPNInstances` return rule/job/instance **definitions with no counters**, and are good 10-30m candidates. But they are POST, and #193 deliberately caches GET only.

Note `smartInfo` is POSTed once **per device** with a different `device=` form value, and the crowdsec/hasync bootgrid POSTs differ only by form body — so **any POST caching must key on the request body, not just the path**, or entries will collide. That is the whole reason POST is excluded today.

Notable: `firewallRules` (cold, definitions) and `firewallRuleStats` (hot, `Evaluations`/`Packets`/`Bytes`/`States`) are separate endpoints fetched inside the same `FetchFirewallRuleStats()` — endpoint-level caching can keep the counters fresh while caching the definitions.

## Explicitly NOT cacheable (checked, ruled out)

- `aliasTableSize` — looks like config, but the same payload carries per-table pf counters (`opnsense/alias.go:13-20`).
- `firewallRuleStats` — `Evaluations`/`Packets`/`Bytes`/`States`.
- `hasyncVersion` — carries `Reachable`, *the* HA-peer-up signal.
- `crowdsecBouncers`/`crowdsecMachines` — carry `LastSeen` heartbeats.
- `qfeedsStats` — `PacketsBlocked`/`BytesBlocked`.
- `smartInfo` — `Temperature` and error counters.
- `healthCheck` — backs `opnsense_up`; caching it would make a dead firewall look alive.
- `interfacesOverview` (`Status`/link-flap), `systemDisk` (`UsedPct`, alerted on), `routingTable` — borderline; ≤60s at most, probably leave alone.

## Observability gap to close alongside this

A cache hit fires no `RequestObserver`, so the per-endpoint API request-count self-metrics drop. That is intentional (it is how you see the cache working), but explicit cache **hit/miss counters** would be better than inferring it from an absence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Re-verify each tranche-1 candidate against its decoded struct + emitted metrics, then cache with the TTLs above
- [ ] Decide on per-endpoint TTL flags vs. one coarse "slow-moving endpoints" TTL (leaning coarse: one flag, sensible per-endpoint defaults)
- [ ] Negative caching of plugin-absent 404s
- [ ] Cache hit/miss self-metrics
- [ ] Body-keyed POST caching (only if tranche 3 is judged worth it)

comments.body:
Tranches 1 and 2 landed in 3b709ce (pushed to `main`). Leaving this open for the remaining items.

## Done

**Negative caching (tranche 2)** — `PluginGatedEndpoints()` in `opnsense/cache.go` lists the 42 GET endpoints whose `Fetch*` already treats 404 as feature-absent. A cached 404 replays as the identical `APICallError`, so those collectors behave exactly as before.

The important design point: the absent TTL is **separate from the positive TTL**, not the same one. A `*ServiceStatus` endpoint's 200 body (`{"status":"running"}`) is live state that must never be cached, while its 404 is safe to cache. Conflating them would have frozen every plugin's up/down signal.

Safety rails, enforced by `TestPluginGatedEndpoints`:
- Only **404** is cached. A 5xx or auth failure is a fault, not a routing fact — replaying one would suppress a real error for the whole TTL.
- Core endpoints (`healthCheck`, `services`, `systemResources`, `firmware`) can never be listed — a cached 404 on `healthCheck` would keep reporting a recovered firewall as down.
- POST entries are rejected (POSTs bypass the cache, so listing one is dead config).

**Positive caching (tranche 1)** — re-verified each candidate against its decoded struct before wiring a TTL, per the caveat in the issue body. `cpuType`, `systemInformation`, `certificates`, `caCertificates`, `acmeCertificates` all carry validity windows / identity only, no counters. Confirmed.

**Config** — one coarse flag `--exporter.cache-ttl` / `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_CACHE_TTL`, default **1h**, `0` disables. Firmware keeps its own 12h flag.

## Measured

Against a mock firewall with no optional plugins, 4 scrapes: **280 API calls with caching off vs 211 with it on** — roughly a third fewer per scrape in steady state, once the cold-cache first scrape is excluded. Verified per endpoint that `healthCheck`, service run-states, `interfaces_info` and rule counters are still fetched on **every** scrape.

Gate green: `go test -race ./...`, `gofmt`, `make docs-check`.

## Remaining (this issue stays open)

- [ ] Cache hit/miss self-metrics (today the cache is only visible as an *absence* in the per-endpoint request-count series)
- [ ] Body-keyed POST caching (tranche 3: `firewallRules`, `cronJobs`, `openVPNInstances`; needs the request body in the cache key so `smartInfo`'s per-device POSTs don't collide) — judged not worth it yet

Final tranche landed in 5e9f561 — closing this.

**POST negative caching is in.** The insight that unblocked it: POSTs were excluded to avoid *body collision* (`smartInfo` is POSTed once per disk), but that only rules out caching a POST's **body**. A **404 is a property of the route, not the payload**, so a path-only key is correct for absence.

I validated that against the live box rather than assuming it, since the whole change rests on "404 always means route-absent":
- absent plugin, any POST body → `404 {"errorMessage":"Endpoint not found"}`
- present plugin, bad resource → `200 {"message":"Invalid device name"}` (`api/smart/service/info` with `device=BOGUS`, `os-smart` installed)

A bad *resource* does not 404, so a cached 404 cannot suppress a live endpoint. Tests enforce both rules, including one that plants a positive entry on a POST endpoint and asserts the POST still reaches the box.

**Measured on the real box** (5 scrapes): `api/crowdsec/alerts/search` 6 calls → 1. Overall **91 → 68 API calls per scrape** in steady state, ~25% fewer, with the health check, service run-states, interface status and captive-portal sessions still fetched every scrape.

The remaining item (cache hit/miss self-metrics) is **not** dropped — it moved to its own issue so this one can close honestly. Body-keyed *positive* POST caching remains deliberately unimplemented: it buys three config endpoints and needs the request body in the cache key, which is not worth it.

title: perf(client): extend the endpoint response cache to other slow-moving endpoints

body:
## Problem

Every enabled collector calls its OPNsense API endpoint on **every scrape** — there is no caching anywhere in the client (`opnsense/client.go`) or the collector layer. At a 15s scrape interval that is ~5,700 calls/day per endpoint.

For the firmware collector this is pure waste. Investigation of the OPNsense core source shows:

- `FirmwareController::statusAction()` only runs the synchronous mirror check (`configdRun('firmware probe')`) when the request is a **POST**. Our `FetchFirmwareStatus()` does a **GET** (`opnsense/client.go:115`), so we are *not* hammering the package mirrors.
- The GET path falls through to `configdRun('firmware product')` → `/usr/local/opnsense/scripts/firmware/product.php`, which reads the cached result off disk: `$ret['product_check'] = json_decode(@file_get_contents('/tmp/pkg_upgrade.json'), true);`

So the data we scrape only changes when the **box's own** firmware check runs — typically daily. But each of our GETs still spawns a configd action and a PHP script on the firewall. With `--exporter.enable-firmware-package-details` (opt-in) we additionally hit `api/core/firmware/info` per scrape, which runs `pkg query`/`rquery` over the ~900-package catalogue — meaningfully heavier local CPU, again for data that changes daily at most.

## Proposed change

Add a **per-endpoint TTL response cache in the API client** rather than a bespoke cache in the firmware collector, so it generalizes to other slow-moving endpoints (a survey of the ~107 endpoints for further candidates is in scope of the discussion, not necessarily this change).

Design:

- Cache the raw successful response body, keyed by endpoint path, with a per-endpoint TTL.
- **GET only.** POST endpoints (see `postEndpoints` in `opnsense/contract.go`) always bypass the cache.
- **Successful responses only** — errors and non-2xx are never cached, so a failure retries on the next scrape.
- The cache must be a shared pointer on `Client`, because `WithContext()` shallow-copies the client per scrape (`opnsense/client.go:331`) — a value field would give every scrape a fresh, useless cache.
- No TTL configured for an endpoint = no caching (current behaviour is the default for everything else).
- A cache hit does **not** fire the `RequestObserver`, so the existing per-endpoint API request-count self-metrics drop visibly — that is the evidence the cache is working.
- Metrics are still emitted from cached data on every scrape, so there are no gaps in the timeseries.

Wire it to firmware:

- New flag `--exporter.firmware-cache-ttl` / `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_FIRMWARE_CACHE_TTL`, default **12h**, `0` disables caching.
- Applies to **both** `firmware` (`api/core/firmware/status`) and `firmwareInfo` (`api/core/firmware/info`), since both are gated by the same daily-ish check cadence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Client-level per-endpoint TTL cache (`SetEndpointCacheTTL`), GET-only, success-only, shared across `WithContext` clones
- [ ] Injectable clock so TTL expiry is unit-testable without sleeping
- [ ] Tests: cached within TTL (one upstream request for N calls), re-fetched after expiry, no caching by default, errors not cached, POST not cached, cache shared across `WithContext` clones
- [ ] `--exporter.firmware-cache-ttl` flag + env var, default 12h, 0 = disabled
- [ ] Firmware status + info both honour the TTL
- [ ] `make docs` regenerated and `make docs-check` green
- [ ] Full gate green: `make test`, `make lint`, `make docs-check`

## Follow-up (separate issue)

Survey the remaining endpoints for other slow-moving cache candidates (config-driven data: aliases, rule definitions, cron table, certificates, etc.), being careful about endpoints whose payload mixes static config with live counters — those cannot be cached.

comments.body:
Done in 9ec1801 (pushed to `main`).

**What landed:** a per-endpoint TTL response cache at the client's request choke point (`doWithContentType`), GET-only, success-only, shared across `WithContext` clones, opt-in per endpoint. Wired to both firmware endpoints behind `--exporter.firmware-cache-ttl` / `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_FIRMWARE_CACHE_TTL`, default **12h**, `0` disables.

**Verified end-to-end** against a mock OPNsense (not just unit tests): three `/metrics` scrapes emitted all 8 firmware metrics each time, while the mock firewall logged exactly **one** call to `firmware/status` and **one** to `firmware/info`. Gate green: `go test -race ./...`, `gofmt`, `make docs-check`.

All acceptance criteria ticked. Follow-ups from the endpoint survey are filed separately.

body:
## Problem

The `opnsense_firmware_needs_reboot` metric's help text says "Whether OPNsense needs a reboot (1 = yes, 0 = no)", but that is not what the upstream `needs_reboot` field means. On OPNsense, `needs_reboot` is set to `1` whenever a base/kernel update is *available* upstream (or a plugin has flagged the reboot-required hook) — it is not a signal that the box is currently pending a reboot because something was already installed. The exporter copies the field 1:1 into the metric without adjusting the semantics or the wording, so the metric name and docs promise "the box currently needs a reboot" while the underlying signal actually means "an available update, if installed, would require a reboot."

This is a labeling/documentation bug, not a data-plumbing bug — the value itself is faithfully passed through, but its meaning is misrepresented to anyone consuming the metric or its generated docs.

## Evidence

`internal/collector/firmware.go:47-48`:
```go
c.needsReboot = buildPrometheusDesc(c.subsystem, "needs_reboot",
    "Whether OPNsense needs a reboot (1 = yes, 0 = no)", nil)
```

`opnsense/firmware.go:113`:
```go
data.NeedsReboot = resp.NeedsReboot == "1"
```

Upstream `/usr/local/opnsense/scripts/firmware/check.sh` on a live 26.1.8_5 box: `needs_reboot` starts at `"0"`, is set to `"1"` if the `pluginctl system.firmware.reboot` hook is set, OR (separately, in the update-check block) when a base/kernel package has a newer version *available* — this is a remote-size query (`opnsense-update -bfSr`/`-fkSr`), not an install-completion check.

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: `product_version` was still `26.1.10` (nothing installed), `status` was `"update"` with 14 packages available including base+kernel, `status_msg` read "This update requires a reboot," and `needs_reboot="1"` — while the separate, correctly-scoped `upgrade_needs_reboot` (major-upgrade signal, from `product.product_check`) was `"0"`. The same misleading wording is propagated into the generated docs (`docs/metrics/metrics.md:272`).

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator sets up an alert on `opnsense_firmware_needs_reboot == 1` expecting it to catch "the firewall installed an update and is waiting for a reboot to apply it." Instead the alert fires (and stays firing, potentially for days or weeks) any time upstream publishes a new base/kernel point release — before anything has been installed on the box. Dashboards labelled "needs reboot" show a persistent red/alerting state that rebooting the firewall does not clear, since the condition tracks update availability, not a completed-but-unapplied install.

## Suggested direction

Reword the help text for `opnsense_firmware_needs_reboot` (and its generated docs entry) to reflect the real semantics, e.g. "whether a pending update requires a reboot to apply, or a plugin has flagged a reboot requirement" — clearly distinct from `upgrade_needs_reboot`, which is confirmed correct and only pertains to major-version upgrades. Consider also renaming the metric if a clearer name (e.g. `update_requires_reboot`) is preferred, alongside a CHANGELOG note since this is a behavior-meaning clarification, not a value change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The help text for `opnsense_firmware_needs_reboot` no longer implies the firewall currently needs a reboot; it accurately describes "available update would require a reboot, or plugin reboot-flag set"
- [ ] `docs/metrics/metrics.md` (and any other generated doc referencing this metric) is regenerated via `make docs` and reflects the corrected wording
- [ ] The distinction between `needs_reboot` (update-availability signal) and `upgrade_needs_reboot` (major-upgrade signal) is documented clearly enough that the two cannot be confused
- [ ] No metric name, label, or value changes are made without a corresponding CHANGELOG entry (if a rename is chosen instead of a pure doc fix)
- [ ] `make docs-check` passes after the change

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in 1d66d54. Reworded the `opnsense_firmware_needs_reboot` help text (and regenerated `docs/metrics/metrics.md`) to describe the real semantics: *'Whether applying the currently AVAILABLE update would require a reboot, or a plugin has set the reboot-required hook … This tracks update availability, NOT a completed-but-unapplied install — it can be 1 for days before anything is installed and is not cleared by rebooting.'* It now explicitly points to `upgrade_needs_reboot` for the major-version-upgrade signal, and I clarified that metric's help too so the two can't be confused.

Kept the metric name and value (faithful passthrough of the upstream field) — pure doc/help-text clarification, so no CHANGELOG/behaviour entry per the rename-only AC. `make docs-check` green; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

The certificates collector always emits `valid_from`/`valid_to` values, even for certificate entries that have no real expiry data. On OPNsense, a "certificate" row in `api/trust/cert/search` can be a **pending CSR** created for external CA signing (`crt` empty, `csr` populated) or a corrupt/unparseable cert blob. In both cases OPNsense's own `Cert.xml` model leaves the `valid_from`/`valid_to` fields as empty strings — they are volatile `TextField`s with no `<default>`, only populated when `Store::parseX509()` successfully parses an actual certificate.

`opnsense.FetchCertificates` parses those fields with `safeParseFloat`, which silently returns `0` on any parse error, including an empty string. `internal/collector/certificates.go` then emits `opnsense_certificates_valid_from_seconds`/`opnsense_certificates_valid_to_seconds` unconditionally for every row, with no guard for the empty/unparseable case. The result is a metric reading epoch `0` (1 Jan 1970) for a certificate that isn't actually expired — it just hasn't been signed yet.

## Evidence

`opnsense/certificates.go:121-122`:
```go
ValidFrom:   safeParseFloat(row.ValidFrom),
ValidTo:     safeParseFloat(row.ValidTo),
```

`opnsense/utils.go:117-123`:
```go
func safeParseFloat(s string) float64 {
	v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
	if err != nil {
		return 0
	}
	return v
}
```

`internal/collector/certificates.go:100-120` emits `c.validFrom` / `c.validTo` `prometheus.MustNewConstMetric` calls for every `cert` in `data.Certificates` unconditionally — there is no check for whether `ValidFrom`/`ValidTo` are actually present/non-zero before emitting.

On the live OPNsense 26.1.8_5 source, `CertificatesField::actionPostLoadingEvent()` (`/usr/local/opnsense/mvc/app/models/OPNsense/Trust/FieldTypes/CertificatesField.php`) only calls `Store::parseX509()` (which sets `valid_from`/`valid_to`) when `node->crt` is non-empty. When `crt` is empty but `csr` is populated — the standard "generate CSR for external CA signing" workflow (`action='external'` in `CertController.php` sets `node->csr` but not `node->crt`) — it instead calls `Store::parseCSR()`, whose return array contains only `name` plus issuer_map fields, no `valid_from`/`valid_to` keys. Those `Cert.xml` fields (lines 125-126, volatile, no default) therefore stay empty strings in the `api/trust/cert/search` response for that row. This specific CSR-pending shape was not directly observed on the test live box (it had no pending CSR rows; all 3 cert rows and 1 CA row there carried normal epoch-second strings), but the mechanism is confirmed against live 26.1.8_5 source, and the repo's own test fixture already encodes this exact empty-string edge case: `opnsense/certificates_test.go:34-43,81-88` has a fixture literally named "Expired Cert" and asserts the resulting `ValidFrom`/`ValidTo == 0` as current (undesired) behavior.

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator creates a CSR under System > Trust > Certificates to get it signed by an external CA — a standard, common workflow. Until the signed certificate is imported back, the exporter reports that certificate row as `opnsense_certificates_valid_to_seconds = 0`, i.e. expired since 1 January 1970. Any expiry alert of the form `(valid_to_seconds - time()) < N days` fires immediately and pages on-call, and any "time until expiry" dashboard panel shows a massive negative outlier for a certificate that is not expired at all, just not yet issued.

## Suggested direction

Mirror the existing `ok`-flag pattern used elsewhere in this codebase (e.g. `parseRFC3339Unix`) for `ValidFrom`/`ValidTo`: track whether the parse actually succeeded, and in the collector skip emitting `valid_from_seconds`/`valid_to_seconds` for a row when the underlying field was empty/unparseable, while still emitting the `info` metric for visibility.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `opnsense.FetchCertificates` (or a supporting helper) distinguishes "field absent/empty" from "field present and equal to epoch 0" for `ValidFrom`/`ValidTo`
- [ ] `internal/collector/certificates.go` does not emit `opnsense_certificates_valid_from_seconds` / `opnsense_certificates_valid_to_seconds` for a certificate row whose source field was empty/unparseable (e.g. a pending CSR)
- [ ] The `info` metric (and any other non-expiry metrics) is still emitted for pending-CSR / unparseable-blob rows
- [ ] A unit test covers a certificate row with empty `valid_from`/`valid_to` (mirroring/updating the existing "Expired Cert" fixture in `opnsense/certificates_test.go`) and asserts no expiry metric is emitted for it, rather than asserting `0`
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in b80a1da. Added a `safeParseFloatOK` helper (returns `(float64, bool)`) and `HasValidFrom`/`HasValidTo` flags on both `Certificate` and `CACertificate`, set true only when the source field actually parsed. The collector now skips `valid_from_seconds`/`valid_to_seconds` (and the `ca_*` equivalents) for a row whose field was empty/unparseable — so a pending CSR or corrupt blob no longer emits epoch 0 (reading as 'expired since 1970' and false-firing expiry alerts). The `info` metric is still emitted for those rows so they remain visible. A genuine `"0"` stays distinguishable from absent.

Also applied the same fix to the CA authorities path (shares the identical bug/file).

Coverage: updated the existing 'Expired Cert' fixture assertion in `opnsense/certificates_test.go` to check `HasValidFrom/HasValidTo=false` (and true for a populated cert), and added `TestCertificatesCollector_Update_PendingCSR` asserting no expiry series but info still present. `make test`/`make lint`/`make docs-check` green; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

The CARP VIP collector decodes a JSON field that OPNsense's live API never sends, so the `vip` label on every `opnsense_carp_vip_*` metric is always empty, and — on any host with more than one address per CARP vhid — the resulting duplicate label tuples crash the entire `/metrics` scrape.

`carpVIPRow` in `opnsense/carp.go` declares `VIP string \`json:"vip"\`` as the source of the VIP address label. On OPNsense 26.1, `getVipStatusAction` in `/usr/local/opnsense/mvc/app/controllers/OPNsense/Diagnostics/Api/InterfaceController.php` builds each CARP status row with the keys `interface`, `vhid`, `advbase`, `advskew`, `subnet`, `status`, `mode` (plus `status_txt`/`vhid_txt`) — there is no `vip` key at all; the actual VIP address is placed in `subnet` (`'subnet' => $subnet['ipaddr']`). As a result `carpVIPRow.VIP` unmarshals to `""` for every real row, and `internal/collector/carp.go` emits `opnsense_carp_vip_status`, `opnsense_carp_vip_advbase_seconds`, and `opnsense_carp_vip_advskew` with `vip=""` on every HA-enabled deployment, making it impossible to tell which VIP is MASTER vs BACKUP.

It gets worse than just an empty label: the same PHP action loops over `['ipv4','ipv6']` for every address associated with a vhid, emitting one row per address. Any vhid carrying both an IPv4 and IPv6 address (or the common "ipalias VIP riding a CARP vhid" pattern) produces multiple rows that share the same `interface`/`vhid` and, with `vip` collapsed to `""`, an identical `(interface, vhid, vip)` label tuple. `prometheus.MustNewConstMetric` panics/`Gather()` errors on duplicate label sets, and promhttp's default error handling turns that into an HTTP 500 for the whole `/metrics` scrape — a total monitoring blackout of the very firewall the exporter is watching for HA failover.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/carp.go:11` — `VIP string \`json:"vip"\`` on `carpVIPRow`, a field key the live API does not emit.
- `internal/collector/carp.go:57-68` — `vipStatus`/`vipAdvbase`/`vipAdvskew` descs declare the label set `[]string{"interface", "vhid", "vip"}`.
- `internal/collector/carp.go:122-149` — the `for _, vip := range data.VIPs` loop passes `vip.VIP` (always `""`) as the third label value for all three metrics.
- Live source (read via SSH from a 26.1.8_5 box): `getVipStatusAction` in `InterfaceController.php` (~lines 250-320) builds each row with `interface`/`vhid`/`advbase`/`advskew`/`subnet`/`status`/`mode` only, sets `'subnet' => $subnet['ipaddr']` for the VIP address, and iterates `['ipv4','ipv6']` per vhid (~lines 273-287), emitting one row per address.
- Test fixtures at `opnsense/carp_test.go:25` and `internal/collector/carp_test.go:22` invent a `"vip"` JSON field and misinterpret `subnet` as a netmask (`"24"`), so the existing test suite validates a response shape the real API never returns and does not catch this.
- CARP is a default-on collector (`exporter.disable-carp` defaults to `false` in `internal/options/collectors.go:86-89,305`), so this executes on every scrape of any HA-enabled firewall.

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: the box's own `getVipStatusAction` source has no `vip` key, and its live `carpStatus` response had `rows: []` (no VIPs configured there), so the empty-rows path is what was directly exercised; the empty-`vip`-label and duplicate-tuple mechanisms follow directly from the PHP source.

## Failure scenario / impact

Trigger 1 (data correctness, every HA deployment): any firewall with CARP configured scrapes fine but emits `opnsense_carp_vip_status{interface="...",vhid="1",vip=""}` for every VIP — operators cannot distinguish VIPs from each other or tell which is MASTER vs BACKUP from the metric alone.

Trigger 2 (availability, common HA configs): a vhid with both an IPv4 and IPv6 address, or the standard pattern of multiple ipalias VIPs bound to one CARP vhid, causes `getVipStatusAction` to return several rows with identical `interface`/`vhid` and an always-empty `vip`. The collector then emits duplicate `(interface, vhid, vip)` label tuples via `MustNewConstMetric`, `prometheus.Gather()` fails, and promhttp returns HTTP 500 for the entire `/metrics` endpoint — not just CARP metrics — taking down all monitoring for that firewall, precisely during the HA scenario the exporter exists to observe.

## Suggested direction

Populate the `vip` label from the row's `subnet` field (the actual VIP address on 26.1) instead of the nonexistent `vip` key, which also makes the tuple unique per address again. Add duplicate-series protection in the CARP collector similar to existing dedupe logic elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. the tailscale collector) as defense in depth, and correct the test fixtures in `opnsense/carp_test.go` and `internal/collector/carp_test.go` to match the real API row shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `opnsense/carp.go` decodes the VIP address from the API's `subnet` field rather than a nonexistent `vip` key
- [ ] A CARP vhid with two addresses (e.g. IPv4 + IPv6, or two ipalias VIPs on one vhid) produces two distinct, non-colliding `(interface, vhid, vip)` label tuples and does not cause `/metrics` to 500
- [ ] `opnsense/carp_test.go` and `internal/collector/carp_test.go` fixtures are updated to match the real `getVipStatusAction` row shape (no `vip` key, address in `subnet`) and assert the corrected label values
- [ ] A regression test exists that feeds multiple rows sharing the same `interface`/`vhid` with distinct VIP addresses and asserts the collector emits distinct series without panicking or erroring
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass

body:
## Problem

The protocol-statistics collector only decodes the IPv4 (`ip`) and ICMPv4 (`icmp`) blocks returned by OPNsense's `netstat --libxo statistics` endpoint. The `protocolStatisticsResponse.Statistics` struct in `opnsense/protocol_statistics.go` has fields for `tcp`, `udp`, `ip`, `icmp`, `carp`, `pfsync`, and `arp`, but no fields for `ip6` or `icmp6`. Because `encoding/json` silently ignores unknown JSON keys, the entire IPv6 statistics block is dropped during unmarshal with no error and no log line.

The resulting Prometheus metrics compound the problem because their names give no indication of the gap: `opnsense_protocol_ip_received_packets_total`, `opnsense_protocol_ip_forwarded_packets_total`, `opnsense_protocol_ip_dropped_by_reason_total`, and the `icmp_*` family all read as generic "IP"/"ICMP" counters, not "IPv4-only" counters. On a dual-stack firewall this silently discards a large share of real traffic from the export — the existing `carp`/`pfsync` metrics already use an `address_family` label for the analogous inet/inet6 split, so this collector is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase's own pattern.

## Evidence

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box.

`opnsense/protocol_statistics.go:17` — the `Statistics` struct declares only these top-level blocks:

```go
type protocolStatisticsResponse struct {
	Statistics struct {
		TCP struct { ... } `json:"tcp"`
		UDP struct { ... } `json:"udp"`
		IP struct { ... } `json:"ip"`
		ICMP struct { ... } `json:"icmp"`
		CARP struct { ... } `json:"carp"`
		Pfsync struct { ... } `json:"pfsync"`
		ARP struct { ... } `json:"arp"`
	} `json:"statistics"`
}
```

The live sample response's top-level `statistics` object additionally contains `igmp`, `ipsec-statistics`, `ah-statictics`, `esp-statictics`, `ipcomp-statictics`, `pim`, `ip6`, `icmp6`, `ipsec6-statistics`, and `rip6` — none of which have a corresponding Go field. The `ip6` block alone is fully populated on the live box: 47,042,625 received packets and 45,452,086 forwarded packets, versus 178,705,919 forwarded on the IPv4 `ip` block — roughly 20% of total forwarded traffic that is discarded on unmarshal.

`internal/collector/protocol.go:193-216` shows the emitted metric descriptors carry no address-family qualifier:

```go
c.ipReceivedPackets = buildPrometheusDesc(c.subsystem, "ip_received_packets_total", ...)
c.ipForwardedPackets = buildPrometheusDesc(c.subsystem, "ip_forwarded_packets_total", ...)
c.ipDroppedByReason  = buildPrometheusDesc(c.subsystem, "ip_dropped_by_reason_total", []string{"reason"})
```

compared to the existing pattern for pfsync (`internal/collector/protocol.go:180`) which already uses `[]string{"address_family"}` for its inet/inet6 split.

## Failure scenario / impact

On any dual-stack OPNsense deployment (IPv6 enabled alongside IPv4, which is common), an operator monitoring `opnsense_protocol_ip_dropped_by_reason_total` or `opnsense_protocol_ip_forwarded_packets_total` sees only the IPv4 stack's counters. If an IPv6-specific routing or drop incident occurs — for example a growing "packets not forwardable" counter on the `ip6` block, or an ICMPv6 flood — none of the exported protocol metrics move at all, because the entire ip6/icmp6 dataset never reaches the collector. The dashboard/alerting built on these generically-named metrics gives false confidence that "IP traffic" is fully observed when roughly a fifth of forwarded packets (on the validated live box) are invisible.

## Suggested direction

Add `IP6` and `ICMP6` struct fields (and any other missing blocks worth surfacing) to `protocolStatisticsResponse.Statistics`, then either emit parallel metrics using an `address_family` label to match the existing `carp`/`pfsync` convention, or add dedicated `ip6_*`/`icmp6_*` metric names. In the interim, document that the current `ip_*`/`icmp_*` series are IPv4-only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `protocolStatisticsResponse.Statistics` in `opnsense/protocol_statistics.go` decodes the `ip6` and `icmp6` JSON blocks (fields/tests added or updated accordingly)
- [ ] IPv6 forwarded/received/dropped/fragment counters are exposed as Prometheus metrics, either via an `address_family` label on the existing `ip_*`/`icmp_*` series or via new `ip6_*`/`icmp6_*` metric names
- [ ] A unit test using a fixture with both `ip`/`icmp` and `ip6`/`icmp6` populated asserts both stacks' values are correctly attributed and non-zero in the collected metrics
- [ ] `make docs` is run and generated metrics/collector docs reflect the new/changed metric names or labels
- [ ] If metric names are unchanged (label-only approach), existing dashboards/alerts referencing `opnsense_protocol_ip_*`/`icmp_*` continue to work without a breaking rename

body:
## Problem

The HAProxy collector fabricates HTTP response-code counters for proxies that never speak HTTP at all. `haproxyResponses()` builds the `hrsp_1xx`..`hrsp_other` map by feeding every field straight through `safeParseFloat`, which returns `0` both for a genuine `"0"` string and for an unparseable/empty string. HAProxy's `show stat` CSV (which the os-haproxy plugin's `queryStats.php` converts to JSON) leaves these `hrsp_*` cells as empty strings for proxies running in `tcp` mode, because the stat is not applicable there — not because the count is zero. The exporter can't tell the two cases apart after `safeParseFloat` collapses them, so it emits a hard `0` for a metric that should not exist at all.

The collector then unconditionally ranges over the resulting six-entry map and emits `opnsense_haproxy_frontend_http_responses_total` / `opnsense_haproxy_backend_http_responses_total` for every proxy, HTTP or not. The bug is compounded by the fact that the code's own doc comment on `haproxyStatRow` already flags that "every value is a JSON string (`""` when HAProxy reports no value)" — the empty-vs-zero ambiguity was a known risk that wasn't handled at the parsing boundary.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/haproxy.go:9-18` — doc comment on `haproxyStatRow` explicitly notes fields are `""` when HAProxy reports no value.
- `opnsense/haproxy.go:116-125` — `haproxyResponses()` funnels all six `Hrsp*` fields through `safeParseFloat` with no empty-check:

```go
func haproxyResponses(row haproxyStatRow) map[string]float64 {
	return map[string]float64{
		"1xx":   safeParseFloat(row.Hrsp1xx),
		"2xx":   safeParseFloat(row.Hrsp2xx),
		"3xx":   safeParseFloat(row.Hrsp3xx),
		"4xx":   safeParseFloat(row.Hrsp4xx),
		"5xx":   safeParseFloat(row.Hrsp5xx),
		"other": safeParseFloat(row.HrspOther),
	}
}
```

- `opnsense/utils.go:117-123` — `safeParseFloat` returns `0` on any parse error, including on an empty string:

```go
func safeParseFloat(s string) float64 {
	v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
	if err != nil {
		return 0
	}
	return v
}
```

- `internal/collector/haproxy.go:226-228` and `:244-246` — the collector unconditionally ranges over `ResponsesByCode` and emits a counter series per code for every frontend/backend, regardless of proxy mode:

```go
for code, v := range fe.ResponsesByCode {
	ch <- prometheus.MustNewConstMetric(c.frontendResponses, prometheus.CounterValue, v, fe.Name, code, c.instance)
}
```

Not confirmed against a live box — the os-haproxy plugin was not installed on the available test appliance (its counters endpoint 404s there). The empty-cell-for-tcp-mode behavior is corroborated externally: the reference `prometheus/haproxy_exporter` deliberately skips emitting a metric when a CSV cell is blank, precisely to avoid fabricating zeros for fields that don't apply to a given proxy/mode.

No existing test covers this: the fixtures in `opnsense/haproxy_test.go` and `internal/collector/haproxy_test.go` only use populated `hrsp_*` values ("0" or real numbers), never an empty string, so there is no regression guard either way.

## Failure scenario / impact

Any os-haproxy deployment with a tcp-mode listener (SMTP, database proxying, TLS passthrough — all common HAProxy uses) causes the exporter to emit `opnsense_haproxy_frontend_http_responses_total{code="1xx"} 0` through `{code="other"} 0` (and the equivalent backend series) for that proxy on every scrape, forever. These are not "no data" — they are constant, permanent 0-value counter series asserting the proxy served zero HTTP responses of each class, when in fact the proxy isn't serving HTTP at all. Dashboards or alerting rules that sum/aggregate HTTP response-code metrics across proxies silently include these fabricated series, and users have no way to distinguish "genuinely zero HTTP traffic" from "not an HTTP proxy" from the exported data.

## Suggested direction

Add a helper that distinguishes an empty CSV cell from a parseable numeric value (e.g. returning `(float64, bool)`), and only populate/emit an `hrsp_*` code's counter when the cell was non-empty. The same ambiguity likely affects other `hrsp`-adjacent or optional numeric fields in the same struct (e.g. downtime/weight on no-check servers) and could use the same fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A row with empty-string `hrsp_1xx`..`hrsp_other` fields (simulating a tcp-mode proxy) does not produce any `frontend_http_responses_total`/`backend_http_responses_total` series for that proxy, for any code class.
- [ ] A row with genuine `"0"` values for `hrsp_*` fields still emits a `0`-valued counter (zero real HTTP responses is preserved as a distinct, legitimate case from "not applicable").
- [ ] A row with real non-zero `hrsp_*` values continues to emit correct counters, unchanged from current behavior.
- [ ] `opnsense/haproxy_test.go` gains a fixture/table case covering empty-string `hrsp_*` fields.
- [ ] `internal/collector/haproxy_test.go` asserts no response-code series is emitted for a tcp-mode-shaped fixture row.
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in 4b6cc40. `haproxyResponses` now only adds a code to the map when its CSV cell is non-empty. HAProxy leaves the `hrsp_*` cells empty (`""`) for tcp-mode proxies (SMTP/DB/TLS-passthrough) where the stat doesn't apply — those are now omitted, so the collector (which ranges the map) emits no `frontend/backend_http_responses_total` series for them. A genuine `"0"` is still parsed and kept as a real zero, preserving 'zero HTTP responses' as a distinct case from 'not an HTTP proxy'. Real non-zero values are unchanged. No collector change needed.

Coverage: `TestHAProxyResponses_EmptyVsZero` (empty cells → omitted; `"0"` → present as 0; real value preserved) and `TestHAProxyCollector_Update_TCPModeNoResponseCodes` (tcp-mode fixture → no http_responses_total series). Existing populated-fixture tests unchanged/green. `make test`/`make lint`/`make docs-check` green; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

The FRR/BGP collector's address-family label normalization is lossy: it collapses distinct upstream address-families (e.g. `ipv4Unicast` and `ipv4Multicast`) onto the same `af="ipv4"` label. When a BGP neighbor is activated in both the unicast and multicast SAFI for the same protocol family, FRR's `show bgp summary json` output (as surfaced via OPNsense's Quagga API) returns two separate top-level blocks, and the exporter turns both into metric series with an identical label set. Prometheus's registry rejects the resulting duplicate series at gather time, and because the exporter's `/metrics` handler uses the promhttp default error behavior, that single gather error takes down the entire scrape — not just the FRR metrics.

The root cause is `frrAFLabel`, which sequentially strips the suffixes `"unicast"` and `"multicast"` from the lowercased AF key. Both `"ipv4unicast"` and `"ipv4multicast"` reduce to `"ipv4"` (and both ipv6 variants reduce to `"ipv6"`), so the mapping is not injective. The per-family loop in `opnsense/frr.go` then appends one `FRRBGPFamily` per raw map key with no deduplication, so two upstream keys that collide under `frrAFLabel` become two families sharing one label tuple, which the collector emits as duplicate `bgp_peers_total`/`bgp_failed_peers`/`bgp_rib_entries` series (and duplicated per-peer series, if the same neighbor is activated in both SAFIs).

## Evidence

`opnsense/frr.go:53-59`:
```go
// frrAFLabel converts an FRR address-family key like "ipv4Unicast" to a
// lowercase label like "ipv4". Unknown keys pass through lowercased.
func frrAFLabel(key string) string {
	lower := strings.ToLower(key)
	lower = strings.TrimSuffix(lower, "unicast")
	lower = strings.TrimSuffix(lower, "multicast")
	return lower
}
```

`opnsense/frr.go:123-131` — no dedup across raw AF keys when building families:
```go
data.Present = true
for afKey, fam := range families {
	af := frrAFLabel(afKey)
	data.Families = append(data.Families, FRRBGPFamily{
		AF:          af,
		PeerCount:   fam.PeerCount,
		FailedPeers: fam.FailedPeers,
		RibCount:    fam.RibCount,
	})
```

`internal/collector/frr.go:180-188` — one series emitted per family, keyed only by `{af, instance}`:
```go
if bgp.Present {
	for _, fam := range bgp.Families {
		ch <- prometheus.MustNewConstMetric(c.bgpPeersTotal,
			prometheus.GaugeValue, fam.PeerCount, fam.AF, c.instance)
		ch <- prometheus.MustNewConstMetric(c.bgpFailedPeers,
			prometheus.GaugeValue, fam.FailedPeers, fam.AF, c.instance)
		ch <- prometheus.MustNewConstMetric(c.bgpRibEntries,
			prometheus.GaugeValue, fam.RibCount, fam.AF, c.instance)
	}
```

`internal/server/metrics.go:68-70` — the scrape handler uses `promhttp.HandlerOpts{}` (zero value = `HTTPErrorOnError`), so any registry gather error (including a duplicate-series collision) turns into an HTTP 500 for the whole scrape:
```go
promhttp.HandlerFor(
	prometheus.Gatherers{h.self, reg},
	promhttp.HandlerOpts{},
).ServeHTTP(w, r)
```

This was not runtime-validated on the reference livebox — that box has no `os-frr` plugin installed (`quaggaBgpSummary.json` returns "Endpoint not found") — but the collapsing behavior was independently confirmed by executing `frrAFLabel` directly: both `"ipv4Unicast"` and `"ipv4Multicast"` map to `"ipv4"`, and both ipv6 equivalents map to `"ipv6"`.

## Failure scenario / impact

A box running the os-frr plugin with a BGP neighbor activated in both the ipv4 (or ipv6) unicast and multicast address-families produces two blocks in `show bgp summary json`: `ipv4Unicast` and `ipv4Multicast`. Both collapse to `af="ipv4"` in the exporter. On the next scrape, the collector emits `opnsense_frr_bgp_peers_total{af="ipv4",instance=...}` (and the failed-peers/rib-entries counterparts) twice with identical labels, and potentially duplicate per-peer series too. `prometheus.Registry.Gather()` fails on the duplicate, and because the handler uses default `promhttp.HandlerOpts{}`, the whole `/metrics` endpoint returns HTTP 500 — blacking out monitoring for every subsystem, not just FRR/BGP.

## Suggested direction

Make `frrAFLabel` lossless — e.g. preserve the SAFI distinction in the label (`ipv4unicast`/`ipv4multicast`) instead of trimming it away — or dedupe families/peers by their resulting label tuple before emitting metrics. Add a unit test using a `bgpsummary` fixture containing both `ipv4Unicast` and `ipv4Multicast` blocks to lock in the fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `frrAFLabel("ipv4Unicast")` and `frrAFLabel("ipv4Multicast")` (and the ipv6 equivalents) no longer produce the same label value, OR the family/peer emission path dedupes by final label tuple before writing to the metrics channel.
- [ ] A unit test with a `bgpsummary` fixture containing both `ipv4Unicast` and `ipv4Multicast` top-level blocks passes without producing duplicate label tuples.
- [ ] `internal/collector/frr_test.go` (or equivalent) asserts that `Collect()` for this fixture does not yield two `MustNewConstMetric` calls with identical label values for `bgp_peers_total`, `bgp_failed_peers`, or `bgp_rib_entries`.
- [ ] A full scrape (`promhttp` registry `Gather()`) against the dual-SAFI fixture succeeds with no duplicate-series error.
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in 3fda9d2. `frrAFLabel` now only trims the `unicast` suffix, so it's injective per SAFI: `ipv4Unicast`→`ipv4`, `ipv4Multicast`→`ipv4multicast`, `ipv6Unicast`→`ipv6`, `ipv6Multicast`→`ipv6multicast`. The overwhelmingly common unicast families keep the short `ipv4`/`ipv6` label (backward compatible — no change for existing dashboards), while non-unicast SAFIs retain their suffix so two distinct upstream families can never collapse onto the same `af` label tuple. A neighbor activated in both SAFIs now yields distinct family and per-peer series instead of a duplicate-series Gather failure (and the ContinueOnError handler from #81 is the backstop).

Coverage: `TestFrrAFLabel` (injectivity across the SAFI variants), `TestFetchFRRBGP_DualSAFI` (fetch layer: distinct family + peer AF labels), and `TestFRRCollector_Update_DualSAFINoDuplicateSeries` (collector: `assertNoDuplicateSeries` + both `ipv4`/`ipv4multicast` present). `make test`/`make lint`/`make docs-check` green; 556 metrics unchanged.
