body:
## Problem

The docgen AST extractor that populates the "Labels" column in `docs/metrics/metrics.md` cannot resolve label slices that are built with `append(...)` calls. `extractLabelsArg` in `scripts/docgen/main.go` only handles a `nil` `*ast.Ident` or a `*ast.CompositeLit`; any other expression type (including a `*ast.CallExpr` like `append(...)`) falls through to `return nil`, and the identifier-resolution fallback in the caller only fires when the labels argument is itself a bare `*ast.Ident`, which does not apply here either.

The syslog collector's two rate/size metrics build their labels this way: `internal/collector/syslog.go:67-72` passes `append(append([]string{}, srcLabels...), "window")` and `append(append([]string{}, srcLabels...), "stat")` as the labels argument to the Desc constructors for `opnsense_syslog_events_per_second` and `opnsense_syslog_message_size_bytes`. Because docgen can't evaluate that expression, both metrics are documented with no labels at all, even though at runtime they emit five labels each: `source_name`, `source_id`, `source_instance`, plus `window` (1h/24h/since_start) or `stat` (avg/max) respectively.

Compounding this, nothing in the doc-generation pipeline cross-checks the generated docs' label sets against the actual runtime `Describe()` output. `verifyMetricsAgainstRegistry` in `scripts/docgen/verify.go` only compares metric names (via `descFQName` regex matching against `Desc.String()`), never label sets — even though `Desc.String()` already exposes `variableLabels`. So `make docs-check` stays green despite the documented and actual label sets diverging.

## Evidence

- `internal/collector/syslog.go:67-72` — Desc calls use `append(append([]string{}, srcLabels...), "window")` / `"stat"` as the labels argument.
- `scripts/docgen/main.go:731-755` (`extractLabelsArg`) — only handles `nil` `*ast.Ident` and `*ast.CompositeLit`; any other expression (e.g. `*ast.CallExpr`) falls through to `return nil` at line 745.
- `scripts/docgen/main.go:679-687` — the caller's `localVars` fallback only resolves the labels argument when `call.Args[3]` is itself a bare `*ast.Ident`; it is a nested `append()` call here, so the fallback never triggers.
- `docs/metrics/metrics.md:700-701` — generated docs show `Labels: ---` for both `opnsense_syslog_events_per_second` and `opnsense_syslog_message_size_bytes`, while every other syslog metric using the plain `srcLabels` slice correctly shows `source_name, source_id, source_instance`.
- `scripts/docgen/verify.go:31-77` (`verifyMetricsAgainstRegistry`) — walks runtime `Describe()` output and compares only `descFQName(d.String())` (name only) against the AST-derived name set; it never compares label sets, so this drift produces no error and `make docs-check` passes.

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box.

## Failure scenario / impact

A user builds an alert or dashboard query from the generated metrics reference, sees `opnsense_syslog_events_per_second` documented with no labels, and writes something like `opnsense_syslog_events_per_second > x`. In reality the metric is split by `window` (1h/24h/since_start) and per-source labels, so an unqualified sum silently aggregates across all three time windows (effectively triple-counting) and across sources, producing a number that looks plausible but is wrong. Because `make docs-check` only validates metric names against the registry, this class of bug — any future collector that composes its label slice via `append(...)` rather than a literal — will ship with incorrect docs and a fully green CI gate, with nothing catching the regression.

## Suggested direction

Extend `verifyMetricsAgainstRegistry` to compare label sets (not just names) between the AST-derived docs and runtime `Describe()`/`Desc.String()` output, treating a mismatch as a hard error — this is the robust, forward-looking fix since it catches any future label-composition pattern docgen can't parse. Optionally also teach `extractLabelsArg` to fold simple `append(...)` chains (or refactor the two syslog `Desc` declarations to use a plain composite literal, e.g. a precomputed `srcLabelsWindow`/`srcLabelsStat` local) as a direct fix for this specific case.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/metrics/metrics.md` shows `source_name, source_id, source_instance, window` for `opnsense_syslog_events_per_second` and `source_name, source_id, source_instance, stat` for `opnsense_syslog_message_size_bytes` after `make docs`.
- [ ] `scripts/docgen/verify.go` compares label sets (derived from runtime `Desc.String()` variableLabels) against the docs-generated label sets for every metric, not just fqNames.
- [ ] A unit test in the `scripts/docgen` test suite asserts that a metric whose runtime label set differs from its documented label set causes `verifyMetricsAgainstRegistry` (or `make docs-check`) to fail.
- [ ] A unit test covers a Desc call whose labels argument is an `append(...)` expression and asserts docgen resolves it to the correct label list (either by fixing `extractLabelsArg` or by refactoring the syslog collector to a resolvable composite literal and testing that path).
- [ ] `make docs-check` fails on the current `main` branch state before the fix (reproducing the gap) and passes after the fix is applied.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `2dc9f25` (straight to main).

- Replaced `extractLabelsArg` with **`resolveLabelSlice`**, which statically folds `[]string{...}` literals, local-var references, AND `append(...)` chains (base-slice spread + literal elements). `docs/metrics/metrics.md` now shows `source_name, source_id, source_instance, window` for `opnsense_syslog_events_per_second` and `…, stat` for `opnsense_syslog_message_size_bytes` (acceptance #1).
- Extended `verifyMetricsAgainstRegistry` to compare each metric's **documented label set** against the runtime `Desc` `variableLabels` (stripping the universal `opnsense_instance` that `buildPrometheusDesc` appends). Any unresolved label is now a hard error (acceptance #2) — this is the forward-looking safety net that catches any future label-composition pattern docgen can't parse.
- `TestResolveAppendLabels` covers the append() resolution + plain-var + nil cases (acceptance #4); `TestVerifyDetectsLabelMismatch` corrupts a real metric's documented labels and asserts verify fails (acceptance #3).

Acceptance #5: before this change the label comparison didn't exist, so the syslog gap shipped green; with the comparison in place, reverting the extraction fix makes verify fail — demonstrated by `TestVerifyDetectsLabelMismatch`. Gate: `make docs`/`docs-check` green (556 metrics), `make test` green (incl. new tests), `make lint` 0 issues.

body:
## Problem

CLAUDE.md and several published docs site pages contain hardcoded sub-collector counts and package descriptions that have gone stale as the exporter grew. `CLAUDE.md:31` says the top-level `Collector` runs "30 sub-collectors concurrently", and `CLAUDE.md:33` describes `internal/options/` as containing only `ops.go` (connection config), `exporter.go` (server config), and `collectors.go` (per-collector switches). Both are wrong: `rg -c "collectorInstances = append" internal/collector/*.go` (excluding tests) returns 47, matching docgen's own `docgen: parsed 47 collectors` output and the 47 `Subsystem` constants declared in `collector.go`. `internal/options/` also contains `otlp.go` (14 flags), `pyroscope.go` (6 flags), `init.go`, and `log.go` — two entire opt-in telemetry config families are undocumented in the bullet.

The root cause is that `CLAUDE.md` is hand-maintained prose, entirely outside the docgen stat-pinning system: `scripts/docgen/stats.go`'s `statRules()` rewrites the "N sub-collectors" figure in exactly 9 allowlisted files (`zensical.toml`, `docs/.meta.yml`, `docs/index.md`, `docs/metrics/*`, `docs/collectors/*`, `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `docs/integration-dashboards.md`), and `CLAUDE.md` is not one of them. The same gap lets stale "30 collectors" prose survive in three more published docs pages that also sit outside the allowlist: `docs/404.md:179`, `docs/getting-started.md:122`, and `docs/troubleshooting.md:43`. `make docs-check` passes green on all of these because it only validates the files `statRules` knows about plus flag/env doc tokens — it never scans the rest of `docs/` for numeric collector/metric claims.

## Evidence

- `CLAUDE.md:31`: `runs 30 sub-collectors concurrently via goroutines` — actual count is 47 (`rg -c "collectorInstances = append" internal/collector/*.go | wc -l` → 47; `docgen: parsed 47 collectors`).
- `CLAUDE.md:33`: `ops.go handles OPNsense connection config; exporter.go handles server config; collectors.go has per-collector disable switches` — omits `otlp.go`, `pyroscope.go`, `init.go`, `log.go`.
- `docs/404.md:179`: `Overview of all 30 collectors and their configuration`
- `docs/getting-started.md:122`: `Overview of all 30 collectors and what they monitor`
- `docs/troubleshooting.md:43`: `Each scrape fans out to ~30 collectors in parallel`
- Contrast with correctly-pinned pages: `docs/index.md:56`, `docs/architecture.md:72`, and `docs/collectors/index.md:11` all correctly say "47 sub-collectors" — proving the pinning mechanism works, it's just missing these 4 files (CLAUDE.md + the 3 docs pages) from its allowlist.
- `scripts/docgen/stats.go:41-73` (`statRules`): confirms the allowlist covers 9 files, none of which are `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/404.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`, or `docs/troubleshooting.md`.
- Verified in a throwaway worktree: `make dashboard && make docs-check` prints `applied 16 stat rules across 9 files` and `docgen: check passed — all generated docs current` while the three stale pages still say "30".

## Failure scenario / impact

A contributor or coding agent following CLAUDE.md for repo conventions (this repo's own onboarding contract) undercounts the sub-collector fan-out by 36% when reasoning about scrape concurrency, API load on the firewall, or whether a change touched "all" collectors. Separately, any user landing on the getting-started page, the 404 page, or the troubleshooting page is told the exporter has 30 collectors — off by 17 — and `make docs-check` gives no warning today or after any future collector addition, since none of these four files are covered by the stat-pinning gate.

## Suggested direction

Fix the stale numbers now (CLAUDE.md count/package bullet, and the three docs pages), and close the systemic gap by either adding these four files to the existing `subCollectors` regex rule in `scripts/docgen/stats.go`'s `statRules()`, or — more robustly — adding a repo-wide scan that fails `make docs-check` on any `\d+ (sub-)?collectors` token in `docs/` (and `CLAUDE.md`) that doesn't match the computed count, replacing the per-file allowlist model.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CLAUDE.md:31` states the correct current sub-collector count (or is reworded to avoid a hardcoded number, e.g. "all registered sub-collectors")
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md:33`'s description of `internal/options/` names `otlp.go`, `pyroscope.go`, `init.go`, and `log.go` alongside the existing files
- [ ] `docs/404.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`, and `docs/troubleshooting.md` no longer say "30 collectors"/"~30 collectors" and instead reflect the docgen-computed count
- [ ] `make docs-check` fails (non-zero exit) if any of these four files contains a collector-count figure that disagrees with the count docgen computes from `collectorInstances`
- [ ] A test or docgen check exists that would have caught the original drift (e.g. asserting the count in `CLAUDE.md` matches `len(collectorInstances)`)

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `1774373` (straight to main).

- `CLAUDE.md` now says **47 sub-collectors** (acceptance #1) and its `internal/options/` bullet names `otlp.go`, `pyroscope.go`, `log.go`, `init.go` alongside the existing files (acceptance #2).
- `docs/404.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` now reflect 47 (acceptance #3).
- All four are added to `scripts/docgen/stats.go` `statRules()` (new `all \d+ collectors` / `~\d+ collectors` patterns + the existing `\d+ sub-collectors` for CLAUDE.md), so **`make docs-check` now fails on drift** — verified: reverting CLAUDE.md to "30 sub-collectors" makes docs-check FATAL, 47 passes (acceptance #4).
- `TestClaudeMDCollectorCount` asserts CLAUDE.md's count equals `len(collector.AllCollectors())` (acceptance #5).

Gate: `make docs`/`docs-check` green, `make test` green (incl. new test), `make lint` 0 issues.

body:
## Problem

`grafana/README.md` contains hand-written prose about the dashboard's tab count/names and the alert/recording rule counts, and none of it is regenerated or lint-checked, so it has drifted from the actual generated artifacts. The dashboard actually has 30 tabs (per `grafana/dashboard-stats.json` and `grafana/build_dashboard.py`'s `register_subsystem_tabs()`), but `grafana/README.md` says "16 tabs" and lists only 16 tab names, omitting 14 real tabs (Aliases, Tailscale, Syslog, Q-Feeds, HAProxy, Nginx, FRR Routing, Monit, CrowdSec, UPS, Captive Portal, Traffic Shaper, HA Sync, Chrony). Separately, `grafana/README.md` says "18 alert rules" while the generated `grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml` actually contains 19 (`make rules` prints `alerts: 19  recording rules: 8`).

The root cause is the same in both cases: `scripts/docgen/stats.go`'s `statRules()` — which pins metric/collector/tab counts into `README.md` and `docs/*.md` via regex find-replace driven by `grafana/dashboard-stats.json` — does not include `grafana/README.md` at all, and has no equivalent rule sourced from the alert-rule generator. `docs/integration-dashboards.md:59` does get the leading tab *count* patched correctly ("all 556 metrics across 30 tabs") but the same sentence's trailing tab-name enumeration is never touched by regen, so it still lists the stale 16 names right next to the correct count of 30 — an internal contradiction in the same sentence. `make docs-check` passes cleanly through all of this because `scripts/docgen/doclint.go` only validates `--flag.name`/`ENV_VAR`-shaped tokens, never tab counts, tab names, or alert-rule counts.

## Evidence

- `grafana/README.md:8` — "a single Grafana v2 dynamic dashboard ... with 16 tabs that auto-show/hide"
- `grafana/README.md:29-31` — "One dashboard, 16 tabs: Overview, System & Resources, Interfaces, Firewall & PF, Gateways & WAN, DNS - Unbound, DHCP, VPN, Routing & Neighbors, Protocol Stats, NTP, Certificates, Services/Cron/DynDNS, NetFlow, CARP/HA, Diagnostics" — missing 14 real tabs
- `grafana/dashboard-stats.json` (checked in, written by `make dashboard`) — `{"metrics": 556, "panels": 441, "tabs": 30}`
- `docs/integration-dashboards.md:59` — "all 556 metrics across 30 tabs" (count correct) immediately followed by the identical stale 16-name parenthetical list (contradicts its own count)
- `grafana/README.md:79` — "alerts/ contains 18 alert rules and 8 recording rules" vs. `make rules` output "alerts: 19  recording rules: 8" and `grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml` containing 19 `- alert:` entries and 8 `- record:` entries
- `scripts/docgen/stats.go`'s `statRules()` list covers only `README.md` (root) and `docs/integration-dashboards.md` with a `dash` regex (`all \d+ metrics across \d+ tabs`) that patches only the leading count, never a trailing tab-name enumeration, and never covers `grafana/README.md` or any alert-rule count
- `scripts/docgen/doclint.go` validates only `--flag.name` and `ENV_VAR`-shaped tokens — confirmed unrelated to tab/alert counts, so `make docs-check` passes despite the drift

Both counts were reproduced against a clean `make dashboard` / `make rules` rebuild at HEAD (git diff empty afterward), so the generated artifacts are ground truth and the README prose is the stale side. Not livebox-dependent — pure repo/docs finding.

## Failure scenario / impact

A user reads `grafana/README.md` before importing the dashboard, sees "16 tabs" and the 16-name list, and concludes 14 real subsystem integrations (HAProxy, Nginx, FRR, CrowdSec, UPS, Captive Portal, Traffic Shaper, Chrony, HA Sync, Monit, Syslog, Q-Feeds, Tailscale, Aliases) aren't covered — possibly skipping deployment for those integrations or filing a false "missing coverage" report. Separately, a new alert rule was added to `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py` at some point, bumping the true count from 18 to 19, but nothing flagged the README mismatch; a user cross-checking "did I deploy all the alerts" against the README undercounts by one, or loses trust in the docs once they notice the generated yaml disagrees. An agent or reviewer relying on this README to verify dashboard/alert coverage reaches the wrong conclusion in both cases.

## Suggested direction

Either extend `scripts/docgen/stats.go`'s stat-pinning to also cover `grafana/README.md` (tab count and, ideally, a generated tab-name list sourced from `grafana/dashboard-stats.json` or the `register_subsystem_tabs` order list) and drop/regenerate the stale tab-name enumeration in `docs/integration-dashboards.md`; and have `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py` emit an alert/recording count artifact (similar to `dashboard-stats.json`) that a new stat rule pins into `grafana/README.md`, so `make docs-check` can catch future drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grafana/README.md`'s tab count and `docs/integration-dashboards.md`'s tab-name enumeration are sourced from generated data (e.g. `grafana/dashboard-stats.json` or the `register_subsystem_tabs` order) rather than hand-typed lists
- [ ] `grafana/README.md`'s alert-rule and recording-rule counts are sourced from a generated artifact (e.g. a stats file emitted by `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py`) rather than hand-typed prose
- [ ] `make docs-check` fails if `grafana/README.md`'s tab count, tab-name list, or alert/recording-rule counts drift from the current generated dashboard/rules output
- [ ] After the fix, `grafana/README.md` states 30 tabs (matching all tab names) and 19 alert rules / 8 recording rules, matching a clean `make dashboard` && `make rules` rebuild
- [ ] `docs/integration-dashboards.md:59`'s tab-name parenthetical no longer contradicts its own stated tab count

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `53061bb` (straight to main).

Everything is now sourced from generated artifacts:
- `build_dashboard.py` writes the ordered `tab_names` into `dashboard-stats.json`; docgen injects that list into a `docgen:dashboard-tabs` marker region in **both** `grafana/README.md` and `docs/integration-dashboards.md` (acceptance #1, #5 — the parenthetical no longer contradicts its own count).
- Alert/recording counts come from `loadRulesStats`, which counts the committed `grafana-managed/*.json` AlertRule/RecordingRule manifests (i.e. the `make rules` output), pinned via new stat rules (acceptance #2).
- `make docs-check` now **FATALs** on tab-count, tab-name-list, or alert/recording-count drift — verified by reverting each (acceptance #3).
- README now states **30 tabs** (all 30 names) and **19 alert rules / 8 recording rules** (acceptance #4). Also added the missing `OPNsenseGatewayDownFailover` row so the alert table matches the pinned 19.

Gate: `make docs`/`docs-check` green, `make test` + `make lint` (0 issues) green.

body:
## Problem

The container security documentation and the Kubernetes deployment manifest both state that the exporter's container image runs as UID 65534, but the image itself is built `FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot`, whose fixed `nonroot` identity is UID **65532**, not 65534 (65534 is the Debian `nobody` UID, a different convention). The Dockerfile's own `USER` directive confirms 65532. The security doc and the k8s manifest were written against the wrong UID convention, so they factually misdescribe the identity the container actually runs as (or, for the manifest, deliberately override it with a different value).

This is a documentation/manifest correctness issue, not a runtime break: Kubernetes' `securityContext.runAsUser` overrides the image's `USER` directive regardless of mismatch, and since the deployment also sets `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` with no writes required outside the mounted volume, the pod still starts fine under 65534. The risk is that anyone hardening a PodSecurityPolicy/SecurityContextConstraint or a `runAsUser` allowlist based on the documented value will key it to the wrong UID.

## Evidence

- `Dockerfile:30` — final stage: `FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot@sha256:...` (distroless `nonroot` variant = fixed UID/GID 65532).
- `Dockerfile:45` — `USER 65532:65532`, confirming the image's baked-in runtime identity is 65532.
- `docs/security.md:168` — states "Non-root execution -- runs as UID 65534 (nonroot)" — wrong UID for this base image.
- `deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml:31-32` — `runAsNonRoot: true` / `runAsUser: 65534` — pins a different UID (65534) than the image's own `USER` directive (65532).

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator reads `docs/security.md`, takes "UID 65534" as authoritative, and writes a PodSecurityPolicy/SecurityContextConstraint or a `runAsUser` allowlist rule keyed to 65534. This doesn't match the image's actual baked-in identity (65532), and while the current manifest's explicit `runAsUser: 65534` override still lets the pod start (Kubernetes overrides the image `USER` at the container-runtime level), the docs remain factually wrong about what identity the image itself uses, and the manifest's choice of 65534 appears to be an unintentional mismatch rather than a deliberate decision. Anyone auditing container identity against the documented value will draw the wrong conclusion.

## Suggested direction

Correct `docs/security.md` to state UID 65532 (matching the Dockerfile's `USER` directive and the distroless `nonroot` convention), and align `deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml`'s `runAsUser` to 65532 to match the image — or drop the explicit `runAsUser` and rely on `runAsNonRoot: true` alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/security.md` states the container runs as UID 65532, not 65534, matching the distroless `nonroot` base image.
- [ ] `deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml`'s `securityContext.runAsUser` is set to 65532 (or removed in favor of `runAsNonRoot: true` alone) so it matches the image's actual `USER` directive.
- [ ] `Dockerfile`'s `USER 65532:65532` directive and the docs/manifest values are cross-checked so all three sources of truth (Dockerfile, docs/security.md, deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml) agree on the UID.
- [ ] `make docs-check` (or an equivalent doclint/grep check) passes with the corrected UID, and no other doc page (e.g. README, any other k8s example manifest) still references 65534 in this context.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `44fa537` (straight to main).

The distroless `:nonroot` base image runs as UID **65532** (Dockerfile: `USER 65532:65532`); 65534 is Debian's `nobody`, a different convention. Corrected all sources to 65532:
- `docs/security.md` — now 65532 ✅ acceptance #1
- `deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml` — `runAsUser: 65532` ✅ acceptance #2
- also `docs/deployment/docker.md` and `docs/deployment/kubernetes.md` (×2), which the issue's acceptance #4 flagged as "no other doc page"

All three sources of truth (Dockerfile `USER`, docs/security.md, deployment.yaml) now agree ✅ acceptance #3. `git grep 65534` across tracked source returns nothing; `make docs-check` green ✅ acceptance #4. The generated `site/` snapshot refreshes from `docs/` on the next docs-sync build.

body:
## Problem

The DHCP tab in the Grafana dashboard hides an entire backend's row (service-health stat, lease-count panels, pool-size panels) whenever that backend's current lease count is zero, instead of hiding it only when the backend is genuinely absent. Each backend row is gated by a "sentinel" query-result variable used with Grafana conditional rendering: the sentinel query filters for `leases_total > 0`, so a running backend with zero active leases produces an empty query result — identical to a backend that isn't configured at all — and the row vanishes.

The underlying metric is correct: `internal/collector/dnsmasq.go` unconditionally emits `opnsense_dnsmasq_leases_total` (including the value `0`) on every successful scrape of a running dnsmasq instance. The dashboard's `> 0` filter conflates "backend not present" with "backend present but idle," so it throws away a legitimate zero sample rather than treating it as a valid signal that dnsmasq is up and simply has no active leases right now. The same `count > 0` gating pattern is used for the Kea and ISC DHCPv4/DHCPv6 sentinels in the same file.

## Evidence

`grafana/tabs/dhcp.py:31-32`:
```python
b.sentinel("has_dnsmasq",
           "query_result(opnsense_dnsmasq_leases_total > 0)")
```
Similarly gated sentinels using the same `> 0` pattern: `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py:35-36` (`has_kea`, `(opnsense_kea_dhcp4_leases_total + opnsense_kea_dhcp6_leases_total) > 0`), and the ISC DHCPv4/DHCPv6 sentinels at `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py:41-46`.

The row gated on `has_dnsmasq` bundles the service-health stat and pool-size panel with the lease counters, so they all disappear together — see `dhcp.py:375-378` for the row composition, and the `dnsmasq_svc` stat definition around `dhcp.py:77-84` (service running/stopped) and `kea_svc` around `dhcp.py:177-184`.

`internal/collector/dnsmasq.go:88-99` shows `Update()` unconditionally sets `leasesTotal = float64(data.TotalLeases)` on every successful scrape, with no gating on whether the backend currently has any active clients — so `leases_total=0` is a normal, valid sample for a running-but-idle dnsmasq instance, not an absence signal.

This is a dashboard-definition issue (`make dashboard` output), not verified against a live box.

## Failure scenario / impact

A fresh deployment enables dnsmasq (or Kea, or ISC DHCPv4/v6) as the DHCP backend but no client has yet requested a lease, or a quiet/low-traffic segment has had all its leases expire overnight. In either case `opnsense_<backend>_leases_total` reports `0`, the sentinel's `> 0` filter excludes it, and the entire DHCP row for that backend — including the "Service Running" stat and pool-size panels — disappears from the dashboard. An operator looking at the DHCP tab at exactly that moment sees no evidence the backend is running at all, and cannot distinguish "DHCP backend is down" from "DHCP backend is up with zero current leases," undermining the very health-status panel meant to answer that question.

## Suggested direction

Gate each row's sentinel on backend presence rather than lease count — e.g. `query_result(opnsense_<backend>_service_running)` or `label_values(opnsense_<backend>_pool_size, interface)` — so a live but idle backend still shows its row. Note the separate round-1 finding about plugin-absent ISC collectors emitting spurious zero metrics is a distinct issue and is better addressed collector-side, not by keeping this count-gating approach.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `has_dnsmasq` sentinel (and the Kea, ISC DHCPv4, ISC DHCPv6 equivalents) in `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py` no longer filters on `leases_total > 0`; it uses a presence signal (e.g. `service_running` or a `label_values` lookup) that is emitted regardless of current lease count.
- [ ] `make dashboard` regenerates the dashboard JSON with the updated sentinel query for each backend row and passes the metric-coverage gate.
- [ ] A documented/tested scenario (unit test or fixture asserting the generated sentinel PromQL string) confirms the dnsmasq row's sentinel no longer contains a `> 0` lease-count comparison.
- [ ] Manually or via fixture data, confirm that with `opnsense_dnsmasq_leases_total 0` and `opnsense_dnsmasq_service_running 1` present, the dnsmasq row (service stat + pool-size panels) still renders.
- [ ] The fix is applied consistently to all four backends (dnsmasq, Kea, ISC DHCPv4, ISC DHCPv6) sharing this pattern in `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py`.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `2d16b13` (straight to main).

All four DHCP-backend presence sentinels now gate on **existence**, not lease count (acceptance #1, #5):
- `has_dnsmasq` → `label_values(opnsense_dnsmasq_service_running, __name__)`
- `has_kea` → `label_values(opnsense_kea_service_running, __name__)`
- `has_dhcpv4_isc` / `has_dhcpv6_isc` → their `leases_total` (ISC collectors have no `service_running` and emit nothing when the plugin is absent — Present-gated, #87 — so existence is a valid presence signal)

`label_values(metric, __name__)` is non-empty whenever the series exists regardless of value, so a live-but-idle backend (leases_total=0) still shows its row — including the service-health stat (acceptance #4). No `> 0` lease comparison remains in any of the four (acceptance #3).

**Guard (acceptance #3):** added a build-time check in `build_dashboard.py` that fails if any of the four DHCP presence sentinels reintroduces a `> 0` threshold. Regenerated `dashboard.json`; coverage 556/556 (acceptance #2).

Note: `has_carp_vips`, `has_captiveportal`, `has_trafficshaper` use the same `query_result(... > 0)` pattern, but they gate **detail-only** rows (no health stat) and sit outside #114's DHCP scope, so I left them as intentional "hide when nothing to show" gating. Happy to revisit them under a separate issue if you'd prefer existence-gating there too.

body:
## Problem

The Grafana dashboard's "Exporter Runtime (Go client metrics)" row hardcodes `job="opnsense-exporter"` into the four PromQL queries it uses for goroutine count, resident memory, heap usage, and CPU seconds. That job label contradicts the exporter's own documented Prometheus scrape configuration, which uses `job_name: opnsense` (so Prometheus attaches `job="opnsense"`, not `job="opnsense-exporter"`). Only the Kubernetes ScrapeConfig CRD example and `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml` use `job: opnsense-exporter`. As a result, anyone who follows the plain getting-started guide gets a dashboard row whose four panels never return data.

Making this worse, the row's visibility sentinel (`has_go_runtime`) queries `label_values(go_goroutines, __name__)` with no job filter at all, so it is satisfied by any Go process being scraped into the same Prometheus/datasource — including Grafana itself, or an unrelated Go service. The row therefore does not reliably hide when the exporter's own runtime metrics are absent; it can stay visible while permanently showing four empty panels.

## Evidence

- `grafana/build_dashboard.py:150-156` — the four panel queries hardcode the job label:
  ```
  go_goroutines{job="opnsense-exporter"}
  process_resident_memory_bytes{job="opnsense-exporter"}
  go_memstats_heap_inuse_bytes{job="opnsense-exporter"}
  process_cpu_seconds_total{job="opnsense-exporter"}
  ```
- `grafana/build_dashboard.py:121` — the row's gating sentinel has no job filter: `has_go_runtime = label_values(go_goroutines, __name__)`, so it's satisfied by any Go process's `go_goroutines` series in the datasource, not specifically the opnsense-exporter's.
- `docs/getting-started.md:106` — documented scrape config uses `job_name: opnsense`.
- `docs/integration-dashboards.md:19` and `:37` — same, `job_name: opnsense`.
- `docs/deployment/kubernetes.md:193` — the doc's recommended static-config path also uses `job_name: opnsense`.
- `docs/deployment/kubernetes.md:161` (ScrapeConfig CRD example) and `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml:19` are the only places that set `job: opnsense-exporter`, i.e. the minority path.

## Failure scenario / impact

A user follows `docs/getting-started.md` and configures Prometheus with `job_name: opnsense` as documented. They then import the shipped Grafana dashboard. The "Exporter Runtime (Go client metrics)" row appears (its sentinel is satisfied because the same Prometheus instance also scrapes some other Go application, e.g. Grafana itself), but all four panels — goroutines, resident memory, heap usage, CPU seconds — are permanently empty because their queries filter on `job="opnsense-exporter"`, a label value that never exists in this setup. The row looks broken/dead rather than correctly hiding itself.

## Suggested direction

Pick one canonical job name across the docs, `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml`, and the dashboard queries, or make the job selector a dashboard variable that defaults to a permissive regex (e.g. `job=~"opnsense.*"`); align the row's visibility sentinel to use the same job selector as the panels so it only shows when the exporter's own Go runtime metrics are genuinely present.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The four "Exporter Runtime" panel queries in `grafana/build_dashboard.py` use a job selector that matches the job name(s) actually documented in `docs/getting-started.md` and `docs/integration-dashboards.md` (or a variable/regex that covers both documented values).

body:
## Problem

The dnsmasq and Kea DHCP lease-detail tables in the Grafana dashboard are built as single-query, instant-query tables. For that query shape the Prometheus datasource always names the numeric sample column `Value` — in these panels that value is the lease expiry timestamp. The table transform config both excludes the `Value` field (`excludeByName`) and simultaneously defines a unit override keyed on `Value` (`dateTimeAsIso`), plus a panel description promising "Value = expire timestamp (shown as ISO date)". Because the field is excluded, the unit override never applies to anything and the rendered table is missing the one column — lease expiry — that these panels exist to show.

This is a self-contradictory config, not a style nit: `grafana/builder.py`'s `table()` helper merges `excludes` into `excludeByName` and independently generates a `byName` matcher override from `unit_overrides`, so excluding and overriding the same field name are two unrelated code paths that silently conflict. The dead override is already baked into the committed `grafana/dashboard.json` artifact for the Dnsmasq Lease Details panel (`excludeByName` contains `"Value": true` while `overrides` still carries a byName matcher on `"Value"` with unit `dateTimeAsIso`).

## Evidence

- `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py:109` — `excludes=["Value", ...]`
- `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py:116` — `unit_overrides={"Value": "dateTimeAsIso"}`
- `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py:118-122` — panel description: `"Value = expire timestamp (shown as ISO date)"`
- Same contradiction repeated at `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py:218` / `:225` (Kea DHCPv4) and `grafana/tabs/dhcp.py:240` / `:247` (Kea DHCPv6)
- `grafana/builder.py:215-217` — `excludes` merged into `excludeByName`
- `grafana/builder.py:222-224` — `unit_overrides` generates an independent `byName` matcher override
- `grafana/dashboard.json` — the "Dnsmasq Lease Details" panel's committed `excludeByName` includes `{"Value": true, ...}` while `overrides` still contains a byName matcher targeting `"Value"` with unit `dateTimeAsIso`, confirming the dead override ships in the generated artifact
- Data source: `internal/collector/dnsmasq.go:127-137` emits the lease expiry as the sample value on `opnsense_dnsmasq_lease_info`, so the timestamp genuinely is the `Value` field being excluded

## Failure scenario / impact

An operator enables `--exporter.enable-dnsmasq-details` or `--exporter.enable-kea-details` specifically to see lease expiry information in the dashboard. The resulting "Lease Details" table renders IP, hostname, MAC, and interface columns but no expiry column at all — the field is silently dropped by `excludeByName`, despite the panel's own description promising it is shown as an ISO date. The operator has no way to see when a lease expires from this panel, defeating its stated purpose. This applies identically to the dnsmasq, Kea DHCPv4, and Kea DHCPv6 lease-detail tables.

## Suggested direction

Drop `"Value"` from the `excludes` list on the three affected tables, rename the field via a `renameByName`/override to something clearer (e.g. `Expires`), and key the `unit_overrides` entry on the new name so it actually applies. While touching this, also verify the epoch-seconds-to-milliseconds conversion needed for `dateTimeAsIso` to render correctly is in place.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dnsmasq Lease Details table (`grafana/tabs/dhcp.py`) no longer excludes the field carrying the lease-expiry value, and that field is visible in the rendered table
- [ ] The Kea DHCPv4 and Kea DHCPv6 lease-detail tables have the same fix applied (no exclude/override contradiction on the expiry field)
- [ ] `make dashboard` regenerates `grafana/dashboard.json` such that the affected panels' `overrides` target a field that is not also present in that panel's `excludeByName`
- [ ] A test or lint check (e.g. in `grafana/build_dashboard.py` or a dedicated test) fails if any table panel defines a `unit_overrides`/override key that is also listed in that panel's `excludes`
- [ ] The lease-expiry value renders as a human-readable ISO date/time in the table, not a raw epoch number

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `0dbfe5c` (straight to main).

For all three lease-detail tables (dnsmasq, Kea DHCPv4, Kea DHCPv6): dropped `Value` from `excludes`, renamed it to **Expires**, and keyed the `dateTimeAsIso` unit_override on `Expires` (acceptance #1, #2). The query is already `epoch_ms()`-wrapped (×1000), so the column renders as a human-readable ISO date (acceptance #5) — verified in the JSON: 3 panels carry an `Expires` dateTimeAsIso override and none exclude the field (acceptance #3).

**Guard (acceptance #4):** added to `builder.table()` (surfaced by `build_dashboard.py`) — fails the build if any table's `renameByName`/`unit_override` key is also in its `excludes`, catching the exact exclude/override contradiction. Coverage 556/556, `make docs-check` green.

body:
## Problem

`tools/opnsense_api_contract/extract.py` extracts the API endpoint manifest by calling `collect_api_modules(args.source)` once, with no per-controller fault isolation. Internally this walks every controller PHP file and parses it with the vendored `phply`-based grammar from the upstream OPNsense docs library (`upstream-docs/lib/__init__.py`, `parse_api_php`). That function catches `TypeError` from `phply` only long enough to print a diagnostic line, then re-raises it. Because `extract.py` wraps none of this in a try/except, a single controller file that the aging `phply` grammar cannot parse takes down the entire extraction run — no partial manifest, no warning, just a crash and no JSON output at all.

This turns one bad PHP file into total tool failure instead of a graceful "N of M controllers parsed" degradation. It is directly reachable today via the tool's own documented usage (pointing `--source` at a real controller tree, e.g. a live firewall's `/usr/local/opnsense/mvc/app/controllers`), and it is a latent landmine for the weekly CI canary: if any future upstream `opnsense/core` or `opnsense/plugins` commit introduces PHP syntax outside the vendored grammar's support (e.g. class-constant array dereferencing), the canary's extraction step dies outright rather than reporting a handled drift.

## Evidence

- `tools/opnsense_api_contract/extract.py:29` — calls `collect_api_modules(args.source)` with no per-file try/except around the controller-parsing loop.
- Upstream docs lib `upstream-docs/lib/__init__.py` (`parse_api_php`, ~line 155-173) — catches `TypeError` from `phply`'s `parse()` only to print a diagnostic, then does `raise e`, propagating the exception to the caller.
- `upstream-docs/lib/utils.py` (`collect_api_modules`) — also has no per-file guard; the first unparseable controller aborts the whole walk.

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: a commercial third-party plugin controller (`.../Zenarmor/Api/InstallerController.php`) contains a class-constant array dereference (`$db = ConfigModel::Databases[$i];`) that the vendored `phply` grammar cannot parse. Running `extract.py --source <controller tree>` against a tree containing that file crashes with:

```
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable
```

exit code 1, no JSON emitted. A per-file skip-and-warn instrumented run showed 160 of 161 controllers parse fine (`ok=160 bad=1`) — the tool has everything it needs to degrade gracefully but doesn't.

Note: the public `opnsense/core` + `opnsense/plugins` repos that the CI canary (`api-contract.yml`) currently clones do NOT contain this Zenarmor file (it's a paid/commercial plugin not in the public plugins repo), so the canary is not broken today — this failure is currently latent for CI but immediate for anyone running the tool against a real deployed box's controller tree, which is the tool's own documented `--source` usage.

## Failure scenario / impact

1. A maintainer or contributor runs `extract.py --source /usr/local/opnsense/mvc/app/controllers` against a real firewall (or any controller tree containing a third-party plugin like Zenarmor/Sensei) to validate or refresh the API contract manifest. The single unparseable controller crashes the entire tool with an uncaught `TypeError`, producing zero output instead of the ~2,392-endpoint manifest minus the one bad file.
2. If upstream `opnsense/core` or `opnsense/plugins` ever merges a controller using PHP syntax the vendored `phply` grammar doesn't support, the weekly `api-contract.yml` canary's "Extract upstream endpoints per ref" step (running under `set -euo pipefail`) dies with exit code 1 — indistinguishable from an infra failure, not the tool's intended "drift detected" exit path. No drift report is produced and the canary stays broken until someone manually patches the parser, right when upstream is actively changing.

## Suggested direction

Replace the single `collect_api_modules` call with a per-file walk (using the same file filters as upstream's `utils.py`) that try/excepts each controller's `ApiParser(...).parse_api_php()` call individually, logs a warning naming the failed file to stderr, and continues with the remaining controllers — keeping the existing `--min` endpoint-count floor as the guard against catastrophic breakage. Consider an optional `--strict` flag to preserve today's fail-fast behavior where desired.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test feeds `extract.py`'s controller-parsing path a directory containing one valid controller and one controller with unparseable PHP (e.g. a class-constant array dereference), and asserts the tool exits 0, emits a manifest containing the valid controller's endpoints, and prints a warning naming the failed file.
- [ ] A unit test confirms that when ALL controllers in the source tree fail to parse (or the parsed endpoint count falls below `--min`), the tool still exits non-zero (the existing floor guard is preserved).
- [ ] A regression test using the reproduced Zenarmor `InstallerController.php`-style construct (class-constant array dereference) confirms it no longer crashes the whole run.
- [ ] `make docs-check` / the `api-contract.yml` canary workflow is unaffected by the change on the current public `opnsense/core` + `opnsense/plugins` source (still reports the same endpoint count as before, modulo any newly-tolerated files).
- [ ] Tool documentation/help text for `extract.py` notes the per-file skip-and-warn behavior (and the `--strict` flag, if added).

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `fca0054`.

- **`extract.py`**: replaced the single `collect_api_modules(source)` call with a per-file walk (`_iter_controller_files`, mirroring upstream `lib.utils`'s exact filters — `*controller.php` under `mvc/app/controllers` in an `.../Api` dir, honouring `EXCLUDE_CONTROLLERS`) that `try/except`s each `ApiParser(...).parse_api_php()` individually, warns to stderr naming the bad file, and continues. The `--min` floor is preserved; added `--strict` for fail-fast. The upstream parser prints its `error in filename ...` diagnostic to **stdout** before raising, so I wrap the parse in `contextlib.redirect_stdout(sys.stderr)` to keep the JSON output clean.
- **Docstring/help** document the skip-and-warn behaviour and `--strict`.

**Tests** (`extract_test.py`, run via `OPNSENSE_DOCS_REPO` like the existing one): `test_one_unparseable_controller_is_skipped_not_fatal` (exit 0, valid endpoints emitted, warning names the file — #1/#3), `test_all_unparseable_below_min_exits_nonzero` (floor preserved — #2), `test_strict_mode_fails_fast_on_unparseable`, and the existing happy-path test still passes.

Note on #3: the current vendored phply **tolerates** the original Zenarmor class-constant array dereference (`ConfigModel::Databases[$i]`) — I verified it parses fine now — so the `testdata/Bad` fixture uses a PHP 8.1 `enum` (confirmed still unparseable by the current grammar) to actually exercise the skip path; the fixture comment records the Zenarmor origin. #4: the per-file walk produces identical output for parseable controllers, so the canary's count on the current public `opnsense/core`+`plugins` is unchanged. All 4 Python tests pass locally against a fresh `opnsense/docs` checkout; Go gate (`make test`/`lint`/`docs-check`) green.

body:
## Problem

`cmd/apicontract/main.go` maintains an `exemptEndpoints` list (firmware, firmwareInfo, keaLeases4, keaLeases6) that the source-diff canary deliberately skips, because these endpoints can't be parsed/verified from OPNsense's documented source. The comment justifying this exemption claims the gap is covered elsewhere: "Real removal of these would be caught by the live-box stage (P3), not the source parser." No such stage exists anywhere in the repo or CI.

The only live-box tooling in the repo is `cmd/apicapture`, and its `captureContracts()` function iterates exclusively over `opnsense/response_contract.go`'s `ResponseContracts()`, which currently contains a single entry (`healthCheck`). It never touches firmware or Kea lease endpoints, so even a manual `make capture` run provides no coverage for the four exempted endpoints. A repo-wide search for "live-box" turns up only this comment and a passing mention in the apicapture README describing a manual, local action — not an automated CI stage. No `.github/workflows/*.yml` job invokes `apicapture` at all. The result is that these four endpoints have zero automated drift detection: the source-diff canary is structurally blind to them by design, and the compensating control the comment promises simply doesn't run anywhere.

## Evidence

- `cmd/apicontract/main.go:22-40` — `exemptEndpoints` list and the comment: `// Real removal of these would be caught by the live-box stage (P3), not the source parser.`
- `cmd/apicapture/capture.go:36-50` — `captureContracts()` iterates only `opnsense.ResponseContracts()`.
- `opnsense/response_contract.go:68-77` — `ResponseContracts()` returns exactly one contract (`healthCheck`); no firmware/kea entries exist.
- `rg -n 'live-box'` across the repo matches only the `main.go` comment and the `cmd/apicapture/README.md` prose describing `make capture` as a manual/local action.
- `rg -n 'apicapture'` under `.github/workflows/` returns zero hits — no CI job runs the capture tool, automated or otherwise.
- Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: `api/core/firmware/status` → 200, `api/kea/leases4/search` → 200, `api/kea/leases/search` → 404 (validating the underlying exemption rationale itself, while confirming no automated check re-validates this over time).

## Failure scenario / impact

A future OPNsense release renames or removes `api/core/firmware/status` or the Kea `leases4`/`leases6` search routes. The source-diff canary is exempt for these four endpoints by design and will not flag it. No live-box stage exists to catch it either, because `apicapture` never captures manifest/GET endpoints outside the single `healthCheck` response contract, and no CI workflow invokes `apicapture` at all. The first signal of the breakage becomes silently broken firmware or Kea-lease collectors on user-facing OPNsense installs — precisely the unannounced-breakage scenario the comment claims is already mitigated.

## Suggested direction

Either build the referenced safety net — extend `apicapture` (or a new mode) to probe every manifest GET endpoint, including the four exempted ones, against a live/beta box in CI and flag non-2xx responses for non-plugin-gated endpoints — or, at minimum, correct the comment in `cmd/apicontract/main.go` to state plainly that these four endpoints are an acknowledged coverage gap with no automated live-box verification, rather than asserting a stage that doesn't exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The comment in `cmd/apicontract/main.go` no longer references a "live-box stage (P3)" unless that stage is implemented and actually runs in CI.
- [ ] `rg -n 'live-box' cmd/ opnsense/` (or equivalent) returns text that accurately reflects real, existing tooling behavior — no aspirational/uninstantiated stages described as if they run today.
- [ ] Either: (a) a new or extended tool/CI job exists that probes `api/core/firmware/status`, `api/core/firmware/info`, and both Kea lease-search endpoints against a live or mocked box and fails on unexpected non-2xx/non-404 status, with a test asserting it runs on at least these four endpoints; or (b) the exemption comment/README is updated to explicitly document these four as an unmonitored blind spot.
- [ ] If a live-box probing stage is added, it is wired into a `.github/workflows/*.yml` job (confirmed via `rg -n 'apicapture'` under `.github/workflows/` returning at least one hit) rather than remaining a manual-only `make capture` step.
- [ ] `make docs-check` (or equivalent lint) continues to pass after the comment/doc changes.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `7b777a1` (option b — corrected the comment to document the blind spot honestly). Building an automated live-box probing stage (option a) would require a persistent OPNsense box reachable from GitHub Actions, which doesn't exist, so per the acceptance's explicit alternative I corrected the claim instead.

- **`cmd/apicontract/main.go`**: removed "Real removal of these would be caught by the live-box stage (P3)" and replaced it with an explicit "Coverage gap (acknowledged)" note stating these four endpoints have no automated drift detection — the source-diff canary is exempt by design, and the only live-box tooling (`cmd/apicapture`/`make capture`) is a manual, local action that captures response contracts, not these manifest endpoints (#1, #3b).
- `rg -n 'live-box' cmd/ opnsense/` now returns only text that accurately describes real tooling (the one match is my sentence stating no such stage exists) (#2). The other repo `live box` mentions (monit_test, dhcp_pools, system_resources_test, apicapture README) are factual and were left as-is.

`go build`/`go vet` clean; `make docs-check` passes (#5).

body:
## Problem

`internal/options/ops.go` resolves `OPS_API_KEY_FILE` and `OPS_API_SECRET_FILE` with a bare `os.LookupEnv(...)` check that only tests `ok`, not whether the value is non-empty. `os.LookupEnv` returns `ok=true` for a variable that is *set but empty* (e.g. `OPS_API_KEY_FILE=`), so an empty value is treated the same as a real file path and passed straight into `getLineFromFile("")`, which calls `os.Open("")` and always fails. The exporter then aborts startup with a misleading "failed to read OPS_API_KEY_FILE" error, even when a perfectly valid API key/secret was supplied via flag or the non-file env var.

This is inconsistent with the sibling secret-resolution helper `resolveSecret` in `internal/options/pyroscope.go` (used for the Pyroscope and OTLP secrets), which explicitly guards `ok && path != ""` before reading the file — and falls through to the non-file value when the `_FILE` env var is empty. `resolveSecret`'s own comment claims to mirror the `OPS_API_*_FILE` precedence in `ops.go`, but `ops.go` itself lacks the guard it's supposed to mirror, so the three secret families (OPS API key, OPS API secret, Pyroscope/OTLP secrets) behave differently for the identical "set but empty" input.

## Evidence

- `internal/options/ops.go:37` — `getLineFromFile` (opens the given path unconditionally; empty path always errors)
- `internal/options/ops.go:58` — `opsAPISecret`: `if env, ok := os.LookupEnv("OPS_API_SECRET_FILE"); ok { ... getLineFromFile(env) }` — no `env != ""` guard
- `internal/options/ops.go:75` — `opsAPIKey`: same pattern for `OPS_API_KEY_FILE`
- `internal/options/pyroscope.go:75` — the correct pattern, for comparison: `if path, ok := os.LookupEnv(fileEnvVar); ok && path != "" { ... }`

Reproduction (built from HEAD):
```
OPS_API_KEY_FILE= ./opnsense-exporter --opnsense.protocol=https --opnsense.address=127.0.0.1 --opnsense.api-key=k --opnsense.api-secret=s
```
```
level=ERROR msg="failed to assemble OPNsense configuration" err="failed to read OPS_API_KEY_FILE\nopen : no such file or directory"
```
Process then exits with status 1 (via `main.go`'s `os.Exit(1)` on this error path).

## Failure scenario / impact

Docker Compose / Kubernetes manifests frequently template secret env vars so they render as empty strings when unused (e.g. `OPS_API_KEY_FILE:` with no value, or a Helm/Compose interpolation that resolves to `""` rather than being omitted). With this bug, that pattern kills the exporter at startup — `open : no such file or directory` — even though a valid `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_OPS_API_KEY` (or `--opnsense.api-key` flag) is present and would otherwise work. The equivalent pattern on the Pyroscope/OTLP secret env vars does not have this problem, so the breakage is specific and surprising to operators who copy a working pattern from one secret family to another.

## Suggested direction

Route `opsAPIKey` and `opsAPISecret` through the existing `resolveSecret` helper (or otherwise add the `path != ""` guard used there) so all three secret families share the same, already-documented precedence behavior, and delete the duplicated `LookupEnv` + `getLineFromFile` blocks in `ops.go`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test sets `OPS_API_KEY_FILE=""` (present but empty) plus a valid API key via flag/env, and asserts the exporter starts successfully using the flag/env value rather than erroring.
- [ ] A unit test sets `OPS_API_SECRET_FILE=""` (present but empty) plus a valid API secret via flag/env, and asserts the same fallback behavior.
- [ ] A unit test confirms that when `OPS_API_KEY_FILE`/`OPS_API_SECRET_FILE` is unset entirely, behavior is unchanged (no regression to the "not set" path).
- [ ] A unit test confirms that when `OPS_API_KEY_FILE`/`OPS_API_SECRET_FILE` is set to a real, valid file path, the value is still read from that file (no regression to the "file present" path).
- [ ] `internal/options/ops.go`'s `opsAPIKey`/`opsAPISecret` use the same empty-path guard semantics as `resolveSecret` in `internal/options/pyroscope.go`, ideally by sharing the same helper.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `9e56123`. `opsAPIKey`/`opsAPISecret` now delegate to the existing `resolveSecret` helper (from `pyroscope.go`), whose `ok && path != ""` guard falls back to the flag/env value when the `*_FILE` env var is set-but-empty. The duplicated `LookupEnv`+`getLineFromFile` blocks are deleted, so all three secret families (OPS key/secret, Pyroscope/OTLP) now share one precedence — resolving the divergence the `resolveSecret` comment already claimed.

The must-be-set enforcement moves to `OPNSenseConfig.Validate` (`api-key must be set`), still covered by `TestValidate_MissingAPIKey`/`_MissingAPISecret`.

New/updated tests in `ops_test.go`: empty `OPS_API_KEY_FILE`/`OPS_API_SECRET_FILE` falls back to the flag; unset behaves as before; a real valid file path still wins over the flag. Gate green: `make test`, `make lint` (0 issues), `make docs-check`.

body:
## Problem

`internal/options/exporter.go:9-12` defines `MetricsPath` as a plain kingpin `.String()` flag (default `/metrics`) with no validation on its value — not `.Required()`, no regex, no non-empty check. `main.go:422` then registers it directly against the default `http.ServeMux` via `http.Handle(*options.MetricsPath, metricsHandler)`, before any check runs. `main.go:432` (`if *options.MetricsPath != "/" && *options.MetricsPath != ""`) does look like it anticipates an empty value, but that guard only decides whether a *separate* landing page also gets registered at `/` — it does nothing to protect the `http.Handle` call at line 422, which already ran.

Go's `net/http.ServeMux.register` panics on an empty pattern rather than returning an error. So if `--web.telemetry-path` (or `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_WEB_TELEMETRY_PATH`) ever resolves to an empty string — e.g. from a templated Helm value or env var that renders blank — the process panics with a raw Go stack trace instead of failing through the exporter's normal config-error path (`logger.Error(...)` + `os.Exit(1)`, used elsewhere in `main.go` for other bad-config cases).

## Evidence

- `internal/options/exporter.go:9-12` — `MetricsPath` kingpin flag, unvalidated `.String()`, default `/metrics`.
- `main.go:422` — `http.Handle(*options.MetricsPath, metricsHandler)` called unconditionally.
- `main.go:432` — `if *options.MetricsPath != "/" && *options.MetricsPath != ""` — only gates the landing-page registration, not line 422.

Reproduced independently by building HEAD and running:
```
./opnsense-exporter --web.telemetry-path= --opnsense.protocol=https --opnsense.address=127.0.0.1 --opnsense.api-key=x --opnsense.api-secret=x
```
Output:
```
panic: http: invalid pattern
  net/http.(*ServeMux).register
  net/http.Handle
  main.main() main.go:422 +0x3ea8
```
Not livebox-validated (this is a local flag/config path, not a call against a live OPNsense box).

## Failure scenario / impact

A user templates `--web.telemetry-path` from an env var or Helm value that renders empty (e.g. an unset template variable substituting to `""`). On startup, the exporter panics immediately with a raw stack trace instead of a clean error message. Under a supervisor that restarts on crash (systemd, Kubernetes), this becomes an unrecoverable crash loop with no actionable log output telling the operator which flag is wrong.

## Suggested direction

Validate `MetricsPath` at startup — require non-empty and a leading `/` — and exit via the exporter's normal `logger.Error(...)` + `os.Exit(1)` config-error path if it fails, matching how other bad configuration is already handled in `main.go`. Alternatively, treat an empty value as equivalent to the default `/metrics`. Keep the fix scoped to validation; don't redesign the flag.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Running the exporter with `--web.telemetry-path=` (or the equivalent `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_WEB_TELEMETRY_PATH=""` env var) exits with a clear, logged config error instead of panicking.
- [ ] A unit test asserts that an empty or non-`/`-prefixed `MetricsPath` is rejected (or normalized) before `http.Handle` is called.
- [ ] The default behavior (`--web.telemetry-path` unset, default `/metrics`) is unchanged and still registers correctly, covered by an existing or new test.
- [ ] `go test ./...` and `make lint` pass with the fix in place.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `945cfb4`. Added `options.ValidateMetricsPath` (rejects empty and non-`/`-prefixed) and wired it into `main.go` right before `http.Handle(*options.MetricsPath, ...)`, exiting via the standard `logger.Error` + `os.Exit(1)` path.

Verified by building HEAD and running with `--web.telemetry-path=`: now logs `level=ERROR msg="invalid metrics path" err="--web.telemetry-path (OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_WEB_TELEMETRY_PATH) must not be empty"` and exits cleanly — no panic/stack trace. Table test in `exporter_test.go` covers empty + missing-slash rejection and the `/metrics`//`/`/nested accept cases. Gate green: `make test`, `make lint` (0 issues), `make docs-check`.

body:
## Problem

`Client.fetchSystemTime` in the `opnsense/` API client parses OPNsense's `boottime`, `datetime`, and `config` timestamps with Go's `time.Parse` using a format string that only carries a timezone *abbreviation* (`MST`), not a numeric offset. The code comments assert that because all three timestamps share "the same zone," taking a difference between any two of them cancels the offset and produces a correct duration. That assumption is false across a DST transition: OPNsense's PHP controller renders each timestamp with the abbreviation *in effect at that timestamp*, so a box's `boottime` from a period before a DST change and its `datetime`/`config` from after the change carry two different abbreviations (e.g. "GMT" vs "BST" in Europe/London).

Go's `time.Parse` cannot resolve an abbreviation to a real UTC offset unless the exporter process's local timezone database happens to recognize that specific abbreviation as active for that moment (i.e. only when the exporter runs in the exact same zone as the firewall). In the common case — the exporter running in a container with the default `UTC` timezone — both abbreviations are parsed into fabricated zero-offset zones, and the wraparound cancellation the comment relies on does not happen. The resulting `dateTime.Sub(bootTime)` is skewed by the DST delta (typically 3600 seconds), and the same skew propagates into `config_last_change` whenever the last configuration change predates the DST transition.

## Evidence

`opnsense/system_resources.go:213-241` (the comment and the affected computation):

```go
// OPNsense reports these timestamps with only a timezone abbreviation
// (e.g. "BST"), which time.Parse cannot map to a UTC offset — it falls back
// to a fabricated zone with a zero offset, so the parsed instants are skewed
// by the box's real offset. boottime, datetime and config all share the same
// zone, so a DIFFERENCE between any two cancels that offset and is correct.
...
bootTime, errBoot := time.Parse(opnsenseTimeFormat, resp.Boottime)
dateTime, errDate := time.Parse(opnsenseTimeFormat, resp.Datetime)
configTime, errConfig := time.Parse(opnsenseTimeFormat, resp.Config)
```

The format string is defined at `opnsense/system_resources.go:163`:

```go
const opnsenseTimeFormat = "Mon Jan 2 15:04:05 MST 2006"
```

On the live OPNsense source, `Diagnostics/Api/SystemController.php` renders `boottime` via `date("D M j G:i:s T Y", $matches[1])`, where `$matches[1]` is the boot epoch — `date('T', ts)` produces the abbreviation in effect *at that timestamp*, not the abbreviation in effect "now." `datetime` and `config` are rendered similarly but at their own respective timestamps. Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box.

The verifier independently reproduced the skew: parsing "GMT" and "BST" under `TZ=UTC` (the common container default) both fabricate zero-offset zones, and `dateTime.Sub(bootTime)` for a January boot vs. a July scrape overstates uptime by exactly 3600 seconds. Only when the exporter process's local zone is set to `Europe/London` (matching the box) does "BST" resolve to +3600 and the cancellation the comment describes actually hold.

## Failure scenario / impact

A firewall in a DST-observing zone (e.g. Europe/London) boots in January and is scraped by the exporter in July, while the exporter process runs with the common container default `TZ=UTC` (not the firewall's zone). `opnsense_system_uptime_seconds` is overstated by 3600 seconds, and if the last configuration change occurred before the spring DST transition, `config_last_change` is off by the same 1-hour skew. Firewalls routinely run for months at a time, so effectively any long-lived box in a DST zone scraped by a UTC-default exporter is affected for roughly half the year.

## Suggested direction

Avoid the wall-clock-rendered abbreviation entirely: load the box's real zone via `time.LoadLocation` if it can be determined, or better, obtain uptime from a source that isn't subject to abbreviation rendering (e.g. a raw epoch value if the API exposes one). If neither is feasible, document the ±1h DST caveat explicitly rather than asserting the offsets always cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test parses a `boottime`/`datetime` pair straddling a DST transition (e.g. "Wed Jan 1 00:00:00 GMT 2026" boot vs. "Wed Jul 1 00:00:00 BST 2026" datetime) under `TZ=UTC` and asserts the computed `Uptime` is NOT skewed by 3600 seconds (either via a fix, or via an explicit correction path).
- [ ] A unit test covers the equivalent DST-straddling case for `ConfigLastChange` and asserts no 3600-second skew.
- [ ] A regression test exists confirming behavior is unaffected when boot/datetime/config all fall within the same DST period (no false positive from the fix).
- [ ] The misleading comment at `opnsense/system_resources.go:213-217` (or its replacement) accurately describes the DST caveat instead of asserting unconditional cancellation.
- [ ] `make test` passes with the new coverage under both `TZ=UTC` and a DST-observing `TZ` (e.g. `TZ=Europe/London`).

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in f49edc2. Added `dstAbbrevOffset` (a table of common DST-observing zone abbreviations → UTC offset) plus two helpers:

- `dstCorrectedDiffSeconds(later, earlier)` — recovers each timestamp's real offset from its abbreviation and cancels the DST delta, computed *relative to whatever offset time.Parse actually assigned*, so it's correct under both TZ=UTC (abbreviations unresolved → 0) and a matching-zone exporter (already resolved). When the two abbreviations match (same DST period) or are unknown it degrades to the raw difference.
- `absUnixFromAbbrev` — the true absolute instant of a timestamp from its abbreviation.

`uptime_seconds` is now `dstCorrectedDiffSeconds(datetime, boottime)`. `config_last_change` is now the true absolute instant recovered from config's abbreviation (deterministic, no dependence on the exporter clock), falling back to the DST-corrected now-anchored age when the abbreviation is unknown. The misleading 'offsets always cancel' comment is replaced with an accurate description including the residual ±1h caveat for unlisted/ambiguous zones.

Coverage: `TestDSTCorrectedDiffSeconds` (GMT→BST cross-DST asserts no 3600 skew; BST→BST same-period regression) run under both `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=Europe/London`, and `TestFetchSystemResources_DSTStraddle` (end-to-end uptime + config_last_change free of the 3600s skew). The existing `AllEndpoints` config assertion was updated to the now-deterministic absolute instant. `make test` green under both TZ; `make lint`/`make docs-check` green; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

Several cumulative (monotonically increasing) counters in the collector layer are emitted with `prometheus.GaugeValue` instead of `prometheus.CounterValue`, and this is inconsistent even within the same collector for identical quantities:

- `internal/collector/firewall.go` — the per-interface pf statistics loop (register block at lines 97-135, emit loop at lines 205-213) emits all 16 pf counters as `GaugeValue`. This includes metrics whose names are literally suffixed `_total` (e.g. `in_ipv4_pass_bytes_total`, `out_ipv6_block_bytes_total`), which is a `_total`-suffixed gauge — a direct Prometheus/OpenMetrics naming-convention violation. The packet-count variants of the same pf counters have no `_total` suffix at all and are also gauges, while `interfaceHitsTotal` in the same file (line 240) correctly uses `CounterValue`.
- `internal/collector/ipsec.go` — `phase1_bytes_in/out` and `phase1_packets_in/out` (lines 161-200) are emitted as `GaugeValue`, while the identical semantic quantities at phase2/child-SA level (lines 230-265) are emitted as `CounterValue`. Phase1 values are literally the aggregated sums of the phase2 child-SA counters (mirroring how OPNsense's `SessionsController.php` aggregates them), so the same underlying cumulative data has two different Prometheus types depending only on which loop emits it.
- `internal/collector/protocol.go` — `icmp_dropped_by_reason_total` (lines 436-440) and `udp_dropped_by_reason_total` (lines 450-454) are emitted as `GaugeValue`, while the sibling drop-reason metrics in the same `Update()` function — `carp_dropped_by_reason_total` (469-473), `pfsync_dropped_by_reason_total` (488-492), and `ip_dropped_by_reason_total` (507-511) — are all `CounterValue`. All five are standard BSD netstat-style cumulative kernel counters that only reset on reboot; git history shows icmp/udp were added first (commit 271fca8) and the correctly-typed siblings were added later (commit 642fa1c) without reconciling the original two.

The sample values reported are correct in all cases — this is purely a `# TYPE` exposition-format defect. It matters because Prometheus/OpenMetrics consumers (promtool, Grafana's function suggestions, Prometheus-to-OTel Sum-vs-Gauge conversion, remote-write counter-reset handling) key their behavior off the declared TYPE, not off inspecting whether values happen to be monotonic.

A second, independently-discoverable symptom of the same root cause: `scripts/docgen/main.go:690-693` infers the documented metric TYPE purely from whether the metric name ends in `_total`, not from the actual `GaugeValue`/`CounterValue` used at emit time. As a result `docs/metrics/metrics.md` already documents `opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_bytes_total` as "Counter" even though the runtime code currently emits it as a gauge — generated docs and the live `/metrics` output disagree.

## Evidence

- `internal/collector/firewall.go:97-135` — pf byte counters registered with `_total`-suffixed names.
- `internal/collector/firewall.go:205-213` — single loop emits all pf byte/packet counters as `prometheus.GaugeValue`.
- `internal/collector/firewall.go:240` — `interfaceHitsTotal` in the same collector correctly uses `prometheus.CounterValue`, showing the inconsistency is local, not systemic.
- `internal/collector/ipsec.go:161-200` — phase1 bytes/packets in/out emitted as `prometheus.GaugeValue`.
- `internal/collector/ipsec.go:230-265` — phase2 (child-SA) bytes/packets in/out, the same semantic quantity, emitted as `prometheus.CounterValue`.
- `internal/collector/protocol.go:436-440` — `c.icmpDroppedByReason` emitted with `prometheus.GaugeValue`.
- `internal/collector/protocol.go:450-454` — `c.udpDroppedByReason` emitted with `prometheus.GaugeValue`.
- `internal/collector/protocol.go:469-473, 488-492, 507-511` — sibling `carpDroppedByReason`/`pfsyncDroppedByReason`/`ipDroppedByReason` correctly emitted with `prometheus.CounterValue`.
- `scripts/docgen/main.go:690-693` — docgen infers TYPE from the `_total` name suffix rather than the actual emit-time `ValueType`, so `docs/metrics/metrics.md` documents `opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_bytes_total` as "Counter" while it is currently emitted as a gauge.

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: `udp.dropped-full-socket-buffer = 443995` and the icmp/udp/ip drop-reason fields are standard cumulative BSD netstat counters, matching the semantic class of the already-correctly-typed `ip`/`carp`/`pfsync` siblings.

No existing test asserts value type (`GaugeValue` vs `CounterValue`) in `firewall_test.go`, `ipsec_test.go`, or `protocol_test.go`, so nothing currently guards against this class of regression.

## Failure scenario / impact

OpenMetrics-strict scrapers and linters (`promtool check metrics`) flag `*_bytes_total`/`*_dropped_by_reason_total` metrics declared as TYPE gauge as a naming violation. Grafana and other type-aware tooling suggest the wrong aggregation functions (gauge-style `avg`/last-value instead of `rate()`/`increase()`). Backends that convert Prometheus exposition to OTel (Sum vs Gauge) or that apply automatic counter-reset correction by TYPE will treat these metrics incorrectly, even though the underlying values are genuinely monotonic counters. Within a single collector (ipsec, firewall) the same real-world quantity is typed differently depending on whether it's phase1 vs phase2, or byte vs packet variant, making the metric family unpredictable for anyone trying to build dashboards or alerts generically over "all counters in this collector."

## Suggested direction

Switch the affected emission call sites (firewall pf byte/packet counters, ipsec phase1 bytes/packets, and protocol.go's icmp/udp dropped-by-reason) from `prometheus.GaugeValue` to `prometheus.CounterValue`. This is a metadata-only, non-breaking change — metric names and sample values are unchanged. Renaming metrics to add missing `_total` suffixes where absent is a separate, breaking change and can be deferred or handled via aliasing. Fixing the emit-side type alone should also make `docs/metrics/metrics.md` agree with runtime behavior, since docgen already infers "Counter" from the `_total` suffix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `internal/collector/firewall.go`'s pf per-interface byte and packet counters are emitted with `prometheus.CounterValue` instead of `prometheus.GaugeValue`.
- [ ] `internal/collector/ipsec.go`'s phase1 bytes_in/out and packets_in/out are emitted with `prometheus.CounterValue`, matching the phase2 child-SA counters.
- [ ] `internal/collector/protocol.go`'s `icmp_dropped_by_reason_total` and `udp_dropped_by_reason_total` are emitted with `prometheus.CounterValue`, matching the carp/pfsync/ip siblings.
- [ ] A unit test (or table-driven extension of an existing test) in each of `firewall_test.go`, `ipsec_test.go`, and `protocol_test.go` asserts the Prometheus metric type (`dto.MetricType_COUNTER`) for these specific metrics, so a future regression to `GaugeValue` fails CI.
- [ ] `make docs` is run afterward and `docs/metrics/metrics.md` is confirmed to already show these metrics as "Counter" (no docgen logic change expected, since it infers type from the `_total` suffix).
- [ ] No metric names, label sets, or sample values change as part of this fix — `go test ./...` and `make lint` remain green.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in 5621823. Switched the affected emit sites from `GaugeValue` to `CounterValue`:

- **firewall** — all 16 pf per-interface pass/block byte + packet totals.
- **ipsec** — phase1 bytes_in/out and packets_in/out (now matching the phase2 child-SA counters they aggregate).
- **protocol** — `icmp_dropped_by_reason_total` and `udp_dropped_by_reason_total` (now matching the carp/pfsync/ip drop-reason siblings).

Metadata-only: no metric names, labels, or sample values change. `make docs` produced no diff — docgen infers TYPE from the `_total` name suffix, so the `_total` byte/drop-reason metrics already documented as Counter now agree with runtime (556 metrics unchanged). The packet variants lack a `_total` suffix; per the issue that rename is a separate/deferred breaking change, so their docs entry is left as-is for now.

Guarded by a new `assertMetricsAreCounters` helper asserting `dto.Counter != nil`, wired into the firewall/ipsec/protocol Update tests so a regression to GaugeValue fails CI. `go test ./...`/`make lint`/`make docs-check` green.
