body:
## Problem

The pf per-interface firewall stats collector copies the raw keys from OPNsense's `api/diagnostics/firewall/pf_statistics/interfaces` response verbatim into the Prometheus `interface` label, with no filtering or normalisation. `pfctl -vs Interfaces` output (what this endpoint wraps) does not return a clean list of physical/virtual devices — it mixes in an `all` aggregate row, OS-builtin and custom pf interface-group rows (`enc`, `lo`, `pflog`, `pfsync`, `tun`, `vlan`, and any user-defined group like `zenvpngroup`), and appends a literal `" (skip)"` suffix to device names that have "skip on this interface" enabled in pf. All of these pass straight through as the sole `interface` label value on all 16 in/out pass/block packet/byte metrics.

This means the label conflates three different kinds of entity (an aggregate total, a group, and a real device) under one label with no way to distinguish them, and the label value for a device is not stable — toggling the pf "skip" option on an interface changes the label text, breaking series continuity, dashboards, recording rules, and joins against `opnsense_interfaces_*` labels that use the plain device name.

## Evidence

`internal/collector/firewall.go:186-214` — `Update()` emits all pass/block packet/byte metrics using `stat.InterfaceName` as the `interface` label with no filtering of `all`, group names, or the `(skip)` suffix.

`opnsense/firewall.go:57-60` — `FetchPFStatsByInterface` iterates the JSON response's `interfaces` map and copies the map key straight into `FirewallPFStat.InterfaceName`:

```go
for name, stat := range raw.Interfaces {
    stat.InterfaceName = name
    ...
}
```

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box. The live `api/diagnostics/firewall/pf_statistics/interfaces` response keys included: `all`, `enc`, `enc0`, `igb0`, `igb1`, `ixl0`, VLAN sub-interfaces, `lo`, `lo0 (skip)`, `pflog`, `pflog0`, `pfsync`, `pfsync0 (skip)`, `pppoe0`, `tailscale0`, `tun`, `tun0`, `tun1`, `vlan`, `zen0`, `zenvpngroup`. `opnsense/firewall_test.go` only asserts `InterfaceName` is populated for a normal device name ("igb0"); there is no test or code path that strips `(skip)`, excludes `all`, or distinguishes group pseudo-entries from real devices.

## Failure scenario / impact

An admin toggles "skip interface" on `lo0` in the pf configuration. The next scrape renames the time series from `interface="lo0"` to `interface="lo0 (skip)"` (and back again if later un-toggled), silently breaking any recording rule, alert, or dashboard join keyed on that label value, and creating a discontinuous series in Prometheus.

Separately, because `all` and pf interface-group rows (e.g. `vlan`, `zenvpngroup`) appear in the same label space as real member devices, a `sum by ()` or similar aggregation over `opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_packets` risks double- or triple-counting traffic whenever a firewall rule explicitly matches on that group or on `all` (on the live box sampled, group/`all` rows currently read 0 because no rule matches on them yet, but this is configuration-dependent and not guaranteed to stay that way).

## Suggested direction

Strip the `" (skip)"` suffix from interface names before setting the label (optionally exposing "skip" as a separate boolean metric or label so the information isn't lost), and either drop the `all`/group pseudo-entries or mark them with a distinguishing label (e.g. `kind="group"` / `kind="aggregate"` vs `kind="device"`) so aggregations don't silently mix entity types.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test on `FetchPFStatsByInterface` (or equivalent) with an interface name of `"lo0 (skip)"` in the raw JSON asserts the parsed/emitted interface identifier no longer contains the `" (skip)"` suffix.
- [ ] A unit test asserts that the `all` aggregate entry is either excluded from collected metrics or exposed with a distinguishing label/kind that differs from real device entries.
- [ ] A unit test asserts that known pf interface-group names (`enc`, `lo`, `pflog`, `pfsync`, `tun`, `vlan`, and arbitrary custom groups) are either excluded or distinguishable from member-device rows via a label, so a naive `sum by ()` over the metric cannot double-count.
- [ ] Toggling pf's "skip on interface" for a device in the underlying data (simulated via test fixture) does not change the interface label value between two scrapes.
- [ ] `make docs` / `make docs-check` pass with any label/metric changes documented (metrics reference regenerated if the label set changes).

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in 9009e04. `FetchPFStatsByInterface` now normalises the pfctl interfaces map before populating the label:

- **Strips the `" (skip)"` suffix** so toggling pf "skip on interface" no longer renames the series (`lo0 (skip)` → `lo0`).
- **Keeps only real network devices** and drops the `all` aggregate and pf interface-group rows (`enc`, `vlan`, `zenvpngroup`, …). Classification uses the fact that FreeBSD interfaces are always `<driver><unit>` and end in a digit, whereas `all` and pf groups (builtin or custom) are bare names with no unit number — so member devices and group/aggregate rows can't share the label space and a naive `sum by()` can't double-count.

Chose exclusion over a `kind` label to keep the label set (and therefore the dashboard/metrics reference) unchanged — no label/metric-shape change, so `make docs-check` stays green.

Coverage: `TestFetchPFStatsByInterface_FiltersPseudoEntries` (mixed fixture with all/enc/vlan/zenvpngroup/igb0/`lo0 (skip)`/`pfsync0 (skip)`/tailscale0 → only the 4 real devices survive, skip-suffix stripped) and `TestFetchPFStatsByInterface_SkipToggleStableLabel` (`lo0` vs `lo0 (skip)` yield the same label). `make test`/`make lint`/`make docs-check` green; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

In the CrowdSec fetcher (`opnsense/crowdsec.go`), the bouncers and machines row payloads are decoded in two passes: an outer envelope decode sets `HasBouncers`/`HasMachines` to `true` once the search endpoint responds successfully, and a second `json.Unmarshal` decodes the actual row list. That second unmarshal is only checked on the success path:

```go
if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal(bouncerRows, &rows); jsonErr == nil {
    // rows appended to data.Bouncers
}
```

There is no `else` branch. If this unmarshal fails — e.g. a CrowdSec plugin update changes the bouncers/machines row shape from an array to an object keyed by ID, or changes a field type outside the `flexString`/`flexBool` tolerance already built into this file — the error is discarded, `rows` stays nil, and `data.Bouncers`/`data.Machines` stays empty. Crucially, `HasBouncers`/`HasMachines` were already set `true` earlier from the envelope, so the collector (`internal/collector/crowdsec.go`) still emits the metric rather than omitting it, and emits it as `float64(len(data.Bouncers))` — i.e. a **false zero**. This is indistinguishable from "no bouncers registered," with no log line, no error, and `scrape_success` still reporting healthy. The exact same silent-swallow-on-`Unmarshal`-failure idiom also exists at `opnsense/frr.go:253`, though that site is not in scope for this issue.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/crowdsec.go:189` and `:217` — `HasBouncers`/`HasMachines` set `true` from the envelope/search success, independent of row decode success.
- `opnsense/crowdsec.go:192` — `if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal(bouncerRows, &rows); jsonErr == nil { ... }` (bouncers), no `else`, no log.
- `opnsense/crowdsec.go:220` — same pattern for machines.
- `internal/collector/crowdsec.go:112-114` — gates purely on `data.HasBouncers` and emits `bouncersTotal = float64(len(data.Bouncers))` unconditionally, so a decode failure emits `0` rather than omitting the series.
- `opnsense/crowdsec.go:15-17` — the file's own header already flags "VERIFICATION: unvalidated against a live os-crowdsec box."
- `opnsense/crowdsec_test.go` — no fixture exercises malformed/undecodable rows; all existing fixtures decode cleanly.

Not livebox-confirmed: the os-crowdsec plugin was not installed on the available test box (`crowdsecBouncers.json`/`crowdsecMachines.json` both returned `{"errorMessage":"Endpoint not found"}`), so the real-world row shape drift trigger could not be directly observed — the code-path mechanism itself was confirmed by direct inspection at HEAD.

## Failure scenario / impact

A CrowdSec/os-crowdsec plugin update changes the bouncers or machines row serialization (e.g. object-keyed-by-id instead of an array, or an incompatible field type). Every subsequent scrape silently reports `crowdsec_bouncers_total`/`crowdsec_machines_total` as `0` instead of erroring or omitting the metric. A "bouncers_total < 1" alert fires, or a dashboard shows the security agent fleet as empty, while exporter logs stay clean and `scrape_success` reports `1` — there is zero diagnostic signal anywhere pointing at the real cause.

## Suggested direction

On unmarshal error for either rows payload, set `HasBouncers`/`HasMachines = false` (so the metric goes absent, consistent with how the message-envelope failure path already behaves) and log a warning including the decode error, mirroring the existing debug log style used elsewhere in this file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test in `opnsense/crowdsec_test.go` feeds an undecodable bouncers rows payload (e.g. an object instead of an array) and asserts `HasBouncers` is `false` and `Bouncers` is empty, rather than `HasBouncers=true` with an empty slice.
- [ ] The same test coverage exists for the machines rows payload and `HasMachines`.
- [ ] On unmarshal failure, a warning-level log line is emitted containing the decode error (verifiable via a test that captures logger output or an injectable logger).
- [ ] `internal/collector/crowdsec.go` continues to omit `crowdsec_bouncers_total`/`crowdsec_machines_total` (not emit `0`) whenever `HasBouncers`/`HasMachines` is `false`, verified by a collector-level test.

title: Fix silent CrowdSec bouncer/machine row decode failures emitting false zero totals

body:
## Problem

Several counter fields populated from OPNsense API JSON responses are declared as plain Go `int` instead of `int64`, in violation of a convention this codebase already established and documented for exactly this reason. `opnsense/utils.go` explicitly widened its string-to-int parsers (`parseStringToInt`, `safeAtoi`, `parseLineRateBits`) to `int64` "so that large counters ... parse correctly on 32-bit architectures too" (a fix that shipped as commit `7f58a29`, referencing upstream issue #81, recorded in `CHANGELOG.md:114`). That migration covered string-parsed fields but missed the JSON-tagged struct fields in `opnsense/firewall.go`, `opnsense/firewall_rules.go`, `opnsense/ipsec.go`, and the `numToInt` helper in `opnsense/protocol_statistics.go`.

On a 32-bit build (`GOARCH=386` or `arm`), Go's `int` is 32-bit wide (max ~2.1 billion). Real production byte/packet counters on a moderately busy firewall routinely exceed that: live-box samples show `in4_pass_bytes` = 64,618,355,886 on a single interface, firewall rule byte totals up to 43,215,459,045, and TCP sent-data-bytes of 8,442,646,036 — all 4-30x over the int32 ceiling. When `encoding/json` tries to unmarshal one of these values directly into a plain `int` struct field on a 32-bit build, it returns an `UnmarshalTypeError`, which `opnsense/client.go`'s `readResponse` wraps into an `*APICallError` and returns — failing the entire `Fetch*` call for that subsystem. The `numToInt` helper in `protocol_statistics.go` takes a different, worse path: it parses via `json.Number.Int64()` successfully, then does a bare `int(i)` narrowing conversion with no range check, silently wrapping large values into negative garbage instead of erroring.

Release binaries built via `.goreleaser.yml` are amd64/arm64 only, so shipped binaries are unaffected — this only bites users who build the exporter from source for a 32-bit target (e.g. an armv7 SBC), which the codebase's own prior 32-bit-safety work implies is a supported use case.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/firewall.go:7-25` — byte/packet fields declared as plain `int`, e.g. `In4PassBytes int \`json:"in4_pass_bytes"\``
- `opnsense/firewall_rules.go:13-18` — `Bytes int`, `Packets int`
- `opnsense/ipsec.go:18-21` — `ipsecSearchResponse` phase1 fields: `BytesIn int \`json:"bytes-in"\`` etc. (JSON-numeric, unmarshaled directly — the hard-fail path). Note: the sibling `ipsecPhase2` struct (lines 34-37) parses its byte/packet fields as JSON strings via `strconv.Atoi` and silently zeroes on overflow rather than erroring — a related but distinct silent-data-loss variant, not the same hard-fail mechanism.
- `opnsense/protocol_statistics.go:9-15`:
  ```go
  func numToInt(n json.Number) int {
      i, err := n.Int64()
      ...
      return int(i)
  }
  ```
- `opnsense/utils.go:11-13` (and ~103-105) — the documented convention this violates: comments explicitly state int64 was chosen "so that large counters ... parse correctly on 32-bit architectures too."
- `.goreleaser.yml:14-16` — `goarch: [amd64, arm64]`, confirming official release binaries are 64-bit only.
- Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: `api/diagnostics/firewall/pf_statistics/interfaces` returns `in4_pass_bytes=64618355886` for `ixl0`; firewall rule stats show byte totals up to 43,215,459,045; protocol statistics show TCP `sent-data-bytes=8442646036`. A standalone repro (`json.Unmarshal` of `3000000000` into an `int32` field) reproduces the exact `UnmarshalTypeError`, and `int32(8442646036) == -147288556` reproduces the silent-wrap behavior of `numToInt`.
- The same `int`-not-`int64` pattern also exists in `opnsense/mbuf.go:24-25` (`BytesInUse`, `BytesTotal`), worth sweeping in the same pass.

## Failure scenario / impact

A user builds the exporter from source for a 32-bit ARM or x86 host (`GOARCH=arm` / `386`). Within hours of normal firewall traffic (any interface passing more than ~2 GiB), the firewall pf-interface-statistics collector, firewall-rules collector, and ipsec phase1 collector begin hard-failing every scrape with an `APICallError` — those metrics disappear entirely. Separately, the protocol-statistics collector doesn't error at all: `numToInt` silently wraps large TCP/UDP byte counters into negative values once traffic exceeds ~2^31 bytes, so `tcp_sent_data_bytes_total`-style metrics go negative/garbage with no error surfaced anywhere, making it a silent-corruption bug rather than a visible outage.

## Suggested direction

Change the byte/packet counter struct fields in `firewall.go`, `firewall_rules.go`, and `ipsec.go` (and optionally `mbuf.go`) from `int` to `int64`, and make `numToInt` return `int64` instead of narrowing with `int(i)`. This should be a mechanical, low-risk change since these fields are already converted to `float64` before being emitted as Prometheus gauges in the corresponding collectors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `opnsense/firewall.go`, `opnsense/firewall_rules.go`, and `opnsense/ipsec.go` (phase1 `ipsecSearchResponse` struct at minimum) declare all byte/packet counter fields as `int64`, not `int`.
- [ ] `numToInt` in `opnsense/protocol_statistics.go` returns `int64` (or is removed in favor of directly widening `ProtocolStatistics` fields to `int64`), with no narrowing `int(i)` conversion remaining.
- [ ] A unit test unmarshals a JSON payload containing a byte-counter value greater than `math.MaxInt32` (e.g. 8,442,646,036) into the affected structs and asserts no error and the correct value is preserved — the test must be architecture-independent (fail today conceptually on a simulated 32-bit `int`, pass after the fix regardless of build `GOARCH`).
- [ ] `go build ./...` with `GOARCH=386` (or `arm`) still compiles successfully after the change (sanity check that the fix doesn't introduce a new 32-bit incompatibility).
- [ ] `go vet ./...` and `make lint` pass with no new findings after widening the fields.
- [ ] Existing collector tests for firewall, firewall-rules, ipsec, and protocol-statistics still pass unmodified (confirming the `float64(...)` conversions at the Prometheus-metric boundary are unaffected by the wider Go type).

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in 4ef3662. Widened the byte/packet counter struct fields to `int64` across `firewall.go`, `firewall_rules.go`, `ipsec.go` (both the phase1 `ipsecSearchResponse` rows and the public `IPsec`/`ipsecPhase2` structs), `mbuf.go`, and the whole `ProtocolStatistics` struct (including its `map[string]int` → `map[string]int64`). `numToInt` now returns `int64` with no narrowing `int(i)`. As a bonus the ipsec **phase2** byte/packet parse switched from `strconv.Atoi` (int, silent-zero-on-overflow) to the tolerant `safeAtoi` (int64), fixing the related silent-data-loss variant the issue flagged.

Values are still converted to `float64` at the Prometheus boundary, so metric output is byte-for-byte unchanged on 64-bit; collector tests pass unmodified.

Coverage: new `opnsense/int64_widening_test.go` unmarshals `8442646036` (>MaxInt32) into each affected struct and `numToInt`, asserting no error and value preserved — architecture-independent. Verified `GOOS=linux GOARCH=386` and `GOARCH=arm` builds compile; `go vet`/`make lint`/`make test` green; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

`FetchInterfaces` (`opnsense/interfaces.go`) parses 14 counter/state fields per interface with `sliceIntToMapStringInt`, a strict helper (`opnsense/utils.go:57-69`) that returns a hard `*APICallError` on the *first* `strconv.ParseInt` failure it hits. `FetchInterfaces` propagates that error immediately (`return data, err`, `interfaces.go:106-108`), discarding every interface parsed so far — including any not yet processed, since Go map iteration order over `resp.Interface` is undefined.

The collector caller (`internal/collector/interfaces.go:156-159`) treats a non-nil `FetchInterfaces` error as fatal for the whole call and returns before even fetching the interfaces overview. `internal/collector/collector.go:838-847` then logs the error, increments `endpointErrors`, and sets `scrapeSuccess=0` for the entire `interfaces` collector — emitting zero metrics for every interface that scrape, not just the one with the bad field.

This is inconsistent with the rest of the package: newer fetchers (`carp.go`, `unbound_dns.go`, `ntp.go`, haproxy, kea) all use the tolerant `safeAtoi`/`safeParseFloat` helpers (`utils.go:106-112`), which default to `0` on a parse failure instead of aborting. `FetchInterfaces` is the outlier still using the strict, all-or-nothing path.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/interfaces.go:94-108` — per-interface loop feeding 14 raw string fields through `sliceIntToMapStringInt`; on error, `return data, err` discards the whole batch.
- `opnsense/utils.go:57-69` — `sliceIntToMapStringInt` returns immediately on the first `strconv.ParseInt` failure (an absent/renamed JSON key decodes to `""`, which `ParseInt` rejects).
- `internal/collector/interfaces.go:156-159` — `Update` returns the error immediately, before calling `FetchInterfacesOverview`.
- `internal/collector/collector.go:838-847` — on a non-nil `Update` error, only logs + increments `endpointErrors` + sets `scrapeSuccess=0`; no partial data is retained.
- `opnsense/interfaces.go:110-113` — the code's own comment documents that this exact endpoint already had a field-shape change across OPNsense versions (link state went from the string `"link state is up"` to a numeric string `"2"`), corroborated by prior fix commit `baf14f0` ("fix(opnsense): correct seven API-shape mismatches found in OPNsense 26.1 audit"). This is direct precedent that field encoding on this endpoint is not stable across releases.
- `opnsense/utils.go:106-112` — `safeAtoi`, the tolerant helper already used by `carp.go`, `unbound_dns.go`, and `ntp.go`, showing the established, safer convention in the same package.
- `opnsense/interfaces_test.go` has no test for a single malformed/missing field among otherwise-good interfaces — the gap is unguarded.
- Not currently reproducible live: all 14 fields parse cleanly for all interfaces (physical, VLAN, PPPoE, tailscale/PPP, loopback, pfsync, pflog, enc0) on a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box. Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box. This is a latent defect, not an active outage.

## Failure scenario / impact

A future OPNsense/FreeBSD release adds an interface type (e.g. a new tunnel driver) whose netstat-derived record omits one of the 14 fields (e.g. "send queue max length"), which decodes as `""`. `sliceIntToMapStringInt` fails `ParseInt` on that one field, `FetchInterfaces` returns an error, and the collector emits **zero** `opnsense_interfaces_*` metrics for **every** interface that scrape — not just the offending one — even though 13 of 14 fields on every other interface parsed fine. Since interface traffic metrics are among the exporter's most-used dashboard rows, this looks indistinguishable from an exporter outage. The same endpoint has already had one real field-shape drift incident (link state format change), so this class of failure is a realistic, not hypothetical, risk for this endpoint specifically.

## Suggested direction

Parse each of the 14 fields with the existing tolerant `safeAtoi` helper (matching `carp.go`/`unbound_dns.go`/`ntp.go`) so a single malformed or missing field degrades to `0` for that one metric rather than failing the whole subsystem fetch; consider a one-time warn-log per unexpected value to preserve visibility without an outage. Reserve hard errors in `FetchInterfaces` for genuine transport/decode failures, not per-field parse issues.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test in `opnsense/interfaces_test.go` feeds a fixture where one interface has one field serialized as `""` (or a non-numeric string) among several otherwise-valid interfaces, and asserts `FetchInterfaces` returns `nil` error with data present for all interfaces (the malformed field defaulting to `0`, not aborting the whole call).
- [ ] A unit test asserts that a genuine transport/decode failure (e.g. non-2xx response or malformed JSON) from the interfaces endpoint still returns a non-nil error, i.e. the fix narrows error scope to per-field parsing only, not all failure modes.
- [ ] `opnsense/interfaces.go` no longer calls the strict `sliceIntToMapStringInt` for these 14 fields; it uses `safeAtoi` (or equivalent tolerant parsing) matching the convention in `carp.go`/`unbound_dns.go`/`ntp.go`.
- [ ] `go test ./opnsense/...` and `go test ./internal/collector/...` pass with the new tests included.
- [ ] `make lint` passes with no new revive/misspell findings introduced by the change.

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

Fixed in b0f9ee0. `FetchInterfaces` no longer routes its 14 counter/state fields through the strict, all-or-nothing `sliceIntToMapStringInt`; each is now parsed with the tolerant `safeAtoi` helper (the convention already used by carp.go/unbound_dns.go/ntp.go). A single missing or non-numeric field on one interface now degrades just that metric to 0 instead of aborting the whole fetch and blanking every interface's metrics for the scrape. Error scope is narrowed to per-field parsing only — genuine transport/decode failures (non-2xx, malformed JSON) still return a non-nil error.

Coverage: `TestFetchInterfaces_TolerantFieldParsing` (one interface with an empty `send queue max length` among valid ones → nil error, both interfaces present, bad field=0, siblings intact) and `TestFetchInterfaces_MalformedJSON` (decode failure still errors). `go test ./opnsense/... ./internal/collector/...` green; `make lint` clean; 556 metrics unchanged.

title: Fix all-or-nothing strict parsing in FetchInterfaces so one bad field doesn't drop every interface metric

body:
## Problem

When `--otlp.enabled` is used, a single metric-consistency error anywhere in the collector registry (e.g. duplicate label values from duplicated cron jobs, DynDNS accounts, services, or WireGuard/NTP peers) blacks out the *entire* OTLP export for that tick — not just the offending collector's metrics, but also the exporter's own healthy self-metrics (`process_*`, `go_*`, health/up).

`main.go` combines the self-metrics registry and the collector registry into a single `prometheus.Gatherers{...}` value and hands that one combined value to the OTel Prometheus bridge as a single gatherer. `prometheus.Gatherers.Gather()` (and the underlying `Registry.Gather()`) is designed to return the partial, successfully-gathered metric families *together with* a `MultiError` when something is inconsistent — this is exactly how `promhttp.HandlerFor` with `ContinueOnError` can still render partial `/metrics` output. But the vendored OTel bridge producer treats any non-nil error from a gatherer as total failure and discards whatever partial families were returned alongside it. Because both registries were merged into one `Gatherers` value before being passed to the bridge, they are treated as a single unit of failure: one bad family anywhere poisons the whole combined gather, and nothing at all is exported that tick.

The bug is silent and does not recover on its own — the PeriodicReader keeps ticking every export interval, hitting the same duplicate every time, so the outage persists for as long as the offending config exists on the OPNsense box, with only a rate-limited warn-level log line as a hint.

## Evidence

- `main.go:396` — `telemetry.Start` is called with `prometheus.Gatherers{selfMetricsRegistry, collectorRegistry}` as a single combined gatherer value.
- `internal/telemetry/provider.go:40` — that combined value is passed into `prometheusbridge.WithGatherer(gatherer)`.
- `vendor/go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/bridges/prometheus/config.go:42-46` — `WithGatherer` appends the value to `cfg.gatherers`, so the producer ends up with exactly one gatherer entry (the merged `Gatherers` wrapper), not two independent ones.
- `vendor/go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/bridges/prometheus/producer.go:51-57`:
  ```go
  promMetrics, err := gatherer.Gather()
  if err != nil {
      errs = append(errs, err)
      continue
  }
  ```
  On any error, the partial `promMetrics` families returned alongside it are discarded entirely rather than exported.
- `vendor/github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/registry.go:746-803` — `Gatherers.Gather()` returns `NormalizeMetricFamilies(...)` (all successfully gathered families, e.g. self-metrics plus every non-duplicated collector family) together with `errs.MaybeUnwrap()` — the partial data is available, it is just thrown away by the bridge.

This was independently verified with a throwaway test mirroring `main.go`'s exact wiring: `Gatherers{healthyRegistry, erroringCollectorRegistry}.Gather()` returned 2 metric families plus a non-nil error, but feeding that single combined value into the bridge via one `WithGatherer` call caused `producer.Produce` to return 0 ScopeMetrics — a total export blackout, including the healthy self-metric. Splitting the two registries into two separate `WithGatherer` calls instead exported the healthy self-metric while only the erroring registry's output was dropped, confirming both the defect and the isolation fix direction. Not livebox-validated (this reproduces purely via the vendored bridge code path, independent of any specific OPNsense box state).

## Failure scenario / impact

An OPNsense box has two cron jobs (or DynDNS accounts, services, or WireGuard/NTP peers) with identical description/command, producing a duplicate label-value combination in one collector's metric family (the round-1 P1 duplicate-label scenario). With `--otlp.enabled` pointed at an OTLP backend (e.g. Grafana Cloud), every export tick gathers both registries as one unit, hits the duplicate-label consistency error, and the bridge silently drops every family — collector metrics AND the exporter's own `process_*`/`go_*` self-metrics/health signal. All series for this exporter go stale simultaneously in the backend, the process itself looks alive, and there is no escalation — only a rate-limited warn log ("otlp export error ... duplicate label values") — so the outage can persist indefinitely until an operator notices the staleness and manually finds/removes the duplicate config on the box.

## Suggested direction

Pass the self-metrics registry and the collector registry to the bridge as two independent gatherers (two `WithGatherer` calls, or `telemetry.Start` accepting `[]prometheus.Gatherer`) so the bridge's per-gatherer error handling isolates a bad collector registry from the healthy self-metrics registry. Consider also wrapping the collector registry gatherer so that a partial-gather error is logged but the successfully gathered families are still returned with a nil error, mirroring `promhttp.ContinueOnError` semantics and converging with any related `/metrics` HTTP-path fix for the same duplicate-label root cause.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit/integration test constructs a self-metrics registry (one healthy gauge) and a collector registry with a manufactured duplicate-label metric, wires them into the OTel Prometheus bridge the same way `main.go` does, and asserts that `producer.Produce` still returns the healthy self-metric's data (non-zero ScopeMetrics) despite the collector registry's error.
- [ ] The same test asserts the erroring collector registry's own bad metric family is excluded (or handled) without causing a total blackout.
- [ ] A regression test covers at least one real-world duplicate scenario (e.g. duplicate cron job descriptions) feeding into the OTLP export path, not just the `/metrics` HTTP path.
- [ ] `make test` passes with the new tests, and the fix does not require disabling OTLP or silently swallowing the underlying config error — it must still be logged.
- [ ] Manual/documented verification that after the fix, an export tick with one bad collector still delivers all other collectors' and self-metrics' data to the OTLP backend.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `ab0fdcc`.

Root cause confirmed against current code: `main.go` passed `prometheus.Gatherers{selfMetricsRegistry, collectorRegistry}` as a **single** gatherer to `telemetry.Start` → one `WithGatherer` → the bridge producer treats any non-nil `Gather()` error as total failure and discards the partial families.

**Fix (`internal/telemetry/provider.go`):**
- `Start` now takes `[]prometheus.Gatherer` and registers each registry with its **own** `WithGatherer` call, so the bridge's per-gatherer error handling isolates a bad collector registry from the healthy self-metrics registry.
- Each gatherer is wrapped in a new `continueOnErrorGatherer` that returns the successfully-gathered families with a **nil** error (mirroring `promhttp.ContinueOnError`) and logs the underlying error **rate-limited** (reusing `errorLogInterval`), so a persistent duplicate can't flood the logs but the misconfiguration stays visible.

**Tests (`provider_test.go`):** `TestBridgeIsolatesErroringGatherer` wires a self-metrics registry (healthy gauge) + a collector registry containing a healthy family **and** a `dupCronCollector` (two identical `description="nightly-backup"` series — the real-world duplicate-cron scenario) through the actual bridge producer, and asserts the self-metric and healthy collector family still reach `producer.Produce`, no blackout, and the gather error is logged. Premise-checked that the raw registry really errors on gather.

Note on acceptance #2: prometheus' `Gather` returns the offending family *alongside* the MultiError rather than dropping it, so the bad family is **handled** (error surfaced via log, no blackout) rather than excluded — the test reflects that accurately.

Gate green: `make test`, `make lint` (0 issues), `make docs-check`. No metric/grafana changes.

body:
## Problem

`scripts/docgen/main.go` derives the "Type" column of the generated metrics reference (`docs/metrics/metrics.md`) purely from a name-suffix heuristic: a metric is documented as `Counter` if its name ends in `_total`, and `Gauge` otherwise. It never inspects the actual `prometheus.ValueType` (`CounterValue`/`GaugeValue`) passed at the metric's `prometheus.MustNewConstMetric` call site in `internal/collector/*.go`. Because several collectors emit `_total`-suffixed metrics as gauges (instantaneous counts, not monotonic totals) and a few non-`_total` metrics are genuinely counters, the generated reference — the repo's "Complete Metrics Reference" — misstates the Prometheus type for roughly 50 of 546 documented metrics today.

`scripts/docgen/verify.go` only compares fqNames between the AST-derived descriptor set and the runtime-registered collectors (`verify.go:52-56` per finding evidence); it does not compare value types. This means `make docs-check` is structurally incapable of catching this class of error — it will stay green even as more suffix/type mismatches are introduced.

## Evidence

- `scripts/docgen/main.go:691-694`:
  ```go
  metricType := "Gauge"
  if strings.HasSuffix(name, "_total") {
      metricType = "Counter"
  }
  ```
  This is the only logic that sets the documented type; the emission call's actual `ValueType` argument is never consulted.

- 46 gauge-valued metrics documented as `Counter`, e.g.:
  - `internal/collector/services.go` — `running_total` declared and emitted with `prometheus.GaugeValue` (services.go:41-42, 65), documented "Counter" at `docs/metrics/metrics.md:686`.
  - `internal/collector/protocol.go` — `icmp_dropped_by_reason_total` (protocol.go:136, 441-443) and `udp_dropped_by_reason_total` (protocol.go:155, 448-450) both emitted with `GaugeValue`, documented "Counter" at `docs/metrics/metrics.md:599` and `:603`.
  - `internal/collector/dhcpv4.go` (`opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_total`), `internal/collector/dnsmasq.go:96` (`opnsense_dnsmasq_leases_total`), `internal/collector/kea.go` (`opnsense_kea_dhcp4_leases_total`), `internal/collector/openvpn.go` (`opnsense_openvpn_sessions_total`), `internal/collector/ntp.go` (`opnsense_ntp_peers_total`), `internal/collector/captiveportal.go` (`opnsense_captiveportal_sessions_total`) — all `GaugeValue`, all documented "Counter".

- 4 real counters documented as `Gauge`:
  - `internal/collector/ipsec.go:230-232` — `phase2_bytes_in`/`phase2_bytes_out`/`packets_in`/`packets_out` emitted with `prometheus.CounterValue`, documented "Gauge" at `docs/metrics/metrics.md:366`.

- `scripts/docgen/verify.go:16-38` — its `fqNameRe` regex extracts only the fqName token from each `Desc` string and diffs name sets between the AST-derived and runtime-registered descriptors; it never inspects or compares `ValueType`, so this class of mismatch is invisible to `make docs-check`.

- The summary line in `docs/metrics/metrics.md` ("Gauges: N, Counters: M") is wrong by the same ~50-metric margin.

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box (the `_total` docgen heuristic and the 7 cross-checked examples — `dhcpv4_leases_total`, `dnsmasq_leases_total`, `openvpn_sessions_total`, `ntp_peers_total`, `kea_dhcp4_leases_total`, `captiveportal_sessions_total`, `services_running_total` — were diffed against the live scrape's `# TYPE` lines and all emit as gauges despite the `_total` suffix and "Counter" documentation).

## Failure scenario / impact

A user (or the repo's own dashboard/alert-authoring tooling) consults `docs/metrics/metrics.md`, sees `opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_total` (or any of the other 45 gauge metrics) documented as `Counter`, and writes `rate()`/`increase()` over it — producing a permanently near-zero panel or a dead alert, because the series is an instantaneous lease/session/service count that moves in both directions, not a monotonic total. Conversely, a user trusting the "Gauge" documentation for `opnsense_ipsec_phase2_bytes_in` (an actual counter) may treat it as a level value and build incorrect capacity/threshold logic instead of a rate. `make docs-check` passes throughout because `verify.go` only diffs metric names, never types.

## Suggested direction

Have docgen resolve each metric's documented type from the `prometheus.{Counter,Gauge}Value` argument at its `MustNewConstMetric` call site (the AST walk already visits these files), falling back to the current suffix heuristic only when a call site can't be resolved. Add a test/gate — e.g. a testutil-driven scrape of the registered collectors compared against the docgen-derived type table — so `make docs-check` fails on any future suffix/type disagreement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test asserts that docgen's documented type for `opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_total`, `opnsense_dnsmasq_leases_total`, `opnsense_services_running_total`, `opnsense_icmp_dropped_by_reason_total`, and `opnsense_udp_dropped_by_reason_total` is `Gauge`, matching their actual `GaugeValue` emission.
- [ ] A unit test asserts that docgen's documented type for `opnsense_ipsec_phase2_bytes_in`, `phase2_bytes_out`, `packets_in`, and `packets_out` is `Counter`, matching their actual `CounterValue` emission.
- [ ] `docs/metrics/metrics.md` is regenerated via `make docs` and no longer documents any of the above metrics with a mismatched type; the Gauges/Counters summary counts are corrected accordingly.
- [ ] `scripts/docgen/verify.go` (or an equivalent new check wired into `make docs-check`) fails CI if a metric's documented type diverges from the `ValueType` used at its emission call site, so this class of drift cannot silently reoccur.
- [ ] The `_total`-suffix heuristic is retained only as a fallback for descriptors whose emission call site cannot be statically resolved, and this fallback path is covered by a test.

docgen now resolves each metric's documented type from the `prometheus.{Counter,Gauge}Value` argument at its `MustNewConstMetric`/`NewConstMetric` emission site (linked to the `buildPrometheusDesc` assignment by the desc-field name, e.g. `c.servicesRunning`). The `_total`-suffix heuristic is retained **only** as a fallback for descs whose emission can't be resolved statically (table-driven collectors emitting through a loop/local desc var) — acceptance #5.

body:
## Problem

The example Kubernetes manifests in `deploy/k8s/` are broken in two independent ways if applied as shipped.

First, `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml` sets `scrapeTimeout: 3s`. The exporter derives its internal per-scrape deadline as the incoming `X-Prometheus-Scrape-Timeout-Seconds` header value minus the `--exporter.scrape-timeout-offset` flag (default 500ms; see `internal/options/exporter.go:26-29`), so a 3s Prometheus-side timeout leaves the exporter only ~2.5s to complete all 30+ sub-collectors, several of which chain multiple sequential OPNsense API calls. On a real (modest home-lab) firewall, full collection takes 2.5-3.2s wall time, so the slowest collectors are routinely cancelled mid-scrape by the per-request context deadline. The HTTP scrape itself still returns 200 with a metrics body, so the failure is silent: affected collectors just report `opnsense_exporter_scrape_collector_success{collector="..."} 0` and their metrics vanish, with no obvious "target down" signal in Prometheus.

Second, the scrape target `opnsense-exporter.svc:8080` in `scrape.yaml` (and the equivalent `opnsense-exporter.svc.cluster.local:8080` in the README's debug `wget` example) is not a valid Kubernetes Service DNS name. Kubernetes Service DNS only exists in the form `<service>.<namespace>.svc.<cluster-domain>`, with the shorthand `<service>` (same namespace) or `<service>.<namespace>`. There is no `.svc` shorthand that omits the namespace. The name as written only resolves in the degenerate case where the exporter happens to be deployed into a namespace literally named `svc`; in any normal deployment (e.g. `default`, or any app-named namespace) it NXDOMAINs.

## Evidence

- `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml:14` — `scrapeTimeout: 3s`
- `internal/options/exporter.go:26-29` — the `--exporter.scrape-timeout-offset` flag (default 500ms) is subtracted from the incoming scrape-timeout header to derive the exporter's internal deadline
- `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml:21` — `targets:` containing `- opnsense-exporter.svc:8080`
- `deploy/k8s/README.md:57` — `wget --quiet -O- opnsense-exporter.svc.cluster.local:8080/metrics`
- `deploy/k8s/deployment.yaml` — defines a Service named `opnsense-exporter` with no namespace field, confirming the example has no namespace literally named `svc`

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: baseline scrapes with a 60s `X-Prometheus-Scrape-Timeout-Seconds` header completed in 2.51s / 2.49s / 3.23s wall time with zero collector failures. Re-running with the exact header value `scrape.yaml` causes Prometheus to send (`X-Prometheus-Scrape-Timeout-Seconds: 3`) produced collector failures on repeated scrapes — e.g. `opnsense_exporter_scrape_collector_success{collector="activity"} 0` and `{collector="kea"} 0` — with exporter log lines such as `endpoint: api/kea/dhcpv6/searchSubnet; ... request aborted: context deadline exceeded` and `endpoint: api/diagnostics/activity/get_activity; ... request aborted: context deadline exceeded`, while the scrape HTTP response remained 200.

## Failure scenario / impact

A user applies `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml` as shipped against a Prometheus Operator setup: on essentially every scrape cycle, the slowest collectors (observed: `activity`, `kea`; more on slower/bigger boxes) get cancelled by the internal deadline. Their metrics silently disappear from Prometheus while the scrape target itself still reports up/200, so nothing looks obviously broken — it's a quiet, partial, and easy-to-miss data loss.

Separately, a user applies `deployment.yaml` + `scrape.yaml` together in any normal setup (e.g. exporter in `default`, Prometheus in `monitoring`, or any app-named namespace): the scrape target DNS name fails to resolve, the target shows down with a resolution error, and zero opnsense metrics are collected at all until the user manually fixes the target hostname. The README's `wget` debug example has the identical bug, so a user trying to debug connectivity by copy-pasting that command also gets a DNS failure.

## Suggested direction

Raise `scrapeTimeout` in `scrape.yaml` to something realistic for a 30+ collector API fanout (e.g. 30s, still comfortably under the 60s scrape interval), and add a comment explaining the exporter's timeout-offset behavior so users size it consciously. Separately, fix the scrape target to a valid Kubernetes Service DNS name (e.g. `opnsense-exporter.<namespace>.svc:8080` with a comment to substitute the deploy namespace, or default to `.default.svc`), and apply the same fix to the README's `wget` example.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml`'s `scrapeTimeout` is raised to a value (e.g. 30s) that leaves enough headroom above the exporter's `--exporter.scrape-timeout-offset` default for a full 30+ collector scrape to complete without hitting the internal deadline
- [ ] A comment in `scrape.yaml` (or accompanying README) explains how the exporter derives its internal per-scrape deadline from `X-Prometheus-Scrape-Timeout-Seconds` minus `--exporter.scrape-timeout-offset`, so users size `scrapeTimeout` consciously
- [ ] `deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml`'s target is changed to a name that is a valid, resolvable Kubernetes Service DNS name regardless of which namespace the exporter is deployed into (e.g. includes an explicit namespace placeholder or `.default.svc`)
- [ ] `deploy/k8s/README.md:57`'s `wget` debug example is updated to use the same corrected, resolvable DNS name
- [ ] `make docs-check` (or equivalent lint) passes after the change, confirming no other doc references the old broken target or timeout value

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `393f998`.

- **`deploy/k8s/scrape.yaml`**: `scrapeTimeout: 3s` → `30s` with a comment explaining the internal deadline = header − `--exporter.scrape-timeout-offset` (500ms) derivation (#1, #2); target `opnsense-exporter.svc:8080` → `opnsense-exporter.default.svc:8080` with a namespace-substitution comment (#3).
- **`deploy/k8s/README.md`**: `wget` example → `opnsense-exporter.default.svc.cluster.local:8080` (#4).
- **`docs/deployment/kubernetes.md`**: the ScrapeConfig block's stale `scrapeTimeout: 3s` → `30s` (its targets were already `.default.svc`).

Verified no other non-generated doc references the old target/timeout (`site/` is the zensical-generated snapshot, regenerated from `docs/` by docs-sync). `make docs-check` passes (#5).

body:
## Problem

The Grafana dashboard's `$interface` template variable is sourced from `opnsense_interfaces_link_state`, whose `interface` label carries the user-configured *description* (e.g. `LAN`, `MGMT`, `IOT`). That variable is then used as an `interface=~"$interface"` filter on the firewall pf-traffic metrics and the netflow cache metrics, but those metric families label their `interface` field with the *kernel device name* (e.g. `igb0`, `ixl0_vlan25`, `pppoe0`), not the description. The two label spaces are disjoint, so a regex match built from one can never match series in the other except by coincidence.

This happens because different OPNsense collectors populate the same Prometheus label name (`interface`) from different underlying identifiers: the interfaces collector uses the interface's configured description (`iface.Name`), while the firewall pf-stats collector and the netflow collector use the OS device name as returned by the underlying pfctl/netflow APIs. The dashboard was built assuming label consistency across these families, which does not hold.

## Evidence

- `grafana/tabs/build_dashboard.py:48-57` — defines `$interface` as `label_values(opnsense_interfaces_link_state{...}, interface)`.
- `internal/collector/interfaces.go:176` (label source `iface.Name`, the configured description) — on the live box, values are `{AAISP, CAM, IOT, LAN, MGMT, VIRGIN, tailscale}`.
- `opnsense/firewall.go:180-213` and `opnsense/firewall.go:58` — `opnsense_firewall_{in,out}_{ipv4,ipv6}_{pass,block}_{packets,bytes_total}` (16 metrics) are labelled from the `pfStatsByInterface` map key, which is the kernel device name — on the live box, `{igb0, ixl0, ixl0_vlan25, pppoe0, ...}`.
- `opnsense/netflow.go:22` — netflow cache metrics carry the `if` field, also a device name (`pppoe0`, `ixl0_vlan25`, `ixl0` on the live box).
- `grafana/tabs/firewall.py:25-118` and `grafana/tabs/netflow.py:83` — apply `interface=~"$interface"` to all of the above (37 metrics total filtered by this variable across the dashboard).
- Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: the interfaces metric's label set and the firewall/netflow metrics' label set are disjoint, non-overlapping strings.
- Note: `interface_hits_total` on the same tab is fed by `FetchFirewallStats` which does use the friendly description, so that one panel is unaffected — only the pf-traffic and netflow panels are broken.

## Failure scenario / impact

A user investigating LAN traffic during an incident selects `LAN` from the dashboard's Interface dropdown. The Interfaces tab continues to work normally, but all 16 firewall pass/block packets/bytes panels and the netflow cache panels go blank ("No data"), because no firewall or netflow series has an `interface` label equal to `LAN`. During an incident this reads as "no firewall traffic on this interface" rather than what it actually is — a variable/label mismatch. The dashboard's default "All" selection masks the bug entirely (works only because `allValue` is `.+`), so it goes unnoticed until someone filters to a specific interface.

## Suggested direction

Either stop applying `$interface` to the pf-traffic/netflow panels since they enumerate a different entity space, or introduce a second variable (e.g. `$device`) sourced from `label_values(opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_packets, interface)` for those panels specifically. Longer-term, consider having the pf/netflow collectors translate device names to interface descriptions so the `interface` label is consistent across the whole exporter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting a named interface (e.g. `LAN`) from the dashboard's Interface variable no longer blanks the firewall pass/block packets/bytes panels when matching traffic exists on that interface.
- [ ] Selecting a named interface from the Interface variable no longer blanks the netflow cache panels when matching traffic exists on that interface.
- [ ] `make dashboard` succeeds and the coverage gate still passes after the fix (no catalogue metric left unwired).
- [ ] The dashboard-as-code has an explicit test or assertion (or documented convention in `grafana/tabs/AUTHORING.md`) preventing a variable sourced from one label-space from being silently applied to metrics from a different label-space in future tabs.
- [ ] `grafana/README.md` or tab-level comments document which metrics use description-based vs device-based `interface` labels, so future panels wire the correct variable.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `b8506a5` (straight to main).

Root cause confirmed against current code: `$interface` enumerates the description-space label (`LAN`/`IOT`/…) from `opnsense_interfaces_link_state`, but the pf-traffic counters and netflow cache metrics label `interface` with the kernel **device name** (`igb0`/`ixl0_vlan25`/`pppoe0`) — disjoint spaces, so a named selection blanked those panels (masked only by the `.+` All default).

Fix:
- Added a second core variable **`$device`** sourced from `label_values(opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_packets, interface)` — lists exactly the devices those panels plot.
- **firewall.py**: all 16 pf-traffic selectors → `DEV = 'interface=~"$device"'`. The description-based `opnsense_firewall_interface_log_entries_recent` panel stays on `$interface` (its label really is the description — issue noted this one is unaffected). ✅ acceptance #1
- **netflow.py**: cache-metric selector → `$device`. ✅ acceptance #2

Verified in generated JSON: 19 `$device` references (16 firewall + 3 netflow), `device` query variable present.

Documentation (acceptance #4/#5): added a hard rule to `grafana/tabs/AUTHORING.md` spelling out the two disjoint `interface` label spaces and which variable each metric family must use, so future panels can't silently cross them.

Gate: dashboard coverage 556/556 (acceptance #3), `make docs-check` green, `make test` green.

body:
## Problem

Eleven multi-query tables across the Grafana dashboard builder key their `renameByName` overrides and `unit_overrides` on Prometheus **metric names** (e.g. `"opnsense_gateways_rtt_low_milliseconds": "RTT Low (ms)"`). This never matches anything.

For a Prometheus instant query with `format=table`, the value field is always literally named `Value`; the metric name only appears in the excluded `__name__` column. When a table panel has multiple `exprs` (multiple queries with refIds A, B, C…), the `merge` transformation disambiguates the columns as `Value #A`, `Value #B`, etc. — never by metric name. `renameByName`/`byName` unit overrides must therefore be keyed on `Value #A`, `Value #B`, ... to have any effect. Keying them on metric names means the rename and unit annotation are silently dead: the transformation runs, finds no matching field, and the panel falls back to showing the raw `Value #A` / `Value #B` headers with no label and no unit.

The repo already documents and correctly applies the right pattern elsewhere (`grafana/tabs/system.py:427-429`, `carp.py:101-108`, `qfeeds.py:50-51`), which makes this a straightforward miskeying bug rather than an unknown convention — `crowdsec.py` even mixes both forms in the same `renames`/`unit_overrides` dict, with one key working and its sibling dead.

## Evidence

- `grafana/builder.py:208-235` — `table()` builds one `PanelQuery` per expr with `instant=True, format=table` and `ref=chr(65+i)` (refIds A, B, C…), then applies `merge` + `organize` transforms whose `renameByName`/unit `byName` overrides operate on the transformed field names (`Value`, or `Value #A`/`Value #B`... when merged).
- `grafana/tabs/system.py:427-429` — in-repo documentation of the convention: "the merge transformation names the value columns 'Value #A'..'Value #D' ... rename THOSE, not the metric names."
- Correct usage (for reference): `grafana/tabs/system.py` (smart_attr_table), `grafana/tabs/carp.py:101-108` (`"Value #A": "Advbase (s)", "Value #B": "Advskew"`), `grafana/tabs/qfeeds.py:50-51` (`unit_overrides={"Value #A": ..., "Value #B": ...}`).
- Broken usage (metric-name keys, dead renames/units):
  - `grafana/tabs/gateways.py:39-48` (RTT Thresholds)
  - `grafana/tabs/gateways.py:68-77` (Loss Thresholds)
  - `grafana/tabs/gateways.py:125-132` (Gateway Flags)
  - `grafana/tabs/gateways.py:147-158` (Probe Configuration)
  - `grafana/tabs/interfaces.py:121-131` (Interface Info: MTU / Line Rate)
  - `grafana/tabs/vpn.py:278-288` (IPsec Phase 2 Rekey & Lifetime)
  - `grafana/tabs/haproxy.py:207-214` (Server Details)
  - `grafana/tabs/monit.py:90-95` (Check Details)
  - `grafana/tabs/crowdsec.py:76-95` and `:107-120` (each mixes a working `"Value #B"` key with a dead metric-name key in the same dict — smoking-gun evidence of the bug)
  - `grafana/tabs/chrony.py:147-155` and `:184-189` (stratum/reachability/last-rx)

This is a dashboard-generation/code defect, not something observable against a live box (not applicable here — the bug is in the Python builder, verifiable by reading the generated panel JSON).

## Failure scenario / impact

A user opens any of the affected tabs — e.g. Gateways → "RTT Thresholds" — and sees a table with two indistinguishable columns headed `Value #A` and `Value #B`, no descriptive label, and no `ms` unit suffix. There is no way to tell which column is the low threshold and which is the high one. The same pattern repeats for Loss Thresholds, Gateway Flags, Probe Configuration (gateways.py), Interface Info MTU vs. line-rate (interfaces.py), IPsec rekey vs. lifetime (vpn.py), HAProxy server status/weight/sessions/queue (haproxy.py), Monit check status/monitored (monit.py), and chrony stratum/reachability/last-rx (chrony.py). The panels render without error, so this is a silent cosmetic defect — it degrades every one of the eleven tables into an unlabeled, unit-less wall of numbers with no runtime indication anything is wrong.

## Suggested direction

Change the `renameByName`/`unit_overrides` keys in the listed tables from metric names to `Value #A`..`Value #N` matching the exprs order (the pattern already used correctly in `system.py`/`carp.py`/`qfeeds.py`), then run `make dashboard`. Consider extending `builder.table()` to accept a `[(expr, column_name, unit)]`-style parameter that generates the `Value #X` mapping internally, so this class of bug can't recur.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four tables in `grafana/tabs/gateways.py` (RTT Thresholds, Loss Thresholds, Gateway Flags, Probe Configuration) key `renameByName`/`unit_overrides` on `Value #A`/`Value #B`/... instead of metric names, and each column renders a human-readable label with the correct unit after `make dashboard`.
- [ ] `grafana/tabs/interfaces.py` Interface Info table, `grafana/tabs/vpn.py` IPsec Phase 2 Rekey & Lifetime table, `grafana/tabs/haproxy.py` Server Details table, `grafana/tabs/monit.py` Check Details table, and both affected `grafana/tabs/chrony.py` tables are fixed the same way.
- [ ] `grafana/tabs/crowdsec.py`'s two mixed-key dicts (`:76-95`, `:107-120`) have their remaining metric-name keys converted to `Value #A`/`Value #B` form so no dict mixes both conventions.
- [ ] A regression check (unit test or `make dashboard`-time lint) asserts that every multi-expr `table()` panel's `renameByName`/`unit_overrides` keys are drawn only from the `Value #A`..`Value #N` set implied by its expr count, failing the build if a metric-name key is used instead.
- [ ] `make dashboard` runs clean after the fix with no metrics left off the dashboard coverage gate.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `4800d96` (straight to main).

Rekeyed all 11 multi-expr tables' `renameByName`/`unit_overrides` from metric names to `Value #A`..`Value #N` in expr order (the pattern already correct in system.py/carp.py/qfeeds.py):

- **gateways.py** — RTT Thresholds, Loss Thresholds, Gateway Flags, Probe Configuration
- **interfaces.py** — Interface Info (MTU / Line Rate)
- **vpn.py** — IPsec Phase 2 Rekey & Lifetime
- **haproxy.py** — Server Details
- **monit.py** — Check Details
- **crowdsec.py** — Bouncer Details, Machine Details (the mixed dicts — dead A-key fixed, working B-key untouched)
- **chrony.py** — Source Status, Source Statistics

**Regression guard (acceptance #4):** added to `builder.table()` — for any table with >1 expr, a rename/unit key that is a referenced metric name, bare `Value`, or an out-of-range `Value #X` is collected and **fails `build_dashboard.py`** (same mechanism as the #78 dateTimeAsIso guard). It listed all **29** dead keys before the fix and passes clean after — verified by watching it fail then go green.

Regenerated `dashboard.json` (`make dashboard`); spot-checked the JSON now carries `"Value #A": "RTT Low (ms)"` etc. Gate: dashboard coverage 556/556, `make docs-check` green, `make test` green.

body:
## Problem

Both the Unbound "Cache Hit Ratio" dashboard gauge and its equivalent Prometheus recording rule compute the ratio as `rate(hits) / clamp_min(rate(hits) + rate(miss), 1)`. The `clamp_min(..., 1)` is a divide-by-zero guard, but the floor value (`1`) is a real, plausible query rate, not an infinitesimal epsilon. Whenever the combined DNS query rate over the evaluation window drops below 1 query/second — overnight, on a quiet home/lab firewall, or on any small deployment that simply never sees 1 qps — the denominator is pinned to `1` instead of the true (sub-1) rate. The result is no longer a ratio: it collapses to `hits_rate * true_ratio`, i.e. the recorded/displayed value scales down proportionally to how quiet the box is, not to actual cache performance.

The rest of `build_rules.py` already uses the correct idiom for this exact situation — `X / (Y > 0)`, a boolean filter that only prevents division by exactly zero without distorting real values (see the `pf_state` and `system_mem` utilization rules) — confirming the `clamp_min(..., 1)` here was an oversight, not deliberate.

## Evidence

- `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:146-148` — recording rule `instance:opnsense_unbound_cache:hit_ratio`:
  ```
  rate(hits[5m]) / clamp_min(rate(hits[5m]) + rate(miss[5m]), 1)
  ```
  Rendered into `opnsense.rules.yaml:186` and `grafana-managed/oxrec-unbound-cache-hit-ratio.json:35`.
- `grafana/tabs/dns_unbound.py:59-64` — "Cache Hit Ratio" gauge panel:
  ```
  100 * rate(cache_hits_total[$__rate_interval]) / clamp_min(rate(cache_hits_total[...]) + rate(cache_miss_total[...]), 1)
  ```
  Rendered into `dashboard.json:14525`.
- Contrast with the correct idiom already in the same file: `pf_state` utilization (`build_rules.py:145`) and `system_mem` utilization (`build_rules.py:152`) both use `X / (Y > 0)` instead of `clamp_min(Y, 1)`.
- Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: lifetime average query rate was ~3.7 qps (246,829 total queries over 66,176s uptime), which plausibly dips below 1 qps in 5-minute windows off-peak, and sits below 1 qps permanently on smaller deployments.

## Failure scenario / impact

A quiet firewall (overnight, or any low-traffic/home/lab deployment) averages, say, 0.3 hits/s + 0.1 miss/s over a 5-minute window — a true cache hit ratio of ~75%. Because `hits+miss = 0.4 < 1`, the denominator is clamped to `1`, so the recorded/displayed value becomes `0.3` (30%) instead of `0.75` (75%). In the extreme, 0.05 hits/s with zero misses (a true 100% hit ratio) displays as 5%, which is low enough to trip a "<50%" red threshold on the dashboard gauge. This produces a false performance alarm that scales with how idle the box is rather than with actual cache behavior, and any future alerting built on the recording rule would inherit the same false signal.

## Suggested direction

Replace the divide-by-zero guard with one that doesn't distort real values in the sub-1-qps range: either use the same `(Y > 0)` boolean-filter idiom already used elsewhere in `build_rules.py` for `pf_state` and `system_mem` utilization, or lower the `clamp_min` floor to a true epsilon (e.g. `1e-10`) that only guards against exact zero.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `instance:opnsense_unbound_cache:hit_ratio` recording rule in `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py` no longer clamps the denominator at `1`; it uses a zero-only guard (e.g. `(Y > 0)` or an epsilon floor) that leaves sub-1-qps values undistorted.
- [ ] The "Cache Hit Ratio" gauge query in `grafana/tabs/dns_unbound.py` is updated with the same fix so the dashboard and recording rule stay consistent.
- [ ] A test or worked example demonstrates that at 0.3 hits/s + 0.1 miss/s the computed ratio is ~75% (not 30%), and at 0.05 hits/s + 0 miss/s it is ~100% (not 5%).
- [ ] `make rules` and `make dashboard` are re-run and the regenerated `opnsense.rules.yaml`, `grafana-managed/oxrec-unbound-cache-hit-ratio.json`, and `dashboard.json` reflect the corrected expression.
- [ ] Existing tests for `build_rules.py` / dashboard generation still pass with the updated query strings.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `0381b26` (straight to main).

Replaced `clamp_min(rate(hits)+rate(miss), 1)` with the `X / (Y > 0)` boolean-filter idiom (the same one already used for `pf_state` and `system_mem` utilization) in **both** the recording rule (`build_rules.py`) and the dashboard gauge (`tabs/dns_unbound.py`). It guards only exact zero and leaves sub-1-qps values undistorted.

Worked example (acceptance #3):
- 0.3 hits/s + 0.1 miss/s → 0.3/0.4 = **75%** (was 30%)
- 0.05 hits/s + 0 miss/s → 0.05/0.05 = **100%** (was 5%)

body:
## Problem

The portable Prometheus alert rule `OPNsenseExporterDown` (`grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml`) uses the expression `opnsense_up < 1`, and its own description — as well as `grafana/README.md` — claim the alert also fires "or the target produced NoData for 15m". That claim is false for the portable Prometheus/Mimir artifact.

In plain Prometheus rule-group semantics, a threshold comparison over an absent time series returns an empty vector, not a match. When the exporter process itself crashes, OOM-kills, or otherwise stops being scrapeable, its `opnsense_up` series goes stale and then disappears entirely (after the ~5m staleness window) — it does not become `0`. An alert expression of `opnsense_up < 1` therefore only fires in the case where the exporter is running and reachable but reports the OPNsense API as unreachable (`opnsense_up == 0`). It cannot fire when the exporter itself is down, because there is no series left to compare.

The "NoData" semantics referenced in the description come from Grafana-managed alerting (`noDataState`), which is a separate artifact generated by the same builder (`grafana/alerts/build_rules.py`). That setting has no effect on the plain-Prometheus rule-group YAML that `build_rules.py`'s own header calls "the artifact most users want." So the coverage gap is real for the majority of users who deploy the portable rules file, while the shared description text was written assuming Grafana-managed alerting's NoData handling applies universally.

## Evidence

- `grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml:6-14` — rule uses `expr: opnsense_up < 1`, `for: 15m`, with a description stating the alert also covers "the target produced NoData for 15m."
- `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:34-43` — sets `nodata="Alerting"`, but this value is only consumed at `build_rules.py:262` where it is written into the Grafana-managed JSON's `noDataState` field. It has no corresponding effect on the plain Prometheus YAML rule-group emission.
- `grafana/README.md:106` — repeats the "or NoData for 15m" claim in the alert table, for the same file recommended to most users as the primary/portable artifact.

Confirmed by adversarial verification (not against a live box — this is a rule-semantics/documentation defect, not something requiring the live OPNsense appliance).

## Failure scenario / impact

The exporter container OOM-kills (or crashes, or its deployment fails) at some point in time. Its `opnsense_up` series goes stale and then vanishes from the TSDB after the staleness window. Because the alert expression is a plain `< 1` comparison, it evaluates to an empty vector and never fires — the critical "exporter/box down" pager is silently skipped. The firewall or the exporter itself may then experience a real outage that goes undetected, because the operator believed (per the alert's own description and the README) that a NoData condition was already covered by this rule. The gap is specifically triggered by the exporter process itself dying, not by the OPNsense API being merely unreachable (which the current expression does correctly catch via `opnsense_up == 0`).

## Suggested direction

For the portable Prometheus rule-group emission, either extend the expression to also catch the absent/stale case (e.g. `opnsense_up < 1 or absent(opnsense_up)`, or an `up{job=~...} == 0` companion rule documented as requiring the user's own job label), or, at minimum, correct the alert description and README text so portable-rules users understand they must pair this rule with a separate absent()/up-based alert to get real "exporter is down" coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test or manual check confirms that `grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml`'s `OPNsenseExporterDown` expression (or an added companion rule) fires when `opnsense_up` is entirely absent from the series, not just when it is `0`.
- [ ] The alert description in `build_rules.py` (and hence the generated `opnsense.rules.yaml`) no longer claims blanket "NoData for 15m" coverage for the portable Prometheus artifact unless the expression actually implements it.
- [ ] `grafana/README.md`'s alert table entry for this rule accurately reflects what the portable YAML file covers (distinguishing it from the Grafana-managed variant's `noDataState` behavior if they still differ).
- [ ] If an `absent()`/`up`-based fallback is added, `make rules` regenerates the rule file cleanly and any golden/snapshot test over `grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml` is updated to match.
- [ ] The Grafana-managed alert variant's `noDataState="Alerting"` behavior is documented as being specific to that variant, not implied to also apply to the portable file.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body: Scope clarification after review with Rob: this finding applies **only to the portable `opnsense.rules.yaml`**. The Grafana-managed rendering of the same rule already handles the exporter-dead case — `build_rules.py:36` sets `nodata="Alerting"` and `grafana-managed/opnsense-exporter-down.json` carries `"noDataState": "Alerting"` — so gcx-pushed deployments are covered. The portable Prometheus rule-group format has no NoData concept, which is exactly why `opnsense_up < 1` silently never fires there when the target vanishes; the fix (e.g. `absent()` clause or an `up{job=...} == 0` companion rule) is needed in the portable artifact only.

Resolved by dropping the portable Prometheus rules format (product decision, 2026-07-03), 2af458a. The NoData blind spot was specific to the portable `opnsense_up < 1` rule-group file, which is now removed. The Grafana-managed `opnsense-exporter-down` manifest already sets `noDataState: "Alerting"`, so the exporter-dead / series-absent case genuinely fires — the README's "or NoData for 15m" claim is now accurate for the single supported (Grafana-managed) format.

body:
## Problem

The `OPNsenseEndpointErrors` alert rule is intended to require *sustained* endpoint errors before firing, so that a brief router reboot or WAN blip doesn't page/warn anyone. Commit `5b6682d` ("alerts: reduce false positives during router reboots") tried to implement this by changing the rule's `for:` duration from `0s` to `15m`, and the shipped annotation claims the alert "has returned errors continuously for 15m" and that the 15m for-duration "filters out transient errors during a router reboot / brief WAN loss."

That fix does not work, because the rule still uses a 15-minute `increase()` window as the alert condition itself: `increase(opnsense_exporter_endpoint_errors_total[15m]) > 0`. `increase(x[15m])` evaluated at time T covers the trailing 15-minute window `(T-15m, T]`, so once any errors occur, the condition stays true for the whole error-burst span *plus* 15 more minutes after the last error. Prometheus's `for` clock starts counting from the first evaluation where the condition is true, so `for: 15m` is satisfied as soon as the last error is within roughly 15 minutes of the first — which is true for essentially any burst that spans more than a single scrape/evaluation interval. The `for:` duration was meant to filter based on how long errors persist, but because the input signal itself is artificially held "true" for 15 minutes after errors stop, the change doesn't achieve that; it only excuses a single, isolated one-scrape error.

The same defective pattern (`increase(...[15m]) > 0` combined with `for: 15m`) also exists for the DNS Unbound "bogus answers" alert in the same file, though only the endpoint-errors alert was adversarially verified in detail here.

## Evidence

`grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:52-57` (rendered into `grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml:33-41`):

```python
A="sum by (opnsense_instance, endpoint) (increase(opnsense_exporter_endpoint_errors_total[15m]))",
```
with `for_min=15` (rendered as `for: 15m`), and an annotation claiming the endpoint "has returned errors continuously for 15m" / that the duration "filters out transient errors during a router reboot / brief WAN loss."

A structurally identical pattern exists at `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py:128` for `opnsense_unbound_dns_answers_bogus_total`.

Not livebox-validated (this is a Prometheus/Grafana alerting-semantics defect, not something that requires a live OPNsense box).

## Failure scenario / impact

A router reboots for 8 minutes (the exact scenario commit `5b6682d` says it tolerates). The exporter keeps scraping and each failed scrape during the reboot increments the error counter, so errors accumulate over `t=0..8m`. `increase(...[15m]) > 0` is then continuously true from roughly `t=0.5m` to `t=23m` (~22 minutes). The `for` clock starts at the first true evaluation (~`t=0.5m`... `t=1m`), so pending reaches 15m and the alert **fires around t=15-16m** — roughly 7-8 minutes *after* the router/box is already fully healthy again — and then stays firing/red until around `t=23m`. The same math applies to any WAN blip of a couple of minutes: any error burst spanning more than one evaluation interval (~1 minute) will fire the alert well after recovery, which is precisely the false-positive class the commit claimed to have fixed. Only a single, truly isolated one-scrape error escapes, and only by a sub-minute margin.

## Suggested direction

Use a short `increase()`/`rate()` window paired with the long `for:` duration so `for` actually measures sustained error presence — e.g. `increase(opnsense_exporter_endpoint_errors_total[2m]) > 0` with `for: 15m`, or equivalent `rate(...) > 0`. Apply the same fix to the Unbound "bogus answers" rule at `build_rules.py:128`, and correct the annotation text to describe the real semantics once fixed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit/regression test (or a documented manual calculation in code review) demonstrates that for an 8-minute error burst followed by recovery, the rewritten `OPNsenseEndpointErrors` expression + `for:` combination does NOT fire (i.e. the condition stops being true well before the `for` duration elapses).
- [ ] The rewritten expression still fires for genuinely sustained errors (e.g. errors continuously present for the full 15+ minutes), preserving true-positive detection.
- [ ] The same fix (short window for the alert expression, long `for:` duration) is applied to the `opnsense_unbound_dns_answers_bogus_total` rule at `build_rules.py:128`, or a follow-up issue is filed if intentionally deferred.
- [ ] The rendered annotation text in `grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml` accurately describes the new semantics (no longer claims errors were "continuous for 15m" if that isn't what the expression checks).
- [ ] `make rules` is re-run and the regenerated `grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml` is committed alongside the `build_rules.py` change.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `586563a` (straight to main).

Shortened the alert-condition window to `increase(opnsense_exporter_endpoint_errors_total[2m]) > 0` while keeping `for: 15m`, so `for` now measures how long errors *persist*:

- **8-minute burst then recovery** (the router-reboot case): `increase[2m] > 0` is true only ~t=0..10m (<15m), so `for:15m` never elapses → **no fire**. ✅
- **Sustained errors** (continuous for 15m+): every rolling 2m window stays non-empty → condition true past 15m → **still fires**. ✅ (true positive preserved)

Annotation text corrected to describe the real semantics. Regenerated `grafana/alerts/grafana-managed/opnsense-endpoint-errors.json` via `make rules`.

**Unbound DNSSEC-bogus rule (`build_rules.py:129`):** left unchanged — it uses `for:0` with a `>5`-count-in-15m threshold, i.e. a legitimate count-in-window alert that fires immediately; there is no `for`-duration for the 15m window to distort, so the #94 defect doesn't apply. Documented inline rather than filing a follow-up.

Gate: `make rules` regenerated, `make docs-check` green (556 metrics), `make test` green.
