body:
## Problem

The API-contract canary (`cmd/apicontract`) classifies GET->POST verb drift — the exact class of change caused by CVE-2026-30868-style tightening of OPNsense diagnostic endpoints — as a `Warning`, not an `Error`. `HasErrors()` only inspects `report.Errors`, so a run containing only verb-drift warnings exits 0. The GitHub Actions workflow that runs this canary weekly gates both issue-filing and job failure on the `drift` output, which is set to `true` only when the tool exits 1 (i.e. only on missing/added endpoints, never on verb drift). The result: a scheduled run that detects an endpoint being tightened from GET to POST finishes green, with the finding visible only inside `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` of that run — nothing files or updates an issue, nothing fails, and nobody is notified.

Worse, the same `drift` boolean (which ignores warnings) also drives a "close drift issue when clean" step. That step will close an existing open api-drift issue with a "cleared" comment purely because `Errors` is empty, even if the current run still has live verb-drift warnings. So the failure mode is not just silent burial of a new finding — it can actively mislabel a still-open drift issue as resolved.

## Evidence

- `cmd/apicontract/main.go:9` — doc comment: "Verb drift is reported but does not change the exit code." Exit code (`os.Exit(1)`) is gated solely on `HasErrors(reports)`.
- `cmd/apicontract/report.go:9-16` — `HasErrors()` inspects only `r.Errors`; `r.Warnings` is never checked.
- `cmd/apicontract/diff.go:92-104` (verb-drift append block itself is `diff.go:96-104`, with context/docstring at `92-95`) — comment explicitly names the motivating scenario: "the CVE-2026-30868 GET->POST tightening class." The finding is appended to `rep.Warnings`, not `rep.Errors`. Confirmed also by `cmd/apicontract/diff_test.go:48-56` (`TestDiffVerbMismatchIsWarning`), which asserts by design that "verb drift must not be an error."
- `.github/workflows/api-contract.yml:103-115` — the "Run contract diff" step sets `drift=true` only in the branch taken when `apicontract` exits 1; a warnings-only run exits 0, so `drift=false` is emitted.
- `.github/workflows/api-contract.yml:126` — the "Open or update drift issue" step is gated on `steps.diff.outputs.drift == 'true'`, so it never fires for a warnings-only run. The workflow's final "Fail the job on drift" step is gated the same way. The report content is only appended to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.
- Also in `api-contract.yml`: the "Close drift issue when clean" step is gated on `drift == 'false' && schedule`, so it can post a "cleared" comment and close an existing api-drift issue even while verb-drift warnings are still present in the same run.

Not livebox-validated (this is a CI/workflow-logic defect, not something exercisable against a live OPNsense box).

## Failure scenario / impact

OPNsense stable/26.7 tightens a diagnostics endpoint the exporter currently GETs to POST-only — exactly the CVE-2026-30868 class the code's own comments cite as the reason this check exists. The weekly scheduled canary run detects the drift, prints a warning table into the job's step summary, and completes with `conclusion=success` — no issue is filed, no step fails, no notification is sent. If a prior api-drift issue happened to be open for an unrelated reason, that same run can close it with an automated "cleared" comment, even though the verb-drift warning is still live. Users who upgrade the exporter's OPNsense target to the newer release get runtime 405s on the affected collector, despite the canary having observed the drift weeks in advance.

## Suggested direction

Keep the exit-code-0 behavior for verb drift if low-noise-by-design is desired, but make the workflow open or update the api-drift issue whenever the report contains warnings — for example, add a `warnings=true` output from `apicontract` (or grep the report for the verb-drift table) and use it (in addition to `drift`) to gate issue creation/update, and to prevent the "close when clean" step from firing while any warnings are present.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test asserts that `apicontract`'s report/output surface exposes a distinct signal (e.g. a `warnings` boolean/output) that is `true` when `rep.Warnings` is non-empty, independent of `HasErrors()`.
- [ ] A workflow-level check (or a test harness simulating the step outputs) confirms the "Open or update drift issue" step fires when the diff step reports warnings-only (no errors), not only when `drift == 'true'`.
- [ ] A workflow-level check confirms the "Close drift issue when clean" step does NOT fire (or does not close/comment "cleared") when warnings are present, even if `Errors` is empty.
- [ ] `TestDiffVerbMismatchIsWarning` (or an equivalent test) continues to pass unmodified, confirming verb drift still does not force a hard CI failure via exit code.
- [ ] A regression test simulates a GET->POST verb-drift-only diff end to end and asserts an issue-filing/update path is triggered (not just a step-summary write).

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `e8cfff8`.

- **`report.go`**: new `HasWarnings(reps)` (independent of `HasErrors`) + `GitHubOutputs(reps)` rendering `drift=<HasErrors>\nwarnings=<HasWarnings>\n`.
- **`main.go`**: appends `GitHubOutputs` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` when set; exit code still gated on `HasErrors` only (verb drift stays exit 0 — `TestDiffVerbMismatchIsWarning` unchanged, #4).
- **`api-contract.yml`**: the diff step no longer sets `drift` from the exit code (apicontract writes both outputs itself); "Open or update drift issue" now fires on `drift == 'true' || warnings == 'true'` (#2); "Close drift issue when clean" requires `drift == 'false' && warnings == 'false'` (#3); "Fail the job" still gated on `drift` only.

**Tests:** `TestHasWarningsIndependentOfErrors` (#1), `TestGitHubOutputsWarningsOnly` (warnings-only→`drift=false/warnings=true`, missing→`true/false`, clean→`false/false`). **End-to-end (#5):** built apicontract, generated a full 107-endpoint upstream from the manifest with one GET flipped to POST-only, ran with `GITHUB_OUTPUT` set → exit 0, file contains `drift=false\nwarnings=true` (issue-filing path triggered). `actionlint` passes. Gate: `make test`, `make lint` (0 issues), `make docs-check`.

body:
## Problem

The OTLP exporter option-parsing code in `internal/options/otlp.go` has three related gaps that all cause the same class of failure: a config that *looks* valid at startup silently produces broken or unintended telemetry export behaviour instead of a fatal, obvious error.

1. `OTLPConfig.Validate` only treats the explicit `--otlp.insecure` flag as "insecure" when checking for a conflict with TLS material (`--otlp.tls-ca-file`, `--otlp.tls-cert-file`, etc). But the OTel SDK independently derives insecurity from the endpoint URL scheme in `WithEndpointURL` (`u.Scheme != "https"`), which runs *after* `Validate`. So `--otlp.endpoint=http://collector:4318` plus a TLS file passes `Validate` cleanly, then fails at exporter construction with `errInsecureEndpointWithTLS`. This is exactly the "non-fatal start failure that silently disables export" the existing check's own comment says it exists to prevent.
2. The `--otlp.protocol` help text and generated docs claim that an empty value "defers to `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`", but the vendored OTel Go SDK never reads that environment variable anywhere (`grep -rn OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL vendor/` returns zero hits). The exporter's own switch statement (`case "http/protobuf", "":`) has already committed to building the HTTP exporter before any such deferral could happen, so the documented behaviour is unreachable — empty always means HTTP/protobuf, silently, regardless of what the operator's environment sets.
3. `parseHeaders` silently discards any `--otlp.headers` segment that doesn't contain `=` (e.g. a colon typo, or garbage) via a bare `continue`, with no error or log. If parsing yields zero pairs, `Headers` is set to `nil`. Downstream, the exporter only calls `WithHeaders` when `len(cfg.Headers) > 0`, so a nil/empty map is indistinguishable from "flag never set" — at which point the OTel SDK falls back to reading `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` itself, directly inverting the documented "when set, replaces `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` entirely" contract.

All three share a root cause: `Validate`/`parseHeaders` model the config too leniently/narrowly compared to what the underlying OTel SDK actually does, so genuine operator mistakes pass validation and only surface later as silent, non-fatal telemetry breakage.

## Evidence

**1. Scheme-derived insecure bypasses the TLS conflict check**
- `internal/options/otlp.go:103-109` — `Validate` rejects `--otlp.insecure` + TLS files, with a comment stating this must be a "fatal, obvious config error" because "the http exporter rejects this at construction (a non-fatal start failure that would silently disable export)".
- `vendor/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp/internal/oconf/options.go:298` — `cfg.Metrics.Insecure = u.Scheme != "https"`, derived from `WithEndpointURL`, independent of the `--otlp.insecure` flag.
- `vendor/.../otlpmetrichttp/client.go:71` — returns `errInsecureEndpointWithTLS` when `Insecure && TLSCfg != nil`.
- `internal/telemetry/exporter.go:81-92` — applies `WithEndpointURL` then `WithTLSClientConfig`, so the conflict is only detected here, after `Validate` has already passed.
- `internal/telemetry/provider.go:35-38` and `main.go:397-398` — the resulting construction error is logged ("failed to start otlp metrics export") but does not call `os.Exit`; the process keeps running with OTLP export silently disabled.
- Independently reproduced by the verifier: `otlpmetrichttp.New(WithEndpointURL("http://collector:4318"), WithTLSClientConfig(tc))` returns `"insecure HTTP endpoint cannot use TLS client configuration"`.
- Note: the grpc variant does NOT have this problem — grpc's oconf prioritizes `GRPCCredentials` over `Insecure` (options.go:150-153), so TLS material is honored, not silently dropped. Scope this fix to the http/protobuf path only.

**2. `--otlp.protocol` empty-string fallback claim is false**
- `internal/options/otlp.go:24` — help text: "When empty, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` is used", propagated into `docs/configuration.md:141` and `:342` via docgen.
- `internal/telemetry/exporter.go:79` — `case "http/protobuf", "":` unconditionally builds the http exporter for an empty protocol value.
- `grep -rn OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL vendor/` — zero hits anywhere under `vendor/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/`; the Go SDK selects protocol via which package is imported, not via that env var.
- `internal/options/otlp_test.go:32` — comment "empty protocol ok (sdk fallthrough)" codifies the same false belief in the test suite.
- Verifier confirmed both `--otlp.protocol=""` and `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=""` parse through kingpin to an actual empty string (no fallback to the flag's own default).

**3. `parseHeaders` silently drops malformed pairs**
- `internal/options/otlp.go:136-154` — pairs without `=` hit `continue` with no error or log.
- `internal/options/otlp.go:192-194` — sets `Headers = nil` when the resulting map is empty.
- `internal/telemetry/exporter.go:72-74` and `:87-89` — `WithHeaders` is only applied `if len(cfg.Headers) > 0`.
- `vendor/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp/config.go:157-165` — documents that omitting `WithHeaders` causes the SDK to read `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` itself.
- `internal/options/otlp.go:32-33` and `docs/configuration.md:139` — "When set, replaces `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` entirely."

None of these were validated against a live OPNsense box (`livebox_validated: false` for all three) — they are exporter/config-plumbing bugs, independent of OPNsense itself.

## Failure scenario / impact

1. An operator deploys with `--otlp.endpoint=http://otel-collector:4318` (http/protobuf, the default protocol) plus a deployment template that also sets `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_OTLP_TLS_CA_FILE`, but does not set `--otlp.insecure`. Startup passes config validation, then logs one non-fatal error line ("failed to start otlp metrics export") and the process runs indefinitely with OTLP export silently disabled — `/metrics` keeps serving normally, masking the problem.
2. An operator sets `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=''` intending to defer protocol selection to a platform-wide `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` env var, exactly as the flag help text suggests. The exporter silently builds an HTTP/protobuf client and sends requests to a gRPC-only collector on `:4317`; every export fails with rate-limited warnings and no metrics are ever delivered, while the visible configuration looks correct per the documentation.
3. An operator sets `OPNSENSE_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS='Authorization: Basic abc123'` (colon typo instead of `=`). Startup succeeds with no warning. `cfg.Headers` ends up `nil`, `WithHeaders` is never applied, and the OTel SDK falls back to reading `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` from the process environment directly — either sending unauthenticated requests (401s, rate-limited warn only) or, worse, silently sending a stale/different token the operator believed had been replaced.

## Suggested direction

For (1), have `Validate` (or `assembleOTLP`) parse `cfg.Endpoint` and treat a non-https scheme as insecure for the http/protobuf TLS-conflict check, producing the same fatal error as the existing `--otlp.insecure` + TLS-files case; scope this to http/protobuf since grpc already handles it correctly. For (2), either implement the `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` fallthrough for real, or drop the empty-string case entirely and make it a validation error, fixing the help text/docs and the stale test comment accordingly. For (3), make `parseHeaders` return an error for any segment missing `=` or with an empty key (and for a non-empty raw string that parses to zero pairs), surfaced as a fatal config error consistent with this file's existing "fatal, obvious config error" stance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test in `otlp_test.go` asserts that `--otlp.endpoint=http://...` (http/protobuf, default protocol) combined with any TLS file (`--otlp.tls-ca-file`, `--otlp.tls-cert-file`, `--otlp.tls-key-file`) fails `Validate` with a fatal error, even without `--otlp.insecure` set.
- [ ] A unit test confirms `--otlp.protocol=grpc` with an http:// endpoint and TLS files is unaffected (grpc path is not treated as insecure-by-scheme).
- [ ] Either a unit test asserts empty `--otlp.protocol` is rejected by `Validate` with a clear error, or (if the fallthrough is implemented) a unit test asserts empty protocol reads `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` and selects the correct exporter; the stale `otlp_test.go:32` comment ("empty protocol ok (sdk fallthrough)") is corrected to match whichever behaviour is chosen.
- [ ] `internal/options/otlp.go`'s `--otlp.protocol` help text and `docs/configuration.md` (regenerated via `make docs`) no longer claim a `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` deferral that doesn't exist, and `make docs-check` passes.
- [ ] A unit test asserts that a malformed `--otlp.headers` value (e.g. `"Authorization: Bearer x"` with no `=`, or any string with zero valid pairs) fails validation with a fatal error rather than silently producing `nil`/empty `Headers`.
- [ ] A unit test confirms well-formed `--otlp.headers` values still parse correctly and continue to replace `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` entirely, per the documented contract.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in `dcd76f3`. Three OTLP config-validation gaps closed in `internal/options/otlp.go`:

1. **Scheme-derived insecure bypass** — for `http/protobuf`, `Validate` now parses the endpoint and rejects a non-`https` scheme combined with any TLS file (`--otlp.tls-ca-file`/`-cert-file`/`-key-file`), the same fatal error as the explicit `--otlp.insecure` conflict. Scoped to http/protobuf; grpc is left untouched (its oconf prioritizes TLS creds over scheme).
2. **False protocol env-fallback** — empty `--otlp.protocol` is now a validation error (the OTel Go SDK never reads `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`). Help text + `docs/configuration.md` regenerated to drop the false claim; the stale `otlp_test.go` "sdk fallthrough" case is corrected to expect an error.
3. **Silent header drops** — `parseHeaders` now returns a fatal error for any segment missing `=`, an empty key, or a non-empty input that parses to zero pairs, instead of silently producing `nil` Headers (which let the SDK fall back to `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`). Empty input stays valid.

All six acceptance criteria covered by new/updated tests in `otlp_test.go`. Gate green: `make test`, `make lint` (0 issues), `make docs-check`.

Reopening-adjacent note (issue stays closed; the gap is fixed in c1ae453).

Found by an audit of every issue closed in the last six weeks, verifying each against the code rather than its closing comment.

Acceptance criterion 4 of this issue said the docs must no longer claim an `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` deferral that does not exist. The closing commit dcd76f3 corrected the two **generated** flag-table rows inside the `<!-- docgen:begin:flags-otlp -->` block, but the false claim also lived in **hand-written prose above the markers**, which docgen never touches:

> Any field left empty falls through to the corresponding **standard OpenTelemetry environment variable** (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`, ...)

That directly contradicted `internal/options/otlp.go`, whose own comment says the SDK "never reads" that variable and whose `Validate` rejects an empty protocol outright.

While fixing it I found a **second** false entry in the same sentence that this issue never mentioned: `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL`. `--otlp.export-interval` defaults to `60s` and is always passed explicitly to `sdkmetric.WithInterval`, so that env var can never apply either — false for a different reason (always-set, not rejected).

Verified which entries are genuinely true and kept them:

| env var | falls through? | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | yes | `--otlp.endpoint` defaults to `""` |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` | yes | `--otlp.headers` defaults to `""` |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | yes | `buildResource` guards on `cfg.ServiceName != ""` |
| `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` | yes | `resource.WithFromEnv()`, no competing flag |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` | **no** | empty is a startup error (`otlp.go:96-99`) |
| `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL` | **no** | always passed via `WithInterval` (`provider.go:65-67`) |

Fixed in c1ae453. `make docs-check` passes — the corrected prose is outside the docgen markers, so it is hand-maintained and will not be regenerated away.

**Lesson worth keeping:** `make docs` regenerates the marker blocks only. A false claim in surrounding prose survives every regeneration, so "the docs were regenerated" is not evidence that a docs criterion was met.

body:
## Problem

`FetchPFStatistics` and `FetchSystemResources` each aggregate several independent sub-endpoint calls, and both deliberately tolerate partial failure: they only return a non-nil error when *every* sub-call fails (`if failCount == len(results) { return data, firstErr }`). This partial tolerance is intentional and correct for the map-typed sections (Counters, MemoryLimits, Timeouts, Disks, Swaps) — those stay `nil` when their source call fails and the collectors correctly skip emitting them.

The bug is that several scalar fields are populated by a *single* sub-call each, and the collectors emit those scalars **unconditionally**, with no success guard. If the one sub-call backing a scalar field fails while others succeed, the struct field is left at its Go zero value, the fetcher still returns a nil error, and the collector emits the zero as a real Prometheus sample — indistinguishable from a genuine value of zero. This affects `state_table_entries`/`searches`/`inserts`/`removals`/`source_tracking_entries` (from `fetchPFStatsInfo`) and `memory_total_bytes`/`memory_used_bytes`/`uptime_seconds`/`load_average` (from `fetchSystemMemory`/`fetchSystemTime`). Notably, the same files already contain the correct pattern for this exact problem (`HasArc` gating `memoryArc`, and the `>0` guard on `configLastChange`) — it just wasn't applied to these fields.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/pf_statistics.go:180-184` — `FetchPFStatistics` returns nil error unless `failCount == len(results)`.
- `opnsense/pf_statistics.go:71-76` — all five PF scalar fields are populated solely by `fetchPFStatsInfo`; if that one call fails while `pfStatsMemory`/`pfStatsTimeouts` succeed, the scalars stay zero.
- `internal/collector/pf_stats.go:99-128` — five `MustNewConstMetric` calls for the scalar fields, no success guard.
- `opnsense/system_resources.go:432-436` — `FetchSystemResources` has the same nil-unless-all-failed pattern.
- `opnsense/system_resources.go` (`fetchSystemMemory`, `fetchSystemTime`) — `memory_total`/`memory_used` and `uptime`/`load_average` each come from one independent sub-call.
- `internal/collector/system.go:117-166` — memory, uptime, and three load-average series emitted unconditionally; contrast with the same file's existing guard patterns: `HasArc` gating `memoryArc` (`system.go:130`) and the `>0` guard on `configLastChange` (`system.go:168`).

This has not been reproduced against a live box (`livebox_validated: false`); the finding was adversarially verified by static re-read of all cited spans at HEAD.

## Failure scenario / impact

A transient 500/timeout on the OPNsense `diagnostics/system`/`systemTime` endpoint while `systemDisk` succeeds causes `opnsense_system_uptime_seconds` to report `0` for that scrape — this reads as a host reboot and can fire false "host rebooted" alerts. In the same scrape, `memory_total_bytes=0` breaks any used/total memory ratio panel (division by zero).

Similarly, if `pfStatsInfo` fails while `pfStatsMemory` succeeds, `state_table_searches_total` (a live counter, e.g. sitting at 471,141,925) drops to `0` for one scrape and recovers on the next. Because this metric is a Prometheus counter, `rate()`/`increase()` over that scrape interval records a phantom ~471M counter-reset spike, corrupting dashboards and any alerting built on those functions.

## Suggested direction

Track per-section success flags for these scalar-producing sub-calls (mirroring the `HasArc` pattern already used in the same files) and have the collectors skip emitting a scalar/series whose backing sub-call failed, preserving the existing partial-tolerance behavior without fabricating zero values.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test for `FetchPFStatistics` simulates `pfStatsInfo` failing while `pfStatsMemory`/`pfStatsTimeouts` succeed, and asserts the returned data exposes that the info-derived scalars are unavailable (not silently zero).
- [ ] A unit test for the PF stats collector asserts that when the info-derived fields are unavailable, `state_table_entries`, `state_table_searches_total`, `state_table_inserts_total`, `state_table_removals_total`, and `source_tracking_entries` are NOT emitted for that scrape.
- [ ] A unit test for `FetchSystemResources` simulates `fetchSystemMemory` failing while other sub-calls succeed, and asserts memory fields are marked unavailable rather than zero.
- [ ] A unit test for `fetchSystemTime` failing asserts `uptime_seconds` and the three `load_average` series are NOT emitted for that scrape.
- [ ] A unit test confirms that when ALL sub-calls for a given fetch succeed, all scalars are emitted as before (no regression to the happy path).
- [ ] `make test` passes with the new guards in place, and existing partial-failure tolerance (map-typed sections silently skipped) remains unchanged.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in 47145c2. Added per-section availability flags mirroring the existing `HasArc`/`configLastChange>0` guards:

- `PFStatistics.InfoAvailable` — set true only when the `pfStatsInfo` sub-call succeeds. The collector now gates `state_table_entries`/`_searches`/`_inserts`/`_removals` and `source_tracking_entries` on it, so a partial failure no longer emits a zeroed counter (which `rate()` would read as a ~500M reset).
- `SystemMemory.Available` / `SystemTime.Available` — set true only when `fetchSystemMemory`/`fetchSystemTime` respectively succeed. `memory_total_bytes`/`memory_used_bytes` are gated on the former, `uptime_seconds` + the three `load_average` series on the latter — so a transient systemTime failure no longer reports uptime=0 (false "host rebooted") or memory=0 (ratio-panel div-by-zero).

Partial-tolerance for the map-typed sections (Counters/MemoryLimits/Timeouts/Disks/Swaps) is unchanged, and the all-success happy path emits everything as before.

Coverage: extended `TestFetchPFStatistics_PartialFailure` (asserts InfoAvailable=false) + new `TestPFStatsCollector_Update_InfoUnavailable`; extended `TestFetchSystemResources_PartialFailure` (asserts Memory.Available=true, Time.Available=false) + new `TestSystemCollector_Update_TimeUnavailable`. `make test`/`make lint`/`make docs-check` green; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

`FetchUnboundOverview` (`opnsense/unbound_dns.go`) unmarshals the unbound-control stats response into `unboundDNSStatusResponse`, which carries a `Status string \`json:"status"\`` field, but the function never checks that field before parsing. When OPNsense's `statsAction()` controller can't reach `unbound-control` (unbound stopped/restarting/socket hiccup), it returns HTTP 200 with `{"status":"failed"}` and no `data` key at all. Because the exporter's response parsing treats any 2xx + valid JSON as success, and `Data` simply stays a zero-valued struct when absent, the collector proceeds to emit the full set of ~60 unbound metrics (uptime, cache, memory, per-rcode, per-type, per-flag counters) all as zero instead of erroring out or emitting nothing.

This is a real-world condition, not a hypothetical edge case: OPNsense boxes running dnsmasq/forwarders instead of Unbound have it permanently disabled, so this collector runs unconditionally (it is default-on, no plugin/404 gating applies since Unbound is core) and emits bogus zero series forever. On boxes where Unbound is enabled, any transient unbound-control failure or restart produces a single-scrape dip to zero on every counter, which corrupts `rate()`/`increase()` queries in Prometheus with phantom resets.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/unbound_dns.go:4` — `unboundDNSStatusResponse` struct defines `Status string json:"status"` but it is unused by the parsing logic.
- `opnsense/unbound_dns.go:270-393` — `FetchUnboundOverview` unmarshals the response and returns `data, nil` without ever checking `response.Status`; when `Data` is absent, all fields default to zero and are passed through `safeAtoi`/`safeParseFloat`.
- `internal/collector/unbound_dns.go:266-457` — emits every uptime/counter/type/rcode/flag/cache/memory series unconditionally from the fetched data, before the collector separately fetches service running-state at line 473 (so it already has the means to detect "unbound not running" but doesn't use it to gate these metrics).
- `internal/options/collectors.go:362` and `main.go:82` — `unbound_dns` is a default-on collector (`exporter.disable-unbound`), so it runs on every box, including dnsmasq-only ones with Unbound fully disabled.
- Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: reading `Unbound/Api/DiagnosticsController.php` `statsAction()` on-box shows `$ret['status'] = "failed"; ... if ($result != null) { $ret['status'] = "ok"; $ret['data'] = $result; }` — on failure the response is exactly `{"status":"failed"}` with no `data` key, at HTTP 200.

```go
// opnsense/unbound_dns.go (struct definition)
type unboundDNSStatusResponse struct {
	Status string `json:"status"`
	Data   ...
}
```

## Failure scenario / impact

1. A box runs dnsmasq or another forwarder with Unbound stopped/disabled. Every scrape of `unbound-control` stats returns `{"status":"failed"}`. The exporter permanently exposes ~60 zero-valued `opnsense_unbound_*` series as if Unbound were running with zero traffic, misleading dashboards and alerts that assume these metrics reflect real DNS activity.
2. On a box where Unbound is normally enabled, a transient failure of `unbound-control` (e.g. during a service restart or socket hiccup) causes a single scrape to report all counters as 0. Any `rate()`/`increase()` query over `opnsense_unbound_queries_total` (or similar monotonic counters) sees a spurious reset-to-zero-and-back, producing an artificial spike/dip in derived rate graphs and potentially tripping alerts.

## Suggested direction

Check `response.Status != "ok"` in `FetchUnboundOverview` and, on failure, either return an error (e.g. an `APICallError`, surfacing as `scrape_success=0`) or a "not present" sentinel so the collector skips emitting these series entirely for that scrape, consistent with how other collectors handle degraded/absent data. `FetchUnboundInfra` has the same unchecked `Status` field but currently degrades harmlessly to an empty list, so it may not need the same treatment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test feeds `FetchUnboundOverview` a mocked `{"status":"failed"}` response (no `data` key) and asserts it returns an error (or another explicit non-success signal), not a zero-valued struct with `nil` error.
- [ ] A unit test confirms that when `FetchUnboundOverview` signals failure, `internal/collector/unbound_dns.go`'s `Update()` does not emit any of the uptime/cache/memory/rcode/type/flag series for that scrape (rather than emitting them as zero).
- [ ] A unit test confirms the existing "status": "ok" success path is unaffected and still parses/emits all fields as before.
- [ ] `go test ./opnsense/... ./internal/collector/...` passes with the new tests included.
- [ ] Manual/regression check: a scrape against a live box with Unbound disabled either surfaces `scrape_success=0` for the collector or exposes no `opnsense_unbound_*` series, but never a full set of zero-valued series.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in c6b652e. `FetchUnboundOverview` now checks the status envelope: `Present` is set only when `status == "ok"`. When unbound-control is unreachable (`{"status":"failed"}`, no data key — Unbound stopped/restarting, or disabled on a dnsmasq-only box) it returns `Present=false` with no error, and the collector returns early — emitting **only** `opnsense_unbound_service_running` (so operators still see Unbound is down) and none of the ~60 uptime/cache/memory/rcode/type/flag stats series. That kills both the permanent-zero-series problem on dnsmasq-only boxes and the phantom rate() resets during transient unbound-control hiccups.

Chose the Present-sentinel over erroring (which would flip scrape_success=0 and log every 15s on a box that has legitimately disabled Unbound). `FetchUnboundInfra` left as-is per the issue (degrades harmlessly to empty list).

Coverage: `TestFetchUnboundOverview_StatusFailed` (fetch → Present=false, no error) and `TestUnboundDNSCollector_Update_StatsUnavailable` (collector emits exactly 1 metric = service_running). Success path unchanged (72-metric collector test still green). `go test ./opnsense/... ./internal/collector/...` green; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

`opnsense/ntp.go` parses the ntpq `when` and `poll` columns with `safeParseFloat`, which silently returns `0` on any parse error. ntpq's `prettyinterval` formatting switches these columns from plain seconds to unit-suffixed strings ("34m", "12h", "3d") once the interval exceeds 2048 seconds, and OPNsense's `ntpd_status.php` passes the `ntpq -pnw` columns straight through without normalizing units. The only special case handled today is the literal `"-"` for `when`; any suffixed value falls through to `safeParseFloat`, fails `strconv.ParseFloat`, and is coerced to `0`.

The practical effect is that the metric meant to represent "seconds since this peer last responded" flips from a large, climbing number to `0` — the encoding for "responded just now" — at exactly the moment a peer goes stale enough to matter. This inverts the staleness signal for any dashboard or alert built on `opnsense_ntp_peer_when_seconds`. The codebase already has prior art for this exact class of bug: `opnsense/chrony.go`'s `parseChronyInterval` helper handles m/h/d/y suffixes for chrony's analogous fields, but that fix was never ported to the NTP peer parsing path.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/ntp.go:61-64` — only `"-"` is special-cased before parsing `When`:
  ```go
  if row.When != "-" {
      whenSeconds = safeParseFloat(row.When)
  }
  ```
- `opnsense/ntp.go:84` — `Poll` is parsed unconditionally: `PollSeconds: safeParseFloat(row.Poll)`
- `opnsense/utils.go:117-123` — `safeParseFloat` returns `0.0` on any `strconv.ParseFloat` error, with no distinction between "zero" and "unparseable".
- `internal/collector/ntp.go:124-134` — `WhenSeconds`/`PollSeconds` are emitted directly to the `peer_when_seconds`/`peer_poll_seconds` Prometheus gauges with no intermediate clamping or validity guard.
- `opnsense/ntp_test.go` has no test case for a suffixed `when`/`poll` value — only `"-"`, plain numeric, and octal-reach cases are covered.
- Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: `/usr/local/opnsense/scripts/ntpd/ntpd_status.php` does `$server['when'] = $peerinfo[4];`, a raw passthrough of the `ntpq -pnw` column with no unit normalization server-side. The live sample currently shows `when="24"` (healthy, small numeric), consistent with the suffix form only appearing once a peer has been unreachable for more than roughly 34 minutes.

## Failure scenario / impact

An upstream NTP peer becomes unreachable. Its `when` counter (seconds since last received packet) grows normally at first, but once it exceeds 2048 seconds ntpq renders it as e.g. `"41m"` instead of a plain integer. `safeParseFloat("41m")` fails to parse and returns `0`, so `opnsense_ntp_peer_when_seconds` drops from ~2048 straight to `0` and stays there for as long as the outage continues — the metric now claims the peer responded an instant ago, during the exact outage window it exists to detect. Any alert rule keyed on "time since last peer response exceeds threshold" will silently stop firing (or never fire) for that peer. The `poll` column is subject to the same coercion but is far less likely to hit the >2048s suffix threshold in practice (typical poll intervals top out around 1024s / maxpoll ~10), so the `when` column is the primary, load-bearing instance of the bug.

## Suggested direction

Parse `when`/`poll` with an ntpq-interval-aware helper analogous to `chrony.go`'s existing `parseChronyInterval` (which already handles m/h/d suffixes), rather than routing straight through `safeParseFloat`. On an unparseable or `"-"` value, prefer skipping the sample or exposing an explicit validity flag over silently emitting `0`, so "unknown" is never indistinguishable from "just responded."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test in `opnsense/ntp_test.go` asserts that `when` values `"34m"`, `"12h"`, and `"3d"` parse to their correct second equivalents (2040, 43200, 259200), not `0`.
- [ ] A unit test asserts the same suffix handling for the `poll` column.
- [ ] A unit test asserts that a genuinely unparseable/unknown `when` value (e.g. `"-"` or garbage) does not produce a value indistinguishable from "responded 0 seconds ago" (either the sample is skipped or a validity flag is set).
- [ ] `go test ./opnsense/... ./internal/collector/...` passes with the new coverage.
- [ ] No existing numeric or `"-"` test cases in `opnsense/ntp_test.go` regress.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in f9001f0. Added a suffix-aware `parseNTPInterval` helper (mirroring `chrony.go`'s `parseChronyInterval`) that converts m/h/d-suffixed values to seconds — `34m`→2040, `12h`→43200, `3d`→259200 — and returns an `ok` bool. `NTPPeer` now carries `WhenValid`/`PollValid`; on `-` or garbage the value is flagged invalid and the collector **skips** `opnsense_ntp_peer_when_seconds`/`_poll_seconds` rather than emitting 0, so "unknown" is never indistinguishable from "responded 0s ago".

Coverage: `TestFetchNTPStatus_SuffixedWhenPoll` (suffix→seconds for when and poll) and `TestFetchNTPStatus_UnknownWhenNotZero` (`-`/garbage → WhenValid=false). Existing numeric and `-` cases still pass; the collector test's count dropped 17→16 because the `when=-` peer no longer emits a when sample. `go test ./opnsense/... ./internal/collector/...` green; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

`opnsense_openvpn_sessions_total` and `opnsense_openvpn_sessions_by_instance` overcount OpenVPN sessions because the exporter treats every row returned by `api/openvpn/service/search_sessions` as a connected client session. The OPNsense controller (`ServiceController::searchSessionsAction`) actually returns three kinds of rows: real per-client session rows (flagged `is_client: true`), a synthetic whole-instance row when a running server has zero connected clients, and a stub row for each enabled-but-not-running server. The exporter's `openVPNSearchSessionsResponse` struct (`opnsense/openvpn.go:19-28`) has no field for `is_client`, and both `FetchOpenVPNSessions` and the collector consume every row unconditionally, so idle or stopped server instances get counted as sessions.

This means the session-count metrics are inflated by one for every enabled OpenVPN server instance that currently has no connected clients (running-with-zero-clients, or enabled-but-stopped), independent of actual client activity.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/openvpn.go:19-28` — `openVPNSearchSessionsResponse.Rows` struct has no `is_client` field, so the client/instance/stub distinction the API provides is discarded on unmarshal.
- `opnsense/openvpn.go:89-117` (`FetchOpenVPNSessions`) — appends every row from the API response unconditionally.
- `internal/collector/openvpn.go:91-99` —
  ```go
  ch <- prometheus.MustNewConstMetric(
      c.sessionsTotal,
      prometheus.GaugeValue,
      float64(len(sessions.Rows)),
      c.instance,
  )

  sessionsByInstance := make(map[string]int)
  for _, session := range sessions.Rows {
      sessionsByInstance[session.Description]++
  }
  ```
  counts `len(sessions.Rows)` and increments `sessionsByInstance` for every row, with no filtering.
- Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box's controller source at `/usr/local/opnsense/mvc/app/controllers/OPNsense/OpenVPN/Api/ServiceController.php`, `searchSessionsAction` (~lines 72-133): client rows are appended with `is_client => true` when `client_list` is non-empty; when a running instance's `client_list` is empty the instance row itself is appended (no `is_client` flag); enabled-but-not-running servers additionally get a stub row appended in a separate loop. None of these non-client rows carry `is_client: true`.

## Failure scenario / impact

A box with one enabled OpenVPN server and zero connected clients reports `opnsense_openvpn_sessions_total=1` (should be 0) and `opnsense_openvpn_sessions_by_instance{description="..."}=1`. A stopped-but-enabled server adds another phantom count of 1. With `--exporter.enable-openvpn-details` set, the per-session `sessions` detail metric also emits a phantom row for each of these with empty real/virtual address fields. Any dashboard or alert built on session count is permanently skewed upward by the number of idle/stopped OpenVPN instances, independent of real client traffic.

## Suggested direction

Add an `is_client` field (as a flexible bool, matching the pattern used elsewhere in this codebase for API fields that vary in JSON type) to the sessions row struct, and filter `FetchOpenVPNSessions`/the collector to only count and emit rows where `is_client` is true. Consider surfacing the discarded instance/stub rows as a separate per-instance running/stopped status metric instead of dropping the information.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test with a fixture response containing a client row (`is_client: true`), a zero-client running-instance row, and a stopped-server stub row asserts `opnsense_openvpn_sessions_total` counts only the client row.
- [ ] The same fixture asserts `opnsense_openvpn_sessions_by_instance` excludes counts from the non-client rows.
- [ ] With `--exporter.enable-openvpn-details` enabled, the same fixture asserts the `sessions` detail metric emits only the real client row, not the instance/stub rows.
- [ ] `opnsense/openvpn.go`'s session struct decodes the API's `is_client` field without breaking existing fixtures that lack it (defaults to false/non-client).
- [ ] `make test` passes with the new fixture-based coverage.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in a0b9c70. Added an `is_client` field (`flexBool`, defaults false when absent) to the sessions row struct and `FetchOpenVPNSessions` now skips any row that isn't a real client row. So the synthetic zero-client running-instance row and the enabled-but-stopped stub row no longer count toward `opnsense_openvpn_sessions_total` / `opnsense_openvpn_sessions_by_instance`, and (with `--exporter.enable-openvpn-details`) the per-session `sessions` detail metric no longer emits phantom rows with empty address fields.

Filtering at the fetch layer means the collector needed no change. Coverage: new `TestFetchOpenVPNSessions_FiltersNonClientRows` (fetch layer) and `TestOpenVPNCollector_Update_ExcludesNonClientRows` (collector: asserts total=1, one by-instance series, one detail row from a client + idle + stopped fixture). Existing session fixtures were updated to carry `is_client:true` on their genuine client rows (they represent connected clients). No metric/label shape change; 556 metrics unchanged.

body:
## Problem

Four plugin-gated sub-collectors — `dhcpv4`, `acme`, `smart`, and `dyndns` — violate the exporter's own convention for handling a missing OPNsense plugin. When the underlying OPNsense REST endpoint 404s (i.e. the plugin isn't installed), the `opnsense/` fetch layer correctly maps that into an empty, zero-value data struct with a `nil` error (mirroring `FetchACMECertificates`'s documented intent), but none of the four data structs carry a `Present`/absence signal. Their `Update()` methods in `internal/collector/` therefore cannot distinguish "plugin absent" from "plugin present with zero items," and unconditionally emit `*_total` gauges as `0`.

This directly contradicts the pattern already established elsewhere in the same codebase: `internal/collector/dhcpv6.go`, `tailscale.go`, and nine other collectors (apcupsd, captiveportal, chrony, crowdsec, frr, haproxy, monit, nginx, nut) gate emission on a presence signal and stay completely silent when the plugin is absent. It also contradicts the exporter's own flag help text (`internal/options/collectors.go`), which explicitly promises these collectors are "silent when the plugin is absent," and a comment in `opnsense/smart.go` making the same false claim.

For `dyndns` specifically, there's a second, compounding bug: `internal/collector/dyndns.go` calls the non-`Optional` variant `client.FetchServiceStatus("dyndnsServiceStatus")` without any presence guard, so on a box without `os-ddclient` this 404s every scrape and logs `failed to fetch dyndns service status` at `Warn` level — at a 15s scrape interval that's roughly 5,760 warn-log lines per day for a subsystem that doesn't exist on the box.

## Evidence

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box (dhcpv4/acme endpoints 404 on this box; dyndns/smart mechanism confirmed by direct code inspection and reproduced in a throwaway build).

- `opnsense/dhcpv4.go:82-85` — `FetchDHCPv4Leases` maps 404 to zero-value struct + `nil`, no `Present` field.
- `internal/collector/dhcpv4.go:74-97` — `Update()` unconditionally emits `opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_total`, `opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_reserved_total`, `opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_dynamic_total`.
- `opnsense/acme_client.go:65-80` — `FetchACMECertificates` same 404-swallowing pattern.
- `internal/collector/acme.go:77-88` — unconditionally emits `opnsense_acme_certificates_total`.
- `opnsense/smart.go:134-166` — `FetchSMARTDevices` same pattern; comment at `smart.go:162-166` falsely claims the collector "stays quiet on boxes without the plugin."
- `internal/collector/smart.go:129-139` — unconditionally emits `opnsense_smart_devices_total`.
- `opnsense/dyndns.go:69-81` — `FetchDynDNSAccounts` same pattern.
- `internal/collector/dyndns.go:69-80` — unconditionally emits `opnsense_dyndns_accounts_total`.
- `internal/collector/dyndns.go:127-130` — calls non-optional `client.FetchServiceStatus("dyndnsServiceStatus")` with no presence guard (contrast: 9 other collectors use the purpose-built `FetchServiceStatusOptional` for exactly this reason; `tailscale.go:105-109` gates on `data.Present` before ever probing service status).
- Contrast/intended pattern: `internal/collector/dhcpv6.go:94-99` gates on a nil-map sentinel and returns early — its own comment incorrectly claims dhcpv4 uses "the same approach."
- Flag docs asserting (falsely) that these collectors are silent when absent: `internal/options/collectors.go:120` (dhcpv4), `:128` (acme), `:132` (smart), `:136` (dyndns).

Live-box `/metrics` output with the ISC dhcpv4 and acme plugins absent (both endpoints 404):
```
opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_total{...} 0
opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_reserved_total{...} 0
opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_dynamic_total{...} 0
opnsense_acme_certificates_total{...} 0
```
For comparison, `dhcpv6` (also 404 on this box) correctly emits nothing for the leases metrics.

## Failure scenario / impact

On any modern Kea/dnsmasq-based OPNsense box (ISC DHCP is deprecated and commonly absent — true of the live box tested), dashboards and alerts see `opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_total == 0` and cannot tell "feature absent" from "feature present with zero leases." An alert such as "DHCP leases dropped to 0" fires permanently and an `absent()`-based alerting rule is defeated. The same applies to `opnsense_acme_certificates_total` on boxes without `os-acme-client` and `opnsense_smart_devices_total` on boxes without `os-smart`. On any box without `os-ddclient`, the exporter additionally emits a `Warn`-level log line ("failed to fetch dyndns service status") on every single scrape — roughly 5,760 lines/day at a 15s interval — purely because the collector probes a service status endpoint for a plugin that isn't installed.

## Suggested direction

Give the four fetchers (`FetchDHCPv4Leases`, `FetchACMECertificates`, `FetchSMARTDevices`, `FetchDynDNSAccounts`) an absence signal — either a `Present bool` field (mirroring the other 9 gated collectors) or the nil-map sentinel already used by `dhcpv6.go` — and return early from each collector's `Update()` when absent, matching the `tailscale.go`/`dhcpv6.go` pattern. Switch `dyndns.go` to `FetchServiceStatusOptional`. Fix the stale/false comments in `dhcpv6.go:94-97` and `smart.go:162-166`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test `TestDhcpv4Collector_Update_PluginAbsent` (mirroring the existing `dhcpv6`/`frr` pattern) asserts zero metrics are emitted when `FetchDHCPv4Leases` signals plugin-absent.
- [ ] Equivalent `TestAcmeCollector_Update_PluginAbsent`, `TestSmartCollector_Update_PluginAbsent`, and `TestDyndnsCollector_Update_PluginAbsent` tests each assert zero metrics on plugin-absent.
- [ ] A test asserts that on plugin-absent dyndns, no `FetchServiceStatus` warn log is emitted (i.e. `FetchServiceStatusOptional` or an equivalent guard is used).
- [ ] `internal/collector/dhcpv6.go`'s comment no longer falsely claims dhcpv4 uses the same silence approach, and `opnsense/smart.go`'s comment no longer falsely claims the smart collector stays quiet on plugin-absent boxes.
- [ ] Manual/integration verification: scraping `/metrics` against a box (or mocked 404 responses) with dhcpv4/acme/smart/dyndns plugins absent produces no `opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_total`, `opnsense_acme_certificates_total`, `opnsense_smart_devices_total`, or `opnsense_dyndns_accounts_total` series at all.
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72

_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in 52a72d8. Added a `Present bool` to each of the four data structs (`DHCPv4Leases`, `ACMECertificates`, `SMARTDevices`, `DynDNSAccounts`), set true only when the endpoint actually responds (a 404 leaves it false), and each collector's `Update()` now returns early when `!Present` — so no `opnsense_dhcpv4_leases_total`, `opnsense_acme_certificates_total`, `opnsense_smart_devices_total`, or `opnsense_dyndns_accounts_total` series are emitted at all on a box missing the plugin. Matches the tailscale/dhcpv6 precedent.

dyndns additionally switched its service-status probe from `FetchServiceStatus` to `FetchServiceStatusOptional`, and the early-return means it no longer even reaches that call on a plugin-absent box — killing the ~5,760 warn-lines/day (`failed to fetch dyndns service status`) at a 15s interval.

Also corrected the stale comments in `internal/collector/dhcpv6.go` (no longer claims dhcpv4 shares its nil-map mechanism) and `opnsense/smart.go` (comment now matches the now-true silence behaviour).

New tests: `TestDhcpv4Collector_Update_PluginAbsent`, `TestAcmeCollector_Update_PluginAbsent`, `TestSmartCollector_Update_PluginAbsent`, `TestDyndnsCollector_Update_PluginAbsent` (the last also asserts no service-status warn log). All assert zero metrics on 404. No metric/label change when the plugins are present; `make test`/`make lint`/`make docs-check` green (556 metrics unchanged).

body:
## Problem

`opnsense_interfaces_link_state` is documented and emitted as a strictly binary gauge ("1=up, 0=down"), but the OPNsense `api/diagnostics/traffic/interface` field it is derived from actually has three states: `"2"` = up, `"1"` = down, and `"0"` = unknown. FreeBSD reports `LINK_STATE_UNKNOWN` (encoded as `"0"`) for netgraph/point-to-point pseudo-devices such as PPPoE and tun/tailscale interfaces, which have no carrier-sense concept at all — it does not mean the interface is down.

The conversion code collapses both the genuine "down" (`"1"`) and "unknown" (`"0"`) cases into the same output value 0, and the Prometheus metric help text asserts that 0 unambiguously means "down". As a result, any interface whose kernel link state is unknown — most commonly a PPPoE WAN, which is an extremely common residential/fiber setup — is permanently reported as down even while it is fully up and actively passing traffic.

## Evidence

`opnsense/interfaces.go:110-116`:
```go
// OPNsense link state values: "2" = up, "1" = down, "0" = unknown
linkState := 0
if v.LinkState == "2" || strings.Contains(v.LinkState, "is up") {
    linkState = 1
}
```

`internal/collector/interfaces.go:110-113` declares the metric help text as strictly binary ("1=up, 0=down"); `internal/collector/interfaces.go:176` emits `float64(iface.LinkState)` unconditionally for every interface with no reconciliation against the overview endpoint's `status`/flags fields (those are only used for the separate `admin_up`/`info` metrics on a different label set).

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: pppoe0 (device for the primary AAISP PPPoE WAN, the default gateway, actively routing 67 GB rx / 59 GB tx) returns `"link state": "0"` from `api/diagnostics/traffic/interface`, while `ifconfig pppoe0` shows `UP,POINTOPOINT,RUNNING,...,LOWER_UP` with no `status:` line (the classic `LINK_STATE_UNKNOWN` signature). The gateway status API independently reports this same interface's gateway as `"status": "Online"`, `"defaultgw": true`, `"loss": "0.0 %"`. Every other (non-PPPoE) interface on the box correctly reports `"link state": "2"`.

`opnsense/interfaces_test.go` only covers `LinkState == "2"` (up) and the legacy string `"link state is down"` (down) — there is no test coverage for the numeric `"0"` or `"1"` cases, so this gap is unguarded by tests.

## Failure scenario / impact

Any OPNsense deployment with a PPPoE WAN (or another carrier-less pseudo-device such as a tun/tailscale interface) permanently exports `opnsense_interfaces_link_state{device="pppoe0"} == 0` even though the interface is healthy and passing traffic. A dashboard panel or alert built on "link_state == 0 means WAN down" fires a false positive forever, and because the value never changes, it also masks a real future outage of that same interface (there's no distinguishable transition to alert on).

## Suggested direction

Distinguish "unknown" from "down": e.g. emit 1 when the kernel reports "2" (up), skip emitting the sample (mirroring how gateway probe `~` values are already skipped elsewhere) or emit a distinct value/label when the kernel reports "0" (unknown), and update the metric help text and docs to describe the tri-state semantics. The interfaces-overview endpoint fetched by the same collector already reports pppoe0's status correctly and could serve as a fallback/cross-check signal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test with `LinkState == "0"` asserts the collector does NOT emit `link_state == 0` (down) for that interface — either the sample is skipped or a distinct non-"down" value/label is used.
- [ ] A unit test with `LinkState == "1"` (genuine down) still asserts `link_state == 0` is emitted, preserving the real-down signal.
- [ ] A unit test with `LinkState == "2"` still asserts `link_state == 1` is emitted (no regression).
- [ ] The Prometheus HELP text for `opnsense_interfaces_link_state` (and any generated docs/metrics reference produced by `make docs`) is updated to describe the unknown-state handling, and `make docs-check` passes.
- [ ] Running the exporter against the live-box fixture data for a PPPoE-backed WAN no longer reports `link_state == 0` while the interface's overview `status` is `"up"`.

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in cfd1d63. `opnsense_interfaces_link_state` is now tri-state:

- `1` = up (kernel "2")
- `0` = down (kernel "1", genuine down)
- `2` = unknown (kernel "0" — carrier-less pseudo-devices like PPPoE and tun/tailscale)

Previously both down and unknown collapsed to `0`, so a healthy PPPoE WAN read as permanently down. Now unknown maps to its own value `2`, leaving up=1/down=0 intact. **Breaking:** anything that treated `link_state==0` OR `link_state!=1` as "down" should match on `==0` only. HELP text + metrics reference updated (`make docs-check` green), and the dashboard's Link State timeline uses a dedicated tri-state mapping (Unknown = yellow) rather than the shared binary UPDOWN.

Verified against the live-box shape: pppoe0 reports kernel `"link state":"0"` while actively routing → now emits `link_state=2`, not `0`. Covered by table tests at both the fetch layer (`opnsense/interfaces_test.go`) and collector layer (`internal/collector/interfaces_test.go`).

body:
## Problem

Several collectors build Prometheus label tuples directly from OPNsense config data without any uniqueness guarantee, and the exporter's HTTP handler is configured to abort the *entire* scrape if the registry's `Gather()` ever sees a duplicate label set. In `internal/server/metrics.go:68-71`, the metrics handler is built with `promhttp.HandlerOpts{}`, whose zero value defaults `ErrorHandling` to `HTTPErrorOnError` — meaning any Gather error (including "duplicate metric collected") turns the whole `/metrics` response into an HTTP 500, not just the offending series.

Three collectors are exposed to this: `internal/collector/services.go:76-84` keys the services metric on `(name, description)` and drops the unique `id` field that OPNsense actually exposes (`opnsense/services.go:5`); `internal/collector/wireguard.go:111-121` keys peer metrics on `(device, device_type, ifname, peer_name)` where `peer_name` is free-form user config that OPNsense does not enforce as unique per interface; and `internal/collector/ntp.go:117-165` keys NTP peer metrics on `server` alone, which collides if two configured associations reference the same remote. The repo already recognizes this exact hazard class and defends against it elsewhere — `opnsense/tailscale.go:101-110` explicitly dedupes tailscale peers with a comment noting duplicate labels would fail the scrape — but services, wireguard, and ntp were left unprotected.

This is a latent/conditional bug: it requires a specific misconfiguration on the OPNsense box (e.g., two wireguard peers on the same device sharing a display name, two NTP associations to the same server, or two services sharing both name and description) to actually fire, but when it does fire the blast radius is total — the entire `/metrics` endpoint goes dark, not just a bad series, causing a full monitoring blackout of the firewall.

## Evidence

- `internal/server/metrics.go:68-71` — the promhttp handler uses `promhttp.HandlerOpts{}`, whose zero value is `ErrorHandling: HTTPErrorOnError`, so any Gather error 500s the whole response.
- `internal/collector/services.go:76-84` — services metrics keyed on `(name, description)`, dropping the unique `id` field present in `opnsense/services.go:5`.
- `internal/collector/wireguard.go:111-121` — wireguard peer metrics keyed on `(device, device_type, device_name, peer_name)`; `peer_name` is free-form user config, not guaranteed unique.
- `internal/collector/ntp.go:117-165` — NTP peer metrics keyed on `server` alone.
- `opnsense/tailscale.go:101-110` — existing precedent: tailscale peers are explicitly deduped with a comment noting duplicate labels would fail the scrape, establishing this is a known/treated hazard class in this codebase, just not applied consistently.
- `internal/collector/collector.go:818` — the collector's `recover()` only catches panics from `Update()`; a Gather-time "duplicate metric" error is not a panic and is not caught there.

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: the live box's three `dpinger` service rows differ only in `description` (not in `name`), so no collision currently fires there; `wireguardClients` returned an empty peer list and `ntpStatus` had a single peer, so neither currently collides either. The verifier independently reproduced the underlying mechanism in isolation, using the repo's exact `prometheus/client_golang` version: a collector emitting two `MustNewConstMetric` calls with identical label values, served via `promhttp.HandlerFor` with `promhttp.HandlerOpts{}`, returned HTTP 500 for the whole endpoint with `"collected metric ... was collected before with the same name and label values"`.

## Failure scenario / impact

Two OPNsense wireguard peers on the same device given the same free-form display name (OPNsense does not enforce peer-name uniqueness), or two NTP associations pointed at the same remote server, or any future service pair sharing both `name` and `description` → the Prometheus registry's `Gather()` call fails with a duplicate-metric error → because the handler uses default `HTTPErrorOnError`, the entire `/metrics` response becomes an HTTP 500 → total monitoring blackout of that firewall (every metric, every collector, not just the colliding one) until the misconfiguration is fixed.

## Suggested direction

Add the unique `id` field into the services label set (or dedupe defensively with a seen-map, mirroring `opnsense/tailscale.go:101-110`) and apply the same defensive dedupe to wireguard peer and NTP server label tuples. Independently, consider setting `promhttp.HandlerOpts{ErrorHandling: promhttp.ContinueOnError}` (or similar) so a single colliding series degrades gracefully instead of blanking the entire scrape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test feeds `services.go`'s collector two service rows sharing `name` and `description` but different `id`s, and asserts the resulting label set is unique (either via the `id` label or a dedupe step) and `Update()` does not produce duplicate label tuples.
- [ ] A unit test feeds `wireguard.go`'s collector two peers on the same device with identical free-form `Name` values and asserts the collector deduplicates (or otherwise guarantees unique label tuples) rather than emitting both as-is.
- [ ] A unit test feeds `ntp.go`'s collector two peer entries with the same `server` value and asserts unique label tuples are produced.
- [ ] A regression test (or documented handler-level test) confirms that a duplicate-metric Gather error does not 500 the entire `/metrics` response — either because the collectors above now prevent duplicates, or because `internal/server/metrics.go` is updated to a non-`HTTPErrorOnError` mode with a test asserting partial output is still served.
- [ ] `make test` passes with the new coverage, and no existing metric output for services/wireguard/ntp changes on the non-colliding live-box shape (i.e., the fix does not alter labels when there is no collision).

Part of the production-readiness bug bash — tracker: #72
_Found by automated bug bash, 2026-07-03. Verified adversarially._

comments.body:
Fixed in 45e3403. Added emit-time dedupe guards to all three collectors, mirroring the acme/certificates/tailscale precedent:

- **services** — skips a second row sharing (name, description).
- **wireguard** — skips a peer duplicating (device, device_type, device_name, peer_name).
- **ntp** — dedupes per-peer series by `server` (first association for a remote wins).

Each drop logs a warning rather than emitting a colliding tuple. This is defence-in-depth alongside the server-side `ContinueOnError` handling shipped in #81, which already prevents a single duplicate from 500-ing the whole scrape. No label or metric-shape change on non-colliding input (live-box shape unaffected). Covered by three new tests using the `assertNoDuplicateSeries` helper.

body:
> **Scope update (2026-07-03):** the portable Prometheus rules format (`grafana/alerts/opnsense.rules.yaml`) has been **dropped** — Grafana-managed alerting is now the only shipped format (commit 2af458a, closing #76/#95). The `promtool check rules` acceptance criteria below are therefore **void** (there is no Prometheus rule-group file to validate); they are replaced by a check that validates the generated **Grafana-managed manifests** and their regeneration freshness. The dashboard metric-coverage gate part of this issue is unchanged and still stands.

## Problem

The Grafana dashboard and alert-rules artifacts under `grafana/` are generated-and-committed files with no CI enforcement, contradicting what CLAUDE.md promises.

`grafana/build_dashboard.py` only exits non-zero when invoked with `--check` (`if check_only and missing: sys.exit(1)` at `grafana/build_dashboard.py:254-255`). The `dashboard` make target (`Makefile:95-96`) runs the script with no `--check` flag, so in normal (write) mode a missing-metric coverage failure is merely printed to stderr and the command exits 0. No workflow under `.github/workflows/` invokes `build_dashboard.py` in any mode — the CI `docs` job only runs `make docs-check` (`go run ./scripts/docgen -check`), a separate Go program that reads the committed `grafana/dashboard-stats.json` verbatim (`scripts/docgen/stats.go:21`) and never re-derives or cross-checks it against the actual dashboard build. CLAUDE.md:59 states unconditionally that this is "**required — a coverage gate enforces this**" and that `make dashboard` "**fails the build if any catalogue metric is left off the dashboard**" — neither is true in CI, and the first claim is only true locally if a contributor happens to pass `--check`.

The same gap exists for the generated alert/recording-rule manifests. `Makefile:98-99`'s `rules` target just runs `build_rules.py` locally with no validation step, and no workflow references the `grafana/alerts` path at all — so an edit to `build_rules.py` (or a committed manifest left stale after a rule change) can land on `main` and ship with nothing catching it.

## Evidence

- `grafana/build_dashboard.py:254-255` — `sys.exit(1)` is gated by `if check_only and missing:`; write mode (no `--check`) always exits 0 even with missing metrics.
- `Makefile:95-96` — `dashboard:` target: `cd grafana && python3 build_dashboard.py` (no `--check`).
- `Makefile:98-99` — `rules:` target: `cd grafana/alerts && python3 build_rules.py` (no validation / no regen-diff step).
- `CLAUDE.md:59` — "run `make dashboard` — it **fails the build if any catalogue metric is left off the dashboard**" and the section header "Dashboard (required — a coverage gate enforces this)".
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:37-52` — the docs job runs only `make docs-check`; grepping all files in `.github/workflows/` for `dashboard`, `build_dashboard`, `build_rules` returns zero hits.
- `scripts/docgen/stats.go:21` — `loadDashboardStats` reads `grafana/dashboard-stats.json` from disk verbatim and only fails if the file is missing or has zero metrics/tabs; it never re-invokes `build_dashboard.py`'s actual coverage computation.

## Failure scenario / impact

A contributor adds a new collector with new metrics, runs `make docs` and commits. Even if they also dutifully run `make dashboard`, it prints `MISSING (10)` to stderr and exits 0; the full CI suite (tests, docs, docker, `ci-success`) is green. The published `grafana/dashboard.json` ships without the new metrics while docs/README continue to claim "all N metrics across M tabs" — exactly the drift the documented coverage gate exists to prevent.

Separately, any future edit to `build_rules.py` (or a manifest committed without regeneration) that leaves `grafana/alerts/grafana-managed/*.json` stale relative to the builder lands on `main` with nothing catching the drift.

## Suggested direction

Make `build_dashboard.py` exit 1 on missing metrics in both modes, or have the `dashboard` make target run `--check` after writing; add a CI job that runs `python3 build_dashboard.py --check` plus a regenerate-and-`git diff` staleness check for `dashboard.json`/`dashboard-stats.json` and the `grafana/alerts/grafana-managed/*.json` manifests, and wire it into `ci-success`'s `needs`. Validate the generated Grafana-managed manifests (well-formed JSON / expected `apiVersion`+`kind`, optionally via `gcx` schema validation). Fix the CLAUDE.md claim to match whichever behavior is implemented.

## Acceptance criteria

body:
## Problem

The API-contract drift canary workflow (`.github/workflows/api-contract.yml`) tries to find and reuse an existing "OPNsense API contract drift" issue so it can dedupe (comment instead of re-creating) and auto-close it once drift clears. Both the "open or update drift issue" step and the "close drift issue when clean" step filter `gh issue list --json ...author` results with a jq predicate that requires `.author.login == "github-actions[bot]"`.

That literal never matches. Since `gh` CLI v2.50 (2024), the `--json author` field for a bot-authored issue is returned as `{"is_bot": true, "login": "app/github-actions"}` — not `github-actions[bot]`. GitHub-hosted runners ship a current `gh` version, so on every scheduled run the `existing=...` lookup evaluates to empty, even when an open drift issue created by this same workflow already exists.

Note this is specific to the `gh issue list --json author` GraphQL-backed path; the separate `api-contract-enrich.yml` workflow uses the REST API (`jq .user.login == "github-actions[bot]"`), where the bot login really is `github-actions[bot]` — that check is correct and unaffected.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/api-contract.yml:132-133` (open/update step) and `.github/workflows/api-contract.yml:147-148` (close step) both contain:

```
existing=$(gh issue list --label api-drift --state open --json number,title,author \
  --jq '.[] | select(.title == "OPNsense API contract drift" and .author.login == "github-actions[bot]") | .number')
```

Verified independently (verifier, not livebox — this is a GitHub Actions/CLI behavior check, not an OPNsense box check): running `gh issue list --json number,title,author` against a real `github-actions[bot]`-authored issue returns `{"author":{"is_bot":true,"login":"app/github-actions"}}`. Running the workflow's jq filter verbatim against that data returns nothing; swapping in `.author.login == "app/github-actions"` returns the issue number. `gh --version` on a current GitHub-hosted runner matches the CLI version where this login shape applies.

## Failure scenario / impact

Monday 06:17 UTC (the workflow's cron schedule), when OPNsense API drift is first detected, the workflow creates issue #N. The following Monday, if drift is still present, the "open or update" step fails to find #N (jq filter never matches) and creates a brand-new duplicate issue instead of commenting on #N. This repeats every week drift persists, filling the tracker with duplicate `api-drift`-labeled issues. When the drift is later fixed, the "close drift issue when clean" step has the same broken lookup, so none of the accumulated duplicates ever get auto-closed — they all sit open indefinitely, turning the canary's issue trail into noise instead of a signal.

## Suggested direction

Change both jq filters to match `app/github-actions` (or accept either login spelling to be resilient to future `gh` CLI changes), or drop the author filter entirely since the `api-drift` label plus the exact issue title is already a unique enough match for this workflow's own issues. Alternatively, switch the lookup to the REST-backed `gh api repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues?labels=api-drift`, where the login is reported as `github-actions[bot]`, matching the existing (correct) logic in `api-contract-enrich.yml`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The "open or update drift issue" step's `existing=` lookup finds an already-open `api-drift`-labeled, correctly-titled issue created by the workflow's own token, and posts a comment on it instead of creating a duplicate.
- [ ] The "close drift issue when clean" step's lookup likewise finds and closes that same existing issue once drift clears, rather than finding nothing.
- [ ] A regression test (or a documented manual verification step run against a real bot-authored issue via `gh issue list --json author`) confirms the jq predicate matches the actual login shape returned by the `gh` version used in CI.
- [ ] Re-running the workflow twice in a row while drift is present results in exactly one open `api-drift` issue, not two.
- [ ] The fix does not change the correct, unaffected REST-based bot-login check in `api-contract-enrich.yml`.

body:
## Problem

`opnsense/activity.go` parses the thread-state summary line from `top -aHSTn` output using a single rigid regex that requires the exact contiguous sequence `N threads: A running, B sleeping, C waiting`. FreeBSD's `top` only prints thread states that are non-zero, in a fixed order (`starting, running, sleeping, stopped, zombie, waiting, lock`), so any header that omits `waiting` (count 0) or inserts `zombie`/`stopped`/`starting` between `sleeping` and `waiting` breaks the strict adjacency the regex expects.

When the regex fails to match, `threadsRegex.FindStringSubmatch` returns `nil`, and `SystemActivity`'s four thread fields (`ThreadsTotal`, `ThreadsRunning`, `ThreadsSleeping`, `ThreadsWaiting`) are left at their Go zero value. `FetchActivity` still returns `nil` for the error — there is no log path for a regex non-match, since the only `Warn` calls in that function guard `strconv.Atoi` on `\d+` captures, which cannot fail once the regex has matched. `internal/collector/activity.go` then unconditionally sends all four gauges from this zeroed struct, so the collector reports scrape success with silently wrong (zero) values.

## Evidence

- `opnsense/activity.go:9` — the regex definition:
  ```go
  threadsRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`(\d+)\s+threads:\s+(\d+)\s+running,\s+(\d+)\s+sleeping,\s+(\d+)\s+waiting`)
  ```
- `/usr/local/opnsense/scripts/system/activity.py:49` (data source, confirmed live) runs `/usr/bin/top -aHSTn -d2 999999`.
- `internal/collector/activity.go:99-125` emits `opnsense_activity_threads_total/running/sleeping/waiting` unconditionally from the parsed struct, with no check that parsing actually succeeded.

Confirmed against a live OPNsense 26.1.8 box: a real `top` run produced a header with no `waiting` segment (`8 threads: 2 running, 6 sleeping`), and the `top` binary's embedded strings confirm the state fragments (`starting,`, `running,`, `sleeping,`, `stopped,`, `zombie,`, `waiting,`, `lock,`) are each emitted only when non-zero. A throwaway regex test against realistic header variants — `"...831 sleeping, 1 zombie, 34 waiting"`, `"...1 starting, 13 running..."`, `"...1 stopped, 34 waiting"`, and `"10 threads: 1 running, 9 sleeping"` (no waiting) — all failed to match; only the clean 3-state `running, sleeping, waiting` header matched.

## Failure scenario / impact

A single transient zombie, starting, or stopped thread present in a `top` snapshot (routine and common on OPNsense, e.g. a short-lived zombie PHP child) produces a header like `879 threads: 13 running, 831 sleeping, 1 zombie, 34 waiting`. The regex fails to match, so for that scrape `opnsense_activity_threads_total`, `_running`, `_sleeping`, and `_waiting` all report `0`, while `scrape_collector_success{collector="activity"}` still reports `1` and no warning is logged. This produces false zero-dips on thread-count dashboards and can trip low-threshold alerts, with no diagnostic trail pointing to the cause. This is an intermittent, data-dependent failure — it recurs any time the process/thread mix on the firewall includes a state outside the exact `running, sleeping, waiting` triple.

## Suggested direction

Parse thread states independently rather than as one fixed sequence: extract the total from `N threads:`, then scan for each `(\d+)\s+<state>` pair (`running`, `sleeping`, `waiting`, `stopped`, `zombie`, `starting`, `lock`) individually, defaulting any absent state to 0. Log a warning when the `threads:` header is present but no state segments parse at all, so a total regex-parsing failure is distinguishable from a legitimately state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test feeds a `top` header containing a `zombie` segment between `sleeping` and `waiting` (e.g. `"879 threads: 13 running, 831 sleeping, 1 zombie, 34 waiting"`) and asserts `ThreadsRunning`, `ThreadsSleeping`, and `ThreadsWaiting` are parsed correctly (not zeroed).
- [ ] A unit test feeds a header with `waiting` entirely absent (e.g. `"8 threads: 2 running, 6 sleeping"`) and asserts `ThreadsRunning`/`ThreadsSleeping` are parsed and `ThreadsWaiting` defaults to 0 without failing the whole parse.
- [ ] A unit test feeds a header with a `starting` or `stopped` segment inserted before `running` and asserts the other states still parse correctly.
- [ ] `FetchActivity` logs a warning (not silence) when a `threads:` header is present but no individual thread-state segment can be parsed at all.
- [ ] Existing tests for the clean `running, sleeping, waiting` header continue to pass unchanged.

comments.body: Fixed in 73ba3f8. Thread states are now parsed independently: a `N threads:` header match sets the total, then each state segment (running/sleeping/waiting, plus starting/stopped/zombie/lock) is scanned on its own and any absent state defaults to 0. A transient zombie/stopped/starting thread (or an omitted `waiting` segment) no longer breaks the match and zeros the gauges. When the header is present but no state segment parses at all, that now logs a warning instead of silently reporting zeros. Covered by four new table cases in `opnsense/activity_test.go`; existing clean-header tests unchanged.
